description: Lack of professional conduct of recruitment agency and/or employer
closed_notes:
This issue was related to worker changing employer and moving to a glove factory. Workers reported that the change of employer was voluntary and that they have received a new contract that include a the minimum wage rate according to the LPA. However, workers were asked to do 14 days of quarantine before staring at the new job and they did not receive wages for those days which was not communicated to workers before they decided to move to the new workplace. 

Even though Seafresh was not part of the process of moving workers to a different workplace they were aware of the process, Issara provided recommendations on how to handled such cases correctly, such as informing the recruitment agency of the source country about the changes, informing DOE, and so on.

The business did not take any action to remediate workers or towards the person in question.

remediation_issara_recommendation: Context: The issue with a worker whose documents were not extended by the business so that the worker ended up being arrest by the local police and being detained from June 22 till today (14-Jul). The worker said that she had given her document and the extension fees to the business since February - 2021 but the business was not able to extend her work permit. She added that she had been working for the business without a valid work permit since February. It is also added that there could be more workers in this situaiton.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The business response ID- 1332

Issara raised this issue with Nike, Nike responded that they have checked with Hong Seng and found as following - The problem is that the DOE said it didn't have the client's information in the system, even though HS had processed her work permit. HS does not know how this could be the case. HS decided to continue to employ her after Jan 2021 without the proper documents.  With rising Covid cases, there was a government Internal Security Operations Command (ISOC) inspection of the factory and they found the client to be working with an expired visa.  HS tried to negotiate with the police but she was taken to the immigration detention center, first to Suan Plu now to another IDC in Bang Khen, and awaiting deportation.  HS was providing her with 3 meals a day while in Suan Plu IDC and also has been paying her daily wages from the date of her arrest.  Now, she is in the Bang Khen IDC, where she is more isolated and HS cannot provide her with the daily meals as they used to at Suan Plu IDC.  HS wants to hire her back after she goes through the MOU process back in Myanmar. Issara has shared the newly announced document by the government which has options for the workers to apply their documents in Thailand.
remediation_notes: The issue with one worker that was arrested by the police because her work permit had expired, which the business failed to extend even though she had already paid the business for her medical check-up, work permit, and visa.  She is currently in a detention center and has been told she will be deported when the borders open.
remediation_action: Issara has alerted the Strategic Partner about this issue, and the SP is in the process of working with the business to resolve the matter.

However, the business had to transfer payments to her through the police at the detention center, and the police made illegal deductions on the money received, so the worker ended up receiving less than what she should have received.

description: Lack of professional conduct of recruitment agency and/or employer
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the recruitment fees being charged by the recruitment agency representative who is stationed in the Cal-Comp factory area. The person who collects the money is being known as a huanna-sub (sub-supervisor in English). The worker reported that they have contacted a person whose name was included in a job announcement to work at Cal-comp. After contacting the phone number from the announcement, the worker was asked to contact another person, a huanna-sub (sub-supervisor in English) who told the worker that she have to pay 2,500 THB for the job application.  

 The worker did not mention the channel through which the announcement about the job vacancy was done nor the name of the huanna-sub who asked her to pay. In addition to that, the worker added that one of her friends was being charged 3500 THB to get a job in Cal-Comp. NOTE: So far, Issara knows about 2 workers being impacted however there could be many more. 

Recommendations for remediation: 
-The business to do an immediate investigation to assess the number of impacted workers and identify the people involved in the recruitment process that has been charging workers. Safeguards should be in place throughout the investigation, and workers should not be targeted by the sub-supervisor or recruitment agency representative. 
-The investigation should also cover the staff from the recruitment agencies to identify the root causes of the issue and understand who was involved in the collection of the money.
- Actions should be taken towards those who collected the money, and the business should clarify with the recruitment agency that no fees should be charged to workers and what are the consequences for not following that policy, such as termination of the contract or disciplinary actions if those involved are Cal-Comp  employees. 
-As part of the investigation and remediation process, the business shall assess how much money new workers have paid and reimbursed them those recruitment fees. 

-The business should set a plan of action with the recruitment agency involved, such as revision of the contract and the penalties for not following the company policy about “zero recruitment fees for workers”, and the actions the agency will take to avoid this from happening again. 

-The business should cross check through different means with the recruitment agency and workers being recruited, how are the services being provided to job seekers, what is the communication like about the job and the recruitment process, etc. 
-One way of conducting the investigation and a vetting process is for Cal-comp to check all the announcements about job vacancies and verify that there are no fees being charged, that the process is handled legally and ethically and that all the recruitment agencies being used work professionally. 

Past history of this case:

Last year (2020) there was a similar case reported and the business conducted investigations for all issues and remediated the impacted workers which is considered a good step made by the company to address issues with recruitment. However, the process took several months and the business did not share with Issara the details of the last investigation conducted regarding walk-in workers being asked to make monetary donations to the Thai RA staff, and only one worker received compensation for that issue. In addition, the company did not follow Issara's recommendation on system change to have communication sessions with all workers and Thai RAs about the company policy of recruitment fees.

Timeframe 1 pay period
remediation_business_steps_taken:
-Issara raised this issue with the business, the business agreed to conduct a vetting process to find out about the announcement that had been made and workers being charged and then get back to Issara.
-The business responded that they have been investigating to find out the person who collected the money from the workers and they have some suspected person for the further investigation. It is added that once the business compete the investigation process, the impacted workers will be reimbursed.
remediation_notes: Two workers reported seeing a job advert for jobs at Cal-Comp and contacted the broker about getting a job as a walk-in worker. The broker told the workers to contact one of the "wanna-said" based in the factory about getting a job. One worker was asked for a payment of 2,500 Baht and the other was asked to pay 3,500 Baht to be able to get a job.
remediation_action: The business said that they outsource hiring to 7 recruitment agencies, and would investigate this matter. It is noteworthy that last year (2020) there was a similar case reported and the business conducted investigations, eventually partially remediating impacted workers, which was considered a good step made by the company to address issues with recruitment. However, the process took several months and the business did not share/collaborate with Issara regarding addressing root causes, to avoid the same issues from arising in the future (as they are now) - for example addressing corrupt supervisors conducting exploitative recruitment, or conducting communication sessions with all workers and supervisors about the company's ethical recruitment policy and prohibition of informal brokering with recruitment fees.
remediation_validation: The business is in the process of investigation; there have been no actions or improvements yet that have been verified by workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for system change

-The business is encouraged to use the Golden Dreams Job Marketplace to have a more direct recruitment process and avoid these kinds of risks of fees being charged to job seekers. It is a high risk for the company who will ultimately be responsible for any fees being charged against the company policy and the buyer code of conduct. 
-The business is also encouraged to promote Golden Dreams Marketplace in their social media and other channels to let job seekers know that they can directly apply through the app and no at all will be charged. 

-Effective communication in a wide range should be conducted in the written and verbal post including disciplinary action for those who break the business's recruitment policy or do not follow accordingly.

Recommendations for remediation: 
-The business to do an immediate investigation to assess the number of impacted workers and identify the people involved in the recruitment process that has been charging workers. Safeguards should be in place throughout the investigation, and workers should not be targeted by the sub-supervisor or recruitment agency representative. 
-The investigation should also cover the staff from the recruitment agencies to identify the root causes of the issue and understand who was involved in the collection of the money.
- Actions should be taken towards those who collected the money, and the business should clarify with the recruitment agency that no fees should be charged to workers and what are the consequences for not following that policy, such as termination of the contract or disciplinary actions if those involved are Cal-Comp employees. 
-As part of the investigation and remediation process, the business shall assess how much money new workers have paid and reimburse them those recruitment fees. 

-The business should set a plan of action with the recruitment agency involved, such as revision of the contract and the penalties for not following the company policy about “zero recruitment fees for workers”, and the actions the agency will take to avoid this from happening again. 

-The business should cross-check through different means with the recruitment agency and workers being recruited, how are the services being provided to job seekers, what is the communication like about the job and the recruitment process, etc. 
-One way of conducting the investigation and a vetting process is for Cal-comp to check all the announcements about job vacancies and verify that there are no fees being charged, that the process is handled legally and ethically, and that all the recruitment agencies are used to work professionally. 

Past history of this case:

Last year (2020) there was a similar case reported and the business conducted investigations for all issues and remediated the impacted workers which is considered a good step made by the company to address issues with recruitment. However, the process took several months and the business did not share with Issara the details of the last investigation conducted regarding walk-in workers being asked to make monetary donations to the Thai RA staff, and only one worker received compensation for that issue. In addition, the company did not follow Issara's recommendation on system change to have communication sessions with all workers and Thai RAs about the company policy of recruitment fees.

Timeframe 1 pay period
remediation_business_steps_taken:
-Issara raised this issue with the business, the business agreed to conduct a vetting process to find out about the announcement that had been made and workers being charged and then get back to Issara.
-The business responded that they have been investigating to find out the person who collected the money from the workers and they have some suspected person for further investigation. It is added that once the business competes for the investigation process, the impacted workers will be reimbursed. 
-The business updated that they have conducted the survey with the newcomer in the past last month but did not find any issue from the survey. The business also reported conducting the survey with the workers who were recruited in August, however, only one worker was found being impacted.

Issara raised this issue with K Narisa (HP focal). She responded that she is aware that the factory is understaffed, however, she will try her best to push the business to work on this issue by the 15th of November.
-The business updated that they have interviewed 171 workers who were recently recruited and found workers being charged 5000-53000 THB by the recruitment agency Number 17. The HP suggested the business conduct interviews with 100% of workers and conduct the reimbursement within December.


Issara had another escalation call with the business, the business responded that they have investigated the original case and repaid the worker.  CC is in the process of interviewing all workers hired since August 2021, 470 total workers of which 210 were hired for production supplying HP.  This is expected to be completed in January 2022 and workers reimbursed.  CC noted there is an issue with hiring of walk-in workers.  Recruitment agencies are using sub-agents.  CC has taken the following actions: they trained the 13 RAs on zero fees, helped them review the job advertisements, and set up the policies/procedures for compliance and RAs not in compliance will be penalized in a 3-step process.  First time, CC will decrease demand of workers from the RA; second time, CC will decrease the demand further, and third time, CC will cancel the service agreement with the RA.

Apart from that, the HP focal, K Narisa suggested Issara to conduct the recruitment fee survey with the worker. Issara will have follow up discussion with the HP and conduct the survey.


K. Piyabutr, CSR, inquired about the completion of the finding report after Issara interviewed the workers.
remediation_notes:
Case #1: 
Two workers reported seeing a job advert for jobs at Cal-Comp and contacted the broker about getting a job as a walk-in worker. The broker told the workers to contact one of the "wanna-said", a representative of the recruitment agency, based in the factory about getting a job. One worker was asked for a payment of 2,500 Baht and the other was asked to pay 3,500 Baht to be able to get a job.

Case #2:
A recruiter was advertising jobs for the business via facebook livestream, offering to take workers from all over Thailand and offering rewards of up to 5,000 Baht to any recruiters that could bring / refer 20 workers to them.
remediation_action:
The business said that they outsource hiring to 7 recruitment agencies, and would investigate this matter. It is noteworthy that last year (2020) there was a similar case reported and the business conducted investigations, eventually partially remediating impacted workers, which was considered a good step made by the company to address issues with recruitment. However, the process took several months and the business did not share/collaborate with Issara regarding addressing root causes, to avoid the same issues from arising in the future (as they are now) - for example addressing corrupt supervisors conducting exploitative recruitment, or conducting communication sessions with all workers and supervisors about the company's ethical recruitment policy and prohibition of informal brokering with recruitment fees.

The business is in the process of investigation and have identified certain suspected persons that may have charged recruitment fees from the workers. 
Once the business competes the investigation, impacted workers will be reimbursed.  The business surveyed new employees that joined in August 2021 but found only 1 worker had paid recruitment fees. 

The Strategic Partner (SP) has requested that Issara conduct a recruitment fee survey on behalf of the business to verify recruitment fees paid.  The SP is in the process of securing agreement on the part of the business to move forward with this.
remediation_validation:
The business is in the process of investigation; there have been no actions or improvements yet that have been verified by workers.  

These issues have been discussed additionally with the Strategic Partner, who has been working with CalComp on escalating issues and CalComp developing a more responsible recruitment process and implementation.  However, issues with current in-country recruitment practices continue to be uncovered, with concerning behavior by Thai recruitment agencies engaged by CalComp and fees being reported by workers.  There is a need to both immediately investigate and repay fees charged to workers in this recruitment, but also develop a more comprehensive plan to address structural issues and resources dedicated to worker recruitment - moving beyond internal company investigations and audits of contracted agencies.  This is particularly pressing given continuing worker reports, continued worker recruitment, and planning for working with Myanmar recruitment agencies for the potential reopening of cross border recruitment.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  Issara has conducted the recruitment fee survey to determine the recruitment fees paid by this group of walk-in workers.  The survey results have been shared with the Strategic Partner and with the business.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for system change

-The business is encouraged to use the Golden Dreams Job Marketplace to have a more direct recruitment process and avoid these kinds of risks of fees being charged to job seekers. It is a high risk for the company who will ultimately be responsible for any fees being charged against the company policy and the buyer code of conduct. 
-The business is also encouraged to promote Golden Dreams Marketplace in their social media and other channels to let job seekers know that they can directly apply through the app and no at all will be charged. 

-Effective communication in a wide range should be conducted in the written and verbal post including disciplinary action for those who break the business's recruitment policy or do not follow accordingly.

description: Lack of professional conduct of recruitment agency and/or employer
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1: 
The issue with the recruitment process. A worker from the factory reported that there were 8 of  her relatives in Myanmar who had applied for the job at Hi-Tech 91 in Thailand since early January 2022. When the factory HR conducted an interview with them via online, the HR said that they all will be selected for the migration and suggested the job seekers stay healthy and alert for the migration. However, a few days later only one worker was informed by the business passing the interview and the rest 7 were informed of failing. The current worker at the factory reached out to the HR to check about her relatives not passing the interview, the HR asked the factory interpreter to check the list of the candidates. The interpreter checked and simply replied that they (7 workers) failed the interview. The worker wanted to know why her relatives failed because during the interview with the  HR, they were told to be selected and asked to stay healthy. The worker also heard some rumors of having to have a special relationship with the  interpreter if anyone wants their relatives or friends to be selected as a successful candidate. All of the candidates are from Bago Division.
Name List of the candidates; 
Min Khant Kyaw
Su Khaing Win
Aung Phyo
Ei Ei Aung
Nya Mwae Pan (Nilar Soe)
Joue Joue Naing (Nyine Nyine Soe)
Htet Arkar Lin
Zin Mar Oo (Successful Candidate) 

Name of the interpreter ; Ms. Jue Jue (Kyu Kyu Hlaing)
Name of the Recruitment ; Libra Life

Recommendations for the remediation;
-The business to work with the recruitment agency and check the candidate list to find out what happened with this group of  jobseekers and communicate back to them the reason why they were told they would be hired but the business has now reversed this decision. 
- Have clear criteria for screening, interviewing, and hiring decisions so that the hiring process is transparent and is not influenced by favors given or expected by the HR staff making the hiring decisions.

Talking Points; 
What is the status of the recruitment with the business recently and at the moment? 
Have there been interviews conducted and shortlisting done with the job seekers? Who from HIT91 is conducting these interviews and who makes the decision on which applicants to hire?
What is the role of the interpreter in the interviews and hiring decisions?

Case #2: 
Client reported that the line supervisor announced that the factory was recruiting walk-in workers and that current workers could refer their friends to come and apply.  So one of her friends called her husband to come and her husband asked to resign from his old job. Last week, he arrived at HT-91 with a cancellation letter; however, the business told him that they cannot accept him because his bank card is not with Siam Commercial Bank. The problem is he cannot apply for a new bank card yet as he would only receive his new work permit with HIT 91 in July 2022. HIT91 also attempted to provide the recommendation letter to Siam Commercial Bank so that the worker could open an account but the bank didn't approve issuing him the bank account.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara has shared this issue with the business. The business responded to conduct an investigation and get back to Issara.


The business will review all 7 workers. However, the company will submit the demand first, and then these workers will be interviewed on 25-30 April. In addition to that, the business has communicated about the business recruitment process that is unbias and no fees for the process.


Issara raised this issue again with the business to confirm about these job seekers. The business noted the job seekers should apply with Libra Life directly.


Case 2: The issue with a worker who was rejected for not having a certain bank.

K. Witsawad, Senior Management, responded that he had already spoken with K. Raweeroge, HR manager, and that due to the Nike COC, the company cannot pay employees in cash and must only pay by bank transfer. Transferring another back except SCB is difficult because this is the bank's payroll system. The company will, however, accept and hire impacted workers who do not have the original worke permit. The company has a solution for transferring money to another bank. Please inform the workers as well.


Case 2#

BHR did reach out to the business and and K. Raweeroge mentioned that this worker hasn't apply the job yet. So the worker would go to apply and get the job with no bank issue on Saturday. Dar Dar talked with the worker for going on apply and be interviewed.
remediation_notes:
Case #1:
A worker from the factory reported that 8 of  her relatives in Myanmar had applied for jobs at Hi-Tech 91 since early January 2022. When the factory HR conducted online interviews with them, HR said that they would be hired and they stay healthy and be ready to travel soon.  However, a few days later only one worker was confirmed as hired while the other seven were told they would not be hired after all. So, the worker reached out to HR to check the status of her relatives' job applications but was simply told by the HR interpreter that seven of her relatives had failed the interview.  The worker also heard rumors that you would need to do favors for the interpreter if you wanted your relatives to get jobs at the factory.


Case #2: 
A worker reported that her co-worker invited her husband to apply for a job because the line supervisor announced that the factory was recruiting walk-in workers and that current workers could refer their friends to come and apply.  The husband applied and was accepted; therefore, he resigned from his old job and came to the factory with the cancellation letter.  However, the business said they couldn't accept him because there were government delays in processing his work permit (to be ready in July 2022) and without his work permit, he couldn't open his bank account at Siam Commercial Bank, which is required for making salary payments. The business had tried to help him open the account by providing the recommendation letter to Siam Commercial Bank but the bank didn't approve issuing him the bank account.
remediation_action:
Case #1: 
The business will review the application of all 7 workers. However, the company will submit the demand first, and then these workers will be interviewed on 25-30 April. In addition to that, the business has communicated to all workers about the business recruitment process, that it is unbiased and zero recruitment fees to the workers.

The business did not confirm whether these 7 job seekers were to be interviewed during the period of 25-30 April.  Instead, it encouraged the job seekers to apply directly with Libra Life, the recruitment agency responsible for the hiring of HIT91 workers in Myanmar, and that Libra Life was still in the process of filling many open positions.

Issara updated the business that 4 remaining job seekers had been asked to apply in-person in Yangon again by Libra Life although they had already done this before.  The business said it would notify Libra Life that these job seekers shouldn't need to make another trip to Yangon to apply.


Case #2:
Issara spoke with the business, and HR noted that they had done all they could to try and get Siam Commercial Bank to open the bank account for this worker but had failed.  Issara is going to speak with the senior management about this because it is a matter of making temporary arrangements for paying the worker's salary while waiting for the work permit to be issued and the worker can open the Siam Commercial Bank account.
remediation_validation:
Case #1:
Issara followed up with the HIT91 worker and she provided an update saying that 3 of her relatives had now secured jobs at HIT70, which is close to HIT91.  Now, 4 of relatives are still waiting.  Since then, the business said that job seekers should apply with Libra Life directly.  Issara provided this information to the HIT91 worker to relay to her 4 relatives still looking for jobs.  The workers noted that since they'd applied previously, they didn't want to travel to Yangon again which was at considerable cost.  Issara will inform the workers about the latest update, which is that the business will inform the recruitment agency directly that they would not have to go and apply again since they had already done so.


Case #2:
Issara will inform the worker regarding this case after hearing back from the business.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for system change. 
-To manage the recruitment process ethically and transparently, Issara to work with the recruitment agency in Myanmar and help the recruitment agency post the job vacancy in the Golden Dreams MarketPlace. 
-Issara will also provide training to all Nike suppliers on “Ethical Recruitment in April 2022.

description: Lack of professional conduct of recruitment agency and/or employer
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client reported that there were 4 workers, including him, who went back to Myanmar on 21 May 2023 with other workers, and they have the issue with getting their passports from Myanmar. There are almost 50 workers who did U-Turn with them and other workers got their passports and they have already signed the contract and are about to come back to Thailand.
When they called and checked with Ko Phyo Min Hlaing, representative of Aung Pyae recruitment agency in Myanmar, he said that their passports got retained by the government as their names are similar to the CDM (Civil Disobedience Movement) staff.  It meant that their passports did not pass the screening process in terms of validating whether the passport' holders are non-involved in anti-government activities. It meant that in order the workers need to get their passport, they will be under interrogation whether they are involved in anti-government activity or not. This kind of interrogation process is a bit scary as they will be tortured. So Ko Phyo Min Hlaing told them if you give 5,000,000 MMK or you will be taking interrogation.
The workers are not afraid to deal with the government if they will be asked some questions. But, they are worried that sometimes, the staff who are involved in the interrogation process are trying to ask the money and they will be tortured even they can give the reason and don't want to pay money.
They have already reported this to the HT-91 line group for "MOU U-Turn". The workers seek help if the business can give them any support regarding this issue. They assured that they are not involved in any kind of anti-government activities. He said both the interpreter and the manager were aware of this.
The manager said that they will only take care of those who got the passports already and will come back soon. They will not take any responsibility to these 4 workers regarding this passport issue. Now, he has already left the line group.
The workers are reaching out to us to see if we can give any support to them or not. The workers add that if the business cannot do anything, they will try to come back to Thailand from illegal channels and try to register for pink cards as the deadline is until 31 Jul 2023.
O&E recommendation:
It would be great if we can check with businesses whether they can give any recommendation letter stating that these workers are working in the factory and not involved in any kind of political activities. Also, it would be good if the business can coordinate with the Myanmar Embassy to approve their recommendation letter too. This would help the workers when the workers have to talk with the government staff on the Myanmar side. From the RA side, I think it's a bit unethical to give the option to the workers like 5,000,000 MMK or you will be interrogated. They should try to coordinate with the government and explain the workers' situation instead.

Here are the workers names and ID cards no. while they worked in HT-91.
1. AUNG THURA (91190603052)
2. THANT ZIN (91190603018)
3. PYONE MOH MOH (91190603119)
4. THIRI SHAN (91190603039)

Recommendations:
- The business to discuss with the RA immediately to ensure that the RA does not collect any fees and helps the workers show they are not involved in anti-government activities and their passports are processed without further delay
- Make every effort to ensure that workers can get their passports
- If providing a letter by the business will help this matter to allow the Myanmar government to issue their passports, the business should provide such a letter to the RA for submission to the government
- Communicate with and update workers what actions the business and RA are taking to help them get their passports

supplier_name: Cal-Comp Electronics (Thailand) Public Co., Ltd. - Samut Sakhon
description: Lack of professional conduct of recruitment agency and/or employer
Lack of professional conduct of recruitment agency and/or employer
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context:
The client Naing Htet Thu from ISA Value stated that he came to Thailand via the undocumented channel in October 2021 and started working on Oct 18 2021 and the business collected 2,450 Baht after 15 days of working in ISA Value for pink card application. The client said, in his recruitment journey, he had to pay transportation fees and other expenses from his own pocket.

TPs:
- What are the company’s current hiring practices, whether through the formal MOU channel or hiring walk-in workers already in Thailand?
- Is it aware of Amazon’s Employer Pays Policy and the company’s obligation to ensure that workers don’t pay for any recruitment-related fees or expenses?

Recommendations for remediation: 
-The business to do an immediate investigation to assess the number of impacted workers and identify the people involved in the recruitment process that has been charging workers. Worker safeguards should be in place throughout the investigation, and workers should not be retaliated against for having spoken out. 
- Disciplinary actions should be taken towards those who collected the money, and the business should clarify with the recruitment agency involved that no fees should be charged to workers and the consequences for not following that policy, such as termination of the contract or disciplinary actions if those involved are Cal-Comp  employees. 
-As part of the investigation and remediation process, the business shall assess how much money workers have paid and reimburse such amounts. 
-The business should set a plan of action with the recruitment agency involved, such as revision of the contract and the penalties for not following the company policy about “zero recruitment fees for workers”, and the actions the agency will take to avoid this from happening again.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that he had migrated to Thailand via the undocumented channel in October 2021 and started working at this factory on Oct 18 2021. The business collected 2,450 Baht from him after 15 days of working for the pink card application.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change
- The business should review its current hiring practices, including how it is hiring workers that are already in Thailand or those that may have migrated to Thailand recently but not through the MOU channel
- The business should develop vetting and selection criteria for the recruitment agencies it will work with.  Issara can provide support with the vetting and selection tool
- Do a full review of current recruitment agencies in Thailand and source countries using the vetting and selection criteria, and consider which RAs to continue working with, which it will stop working with, or new RAs to work with in the future
- Review the management service agreements with each RA, update the MSAs to ensure transparency and zero fees for workers.  Develop MSAs with source country RAs directly.  Issara can provide support with the MSA checklist tool
- Check all job vacancy announcements that its RAs are posting, ensure the announcements make the zero fee policy explicit
- Provide full and accurate job description information for all future job vacancies to the RAs

description: Lack of professional conduct of recruitment agency and/or employer
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Two years ago, SFP failed to extend the visa and WP for 10 workers and it would process the MOU u-turn process for them.  They had to go back to Myanmar to do MOU U-turn with the help of SFP and Arborfield RA.  However, with Covid-19 lockdown measures and the shutdown of the MOU process, they have not been able to return to work at SFP.  One worker that called us has been staying at the dorm provided by the recruitment agency for the past two years and is now hoping to come back to Thailand very soon. His family (daughter and wife) are working at SFP and are waiting for him to come back to Thailand.

Talking points:
Is the business aware of this case and other workers that were unfortunately stuck during the U-turn process because of the Covid lockdown and MOU hiring suspension?
This worker’s family members are currently working at SFP and have made queries about this worker?  Why was there no response from the business?
Arborfield RA is waiting for the business answer on this worker’s hire.  Has the business responded to the RA?

Recommendations for remediation:
The business should check its files to review the history regarding this worker that has been stuck in Myanmar while attempting to do the MOU U-turn process, which the business instructed the worker undertake
The business should coordinate with Arborfield RA to ensure that the worker is hired as an MOU worker and the process for his return to Thailand expedited, given that he has been waiting in Myanmar for two years now
The business to communicate to the worker to clarify what the business will do to support the worker, explaining the process and schedule of what needs to happen to process the needed documents and transport him to Thailand

Recommendations for systems change: 
The business to review its management service agreements with its recruitment agencies, to ensure that there are clauses in the agreement regarding reporting channels for workers during the recruitment process (including the MOU U-turn process) and worker reports are responded to
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business Responses: 
K. Sophon said the business was aware of this case and other workers that were unfortunately stuck during the U-turn process. The SFP is checking all the worker that was stuck on the Myanmar side during Covid-19 and how many people would like to come back and work for the SFP? 
SFP will not recruit the job seeker who was over 50 years old and it is the SFP policy. But for this U Thein Tun (MOU U-turn) case is not a job seeker and SFP will consider it a special case. K. Sophon will check with the production manager and get back to Issara again on 10 June 2022. 

SFP recruitment plans for 2022: 
SFP plans to recruit Myanmar MOU workers in Sep 2022, around 50 - 100 workers. Now SFP is checking whether they can recruit Myanmar workers or not? Information has been provided and the SFP will recruit MOU workers directly with Arborfield RA from Myanmar and no Thai RA. 

Refresher Kick-Off with SFP in June 2022 : 
K.Sophon will inform the SFP management team and provide more updates for Issara - SFP refresher kick-Off, SFP management team contact number, and email address on 10 June 2022.

One worker that called Issara has been staying at the dorm provided by the recruitment agency for the past two years and is now hoping to come back to Thailand very soon. His family (daughter and wife) are working at SFP and are waiting for him to come back to Thailand.
remediation_action:
Issara has contacted the business but HR has not been responsive and we have not been able to discuss the case with SFP.

Issara also contacted Arborfield recruitment agency regarding this case. 
The recruitment agency said it was waiting for the decision from SFP as to whether the business will hire him at this point.  The recruitment agency also noted this worker had not originally been hired by Arbourfield for SFP, and there was the question as to whether this worker would be eligible to be hired as an MOU worker because he is 51 years old now and the Thai Immigration law has a maximum age limit of 50 years.

closed_notes: Issara had meetings including escalation calls with TU's Sustainability Director and recommended that no workers that had already resigned should be held against their will or coerced into returning to work.  TU explained that they didn't want the workers leaving the province illegally given the current Covid-19 restrictions.  The Sustainability Director said they would escalate the matter to the factory MD. The following day, TU completed the process of issuing official separation documents for the workers. However, workers were held by the business against their will for 3 days. In addition to that, the workers mentioned having some missing payments for their daily wages from the business. Workers added that they refused to wait for the business to conduct the investigation for their missing payment as they wanted to leave the area as soon as possible. However, it is the business's responsibility to make sure that all workers are paid all of their wages upon their departure. Having a debt to pay to the workers after they leave their job is against the local law. Issara is checking with the workers if they want the business to process their missing payment since they are free from business control. If the workers request Issara to discuss with the business, the issue will be opened under other KPI related to the missing payment. As additional information, workers shared that two-thirds of Burmese workers have left the business by several means because of the poor working conditions.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A group of 11 workers who have submitted resignation a week ago and were preparing to depart are not being allowed to go by the business. The workers reported that their belongings were taken by the business when they were about to leave in a van and that they now do not have a place to stay since they have already given back their rooms. Workers reported the reason for leaving job is as follows:
(1) discrimination against nationalities at the workplace,
(2) the business not keeping the promise of paying double for the working hours during COVID-19 restriction as promised,
(3) translator not being helpful and being biased by just listening to the business and not the workers. 

Recommendations: 
-As it is a worker's right to resign and leave the company, the business shall immediately investigate why this group of workers were not allowed to leave. And then come to an agreement with workers for their departure from the company without restrictions.
-Since the business made the taxi driver leave without the workers, it will be challenging for workers to find a new driver, therefore, the business is suggested to help workers find a new taxi/van for workers safe return. -Since the vaccination is a workers personal health matter, the business should provide vaccination cards or any support documents as proof that workers have received vaccination. If the business does not have such documents, the business should coordinate with the health organization that provided the vaccine to make sure all workers receive the vaccination card. 
-The business should immediately check with all workers and provide their missing daily wages if any. 


Talking Points: 
-What is the reason why this group of workers were stopped by HR? 
-Is business aware of this issue? 
-Workers have reported several workers leaving the job because of several repeated issues in the workplace, what is the business understanding of this? Does the business seek workers' feedback and have done anything to improve the working condition rather than stopping workers from leaving? 
- What was communicated to workers as reasons for not being allowed to leave the company?
-What was the reason for the business calling the police and threatening the workers? 

Added TPs; 
Because workers have resigned and are asking to depart, this situation should be addressed in less than the 3-4 day timeline suggested by SCC.
No resigned worker can be held against their will, or coerced into returning to work
Resigned workers can be provided vaccine certificates and COVID tests to ensure there are no positive cases before departure
Workers can be clearly offered a return to work, with no coercion, and with clear communication on next steps
Because this situation has escalated, Issara can jointly speak with HR and the group of workers if desired, to support communication.
Issara also recommends we provide training to HR reps at SCC, on COVID and other protocols for workforce management.

ETI Base Code 1.2. Employment is freely chosen; workers not required to lodge deposits or documents with employer, and free to leave with reasonable notice

Workers off-shift should be free to leave their workplace and dormitories, with no threats or assertions of control over their movements. Workers should never be treated as the property of employers, recruiters, brokers, or agents; and, their movements should never be restricted by these actors. Workers should be free to leave their jobs with reasonable notice.

The Sustainability Director said they would escalate the matter to the factory MD. The following day, TU completed the process of issuing official separation documents for the workers. Workers added that they refused to wait for the business to conduct the investigation for their missing payment as they wanted to leave the area as soon as possible. However, it is the business's responsibility to make sure that all workers are paid all of their wages upon their departure. Having a debt to pay to the workers after they left their job is against the local law. Issara is checking with the workers if they want the business to process their missing payment since they are free from business control. In general, workers added that two-third of Burmese workers have left the business by several means because of the poor working conditions.
remediation_business_steps_remaining: The business to conduct the investigation for the workers missing wages and transfer the money to the worker's bank account.
remediation_notes: A group of 11 workers who had submitted their resignation letters a week prior were preparing to depart by van when they were not being allowed to go by HR staff and the security guard.  They also packed up and left the company dormitory so now have no place to stay. In addition workers noted that they hadn't received their wages for some days.
remediation_action:
Issara reached out to the business immediately.  The business explained that HR had communicated to the workers about the government's travel restrictions to prevent the spread of Covid-19, and that they are not allowed to travel outside Songkhla province because it is currently a Covid-19 red zone.  They said police had come to enforce the travel restrictions and the van driver left without taking the workers after talking to the police.  Regarding vaccination certificates that would be important for when the workers travel back to Myanmar, the business said the document issuance was delayed by the hospital and would be provided to the workers when issued.  For now, the business said the workers are still living in the private dorm and the workers can ask the landlord to stay in the same place. 

The business will get back to Issara with corrective actions within 3-5 days.

The business further updated Issara saying pictures of HR staff with negative comments regarding this incident had been posted on social media and they wanted the workers to remove the posts.

Issara escalated this issue with TU's Sustainability Director, and recommended that no worker that had already resigned should be held against their will or coerced into returning to work.  TU explained that they didn't want the workers leaving the province illegally given the current Covid-19 restrictions.  The Sustainability Director said they would escalate the matter to the factory MD.  The following day, TU completed the process of issuing official separation documents for the workers so that they can leave.

Regarding the wages, the business noted that they could investigate what had happened with workers wages and compensate workers accordingly.
remediation_validation:
Issara followed up with the workers and provided an update, explaining that the business had said they were following government rules of not allowing inter-provincial travel and that the business would get to Issara in 3-5 days about next steps.  

The workers did not want to stay there anymore; they felt pressured and forced to go back to work.  They were even willing to pay any government fines if there were any for crossing province lines.  Since they have resigned, they don't understand why the business is not letting them leave.  They just want to be able to travel back to Myanmar. 

Regarding the social media posts, the workers said they did not take any photos or videos during the incident nor did they post anything on social media or ask their friends to do so.

The workers have confirmed that they have officially resigned from their jobs and are free to leave.

Regarding the wages, workers noted not wanting to wait for the business to conduct an investigation, as they wanted to leave as soon as possible without waiting for any compensation.
remediation_results: The business processed the official resignation of the workers and the workers have been allowed to leave.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
System Change:
-It is the  business responsibility to have good working conditions that allows workers to feel ethically and fairly treated. This will reduce workers turnover rates, as workers would not feel the need to leave the job. In order to assess the level of satisfaction of workers and identify the areas of improvement, the business is recommended to conduct an internal survey or Issara’s worker satisfaction survey to address the root cause of the issue and improve the system. 
-The business to communicate with the HR and the security guard about the business policy on freedom of movement and rights to make decisions. The communication should include the action that will be taken against the offender. 
-The business should communicate with all the workers about their plan to improve the working conditions and maintain the workers. Otherwise, there could be more workers planning to leave the job.
systems_change_business_steps_taken: The business has not taken any action to improve the system. Therefore several workers keep reporting to Issara about their departure from the factory
systems_change_business_steps_remaining: The business to take proper action to improve the system and retain workers as suggested by Issara.

description: Lack of professional conduct of recruitment agency and/or employer
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Robert from Royal Gate International, Myanmar RA, reached out to Issara as he was informed by MD of Htay RA that someone from TUM contacted them on 22nd May (Sunday) and asked to cancel the job interview that they are planning to have on 23rd May (Monday). Almost all the job seekers were either on the way to Yangon or already arrived. They sought assistance from Robert and since he knows that Issara is working with TU, Robert offered his help to check and confirm what has happened with TU and how Issara can help. 

According to Htay RA, the interview was cancelled as Andy Hall asked why TUM had selected a new RA instead of working with current RAs and if they continued with the recruitment, he would let TU's customers know about this. Htay RA was confused and wondered why TUM has to cancel everything based on one person's comment while this might cause a big problem to Myanmar RA if job seekers report the case to MOLIP that the job interview was canceled without having any good reason. RA had to inform and apologize to the job seekers about the cancellation and they feel unfair that job seekers had to cover the costs based on this unexpected short-notice cancellation. Robert also checked with Andy but Andy said that he is no longer with MWRN and denied having anything to do with the situation.  

TUM demand of 800 workers (200 workers x 4 batches) was approved by Thai DOE in December 2021 and approved by Myanmar MOLIP in March 2022. TUM selected Htay RA and had a business deal since early 2022; however, TU never shared this information with Issara as part of recruitment updates and planning. 

Robert updated Chaw to update that Htay RA has been informed by TUM that TUM will have an auditor working for TUM who is based in Yangon conduct an assessment with Htay sometime soon.  Chaw asked who from TUM contacted Htay but Robert does not have the information and it seems like Htay does not want to provide that information to Robert/Issara. 

Chaw followed up with Robert to get update on the job interviews for TUM.  Robert confirmed that the interview had been canceled and TUM said that they will have to conduct an audit of Htay and only after that, will they be able to resume the recruitment. 

Htay RA mentioned to TUM that they are planning and willing to engage with Issara but the contact person from TUM replied that they do not work with Issara. This has led to Htay not contacting Issara directly but providing updates to Robert.
remediation_business_steps_taken: The TU has already consulted with that RA, and they are working with the RA to reimburse the job seekers who returned home. The TU will soon hold a meeting and training for the Myanmar RA. And the TUM is still recruiting these job seekers in accordance with the plan.
remediation_notes: A recruitment agency contracted by the business to hire MOU workers from Myanmar had scheduled interviews with many job applicants but was asked by the business just a day before the day of the scheduled interviews to cancel the interviews and put the recruitment process on hold.  This has led to many applicants traveling to Yangon from various parts of the country spending considerable time and money for the transport, meals, and accommodation only to be informed at the last minute that their interviews have been cancelled.
remediation_action: Issara has raised this with the business, and the business HR will investigate the incident.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The worker came to work on an MOU contract a few years ago but could not go back to Myanmar to extend his MOU during COVID. As a result, the company, like other factories, processed the work permit and visa extension for him in Thailand. In July 2022, the workers were asked to apply for a new passport at the Embassy in Bangkok, and it cost 7,000 THB per person. The factory has now informed them that they must return to Myanmar to get a new MoU contract. From what he knows, he shouldn't have to go back to Myanmar to extend his MOU contract because he knows workers in other factories that are in a similar situation but don't have to go back for this. He would like to get clear information from the business.

TPs:
-For MOU workers who need to extend their MOU contracts, what is the company doing to facilitate that process?  Are workers required to travel back to Myanmar to renew their MOU contracts?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Communicate clearly with workers that need to renew their MOU contracts about the extension process and whether they need to return to Myanmar to do so.  Provide sufficient information so that workers know what needs to happen when and how the company will support them during the process.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers unapproved documents. A group of workers who were recruited under the "Recalibration Program" in 2022 reported not getting their documents since they have started working for this factory. They said that it is not clear if their documents are being processed or not. 


Talking Points: 

-What is the status of these workers? 
-What has the business done so far? 


Recommendations: 

The business to clearly communicate with the workers if the issue is with the government site.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business responded that there are about 450 workers in this situation, the business has been trying so hard, visiting the immigration once a week to follow up. However, the government process is extra slow which caused all the delays. The good news is that the business was able to pay the registration fee to the immigration for half of the workers which means their documents are to be approved and distributed soon. For the remaining workers, it is not sure if they will be rejected or accepted, if they are rejected, the business will do the appeal as they need more workers. 

Issara suggested the business to communicate with all of the workers about these updates. 

Business responded that it is impossible for them to do so as there are so many  workers and are in different shifts. 


Issara suggested the business to issue such an update in writing so that Issara can help communicate with the workers. The business agreed to do that, however the business failed to do so. 

Several months later, the business updated that they were able to register half of the workers out of 450 and distributed their documents in their hands. However for the remaining workers who did not pass to be registered and officially work in Malaysia, the business has been trying to register under another round of "Recalibration 2.0" which is less strict than the previous one. The business is hoping to complete the application by the middle of June,2020. However, the business is not sure when the work permit will be distributed to the workers. 

Issara has updated the business response to the workers.

Workers have been following up with the Issara, however Issara is not able to get the clear update from the business yet.

description: Lack of professional conduct of recruitment agency and/or employer
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: the client arrived in Malaysia on 19th October 2023. upon arrival they were picked up by a Tamil broker who they referred as Boss. the first month or so after they came they did not have any work, until the Tamil broker sent them to this place to work. following are the issues and findings from the client:

- there are 5 of them.
- before departure from Bangladesh they were told their job is in plum oil industry. however, they are given work to harvest tomatoes. 
- they have been working in this place for 17 days. 
- instead of 8 hours shift they have to work 12 hour shifts. 
- they were promised that they could make up to RM2200-RM2300, but are told they will be paid RM20 per day.
- the Tamil guy who sent them here is not replying to their calls and messages, asking them "why they have so many problems".
- they asked the Tamil broker to give them different job, but he did not agree.
- they do not have their passport with them, they believe their passport is with the Tamil broker. 
- they are planning and trying to leave the place and find other places to work. 

Issara had a follow up call with them and following are the updates received from the client: 

- 5 of them left the workplace in the afternoon. 
- they contacted the Tamil broker prior to them leaving, stating their plan to leave and come to him. he responded by saying, if they leave the place he will not be liable for them. 
- they also consulted their recruitment agency back in Bangladesh. the agency suggested them to leave and go to the Tamil broker and assured them if they face any problems they will help. 
- together all 5 of them received RM500 for working 12 hour shift of 17 days. 
- they are paying the taxi they rented by themselves. 
- location they are going to is: Taman Desa Aman, 09400 Karangan, Kedah, Malaysia

Issara staff is engaged with them following all the updates provided by the client.

A worker reported that he was recruited as an MOU worker by Touch Manak Manpower Supply recruitment agency, and he paid around 650 USD for the recruitment fees. remediation_notes: The worker reported that the business informed eight workers that their work permits would not be extended and their last day would be May 24, 2020. These workers, who joined the company in October 2018 as Walk-In MOU workers, were reportedly promised 30,000 Baht in severance pay and a cancellation letter around June. However, since their visas and work permits expire on June 5, they fear it's impossible to find a new employer. They seek Issara's help to negotiate with the business and address this poor company policy and communication.
remediation_action: Issara Institute conducted a remediation call with the supplier to discuss the company’s recent decision to lay off eight migrant workers for KPIs #xxx, xxx and xxxx. Here are the findings of the discussion: - The company called the eight workers to a meeting to inform them of the company’s decisions not to extend their contracts and carry out the MoU U-turn, which was due to the need to downsize its workforce over decreasing client orders and downward business performances. The workers were given an acknowledgement letter to sign. - Their last day of work is May 24, 2020. The company asked the worker if they want to go back to Myanmar. If so, they will provide transportation for them. The workers said they want to continue staying in Thailand. - The severance pay will be given to the workers on May 23, 2020, with the amount varying based on the period of their employment. The cancellation letter will be provided to workers on June 8th, as the DoE will take time to process it. However, it is still within the 15-day time frame required by law. - The company will likely implement further cuts in their workforce in the future due to its downward business outlook. However, they are currently unsure how many workers will be laid off and when. This depends on whether the company can finalize the pending orders with the clients in the upcoming months or not. The criteria for choosing which workers to let go is based on their work performance and skills. - The workers expressed concerns over not being able to find new jobs in time before their work permit expires. This might be because the workers are not yet aware of the 60-day grace period, which starts after their last day of work at the company and during which they can stay in Thailand to look for new employers with the cancellation letters. In this regard, the business will inform the workers of this grace period this week to help address and alleviate their concern. - Regarding the potential future lay-offs, the company will try to inform the workers as soon as possible, but it depends on the trends of client orders. In any case, they will include and reiterate the 60-day grace period policy in their communications to laid off workers in the future.
remediation_validation: Issara has communicated back to the workers why the business cannot make an announcement to the entire factory about adjusting their workforce demands. However, the business is willing to provide a job change letter if workers wish to change jobs in advance of termination and the workers are now aware that they have 60-days grace period to look for another jobs. Overall, the workers understand the situation now and are aware that the business is ready to support them with a job change letter and they have 60 days to find a new job as well. Plus the business will be providing them with severance pay. Issara is accordingly closing this case.
remediation_results: Workers raised this issue in the first place as they were not aware that they have 60-days grace period to find a new job and the business will also provide them with a job change cancellation letter and severance pay. They are satisfied with the outcome and Issara is accordingly closing this case.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Including this client 210 other Bangladeshi workers were brought to Malaysia with calling visa promising a job here. it has been 4 months since then and they are not provided with any work. moreover, following are the issues that the client shared: 

- they are kept somewhere in JB and are not allowed to go out of the confinement.
- there was a Bangladeshi (contact given in issue link) broker through whom they came who is believed to be retaining their passport. when they kept asking for the passport, allegedly he said, "if you guys continue to ask for your passport, we will burn them" and now he is not reachable anymore.   
- they are not given food regularly, don't have access to fresh water to drink, and the electricity is irregular. 
- they are not allowed to go the embassy. 
- there is a Tamil, Malaysian who is kept to look after them, who allegedly physically abuse them. 
- the client and the workers have reasons to believe the normal police are taking bribe to overlook this issue. so they have no where to go. 
- they are kept and forced to stay there against their will. 
- both from the origin and the destination side they have not received any support.
- the client even requested if Issara can, they should send the immigration police. 

the client was requested to share contacts of other victims to connect and get more details by Issara staff.

this call made to get consent from the client to share the issue details with other organization or give his contact to other organization to handle their case. 

The client gave consent to share the issue details BUT DOES NOT WANT HIS PRESONAL INFORMATION AND/OR NAME TO BE SHARED OR HIGHLIGHTED ***

He wants to keep his name PRIVATE, as we does not want to risk anything happening to him.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
this call was made to update the client about sharing his contact information with Our Journey to handle his case. following are the points discussed in this call:

- his case was referred to Our Journey, an organization which helps and works towards the fair practice of migrants rights.
- he can expect to receive call from Our Journey, as his whatsapp contact and name was shared with the organization, and he can freely share his problems with them.
- it was shared with him that Issara staff has shared and discussed with Our Journey about his case, but he might receive question that he already answered with Issara staff. 
- he was requested to keep Issara staff posted once he receive their call. 

Issara staff will remain in contact with him following the progress of his case.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Newly hired Lao MOU workers noted that they paid 3.8 million kip and 10 million kip (31,240 Baht); they paid to the recruitment agency but have not received the reimbursement.  The Lao workers also said they had been informed that they would be provided with the essential items such as a mattress, bed, pillow, rice cooker, etc.  However, when they arrived, their dorm room was empty. 

Talking points:
-Is HR aware that workers were promised to be supplied with basic living supplies but they did not receive them when they arrived?
-How does HR instruct the recruitment agency to communicate accurately the terms and conditions of the contract and details about the living arrangements that will be provided?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Investigate what was promised to workers about supplies to be provided to them in their living quarters and what was actually provided to them on arrival.
-Provide such promised supplies to workers without delay
-Communicate to the newly arrived Lao workers about what happened and the actions the business is taking to make amends.
-Train the recruitment agencies working with Seafresh to ensure that the agencies communicate accurately the terms, conditions, and benefits of employment so that the workers actually get what they were promised.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Narumon, HR mentioned that HR conducted the survey with the workers. There are two groups of Lao workers. The first group already got the reimbursement. The second group is in the process of reimbursement. She will send us in detail of the plan and timeline for this reimbursement next week.

Seafresh had a meeting and trained with the recruitment agency regarding the cost and fee that the workers paid and also the facilities that the worker misunderstood that provided the essential items such as a mattress, bed, pillow, rice cooker, etc. According to Seafresh policy, the dorm provides for the room and bed not just items that were mentioned previously. However, Seafresh clearly communicated with the workers regarding the employer pay policy and dorm policy when the worker arrived at the orientation session.


K. Narumon, HR, informed us that the 500 THB reimbursement will be transferred into the workers' bank accounts on December 16.
remediation_notes: Newly hired Lao MOU workers noted that they paid 13.8 million Lao kip (31,240 Baht) to the recruitment agency but have not received the reimbursement.  The Lao workers also said they had been informed that they would be provided with the essential items such as a mattress, bed, pillow, rice cooker, etc.  However, when they arrived, their dorm room was empty.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change
-Revise the management service agreements (MSA) with the recruitment agencies so that it clearly states how the recruitment agency will communicate accurately to the hired workers the terms, conditions, and benefits of employment so that workers actually get what they were promised upon arrival.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Star Butterfly general service Co.ltd
Hoi Yun SDN.NHD. 
 
Recruitment background.
 
10 workers 5 Male and 5 Female were recruited in Mid November 2022. However 2 female workers out of 10 had to pay 5,100,000 Kyats (2424.50 USD)  for the recruitment fees to the broker who was recruiting workers for an Agency named “ Star Butterfly general service” in Myanmar. The rest of the 8 workers did not have to pay any fees for different reasons such as having their relatives in the workplace, being recruited with Zero fees however they also heard that they will be deducted their salary by the employer. However, the contract does not mention the zero recruitment fee. 

Main issues 

They started working on the 18th of November,2022. Two female workers out of 8 called Issara to report the following issues. 

1) Different working conditions from what they were promised for. Their contract does not mention the type of work.Once they apply for the job, the broker said it is packaging of the seafood product, however, workers are having to work at the place which is similar to the pier where they have to sort fresh fish. These two workers said that they have health issues working with the ice and water which is why they did ask the broker about the type of work, the broker said that they will not need to touch water and ice at all but now things turn out the other way around. 
2) Not getting a weekly day off as mentioned in the contract. 
3) Having to work on an hourly rate not daily rate which is against  the contract. 
4) Not getting Malaysian Public holidays.
5) Not having their documents such as passport and permit  in their hand, only provided with the copy of it. 
6) Not knowing when they will receive their wages. They started working on 18th Nov but have not received their wages yet and are not sure when they will receive it. 
7) Not having a safe community to live in; they said that there are only 3 single girls and two females with their husband then the rest of the workforce is male workers, the environment is not safe because of the drug users. These two workers do not feel safe to continue working there. They called the broker to complain about the situation but were told not to complain as they have been working already. They do not have contact with the recruitment agency.

Issara sent a message to follow up with her to learn her expectations for her cases, she said that she and her friends received a salary for 8 days only even though they have worked for about 25 days. The employer said to them that they retain their 15 days of wages as deposit. In addition to that, the employer did not pay for the days that he was not able to provide job, did not get paid for over time as worked, they worked 3 hours of IT some days but received only 2 hours of wages. Workers tried to negotiate to work daily basis but not on an hourly basis, however the employer forced them to work hourly basis. Workers said that they will discuss with the broker who they worked with to get this job, however the employer said not to discuss with the agency or the broker but to decide by themselves. Given that, the workers have called the broker, the broker said that they will inform the agency and agency will try to negotiate. Workers were asked to wait and see for one month.

The worker said that they have reported to the broker about their situation, the broker had suggested them to wait one month until next pay day and see if they need to reach out to the recruitment agency. However, their current situation is that they are not provided with a full day of work, it has been three days that they have been working for only half a day. description: Document retention
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client worked at a Korean BBQ restaurant located in KL Kepong Jalan Metro Perdana, which is one of fifteen branches of the restaurant chain. Out of the fifteen branches, this particular one was problematic. The restaurant has six Nepali and thirteen Burmese workers. The owner's son is abusive towards the Nepali workers, creating a hostile work environment. Issara is able to speak with two workers. They have been working for this employer for 10 months. They are all MoU workers. They are reporting as a group of 5 Nepali workers, but the client is quietly reporting. The client and the workers want to either be transferred to another branch under the same company or find employment in another company. The client has debts to pay and doesn't want to return to Nepal. The workers have a contract they made in Nepal, but the company made another contract which the client doesn't have and is unaware of its contents.
Following are the major issues reported by workers.

1) Document retention: Workers passports are held by the employer since they started their employment. The company also kept their passports and didn't provide them with worker ID cards (Jalan cards) or necessary documents. 

2) Restriction of Movement: The workers were not allowed to leave the premises, and this restriction also made it difficult for their friends to visit them.

3) Unfair suspension: Workers were frequently suspended for minor mistakes or even without any reason. During these suspensions, the company did not provide any food, and the workers were not allowed to go out and get their own. They were also denied access to basic amenities, like cooling fans, during these periods. One incident occurred when a friend of the client was suspended for simply asking a Burmese worker to clean a stain. The owner verbally abused him and kept him in detention (suspension) for 28 days. Throughout this time, the company did not provide any food or salary, leaving the workers in a dire situation. His friends attempted to provide food secretly, but they had to be cautious as the company would punish them if they were caught bringing in more substantial amounts of food or any food.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: 

-One of the clients shared that his nephew came to KL, Malaysia on October 4th, 2023 through AGA International, RL: 530, a recruitment agency in Bangladesh. he paid a total fee of 420,000tk to the agency for visa and everything. an addition of 10,000tk was spent for medical check up on their own. Total 3905 USD. 

- a total of 400 workers came in separate groups along with him through the same agency. the clients nephew signed a contract for Orionplus Construction (M) SDN BHD, for the contract he paid 2,000tk in Bangladesh (which is a common practice for signing and getting contract in hand, according to the client). 

- since their arrival in Malaysia they have not been provided with any job yet. they are kept together in groups in a facility on factory site. the agency and Orionplus promised them that between 15th-17th November they will provide them with CIDB card and only after then they can start working. 

- in the beginning they were told that if someone finds work and wishes to leave the place they could, by paying RM1,000-RM1,500 they can take their passport and leave. soon after, they announced and stopped the practice. 

- from 4th October they were given RM50 weekly for food, which is to be deducted from their salary once they start working. 

the client provided a contact number of a representative of Orionplus, (03-4131 9961) and upon request of Issara staff shared the contract of his nephew and one of his friend, who were contacted directly to double check the issues. they shared the same concern, that they have not started working yet and they are worried that they can not start earning money after leaving their country. 

according to the management of the business, since the workers got their training classes to acquire the CIDB card on 4th November 2023, they should be receiving their CIDB card within the next 15 days since the test. but until now they have not received the card nor any work. 

the current updates are the followings:

- the workers has done the CIDB training, but they have not received the physical card yet. 
- online tracking of the card says its in the process of delivery (find it in the issue link along with the contract).
- the Bangladeshi broker who was the focal to bring them here is not answering their calls anymore.

the client is requesting Issara to if possible contact the management and ask when can they start working, because when the victims ask these questions to the management they are not given any answer and are often ignored.

Issara is trying to get the consent from the clients to refer their case to another local organization in Malaysia.

Context: Including this client 210 other Bangladeshi workers were brought to Malaysia with calling visa promising a job here. it has been 4 months since then and they are not provided with any work. moreover, following are the issues that the client shared:

- there was a Bangladeshi (contact given in issue link) broker through whom they came who is believed to be retaining their passport. when they kept asking for the passport, allegedly he said, "if you guys continue to ask for your passport, we will burn them" and now he is not reachable anymore.   
- they are not given food regularly, don't have access to fresh water to drink, and the electricity is irregular. 
- they are not allowed to go the embassy. 
- there is a Tamil, Malaysian who is kept to look after them, who allegedly physically abuse them. 
- the client and the workers have reasons to believe the normal police are taking bribe to overlook this issue. so they have no where to go. 
- they are kept and forced to stay there against their will. 
- both from the origin and the destination side they have not received any support.
- the client even requested if Issara can, they should send the immigration police. 

the client was requested to share contacts of other victims to connect and get more details by Issara staff.
