description: Document retention
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: the client arrived in Malaysia on 19th October 2023. upon arrival they were picked up by a Tamil broker who they referred as Boss. the first month or so after they came they did not have any work, until the Tamil broker sent them to this place to work. following are the issues and findings from the client:

- there are 5 of them.
- before departure from Bangladesh they were told their job is in plum oil industry. however, they are given work to harvest tomatoes. 
- they have been working in this place for 17 days. 
- instead of 8 hours shift they have to work 12 hour shifts. 
- they were promised that they could make up to RM2200-RM2300, but are told they will be paid RM20 per day.
- the Tamil guy who sent them here is not replying to their calls and messages, asking them "why they have so many problems".
- they asked the Tamil broker to give them different job, but he did not agree.
- they do not have their passport with them, they believe their passport is with the Tamil broker. 
- they are planning and trying to leave the place and find other places to work. 

Issara had a follow up call with them and following are the updates received from the client: 

- 5 of them left the workplace in the afternoon. 
- they contacted the Tamil broker prior to them leaving, stating their plan to leave and come to him. he responded by saying, if they leave the place he will not be liable for them. 
- they also consulted their recruitment agency back in Bangladesh. the agency suggested them to leave and go to the Tamil broker and assured them if they face any problems they will help. 
- together all 5 of them received RM500 for working 12 hour shift of 17 days. 
- they are paying the taxi they rented by themselves. 
- location they are going to is: Taman Desa Aman, 09400 Karangan, Kedah, Malaysia

Issara staff is engaged with them following all the updates provided by the client.

description: Document retention
closed_notes: Workers updated that they approached the broker and got their passport back and through the help of the RA back in Bangladesh (Baron Overseas Limited) they got a job in the plum industry. They added that they will work for 8hrs a day for RM1500 per month.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
In June 2022, TUS announced, via translator, that they will be recruiting workers when the government opens registration for undocumented workers. The translator posted the announcement on his personal Facebook. Several workers from TUS invited their relatives and friends from Myanmar. Many of them came to Thailand using the informal channel. It’s heard that they had to pay 25,000 baht to brokers (it might be the broker couple) who arrange the transportation from Myanmar to Thailand because they also announced the job vacancy on their Facebook saying that they can help the job seekers to come to Thailand and there are no job application fees. 

When the job seekers arrived in Thailand, the broker couple (Kyang Sayar and Ma Mee), who are not TUS employees, told them that they should register pink card with other different employers first. So that it will be easy for the workers to move to TUS when TUS accepts the workers. The couple charged 13,000 per job seeker for pink card registration.

When TUS interviewed applicants for recruitment, none of these workers were invited to be interviewed. We don’t know exactly what’s the reason behind it. Maybe the workers didn’t have the document required by TUS. Maybe TUS heard about the brokers charging money from the workers. It’s unclear. There are about 70 workers using the service of the broker couple. TUS accepted other workers coming that are not tied with the broker couple. 

Getting rejected by TUS, the brokers took the workers to SCC to apply for jobs. The workers were rejected by SCC as well. Again, it’s not known why. However, some of them got accepted when they mentioned the name of TUS interpreter, who reports this information. 

The TUS interpreter, our ambassador, wants Issara and TUS to know about how the brokers are exploiting job seekers and migrant workers at TUS factory. He said he will send us the photo of the broker couple. He stresses that Issara keeps him confidential.

Talking points:
- Update TUS about this risk of brokers taking advantage of a company hiring announcement and charging fees to job seekers
- Is TUS aware that based on the company announcement, existing workers invited their friends and family back home to come to Thailand for this job opportunity?
- Is TUS aware of this broker activity?
- How did TUS determine which applicants to invite for the job interviews?  The job seekers that came with the broker were denied the opportunity to interview for the job.

Recommendations for remediation:
- Investigate this matter regarding the broker activity, and the TUS process for selection of workers to be hired as pink card workers.
- Communicate clearly to workers for all hiring announcements what kinds of job seekers should apply.  For this recent hiring of pink card workers, this was meant for undocumented workers already in Thailand and not for job seekers in Myanmar.
- The recruitment announcement should be clear what kind of job seekers the company will hire, and that broker fee should not be paid by the job seeker, to reduce the risk of brokers taking advantage of the opportunity to charge workers.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that there was an unknown broker who calls via the company's number (landline) asking whether TUS accepts workers or not because he had 200 job seekers who are looking for a job. However, the HR recruitment team has informed the broker that the company has a policy not to recruit workers through brokers. Therefore, the proposed group of job seekers was not accepted. HR clearly mentioned that they do not accept workers through brokers.
remediation_notes: In June 2022, TUS announced that it would hire workers when the pink card registration round opened.  TUS workers informed their relatives and friends in Myanmar, and many traveled to Thailand by paying a broker to smuggle them across the border.  This broker also charged them for the pink card registration but then when they went to TUS to apply for jobs, they were not considered for hiring by TUS.  The broker then took them to ITC to get jobs there but they were not accepted there either.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issara had an ongoing meeting with the business where the business explained that they only cover the recruitment fees for new MOU workers when workers are first recruited. However, other recruitment related fees such as document extension (work permit renewal, ongoing documentation related to employment) are not covered by the business. The business pays the fees in advance but those fees are then deducted from workers paychecks. This practice is against an employer pays policy, as all recruitment fees, including document extension costs, should be covered by the employer.


Talking points:
- We really appreciate our open discussion on current practices, recruitment in general, and how our partnership can work.
- Thanks a lot for raising that currently workers are paying for work permit and visa renewal, or other fees related to ongoing employment such as an updated health check.
- In our ongoing discussions with Nike, we clarified that these fees would fall under their employer pays policy, and should be covered by the employer.  This is also pretty standard for all definitions of employer pays.
- Our recommendation would be to change this practice now, and clarify with workers that these fees will be paid directly by Everest.  You can confirm this shift to us and to Nike.
- Issara and Nike will follow up on the previous practice and include this in our discussions with all Nike suppliers on ways forward in recruitment practice and learning.
- Issara can support the business to fully investigate if all workers are being charged these types of costs, and ensure full documentation of all affected workers, costs paid, and recommendations for repayment of recruitment and employment fees charged.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara has escalated this issue with the business, the business was not very clearly aware of the Nike policy regarding the Employer Pay Policy. The business responded and said that they will conduct payback to the workers. It was not clear with the process and the timeline. The business added that they will start following the employer pay policy starting from 2022.
The workers confirmed receiving their documents extension fees back from the employer. The amount that they have received was 13,500 THB per worker. 
This issue will remain open until Issara conducts the recruitment fees survey and analyse the amount that the workers have paid so far. After the verification through survey, Issara will consider to close the case with associated rating. At this point, it is hard to say whether the paid amount to the workers is align with what the workers have paid.
remediation_notes: Issara had an ongoing meeting with the business where the business explained that they only cover the recruitment fees for new MOU migrant workers (there are an estimated 28 Cambodian workers affected) when workers are first recruited.
remediation_action:
The business explained that they pay the fees in advance but those fees are then deducted from workers paychecks.

This issue was escalated to the company management and the company responded that they had consulted with the Strategic Partner in Thailand and that the Cambodian workers' recruitment fees would be reimbursed.

Starting in 2022, the company will implement the employer pay policy for extension fees. The company has shared the draft policy announcement with Issara, which will be reviewed and feedback provided.

The business has paid back the workers the amount of 13,350 Baht to the Cambodian workers.  It has also agreed to have Issara conduct the recruitment fee survey with the Cambodian workers, and this is in progress.
remediation_validation: The reported fees charged to workers would violate an employer pays or responsible recruitment policy or commitment, as these types of costs are directly related to recruitment and ongoing employment, such as a work permit renewal.  Issara will be conducting a recruitment fee survey to fully investigate if all workers are being charged these types of costs, and ensure full documentation of all affected workers, costs paid, and recommendations for repayment of recruitment and employment fees charged.
remediation_results: This issue will be closed after we get preliminary findings from the recruitment fee survey to determine additional fees workers may have paid in addition to what the business has paid back to workers.

description: Fees charged by employer: legal but not ethical
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Several workers reported that they had paid for visa extension and 90-day report fees and had not yet been reimbursed. One worker paid her line supervisor 4,000 Baht for the visa extension and 60 Baht for the 90-day report in May 2022. Another worker said he and his wife did the visa extension since February 2022, paying 2,700 baht each but never got the reimbursement. Still another worker said she had been reimbursed for the 90-day report fee but her visa extension fee of 2,700 Baht she still hadn't received back. However, she is sure that the factory will pay her back, so she isn't worried about that. She added that there are thousands of workers in the same situation so the business will probably repay batch-by-batch.

Talking points:
-Workers have reported paying different amounts for their visa extension, and some have been reimbursed while others haven't.  What are the reasons for this differing amounts workers are paying up-front and different times when workers are being reimbursed?

Recommendations for remediation:
-The business to announce to all workers, verbally and in writing, the process and timeframe for reimbursement since it is adhering to the EPP
-HR to reimburse the amounts workers have paid for the visa extension or 90-day report, and to provide pay slips that state the amount returned.
remediation_business_steps_taken: K. Sarayuth, HR, said that the company is currently working to reimburse workers who paid for the document extension. However, since the beginning of this year, the worker should not have been charged any fees; the company would cover them. They will look into this matter. In terms of communication, the company has already informed all workers of this policy. He will provide us with a written announcement about the policy.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
On 25 April 2022, a worker and her husband paid 9,000 baht for passport renewal. The worker heard the news about the reimbursement so she asked the interpreter but the interpreter asked the worker to wait as the reimbursement was to be done batch by batch. Till now, workers haven't received any reimbursement yet. Workers would like Issara to cross check with the business for them. Worker ID: C107214, C107175

In September 2021, the worker paid 4,200 baht for visa extension and paid another 9,000 baht for passport renewal. But the worker only received the reimbursement of 4,200 baht from the business. O&E also checked for the receipt but the worker said it is gone. Worker ID: C106375

On 27 April 2021, a worker and her husband paid to HR 13,300 baht each. But due to Covid, HR couldn't process the passport renewal for them and HR returned 2,000 Baht to each of them. Then in 2022, each paid another 9,000 baht for passport renewal. They received the reimbursement of 9,000 Baht from the business. The worker checked with HR as to why they were not being reimbursed for the original 13,300 Baht which they had paid back in 2021, of which they only got 2,000 baht back. HR said this is because the reimbursement was supposed to cover all the expenses that happened in 2022 only. O&E also checked whether they have the payment receipts but they couldn't find it. Worker ID: C104011

TPs:
-How is GFPT currently conducting the reimbursement to workers as a result of the recruitment fee survey conducted by Issara?
-What is GFPT covering in terms of recruitment fees and costs?  Do you have a detailed list of this?  Is the passport processing fee covered by GFPT?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Check the payments made by workers and reimburse them for those amounts, if not already done so. Provide pay slips or receipts for the reimbursements so workers understand what the reimbursements are for
-Communicate with clearly, in written and verbal form, to workers what the reimbursement is for and how the company is implementing the EPP, including the specific details on what fees and costs are being covered by the company.

description: Fees charged by employer: legal but not ethical
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that all MOU workers who will complete their 4 years or 6 years of their contracts and visa in 2023 were called to a meeting by the business on 6th November and were informed that they would need to apply for pink cards and it will cost 22,000 Baht and the workers must pay 14,500 Baht as a down payment by the end of this month. The business said that although the workers have another option of going back Myanmar and doing MOU again, it is not preferable for the business since the duration of the process is uncertain. At the same time, the workers are wondering how they will be able to apply for pink cards since the application period has already ended and why it will cost so much. They need more clarification on why they need to go through the pink card application process and the cost.

TPs:
-How many workers will need to extend their MOU contracts in 2023?
-What is the company's plan to extend their contracts?
-Does the company have an Employer Pays Policy?
-Is HR aware that some of its customers expect MMP to implement the EPP and ensure that workers don't pay for any recruitment fees?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Make arrangements so that the costs for renewing the work permit, visa, and employment contracts are covered by the businesses, and workers do not pay for any of these fees
-Communicate clearly to all workers that need to extend their contracts, work permits, and visas, verbally and in writing, how the company will process the proper legal documents for them.  Be clear in the communication about when this will be processed and what costs will be covered by the company and what costs covered by the workers

description: Fees charged by employer: legal but not ethical
Fees charged by employer: legal but not ethical
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A recently recruited worker with RS Cannery reported that when he was looking for a job, he was told that he only needed to pay 18,000 baht as the fees but when he arrived at the factory, the business charged 26,000 baht and they told the worker that there were additional documentation fees at the destination country. Worker also reported that the business told him that workers need to cover the recruitment fee on their own, including the accommodation fees of around 3,000 baht per month. He further reported that the business coaches the workers that whenever visitors ask they need to be told that the business covers all related recruitment fees and also supports them on the accommodation fee.

*** Please also refer to related  KPI#2412 pertaining to Toilet Breaks, Holiday Pay issues and KPI# 2399 pertaining to Holiday payment issues reported by this worker ***

BHR Recommendations and Talking Points
1. Liaise with O&E and find out more information about how and on what date the worker paid the 26,000 Bahts fees. Who did he pay the fees to and if he has any evidence of this payment. 
2. Arrange a remediation call and discuss the issue reported by the worker about unethical recruitment fees charged by the business. 
3. Diplomatically try to convince the business to acknowledge and reimburse the fees to the worker.
3. Encourage the business to follow ethical code of conduct and request to review ER policies and MSAs.
5. Perform worker validation.
6. Close the issue.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara has escalated the issue with relevant Strategic Partners after multiple attempts to engage the supplier to discuss worker feedback alleging serious labor issues.  The supplier has been unresponsive. Following escalation with SPs, Issara will now be meeting with RS Cannery to discuss the open cases on 05-Sep-2024.

5-Sep-2024
Business Response #3279
The business has an EPP policy for covering all recruitment costs for the workers. They interviewed the workers when they arrived, none of them mentioning that they need to pay for their recruitment fee, but they are not sure whether the workers end up paying to the broker or not. description: Debt bondage
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client worked at a Korean BBQ restaurant located in KL Kepong Jalan Metro Perdana, which is one of fifteen branches of the restaurant chain. Out of the fifteen branches, this particular one was problematic. The restaurant has six Nepali and thirteen Burmese workers. The owner's son is abusive towards the Nepali workers, creating a hostile work environment. Issara is able to speak with two workers. They have been working for this employer for 10 months. They are all MoU workers. They are reporting as a group of 5 Nepali workers, but the client is quietly reporting. The client and the workers want to either be transferred to another branch under the same company or find employment in another company. The client has debts to pay and doesn't want to return to Nepal. The workers have a contract they made in Nepal, but the company made another contract which the client doesn't have and is unaware of its contents.
Following are the major issues reported by workers.

1) Document retention: Workers passports are held by the employer since they started their employment. The company also kept their passports and didn't provide them with worker ID cards (Jalan cards) or necessary documents. 

2) Restriction of Movement: The workers were not allowed to leave the premises, and this restriction also made it difficult for their friends to visit them.

3) Unfair suspension: Workers were frequently suspended for minor mistakes or even without any reason. During these suspensions, the company did not provide any food, and the workers were not allowed to go out and get their own. They were also denied access to basic amenities, like cooling fans, during these periods. One incident occurred when a friend of the client was suspended for simply asking a Burmese worker to clean a stain. The owner verbally abused him and kept him in detention (suspension) for 28 days. Throughout this time, the company did not provide any food or salary, leaving the workers in a dire situation. His friends attempted to provide food secretly, but they had to be cautious as the company would punish them if they were caught bringing in more substantial amounts of food or any food. 

Recently, the victim was suspended by the company for two months. During this period, he received no salary or food from the company. The suspension was a result of the employer demanding the victim to memorize the restaurant menu quickly.

If workers demand to change the employer, they are asked to work 4 months without pay and there are some workers who have accepted this situation as they could not bear the harsh working environment. 

4)Physical abuse: Physical assault includes being kicked, slapped on the face and belly, and having ears pulled. The employer even physically assaulted the client's genitals. Such harassment occurred almost daily and targeted everyone except.

5) Long working hours and incorrect payment: Workers have to work 14-15 hours a day. In return, they received a basic salary of 1500 RM and a 300 RM overtime allowance each month. 

6) Lack of Sick Leave: Even when the workers fell ill, they were forced to work, as the owner wouldn't allow them to stay in the hostel. 



Moreover, during salary payment time, the owner would abuse the workers and suspend them for minor mistakes. The owner often used the workers as a target for his frustrations, taking out his stress related to the business on them. Whenever the business is slow he will start abusing the worker for no reason.

#Case 1
Context: Switching working tasks from peeling shrimps to general cleaning. At Line: 2111, Building 2, There are 10 workers who were asked to help for general cleaning. The workers signed the consent and thought it is just a temporary task for a few days. The consent was written in Thai, just the name was in Burmese. After signed HR told them that this is for 3 months. However, the workers have discussed this case with the HR staff many times. HR replied they will arrange to change the workers but there is no job for them in the production line. 

-Remedying issues for those who do not consent to change their jobs.  Workers who were forced/coerced to change jobs and who do not want to continue doing so should be moved back to the original working line. 
-Workers should not be forced or coerced to sign any documents that they do not understand. All documents should be provided in the worker native language. 

Timeframe: immediately 

Case 2: Forced to change the work location and type of work stipulated in the employment contract. Workers report being moved to shifts on nearby shrimp farms. Workers described the selection criteria of workers being sent to the farm as involuntary. However, according to other workers SEAFRESH is not sending workers to the shrimp farm anymore)

Workers reported that this practice has stopped. However, the business should recognize that these practices are against the MOU contract and that workers should not be forced or coerced under any circumstances to do a job different from what they were hired to do.

Workers report: Workers report being moved to nearby shrimp farms. Workers described the selection criteria of workers being sent to the farm was involuntary.

description: Workers placed in workplace and jobs different from what they were recruited for
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers being moved to a new building (Building No.10) without proper communication, consultation and the consent. Workers added that the line supervisors pick the workers they want to send to but do not ask whether workers are willing to be moved or not. Workers want the line supervisor to practice the voluntary moving process because there are some workers who want to be moved but not being moved while some not wanting to move but being moved. Reported by the workers from building 7 and 9 by Cambodian and Burmese workers. 

Recommendations 
-The HR shall work with the production and revise the plan for assigning workers to Building 10, that workers being asked to move will be consulted in advance and moved only with their consent
-The business action shall be taken immediately  to prevent the involuntary relocation that workers are currently reporting. 
-The business should be transparent about its workforce needs in the new building and explain to workers the criteria being used to select workers for the move, and that the move for those being asked to move will be voluntary. 

Talking Points
-What product is being produced in building 10? 
-What is the process of selecting workers to move to the new building? Is this relocation temporary or permanent? Does this move involve performing different tasks than previously performed and is this reflected in the workers’ contracts, with a new contract or amended contract? 
- Are you aware that some workers that want to move to Building 10 are not being asked to do so and others that don’t want to move are being moved without their consent?
-How many workers have already been moved and how many more are you planning to move? 
-How does the business manage the workload to make sure that workers remaining in Buildings 7 and 9 are not overworked due to workers being moved from those buildings to Building 10?

Time Frame _ 1 week.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issra raised this issue with the business, the business agreed to conduct a communication and follow the voluntary process. Issara is checking with the workers.

The issue with the relocation of 70 workers to TU. 



-There should not be any coercion to sign the relocation agreement paper. Asking worker's consent should be involved at least one recruitment focal from HR. If workers consent to move, a new Employment Contract must be issued, which requires approval by both the Thai and Myanmar Governments. The Myanmar recruitment agency and Myanmar Government Labour Attache should be informed by being provided with a list of workers moving to another factory.

**Talking points**

-Is the company planning to relocate workers? If yes, how many workers and what is the process of informing workers about this option and finding volunteers to move? 
-How and who will explain the voluntary nature of the consent form signing process? Workers reported that the supervisors already selected workers to be sent to a different company, but they haven't been asked to sign any documents and workers were also not given information about the voluntary nature of being relocated. Thus, ask the business what is the process to explain workers their options, who is involved in the communication of this plan and the relocation of workers? Explain to the business the importance of making sure the relocation of workers should be completely voluntary and that the appropriate procedures should be followed for those workers that accept being relocated.
remediation_business_steps_remaining: The Business did not take any action that was recommended by Issara.
remediation_notes: A total of 70 workers at Okeanos were reportedly compelled to move to work at another facility owned by Thai Union.  Workers reported that they were not given a choice in the matter.
remediation_action: Okeanos stated that they investigated the issue and that workers were told that moving to the other facility is voluntary.
remediation_validation: Okeano's report conflicts with worker views. Workers stated that the communication did not take place. Workers believe that the process was not voluntary, that their names were simply being picked by their supervisors, and that the group of 70 workers were only briefed on the move and the nature of the work at the other facility.
remediation_results: Okeanos and Thai Union were not willing to take further action, re-investigate, or allow workers to return to Okeanos.  Issara therefore considers the case closed unsatisfactorily. Worker reports signal risk of forced relocation among Thai Union facilities.

-The business is suggested to explain to the workers about the 75% of wages for those days where there isn't any work for the workers, for those who do not consent to move and will stay at Okeanos.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Mr. Tun Tun Win: Worker ID #91190603131.  The client joined HIT91 as an MOU worker in 2019 but was being assigned to the Hi-Tech warehouse in Suksawat Soi 64. This location was known as HIT64 and there are about 7-8 workers there. In HIT64, the business stocks rolls of different garments and the workers in that site have to work with stock-in/out and deliver the garments to-from HIT91 and HIT70. The workers have to carry the heavy garment rolls. After working there for two years, he is suffering from a stomach problem and so he cannot manage to work there anymore. He has to be hospitalized for a week and then after he is  discharged from the hospital, the doctor recommends that the job is not suitable for him anymore. So on 16 Apr 2022, he asked to move and work at HIT91 as a sewing worker.

But now, he is in a probation period and the production manager, P'Man, told him that his performance is not satisfactory as a sewing worker. They had him try and work in the ironing section too but because he injured his foot in an accident while he was working in HIT64 and he cannot manage to stand for very long. If a worker with 3 years sewing experience can sew 40 pieces per hour, he can manage to sew like 30 pieces.  And he has been asked to sew many different patterns and designs, with each taking time to get better at.  He would like the business to give him more chances to try as a sewing worker or if they are not happy with his performance, to consider having him work in the cutting or printing lines because he cannot manage to carry heavy loads in HIT64 and he cannot stand for long to do ironing work.

Talking points:
-Is the business aware that this worker was hired as an MOU worker at HIT91 but was assigned to work in another HIT facility for two years?
Recommendations:
-Workers should be provided with comprehensive job information before signing the employment contract, and the business should assign the worker to the location and provide the working conditions as promised originally

remediation_issara_recommendation:
14 workers were recruited by Pyae Paing Hmue RA to work in TMCL Energy Service Company and sent to Thailand on 1 Dec 2023 but placed in other workplaces. - The RA to coordinate with the employer so that the workers can be employed at the workplace as per their contract immediately.

Recruitment background.
 
10 workers 5 Male and 5 Female were recruited in Mid November 2022. 4) Not getting Malaysian Public holidays.

6) Not knowing when they will receive their wages. They started working on 18th Nov but have not received their wages yet and are not sure when they will receive it.

#Case 2
Context: The issue with 59 workers who were relocated to a Bread factory in Chonburi from Seafresh not receiving correct daily wages and being asked to work with the peace rate. No contract is being provided to these workers.


Issara recommendations.

#Issue 1

#Issue 2
Talking Points for Seafresh and TMCL. 

Please ask the businesses the following questions. 

-How was the relocation process handled for this group of workers? Who was in charge of it from Seafresh HR?  Who is the Myanmar recruitment agency and How was the Myanmar recruitment agency communicated about this relocation? 
-How many batches and the number of workers have been moved to different facilities from Seafresh so far? 
-Does Seafresh have more plans to relocate more workers? If yes, where and how?
-Is the TMCL aware of the worker's current situation? If yes, what has TMCL done so far for this issue? 
-Is the TMCL aware that the workers have not received their contract in their hand and the WP still in the process?
-What is the visibility of the Seafresh on the working conditions of this bread factory and the others? If the business is aware of this issue, how is the business going to help these workers? Any support that Seafresh is planning to provide to these workers? 

**Internal note for BHR**
_ Regarding worker's contracts and the work permit, how is the business helping to make sure these workers have their all documents in their hands? 
_ How many workers and what was the duration of their work in Seafresh and also type of documents. Such as,  how many MoU and how many CI workers?
remediation_business_steps_taken:
#Case 1
Business response
The company always communicates to TMCL when the workers moved from the company, and TMCL takes the responsibility to inform RGI as agreed on the contract. And the company needs to inform the government within 15 days to comply with the laws."

Workers update, 
This issue is considered to be closed since Issara can not contact the worker anymore. 

#Case 2

The company always communicates to TMCL when the workers moved from the company, and TMCL takes the other responsibilities as agreed on the contract.

Workers update;
The recruitment agency communicated to the workers that they will issue a job changeable cancellation letter if the workers want to find a new job. Since then, Issara could not contact the workers.
remediation_notes:
Arrangements were made for workers, on-site, to work for a new employer - a bread factory. Workers
report illegally low wages at this new employer and not receiving a proper contract. Several meetings on this issue. The business claimed that the recruitment agency announced this job opportunity and the workers made the decision to move to the new employer. The business stated that it is the  responsibility of the recruitment agency to help these workers. The role and involvement by the supplier HR in vetting or allowing the recruitment agency to recruit current workers was a key point
of concern. The former workers recently updated that they are in the process of moving to another
employer which is believed to have better working conditions. The supplier stated that they will discontinue the practice of allowing recruitment agencies to enter the facility to recruit workers for jobs elsewhere. Result: Policy Change
systems_change_issara_recommendation: -Recommendations for the system change will be provided after talking with the business and understanding their process and their involvement.

remediation_notes: Arrangements were made for Seafresh workers, on-site, to work for a new employer - a bread factory. Workers, however, reported illegally low wages at this new employer and not receiving a proper contract. While Seafresh is not responsible for the actions of another employer, Issara's view is that when Seafresh supports the arrangement of its MOU workers to move to another business and allows the recruitment agency to solicit worker on its own premises, it bears some  responsibility and should have conducted reasonable due diligence that the job being offered by the other business to its current employees was legitimate.
remediation_action: Several meetings regarding this issue. The business claimed that the recruitment agency announced this job opportunity and the workers made the decision to move to the new employer. The business also stated that it is the responsibility of the recruitment agency to help these workers. The role and involvement by HR in vetting the supplier or allowing the recruitment agency to recruit current workers was not viewed by Seafresh as their responsibility.
remediation_validation: The former workers recently updated that they are in the process of moving to another employer which is believed to have better working conditions.
remediation_results: Policy change. Seafresh stated that they will discontinue the practice of allowing recruitment agencies to enter the facility to recruit workers for jobs elsewhere. Accountability and responsibility on this issue, however, was not agreed upon. The issue did prompt Seafresh to have clearer discussions with their recruitment agency regarding the terms and conditions of their contracts and roles and responsibilities of each party. The recruitment agency communicated to the workers that they will issue a job changeable cancellation letter if the workers who moved want to find a new job. Since then, Issara has not able contact the impacted workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: -Recommendations for the system change will be provided after talking with the business and understanding their process and their involvement.

closed_notes: This is rated as "Poor" because for both issues, the business responded that they have communicated with the recruitment agency and workers before the relocation. Given that, the business did not collaborate with the recruitment agency to help the workers. The recruitment agency announced to the workers that they will issue a job cancellation letter if any workers wanted to find a new employer. remediation_issara_recommendation:
#Case 1
Lack of professional conduct of recruitment agency and/or employer
Changed Employer (Top Glove)

#Case 2
Context: The issue with 59 workers who were relocated to a Bread factory in Chonburi from Seafresh not receiving correct daily wages and being asked to work with the peace rate. No contract is being provided to these workers.


Issara recommendations.

#Issue 1

#Issue 2
Talking Points for Seafresh and TMCL. 

Please ask the businesses the following questions. 

-How was the relocation process handled for this group of workers? Who was in charge of it from Seafresh HR?  Who is the Myanmar recruitment agency and How was the Myanmar recruitment agency communicated about this relocation? 
-How many batches and the number of workers have been moved to different facilities from Seafresh so far? 
-Does Seafresh have more plans to relocate more workers? If yes, where and how?
-Is the TMCL aware of the worker's current situation? If yes, what has TMCL done so far for this issue? 
-Is the TMCL aware that the workers have not received their contract in their hand and the WP still in the process?
-What is the visibility of the Seafresh on the working conditions of this bread factory and the others? If the business is aware of this issue, how is the business going to help these workers? Any support that Seafresh is planning to provide to these workers? 

**Internal note for BHR**
_ Regarding worker's contracts and the work permit, how is the business helping to make sure these workers have their all documents in their hands? 
_ How many workers and what was the duration of their work in Seafresh and also type of documents. Such as,  how many MoU and how many CI workers?
remediation_business_steps_taken:
#Case 1
Business response
The company always communicates to TMCL when the workers moved from the company, and TMCL takes the responsibility to inform RGI as agreed on the contract. And the company needs to inform the government within 15 days to comply with the laws."

Workers update, 
This issue is considered to be closed since Issara can not contact the worker anymore. 

#Case 2

The company always communicates to TMCL when the workers moved from the company, and TMCL takes the other responsibilities as agreed on the contract.

Workers update;
The recruitment agency communicated to the workers that they will issue a job changeable cancellation letter if the workers want to find a new job. Since then, Issara could not contact the workers.
remediation_notes: Arrangements were made for Seafresh workers, on-site, to work for a new employer - a bread factory. Workers, however, reported illegally low wages at this new employer and not receiving a proper contract. While Seafresh is not responsible for the actions of another employer, Issara's view is that when Seafresh supports the arrangement of its MOU workers to move to another business and allows the recruitment agency to solicit worker on its own premises, it bears some  responsibility and should have conducted reasonable due diligence that the job being offered by the other business to its current employees was legitimate.
remediation_action: Several meetings regarding this issue. The business claimed that the recruitment agency announced this job opportunity and the workers made the decision to move to the new employer. The business also stated that it is the responsibility of the recruitment agency to help these workers. The role and involvement by HR in vetting the supplier or allowing the recruitment agency to recruit current workers was not viewed by Seafresh as their responsibility.
remediation_validation: The former workers recently updated that they are in the process of moving to another employer which is believed to have better working conditions.
remediation_results: Policy change. Seafresh stated that they will discontinue the practice of allowing recruitment agencies to enter the facility to recruit workers for jobs elsewhere. Accountability and responsibility on this issue, however, was not agreed upon. The issue did prompt Seafresh to have clearer discussions with their recruitment agency regarding the terms and conditions of their contracts and roles and responsibilities of each party. The recruitment agency communicated to the workers that they will issue a job changeable cancellation letter if the workers who moved want to find a new job. Since then, Issara has not able contact the impacted workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: -Recommendations for the system change will be provided after talking with the business and understanding their process and their involvement.

description: Inaccurate / misleading / poor information about job: deceptive mis-information
remediation_issara_recommendation: Context: The issue with a fake job announcement that was made by a Facebook user. The Facebook post says that Cal-Comp is recruiting MoU workers from Myanmar which is not aligned with the current policy. Thailand has not been recruiting workers at the moment. The announcement also mentioned the requirements from the job seekers in order to apply for the job and also provide the contact information of the focal person if job seekers have any questions.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they do not work with the recruiter (Facebook Post host) whose name is "Blue Sky". However, the business responded that they have been working on the system improvement and action plans, and will have communication with all of the recruitment agencies that they work with to prevent this happening in the future. The business confirmed having done the communication with all of the recruitment agencies that they work with. It is added that the suggested communication was for the recruitment agencies to make a wide announcement about the suspended recruitment process for MoU workers from Myanmar to Thailand.  In addition to that, the post about the job announcement has been deleted and the facebook user has changed his/her user name.
remediation_notes: A fake job advertisement had been posted on Facebook saying that Cal-Comp was hiring workers from Myanmar through the MOU process.  The person that posted the ad posed as a recruitment agency, providing contact information so job seekers could call in with queries.
remediation_action: Issara raised this issue with the business, and the business confirmed that they are not working with the Facebook user going by the name of "Blue Sky". The business is working to prevent such false advertising in the future.
remediation_validation: The fake job post has since been deleted and the facebook user has changed his user name.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: -The business to communicate with all of the recruitment agencies to prevent such fake job announcements in the future.

remediation_issara_recommendation: Workers in the "MOU 19 Group" noted that the business told them in the 3rd week of April 2023 that they had to stay in Myanmar at most 7-8 months and then they will be called back as MOU U-Turn workers. They stayed in touch with the company interpreter via a Facebook group and FB messenger. The business also took copies of their Household Registrations and National IDs to arrange for the U-Turn process. On 17th Nov 2023, the business sent a message via FB messenger group that if they would like to come back to SF-2513, they must go to Arbourfield agency by 20 Nov 2023 and submit their passports to arrange U-Turn and the business also said that the workers don't need to pay any money to agency as the business had already paid to agency. Believing this information from the business, the 13 workers from MOU 19 group went to Yangon and arrived at Yangon on 20th Nov. But the agency told them that their names are not in the U-Turn list of SF-2513. They spent 50,000-80,000 MMK each to go to Yangon (she traveled there from Ayeyarwaddy) but they have lost their money, time and effort. They would like to request the business to consider hiring them back as originally promised.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 20 Nov 2023

K Sophon and K Supreeya, HR stated that the MoU Group 19 was the end of the MoU contract. They insist that they did not promise the workers that they would do the MoU U-Turn process, but they did tell the workers that if they wanted to apply for a job at Siam Food 2513 again, they could submit their passport and application to the recruitment agency in advance, and when the company has job vacancies or decides to recruit MoU, they would be prioritized because they are former workers with experience. However, the company has yet to make a decision. The MoU workers will most likely be recruited in April 2024. So, as previously stated, they will communicate clearly with the workers again by next week.

DATE: 23 Nov 2023

According to K. Sophon, HR Director, there is currently no final decision to submit the demand name list to for the MoU U-Turn for this group. They are holding internal discussions to determine when the workers will be hired back. They used to collaborate with Golden Gate (Thai RA), who in turn collaborated with Abourfield (Myanmar RA). They are, however, evaluating Golden Gate and Abourfied and looking for other recruitment agencies as options. They will most likely work directly with the source side recruitment agency. They will use the heatmap that Issara shared for their consideration as well.  In terms of the miscommunication caused by the interpreter, they will investigate and communicate clearly to the workers when they will hire the worker back and by which recruitment agency.


DATE: 1 Dec 2023

Issara shared a screenshot of the Line group in which the interpreter communicated with the workers about applying for new passports for the MoU U-Turn. K. Sophon, HR Director, responded that he needs to have an additional investigation with the HR team and the interpreter. If this is the case, he will consult with management. 1. The rationale for moving forward with this MoU U-Turn group 2. Reimburse workers for the passport fee and costs. So we agreed to meet again on December 7 to discuss the corrective action plan.

DATE: 7 Dec 2023

The meeting was attended by K. Sophon, HR Director, K. Supreeya, HR Manager, and an interpreter. They insisted that the company had not yet decided to submit the demand with the name list to initiate the MoU U-Turn process. However, the interpreter only communicated with the workers so they to prepare the documents, which the workers misinterpreted. However, they would like to work with Issara to find a solution. By preparing a budget to present to their management for reimbursement to workers who will return to the company. They would like Issara's assistance in clarifying the passport fee standard through a recruitment agency rather than a broker.  They also stated that they are considering hiring a new recruitment agency and will use our ER toolkit- RA vetting and selection tool to do so. They will most likely submit this list of workers' names in January 2024, and the workers will be able to return by April 2024, but they must wait for the final decision from their management with the budget proposal with the recruitment agency. So we decided on the following steps.
1. Issara can assist SF2513 in determining the legal passport fee (apply through a recruitment agency rather than a broker).
2. Issara assists in communicating with the workers that they currently have the option of applying to another factory; if the workers still want to return to work at Siam Food Factory, they must wait for the company's decision, and the workers will be on the top list for name list and will be reimbursed.
3. After receiving the passport fee information from Issara, they will prepare a budget to present to their management for the MoU U-Turn process with reimbursement.
4. The company will notify Issara in January 2024 with an update on the MoU U-Turn process and confirmation.

DATE: 13 Dec 2023
K. Sophon, HR Director clarified that The company is considering when to bring in these two Myanmar workers. In this case, the company will use the average fee of 3,000 Baht and explain it to the workers so that they understand. Furthermore, the company will reimburse the travel expenses according to company policy.
remediation_notes: A worker in a group of 34 workers had been sent back to Myanmar on 27 May 2023 for the MOU U-turn process and was informed on 17 Nov 2023 that they should travel to Yangon and contact the recruitment agency by 20 Nov 2023 to get ready to return to Thailand.  However, when 13 workers arrived, the recruitment agency informed them that they were not on the MOU U-turn worker list.
remediation_action:
The business responded that for this group, their MOU contracts had ended and they did not promise the workers that they would be hired back as MOU U-turn workers. They only told them that they could re-apply and if the company had job vacancies, they would be prioritized for hiring. However, the company has yet to make a decision on hiring more workers and any MOU workers will most likely be recruited only in April 2024 after submitting the name list in January 2024.

HR clarified that the company will consider re-hiring these workers, and reimburse 3,000 Baht for the passport fee and will also cover the travel expenses according to company policy.
remediation_validation:
Workers updated that they have since heard that the business is considering the MOU U-turn process for them and are looking to select a Myanmar recruitment agency to handle this process.

These workers are very disappointed because they paid high passport costs through a broker to expedite the process (there are currently huge delays in processing passports) in anticipation of returning to work with the company. 

Issara provided an update to workers about the company's position in terms of when they may be re-hired and what costs would be reimbursed by the employer, such as the 3,000 Baht for the passport fee and travel expenses. Two workers are going to wait to return to work here while the others are not willing to wait so long.
next_description:
- O&E communicates and validates with the workers.
- get update in Jan 2024 about the inclusion of these workers in the name list and also the reimbursement of expenses to workers

description: Inaccurate / misleading / poor information about job: deceptive mis-information
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Including this client 210 other Bangladeshi workers were brought to Malaysia with calling visa promising a job here. it has been 4 months since then and they are not provided with any work. moreover, following are the issues that the client shared: 

- they are kept somewhere in JB and are not allowed to go out of the confinement.
- there was a Bangladeshi (contact given in issue link) broker through whom they came who is believed to be retaining their passport. when they kept asking for the passport, allegedly he said, "if you guys continue to ask for your passport, we will burn them" and now he is not reachable anymore.   
- they are not given food regularly, don't have access to fresh water to drink, and the electricity is irregular. 
- they are not allowed to go the embassy. 
- there is a Tamil, Malaysian who is kept to look after them, who allegedly physically abuse them. 
- the client and the workers have reasons to believe the normal police are taking bribe to overlook this issue. so they have no where to go. 
- they are kept and forced to stay there against their will. 
- both from the origin and the destination side they have not received any support.
- the client even requested if Issara can, they should send the immigration police. 

the client was requested to share contacts of other victims to connect and get more details by Issara staff.

this call made to get consent from the client to share the issue details with other organization or give his contact to other organization to handle their case. 

The client gave consent to share the issue details BUT DOES NOT WANT HIS PRESONAL INFORMATION AND/OR NAME TO BE SHARED OR HIGHLIGHTED ***

He wants to keep his name PRIVATE, as we does not want to risk anything happening to him.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
this call was made to update the client about sharing his contact information with Our Journey to handle his case. following are the points discussed in this call:

description: Inaccurate / misleading / poor information about job: deceptive mis-information
remediation_issara_recommendation: 60 MOU workers were recruited by Myanmar Agency Diamond Stair and arrived in Thailand in the second week of Jan 2024. The workers paid 5 million kyats. The agency promised to get them proper cancellation letters from a nominal employer and place them in a perfume factory or purified water factory within a week of their arrival. For getting the cancellation letter and finding them new jobs, the agency charged another 500,000 kyats to workers. However, it's been like more than a week and they haven't got any jobs yet. During this time, they are staying in a big worker housing near Bang Bo market, Bangkok, and the owner is charging them 120 Baht each daily for food and accommodation. In the present situation, the workers have no money in hand and need jobs as fast as possible. So they contact Kyaw Naing (Thai based Myanmar agency staff) and Myanmar agency but they didn't get a proper response. So they asked Issara for help. Issara suggested calling MOEAF and provided an MOEAF contact number.
remediation_notes: A group of MOU workers were recruited by a Myanmar recruitment agency and arrived in Thailand in the second week of Jan 2024, for which the workers paid 5 million kyats each. The agency promised to get them proper cancellation letters from a nominal employer and place them in a perfume factory or purified water factory within a week of their arrival. For getting the cancellation letter and finding them new jobs, the agency charged another 500,000 kyats to workers. However, it's been like more than a week and they haven't got any jobs yet. During this time, they are staying in a big worker housing area and the owner is charging them 120 Baht each daily for food and accommodation.
remediation_action: Issara suggested calling MOEA and provided them with the contact number.
remediation_validation: Workers updated Issara that on 16 Jan 2024, the recruitment agency director came to the worker housing. By that time, some had already found new jobs on their own. So the director asked the remaining workers if they would like to get 5,000 Baht back (equivalent to 500,000 kyats which they had paid for the cancellation letter and new jobs) or if they would like to wait for new jobs that the agency would find for them. 15 workers took the refund to find new jobs on their own; they have now found jobs in a mattress factory in Samut Sakhon, and 20 workers got jobs in a chicken factory in Chonburi with the help of the recruitment agency. Only 6 workers are still waiting for jobs.

original document?

Recommendations
-Since this document is the document of the worker's health matter, this document should be in the worker's hands, as it is a personal document. remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with fifty workers who were involuntarily relocated to TUF from Okeanos wanting to resign from TUF as they are not happy with their new working condition. They added that they wanted to make sure that they received job changeable cancellation letter to find the new job somewhere else. 

Issara recommendations:

-It is strongly recommended for the business to provide departing workers cancellation letters that state the reason for departure as the business cannot provide sufficient work for them, which will allow the workers than to find new employers. 

-it is recommended for the business to make sure all these fifty workers who were involuntarily relocated have the options whether they want to continue working with TUF, return to Okeanos or want to find another job.
remediation_notes:
Talking Points:

-Please ask the business how many workers from this group have already left and what was the remark that was given in their job cancellation letter if there are some workers that have already left. 
-Please suggest the business to make the correction if some workers have already received improper job cancellation letter. 
-Please share with the business that this is the responsibility of the Okeanos and TUF to make sure these fifty workers have proper job cancellation letter to continue work in Thailand. (If needed).
-Please share with the business that several workers who left TUF are ending up becoming undocumented and working with improper documentation such as invalid and incorrect work permit. This situation is happening because workers are having difficulties to find an employer that accepts the cancellation letter provided by TUF, so workers have to find an employer that do not follow the right procedures to hire workers.  
-Explain the process that the employer can follow to amend the cancellation letter remark, to help workers be able to apply for another job. 
-Explain to the employer the other way they can help workers. By signing the 'Certificate of Responsibility for expenses from hiring foreign workers of former employers’. Share with the business for the supporting documents that can help the workers to apply for a new employer. 


Conditions for changing employers for MOU workers.

1. The employer terminated / the employer died.
*2. The employer goes bankrupt. Or reduce production capacity because there is no work for the workers
3. The employer or the employer representative or the supervisor has abused or attacked the employee
4. The employer does not comply with the employment contract.
5. Employees work in working conditions or working environments that may cause damage to employees’ life, body, mind or health.
*This is the preferred reason to be given, that the business has no work for the workers
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business to make sure that the workes who are being relocated have full consent and voluntary. TUF is also recommended to have their own voluntary consent form and pre-departure communication to explain the working condition and also to seek the voluntariness. 

-The business to clearly communicate with the workers about the process of receiving job cancellation letter including the time frame.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers who resigned from a ladybird to find another job due to lower-income (No OT), the heavy workload during regular working hours, and newly restricted rules received a cancellation letter with a remark of resignation which makes it difficult for workers to apply to another job. ID - 11601.

-It is ethically recommended for the business to provide to departing workers cancellation letters that state the reason for departure as the business cannot provide sufficient work for them, which will allow the workers to find new employment. This is what is ethically recommended given that migrant workers have paid for high recruitment fees and have debts that they have to pay back and the current income is not enough for them to cover their expenses. 
-It is recommended that for those workers that have already left, that the reason for departure on their cancellation letters are changed to the business cannot provide sufficient work for them or coordinate with the new employer that the worker has found to provide supporting documents to allow the worker to legally work for the new employer.

Added talking points for CD to have an escalation call with the business's director level. (2 Nov 2020) 


a.       We’ve received urgent calls over the weekend from former Ladybird workers reporting a series of serious issues (describe these 3 issues) and are saying that these are the reasons why they have resigned or want to resign.  There are 2 recently resigned workers in particular who have left for these reasons, and we get the sense that there are many more who may resign.  These seem to be legitimate issues; is Ladybird aware of these, and if so are you working to address them?

b.       If Ladybird is still getting orders from customers, which they obviously are, then why in the past 7 months have they been overworking workers and not paying OT?  Why not let them work at the same pace and pay them OT as before?

c.       The cancellation letters being issued that say “resigned, return to Myanmar” are unethical and coercive – we understand that you need to retain your workforce due to current border lockdowns, but it is not responsible to be writing cancellation letters that you know will make it impossible for the worker to find another job. 
d.       At this point, these workers have the right to leave with such grievances that are not really being responded to properly, so the ethical thing to do is (a) write these 2 former workers a proper JCL and reissue it today, since their deadline is in 3 days, and it should be as per our recommended language (be prepared to lay this out to them exactly) and doesn’t ruin their chances of getting a new job given the obvious COVID situation, and (b) prepare and issue their recruitment repayments.

e.       It sounds like workers are still being forced to show an MC to be paid sick leave; is this correct?  If so, workers should immediately be paid back for whenever they have taken 1-2 days of sick leave but not been able to produce an MC.  HR records should be able to show this – are Ladybird’s HR records able to identify the workers who took sick leave but were not paid for those days as per the law, and then issue them a reimbursement as required by law?  Within how many pay periods?  If Ladybird HR records cannot do this, do they need our help with an investigation/worker survey?

-Please share with the business that some workers received the proper letters but these workers did not. It is very challenging for the workers to survive with only daily wages because they have to support their family since Myanmar is in a lockdown due to COVID-19 worst situation. Not having proper job changeable letters can lead the workers to become undocumented and working with improper documentation such as invalid and incorrect work permits. This situation is happening because workers are having difficulties finding an employer that accepts the cancellation letter provided by Ladybird, so workers have to find an employer that does not follow the right procedures to hire workers.

remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issue #1. 11-June-2021.Business response ID - 1255.

The business - The business responded that the workers are not happy to participate in skill training which is required by the buyers. The business said that they will conduct the investigation, however, gave an uncertain response about the recommended survey to access the collective response from the workers.

Issue #2. 11-June-2021.Business response ID - 1255.

The business responded that the worker was communicated before he resigned however, the worker committed to resigning. The business responded that it is not possible for them to re-hire this worker and the remark that he received in the job cancellation letter has mentioned that the worker is debt-free which means that the worker supposed to be able to find a job. Issara checked with the worker and updated them that he has not been able to find a job with the provided letter. Apart from that, the worker's job cancellation letter has expired so that he has no opportunity to apply for a job. Since this is our of Issara control, Issara decided to close this case.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations; 
-To have open discussion sessions between  HR and workers to understand better what are the challenges being faced by workers and what is driving them to resign. During these discussions, the business is encouraged to share with workers what the business actions are to address these issues.
-The business could also conduct an internal survey to learn why workers want to resign and what can help them remain in Ladybird. Issara can help with the survey questionnaire. Surveys should be conducted in a confidential way where workers feel safe to share the issues that they are facing. 
-The business shall work on a plan to address the issues that are raised in the survey by the workers. 
-The business shall provide training to all supervisors including translators.
-The business shall revise the grievance channels that are meant for workers to raise their issues. The revision should focus on workers' confidentiality and the no retaliation policy. Workers have expressed their concern about raising issues with HR, out of fear of retaliation from their supervisors, therefore it is strongly recommended for the business to reinforce a no retaliation policy and make sure all supervisors are aware of the policy, follow it and face consequences if they commit any actions against such policy.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The issue with a worker who received a home returning letter for resigning from job.

Recommendations; 
-The language used in SEAPAC worker cancellation letters, “resigned, return to Myanmar” is making it essentially impossible for workers who are leaving SEAPAC(for reasons noted below) to be hired by new employers, also making workers more vulnerable during this covid-period. 
-It is ethically recommended for the business to provide departing workers cancellation letters that state the reason for departure which will allow the workers to find new employers.
- The issuing of the cancellation letter should be done within the period of time that workers have to find a new employer.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The business clarified that before the worker left the company, HR had an interpreter explaining to the worker the consequences as follows.
1. The company would like to retain the worker to work at the company and tried to help the worker to change the production line but the worker didn't want to.
2. The company informed the worker if the worker would like to resign the cancellation letter need to be noted that 'resign' and the worker could not change to the new employer according to the MoU practice and Thai law.
3. The company already informed DOE of the worker's resignation. The DOE could not change the reason - mentioned by HR. However, HR was open for the worker to re-ire if the worker has difficulties finding a new employer. The business also added that the worker would be assigned to work for the production wherever she feels more compfortable. 
Issara contacted the worker and updated the business response, however, the worker refused to be back and continue finding a new employer in her own way.

Issara raised this issue with Nike, Nike responded that they have checked with Hong Seng and found as following - The problem is that the DOE said it didn't have the client's information in the system, even though HS had processed her work permit. description: Proper legal documents not provided to worker
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with some workers whose visas have expired as it was not extended by the business even though workers provided to HR staff their passports and visa fees extension on time. Workers added that only their work permits have been extended so that some of them have been working without a valid visa since June, 2021. 


Talking Points

-Workers reported to Issara that their visas are not being extended on time and now the workers are working with invalid visas. What is the business understanding on this issue? 
-How many workers are there in this situation?
-What is the process for this group of workers? 
- What is the company’s plan to prevent workers from having issues with the local police for not having valid visas? And what kind of support would they provide in case it actually happened? 

Recommendations

-The business shall have a communication session with the workers and explain in detail how the process is being handled, by whom, timeframes and an explanation of why their documents have not been extended, and how would the company respond in case there are any penalties imposed by the immigration office. 
-The communication should also include information on how the company would protect workers from having any issues with the local police for not having valid documents.
-In ethical recruitment practices, it is the employer's responsibility to make sure all workers' documents are up to date and workers receive clear information about the process.

วันนี้มีมติ ตาม.สำคัญเรื่องการบริหารจัดการแรงงานข้ามชาติ โดยสรุปดังนี้
1. กลุ่ม 4 สิงหาที่ยื่นบต.48 แล้วให้อยู่ได้ถึง 31 มีนา64 และให้ยื่นขออนุญาตทำงานได้ต่อจนถึง 13 กพ.66
2. กลุ่ม20 สิงหา62 ที่จะหมดอายุ 30 กันยาให้ยื่นต่อใบออนุญาตก่อนหมดอายุ จะได้อนุญาตให้อยู่และทำงานได้ถึง 13 กพ. 66
สำหรับกลุ่มหมด 31 มีค.65 ให้ยื่นขออยู่และทำงานจนถึง 133. กพ 66
3. กลุ่ม mou ครบ 4 ปี ให้อยู่ตออีก 2 ปีนับจากวันที่ใบอนุญาตทำงานเดิมหมด
4. ให้คนที่ใบอนุญาตทำงานสิ้และสิทธิในกานทำงานสิ้นสุด ตั้งแต่ 1 มกรา - 13 กค 64 หรือก่อนวันที่ประกาศกระทรวงมหาดไทยและปรกาศกระทรวงแรงงานขะบังคับใช้ ให้ยื่นขออนุญาตทำงานกับกรมการจัดหางาน และให้ทำงานได้ถึง 13 กพ.66 โดยต้องส่งผลตรวจสุขภาพและวีซ่าภายใน 27 กค. 65 รวมถึงให้ยกเว้นเงื่อนไขการเปลี่ยนนายจ้าง และให้กลุ่มประมงเพิ่มนายจ้างได้รวมไม่เกิน 3 คน
5. ให้ขยายเวลาเปลี่ยนนายจ้างจาก 30 วันเป็น 60 วัน (ใช้จนถึง 13 กพ.66)
6. กรณีพาส ci td หมดอายุ ให้ทำให้เสร็จภายใน 27 ก.ค.65  
7. ทางพม่าจะจัดตั้งศูนย์ทำ CI 5 แห่ง สมุทรสาคร สมุทรปราการ ระนอง ชลบุรี และเชียงใหม่ โดยให้ตม. และจัดหางานไปดำเนินตีวีซ่าและออกใบอนุญาตทำงานในศูนย์เลย โดยให้ศูนย์เปิดถึง 27 กค. 65 ถ้าไม่เสร็จให้ประสานในช่องทางทางการทูต โดยให้ดำเนินการต่อไปก่อนได้

Context: A workers Mr. Zaw Htet Aung, ID:111160214, his 4-year MoU contract, visa, and work permit expired on 26 Feb 2022 and his documents have not been extended yet. Recently, the business assisted the worker for the passport extension; however, he had to pay 3,300 Baht for the transportation cost. The worker has not got a valid visa and work permit yet. 

Talking Points; 
What is the status of this worker? How many workers are in this situation? 

Recommendations
Given that the government has allowed this group of workers to extend their visas and work permits in Thailand, the business should expedite the process of visa and work permit extensions for all workers.
The worker has reported having to pay 3,300 THB for the passport extension trip, what is the business policy for the workers passport extension?  (Internal Note; The COC  has not clearing mentioned about the passport extension or application fees). 
The worker’s documents should be extended and the worker should be re-assigned to work in his original working line as mentioned in the contract.

description: Proper legal documents not provided to worker
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the COVID-19 vaccination Certificate not being provided to the workers who have resigned from the business. Workers who have resigned from the business reported that they have not received the COVID-19 vaccination certificate from the business, therefore, they approached the business but were told by two of the translators named Ma Dar and Ma Ju Juu that the business won’t issue the certificate to those who leave the business. 

Recommendations: 
The business shall conduct an investigation immediately to find out why workers who resigned were not provided with their vaccine certificates, which is needed to show evidence of vaccination when traveling, etc. 
Workers have the right to be provided with the necessary personal identity documents such as vaccine certificates, and they should not be withheld from them.  Willfully withholding such documents is a legal violation 
To provide vaccine certificates to all workers that have resigned after receiving the vaccination, the business should communicate with the current workers to assist in getting in touch with those that have left without the certificate. Issara can assist in communicating with Hi-Tech workers in this regard. 

-Talking Points. 
- If the business arranged for its workers to be vaccinated, how did it arrange for the vaccinated workers to get their vaccine certificates?
- Why is it that only workers who resigned were not provided with their vaccine certificates?
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara raised this issue with the business and suggested for the investigation.The business replied to Issara by saying that they have checked with the social security office and learned that the new employer of the worker or the worker himself have to request the document because the previous employer is not belong to this worker anymore. Issara has updated the business response to the worker and suggested to check with the new employer or visit the Social Security Office by himself.
remediation_notes: A worker who was leaving the company asked for her vaccine certificate since she had been vaccinated at the factory.  However, the business did not provide the certificate to her.
remediation_action: The business investigated this matter, and checked with the social security office regarding the issuing of the vaccine certificates.  The social security office advised that since the worker had left and was now with a new employer, the worker or the new employer would have to request for the certificate.
remediation_validation: Issara updated the worker saying her former employer couldn't help her in getting the vaccine certificate and advised that she request the new employer to make the request or visit the social security office herself.
remediation_results: Now that the worker had a new employer, the former employer could no longer request the Social Security office to issue the vaccine certificate to the worker.

This case didn't happen. But if it happens, it's probably the case that migrant workers are a walk-in group, applying for a job and being hired as an employee. This group of employees will not be able to use social security rights immediately because they may not have rights in the case that they must have paid contributions for 3 months within 15 months, but the company has purchased health insurance for employees who have not received social security benefits for a period of 4 months. If these employees are sick, they must use health insurance instead.

Action:
In the case of an incident
1. In employee orientation will increase the knowledge of foreign employees who have not received social security rights that if there is an illness, health insurance must be exercised until the SS benefit active.
2. HR makes a copy of the health insurance policy for employees to keep in their passport in case of emergency.
3. If there is an illness, inform HR through an interpreter to help coordinate with the hospital to facilitate

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The issue with the workers 90 days report not being properly handled by the business. Workers from building 10 reported not receiving their updated 90 days confirmation receipt from the business even though they have provided their required documents to the business on time. The business made the announcement to issue the receipt on 27th December 2021, however, the business failed to do so. 

Recommendations: 

The business shall investigate and issue the 90 days report receipts to the workers. 
The business should communicate with all workers and explain why the process is taking longer and what are the options for the workers if they do not receive their receipt on time. 
Since a 90 days report is a legal document for migrant workers, workers need to have it in their hands for any kind of communication and transportation, that is why the business should make sure it is extended and distributed with the workers on time to avoid workers having to face issues with the officials. 
The business’s focal person who handles the 90 days report should be communicated and investigated to find the challenges that delay the process. 

Talking Points: 
Has the worker's 90 days report been updated? If yes, what are the challenges to issuing it to the workers?
