supplier_name: Nan Yang Garment Co., Ltd. (Nakhon Pathom)
description: Proper legal documents not provided to worker
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1:
Workers reported that 208 pink card workers were fired on January 31, 2023, with the business paying them severance pay. The business should have extended their visas and work permits by February 13, 2023, but they did not. Among 208 workers, over 20 workers were promised by an HR staff member, P' Dao, to extend their visas and work permits under his name as the employer. P' Dao became their new employer solely to extend documents but not provide a proper job. He promised that the workers could currently stay in Thailand and when they found a new employer, he would provide the WP application form as needed. He collected 4,000 Baht from each worker who needed to extend their work permit and 7,000 Baht from each worker who needed to extend both their visas and work permits. He told the workers not to tell the business about this because he just wanted to help them out. After almost a month, P' Dao still has not provided the workers with their WP application forms. Now, the workers have not been able to start working with the new employer and don't have enough money to pay for their room rent and daily expenses. 
 

Case #2:
A worker resigned on January 29, 2023, and the employer promised that the proper cancellation letter to change employers would be provided to him.  The worker has not yet received the cancellation letter, even though he followed up with the factory interpreter many times. It's been almost a month, and he is concerned that the cancellation letter will expire; he is waiting for it to work at another factory (TGM) in Nonthaburi.

The worker provided his consent to share his name and worker ID with the business.
Name: Nay Htet Lin 
Worker ID: 64090361



Recommendations:
- Workers should be provided with the needed documents so that they can secure jobs with new employers
- For the cancellation letter, the reason stated in the letter should be such that the worker can find a new employer with it.
- HR staff should not be charging fees to workers for visa and WP extensions and acting as an employer when in fact he is not employing those workers. Take disciplinary measures according to the company's disciplinary policy (NOTE: Case #1 to be discussed ONLY after risk assessment of potential harm to workers)
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Case #2
K. Thanatkorn, HR manager, checked with DOE and responded that DOE has an appointment with HR on March 10 to receive the cancellation letter, which has been delayed due to the DOE process. HR will notify the worker to receive the cancellation letter.
remediation_notes:
Case #1: Workers reported that 208 workers were fired on January 31, 2023, with no warning but with the business paying them severance pay. The business had communicated that their contracts would be extended but it was not. Among this group, over 20 workers paid money to an HR staff member to extend their visas and work permits with this HR person as their employer, on paper but not in reality. He promised that he would provide the work permit application form to them when they had found new employers. After almost a month, he still has not provided the workers with this document. Workers have found new employers and the new employers are saying this document is needed for them to start work. Now, the workers have not been able to start working with the new employer and don't have enough money to pay for their room rent and daily expenses. 

Case #2: A worker resigned on January 29, 2023, and the employer promised that the proper cancellation letter to change employers would be provided to him.  The worker has not yet received the cancellation letter, even though he followed up with the factory interpreter many times. It's been almost a month, and he is concerned that the cancellation letter will expire; he is waiting for it to work at another factory (TGM) in Nonthaburi.
remediation_action:
Case #1: Issara has not raised with the business this particular issue of its HR staff acting independently to process the visas and work permits for the 20 workers due to concerns that if the business were to take disciplinary action against its HR staff, then the workers may not receive the documents they are asking from him. 

Case #2: The HR manager checked with the Department of Employment (DOE) and received an appointment on March 10 to receive the worker's cancellation letter (there was delay on DOE's side to process this letter).
remediation_validation:
Case #1: Issara has explained to the workers that according to the Department of Employment (DOE) process, their new employer does not need to get all the application form documents to register them as his employees because DOE has those records already.

Case #2: The worker confirmed that he received his cancellation letter on 10th March and he is now trying to find work with another employer.

supplier_name: Nan Yang Garment Co., Ltd. (Nakhon Pathom)
description: Proper legal documents not provided to worker
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Several workers did not receive their visa and work permit extensions (expired in Jan and Feb 2023) as promised by the business earlier this year. They requested the business support in getting their documents extended but the business told them they would apply pink cards for them.  Then on June 24, 2023, without any warning, HR staff informed them that they needed to return to Myanmar to apply for new passports within 30 days.  The workers include a worker that holds a passport for job (PJ), another that holds a certificate of identity (CI), and six others that lost their PJ passports.

Talking points: 
- Does the business intend to extend these workers' contracts and continue employing them?
- Why did the business not extend their legal documents before they expired in Jan and Feb of this year?
- Why did the business wait until June to suddenly require workers to return to Myanmar to renew their passports when earlier the business had told them they would get pink cards in Thailand?
- Why do some of these workers need to apply for new passports when 2 of the 6 already hold a PJ or CI?

Recommendations: 
- The business should provide severance pay if the business cannot extend their work permits and visas and will let the workers go
- If the business will continue employing these workers, the business should arrange for, and pay for the fresh MoU process and for the workers to be assured they will be safe in Myanmar during the waiting period before returning to Thailand.
- Communicate clearly to workers what the process will be, to allay the concerns and stress of the workers who are not sure what will happen to them

Additional recommendations: (13 July 2023)
- Inform the business that there will likely be a pink card registration that the government will announce in the near future and that this will be an alternative to workers doing the MOU U-turn process
- The business to consult the workers and to provide the details of both options: 1) MOU U-turn process and 2) the pink card registration.  The details should include the process steps involved, the costs/fees for each step, the expected timeline; and agencies or staff involved in facilitating each step of the process
- The business to decide, with worker input and consent, the preferred option and to provide the necessary support to each worker so that they can return to work with all required legal documents.
remediation_notes: Several workers did not receive their visa and work permit extensions (expired in Feb 2023) as promised by the business earlier this year. They requested the business support in getting their documents extended but the business told them they would apply pink cards for them.  Then on June 24, 2023, without any warning, HR staff informed them that they needed to return to Myanmar to apply for new passports within 30 days.  The workers include a worker that holds a passport for job (PJ), another that holds a certificate of identity (CI), and six others that lost their PJ passports.
remediation_action: Issara escalated this issue to Nan Yang BKK.  The business noted that these workers had difficulties getting their CI/PJ renewed due to several reasons. One lacked documents (nationality ID card and household registration) that the Myanmar embassy required to renew the PJ; for another, his name was a duplicate with another person so needed to return to Myanmar to confirm his identity; others were waiting for their CIs to be issued but the CI center closed and were told they would need to get it in Myanmar. The business had no intention of letting the workers go but wanted to continue employing them but they hadn't be able to extend their visa and work permit because of the delays in workers getting their CI/PJ. The business said the workers didn't want to return to Myanmar but just wanted to get severance pay after dismissal.  Issara recommended that the business support the workers to return to Myanmar and come back as fresh MOU workers, and to let the workers know that the business will cover the costs and ensure their safety throughout the process.
remediation_validation:
The worker provided an update saying that the business told them on June 24, 2023, to sign the document that said the workers would take 30-day leave to go back to Myanmar to apply for a new passport. The workers did not sign the documents. Again, on June 28, 2023, the line supervisors told the workers that they would have to stop working with Nan Yang on July 1, 2023.  But on July 1, 2023, HR told them they could work until the end of July 2023.  

A worker further updated that HR staff met with them on July 8, and informed them that they would take 90-day leave to return to Myanmar, stay in their home town, finish the MoU process, and then return to the workplace. When the workers asked for the recruitment agency name, timeline, cost, and detailed process regarding safety, HR said that the business would cover the cost but no information about RA or the MoU process was provided to the workers. The workers would like the business to submit the name list with their names included, according to the recent Thai government policy announcement. As is anticipated, the workers would like to be registered as pink card workers in the upcoming registration of undocumented workers (confirmed but not yet formally announced). description: Proper legal documents not provided to worker
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context;  A group of workers who were recruited under the recalibration program by a local agent to work for Mapa glove reported not receiving their documents as of yet. They said that there are 8 of them in total (Seven Indonesian and one Nepalese). According to the workers, they are working under the management of the agent and receive their wages through the agent. They have reported not having a passport or a permit. In addition to that, workers also reported not having employment contracts with MAPA Gloves. When they have issues at the workplace, they are told to report to the agent which means they do not have access to the business grievances like other workers. Workers reported that they are happy with the working conditions, however, they wanted to have proper documentation in their hands of their safety. 

Talking Points; 
Issara team to focus on the worker's confidentiality and the safeguard for the workers and explain the business until they understand the importance of the worker's safety. 
What is the business understanding of this group of workers? How many workers were recruited during the recalibration period? 
How are the documents of these workers being managed? What is the reason why these workers have not gotten their documents even after 8 months of their work in the factory?  Who pays the monthly salary of these workers? The business or the agent? 
According to Malaysian Law, since 1 April 2019, an agency is not allowed to be the principal employer; they can only act as a recruiter. What are the business understanding and interpretations of this law?
If the business is aware that these workers are being employed under the agent, what are the challenges for the business to hire them directly under Mapa company? Has Mapa ever thought about the risks of having an agent managing the workers this way?

Recommendations for remediation and system change. 

If there are no major challenges, the business is suggested to process recruiting these workers under the company name. Before processing any steps for these workers, the business should make sure that the agent does no harm to the workers. Workers should not be asked or pressured for making calls to Issara. 
Workers and the agent should be clearly communicated about the business plan of action. 
The business should find out why these workers' documents are not being issued so far and communicate the status with the workers.
Workers should have a proper contract including information about their rights, grievances, and benefits like other workers, and they should be informed and treated like they are Mapa’s employees
Workers should receive their official documents to be able to work legally under the law of Malaysia. And for any good reason that Mapa cannot provide the documents, workers should be informed about this with a timeframe of when they can get their documents.
Workers should receive their wages through Mapa Glove not through the agent to avoid timely and accurate payment, and Mapa should have a mechanism to check and confirm this with workers and should ensure that there will be no reprisal for reporting or sharing information with Mapa and Issara. 
Workers should have access to the grievances of Mapa Glove and be remediated accordingly. Mapa may also share Issara worker voice channels should workers want to communicate in their own language and if they wish to do so for different reasons.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
This group of workers were recruited under the "Recalibration Program" through an outsourcing agent. Outsourcing through an agent during the COVID-19 outbreak is legal. These workers are under the process of legalization by the agent. Only after the legalization process is completed, the workers will become official workers of Mapa and will get the contract as well. The process is taking longer than expected by the government side and it has announced it to complete the process at the end of 2022. The business expects to finalize the process by then. 

Next steps; there are no clear next steps from the business side since the business has no leverage to do anything. It depends on the government. However, Issara communicated with the workers about the business response.
remediation_notes: A group of workers who were recruited under the recalibration program by a local agent to work for Mapa glove reported not receiving their documents.
remediation_action: After going through the process of legalization run by the agent, the workers will become official workers of Mapa and will get their contract as well. The process is taking longer than expected by the government side and it is expected to take until the end of 2022.
remediation_validation: Mapa will inform the process to the workers and Issara will also inform the workers.

Context; The issue with an Indonesian worker who has been working for Blueberry for about 10  months reported saying that she gave her documents to the business for the legalization process; however, she has now decided to leave the company as she is not happy with the working conditions. Since she has decided to leave the job, she has stopped going to work to perform her duty for about 5 days now.  However, her passport is with HR and when she approached HR for her passport return, HR asked for 1500 MYR from her saying that her passport is with immigration to obtain a working permit. Until now she said she never had a medical check, an important phase to obtain a working permit. 

She also reported the poor behavior of the line leader (female, Chinese Malaysian).  She added that the line leader would shout at the workers when she is not happy with their work. When she shouts, she uses inappropriate words such as using sexually related words and comparing workers with animals which makes her want to discontinue working for the company. 

Talking Points; 
What is the process for the workers who were recruited under the recalibration period? What about the fee? Why is she being asked for the money when Ramatex practice “Zero recruitment fees”? 
Any supporting documents for workers for them to go out if their docs are on the process. 

Recommendations for remediation. 
The business shall conduct an investigation into why this worker has to pay for the document fees and find out the process for her including the workers who were recruited under the recalibration program. 
The business to make sure safeguards are in place for the worker during the investigation process. The relevent HR staff and line leaders should be clearly communicate about the business’s no-retaliation polity.
Once the investigation is conducted, the business to conduct communication with all workers under “RP” program about the status of their documents and explain the fees that they should not be paying. 
The business to take disciplinary action against the HR who charges money from the workers and also communicate with relevant staff to prevent this from happening in the future.
remediation_business_steps_taken:

If there are any workers who want to leave the job, Triston is the one who signs the resignation. Triston so far has not received any resignation letter that needs his signature from Blueberry and Blueberry is the factory that has lest turnover rate. If workers want to leave the job, they can just fill the resignation simply and the rest process will be handled by HR and other relevant teams. Triston will do his own internal investigation making sure safeguard for the worker is in place. 

The document process is taking longer than expected from the government side, the government has announced to finalize the processes at the end of this year.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Many workers recently dismissed by Cal-Comp SMSK have been trying to get cancellation letters so that they can find new employers.  Those that were recruited through one Thai Recruitment Agency noted that they had received communication from the agency staff saying that they needed to find a new employer first within 30 days and only then would the agency process the cancellation letter with the Department of Employment. The workers want to get their cancellation letters because new employers want to see these letters before making the decision to hire migrant workers.  It is not clear why the business is not providing these cancellation letters directly to workers and communicating with the workers via the Thai recruitment agency. 

TPs:
- How is the business handling the separation process with the workers it recently dismissed and ensuring that they receive cancellation letters so that they can find new employers?
- Is the business aware that the Thai RA is demanding that workers find new jobs first in order to get their cancellation letters, when it should be the other way around?

Recommendations:
- Communicate directly with the workers about when the business will process the cancellation letters with the DOE and when it will provide those letters to the workers
- Provide the workers with the cancellation letters issued by the DOE without delay, preferably directly rather than via a third party

remediation_notes:
An MoU worker called to report an issue with the cancellation letter provided to a group of 57 workers working at the plant that they are not able to use it to apply for jobs in different provinces, as the new employer have rejected their candidature stating that the cancellation letters are not eligible for changing jobs. Two separate batches of workers are impacted by this issue.

BHR spoke with an electronics factory to hire these workers and they require a list of names and other details to process the cases. However, on two days later that factory advised that they have already found the necessary number of workers as they had a walk-in of over 7000 workers for 200 positions they were hiring. So jobs for these workers are no longer available.

The management at this plant have acknowledged that in some provinces the "resignation" remarks on the cancellation letters are interpreted differently so it is possible that the workers are having issues with new employers. In that event, management is open to modification of remarks in the cancellation letter.

The following week, some workers did try to reach the business about this problem however they were denied access. Plant management has requested Issara to find out from MoL/DoE about the process to re-issue cancellation letters so they can advise all impacted workers and handle the cases accordingly. We did so and letters were re-issued based on our guidance.
remediation_action:
Plant management have acknowledged that in some provinces the "resignation" remarks on the cancellation letters are interpreted differently so it is possible that the workers are having issues with new employers. In that event, workers can contact HR and they are open to modification of remarks in the cancellation letters. Issara to schedule a formal remediation call with management for agreement on business actions for the closure of this issue.

The follwing week, some workers did try to reach the business about this problem however they were denied access. Management has requested Issara to find out from DoE about the process to re-issue cancellation letters so they can advise all impacted workers and handle the cases accordingly. We did so and letters were re-issued with this guidance.

In addition, Issara is helping the workers to find new job opportunities on Golden Dreams and from speaking with other businesses in our orbit.
remediation_validation:
Workers confirm that despite management saying that they were welcome to contact HR, they have been denied access at every turn.

They are now focused on getting cancellation letters that will allow them to switch employers without returning to Myanmar, and, finding actual jobs.
remediation_results: We successfully obtained the correct cancellation letters to allow workers to switch employers in-country without returning home. The workers are now focused on finding new jobs and avoid having to return to Myanmar given the civil war, and have a few leads. Workers have up to 60 days to find a new job with the corrected cancellation letter.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker called to report that in these few months, on a few occasions, the line supervisor asked workers to complete the target before they could leave during their two hours of OT work, which resulted in workers having to work 5–10 minutes extra but they received payment for only two hours. The workers don't appreciate this practice, even though it doesn't happen all the time, because they need to catch the bus on time; otherwise, the bus will leave them.

Details information:
- Plant: Processing Plant (Brae Roub)
- Department: Kirami
- Line: S3
- There are 6 lines, and each line has 70–80 workers.

Aside from the issue raised above, the worker has two follow-up questions for the business:
1. Will I be targeted if I urge or raise an issue against supervisors or an issue that happened at the workplace? The worker's concern that the business will not do visa extensions or renew the documents for him when he completes the 2/4 MOU contract.
2. Any disciplinary action that leads to not renewing or terminating the workers' contracts? The decision made by the line supervisor or HR?

Recommendations:
- The business to investigate this matter, as to why supervisors are requiring workers to stay longer than 2 hours for OT to reach a target but workers are not paid for the additional time worked
- Investigate with worker safeguards and zero tolerance for anyone retaliating against workers for reporting this issue
- Line supervisor to be re-trained and disciplined, as per the company's disciplinary policy
- HR to make an announcement, verbally and in writing, about the what is expected for OT without pressure or force to meet a certain target
- Reimburse workers for additional time they spent worker beyond the 2 OT hours, which should be logged in the time-in / time-out system

systems_change_issara_recommendation: Conduct line supervisor training (Issara can provide this training free of charge)

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: the client arrived in Malaysia on 19th October 2023. upon arrival they were picked up by a Tamil broker who they referred as Boss. the first month or so after they came they did not have any work, until the Tamil broker sent them to this place to work. following are the issues and findings from the client:

- there are 5 of them.
- before departure from Bangladesh they were told their job is in plum oil industry. however, they are given work to harvest tomatoes. 
- they have been working in this place for 17 days. 
- instead of 8 hours shift they have to work 12 hour shifts. 
- they were promised that they could make up to RM2200-RM2300, but are told they will be paid RM20 per day.
- the Tamil guy who sent them here is not replying to their calls and messages, asking them "why they have so many problems".
- they asked the Tamil broker to give them different job, but he did not agree.
- they do not have their passport with them, they believe their passport is with the Tamil broker. 
- they are planning and trying to leave the place and find other places to work. 

Issara had a follow up call with them and following are the updates received from the client: 

- 5 of them left the workplace in the afternoon. 
- they contacted the Tamil broker prior to them leaving, stating their plan to leave and come to him. he responded by saying, if they leave the place he will not be liable for them. 
- they also consulted their recruitment agency back in Bangladesh. the agency suggested them to leave and go to the Tamil broker and assured them if they face any problems they will help. 
- together all 5 of them received RM500 for working 12 hour shift of 17 days. 
- they are paying the taxi they rented by themselves. 
- location they are going to is: Taman Desa Aman, 09400 Karangan, Kedah, Malaysia

Issara staff is engaged with them following all the updates provided by the client.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with one worker that was arrested by the police on June 2021 because her work permit had expired, which the business failed to extend even though she had already paid the business for her medical check-up, work permit, and visa.  She is currently in a detention center and has been told she will be deported when the borders open. The worker added that he was working for the Hong Seng without a valid Work Permit since February to she was arrested. 

**This KPI is triggered by the issues where workers' wages were illegally deducted by the immigration police officer and being dealt with under the following KPIs 1466, 1467, 1468. 

Issara has shared the newly announced document by the government which has options for the workers to apply their documents in Thailand.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had meetings with Nike, Nike updated checking with the business and found the issue with the immigration. Nike added that the business has submitted worker's documents for the extension on time, however the immigration office could not find the worker information in the system and the worker ended up being arrested and detained. Several months later, the SP provided an update saying that the business had arranged for the worker to be released from the immigration detention center, and processed her working papers. Issara followed up with the worker and was found mentally and physically healthy. However, the worker added some illegal deductions (100THB for 1000 THB) from her wages by the immigration officers every time that the business transferred her salary to her through immigration officer. This is an illegal deduction and the police should not have charged the worker such fees.  Nevertheless, she did not want to request the return of the money the police had taken from her, and was happy to have received wages from the business and to be out of the detention center.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Irrelevant.

description: Issue with deductions: illegal and/or excessive
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue with deductions for bathroom breaks during OT when workers return from the toilet later than the 15-minute break. And if workers are late to work about 1-5 minutes, they are forced to deduct half of that day’s OT wage. And they will receive a lower year-end bonus based on the numbers of these deductions.

Talking points:
-Are workers able to take toilet breaks if needed during their OT hours?
-How is the OT hours of workers recorded and how is the payment calculated?  Does the business deduct any pay for penalties such as being late from a toilet break?
-How is the year-end bonus calculated?

Recommendations:
-Workers should be allowed to use the toilet when needed, and payment for OT hours worked should be paid in full
-Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, the policy for payment of OT hours and clarify that there are no deductions for the OT hours worked

description: Issue with deductions: illegal and/or excessive
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers arrived on Dec 22, 2023 (sent by Pwint Phoo Aung RA), and started work on Jan 15, 2024. They all had to work and paid as piece-rate workers. About 10 workers cannot finish the target, and they requested the Thai RA interpreter to become daily rate workers. However, the Thai RA interpreter told them that they have to pay money if they want to be daily wage workers. They work from 6:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. but they earn only 348 THB, which is only the daily minimum wage. The employer also deducted six days of their wages as a "deposit" on Jan 24, 2024.

Recommendations:
- The business should not make any deductions that workers don't consent to and that are not allowed by law.  Any legal deductions not to exceed 10% of the pay as per the law.
- Communicate this clearly to workers so they understand the terms and conditions of payment.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 7 Feb 2024

K. Nutthapol, MD received the case detail with the issues. They will investigate and get back to us with the investigation result and corrective action by next week.
remediation_notes: Workers started work in January 2024 and were told they would be paid on a piece rate basis but they are working around 11 hours each day but only being paid approximately the daily minimum wage. The employer also made deductions during the very first payment period, which workers did not consent to.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - HR systems should have a clear policy on complying to Thai labor laws, and to not institute any deductions that are not allowed by law. The policy should be clear that workers should always consent to any deductions to be made.
next_description: get the business corrective action.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The issue with delayed payment and the payslip. Workers explained that they were told by the business that they would receive double payment for regular working hours if they came to work, as many other workers were in quarantine, so as an incentive they would receive that extra payment. Workers reported that they have not received the correct payment for the July 20th and August 5th payroll. They added that some of them have not received the payslip of those two payrolls, however, some of them who have received the payslip reported that the format of the payslip was changed and it is not in their language so it is difficult to understand their missing wages correctly. 

Recommendation:
_The business shall provide the payslip to the workers immediately, in a format and language workers can understand easily. The payslip should include clear information about the wages, incentives, and deductions. 
_The business shall check the payment system to identify the issue with the missing payment and remediate workers according to what they were promised. 
_The business shall communicate with the workers to approach the HR focal person if they have any issue with their wages. 


Talking Points:
-What is the business understanding on this issue with the payment? 
-Have there been any changes with the payslip recently? 
-Have there been any communication with the workers about the changes of the payslip? 

Time Frame 1 week

description: Timesheets/payslips/other basic pay-related documents not provided to worker
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that he works from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. (sometimes until 7:15 p.m.) for the day shift but the line supervisor asks workers to scan out at 6:30 pm. So, it seems like the worker has been working for OT for around 3–3:15 hours but the worker received only 2:30 hours of OT. Due to many workers complaining about this missing OT payment, the business has stopped providing the pay slip to the workers. Additionally, the worker said that during long public holidays such as Songkran workers were asked to work, but he didn't come to work because it was a public holiday that had been announced in the factory. But when he came back to work, the line supervisor gave him a warning letter.

TPs:
- What is the company policy in terms of public holidays announced by the company? Are there instances where line supervisors can ask workers to report to work on any of these public holidays?  If so, for what reason and who makes this decision (the line supervisor or someone higher up?)

Recommendations:
- The company should investigate why after repeated complaints from workers about not being fully paid for their OT work, the company has not responded to this and why a worker received a warning letter for not consenting to work on a public holiday
- Ensure safeguard for the workers and all supervisors are reminded about the company's zero tolerance on retaliation against workers reporting issues
- Clearly communicate to supervisors and workers about the OT policy, number of OT hours to be worked and the company's commitment to pay fully the OT hours worked
- Remediate workers that worked extra OT hours but were not paid for those hours worked
- Rescind the warning letter that may have been issued to a worker that did not consent to work on a public holiday but the line supervisor had required workers to report to work
remediation_notes: A worker reported that he works from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. (sometimes until 7:15 p.m.) but the line supervisor asks workers to scan out at 6:30 pm. So, the system logs their OT hours at only 2.5 hours when in reality they have worked around 3–3:15 hours. Due to many workers complaining about this missing OT payment, the business has stopped providing the pay slip to the workers.
remediation_action: The Strategic Partner reached out to the business but the business declined to engage with Issara regarding this issue.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Conduct training for the HR team on the company policy to provide all workers with pay slips with full information on wages and deductions, in the language of the workers and that they receive their pay slips on a timely basis.

systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Issara had discussed this issue with the business in the past, however, there was no action. Therefore, Issara sent an email to Tesco to better Tesco's position on this issue. 

I've been meaning to ask you about a payslip issue we have discussed with BFI for quite some time now.  BFI currently provides payslips to their workers that are only in the Thai language.  In an effort to make improvements, they have put on the announcement board a sample of the payslip with translations into Khmer so the Cambodian workers can make sense of their payslips.  We have recommended that the payslips provided to all workers should be in both Thai and Khmer but they have said it would be too much of an investment to make this change and that previous audits by Tesco had not made an issue of this.  I wanted to ask you about Tesco's position on payslips and whether they should be in the language of the worker.  Ideally, we would like to get your support in dealing with this issue with BFI so would be great to hear from you about Tesco's position.

It is added that developing the application in workers language will be finished at the end of the year (2021). To solve the problem for short time, the business added sample of Khmer language pay slip in the application so that the workers can reference their payment if they had any queries. Issara checked with the workers, the workers confirmed being able to access the sample of the pay slip in their language in the application.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the COVID vaccinations side effect. Workers reported not receiving medical certificates from the in-house medical staff to be paid for sick leave when they have vaccine side effects and wanted to take rest. In addition to that, a worker who received the vaccine and had side effects also reported not receiving a daily wage for his sick leave days even though he has followed the business protocol in order to take sick leave. 

Recommendations: 
-The business shall communicate with all workers including medical staff about the potential side effects those receiving the vaccine might experience in the next few days after getting the shot. The communication should inform workers that those experiencing some side effect symptoms that would not enable them to work properly can take medical leave according to the business procedure of informing the focal person about their leave. 
-Workers who took sick leave and were being asked to present a medical certificate issued by the medical staff should be reimbursed and paid according to the sick leave section from LPA. 
-To avoid impacts on production due to many workers from the same line taking sick leave, the business could rearrange the schedules for different groups of workers getting the vaccine, for instance, instead of doing it by production lines, it could be by batches from workers from different lines.

-How many workers have been vaccinated so far? 
-How has the business communicated with the workers about the common side effects that those receiving the vaccine might experience and what is the process to take sick leave? 
-How many workers have been approved for sick leave after the vaccinations? 
-Has the in-house medical staff received any communication about the vaccine side effect that the workers could face? If yes, what was the communication?

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that he did not receive full wages for OT worked in April and May 2022, and also did not receive wages for two days of sick leave in September 2022.  In April and May 2022, he was asked to work 2.5 OT hours everyday but when he received his pay slip, he was not paid for 9 OT hours. The worker brought the pay slip to line supervisor, which was signed by the line supervisor and manager to verify the missing payment and the worker was instructed to take it to the accountant. In his next payday, he still did not receive the missing payment and in addition he found there was another missing payment for one working day during that pay period.  He did the same with this second pay slip, which was signed by the line supervisor and manager to verify the missing payment and he brought this to the accountant. One and a half month later, he only received 304 baht as reimbursement.  In summary, he was not paid for 9 OT hours and 1 working day, but only received 304 Baht as reimbursement. 

The worker also took sick on 12-13 September, 2022. When he returned to work, he gave a medical certificate to his line supervisor and manager for their signature and then gave it to the accountant. But on 20 Sept 2022, during the payday the worker didn't receive 2 days payment for those sick days.

description: Very late or missing payments
remediation_notes:
Context: The issue with 15 days of OT wage being paid 15 days after the payday. Workers that resigned and go back to their home countries do not have access to their Thai account, so the business is using informal channels to pay the OT wages to workers after they go back to Myanmar. 

Business explanation on their payment system (Aug 2019):for daily wage workers, the payment is done 15 days delayed because GFPT needs that time to check sick leave, absences, or other leave and then GPFT can make the correct payment. And for OT for monthly workers they need 1 month to check with line supervisors if the OT hours are correct. Line supervisors have the records of approved working hours. GPFT does not use the scanning system because there is no way for them to cross check if the workers leave the factory after fishing working or not. When workers resign they can get their money through a friend or family member, GFPT recognizes that this is not the best way to do it but that is the practice right now. Issara recommended GFPT to reconsider their payment system and to find ways to pay workers on time. GFPT will discuss internally with the HQ to find a way to improve the efficiency.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business to revise their payment system to make the full payment of wages to workers that resign on their last day of employment.   

-Recommend Issara Academy training to HR staff.  

Issara can also provide tailored training to full HR teams on-site, and provide systems review with tailored recommendations to eliminate labour risks."

Legal reference: ETI Base Code 5.2. Living wages paid; workers provided with written contract with wage info prior to employment

 
timeframe: 2 payment periods for the business to revise their payment system

description: Very late or missing payments
Very late or missing payments
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with a worker who was told by the business not to come back to work as she is in her advance pregnancy period. The worker said that she has not received her daily wages during the days that she was not allowed to work. The worker added not being clearly communicated about her rights as a pregnant worker and not knowing whether she will receive the payment and maternity leave according to the LPA or not. Worker’s personal information : Passport: N01017427, Name: Sreypeou Nuon, and Working ID:  0104347.

Recommendations: 
-The business to conduct clear communication with the worker and explain her rights as a pregnant worker in Thailand and how the business will support her to get her benefits from the business and the social security fund. 
-The worker should be provided with 90 days of paid maternity leave and 8 days of unpaid leave if the worker wishes to take those 8 days. 50% of the maternity leave payment should come from the employer and the rest 50% to be reimbursed from the Social Security fund. 
-Worker added that she will deliver her baby in a few weeks, therefore the business shall provide/facilitate assistance to the worker as needed such, as interpretation, full information on medical assistance, and how to get all proper documentation such as the baby’s birth certificate, the child-raising fund process, etc. 
-The worker added not receiving her wage for September, the business shall provide her wages in a timely manner.  

Talking Points;
-Is the business aware of this worker's condition? If yes, what has been communicated to her about her job position, her wages, and her benefits as a pregnant worker? 
-What was the reason why the worker did not receive her wage for the month of September? And how is the company processing the benefits for the worker through the SSO?
-How many workers are there in this situation? 

Time frame: 1 week.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had several meetings with the business, the business responded that they are open to providing maternity leave starting from the date as requested by the worker and also assisting the worker with the required documents for the social security benefits for her delivery. The business confirmed to provide the daily wage for the workers for the first 45 days according to the law and help coordinate with the SSF for the rest of 45 days of her daily wages. Issara follow up with the worker, the worker updated having close contact with the HR for the further process and confirmed not having concerns anymore. The worker will receive 27000THB of daily wages during her maternity leave.
remediation_notes: A worker who was told by the business not to come back to work because she is in an advanced stage of her pregnancy. She has not received her daily wages during the days that she was not allowed to work.
remediation_action: Issara had a meeting with the business, and the business responded that they have been working with the worker and will approve worker's maternity leave starting from the date that she was admitted to the hospital as requested by the worker. And the business will process the documents for compensation from Social Security during the maternity leave period and will receive the worker back whenever she is ready to get back to work.
remediation_validation: The worker confirmed that she wanted to take maternity leave from the date she was admitted to the hospital for the period of leave allowed to her, and receive daily wage compensation for that period as according to the law.
remediation_results: The pregnant worker and the business have agreed on the period of the maternity leave, the business will process the daily wage payment during the maternity leave period and will welcome the worker back to work once she is ready to return to work.

description: Very late or missing payments
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the missing payment of the worker's daily wages during their quarantine period and Bubble and Seal Period. Workers added that there are several workers including pregnant workers who have not received any payment or lower payment than what they used to receive. It is added that there is no clear communication from the business side for their missing payment. In addition to that, some workers who have received some payment have reported not getting a payslip. 


Recommendation:
-The business shall provide the payslip to the workers immediately, in a format and language workers can understand easily. The payslip should include clear information about the wages, incentives, and deductions. 
-The business shall check the payment system to identify the issue with the missing payment and remediate workers according to what they are supposed to be paid. 
-All workers should receive the right payment within the next pay period 
-The business shall communicate with the workers to approach the HR focal person if they have any issue with their wages so that the HR can verify the right amount workers should receive. The focal person should be clear on how to communicate with the workers when workers approach the office. 
-Workers who were quarantined or placed in Bubble and Seal housing and not working should have a clear leave policy that is paid properly. 
- Pregnant workers, in particular, should be fully paid for any days they were in company housing and not working, with a clear policy on what types of leave are applied (cannot be unpaid leave).  
- As workers are unable to afford their current costs, this should be immediately investigated with workers quickly paid properly in the current pay period.

Talking Points:
-What is the business understanding on this issue with the payment? 
-Have there been any changes with the payroll recently? 
-Have there been any communication with the workers about the changes to the payslip? 



Time Frame 2 weeks.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the business, the business argued that they have investigated and found 6 of the pregnant workers not receiving their daily wages because they wrongly requested (using business leave instead of sick leave) during theirs quarantine. The business added that they have corrected workers' leave and have paid them since 20th October. Issara checked with the workers, workers did not agree with what the business has responded and they have still updated not receiving their payment till the 29th of October. In addition to that, when workers reached HR for their issue, workers were told not to report the issue to Issara.

Issara escalated to the TU Sustainability Director and HR at HQ that this is a larger group of workers beyond the 6 workers that TUS investigated and identified as having used personal leave instead of sick leave and TUS had fixed the issue and paid those workers.  The business said it would investigate the missing payments and understands the urgency of the workers.  TUS will also announce to workers to go to HR and report any missing payments to speed up the process.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that several TUS workers, including pregnant workers, have not received any wages or received differing amounts for the past two payment periods when they were in bubble and seal housing or in quarantine.  No pay slip was provided and no explanation provided for the payments to workers.
remediation_action:
The business is following up on this matter and requested more information from Issara and also for affected workers to report directly to HR.

The business investigated the matter and found that 6 pregnant workers had not received their daily wages because they requested business leave instead of sick leave for their quarantine days. The business said it made the correction and processed payment on 20th October.

Issara escalated to the TU Sustainability Director and HR at HQ that this is a larger group of workers beyond the 6 workers that TUS investigated and identified as having used personal leave instead of sick leave and TUS had fixed the issue and paid those workers.  The business said it would investigate the missing payments and understands the urgency of the workers.  TUS will also announce to workers to go to HR and report any missing payments to speed up the process.
remediation_validation: Issara checked with the workers, and the workers said they had not received their missing payments as of 29th October.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
System change recommendations:
-The business should make clear announcements in writing and verbally about the payment of the wages during quarantine periods, and during the B&S measures. 
-The business should encourage workers to contact HR staff and/or use any grievance mechanism they feel comfortable using to share any issue or concern they might have. 
-Issara recommends tailored training to HR staff

In the first report, the business argued that their investigation found 6 of the pregnant workers that TUS investigated and identified as having used personal leave instead of sick leave. TUS fixed the issue and remediated the workers. In addition to that, Issara escalated to the TU Sustainability Director and HR at HQ and explained that this is a larger group of workers beyond the 6 workers, therefore TUS was suggested for additional investigation. After the business conducted another investigation, 68 employees who were infected with COVID-19 and had a history of more than 30 days of sick leave (41 Thai employees and 27 Burmese employees) were identified for payment for those days missed due to Covid-19.  50% of wages is to be paid by the Social Security office and 50% was paid by the business this year only. Furthermore, the business identified another 35 employees who had close contact with COVID-19 patients and ordered the company to quarantine. They were allowed to take up to 30 days of sick leave and the business has paid wages for quarantine days to all 35 workers. In total 6+ 68 + 30 = 104 workers have been remediated. description: Very late or missing payments
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with missing payment: A worker reported her missing payment. She said that the business replaced the new scanner on the 1st of Oct but the scanner did not scan her working hours properly on that day. That is why she had one day of missing payment from the business on her payroll. In addition to that, the worker reported that she had approached building 6 which is known as a building to report workers issues, but she was told to reach out to her line leader by the building 6 officer, when she approached her line leader, the line leader asked her to report to her foreman. She reported to her foreman, but the foreman did not take any action to address her issue. The worker wants her missing payment for one day. 

Recommendation for remediation: 
_The business shall check the payment system to identify the issue with the missing payment and remediate workers accordingly. 
-The HR team shall work with the finance team to make sure workers are paid correctly. And the timeframe to proceed with the payment should be communicated to workers. 
-The business should communicate to the impacted worker and explain the date of the payment that she will receive. The communicator should be from HR, NOT from the production line to avoid the risks for the worker. 
-The business should also make an announcement in writing and verbally, inviting workers to approach HR if they have also faced similar issues with the payment due to the system malfunction. And the business should remediate impacted workers accordingly. 

Talking Points: 
-What kind of issues are being handled in building 6? 
-Is building 6 being managed by HR or any other team? 
-What is the responsibility of the leaders and the foreman if workers have issues? 
-What is the business response on this issue where the worker's issue was not being managed or reported by the foreman? 


Recommendations for system change
-The business shall re-communicate with all workers who or where to reach out if their issues are not solved by relevant staff. 
-For the issue with the unresponsive grievance mechanism, the business should clearly communicate with all relevant staff about their responsibilities to make sure that workers’ issues are properly responded to. 
-Issara recommends training for all parties in charge of handling and responding to workers' grievances. Tailored training on this matter can be provided by Issara Institute. And/or the business can conduct comprehensive training for all relevant staff. 

Time frame: One pay period.

supplier_name: Cal-Comp Electronics (Thailand) Public Co., Ltd. - Samut Sakhon
description: Very late or missing payments
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A client reported that she is an MOU worker who came with Golden Royal Mandalay in 30 Jan 2023. When Cal-Comp dismissed the workers in Samut Sakhon site, his brother was also in the group. So, she talked with the Thai recruitment agency no.45 staff "Mr. Wai Yan Soe" if she can also get the cancellation letter to find another job like her brother since she doesn't want to keep working there alone. "Mr. Wai Yan Soe" told her that she can. So she resigned and her last working day was Apr 3, 2023. After that, she contacted Wai Yan Soe many times and he told her that he will get the cancellation letter for her. She hasn't received the cancellation letter but she cannot contact Wai Yan Soe anymore. She is wondering if we can help her to get the cancellation letter. She said she still needs to get paid 10 days of wages from Cal-Comp. 

O&E called and checked what is the reason why she hasn't received the latest wage for 10 days. She said, this 10 days wage was kept as a deposit while the workers start working. The worker also adds that it is a tradition that Cal-Comp used to do this practice. So the workers should the employer knows in advance before they leave so that they can get back the wage for these 10 days.

However, she said that she doesn't have the pay slip anymore. She just wants the cancellation and it's ok even she didn't get back the wage for 10 days.

His name is Pan Sandar.
ID: C-375620
Starting Date:30 Jan 2023
Last working day: 3 Apr 2023
Thai Recruitment agency no.45

TPs:
- Is it company practice that 10 days of wages are held from workers as a deposit? Is this something the business is doing or the Thai RA?
- What is the deposit for? And how is it returned to workers when they leave?
- The only deduction the employer is able to make is as compensation to the Employer for damage caused by the Employee either wilfully or with gross negligence, with the prior consent of the Employee, and it should not exceed 10% of the payment.

Recommendations:
- The business should not withhold any wages from workers, and should return this money to the worker that has resigned immediately
- The business to communicate clearly and transparently to all workers, verbally and in writing, its policy that it doesn't withhold any wages from workers except for a few restricted instances and what deductions are to be made from their pay (such as social security contributions)
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Anchan, HR sent us an email to clarify as follows. 
Normally, our company will release salary twice as follows

~ 1st time, the release due date will be set for every 1st by calculating the working day during 5th – 19th

~ 2nd time, the release due date will be set for every 16th by calculating the working day during 20th – 4th

For this case;

Employee had worked on January 30th to February 4th. Therefore, the employee will receive the salary on February 16th.


K. Anchan, HR CC (SMSK) shared with us the worker's payroll record, that the work was paid on March 20th-3rd, 2023. 

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-jsaq2k_XWWoqZKzvPR7dvcsEdEUZmiG/edit#gid=1754267130
remediation_notes: An MOU worker that resigned and is waiting for the cancellation letter from the business also noted that she didn't receive wages for 10 days, which is something the business has withheld as a deposit when a worker starts working.

of employees at various card swipe points in the HR system.

Root Cause:
Following our investigated, it is found that it may be due to a overdue payment in employee salaries cycle causing the company
to not be able to pay in time for the actual pay period but the company (HR) collects the number of employees who are overdue
payment each month in the HR database to make payments in the next round instead. There may be some groups of employees
who are not yet aware of this. Even though the factory regularly has morning talks on this matter.


Preventive Action:
Short Term: CPRAM will conduct a morning talk in 3 languages: Thai, Cambodian, and Burmese for all employees and all
nations to understand and acknowledge in the matter of receiving a refund payment in the next payment period. If there is a
problem of overdue payment. (Date to be completed: 11.09.2023)
Long Term: The Human Resources Department will separate the detailed information on overtime pay in the employee's
payment form, if there is overtime payment added from overdue payment in the previous actual payment cycle in order to
notify the employees that the overdue payment has been paid in the next payment period. (Date to be completed: within 2024)
remediation_notes: Issara received a report that there is a miscounting of the OT hours, which they think is to due to the ID card scanner problems.  Workers don't dare to raise this concern with the line supervisor or HR.

systems_change_issara_recommendation: Review the HR recording system to ensure that all hours worked by workers are properly documented and paid for in a timely manner

supplier_name: Daorae (Desa Sri Hartamas) Sdn Bhd, a Korean BBQ restaurant
description: Very late or missing payments
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client worked at a Korean BBQ restaurant located in KL Kepong Jalan Metro Perdana, which is one of fifteen branches of the restaurant chain. Out of the fifteen branches, this particular one was problematic. The restaurant has six Nepali and thirteen Burmese workers. The owner's son is abusive towards the Nepali workers, creating a hostile work environment. Issara is able to speak with two workers. They have been working for this employer for 10 months. They are all MoU workers. They are reporting as a group of 5 Nepali workers, but the client is quietly reporting. The client and the workers want to either be transferred to another branch under the same company or find employment in another company. The client has debts to pay and doesn't want to return to Nepal. The workers have a contract they made in Nepal, but the company made another contract which the client doesn't have and is unaware of its contents.
Following are the major issues reported by workers.

1) Document retention: Workers passports are held by the employer since they started their employment. The company also kept their passports and didn't provide them with worker ID cards (Jalan cards) or necessary documents. 

2) Restriction of Movement: The workers were not allowed to leave the premises, and this restriction also made it difficult for their friends to visit them.

3) Unfair suspension: Workers were frequently suspended for minor mistakes or even without any reason. During these suspensions, the company did not provide any food, and the workers were not allowed to go out and get their own. They were also denied access to basic amenities, like cooling fans, during these periods. One incident occurred when a friend of the client was suspended for simply asking a Burmese worker to clean a stain. The owner verbally abused him and kept him in detention (suspension) for 28 days. Throughout this time, the company did not provide any food or salary, leaving the workers in a dire situation. His friends attempted to provide food secretly, but they had to be cautious as the company would punish them if they were caught bringing in more substantial amounts of food or any food. 

Recently, the victim was suspended by the company for two months. During this period, he received no salary or food from the company. The suspension was a result of the employer demanding the victim to memorize the restaurant menu quickly.

If workers demand to change the employer, they are asked to work 4 months without pay and there are some workers who have accepted this situation as they could not bear the harsh working environment. 

4)Physical abuse: Physical assault includes being kicked, slapped on the face and belly, and having ears pulled. The employer even physically assaulted the client's genitals. Such harassment occurred almost daily and targeted everyone except.

5) Long working hours and incorrect payment: Workers have to work 14-15 hours a day. In return, they received a basic salary of 1500 RM and a 300 RM overtime allowance each month. 

6) Lack of Sick Leave: Even when the workers fell ill, they were forced to work, as the owner wouldn't allow them to stay in the hostel. 



Moreover, during salary payment time, the owner would abuse the workers and suspend them for minor mistakes. The owner often used the workers as a target for his frustrations, taking out his stress related to the business on them. Whenever the business is slow he will start abusing the worker for no reason.

description: Very late or missing payments
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that he works from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. (sometimes until 7:15 p.m.) for the day shift but the line supervisor asks workers to scan out at 6:30 pm. So, it seems like the worker has been working for OT for around 3–3:15 hours but the worker received only 2:30 hours of OT. Due to many workers complaining about this missing OT payment, the business has stopped providing the pay slip to the workers. Additionally, the worker said that during long public holidays such as Songkran workers were asked to work, but he didn't come to work because it was a public holiday that had been announced in the factory. But when he came back to work, the line supervisor gave him a warning letter.

TPs:
- What is the company policy in terms of public holidays announced by the company? Are there instances where line supervisors can ask workers to report to work on any of these public holidays?  If so, for what reason and who makes this decision (the line supervisor or someone higher up?)

Recommendations:
- The company should investigate why after repeated complaints from workers about not being fully paid for their OT work, the company has not responded to this and why a worker received a warning letter for not consenting to work on a public holiday
- Ensure safeguard for the workers and all supervisors are reminded about the company's zero tolerance on retaliation against workers reporting issues
- Clearly communicate to supervisors and workers about the OT policy, number of OT hours to be worked and the company's commitment to pay fully the OT hours worked
- Remediate workers that worked extra OT hours but were not paid for those hours worked
- Rescind the warning letter that may have been issued to a worker that did not consent to work on a public holiday but the line supervisor had required workers to report to work
remediation_notes: A worker reported that he works from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. (sometimes until 7:15 p.m.) but the line supervisor asks workers to scan out at 6:30 pm. So, the system logs their OT hours at only 2.5 hours when in reality they have worked around 3–3:15 hours. They are not being fully paid for their OT work.
remediation_action: The Strategic Partner reached out to the business but the business declined to engage with Issara regarding this issue.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Conduct line supervisor training to build capacity of line supervisors in their understanding of company policies (such as OT hour caps and how hours worked are logged properly) and ensure the clock-in / clock-out system are not improperly manipulated by the supervisors

description: Very late or missing payments
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that he works from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. (sometimes until 7:15 p.m.) for the day shift but the line supervisor asks workers to scan out at 6:30 pm. So, it seems like the worker has been working for OT for around 3–3:15 hours but the worker received only 2:30 hours of OT. Due to many workers complaining about this missing OT payment, the business has stopped providing the pay slip to the workers. Additionally, the worker said that during long public holidays such as Songkran workers were asked to work, but he didn't come to work because it was a public holiday that had been announced in the factory. But when he came back to work, the line supervisor gave him a warning letter.

TPs:
- What is the company policy in terms of public holidays announced by the company? Are there instances where line supervisors can ask workers to report to work on any of these public holidays?  If so, for what reason and who makes this decision (the line supervisor or someone higher up?)

Recommendations:
- The company should investigate why after repeated complaints from workers about not being fully paid for their OT work, the company has not responded to this and why a worker received a warning letter for not consenting to work on a public holiday
- Ensure safeguard for the workers and all supervisors are reminded about the company's zero tolerance on retaliation against workers reporting issues
- Clearly communicate to supervisors and workers about the OT policy, number of OT hours to be worked and the company's commitment to pay fully the OT hours worked
- Remediate workers that worked extra OT hours but were not paid for those hours worked
- Rescind the warning letter that may have been issued to a worker that did not consent to work on a public holiday but the line supervisor had required workers to report to work
remediation_business_steps_taken: The business conducted an investigation of the entire operations and found that it was related to the employee’s weekly working hours exceeding 72 hours. The Supervisor had workers clean the production lines, an extra half-an-hour extended beyond the actual clock-out time. The incident involved 4 Cambodian workers and this happened three times, which is in violation of the Company’s Rules and Regulations.  Therefore, a written warning was issued to the Supervisor in question and it was communicated to all parties concerned that resorting to such a practice was decidedly prohibited. The business will reimburse the missing wage payment to the 4 workers, as of the payment round of 25 August 2023.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that he works from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. (sometimes until 7:15 p.m.) but the line supervisor asks workers to scan out at 6:30 pm. So, the system logs their OT hours at only 2.5 hours when in reality they have worked around 3–3:15 hours. They are not being fully paid for their OT work.

description: Issue with time card scanners/manual recording/systems to register working hours
remediation_issara_recommendation:
[Issue from in-person outreach]
SFP makes sure no workers are late to work. But SFP doesn’t allow workers to leave work on time. The line supervisor called (Hua Na Poe) makes sure no workers get out before the work is finished by standing and waiting at the exit. Many times, the workers end up working for extra 5 to 10 minutes which they don’t get paid for. She wears an orange cap. 

Talking points:
- How does the clock-in / clock-out system work to record working hours of workers?
- Is HR aware that line supervisors are demanding workers stay later than their regular shift and are not paid for the extra time worked?

Recommendations for remediation:
- Review the clock-in / clock-out system and identify why additional work beyond the regular shift is not being recorded and paid to the workers
- Investigate why the supervisors are keeping the workers beyond the regular shift with such extra work being unrecorded and unpaid
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Workers need to stay later after their shift and not paid for 5-10 minutes extra

Business Response: 10 June 2022
K. Sophon responded that the clock was out at 4.30 pm. The workers prepare to clock out at 4.25 pm so it’s not 4.30 pm yet. It might be the case that the workers’ watch is set to 5 minutes before. However, he will investigate this issue and get back to us.


Business Response: 22 June 2022,
K. Sophon needs more time to investigate and will get back to us by Jul 1st.

description: Issue with time card scanners/manual recording/systems to register working hours
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that the facial recognition scanner is often malfunctioning and workers coming in at 6am often have to go back and re-scan at 6:30am after work has started or the line supervisor needs to make a manual note. There is a technician that can help fix the issue with the scanner but he often blames the workers for the malfunction and refuses to help them sort out the issue. If their working hours are incorrectly recorded because of this, then they have to go to HR to get it sorted.

Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter and identify the problem with the scanner so that workers don't have to ask for the technician to fix the issue or for the line supervisor to have to make a manual note of the workers' starting times
- Have clear procedures for what workers need to do if the scanner doesn't work in the future so that it doesn't disrupt with their work and those responsible for responding with the fix do so in a timely manner
- Communicate to the workers the business actions to fix this technical issue, when it will be fixed, and what workers should do if the scanner doesn't work in the future.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 1 Nov 2023

K. Wichai, HR Manager, would like to know if this is from the TUM or ITC buildings. We confirmed that this is a TUM structure. He explained that if the worker was wearing a hat or if anything changed on his or her face, the system might not scan properly. They will, however, investigate this matter and identify the problem with the scanner, as well as communicate with the workers who are having issues with the face scanner to contact HR directly to rescan the worker's face again and add to the system to ensure that the worker can have face scanner easily, timely, and properly. And Issara can help to communicate to the workers to contact HR directly. They will send us the corrective action next week.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that the facial recognition scanner that records their clock-in times often malfunctions
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Conduct annual reviews of the systems in place for recording workers' clock-in and clock-out times so that workers are paid fairly according to the actual times worked.
next_description: follow up the business corrective action.

description: Issue with time card scanners/manual recording/systems to register working hours
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that since the business started using a new system to manage the workers and record working hours and overtime, the Cambodian workers have been losing their OT pay. The workers also reported this issue to the line supervisor and HR but there is no solution yet. 

TPs
- How are the working hours recorded?  Is there a scanner to clock-in and clock-out? Are actual working hours and OT hours recorded manually?

- Investigate this matter and identify why the system is not reflecting the actual hours worked by the workers
- Communicate with workers clearly about how the working hours are actually recorded, and also announce channels whereby workers can report any problems with how their work time is being recorded.
remediation_business_steps_taken:

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue at the meat grinding machine temperature is increased by the line supervisor in order to complete the target faster.

Context:

timeframe 1 payment period
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business response. 
After Issara's suggestion for the business to conduct an investigation, the business got back to Issara with their investigation result. When the factory sends the workes to the farm, the number of workers being sent is not correctly provided to the destination line.  Which creates the workes not receiving enough issues. However, the business stopped sending workers to shrimp farms which cease this issue automatically. Issara had not received any explanation of the reason for not sending workers to the farm.

description: Unsafe or hazardous working conditions (OSH issues)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue # 1. 
Context: The issue with the covid-19 preventions concern. Community members around the factory reported their concern regarding the infected cases in Seafresh. The caller said that they have heard that there are around 10 infected workers in the Factory, however, there are no clear prevention measures to prevent the community from larger impact. 

Talking Points: 
-How many workers have been infected and what have been the prevention measures so far? 
-How have the business communicated with the workers the measures being taken to control the spread to larger groups of workers? 
-Have there been any communication and coordination with the local government to implement preventive measures? 

Recommendations: 
-The business shall make a clear communication to the workers verbally and in writing about the action that the business has been taking to control the spread of virus and the long term plan to control the spread to larger groups. 
-The business is also recommended to encourage workers to use the internal grievance mechanism and/or contact Issara if they have any questions and/or concerns about the prevention measures.

Issue # 2. 

Context: The issue with the workers being told that if they  have COVID symptoms they should go  to the internal clinic and have Pah Talajone for three days and have home quarantine for three days and get Pah Talajones for another three days if they do not get better. Workers reported the business not conducting the COVID-19 tests and having options to go to the hospital if they tested positive. 

Recommendation: 
The business shall provide the options to the workers to get a  COVID-19 test if they have any symptoms. If workers test positive, the company should follow the health officials recommendations depending on the severity of the symphons, such as  hospitalization or home quarantine, and also follow up tests according to the government procedure in Chumphon province. 
If there are workers at risk, meaning that they have been in contact with a positive case, then workers should be asked to stay in quarantine and then do a COVID test before returning back to home. This test shall be facilitated by the business.  

Talking Points: 
How many workers have been tested positive at the moment? 
What has been the process to control the spread and also the treatment for the positive workers. 
What has been the communication with the government in this regard? 
Are there any workers in the government or the factory quarantine center? 
What has been the ATK test process? 
Workers reported receiving the announcement about the internal treatment with Pah Talajone, what is the business understanding of this?
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issue # 1. 
The business response ID: 1514

Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have been following the government public health policy closely and have assigned the focals to work in order to control the spread. The measures that the business has been following are such as; washing hands, wearing masks, social distancing, visiting the medical center for any COVID-19 related symptoms and so on. Issara is trying to reach out to the worker.

Issue # 2. 

Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have voluntary to get the treatment and no workers are forced to under go for the internal (factory clinic) treatment. And about the herbal  medicine, the  business made a written announcement to inform the worker about the voluntaryness whether to take the medicine provided by the business or not. Issara is checking with the workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for system change:
-The business is recommended to make clear verbal and written announcements about the measures being taken to prevent the spread of COVID-19. Such announcements should include information on COVID testing, quarantine period, access to medical services, payment of wages during quarantine periods, factory cleaning, etc.
