description: Unsafe or hazardous working conditions (OSH issues)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue from workers who are back to work after the explosion nearby factory reported having to breathe unhygienic air pollution, not having proper space for their lunch, and not having purified drinking water in their workplace.

Talking Points:
-Workers have reported that the quality of the air is not good, that they can smell smoke and they do not have proper masks to protect them from that air. In addition, workers are reporting that they do not have a proper space to have lunch and that the drinking water provided is not purified. What is the current situation at the factory and how are these issues reported by workers being addressed? 
-What has been the official order for this matter? Any measures recommended by the government?
-Have the official permission to resume operations been communicated with the workers?  

Recommendations: 
-The business shall conduct a communication session with the workers about the official order related to the incident. The communication should address workers’ concerns regarding health consequences for having breath to the smelly air. The business is recommended to emphasize that the operations have been resumed because it is safe to do so according to official announcements so that workers do not need to worry about it. 
-Workers have added that the ground where they have their lunch has some flooding and mud, so it is suggested that the business communicates to workers the steps and timeframe of the canteen reconstructions. It is also suggested to communicate with the workers if the company could arrange other areas for lunch breaks in the meantime. 
-Regarding the drinking water: some workers have reported being offered tap water for drinking while others are being asked to bring their own drinking water. Therefore, the business is recommended to provide purified drinking water to all workers to reduce the risks of workers getting sick. For the workers that are being asked to bring their own water, what they can carry might not be enough to keep them hydrated throughout the workdays, so it is recommended that the business find another solution in the meantime.  If there has been an official announcement from the government about the safe consumption of the water, then the business is recommended to make this clear to all workers to address their concerns.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
16-Jul-2021. 

Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have followed the government instructions and the working condition is safe. The business agreed to conduct the communication with the workers to address their concerns.
remediation_notes: The issue with workers who have been asked to resume work after there was an explosion in a nearby chemical factory fearing for their health because they can still smell the toxic air and have difficulty breathing, and drinking water is no longer provided to them by the business.  They also do not have a proper space for lunch because the canteen was damaged when the chemical factory exploded.

-who will cover the treatment costs (SSF, employer?) 
-quarantine centers and services
-the process that the infected and not infected workers will have to follow (self-quarantine, etc.)
-the payment of the wages for the days of quarantine whenever needed

-Which hospital or quarantine centers are the workers being sent to?

How has the business managed the workers who share the dormitory and production lines?  
-How have the workers been communicated about the COVID-19 treatment fees?

description: Unsafe or hazardous working conditions (OSH issues)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Unsafe or hazardous working conditions (OSH issues). The worker from Breaded line reported that they suffer sore throat and eyesore from the chemical solution that’s used for cleaning. The workers can hardly work in the line production when the cleaners use the solution to clean the line. They get scolded when they ask line supervisors to tell the cleaner not to use the chemical too much. 

Recommendations; 
The business shall conduct an investigation to find out whether the cleaning agent being used is certified to be safe for use in cleaning this production line and identify why workers are suffering negative symptoms (sore throat and eye sores) when the particular cleaning product is used. 
Investigate why the line supervisors did not respond appropriately to workers that reported getting sick from being exposed to the chemicals in the cleaning product used.  Take disciplinary action as appropriate based on the investigation result. 
Conduct the investigation involving affected workers and those using the cleaning products
Develop a plan of action based on the investigation results to ensure that workers have a safe and a healthy working environment and any cleaning products used are within safety standards. 
The business should communicate to all workers about the business’s plan of action to address this issue and provide transparent information about cleaning products being used and that they are safe for workers.  
Since this is the issue with the chemical, this should be considered a serious issue and the business should take action immediately. 
Remind workers about  the internal grievance channels, how workers can report any issues, noting the focal points that will be handling all issues, timeframe for the issues to be solved, and proper safeguards for those reporting grievances. 


Talking Points;

Has the business received these complaints from the workers? 
Are there any channels for the workers to raise this kind of health related issues?
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara raised this issue with the business, the business agreed to conduct an investigation and get back to Issara.
remediation_notes: Workers reported suffering sore throats and eyesores from the cleaning product being used to clean their working line.  They can hardly work in the line when the cleaners use the chemical cleaning agent to clean the line. When they reported this to their line supervisors, they were scolded rather than having the matter addressed immediately, given the threat to the general health of the workers.

-For how long the workers are having these stomach/GI problems.
-Have they been informing about this to their line supervisors? If yes, what is the line supervisor’s response?
-Have they gone to the factory clinic?
-Do they sign the register there when they visit the clinics?
-What kind of medication or advice is being given by the clinic staff?
-Are the clinic staff always present when needed?
-Do any doctors visit the clinic during the week on calls?
-Are workers taking sick leaves due to this issue? Try to inquire how frequent these sick leaves are?
-Do the workers bring their own food or eat in the canteen? How is the quality of food in the canteen? 
-From where do the workers drink water? Is it possible that the drinking?water in the factory is contaminated that is causing stomach issues?
-How are the workers so sure that the irregular breaks are causing the stomach problems and not the food and water that they are consuming?
-Have the workers been self-medicating about these problems? How do they treat themselves?
-Find out if workers from other production lines are also reporting stomach problems as it can help to identify if the factory food, water or hygiene issues in the canteen are the cause of these stomach problems.

----------------------------------------------
Relevant National Laws (Thailand)
----------------------------------------------
1. The Occupational Safety, Health, and Environment Act (2011)
This is the primary legislation in Thailand addressing OSH responsibilities for employers.

Section 6: Employers are required to provide safe and hygienic working conditions to prevent harm to workers' life, health, and property.
Section 22: Employers must provide necessary safety equipment, regular medical examinations, and appropriate training on workplace safety.
Section 9: Employers must report occupational injuries or diseases to relevant authorities, especially in cases of severe injuries, illnesses, or fatalities.
Section 13: Employers must establish a safety  officer/committee in workplaces with more than 50 employees to ensure that safety protocols are being followed. 

2. The Labor Protection Act (1998)
While primarily focused on labor rights, it includes provisions related to worker safety and health:

Section 6: Defines “work safety” and mandates that employers must ensure their workplaces are free from conditions that can cause harm to employees.
Section 108: Employers with 10 or more employees must have written safety rules and provide OSH-related training to employees.

3. Ministerial Regulations
Various ministerial regulations supplement the OSH Act, detailing specific employer obligations for different industries:

Ministerial Regulation No. 2 (2006): Requires that workplaces meet minimum safety and health standards, including ventilation, lighting, and sanitation.

4. Workmen’s Compensation Act (1994)
This act makes employers liable for compensating employees who suffer work-related injuries or diseases:

Section 13: Employers must pay for the medical expenses, rehabilitation, and any disability benefits that arise due to workplace injuries or occupational illnesses.

-------------------------------
International/Global Standards
-------------------------------
The ILO has developed several conventions, recommendations, and standards that deal with employer obligations regarding Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) issues, particularly in factories and other industrial settings. Though not legally binding, this code of practice offers practical guidance for factory employers on OSH issues, focusing on preventive measures, accident reporting, and worker protection.

- ILO Recommendation No. 97 - Protection of Workers' Health Recommendation (1953)

Paragraph 2: Employers must monitor and control harmful occupational exposures to chemicals, physical agents, and biological agents. Workers should not be subjected to conditions that could lead to occupational diseases.

Paragraph 3: Work schedules, task assignments, and the physical and mental load of work should be structured in a way that does not cause excessive strain on workers.

Paragraph 6: Employers must provide preventive health measures, including regular health checks, medical supervision, and early detection of occupational diseases to avoid long-term health damage.

- ILO Convention No. 121 - Employment Injury Benefits Convention (1964)

Article 1: Employers are responsible for compensating workers who suffer from work-related injuries, diseases, or fatalities.

Article 7: Employers must ensure that workers are insured or covered for employment injuries, including healthcare and financial benefits.

-------------------------------
Buyer CoC
-------------------------------

-------------------------------
ILM KPI Goal
-------------------------------
All workers have the right to a safe working environment. It is the responsibility of the employer to provide a safe working environment to all workers at all times. This includes the provision of proper tools, safety equipment, safety protocols, and designated safety focal points to ensure safe and healthy working conditions at all times. These should be provided at no cost to workers.

---------------------------------
Possible Root Causes and Evidence
---------------------------------
-------------------------------
Environmental/Workplace Causes
-------------------------------
Irregular meal timings and breaks (Refer KPI#2392) and long OT hours without breaks (Refer KPI#2391)

Food in the canteen or drinking water at the factory may also be the cause of stomach/GI problems.

Evidence: Workers reporting gastrointestinal/ stomach problems 
It is common knowledge that food or water contamination can cause mild to serious stomach ailments

----------------------------------
Business Systems/Shortfalls Causes
----------------------------------
No proper work shift planning

Management unaware of any reports from the factory clinic about stomach problems. 

Evidence: Scattered, inconsistent and weird break timings. This OSH issue has been going on for some period

------------------------
People-related Causes 
------------------------

----------------------------------
Remediation Recommendations & TPs
----------------------------------
- Send the workers immediately for medical assessment to the factory clinic and if necessary referrals to the hospital.
- Recommend the business to investigate and assess the quality and hygiene of food in the canteen and drinking water available in the factory. Ask them to check the clinic records or with production staff if workers from other production lines are also reporting stomach problems.
- Train the factory clinic staff to inform management if they see many workers coming with similar problems.
- Provide training to line supervisors to be vigilant and monitor the health of workers. If illnesses and health issues are identified they must send them for medical checks.

---------------------------------------------
Worker Requests from Workers for Remediation
---------------------------------------------
Are the workers reporting the issue requesting anything in particular for remediation? - Fixed break times or at least considerations that lunch breaks cannot be taken at 10AM in the morning.

Is the request from workers in line with international standards and norms?- YES 

Is the request from workers safe for themselves, and presenting no possible risks or harms to others? - YES

In conclusion, can/should the request from workers be included in Issara’s recommendations to the business? - YES 

What needs to be communicated back to the workers reporting the issue? -
That their health issues have been communicated the business and further business action will be communicated to them by Issara. 
Workers should also be made aware of their rights under the Workmen’s Compensation Act (1994) that employers must pay for the medical expenses that arise due to workplace injuries or occupational illnesses.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Benefits to Business if the issues raised by worker(s) were properly addressed and no longer impacting the business’ operations/ workplace
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Emphasize that by following these recommendations, business can significantly reduce the risks associated OSH issues like gastrointestinal stomach problems, creating a safer and healthier work environment for workers that will lead to consistent production outputs.
This would also ensure that the worker's safety is addressed within the framework of Thai labor law making the business complaint and preventing any plausible future legal complaints and proceedings.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
How could the issue, and Issara’s role in the remediation process with the business, be framed to the supplier (and the SP, if involved) as Issara helping to support that benefit (as a positive force)?
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Following Issara’s recommendations can help ensure that the business not only complies with Thai labor laws but also aligns with international best practices, providing a safe and healthy work environment for all workers and also strengthens their brand image and ethical work practices to global buyers making positive impacts on their sales and revenue.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
On Sep 10, 2024: Issara made two calls to relevant authorities for guidance:

- Issara called the Department of Labor Protection and Welfare under the Ministry of Labor to ask for information pertinent to the worker-reported issues from MMP. Issara gave the DLPW the general details of the case and asked for their guidance. DLPW said that as it is a health issue resulting from irregular work hours and breaks, the applicable legal framework would be the Labour Protection Act, which stipulated that:

1) the maximum number of working hours of employees in Thailand is 8 hours a day and not more than 48 hours a week, and the maximum number of overtime working hours is limited to not more than 36 hours a week; 

2) All employees are entitled to a daily rest period of at least 1 hour after working for 5 consecutive hours. Any Overtime Work after normal working time is more than two hours, the Employer shall arrange for the Employee to take a rest period of not less than 20 mins BEFORE the Employee commences the Overtime Work.

DLPW suggested that based on these provisions and the fact that the workers in the case work from 7.30am to 10:00pm almost everyday with irregular breaks, it is highly likely that there are infringement and/or violations of the Labor Protection Act (LPA) here. DLPW suggested that the workers in question, or even Issara, should report the case to the Labour Inspection Department of Samut Sakhon and provide their contact number to us (034-413-729 / 034-413-730). The Labour Inspectors are authorized by Section 139 of the LPA to conduct surprise visits and investigations at the business once they receive the complaints. The law allows for these complaints to be filed anonymously to protect the workers. Once the Inspector visits and finishes their investigation of the case, they will file an order within 60 days. The public also has rights to monitor the case and the investigation conducted by the Inspector. If the Inspector finds that the business violates the law and the business refuses to comply with their order, the case will be referred to the Labor Court.

According to the DLPW officer, whether or not the Occupational Safety, Health and Environment ACT B.E. 2554 (A.D. 2011) (OSHE Act) is applicable to this case or not is another question to be explored during or after the investigation of the Labor Inspector. For now, it is easier to approach the case using the working hours- and breaks-related provisions under the LPA as workers can just file a general complaint or give the Labour Inspector anonymous tips so that the Inspector can go in and conduct the investigation right away. For this to become a matter under the OSHE Act, there will need to be reports of machinery-related injuries, accidents or death, or of biohazard or fire incidents that are related to the operations of the businesses for the OSHE Safety Inspector to conduct the investigation. This means that if it is found during the investigation of the Labor Inspector (under LPA) that the illness of the workers is NOT a result of the irregular break and long working hour issues, BUT of a scenario in which workers are exposed to biohazard or other health-threatening substances and materials when trimming the fish (either due to the nature of the works itself or to improper PPEs); then this becomes an issue under the OSHEA Act, which will be dealt by the OSHE Safety Officer.

- Issara called the Division of Occupational and Environmental Diseases (02-590-3864) under the Department of Disease Control (the Ministry of Health) to ask for legal and health-related information pertinent to the worker-reported issues from MMP. Issara called to ask for health-related information from the Department of Occupational and Environmental Diseases and explained the general symptoms of the workers to the officer taking the case. 

The officer said that to investigate the causes of their health issues, one has to look at two things:

1) The behaviors and daily life of the workers: Irregular meals and lunch hours can indeed be a contributing factor to gastrointestinal problems.

2) The environments that the workers live and work in: We can dismiss water from a potential cause as workers report drinking safe potable water from a filtered water fountain of the factory. Whether or not it is food-related, this has to be investigated further if workers eat properly cooked and heated food, or how often they eat raw food, the latter of which might lead to infection. The working conditions have to be investigated as well to know whether or not, while handling and trimming the fish, the workers have proper PPEs or are exposed to biohazard/health-threatening substances or not. If yes, this will fall under the DLPW’s authority.

---------------------------------
remediation_notes: This issue was reported by a worker from MMP who is currently working in the fish-trimming line (C&D). The worker reported 6 issues that are dealt in relevant KPIs and this KPI deals with issues regarding lunch break and other breaks. Worker reported that there are altogether 500 workers in the fish trimming line A-G and currently all trimming line workers are having issues with lunch breaks. She stated that the fish trimming line workers never have normal lunch breaks and their breaks are irregular on a nearly everyday basis. Sometimes when they have a large quantity of steamed fish, their lunch breaks are usually late and if they don't have many steamed fish to trim, their lunch break comes early. When the machine breaks down, they have to take their lunch breaks early. On some days workers start work at 7:30AM and the business gives them a lunch break at 10:00 AM and then an OT break of 30 minutes at 1:00 PM but after that they have to work continuously until 10 PM without any breaks.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- Use technology for Scheduling: Introduce a time management or shift management system that tracks when workers are due for their breaks. This can help avoid missed or delayed breaks and ensure that breaks are evenly distributed among workers. On a simpler level other time tracking tools like time clocks or digital attendance systems can be used to track when workers take their breaks, ensuring compliance with the schedule.

- Establish a Feedback System: A clear and accessible mechanism through which workers can report concerns about irregular breaks without fear of retaliation. This can be done through suggestion boxes, a hotline, or meetings with HR.

- Enforcement Training to Line Supervisors and Production Managers: Provide training on how to monitor and enforce break times fairly and consistently.

- Regular audits: Conduct regular audits to ensure breaks are being provided on time and in accordance with the law. Evaluate whether workers are satisfied with the break schedules and make adjustments as necessary.

Context; The issue with an Indonesian worker who has been working for Blueberry for about 10  months reported saying that she gave her documents to the business for the legalization process; however, she has now decided to leave the company as she is not happy with the working conditions. Since she has decided to leave the job, she has stopped going to work to perform her duty for about 5 days now.  However, her passport is with HR and when she approached HR for her passport return, HR asked for 1500 MYR from her saying that her passport is with immigration to obtain a working permit. Until now she said she never had a medical check, an important phase to obtain a working permit. 

She also reported the poor behavior of the line leader (female, Chinese Malaysian).  She added that the line leader would shout at the workers when she is not happy with their work. When she shouts, she uses inappropriate words such as using sexually related words and comparing workers with animals which makes her want to discontinue working for the company. 

Talking Points; 
What is the process for the workers who were recruited under the recalibration period? What about the fee? Why is she being asked for the money when Ramatex practice “Zero recruitment fees”? 
Any supporting documents for workers for them to go out if their docs are on the process. 

Recommendations for remediation. 
The business shall conduct an investigation into why this worker has to pay for the document fees and find out the process for her including the workers who were recruited under the recalibration program. 
The business to make sure safeguards are in place for the worker during the investigation process. The relevent HR staff and line leaders should be clearly communicate about the business’s no-retaliation polity.
Once the investigation is conducted, the business to conduct communication with all workers under “RP” program about the status of their documents and explain the fees that they should not be paying. 
The business to take disciplinary action against the HR who charges money from the workers and also communicate with relevant staff to prevent this from happening in the future.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The business responded, that they never charge workers any recruitment fees. For the workers that were recruited under the "Recalibration Program" were handled by the runner that Ramatex has. If there are any workers who want to leave the job, Triston is the one who signs the resignation. Triston so far has not received any resignation letter that needs his signature from Blueberry and Blueberry is the factory that has lest turnover rate. If workers want to leave the job, they can just fill the resignation simply and the rest process will be handled by HR and other relevant teams. Triston will do his own internal investigation making sure safeguard for the worker is in place. 

The document process is taking longer than expected from the government side, the government has announced to finalize the processes at the end of this year.

description: Document retention by supervisors/brokers/employer
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that he needed to get surgery for which he was in the hospital for 15 days, with costs covered by the employer. He said it seems he was discharged at the urging of the employer who wanted him to return to work.  However, his surgical wound has not healed and it seems the stitches are tearing apart. He has also received less than what his monthly salary should be last month, and his passport is being withheld by the employer.

Recommendations:
- Advise the worker to go to the hospital and seek medical attention directly. Also, he should contact the Nepal embassy for assistance.
- Option 1: Issara to contact the employer directly to advise him of his responsibilities that the worker is given the proper medical care and time to fully heal before returning to work and that the costs should be covered by insurance or the employer rather than the worker.  This is of primary concern.  However, there is also the issue of withholding of wages and document retention, which the employer should be advised to correct. This advice may need to be given after the worker has received the proper medical attention first, lest there be a risk that the employer may refuse to support the worker on all counts.
- Option 2: Issara to refer to partner CSOs if such appropriate partners are available
remediation_notes: A worker reported that he needed to get surgery for which he was in the hospital for 15 days, with costs covered by the employer. He said it seems he was discharged at the urging of the employer who wanted him to return to work.  However, his surgical wound has not healed and it seems the stitches are tearing apart. He has also received less than what his monthly salary should be in the previous month, and his passport is being withheld by the employer.

description: Gender and/or sexual harassment
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; The issue where a male worker using the female worker's toilet and taking photos once in a while at the male toilet. The Thai staff is actually a male with eyeglasses but he uses the female toilet. The client said he is a "Mane Ma Shar" guy who wants to become a girl.

-Recommendations; 

-The business to immediately investigate and assess how the attitude of this worker is affecting female and male workers by talking with workers from all nationalities and genders while guaranteeing confidentiality and safeguards. 
. Based on the results of the investigation, the business should provide/clarify recommendations of proper behavior of employees to make sure workers do not feel uncomfortable and/or experience sexual harassment.  

Talking points; 

-What is the position of this worker? Is he assign to take photos? If yes, what is the purpose? Please note that workers should be given privacy while using the toilet, so this kind of behavior should not be acceptable. 


Time frame 1 week.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
18-may-2021

The business - HR mentioned that there are two locations of toilets at building A. One toilet is in the production
line and another one is upstairs. However, the business will investigate this matter and get back
to us. And they will emphasize and communicate with the workers about proper behavior and
use of the toilets and the no-sexual harassment policy.

The business ; 21-May-2021
All workers received training on personal hygiene, and GMP standards at the orientation, and refresh training annually.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Issue with the sexual harassment: Several workers reported sexual harassment being practiced by the production manager in different ways as following: 

Worker A;
It has been reported that he tends to offer Overtime and extra bonuses in exchange for date nights and  intimate relations and those women who decline his offer are being treated poorly. It has been reported that there was an Indonesian female worker who may have gone out for a date with him but later left the job. It is also reported by one of the aunties saying that her niece has gone out for night dating a couple of times with that manager ( Note: This information was shared by the Aunt of the girl who went out with this manager, however this aunt has recently left and is in Nepal at the moment). 

Worker B; 
There was also an incident where this manager dragged the stripe of a female worker's bra at the workplace. He uses very rude and unpleasant words with the workers if he is not happy with those particular workers. Words that he uses are ; comparing female workers' appearance and their private parts and saying that your private part looks like this and that based on your appearance. He also uses the word D**** when he verbally abuses workers. It is generally reported by male and female respondents saying that there are more than a couple of female workers (Nepalese and Indonesian) who went out with his manager already (second hand information). 

Worker C; 
He normally approaches naive workers and newly recruited workers. For those who do not speak Malaysian language, he will ask someone as a mediator. The mediator will communicate with the targeted client and a grab car will be sent to pick her up at the housing.  For those who speak the language, he will firstly ask for the phone number and start the conversation.


Taking Points 
- Does the business have policy on sexual harassment? If yes, when was the last time it was shared and communicated with all employees? 
- Has the business ever received issues on the sexual harassment? If yes, what was the action against the harasser? 


Recommendations

- The business shall conduct investigation to find out this issue and  workers that might have been impacted more. After the investigation, the business to make sure expectations of the victims are addressed. 
- The business shall make sure there is no retaliation against workers during and after the investigation. 
- The business shall check CCTV around the area where the offender works as part of investigation. 
- Issara to provide psycho social support to the workers if needed.

22 May, 2023. 
 Three workers updated Issara that they had already spoken with the business at the coffee shop and had the conversation about their experiences on the behavior of the manager. Workers were asked to provide any evidence they may have.

supplier_name: Daorae (Desa Sri Hartamas) Sdn Bhd, a Korean BBQ restaurant
description: Gender and/or sexual harassment
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client worked at a Korean BBQ restaurant located in KL Kepong Jalan Metro Perdana, which is one of fifteen branches of the restaurant chain. Out of the fifteen branches, this particular one was problematic. The restaurant has six Nepali and thirteen Burmese workers. The owner's son is abusive towards the Nepali workers, creating a hostile work environment. Issara is able to speak with two workers. They have been working for this employer for 10 months. They are all MoU workers. They are reporting as a group of 5 Nepali workers, but the client is quietly reporting. The client and the workers want to either be transferred to another branch under the same company or find employment in another company. The client has debts to pay and doesn't want to return to Nepal. The workers have a contract they made in Nepal, but the company made another contract which the client doesn't have and is unaware of its contents.
Following are the major issues reported by workers.

1) Document retention: Workers passports are held by the employer since they started their employment. The company also kept their passports and didn't provide them with worker ID cards (Jalan cards) or necessary documents. 

2) Restriction of Movement: The workers were not allowed to leave the premises, and this restriction also made it difficult for their friends to visit them.

3) Unfair suspension: Workers were frequently suspended for minor mistakes or even without any reason. During these suspensions, the company did not provide any food, and the workers were not allowed to go out and get their own. They were also denied access to basic amenities, like cooling fans, during these periods. One incident occurred when a friend of the client was suspended for simply asking a Burmese worker to clean a stain. The owner verbally abused him and kept him in detention (suspension) for 28 days. Throughout this time, the company did not provide any food or salary, leaving the workers in a dire situation. His friends attempted to provide food secretly, but they had to be cautious as the company would punish them if they were caught bringing in more substantial amounts of food or any food. 

Recently, the victim was suspended by the company for two months. During this period, he received no salary or food from the company. The suspension was a result of the employer demanding the victim to memorize the restaurant menu quickly.

If workers demand to change the employer, they are asked to work 4 months without pay and there are some workers who have accepted this situation as they could not bear the harsh working environment. 

4)Physical abuse: Physical assault includes being kicked, slapped on the face and belly, and having ears pulled. The employer even physically assaulted the client's genitals. Such harassment occurred almost daily and targeted everyone except.

5) Long working hours and incorrect payment: Workers have to work 14-15 hours a day. In return, they received a basic salary of 1500 RM and a 300 RM overtime allowance each month. 

6) Lack of Sick Leave: Even when the workers fell ill, they were forced to work, as the owner wouldn't allow them to stay in the hostel. 



Moreover, during salary payment time, the owner would abuse the workers and suspend them for minor mistakes. The owner often used the workers as a target for his frustrations, taking out his stress related to the business on them. Whenever the business is slow he will start abusing the worker for no reason.

remediation_business_steps_taken:
11-June-2021.Business response ID - 1255.

The business - The business responded that the workers are not happy to participate in skill training which is required by the buyers. The business said that they will conduct the investigation, however, gave an uncertain response about the recommended survey to access the collective response from the workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations; 
-To have open discussion sessions between  HR and workers to understand better what are the challenges being faced by workers and what is driving them to resign. During these discussions, the business is encouraged to share with workers what the business actions are to address these issues.
-The business could also conduct an internal survey to learn why workers want to resign and what can help them remain in Ladybird. Issara can help with the survey questionnaire. Surveys should be conducted in a confidential way where workers feel safe to share the issues that they are facing. 
-The business shall work on a plan to address the issues that are raised in the survey by the workers. 
-The business shall provide training to all supervisors including translators.
-The business shall revise the grievance channels that are meant for workers to raise their issues. The revision should focus on workers' confidentiality and the no retaliation policy. Workers have expressed their concern about raising issues with HR, out of fear of retaliation from their supervisors, therefore it is strongly recommended for the business to reinforce a no retaliation policy and make sure all supervisors are aware of the policy, follow it and face consequences if they commit any actions against such policy.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Added on (9,June,2021). This issue has also been dealt with under 792 and 1434.
Context: The issue with the pregnant workers being questioned about the frequency and the duration of their toilet breaks by the line supervisors whenever they request to use the toilet. 

Recommendations. 

-The business to make clear announcements to all pregnant workers and their supervisors about the business policy for taking breaks as needed without any pressure or questioning. 
-The business should also provide training to line supervisors regarding fair treatment for pregnant workers and how to respond to the different needs that come with pregnancy, such as the provision of chairs, use of toilets without restrictions, having rest breaks, and so on.  
-The announcements should also focus on no discrimination by nationality or gender and no bias treatment. 
-The business to introduce the focal person workers can reach if they have any issue that they want to raise. This should include the safeguard and confidentiality for their reported concerns.
-To maintain visibility of working conditions that is workers' voices driven, the business should have a regular follow-up system with the workers to make sure that the workers are using the grievance channels that are meant for them and the actions are being properly taken. 

Talking points. 

-Who is the focal point for the workers to reach out for their issues at the moment? 
-Have the business communicated about the confidentiality and no retaliation policy with the workers recently? Given several reports and the concerns that are raised by the workers, the business is suggested to re-communicate about the no-retaliation policy. 
-When and how did the business last introduce the focal person with workers? If it was a long time ago, the business is suggested to re-communicate with the workers to remind them so that they are aware of the channels and the focal person.

Issara checked with the worker and the worker also confirmed about the business response taking place.

description: Discrimination – by gender/nationality/ethnicity/other in the work area
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: the issue with the COVID-19 infection and workers being discriminated against nationalities. Workers reported the spread of the virus and increasing infected workers in the factory, therefore, the business practice bubble and seal measure and moved Burmese workers to the business dorm where the business agreed to provide three meals but workers have reported not received meals properly. In addition to that, the business provides different types of meals to different nationalities. It is added that the Thai workers receive bigger portions with meat and vegetables where Burmese workers are provided with only one piece of meat and soup with smaller portions.  Given the current bubble and seal policy, the business moved Burmese workers to the dormitory inside the factory but Thai workers are still commuting from their homes which creates the feeling of insecurity among Burmese workers to work along with the Thai workers, added by a worker. 


Recommendations: 
-The business to clearly communicate with the workers about the business plan to control the spread of the virus to a bigger number of workers in the factory and in the community.
-The business should also clearly communicate with the workers i) why they are being pushed to get back to work before completing the 14 days of quarantine, which is against the doctors’ recommendation, ii) what are the measures being taken by the business to make sure that those that have been exposed and in closed contact with positive cases do not spread the virus at the workplace if they are being asked to work before being able to confirm if they are positive or not. 
-The business should assign focal and introduce the vocals with the workers for the workers to reach out to them whenever they have questions and concerns related to COVID-19. 

Talking points:
-Is the business aware that the workers are being asked to get back to work before completing their 14 days of quarantine suggested by the doctor?  
-Workers reported being threatened of not receiving regular meals, not receiving wages for quarantine days, and even getting fired from work if they do not follow the business suggesting to get back to work before completion of 14 days of quarantine. What is the business understanding of this? 
-What has been the business action to control the number of impacted workers? 
-How many workers have been tested for COVID-19 so far and what is the testing process? 
-Are the COVID-19 regulation measures applied equally for Burmese and Thai workers, if not how so? According to the workers' report, there are different regulations for Thai, for instance, they have fewer restrictions of movement. This creates a feeling of insecurity among Burmese workers to work along with Thai workers who could have greater exposure to the virus. So what is the company policy, what is the plan to deal with these issues, and are the regulations applied equally for all workers?  


Please share the latest government announcement regarding Bubble and Seal measures. 

If the factory found a positive case for Covid,
They should notify the authority within 3 hours.
The public health authority will conduct a random test for 10% of their workforce (in the working station where the covid patient found and related working station).
The factory should do a deep cleaning and disinfecting the area
 If there are more than 5% positive cases found from the random test (10% of the workforce), or there is any risk of spreading to the neighboring community. The factory should implement the Bubble and Seals" measures.
For the Bubble and Seals, the factory shall do as follows:
preparing accommodation for workers in the factory, the workers who wish to continue working shall stay in the compound. They could not commute between their dormitory and factory. In the case where the factory provides accommodation to workers outside the factory compound, they shall provide the transport between accommodation and factory (sealed route).
set up organization quarantine/factory quarantine
set up field hospital or community isolation for the workers in the factory
The factory shall provide provisions (Food, essential goods, medicine, and medical equipment) and facilities to workers who stay in the bubble and seals.
6.	Failure to comply, may result in temporary shutdown and may be subject to a Maximum THB 100,000 fine or 1-year imprisonment, or both.
This order is effective since 4 Aug 2021

Source: 
https://covid.songkhla.go.th/files/com_announce/2021-08_62565c030491197.pdf

Additional guidelines for COVID prevention and response can be found in the “Guidance for Thai Companies: Care of Workers Affected by
COVID-19” some of the recommendations includes the following:
Keep workers informed
Ensure the correct timing for testing 
Ensure no discrimination
Ensure workers are properly paid during the quarantine period 
Ensure decent quarantine conditions 
Provide mental health support
remediation_business_steps_taken: The business has updated the shut down of the factory for five days to do the sterilization. Workers have updated receiving three meals during the shut down, however they are still concern to get back to work as they fear not receiving enough lunch based in their past experience and also being discriminated against nationalities. Workers added that they do are doing okay during the shut down as they do not have to see the different treatment by the business to different nationalities because only Burmese workers live inside the factory dorm. They added ongoing concern related to the insufficient lunch when the factory re-opened. Workers said that they can survive with the potion of meals provided by the business during the shut down because they do not have to work hard. However, when it comes to the working days, they do not feel enough with the portion and the types of curry and vegetables.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that the business has been practicing "bubble and seal" measures for only Burmese workers.  Bubble and seal measures are a Thailand government directive on approaching quaratine, testing and needed measures to prevent and contain COVID, which are deemed necessary at sites or areas with increasing or reported cases. Burmese workers have been moved to the business dorm inside the factory compound (from their other housing) and promised to be provided with three meals a day (as they are not in their regular housing), but Thai workers are still commuting to work as usual from outside (which is a violation of the bubble and seal policy). In addition to that, it is reported Burmese workers are receiving smaller portions of meals with a piece of meat and soup while Thai workers receive bigger portions with several types of curry, vegetables and meat.
remediation_action:
Issara has provided clear guidance on COVID testing, quarantine and prevention measures in Thai language to all employers, and discussed measures with suppliers.  The business said they are following government protocols for the "bubble and seal" measures to control the spread of Covid-19.

Issara had an escalation meeting with TU which was attended by K Prad, K Vorarat (corporate HR), K Supana (business partner in charged on TUS) to discuss these issues. 

TU responded that the Bubble and Seal measures apply to workers from all nationalities. For the provision of food, TU explained that the vendor prepares Thai food and Burmese food following migrant workers feedback of not liking the Thai food, but that the quality of the food is the same for all. However, workers reports about the quality of food are contradictory to the business response.
remediation_validation: Workers report that bubble and seal measures are not being conducted for all Thai workers, only Burmese workers.  Additionally, workers report the factory is providing higher quality food to Thai workers in the bubble and seal, and inferior food to Burmese workers.

Context: the issue with the COVID-19 infection and workers being discriminated against nationalities. -The business should also clearly communicate with the workers i) why they are being pushed to get back to work before completing the 14 days of quarantine, which is against the doctors’ recommendation, ii) what are the measures being taken by the business to make sure that those that have been exposed and in closed contact with positive cases do not spread the virus at the workplace if they are being asked to work before being able to confirm if they are positive or not.

-Is the business aware that the workers are being asked to get back to work before completing their 14 days of quarantine suggested by the doctor?

-What has been the business action to control the number of impacted workers? 
-How many workers have been tested for COVID-19 so far and what is the testing process? 
-Are the COVID-19 regulation measures applied equally for Burmese and Thai workers, if not how so? According to the workers' report, there are different regulations for Thai, for instance, they have fewer restrictions of movement.  If there are more than 5% positive cases found from the random test (10% of the workforce), or there is any risk of spreading to the neighboring community. The factory should implement the Bubble and Seals" measures.

preparing accommodation for workers in the factory, the workers who wish to continue working shall stay in the compound. They could not commute between their dormitory and factory. set up organization quarantine/factory quarantine
set up field hospital or community isolation for the workers in the factory

6.	Failure to comply, may result in temporary shutdown and may be subject to a Maximum THB 100,000 fine or 1-year imprisonment, or both.

remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business responses: 

Issue: Workers PR (processing) night shift said that the supervisor named "Morn" when the workers ask for sick leave, the supervisor does not allow it, but if it is a Thai workers, easier to allow.

cause/action: 
The HR conducted survey by randomly selected 8 workers at the night shift processing line where Pi Morn was the supervisor to ask if the supervisor had ever refused to allow workers to take sick leave. The workers were randomly given feedback that the supervisor never refused.

The HR department and the factory manager called the supervisor "Morn" to ask more questions. Khun Morn insists that he has never refused sick leave for both Thai and Burmese workers. He acknowledged the non-discrimination policy and considered approving leave according to the same rules for both Thai workers and Burmese workers.

However, in the case of some workers with taken sick leave often, Khun Morn would ask for more details about the sickness of the worker because he worried if the worker had chronic illnesses. 

HR trained all supervisors and they are communicated, taught, and emphasized on communication methods on how to communicate and treat workers appropriately and it has always been a matter that the company has given importance to. If the worker faces a case where the supervisor speaks badly, the worker can report the matter through the company grievance channels as usual.

Status: Done 
Responsibility: Production and HR
remediation_notes: A supervisor is discriminating against Burmese workers. She threatens the Burmese workers who take sick leave by telling them to go to the office to meet with the manager. However, she does not say anything to Thai workers who do the same.
remediation_action: Issara has raised this issue with the business, and the business investigated the matter.  The business found that the supervisor had not denied sick leave to any workers; however, for workers that were taking sick leave frequently, she asked detailed questions about their health condition out of concern that they might have a chronic illness.  The business has always placed great importance on training supervisors to communicate effectively with, and behave appropriately towards, the workers.
remediation_validation: Issara is following up with the workers given the business response

Recommendations for systems change
Conduct training for all line supervisors on the implementation of the company’s non-discrimination policy

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; The issue with a discriminative supervisor who discriminates against workers based on nationality and gender. Workers have reported that the supervisor discriminates in providing workload and breaks. The supervisor sometimes chases Burmese female workers to the toilet and asks them to hurry and also shout at them if they could not meet her demand. However, Thai workers and Burmese male workers will not be shouted at but are helped. Building 3. Line F21. Supervisor Name- P Par. 


Recommendations: 

-The business should immediately investigate this specific line supervisor. The investigation should include worker voice with the safeguard for the workers. The business should guarantee confidentiality during the investigation to avoid retaliation. 

-Based on the results of the investigation the business is recommended to take actions based on their policy, this could mean provide feedback to the supervisors, and/or verbal warning. In addition, it is recommended that the business provide training to supervisors on fair and ethical treatment towards all workers. 

The investigation result should be shared with the workers including the disciplinary action according to the business policy. 

-Workers should be treated fairly regardless of their nationalities and gender. Therefore, it is recommended for the business to reinforce a non-discrimination policy among line supervisors and workers to avoid this kind of situation. 

-The business to make sure that the workload is distributed fairly to all workers. 

-All workers should be able to access all their breaks as stipulated in the company policy and LPA.  

Talking Points; 
-Please share with the business the detail of the issue.
-Is the business aware of this issue? If yes, what was the action? If not, please provide Issara recommendations. 
-Workers reported that they are being discriminated against in distributing workload in the production line, How does the business make sure that all workers receive a fair workload? 


Time frame 2 weeks.
remediation_business_steps_taken: The business agreed to take action toward the specific supervisor. The business confirmed having done the communication on the following topics to make sure that workers are treated fairly. The business invited the supervisor for the meeting and communicated about fundamental rights of the workers in the workplace including no threat, no sexual harassment, no verbal abuses by the supervisors, rights and duties under LPA, rights of freedom of movement, rights for medical care and safe and standard workplace. Workers confirmed that in the investigation process, they were given chance to have a discussion and five workers (3 female and 2 male) were given chance to speak with the investigation team to present their issues. As a result, their supervisor's behavior has improved and workers confirmed having a happy working environment.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-Communicate with the workers about their rights when taking any breaks. The communication should include a no-discrimination policy. The business is suggested to have a zero-tolerance for discrimination in the workplace and abuse of power towards each other. 

-Issara can provide training to all line supervisors, translators, and HR if needed.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers from the Pla-Sud line reported about OT working hours not being informed in advance, workers not getting 20 minutes of breaks before starting OT hours, workload being discriminatively distributed against the nationality however, the worker did not give full consent to Issara to raise this issue with the business. 

Talking Points

-We understand that TU has a no retaliation policy that should be used to protect workers when they share their grievances through any channel. So we would like to learn more about TUF investigation processes whenever there is a case that is affecting workers on a small working line. 
-How would HR investigate a case, if the issue is connected to the line supervisors? How would sage guards be put in place to make sure workers on the small working line are not targeted or seen negatively by the supervisor or other employees? Can you please describe the process of investigation?
-When the business conducts an investigation involving a line supervisor, is the supervisor notified about the issue in that specific production line? Or how is that information handled?
-If workers have an issue from a small line but also have concerns about being retaliated by the supervisor, what is the business’s strategy to resolve such issues in such condition? 
-Has the TUF communicated about TUs no-retaliation policy to all workers and supervisors? If so, when and how? If not, any plan for that? 
Because workers express not being aware of the TUs’ no retaliation policy.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Since the worker did not give consent to share the issue with the business and it also has risks to share the name of the production line with the business as it is a small production with a small number of workers, Issara approached the business to learn about their process of investigation for such kind of issues where has risks for the workers being target by their supervisors as it is a small room. Issara checked with the business about their No Rataliaiton posily. The business responded that  No retaliation policy has been implemented since 2015, this was communicated to all workers in both Thai and Burmese languages. This is also emphasized in the annual training. Therefore, workers feel to raise their concern directly to HR. In addition to that, the business's external audit also has not found any issue with the compliance of the policy. The business added having different ways to conduct the investigation based on the issues. As the business response was not very clear for raised concern, the Issara team decided to escalate with the presentation with the Thai Union Groups team about the issues that need systemic improvement.

description: Discrimination – by gender/nationality/ethnicity/other in the work area
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that his line supervisor (P Skee, who has since already moved to another different line) was discriminating against Burmese workers by moving them temporarily (for a couple days to a week at a time) to go work in different lines where they are not familiar with the tasks being performed in those lines but the supervisor doesn't ask the Thai workers to do this.  The Burmese workers want to be able to work consistently in the line where they are familiar with the tasks and have become better at those tasks over time.  They don't want to be move around while Thai workers get to stay in the same line.

TPs:
-What is the company's practice in terms of placement of workers in various production lines?  Is there a schedule for moving workers around to different lines intentionally?  If so, what are the reasons for this?
-The practice of moving workers to work temporarily in a different line before returning to his/her usual line seems to be assigned to workers unevenly, with Burmese workers feeling like it is only happening to them while it is not being required of the Thai workers.  What are the reasons for this?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Investigate this matter to establish why workers and only Burmese workers are being moved around to different lines temporarily.  Check records of which lines workers worked in and the dates when workers were moved to different lines.  Interview Burmese workers to get their perspective on why they think this is affecting their work performance and feel as though the company is discriminating against Burmese workers.  Ensure worker safeguards according to TU's non-retaliation policy
-Take disciplinary action against the supervisor according to the investigation results and the company's disciplinary policy
-Communicate with all workers about the company's practice regarding assignment of workers to certain production lines and why workers may be working in different lines and explain clearly how this is NOT a discriminatory practice.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Root Cause:
From the investigation, the following facts were found.

Fried products production line There is a Khun Nui, Dept Manager, Khun Mook, assistant team leader position, and Khun Ski, a senior daily 1. worker position who works as an assistant supervisor for the night shift.
2. Worker allocation for each production line, depends on the daily production plan to meet the needs of customers.
3. The move of work points can occur from 2 situations:
3.1. There is no production plan in that production line. The workers will be moved to work at other lines throughout the job site, considering the suitability of manpower and skills/experience required for each production line.
3.2. There is a partial production plan. Some workers will be transferred to help at other points with the following criteria.
Groups of workers who require expertise or experience in working at that point will not be considered to move the work site, such as workers who are responsible for cleaning the production line area because, at the end of the work, there will be cleaning. This group of workers has the skills to understand the areas that need special care and have the knowledge and ability to use chemicals. And the workers who look at the product code, inspect the quality, and the workers who record the production information (Thai workers) This group of workers has skills in reading and writing, understanding the product code system, checking the quality before entering the frying machine, including being able to calculate the numbers in the production line.
For the other workers besides those groups, If the workers move to help with other work. Supervisors select the workers who have previous work and are able to perform the job so that workers can perform smoothly at the point of departure and earn special rewards. There Khun Ski is a supervisor to help the workers who move to other locations.

Corrective Action:
Supervisors communicate and clarified with the workers in order to gain further understanding of the reasons for moving the production line and various criteria for consideration.

description: Discrimination – by gender/nationality/ethnicity/other in the work area
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The issue with annual leaves not being approved for Burmese workers. Workers reported that two weeks ago the business announced to the workers that they can take their annual leave on 16 and 17 after the Songkran holiday but on Monday(5 Apr) the business announced that they only approved Thai workers leaves 5 workers per line. None of the Burmese workers' leaves are approved. 

Recommendations; 

-The business to revise the annual leave approved list and go through a fair process providing equal opportunities to take leave to workers regardless of their nationality. Since the business has explained to workers that due to production planning only 5 workers per line can take annual leave, the business is suggested to do a lucky draw among all workers that have summitted the leave request or come up with another solution to make the process fair to all workers. 

The business had suggested the workers take annual leaves on those days, so many Burmese workers already had a plan for the days off, therefore, it is important for the business to make a fair decision and give same opportunities to all workers (Thai and Burmese). 


Talking Points; 
-Why did the business first communicate to workers saying they could take leave on the 16-17th but now suddenly the business is saying only a limited number of workers can take leave per line (confirm whether it's 5 per line as reported by workers)?  Let the business know many workers have made plans already based on the business' original announcement. 
-Why is the business now limiting the number of workers that can take leave on the 16-17th to five per line?
-What is the business' selection criteria for who gets to take leave and why were only Thai workers approved for leave on the 16-17th? 
-Who made the decision to approve only Thai worker's leave? Is HR aware that only Thai workers' leave requests have been approved?

One day
remediation_business_steps_taken:
-Escalation call. The business response ID - 1262.

Issara had an escalation call with the business, the business responded not having such bias practice to approve workers' annual leave. However, the business to announce the non-discrimination policy (but not specify the past issue during Songkran), and coach supervisors on proper implementation of the policy moving forward.

description: Discrimination – by gender/nationality/ethnicity/other in the work area
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers annual bonus not being distributed fairly among different nationalities. Workers added that the business used to provide one month of annual bonus to all nationalities a few years ago, however since then the business has stopped the practice of providing one month of annual bonus to the foreign workers (Cambodian). Thai workers received one full salary at the end of the year unlike Cambodian workers. Workers used to approach the HR but they were told that this is the decision of the management to provide only to the local workers. 

Recommendations: 
The business to conduct an investigation to identify the root cause of the unequal distribution of the annual bonus. 
The business is recommended to treat all workers equally and bonuses are not granted based on nationality or gender. 

Talking Points: 
What is the business understanding on the issue and how bonuses are determined? 
Based on the workers' report, their fair distribution has been discontinued since a few years back, what was the reason for this? 
ETI: 
Goal: There should be no prejudicial assignment of any sort on the grounds of gender, ethnicity, nationality, race, religion, age, or appearance. Worker-reported discrimination should be treated as a legitimate workplace matter by HR and management.
Code: ETI Base Code 7.1. No discrimination in hiring, pay, training, promotion, etc.
Description: There is no discrimination in hiring, compensation, access to training, promotion, termination or retirement based on race, caste, national origin, religion, age, disability, gender, marital status, sexual orientation, union membership or political affiliation.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara has escalated this issue with the business, the business responded that according to the decision from the business management, the foreign workers are provided with the lower bonus than local workers. The business has not taken Issara recommendations to have equal distribution with all workers.

Issara has raised this issue with Nike given that the response from the Everest management was concerning for the reported issues, however, there was no clear response from the Nike team upon this case. Issara has requested the Nike team to have a try party call to discuss this issue  but Nike has not respond on request for several weeks.
remediation_notes: The issue with the workers annual bonus not being distributed fairly among different nationalities. The business used to provide an annual bonus (equal to a month's salary) to all nationalities; however, the workers noted that this annual bonus was discontinued a few years ago only for the foreign workers (Cambodian). Thai workers still received this annual bonus at the end of the year, unlike the Cambodian workers. Workers asked HR why this was the case but were told that this is a management decision to provide only to the local workers.
remediation_action:
This issue was escalated to the business management team.  The business to conduct an investigation and find out why the annual bonus is being paid out based on nationality.  

The business responded saying that due to Everest's policy of making decisions at the highest management level, Cambodian employees receive a lower bonus than Thai employees.  This is an inadequate response and no rationale has been provided as why bonuses are being determined based on nationality.
remediation_validation: Workers have not been contacted in this case as there has been no corrective action taken by the buisiness
remediation_results: We are closing this issue with a poor rating due to the business' lack of response.  It has only noted that the company's management has decided that Cambodian employees will receive a lower bonus than Thai employees.  Such a discriminatory practice based on nationality would be in violation of Nike's policies.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
The business should clearly communicate with all workers about the business plan to solve this issue and the plan for the future to avoid this from happening again. 
The business to introduce with the workers about the no-discrimination policy and revise in the workers mannual if required. 
Introduce or strengthen the business grievance mechanism and the focal point to whom workers can reach out whenever they have issues. Safeguards for using the grievance channel should be widely announced with the workers to make sure workers feel safe to use it. 
Issara can provide training to the HR staff and guide on implementing the policy if required.

description: Discrimination – by gender/nationality/ethnicity/other in the work area
closed_notes: We are closing this issue with a poor rating due to the business' lack of response.  It has only noted that the company's management has decided that Cambodian employees will receive a lower bonus than Thai employees.  Such a discriminatory practice based on nationality would be in violation of Nike's policies.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers annual bonus not being distributed fairly among different nationalities. Workers added that the business used to provide one month of annual bonus to all nationalities a few years ago, however since then the business has stopped the practice of providing one month of annual bonus to the foreign workers (Cambodian). Thai workers received one full salary at the end of the year unlike Cambodian workers. Workers used to approach the HR but they were told that this is the decision of the management to provide only to the local workers. 

Recommendations: 
The business to conduct an investigation to identify the root cause of the unequal distribution of the annual bonus. 
The business is recommended to treat all workers equally and bonuses are not granted based on nationality or gender. 

Talking Points: 
What is the business understanding on the issue and how bonuses are determined? 
Based on the workers' report, their fair distribution has been discontinued since a few years back, what was the reason for this? 
ETI: 
Goal: There should be no prejudicial assignment of any sort on the grounds of gender, ethnicity, nationality, race, religion, age, or appearance. Worker-reported discrimination should be treated as a legitimate workplace matter by HR and management.
Code: ETI Base Code 7.1. No discrimination in hiring, pay, training, promotion, etc.
Description: There is no discrimination in hiring, compensation, access to training, promotion, termination or retirement based on race, caste, national origin, religion, age, disability, gender, marital status, sexual orientation, union membership or political affiliation.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara has escalated this issue with the business, the business responded that according to the decision from the business management, the foreign workers are provided with the lower bonus than local workers. The business has not taken Issara recommendations to have equal distribution with all workers.

Issara has raised this issue with Nike given that the response from the Everest management was concerning for the reported issues, however, there was no clear response from the Nike team upon this case. Issara has requested the Nike team to have a try party call to discuss this issue  but Nike has not respond on request for several weeks.
remediation_notes: The issue with the workers annual bonus not being distributed fairly among different nationalities. The business used to provide an annual bonus (equal to a month's salary) to all nationalities; however, the workers noted that this annual bonus was discontinued a few years ago only for the foreign workers (Cambodian). Thai workers still received this annual bonus at the end of the year, unlike the Cambodian workers. Workers asked HR why this was the case but were told that this is a management decision to provide only to the local workers.
remediation_action:
This issue was escalated to the business management team.  The business to conduct an investigation and find out why the annual bonus is being paid out based on nationality.  

The business responded saying that due to Everest's policy of making decisions at the highest management level, Cambodian employees receive a lower bonus than Thai employees.  This is an inadequate response and no rationale has been provided as why bonuses are being determined based on nationality.
remediation_validation: Workers have not been contacted in this case as there has been no corrective action taken by the buisiness
remediation_results: We are closing this issue with a poor rating due to the business' lack of response.  It has only noted that the company's management has decided that Cambodian employees will receive a lower bonus than Thai employees.  Such a discriminatory practice based on nationality would be in violation of Nike's policies.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
The business should clearly communicate with all workers about the business plan to solve this issue and the plan for the future to avoid this from happening again. 
The business to introduce with the workers about the no-discrimination policy and revise in the workers mannual if required. 
Introduce or strengthen the business grievance mechanism and the focal point to whom workers can reach out whenever they have issues. Safeguards for using the grievance channel should be widely announced with the workers to make sure workers feel safe to use it. 
Issara can provide training to the HR staff and guide on implementing the policy if required.
systems_change_business_steps_taken: None

description: Discrimination – by gender/nationality/ethnicity/other in the work area
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1:
Harsh treatment and verbal abuse of Burmese workers: Burmese workers at Mango Line are being discriminated against, with line supervisors yelling at the Burmese workers when they take toilet breaks, saying “why are you taking so long?” or "why do you use the toilet so often”. At the same time, Thai and Lao workers are not verbally abused in this way. 

Case #2: 
The Burmese workers reported that certain bonuses and incentives are paid only to Thai workers. They used to get the annual bonus like Thai workers many years ago but not anymore. Thai workers also get a 500 baht diligence incentive (full attendance) every 15 days. Non-Thai workers do not get the privilege.

Recommendations for remediation:
- Investigate line supervisor behavior towards workers; ensure workers provide input and there are safeguards in place to protect workers from retaliation
- Take disciplinary measures against supervisors that have discriminated against Burmese workers based on their nationality
- Review the company’s bonus & incentive system and ensure that any bonus and incentive pay is the same to workers regardless of nationality
- Communicate to all workers and clarify the company’s bonus and incentive system
remediation_business_steps_taken:
discrimination by nationality:  (Case #1) harsh treatment and verbal abuse to Burmese workers; (Case #2) bonus and incentives paid only to Thai workers (This #2 secluded to CD to discuss with SFP MD) 

Business Response: 10 June 2022

K. Sophon stated that the annual bonus will be provided for the full-time employees only, not the MoU workers who have a contract period. He will share the policy of benefit for employees. The company communicated to all workers through the migrant representative (the company set this position for employer-employee communication) regarding the annual bonus. For the diligent allowance, he’s not so sure, he will check and get back to us. For the supervisor's behavior, he will investigate and get back to us.


Business Response: 22 June 2022,
K. Sophon responded that the workplace environment is too loud sometimes. The supervisors might talk louder than normal but it’s not verbally abusive. And different supervisors’ personalities have different styles but anyway it’s not verbally abusive. K. Supreeraya added that she’s aware of this issue before and the investigation result is that it’s not verbally abusive but because the production line is noisy and some supervisors might speak loudly. The action has been conducted, HR conducted the employer-employee communication with supervisors.

At the same time, Thai and Lao workers are not verbally abused in this way. 

Case #2: 
The Burmese workers reported that certain bonuses and incentives are paid only to Thai workers. They used to get the annual bonus like Thai workers many years ago but not anymore. Thai workers also get a 500 baht diligence incentive (full attendance) every 15 days. Non-Thai workers do not get the privilege.
remediation_action:
Case #1:
The business responded that the workplace environment is very loud and so the supervisors need to sometimes talk louder than normal but it’s not verbally abusive. And different supervisors have different personalities but again, it’s not verbally abusive. 

Case #2:
The business noted that the annual bonus is provided for full-time employees only, not the MoU workers who have a contract period. He will share the policy of benefit for employees. The company communicated to all workers through the migrant representative regarding the annual bonus.

Issara is planning to visit and meet with the business HR in-person but the business has yet to agree to a visit.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change
- Update or draft the non-discrimination policy and implementation guide to ensure that all supervisors treat workers equally and don’t discriminate based on nationality, gender, etc.
- Ensure there is a non-retaliation policy and workers safeguard measures are in place so workers can raise their voices without fear of punishment
