description: Discrimination – by gender/nationality/ethnicity/other in the work area
Discrimination – by gender/nationality/ethnicity/other in the work area
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers are reporting that they are being treated worse than the Thai workers. When they take annual leave or sick leave, the department head won't say anything to the Thai workers. But when the Myanmar workers take leave, the department head will ask many questions about why they had been absent and saying that if they took leave frequently, they would not be given OT hours or future leave would be unpaid. She also speaks nicely to Thai workers but shouts at the Myanmar workers.

Recommendations:
- Supervisors should treat workers under their supervision equally, without being perceived as discriminating against a certain group of workers
- Conduct an investigation, and take disciplinary measures as per the company's disciplinary policy. Ensure worker safeguards
- Train the department heads and supervisors on proper equitable treatment of workers, with zero tolerance against discrimination of any kind
remediation_notes: When the workers take annual leave or sick leave, the department head won't say anything to the Thai workers but with the migrant workers, she will ask many questions about why they had been absent and saying that if they took leave frequently, they would not be given OT hours or future leave would be unpaid. She also speaks nicely to Thai workers but shouts at the migrant workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- Conduct regular (annual) performance appraisals of those in supervisory roles; develop improvement plans for those that need it and track performance improvement over time.
- Review the non-discrimination policy and procedures; regularly train supervisors on this

remediation_business_steps_taken:
KPI 2070 and 1626: on 16 October 2023, BHR called to follow up with Khun Krit. He has done the investigation in the cutting line and he insisted that there's no such case happened in the cutting line. On 30 September, he did the training on sick leave and leave in general, as well as, employer-employee communication, to all the line supervisors and conducted a special session with line supervisors in the cutting line. None of the supervisors had ever asked the workers to show a medical certificate for sick leave before. Often times when the workers want to take sick leave, the line supervisors give permission to all cases. None of the line supervisors accepted that they shouted at the workers or made the workers felt like they are servants.
He said he knows the worker who reported the issue but he didn't get a chance to talk to that worker. But he just talked to all the line supervisors in the cutting line. There're just a few line supervisors in that line. None of them accepted that such case ever happened. Khun Krit is happy to conduct further investigation and talk to the worker. BHR will follow up with him again at the end of this week.

20 Oct 2023: Khun Krit investigated yesterday by talking to 5 Myanmar workers in the cutting line one by one in his office, including the one he thinks has reported the issue. He asked questions like, "Have any of the supervisors ever made you feel like a servant?", "Do you feel like doing excessive work?", or "Have you ever been asked to show a medical certificate by a supervisor before?".  Everyone said no even when Khun Krit confirmed that they won't be targeted or there won't be any threats or retaliation against them. So I told him that we would have our O&E officer validate with the workers.
remediation_notes: When the workers take annual leave or sick leave, the department head won't say anything to the Thai workers but with the migrant workers, she will ask many questions about why they had been absent and saying that if they took leave frequently, they would not be given OT hours or future leave would be unpaid. She also speaks nicely to Thai workers but shouts at the migrant workers.
remediation_action: The business will investigate the matter, ensuring workers are safeguarded. In terms of the leave policy, the business said it makes verbal announcements to explain the policy to workers on a regular basis and also has put up the written announcement in five locations throughout the factory.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- Conduct regular (annual) performance appraisals of those in supervisory roles; develop improvement plans for those that need it and track performance improvement over time.
- Review the non-discrimination policy and procedures; regularly train supervisors on this

description: Discrimination – by gender/nationality/ethnicity/other in the work area
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported for the past couple months, they have not been given OT hours, with the manager citing a lack of orders but when there is OT, it is not given to Bangladeshi workers but given to Nepali and Myanmar workers.  The business also force them to meet daily targets which have been increased. When workers raise the issue of these increased targets, the employer will tell them they can leave and go back to Bangladesh if they can't keep up.

NOTE: The worker would like Issara to raise this issue with the business but doesn't want his identity to be disclosed.

Recommendations for the employer: 
- The employer should communicate clearly to workers about the production demands and the forecast for OT hours in the coming months. 
- The employer should clarify that daily targets are not tied to the daily wage. Workers are to be paid per 8-hour shift as per the contract, whether or not targets are met. Any time worked beyond the 8-hour period should be paid as OT.
- The employer should have an equitable and non-coercive OT system that doesn't favor workers from any nationality over another. Communicate how OT hours are offered to workers to show that it is fairly distributed and non-discriminatory
remediation_notes: Workers reported for the past couple months, they have not been given OT hours, with the manager citing a lack of orders but even when there is OT, it is not given to workers from one country but given to workers from other countries.  The business also force them to meet daily targets which have been increased. When workers raise the issue of these increased targets, the employer will tell them they can leave and go back home if they can't keep up.

-Clearly explain and communicate the findings to the workers.
-Take disciplinary action against those responsible for this issue.

description: Discrimination on workloads and assignments
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Kyi Kyi is a worker from F Food-6 working line (new building) and she is currently working on a day shift. According to Kyi Kyi, there are 26-28 workers in her working line. Some days approximately 13-15 workers of F Food-6 have to work in the store room. When it comes to OT allocation, almost all of the workers got OT except 3 workers including herself. On the day, the 13-15 workers have to go to the store room and get a minimum of 3.5 hours OT. Those who remain in the original line ( approximately 10-11 workers) often get OT like 3 hours of OT. However, she and her two friends seldom got OT. On a weekly basis, she and her 2 friends got maximum 6 hours of OT in a week while others got minimum 18 hours of OT. Kyi Kyi added that there are two main people who manipulate ( may be discriminated against) 3 workers in terms of allocation OT. They are her line-supervisor Ms.Pho and her line-leader Kay Thi Aung. These line-supervisor and line-leaders hate Kyi Kyi for contacting Issara and mobilizing workers for Issara training and they hate the other two workers for not buttering them up. So they don't give these 3 workers OT opportunity as much as they gave to other line-workers. When it comes to the assigned job, Kyi Kyi always assigned for heavy tasks ( even in the time she just came back from her maternity leave) such as; washing big tray and putting the heavy tray onto the cart of shelf. And the line-leader Kay Thi Aung is always complained about her performance and find her fault.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker in a production line for descaling and deboning fish reported that they work as a team of 8, with one descaling while the other 7 debone. There are around 30 Thai and Burmese workers in the "sin-tike" production line where workers have to set up the bobbin in the machines. They get regular OT from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. almost every day but the supervisor provides extra OT hours on top of that from 8:00 to 10:00 p.m. and work on Sundays for double pay to only 7-8 workers. This has been happening for over a year, and the workers want the supervisor to distribute the OT hours and double-pay work broadly to the whole group rather than just to the 7-8 workers.

NOTE: Several workers called Issara about this same issue

TPs:
- What is the business' OT policy and maximum working hour cap per week?  Ask for the written policy regarding OT.
- How is OT work offered to workers, based on what criteria?

Recommendations:
- OT hours should be offered to workers fairly, without discrimination or on a preferential basis
- Investigate the matter, with worker safeguards. The business to make it clear to the supervisor not to target the workers after this investigation. Check HR records of OT hours worked, by worker.
- If the supervisor has been offering OT hours preferentially and unfairly, discipline the supervisor according to the company's disciplinary policy.
- Communicate to workers, verbally and in writing, the business' method of offering OT hours to workers and explain the fairness of the method
remediation_notes: There are around 30 Thai and Burmese workers in a production line where workers have to set up the bobbin in the machines. They get two OT hours almost every day but the supervisor provides two extra OT hours on top of that and work on Sundays for double pay to only 7-8 workers. This has been happening for over a year, and the workers want the supervisor to distribute the OT hours and double-pay work broadly to the whole group rather than just to the 7-8 workers.
remediation_action: Issara raised this issue with the business, and HR wanted to get more specific information from Issara about in which line this was taking place to be able to investigate the matter. HR said the OT policy is maximum of 12 OT hours per week and maximum of 3 days per week, meaning this would be 4 OT hours for 3 days per week.
remediation_validation: A worker updated Issara saying that on June 6, 2023, around 8:30 a.m., a director and the interpreter had already visited the production line and met with the workers, asking about the overtime. After that, the director asked the supervisor to provide OT fairly to all the workers equally from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. only. The workers would like to say thanks to the director for coming and listening to their voices, and they are happy and satisfied.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- Ensure that the business has a clear policy on OT work, which provides a fair system for offering OT hours to workers without discrimination or preferential treatment.
- Ensure that the business trains supervisors on proper implementation of the OT policy so that they do not abuse their position of authority

description: Discrimination on workloads and assignments
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Ms.Mae Nu and Ms. Hnin from GFPT called to report the issues happening in GFPT Pae Lu Section Myanmar cleaning workers. She reported that Pae Lu section are located on two different floors, it is 2nd and 4th Floor of GFPT main building. There are altogether 80 Myanmar cleaning workers out of 130 cleaning workers for these Pae Lu Sessions (for day/ night shifts). When it comes to the workload and assignments, the chief line-supervisor of Pae Lu Session usually assign Myanmar workers to work the difficult and tiring jobs but not to Cambodian and Thai workers. For example, Myanmar workers are assigned to work toilet cleaning tasks, drain cleaning tasks while other nationals are assigned to clean the production floor. When Myanmar workers can't take the assigned tasks anymore, they approached the chief line-supervisors and asked to assigned other tasks, the chief line-supervisor asked the Myanmar workers " Would you like to take my role of giving tasks to workers?  then wear my caps and write down your name in the assignment tracker by yourself for what tasks you are willing to do". The workers regard this as power abuse and humiliating the workers According to these two workers, there are 3-4 Myanmar workers in 2023 who had to sign the warning for negotiation over the assigned tasks.

TPs:
- What are the cleaning tasks in the Pae Lu section? Are they tasked to do "cleaning" for the whole shift or is this something they do for a certain portion of their work shift? Of the 130 workers tasked with "cleaning duties", how are the tasks assigned to workers and by whom?
- Is HR aware that Myanmar workers are given the more difficult tasks while the Cambodian and Thai workers get the easier tasks?

Recommendations:
- Investigate this mater; identify how tasks are allocated and assigned among the workers assigned cleaning duties. 
- Communicate to workers clearly about how cleaning tasks are allocated to workers, and demonstrate that the assignments are done "fairly" without discrimination by nationality of the worker
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 6 Nov 2023

K. Sarayuth, Human Resources focal, and K Rungnapa, Employee Relations Dept. They explained that the GFPT 'Hygiene Department' handles all cleaning tasks. They were unaware of the situation, so they must investigate the workers' assignment to this department. They will also communicate clearly to the workers about how cleaning tasks are assigned fairly. They will send the corrective action by the end of next week.

DATE: 16 Nov 2023

K. Sarayuth shared the statement from the investigation as follows.
The Health Department follows the Business Ethics Code Guidelines. It is carried out with integrity and sincerity. Do not discriminate against workers because of their race, religion, gender, marital status, or physical disability. Cleaning and keeping the bathroom clean workers of Thai and Cambodian nationality are also performing such work. There are no green books or other documents at the health department. which requires work to be signed at each work point. The Health Department arranges for work to be allocated and assigned to workers based on worker knowledge, ability, and suitability.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that workers from one nationality are assigned the difficult cleaning duties while the workers from other nationalities get the easier cleaning tasks. They feel the supervisor is discriminating against them in terms of the tasks assigned to them.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Have a clear non-discrimination policy and train all supervisors and workers on how this is implemented in practice
next_description: validate with the workers.

description: Unfair dismissal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A Cambodian worker went to the smoking area during the break time where he noticed that a power bank charger had been left there.  Thinking it belonged to one of his Cambodian co-workers, he took it and left it in his locker to return it to the owner later.  A few hours after, he received a call from HR asking him to sign the resignation letter. HR told him that he was being dismissed for stealing the power bank. He responded that he had no intention to keep this power bank but to return it to its owner because he thought that it belonged to one of the Cambodian workers. But HR still forced him to sign.

Talking points:
-What is the company policy for immediate dismissal without first giving a warning?
-Did the company investigate the matter properly and establish why the worker had taken the power bank?
-Is HR aware that the worker intended to return it to its owner and he thought he was helping the owner out by keeping it safe until after work?

Recommendations:
-Investigate the matter fully, making sure to interview the worker that took the power bank and says he intended to find the owner and return the power bank to him/her
-Consider canceling the dismissal and keeping this worker on as an employee
remediation_business_steps_taken: An officer from the Purchasing Department received the call and mentioned that please contact K. Ann, HR Manager now she is on leave and will be back Oct 13. So please call again.

description: Unfair dismissal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Ms.Nyein Lae Maw,from TUF fish peeling line reported that she and her colleague, Sandar Cho were unfairly dismissed on 29th August 2023. On 28th August Ms Nyein and Ms. Sandar were assigned to work as a pair in fish peeling tasks. In the nature of fish peeling tasks, the pair (two workers) usually have to do deboning and removing blood. For the morning session (before lunch), Nyein finished 18 kilos while Sandar finished only 9 kilos. In the afternoon like 1pm the office called both of them and asked the reason for the unrealistic kilo difference. The workers explained that this is the very first time for them that much kilo difference but they didn't do it intentionally and they can balance their work done in the afternoon session but the business didn't accept their explanation and accused them that the worker did the job unethically and deceitfully. On 29th August, both of them were dismissed. In this matter the workers thought that they were unfairly dismissed because they have never got warning nor never sign any warning letter for this type of mistake.

TPs:
- Two workers were recently dismissed.  What is the reason for the dismissal?  Is it according to the company's disciplinary policy and were there fair grounds for immediate dismissal, since these workers had not received warnings in the past?

Recommendations:
- Investigate this issue, and establish the reasons for the dismissal.
- Explain clearly to the workers why the company took such actions, if indeed there were clear grounds for immediate dismissal
- If the reasons for dismissal are not sufficient to merit immediate dismissal, the company hire the workers back immediately
remediation_business_steps_taken: K. Varrorat, HR manager, responded that they were unaware of this issue. She requests more information, asking if Issara can provide a specific production line number because the fish peeling ling is a large area, as well as the impacted two workers' ID numbers. They will, however, investigate and respond with corrective action within 7 working days.
remediation_notes: Two workers reported being dismissed for something that the business said was unethical but they couldn't understand exactly they had done wrong. In addition, they had not received any warnings previously so they don't understand what they could have done to deserve immediate dismissal.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Review the company's disciplinary policy, and review how this is communicated to all workers.  This should be communicated, verbally and in writing, on a regular basis to refresh workers on what actions on their part can lead to disciplinary actions and in some cases to dismissal.

remediation_action:
Issara raised this with the business, and the HR manager was unaware of this issue. She requested more information, such as the production line number because the fish peeling section is a large area, as well as the impacted two workers' ID numbers. They will, however, investigate and respond with corrective action within 7 working days.

In the latest update, the business noted that workers working in pairs have been instructed to report equal number of fish trays processed as this affects the worker's performance and related incentives. In this instance, one worker reported 6 trays while the other reported only 1 tray, because the worker reporting only 1 tray was away from work for many days and so wouldn't be getting much in terms of incentives. The business sees this as workers trying to manipulate the numbers fraudulently to increase one's incentive pay, which the business decided is a serious offense meriting immediate dismissal

In the country escalation, the business noted that it will re-investigate this case and reconsider the decision to dismiss the workers.  Based on the investigation, the company confirmed that there had been communication to workers in April 2023 (which the workers acknowledged and signed) that not equally sharing the number of trays completed would result in immediate dismissal, and checked with workers to make sure they understood this policy in September 2023, which they said they understood.  The business will not change its decision to dismiss these workers but will have additional communication sessions with workers about this policy so that workers are reminded that non-compliance can lead to immediate dismissal.
remediation_validation:

description: Unfair dismissal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
To immediate investigate the reasons why the workers was dismissed. The investigation should be conducted ethically taking into account safeguards for the worker. The investigation should aim to understand why the worker was dismissed and if the business policy and buyer CoC were followed. The investigation should include workers voice. 

If it is found to be a case of unfair dismissal the business should compensate the worker according to the Thai labour law or hire the worker back and compensate her for the days she did not receive payment (if that was the case). The reintegration to the workplace depends on the workers desire to do so (and the business willingness). In any of the cases, the worker should be compensated. 


A severance pay will have to be paid to the employee when he/she is dismissed without any reason. The severance pay is based on the duration of the employment according to Section 118 of the labour protection act. In addition to the severance pay, the employer would have to pay compensation for not informing the worker before 1 payment period as stipulated on the LPA. In this case, it would be 1 month of salary in addition to the severance pay.

description: Unfair dismissal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The issue with a worker being dismissed after being abused by his leader. 

Recommendations for remediation
To immediately investigate the reasons why the workers were dismissed. The investigation should be conducted ethically, taking into account safeguards for the worker. The investigation should aim to understand why the worker was dismissed and if the business policy and buyer CoC were followed. The investigation should include workers' voice, this includes 1) talking with the workers involved in a safe environment where workers can talk freely, 2)witness - other workers that were present when the events occurred, and 3) check the CCTV. 

If it is found to be a case of unfair dismissal the business should consider re-hiring the worker.

Or if the business decides not to hire the worker and this is a case of unfair dismissal, the company should pay severance pay to the impacted employee. The severance pay is based on the duration of the employment according to Section 118 of the labor protection act. In addition to the severance pay, the employer would have to pay compensation for not informing the worker before 1 payment period as stipulated on the LPA. In this case, it would be 1 month of salary in addition to the severance pay.

-Also note that physical assault is a violation of criminal law:
Thai Criminal Code B.E. 2499 (1956), Section 391: Attack on Another. Any person who commits a forcible attack against another shall, if the attack is not serious to the extent causing the victim to sustain any bodily or mental harm, be liable to imprisonment for not more than one month, or a fine not exceeding 1,000 Baht or both.


Talking points; 

Please share the detail of the story ( and ask the following questions. 

-Is HR aware of this issue? If yes, was there any investigation conducted, by whom, and what were the results of the investigation? 
-Who decided to dismiss the worker that was physically assaulted?
-Who has the power to immediately dismiss the workers? Does the production manager have the power to dismiss the workers? 
-What is the business policy on immediate dismissal.

-What is the business's policy for such cases, when there is a working physical assaulted by another worker? 
According to the impacted worker, his leader assaulted him physically and he did not hit him back, so why did the company decided to dismiss him?

- Ask the business not to report the dismissal of this worker to DOE until there is a clear investigation and the company can guarantee that the company policies, buyers' CoC, and workers' rights are followed.


Added talking points (10 Feb 2021)

What was the investigation result? 
What has the business done to prevent such issues in the future? Any communication? 
Is there any destined committee to conduct the investigation for such cases?

-Is having snacks at the production line a cause for immediate dismissal? Is there no first or second warning policy before dismissal? 
-If immediate dismissal is not the business policy or if the policy hasn’t been clearly communicated, the business should consider rehiring workers back or paying compensation for unfair dismissal. Note for BHR. 
-Please explain to the business that the worker cannot return back to Cambodia due to border closure. Therefore, the business is suggested to ethically consider for the worker during this time if it was the worker's fault.  

Talking points; Please share the details of the story ( and ask the following questions). 

-Is HR aware of this issue? If yes, was there any investigation conducted, by whom, and what were the results of the investigation? 
-What is the business policy for immediate dismissal? How are these policies being communicated with the workers? 
-What are the actions that lead to the immediate dismissal? Can the business share that policy with Issara? 

-Ask the business not to report the dismissal of this worker to DOE until there is a clear investigation and the company can guarantee that the company policies, buyers' CoC, and workers' rights are followed.
-If there was any investigation that has taken place, what was the investigation result? What has the business done to prevent such issues in the future? Any communication? 

Time frame within 1 day.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
06/25/2021 (ID - 1288).
Issara reached out to the business to raise the issue, the business responded that the worker was not fired, however since the worker broke the business COVID-19 policy, she has received a warning letter. The supervisor who told the worker was fired received the communication about the grievance process that needs HR approval for any action. Issara has checked with the workers and the worker has confirmed getting back to work.

description: Unfair dismissal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A worker, San Lwin Oo from Cal-Comp(Petchaburi), Factory 10, Line FATP-3, ID - C17 C708 was caught smoking in the toilet on 23rd March. And the next day, he was brought to HR Office and had to sign warning letter. On that day when he checked with HR staff if the paper he signed is warning letter or dismissal letter, the HR staff clearly stated that it is just warning letter. So the worker tried to go back and work to his line but unfortunately, the foreman said that he is not allowed to work and asked him to go back home. After that the sub-recruiter ( 1-PS) brought him home and take his photo of passport and said it is for resigning from job. Since then he is not allowed to go work. According to the worker, smoking is not a major offences that worthy to dismiss according to cal-comp policy. 

Recommendations for remediation 
-Clarify the status of the worker.  Has he been dismissed?  Under what grounds?  Is smoking grounds for immediate dismissal according to company policy?   Has he been issued a warning?  Why has he not been permitted to return to work?
-If there was a miscommunication between HR and the foreman, conduct an investigation as to why this happened.
-Communicate clearly with the worker about his status, whether it is a dismissal or a warning
-If he was given a warning but mistakenly kept from returning to work, the business should immediately inform him to return to work and pay for the wages of the days he wasn’t allowed to work.
-If he was dismissed in compliance with company disciplinary policy, it is suggested that the business issue him with a job changeable cancellation letter in order to help the work to be able to find a new employer in Thailand 


Talking points; Please share the details of the story ( and ask the following questions). 

-When the worker was called to the HR office, he was informed that he was receiving a warning and was asked to sign the written warning.  Is HR aware that the foreman communicated a different message saying he was dismissed and did not allow him to return to work since March 23rd?  Why was there a discrepancy in the communication provided by HR and the foreman?
-What is the business policy for immediate dismissal? Is smoking in the toilet grounds for immediate dismissal? How are these policies being communicated with the workers? 
-What is the current status of the worker?  Has he been dismissed?  If so, what has HR communicated to the worker? 
-Ask the business not to report the dismissal of this worker to DOE until there is a clear investigation and the company can guarantee that the company policies, buyers' CoC, and workers' rights are followed.
-If there was any investigation that has taken place, what was the investigation result? What has the business done to prevent such issues in the future? Any communication? 

Time frame within 1 day.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the business, the CSR team member who joined the meeting was not aware of this issue, the business agreed to conduct the investigation and get back to us.

CSR, shared the findings of the investigation, which revealed that, according to the rules and regulations, the workers smoked in the bathroom, which is near to the storage of flammable materials or objects containing fuel. And this worker was aware that this area was restricted previously. So this is a very serious case, and the disciplinary action is dismissal, according to the disciplinary measure.

Issara is checking with the business.

description: Unfair dismissal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker called to say that he was dismissed for one incident where he was due to work the night shift but left after a few hours (he went for a dinner break then fell asleep for several hours and decided to go home). The next day, the HR manager asked him to come for an 8am meeting but he missed the meeting as he only went there at 10am. He went to the office again at 5pm and the HR interpreter asked whether he had gotten drunk and asked why he had missed work so he explained what happened. He was dismissed for the reason that he had been absent from work very often. The worker thinks this is unfair because in the past, whenever he needed to be absent from work, he had sought permission from the line supervisor but it was the supervisor that had not approved his request. 

TPs:
- What is the reason for this worker's dismissal?
- Has he received a warning about being absent in the past?
- What is the company's disciplinary policy for this kind of offence (being absent from work)? Is it verbal warning, written warning, suspension, and then dismissal?

Recommendations:
- Workers should be disciplined according to the company's disciplinary policy; he should be issued a verbal warning, written warning, suspended, and then dismissed, not dismissed immediately without having previously received such previous warnings
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 15 Feb 2024

K. Yaowapa (Gae) HR, explained that the worker's behavior is not good. He used to pee in the locker area. He slept 00.30-3.00 am. on the night of 2 Feb until the morning of 3 Feb. On the same day, he slept on the soccer field. He also took a lunch break longer and came to work not on time. When HR inquired he said he worked normally not take a nap or break longer. But the CCTV showed him sleeping. He said that he just took a nap not a serious issue. HR investigated and interviewed the coworkers and found out that this worker also got drunk often. HR appointed him to meet at 8 am and he missed the appointment. First, HR gave a verbal warning and then he still did not improve so tried to give me a written warning but he didn't sign and admit. He just only said to HR 'You wanna fire me' He defied HR and He didn't want to improve his behavior.

Reasons for dismissal
1. He lies and not admitted and he chooses to not listen and understand
2. This impact on the production capacity and the business
3. He got drunk and worked often.
4. He refuses to admit and sign the warning letter according to the disciplinary 
5. He had a chance to come to explain but he missed the appointment
6. He defied HR and refused to improve his behavior
Note: HR communicates through the interpreter and he also can understand the Thai language.

Timeline:
On 5 Feb, he got a verbal warning about the he slept during working time.

description: Unfair dismissal
remediation_issara_recommendation: Workers were asked to resign without severance pay. The main issue is that workers are terminated without having a documented extension and no severance pay.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that various groups of workers were asked to resign from their jobs without receiving any severance pay.
remediation_action: After pressure from the Strategic Partners, Issara was able to meet with SFP HR at the Bangkok Headquarters.  HR explained that migrant workers were hired as MOU workers or walk-in workers with different contract end dates. At the end of a migrant worker's contract, the business considered whether the contract can be extended as per Thai government regulations and also whether the worker's performance was satisfactory. If the contract could not be extended because of the government regulations or because of poor performance, the business considered this as separation at the end of a contract and not as a dismissal and was not obligated to provide severance pay.  Subsequently, the labor case was brought by the workers, and the out-of-court settlement was for the business to pay severance to the workers, in the amount of 20,000 Baht for each worker.

supplier_name: (SKP -BP) Syarikat Sin Kwang Plastic Industries Sdn. Bhd. (BP Plant)(18591-D)
description: Unfair dismissal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A group of workers which includes 28 of them reported being dismissed unfairly by the business without prior notice. They added that in that group, they have workers in different document types, some of them have been there as a regular MoU, and others were recruited under the “Recalibration program”. The business informed workers about their dismissal on the 21st of September and asked them to stop working starting from 22 September and be ready to be repatriated on the 30th. Workers found it very challenging to be repatriated as they were not prepared to do so and they had no idea about their documents. Workers who were recruited under the MoU process reported their documents not being provided by SKP for a year or more for some workers, and other workers who were recruited under the recalibration program reported having to provide their documents to the SKP since they arrived till now. 

Specific case about Thandar Linn. 
Worker name - Thandar Linn (ID 505554)
HR name - Ms. Fienaz
There is a specific worker who approached Issaara for a specific investigation of her case as follows. She was recruited under the recalibration program in November 2021, 11 months from now. Since her arrival to the SKP, she was given an employment contract and told that her document will be processed for legalization. Since then, she was never asked to do neither medical checkups or fingerprints. She was suspected to the business not having done anything to her document for the extension. When she arrived to the factory, she had a valid passport, visa, and 5 months of WP. If she was dismissed before her work permit expired, she would had returned back to her previous employer. When she was informed about her dismissal by the SKP HR (Ms. Fienaz), she asked what was the reason for her dismissal, Ms. Fienas replied that it was because of the delay from the business side to submit her documents for the legalization process. Because of this poor management of the HR, worker feel very upset and is not completely ready to return back as her place in Myanmar is not a safe zone given the political situaiton. Worker added there are many more workers in the same situation which she wants the business to stop doing this. She has decided to continue staying in Malaysia regardless of her document status. HR provided her passport yesterday and she is waiting for her salary. After that, she will leave SKP’s housing. 



Talking Points; 

-Given SKP’s previous reasons that there are 28 workers who were dismissed and in a plan to repatriate, can we get the detail of the workers who are being repatriated? 

-Which nationalities, how many workers were recruited under RP, and how many under the MoU process? What were the reasons specifically? If blacklisted, for what reasons? 

-What is the business understanding of the Thandar Linn case? She was told by Ms. Feinas that it was the delay from the HR side. If that is the reason, it is unfair for her as it was not a mistake from her side but from the business. In Issara’s opinion, this worker deserves compensation according to Malaysian law. What is the business understanding? 

As it was previously mentioned there are 138 workers who were in the process of appealing, what is the status and possible outcome for them?

Recommendations; 

-Individual workers are to be clearly communicated about their dismissal with written proof. 
-Those who were dismissed because of poor management from the business side should be considered for compensation equal to one month's salary according to contract clause No. 19 C.
-The remaining who are under the appealing process should be clearly communicated about their document status and the expected date for them to receive their document in their hand.
-The business to make sure all workers have proper documentation in their hands. 


Reference: Severance payments

EA Employees who have been employed for 12 months or more are entitled to the following minimum statutory severance payments pursuant to the Employment (Termination and Lay-Off Benefits) Regulations 1980:
10 days’ wages for every year of employment under a continuous contract of service with the employer if he has been employed by that employer for a period of less than 2 years.
15 days’ wages for every year of employment under a continuous contract of service with the employer if he has been employed by that employer for 2 years or more but less than 5 years.
20 days’ wages for every year of employment under a continuous contract of service with the employer if he has been employed by that employer for 5 years or more.
For non-EA Employees, the entitlement to severance payments depends on the employment contract. If the contract is silent, there is a general expectation that a financially-able employer should pay reasonable severance compensation.
10:19
The Employment Act sets out minimum statutory benefits and entitlements. However, most of the Employment Act only applies to employees who fall within the scope of the Act (referred to here as “EA Employees”). 
EA Employees are generally — (1) those whose wages do not exceed RM2,000/month; or (2) those who, irrespective of wages, are engaged in manual labor, engaged in the operation/maintenance of vehicles, supervising/overseeing other employees engaged in manual labour, are engaged in any vessel, or are engaged as a domestic servant.
This distinction between EA Employees and non-EA Employees is important, and the employment terms and conditions of non-EA Employees are usually freely negotiable between employer and employee and would be whatever is set out in the employment contract and other employment documents. Having said that, as general market practice, most non-EA Employees would be contractually-entitled to benefits as good as or better than those provided in the Employment Act (with obvious exceptions such as entitlement to overtime payments).
Reference; Remedies for Unlawful or Unfair Dismissal


Filling a complaint with the Director General of Industrial Relation:

In the event an employee feels that their dismissal is unlawful or unfair, the employee must file a complaint with the Director General of Industrial Relation within 60 days of their dismissal[9].

Thereafter, the department will attempt to settle the matter between the employer and employee[10]. If it fails, the department will then notify the Minister in charge of human resources[11] and the Minister may refer the matter to the industrial court[12].

If the court favours the employee’s case, the court can either order that the employee be reinstated or be compensated, based on the factors laid down in the act[13]. Either party can still appeal to the high court if they are not satisfied with the outcome.

Inherent Power of Minister Responsible for Human Resources:

The minister may also compel the employer to provide benefits to the employee[14].

Filling a Civil Claim:

Alternatively, an employee can claim for damages for breach of contract in the civil court.

description: Unfair dismissal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Client Name - Yan Lin Kyaw (ID - 16420394).  The client called and reported his unfair dismissal without prior notice and after only one warning

On 13 Nov 2022 (Sunday), he and other 5 Burmese workers are working in their line, for that day there is no production time and just cleaning and washing their line, and they ate some snacks, coffee, and soft drink while working, at that time their Line Supervisor saw and took photos, and he warned about to don't do like this again, after that they went back their home. When next morning, 14 Nov 2022 (Monday), the client and other workers are going to their work regularly, but their supervisor denied to work that day regarding the HR decision they will be suspended for 3 working days.  They also accepted that decision, and went back home again. On 16 Nov 2022 (Wednesday), their Line Supervisor call them and ask them to come to the HR office, at that time one Lady (age around 40, chubby body, maybe Discipline Officer of HR department) said: "we don't want to terminate you because of rule violation because if so you can't apply for other jobs, so that you must submit resignation letter yourself, that will be good for you". So they were forced to write resignation letters at that time, and they are confused but they did what HR said. And HR also said they need to come and pick up their cancellation letter on 26 Nov 2022. 

So for this case, he said, he already has over 1 year of working experience in PFI, and never violated the rules and regulations before, this is the very first time for him, but HR and the supervisor didn't issue warnings first but dismissed him directly. He also said he and other workers just ate snack and coffee/soft drinks only, not alcohol or drugs. So he wishes that the business be fair and follow the normal disciplinary policy and re-consider his status.

TPs:
-What is the company's disciplinary policy?  What are the grounds for immediate dismissal?

Recommendations for remediation:
-This is the first time the workers have been found to have broken company regulations and so should be issued with a warning according to the company's disciplinary policy rather than being immediately dismissed
-Consider to re-instate the workers and noting the first warning in the HR personnel files
-Communicate with these workers about the company's decision, and re-instate the workers

They ate some snacks, coffee, and soft drinks while working but their line supervisor took photos of them doing so and warned them not to do this again. The next morning, when they reported to work, their supervisor informed them that they were being suspended for three days.  On the third day, they were called into the HR office, where they were advised to sign resignation letters because they were being dismissed but if the company were to terminate them for breaking the company rules, they would have trouble finding other jobs.  They were confused but did as HR told them to do. He had never broken any rules in the past nor received prior warnings but was now being summarily dismissed, which he feels is unfair.

description: Unfair dismissal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
2 workers at Pataya Food, (Bang Par Site), ROAT Station (loading & unloading work) were unfairly dismissed on 28th Sept 2023. The client reported that the chief line-supervisor P.Yon was very verbally abusive, put so much workload on the workers and he always threatened workers saying "I can dismiss you anytime". So the 9 workers reported his abusive behavior to the office in the 2nd week of August 2023. As a consequence of this, P. Yon retaliated against the 9 workers. He assigned one staff to keep eyes on these 9 workers and find fault and take the photos of these workers actions and the movement. On 28th September, the two workers out of nine workers Mr.Ko Ko Naing (Worker ID - 16220872) and Mr. Khin Zaw (ID-16320532) were called to the office and accused of smoking in a non-smoking area and were immediately dismissed. The manager showed them a photo of them smoking and forced them to sign on the dismissal letter. Actually the area where they smoked is not a non-smoking area but it is an official public smoking area where office staff, truck drivers and other production workers come to smoke. On that day they were caught smoking, there were another six or seven workers smoking in that smoking area but only this two of them were caught in the photo. According to the client, there used to be signboards written in Thai and English as  " Smoking Area" but the manager put it down in the next few days of their dismissal.

Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter immediately.  Workers should not be targeted for dismissal as retaliation for reporting a grievance against their supervisor.  Ensure worker safeguards in place.
- Reinstate the workers, given that they were smoking in an approved smoking area, which was only changed to a non-smoking area after the workers' dismissal.
- Take disciplinary action against the supervisor, as he deliberately sought to find fault that led to the dismissal of workers that he targeted

Deadline: 1 week
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 4 Oct 2023

K. Juthams, HR manager, informed K Nok, HR, who is aware of this case and knows the details, that on September 28, 2023, the production manager from the Mahachai site went to the Bang Pla site. When he arrived, he noticed these two employees smoking in a prohibited area. So the pictures were taken by the manager. Since December 2022, she has been adhering to the GMP standard. Employees will no longer be permitted to smoke on the factory grounds. Since then, HR has communicated this standard for the three-month period of December to February 2023. And because smoking in the factory area is a serious violation, any employee who smokes or violates the rules and regulations will be dismissed without a verbal, written, or suspension warning. There were some employees, even the supervisor, who were dismissed before these two workers. They added that while HR communicated through the HR Official interpreter that the workers were aware of the rule but the workers continued to smoke in that area.

(Internal note: O&E and BHR responded that the workers didn't know that area was prohibited area. However, K Nok, doesn't believe the workers, she said that the workers already know it)


They will share the GMP communication session photos with us. They will also ask the other seven workers if they didn't know it before.

systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Ensure workers are not targeted for reprisals, and that there is regular training on the non-retaliation policy

description: Unfair dismissal
closed_notes: Issara is closing this case.  The worker that reported this issue is exceedingly happy that she is able to continue to work at Nan Yang and has not been let go as she had initially been told.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Nan Yang (SMSK) is terminating many workers' contracts in recent months. The factory provided wages for a month to pink-carded workers as a form of compensation before letting them go. The factory is also terminating MOU (4, 5, and 6-year) workers' contracts very frequently without severance pay.

On 29 January 2023, the interpreter Zin Ko Ko informed 6 MoU workers who completed 6 years that they will be terminated on 2nd Feb 2023. Since last month, the worker had asked the interpreter whether she would be terminated or not and had requested to be informed at least one month in advance so that she would have time to prepare. At that time, the interpreter told her that the factory had no plans to terminate the workers. Now, however, they were told of their termination only THREE days in advance, with no severance pay even if they reported the case to DLPW or DOE. During their conversation, two HR staff communicated this and the interpreter translated for them.

The worker observed that the factory does not terminate the workers in one large group to avoid collective action on the part of the workers. That's why the workers are terminated in a small groups separately. 

She was very sad and cried during the call and requested Issara to help her. She received Issara's number from the ambassadors who joined the training this weekend (29-Jan).

TPs:
- Clarify with the business why workers' contracts are being terminated, without severance pay and with very little advance notice.

Recommendations for remediation:
- Workers should be informed well ahead of time if the company intends to discontinue workers' employment contracts so that they can plan for alternatives
- If contracts will not be extended, severance pay should be provided based on the years of service and cancellation letters provided so that they can find alternative employment
remediation_notes: A worker reported that on 29 January 2023, she in a group of six workers completing 6 years of the MOU contract were informed by the interpreter only three days in advance that their contracts would be terminated on 2nd February 2023.  They would not receive severance pay for their years of service either. The worker thinks that the factory may be terminating the workers in small batches to avoid collective action by a large group of workers.
remediation_action: Issara raised this with the business and the HR manager stated that the business intends to continue employ these workers and will process the extension of the workers' legal documents. He cited that there was miscommunication between the interpreter and the workers.
remediation_validation: Issara followed up with the worker and she updated the good news that she and the others were called into the HR office and they were informed that the workers would continue working as usual and that there was no need to worry about their legal document extension because the business would handle this. The interpreter told the workers that the HR staff was curious as to who might have reported this to Issara. The interpreter said HR is now busy arranging for the workers' document extensions because of the worker's voice coming from Issara.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  The worker that reported this issue is exceedingly happy that she is able to continue to work at Nan Yang and has not been let go as she had initially been told.

Context: Several workers reported being dismissed from work without pre- notice. They said that they were recruited under the re-calibration program as a walk-in worker. Since then, the business has taken their passport for the registration, however workers were informed of being dismissed. 

Talking Points: 

- What caused these workers to be dismissed? 

Recommendations: 

- The business should clarify the reason for dismissal and reconsider to hire them if possible. 


Issue #2
Context: Unfair dismissal- A worker who has been working for the SKP for about 9 months called and reported that he has been asked to sign a document to be sent back with the reason of being absent from work frequently. The worker said that he has not been missing from work for more than 3 days in 9 months and it has not been two years according to his contract. He does not want to go back to Myanmar yet.



Talking Points: 

- What caused this worker to be dismissed? 

Recommendations: 

- The business shall look into his attendance to learn the number of days he has been missing from work. 
- If the workers have not been missing from work for more than 3 days as reported by the worker, the business should reconsider his dismissal. 
- If the worker is found out to be having several days of absent, the business should consider to provide compensation based on the Myanmar and Malaysian contract.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issue #1. 

The businesses responded that the reason for workers' laid-off is not because of the business but because of the government process. The business has submitted all required documents to immigration to apply for the work permit for all workers who are in need, and after several months, the immigration replied back to SKP with the list of workers whose work permits could not be granted. The business tried appealing but only some were granted but 28 still got rejected.

Issara suggested the business to do the communication with the workers about their appealing process so that they can be prepared. Workers who were laid-off have reported Issara saying that they were not prepared to go home or find another job as they were not given any prior notice. However, the business has agreed to communicate.



Issue #2.

The business responded that they have never informed the workers being dismissed, it was a misunderstanding. The business has communicated with the worker. 

The worker confirmed being communicated about misunderstanding and now it is confirmed that the worker will not be dismissed.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that he has been asked to sign a document to be sent back to Myanmar with the reason of being absent from work frequently.
remediation_action: The business responded that worker was never informed about the dismisal and communicated to the worker that it was the misunderstanding.
remediation_results: The worker confirmed being communicated about misunderstanding and not being dismissed.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: The business to conduct a dive investigation with the HR team to identify the root cause. Issara to support as needed.
systems_change_business_steps_taken: Business informed the workers and HR team was informed to strengthen employer-employee communications.
systems_change_business_steps_remaining: To have clear communication channels handled by trained staff with close supervision and effectivness validated by workers.

description: Unfair dismissal
remediation_notes: Seven workers had their MOU contracts, work permits, and visas that already expired (with different dates, from January onwards). Since Oct & Nov 2022, the workers followed up with YRC many times and YRC promised that their documents would be extended by the factory and no need to be worried. On April 26, 2023, YRC asked them to resign; however, the workers did not agree.  Since then, YRC changed their position and said the business would facilitate the U-turn process but did not provide assurances about accommodation in Yangon so that they can be safe and don't have to travel back to their home villages. These workers have overstayed and have been working at YRC without the proper documents; there is concern that they may be blacklisted and not allowed to enter Thailand again.
remediation_action: YRC HR responded that during the formal HR transition period, he was unaware of this. So he only discovered this matter recently. He’s not sure how to do the next step so he will discuss this with the MD and get back to us. After this, HR said YRC will proceed the MoU U-Turn for all workers by beginning to send them back to Myanmar after May 15. They have all of the employees' names and are in the process of submitting the demand name list to DOE. HR said they will inform workers of this policy on May 3, 2023. YRC will cover all recruitment fees and provide a 3,000 Baht allowance to each worker who returns to Myanmar to await the process. YRC however declined to ensure that the U-turn process would be safe for the workers and accommodation would be provided for them while awaiting the return.
remediation_validation: The workers clearly mentioned that they would like to get severance pay for their dismissal; except for one worker, they do not want to go through the MoU U-turn process because there is no place to stay in Myanmar.

description: Unfair dismissal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
There are four MoU workers whose visas and work permits will expire in August 2023. The HR staff informed them that they would be let go after the documents expired. The HR department said each worker would be provided with 10,000 THB upon separation. The workers would like to get severance pay according to the number of working years at YRC. They would also like to get proper cancellation letters to change employers because they would like to try to change the employer before they leave the country.

Myo Kyaw Zin's Visa/WP expires on August 15, 2023. Last working day on August 10, 2023. 
Aung Ye Naing's visa/WP expires on August 6, 2023. Last working day on August 3, 2023.

Talking points:
- Why has the business chosen to not extend these workers' employment?  Is it due to performance or is it due to government regulations?
- Is the business aware that the Thai DOE considers that migrant workers should receive severance pay when the business ends the employment, just like Thai workers?

Recommendations: 
- Provide severance pay to worker according to their years of service
- Provide cancellation letters so that they can find new employers here in Thailand, given that the situation in Myanmar is unstable and potentially unsafe for them to return
- Consider offering the workers the option of doing the U-turn process so that they can return to work on a new MOU cycle
remediation_notes: There are four MoU workers whose visas and work permits will expire in August 2023. The HR staff informed them that they would be let go after the documents expired. The HR department said each worker would be provided with 10,000 THB upon separation. The workers would like to get severance pay according to the number of working years at YRC. They would also like to get proper cancellation letters to change employers because they would like to try to change the employer before they leave the country.
remediation_action: Issara reached out to the business, and HR responded that they had consulted with the Thai Department of Employment and DOE had advised that the business doesn't have to pay for severance since the contract is ending and it's not the business dismissing the workers. Therefore, YRC will only provide 10,000 THB each to the 4 workers. YRC also doesn't have plans to do the MoU U-turn for these workers because the business orders have decreased and they are more keen to hire Thai workers because hiring migrant workers is difficult given the inconsistent government policies on migrant worker management. Finally, the business said it will cover the costs for the repatriation of these workers back to Myanmar.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Have a clear policy on worker separation and how this will be dealt with, whether it will be to pay severance just like the company would do for Thai workers.

supplier_name: Food and Drinks Public Co., Ltd.
description: Unfair dismissal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that those working at F&D but hired by a sub-agency will be let go on Nov 1, 2023. These workers are concerned about finding a new job now, and some workers need to renew their documents before they can change employers. The business made this announcement only a few weeks ago and the sub-agency promised to find them new jobs if they could wait until the new year. Now some workers are looking for new jobs, and some workers are trying to get documents that could be used to change employers. 

TPs:
- How long has F&D had workers that were hired by a sub-agency and not directly by F&D?
- Why are these workers being discontinued?  Is it because there is not enough production?  Or is F&D trying to discontinue the practice of workers being hired by a sub-agent?

Recommendations:
- The business to consider hiring the current workers directly rather than through a sub-agency; to transfer those workers from the sub-agency to be officially employed by F&D
- If the business is unable to continue hiring these workers, take responsibility and ensure these workers have all the proper documents that will allow them to find another employer
- Communicate to these workers clearly what actions F&D will take: whether to hire them back officially as F&D workers or to provide them with the right documents to change employers
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 7 Dec 2023

Issara sent an email requesting a remediation call but received no response from Food and Drinks. Issara attempted to contact them by phone but was unsuccessful.

DATE: 14 Dec 2023
Able to contact by phone

K Suchart, Plant Manager, explained that he knew the issue. The subcontractor chose to leave the job with F&D. The company intends to keep the workers. These workers are the subcontractors' employees. He attempted to contact the subcontractor many times but was unsuccessful. He did, however, confirm that F&D no longer uses any subcontractors. F&D will hire and recruit workers through legal channels. (MoU and walk-in). In this case, if Issara can assist in communicating to the workers that if they want to work at F&D, they can apply directly to F&D, but please ensure that the workers have legal documents.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that those working at F&D but hired by a sub-agency will be let go on Nov 1, 2023. These workers are concerned about finding a new job now, and some workers need to renew their documents before they can change employers. The business made this announcement only a few weeks ago and the sub-agency promised to find them new jobs if they could wait until the new year.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Ensure the business is legally compliant and only have workers that are legally hired directly by F&D
next_description: communicate and validate with the workers.

description: Unfair dismissal
Unfair dismissal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker (mobilizer Ko Hein) reported that on 8th Jan 2024, the business called 270 CI workers (including him) and informed them that they will be laid off and their last working day will be 15 Jan 2024. The reason given for the layoff was that they had not met the 98% work attendance target. When the workers asked for severance, the business said that it won't provide severance because workers are dismissed not for low production. However, the business said that they will provide necessary documents for those who would like to move to a new employer before 13 Feb 2024. In this situation, most of the workers regarded this dismissal as unfair dismissal because there is no 98% attendance requirement mentioned in the worker manual or employment contract.

NOTE: Initially this was affecting 270 workers.  In a follow-up call, around 50 workers will be allowed to continue working at CMC because they are at 97% attendance rate.  Now, this issue is affecting 220 workers.

TPs:
- When is the end date of these workers' current contracts?
- What are the reasons for these workers being dismissed? Workers understand it's for not having worked 98% of the time, which is not something that can be seen as legal grounds for dismissal
- Why were they notified on such short notice?

Recommendations:
- Review whether this decision to dismiss these workers can be considered fair dismissal. If unfair, workers should be retained and employment continued for this group of workers.
- Communicate clearly to workers what the decision is.  If the workers are to be dismissed, the reason for dismissal should be stated and if there are no valid legal grounds for dismissal, appropriate severance payments are to be paid to all workers. If the workers will be retained after review, communicate this change clearly
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 24 Jan 2024

K Itchaya, HR manager, responded via email with the available remediation call times of 22 February and 18 March 2024, which are too long according to the ILM case management protocol. BHR had a phone call to her. She responded that she needed to notify CMC management about Issara's proposal. Because CMC previously worked with Issara for MARS pet care, but MARs is no longer a strategic partner with Issara. BHR explained that there was an ALDI in the ILM that was still SP. She responded that ALDI is no longer one of our customers. There have been no orders from ALDI in a long time. So, if Issara wishes to make a formal call, they must first understand the nature and scope of the issue. BHR explained that CMC and Issara can collaborate while remaining in the ILM supply chain even if SPs are not present. So BHR briefly explained the issue. So she responded that all migrant workers whose contracts will expire and CMC will not extend the contracts or documents. In January 2024, DLPW and DOE convened a meeting with CMC and workers.  So CMC will proceed with 100% severance pay for the workers in accordance with the law.  She stated that Issara can validate this matter with the workers. CMC cannot share the amount and details.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that they were informed that they would be dismissed in a week's time, and the reason given was that they had not met the 98% work attendance rate, which they didn't know previously was a requirement or that it would lead to their dismissal.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Review HR procedures for employment contract terms and conditions, how contract terminations are to be decided and handled, and how/when they are communicated to employees
next_description: validate with the workers.

Because CMC previously worked with Issara for MARS pet care, but MARs is no longer a strategic partner with Issara. BHR explained that there was an ALDI in the ILM that was still SP. She responded that ALDI is no longer one of our customers. There have been no orders from ALDI in a long time. So, if Issara wishes to make a formal call, they must first understand the nature and scope of the issue. BHR explained that CMC and Issara can collaborate while remaining in the ILM supply chain even if SPs are not present. So BHR briefly explained the issue. So she responded that all migrant workers whose contracts will expire and CMC will not extend the contracts or documents. In January 2024, DLPW and DOE convened a meeting with CMC and workers. remediation_issara_recommendation:
A Cambodian worker reported that 30 pregnant Cambodian workers' contracts before their 2-year MOU contract end date. The worker added workers paid a lot of money for the recruitment fees to work with CPF (12,000-20,000 THB). 

Recommendations
- The workers should be formally informed by the business about the terms and conditions of their dismissal
- CPF Saraburi to pay the full wages for the time left until their contracts expire, given they are being dismissed earlier than what is stated in the contract
remediation_business_steps_taken:
1. Contract renewal or dismissal
If the business does not want to renew their contracts, we cannot do anything with it because it's up to the business but Khun Tithipol will try to see with CPF Saraburi if those pregnant workers in Cambodia get paid or not if their contracts are not renewed. If the business doesn't want to renew their contracts, at least they should get paid according to the Thai law which will comply with the legal requirement. The workers should be formally informed by the business about the terms and conditions about dismissal or renewal of contract and compensation. If CPF Saraburi decides to pay the full amount for the time being until their contracts are finished, that's the best. The same approach can apply to all 107 workers whom the business does not want to renew their contracts. O&E officer to find out with the workers how the renewal of contracts are informed to the workers and if they get the compensation. 

2. Recruitment fee
CPF does not cover passport fee, accommodation in Cambodia, and transport costs from the village to Panompen. These costs that CPF doesn;t cover, the workers have to pay by themselves. O&E will need to find more information and the specific cost breakdown of the recruitment fees that the workers have paid. What exactly are those costs? If the costs incur in Myanmar, the workers will have to pay. By Jan next year, Tesco will try to push the CPF Saraburi to cover the passport fee.

3. Unresponsive grievance mechanism 
Khun Tithipol needs more information. O&E to get back to the workers and ask them about the LPN to understand if the workers are aware of the LPN grievance mechanism and their experience in using it, for example, hotline and what kinds of announcement are being made at the factory.

description: Proper tools/safety equipment/other equipment not provided: minor or isolated issue
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Five Cambodian workers were required to buy their own equipment to perform their work, such as knives for cutting the fruit in their production line.  If they did not have this equipment, they were forced by their supervisor to leave the work for that day. In the past, all of the necessary tools and equipment were provided by the business and there were many Cambodian workers but now most of them are leaving since the working conditions here have not improved and the amount of money they earn is not much.

Note: Issues raised during in-person outreach. Workers who reported these issue did not want to share their identities.

Talking points:
Does the supervisor have the authority to send workers home without pay?  
Is HR aware of this?
What is the company’s process for making such decisions?

Recommendations for remediation:
Investigate this issue, include worker voice in the investigation and ensure worker safeguards
Workers should be provided with all equipment, tools, and protective gear needed to perform their tasks
Discipline the line supervisors that forced workers to get their equipment and sent them home without pay
Remediate the workers directly affected, both the lost wages and the cost of the equipment workers had to buy

remediation_issara_recommendation:
WV Call Summary
---------------
This issue was reported by a worker named Ms.Poe Myar from MMP who is currently working in the fish-trimming line (C&D). This KPI deals with inadequate canteen furniture. Workers have reported that there are inadequate tables and chairs in the canteen to accommodate all workers. This situation has become a bit more problematic recently after several new walk-in workers have been recruited

-------------------
KPI Issue Summary
-------------------
Forced Overtime work by factory workers on coercion by line supervisors.
 
----------------------
Other Related KPIs
----------------------
*** The worker reported 5 other issues that are dealt in relevant KPIs as outlined below: 

KPI#2392 - Issues with Break Timings and Rest periods
KPI#2394 - Occupational Safety and Health(OSH) issues. Irregular breaks issue is impacting the health of workers and some trimming line workers have started suffering from stomach problems. 
KPI#2391 - Forced OT issues
KPI#2393 - Security Issue: Not enough lockers and CCTV cameras in locker rooms

--------------------------------------------------------
Impacted Workers - Production Line/Shifts/Other Details
--------------------------------------------------------
500  - Worker is one of the 500 workers on the fish trimming line.

-----------------------------------------------
Additional O&E Fact-Finding Questions (if any)
-----------------------------------------------


----------------------------------------------
Relevant National Laws (Thailand)
----------------------------------------------
Thai labor law does not specifically mandate employers to provide canteen facilities to factory workers. However, there are general regulations under the Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) and other health and safety standards, particularly those enforced by the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare, that ensure workers' welfare in broader terms.

In the context of Thailand's seafood industry that has a significant international oversight, worker welfare, that includes meal breaks and canteen facilities, is guided by occupational health and safety standards, sector-specific practices, international certifications, and ethical labor requirements.

While Thai Labor Law does not specifically require canteens in seafood factories, employers must ensure that working conditions support workers' health and safety. Factories are required to comply with the Labour Protection Act and related OSH standards. Many seafood factories in Thailand, especially those working with international buyers, voluntarily provide canteen facilities to meet international standards set by organizations such as the International Labour Organization (ILO) and certifications like Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) or Fair Trade USA.

-------------------------------
International/Global Standards
-------------------------------
ILO Standards: Many seafood factories aim to comply with the International Labour Organization (ILO) conventions, which emphasize worker welfare, including the provision of clean and safe eating facilities. This includes provisions for Adequate Space and Ventilation which implies that the canteen should be large enough to accommodate the workforce, with proper seating, ventilation, and lighting to create a comfortable environment.

-------------------------------
Buyer CoC
-------------------------------
International buyers often require seafood factories to meet welfare standards, which include providing canteens or ensuring workers have access to adequate and safe meals. These requirements may be part of certification schemes like Fair Trade or Marine Stewardship Council (MSC).

-------------------------------
ILM KPI Goal
-------------------------------
Employers should provide a safe and hygienic work environment to all workers, including proper tools, safety equipment, and other required equipment at no cost to workers.

---------------------------------
Possible Root Causes and Evidence
---------------------------------
-------------------------------
Environmental/Workplace Causes
-------------------------------
Significant increase in the workforce has led to a shortage of tables and chairs in the canteen
Evidence: Workers have reported the hiring of a large number of walk-in workers.

----------------------------------
Business Systems/Shortfalls Causes
----------------------------------
Business has failed to undertake an overall facilities assessment with a planned increase in workforce.
Evidence: There is overcrowding in the canteen and existing furniture is inadequate.

------------------------
People-related Causes - N/A
------------------------

----------------------------------
Remediation Recommendations & TPs
----------------------------------
- Recommendation to provide additional furniture to accommodate the increased workforce.
- Business can also investigate if some tables and chairs have become damaged and unusable over time and can replace them.

---------------------------------------------
Worker Requests from Workers for Remediation
---------------------------------------------
Are the workers reporting the issue requesting anything in particular for remediation? - Yes. Workers are requesting that enough chairs and tables are provided in the canteen that can accommodate all workers comfortably during their lunch break

Is the request from workers in line with international standards and norms?- YES

Is the request from workers safe for themselves, and presenting no possible risks or harms to others? - YES

In conclusion, can/should the request from workers be included in Issara’s recommendations to the business? - YES

What needs to be communicated back to the workers reporting the issue? -
That the issues have been communicated to the business and suggested action for remediation will also be communicated back to them through Issara.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Benefits to Business if the issues raised by worker(s) were properly addressed and no longer impacting the business’ operations/ workplace
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
By following these recommendations, MMP can ensure that canteen facilities provided to workers are compliant with Thai labor laws, respect workers' rights, and align with international standards/guidelines. This would not only help prevent overcrowding in canteen during lunch hour but also foster a positive and productive work environment, providing adequate rest and well being of workers.
This would also help in retention of a satisfied workforce ensuring consistent production and help to uplift the brand image of the business infront of global buyers.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
How could the issue, and Issara’s role in the remediation process with the business, be framed to the supplier (and the SP, if involved) as Issara helping to support that benefit (as a positive force)?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Following Issara’s recommendations can help ensure that the business not only complies with Thai labor laws but also aligns with international best practices, providing a safe and healthy work environment for all workers and also strengthens their brand image and ethical work practices to global buyers making positive impacts on their sales and revenue.

Workers trust Issara and the business can leverage that trust to communicate policy changes, remediation measures and actions aimed at ensuring worker welfare and satisfaction. Issara can also help in educating workers on a number of issues and clarifying policies and rules that would prevent future disputes and confusion with the business.
