remediation_issara_recommendation:
#Issue 1. May - 2020.
-The business should provide enough personal protective equipment to employees ( apron, Gloves, and ears cover).  
-Initiate remediation process: assess workers impacted (those who had to buy extra materials with their own money); make payments within 2 pay periods. The remediation plan should be communicated to all workers.
-Business to do an immediate investigation to identify the root causes of the issue and who is not following the company policy and take disciplinary actions accordingly.

#Issue 2. 12-07-2020.
Context: The issue with a couple of Cambodian workers not receiving enough and adequate PPE (gloves) in their working line (Pay TN, line Patong) where the workers have to cut the fish belly, and the line supervisor not approving glove replacements forcing workers to tape up gloves with holes in them for re-use. ILM ID - 9945

-The business should provide enough personal protective equipment to employees (such as aprons, gloves, and ear covers), and replace them according to a set schedule rather than leaving it to the discretion of supervisors to approve replacements.  
-Business to conduct an immediate investigation to identify the root causes of the issue and who is not following the company policy and take disciplinary actions accordingly.

#Issue 3- (13-Oct).
Context; The line supervisor collecting 5THB per worker for PPE.
(Internal note: the calculation of the amount owed to workers is only based on the report on call 11427, however, other workers have reported having to buy PPE but we do not have the amount workers had paid so it isn't included below)


                                                                                     **TALKING POINTS**
# Issue 1 
-This issue is happening at the cat Food Line 2 ( Cafe 6& 7 Line literally). They get new apron and gloves every 2 months while other workers are receiving new materials every week. 
-Workers have been spending their own money to buy the PPE from the shop. 
-The line supervisor from this line only provides the PPE when they have the visitors. Remind the business that safeguards should be in place while the investigation and remediation are being conducted. 
-Workers have reported this issue to the line supervisor (green hat) but never got the assistance/remediation.

#Issue 2 
**Internal Note for BHR**
-Please be reminded that this issue was reported at the same time as the issue with a Cambodian worker being treated poorly by one male abusive supervisor. 
-Please start the talking point by saying that we have been receiving calls regarding the PPE issue from different lines quite frequently. 
-How does the business monitoring the condition of the protective equipment of workers to make sure that all workers have adequate PPE for their work? 
-Does the business have a system to replace the protective equipment on a regular basis, according to a set standard?  If so, how often is the protective equipment (in this case, gloves) replaced? 
-Workers from this specific line have also reported more recently receiving new gloves.  However, what has the business done to ensure that this situation doesn't happen again in the future?

#Issue 3- 
-Please share the issue in detail with the business. 
-Please provide Issara's feedback as follows: 
-The business has not taken Issara's recommendations for the system change yet.
-The business neither communicated with the line supervisors nor took remediation actions for the issue with money that the workers have to pay for the gloves and no disciplinary actions were taken towards the supervisors who were not strictly following the business policy.  
-In the previous meeting, the business said that they do not have a cooperative market in their factory, several workers confirmed having this marked and still being collected the money for the PPE. Please give the following information to the business 1) Schedule for opening the market. 2) PPE that is being sold is exactly the same as the business materials. 3)Share the information (line) of the workers and the supervisor who recently collected the money for PPE. 
4) Provide the price of each material as mentioned in the worker voice call.  Please share the business that workers only get PPE whenever they have visitors.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
#Issue 1.
The business only explained its policy regarding PPE, however, did not commit to taking action. It was added that the workers can reach out to HR if they have any issues with the PPE. 

9 June  2020; Workers from Catfood Cafe 6&7 got new aprons, gloves, and shoes on 1st June. (CLOSED). 

#issue 2. (30-Jul-2020) 
The business agreed to have a meeting with the production manager and distribute the PPE to the workers. 

24/08/2020. The worker updated that the business has provided the PPE as they have required and also the supervisor in this specific line is allowing the workers to access the PPE whenever is needed. (CLOSED)


#Issue 3. 13 Nov,20; 
The business conducted the investigation and found the issue. The staff who used to sell the PPE received the written warning and workers were distributed the PPE as required. For the reimbursement, the business announced the workers to reach out to the HR office for the remediation, however, only 3-4 workers have done so. The business added that some workers simply refused to be remediated. 

27-Nov; Workers confirmed receiving PPE as required and also confirmed the investigation taking place. Workes also added that they do not want their money back but the system to be improved.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The company should explain to all workers what are the disciplinary actions for those who do not follow the company policy.   

Communication.  
-Effectively communicate to workers (verbally and in written) the company policy on PPE, and contact information of focal points, actions that will be taken by the business for investigations and safeguarding, and timeframes. 
-The business to produce a clear set of visual standards and post on notice boards and announce verbally to ensure workers have clarity on the policy of PPE on when and how they should apply for kits replacement. 

-The business to revise the PPE distribution and tracking system to make sure all workers in the production lines receive the same standard amount of PPE and that they are regularly replaced. 

-Issara can also provide tailored training to full HR teams on-site, and provide systems review with tailored recommendations to eliminate labour risks.

Its added that it might take another one month for them to work on the system.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker asked for a new pair of gloves as she broke/tore her glove. The line supervisor (P Mon) refused to give her new gloves as requested. The worker had to pick up a pair of gloves from the trash bin and continued working. Each worker is given a new pair of gloves every day. Normally, they can request a new one if it's broken.

Talking points:
What is the business policy on ensuring that workers are provided with proper personal protective equipment (PPE) such as gloves?
How is the PPE inspected and when is it replaced?

Recommendations for remediation
Investigate this incident and identify why the torn gloves were not replaced for the worker requesting it.  Implement according to TU’s non-retaliation policy 
Communicate to all workers and supervisors the process for requesting and receiving replacements for PPE, with clear examples of equipment that is deemed unusable and needing replacement
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business responses: 
Issue 
PR Line worker (Processing) night shift reported that the gloves were torn and a worker went to ask to change the new gloves with the supervisor named "Morn". The supervisor did not allow it. Workers use the torn gloves to continue working.
 
Business responses:
The company provides gloves to workers for work. In the case of the worker's gloves are damaged, such as torn gloves, leaked gloves, the worker can bring damaged gloves to request a new gloves at the supervisor or the administrative staff of the department unit before entering the work.

In the case of of worker wants to change gloves during working hours, the worker can request a replacement at the administrative staff. Because the supervisor's working in the production line. However, the worker must bring old gloves to request for replacement. To make sure that there would be no broken gloves mixed with the product.

From the investigation with Khun Morn, he insisted that he never refuses if the worker brings a damaged gloves to replace a new gloves, except when he is in the production line, he would inform workers to request a change at the administrative staff.

From the survey with randomly asking 8 workers, the workers who randomly inquired if the gloves were damaged, could request to change the gloves at the supervisor. However, the most of workers still do not know that in the case of requesting to change during the working hours, they can request a change at the administrative staff.

In this regard, the HR, factory manager, and supervisors have communicated with all workers that how to request changing gloves.

Status: Done 
Responsibility: Production and HR
remediation_notes: A worker asked for a new pair of gloves because they were torn. The line supervisor refused to give her new gloves as requested. The worker had to pick up a pair of gloves from the trash bin to continue working.

The business found that the workers did not know that if their gloves need to be replaced during their work shift, they should go to the Admin department to get new gloves.  HR, production manager, and supervisors have announced to all workers the channel through which workers should get their gloves replaced.
remediation_validation: Issara is following up with the workers on the business response.

description: Social Security issue (access to health care): minor issue
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; Workers who are requested to quarantine at home due to being in close contact with Covid-positive person who is not a LB worker will not get paid for those days.


Talking Points; 
Workers have reported not receiving their daily wages if they have to take quarantine for being in close contact with their family members who are not the workers of Ladybird, what is the business policy in this case? 
How many workers are in this situation and what has been the process for them so far? 
How many days of quarantine are required for close contact cases? Who pays for those quarantine days? 
Has the business checked the government regulations on what Covid-related care services are to be covered by SSO and whether and how quarantine days for Covid close contacts are to be paid?  

Recommendations:
-The business should confirm the latest government regulations related to quarantine periods for Covid close contacts and how pay for missed working days due to quarantine is to be handled
We have received the update that the government regulations are as follows:  
-If a worker is found to be positive at the factory, she/he is supposed to be sent to the hospital for the PCR test and if confirmed as positive, receive the medical certificate and recommended to quarantine. The worker should get paid sick leave during those days. 
-If a worker is a close contact, s/he should visit the hospital and report why she/he is at high risk and get the recommendations from the hospital. The regular recommendations for vaccinated people is to take 10 days of quarantine and do another test on the 10th day. -If the result is negative, then the worker can start working. In terms of the wages for the high risk workers who have a medical certificate for their quarantine days, the employer can submit the worker information to the SSF for the 50% of wages. 
-If the worker is not allowed to go to the hospital but the employer orders the worker to take quarantine, it is the responsibility of the employer to pay the worker wages. 
The business should communicate with the workers about how quarantine days for close contacts will be paid.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have the policy where workers have to practice social distancing at any time including in their home. The business added that they assigned to the suspected workers to take 5 days of quarantine without pay because they get to close contact which against the business policy. Issara have provided the recommendations, the business agreed to have internal meeting with the management and get back to Issara.
remediation_notes: Workers who are requested to quarantine at home due to being in close contact with a Covid-positive person who is not a LB worker will not get paid for those days.
remediation_action: Issara raised this issue with the business, and the business responded that they have the policy where workers have to practice social distancing at any time including in their homes. The business added that they assigned suspected workers to take 5 days of quarantine without pay because they had not practiced social distancing as per business policy.

description: Social Security issue (access to health care): minor issue
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A worker from Sewing Line 2 reported that in the second week of February, her line supervisor announced that workers can’t get free Covid tests or Covid-related medical care at the hospital under social security coverage anymore.  From now on, the workers will have to pay 2,500 Baht for a Covid test. 

Talking  Points; 
-Workers have reported not having access to their SSF for Covid-related care. What is the business understanding on this issue? 
-Has the business checked the government regulations on what Covid-related care services are to be covered by SSO?  

Recommendations:
- The business should clarify with the SSO as to what Covid-related medical services are covered for those with social security coverage
- Communicate with all workers about their health care coverage including Covid-related care under the social security system
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have a policy where if a worker is feeling unwell, they have to approach HR and request the ATK test kit. If the ATK kit results positive, the workers will have to go to the Social Security Hospital for the additional test. If any workers want to do the PCR test by themselves, they have to pay. However, the business conducted an investigation and identified that the workers had misunderstandings about the process.

To solve the issue, HR has trained and communicated with the line supervisors and will communicate with the workers. Issara checked with the workers, and workers have confirmed not having issues anyfurther.
remediation_notes: A worker from Sewing Line 2 reported that in the second week of February, her line supervisor announced that workers can’t get free Covid tests or Covid-related medical care at the hospital under social security coverage anymore.  From now on, the workers will have to pay 2,500 Baht for a Covid test.
remediation_action:
Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have the policy where if a worker is feeling unwell, they have to approach HR and request for the ATK test kit. If the ATK kit result is positive, the workers will have to go to the Social Security Hospital for the PCR test. The business clarified that if any worker wants to do the PCR test by herself, this would be on personal expense.

The business conducted an investigation and found that the workers had misunderstood this policy to mean that Covid-related testing and medical care would not be covered any longer.  To solve the issue, HR has trained the line supervisors on how to communicate this to workers and has been working on the written policy. The written policy will be announced to the workers in early April. Issara is checking with the workers.

description: Social Security issue (access to health care): minor issue
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The workers reported that for emergency care or accident cases, the business advised them to get medical care at a hospital not designated under the Social Security coverage.  In such cases, the workers have to pay the cost in advance and they get reimbursement later. This does not happen frequently but the workers would like to know why the business is doing this.

Talking points:
Are there instances when the business will request workers to get treated at hospitals other than the SSO-designated hospitals?  If so, what are the reasons for this?

Recommendations for remediation:
The business to clearly communicate to the workers the company policy on workers’ access to healthcare and relevant coverage under Social Security.  If certain medical care is to be had at hospitals not under Social Security coverage, the reasons are to be clearly stated.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Witsawad - This is all clear that the company would treat the workers more than SSO hospital. Because in some cases, the workers cannot be recovered by SSO hospital. The company would like the workers to be healthy and be recovered as soon as possible to 100% and ready to work. But for symptoms like fever or any non-serious condition, the workers would be treated by the SSO hospital.


The investigation result:
This case didn't happen. But if it happens, it's probably the case that migrant workers are a walk-in group, applying for a job and being hired as an employee. This group of employees will not be able to use social security rights immediately because they may not have rights in the case that they must have paid contributions for 3 months within 15 months, but the company has purchased health insurance for employees who have not received social security benefits for a period of 4 months. If these employees are sick, they must use health insurance instead.

Action:
In the case of an incident
1. In employee orientation will increase the knowledge of foreign employees who have not received social security rights that if there is an illness, health insurance must be exercised until the SS benefit active.
2. HR makes a copy of the health insurance policy for employees to keep in their passport in case of emergency.
3. If there is an illness, inform HR through an interpreter to help coordinate with the hospital to facilitate

- Communicate clearly to workers the procedures and steps for them to follow when they need medical attention, including how to request and receive transportation service to medical facilities

description: Social Security issue (access to health care): minor issue
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers said that if they go to the clinic appointed by the factory, the clinics do not provide MC unless the workers are in a critical situation. Given that, workers prefer to go to the clinic that has Burmese doctor so that they can express their health conditions and get MC as needed. However, workers are not getting reimbursed for such medical expenses. In addition to that, when they go to work with that MC provided by the Burmese doctor, they have to sign a document provided by their line supervisor. If they get MC from the factory appointed clinic, they do not have to sign the document. 


-Workers want to know why they are not getting reimbursement and why having to sing a letter when they go to see a doctor that speaks Burmese?
remediation_business_steps_taken: 6th Dec, the business will conduct an investigation and get back to Issara.
remediation_notes:
Workers said that if they go to the clinic appointed by the factory, they could not communicate well and they do not provide MC unless the workers are in a critical situation. Given that, they prefer to go to the clinic that has Burmese doctor so that they can express their health conditions clearly and understand the advice from the doctor. When workers go to other clinics that have doctors, they cannot get reimbursement for medical expenses, and when they got the MC provided by the Burmese doctor, they have to sign a document provided by their line supervisor. 

Workers want to know why they are not getting reimbursement and why having to sign a letter when they go to see a doctor that speaks Burmese?
remediation_action: The business has explained the medical treatment process and shared the panel clinics that workers can reach out to. The business also shared the medical leave process.
remediation_validation: Issara checked with the workers if they had any receipt or days that they did not get paid, however, workers could not provide the evidence. Issara communicated with the workers about the business sick leave policy and encouraged them to share the information and reach out to Issara should there be any issues.
remediation_results: No workers have reported further concern and Issara team will proactively check with workers on this issue once in a while.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Business to communicate the policy to workers and have written annoucement shared with workers as well as with Issara.

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: dispute without violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
#Issue 1. 
Context; several workers reported not being allowed to use their annual leave as they wish. Supervisors do not approve the worker's request if they have high demands but ask the workers to take consecutive leaves when the business has fewer demands. 


Please refer to the recommendations for the system improvement.

#Issue 2. 
The issue with the internal sick leave process when workers get sick during the working day and while working. Workers updated that they have to pass 4 steps to be able to return home for sick leave if they get sick while working. 

-Waiting for O & E's update.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
According to Labybird's police regarding the annual leave, business workers are entitled to take the annual leave. The workers can request the annual leave and be approved by HR directly not the supervisor the same as sick leave but it depends on the production plan. For example, there were 10 workers on the production line. And  4 workers requested to take annual leave on the same day but The production manager already planned for that line should have at least 8 workers to work on that day. So 2 workers could take leave but for another 2 workers could not. However, HR and supervisor communicated to the workers and decided case by case depends on the workers' reason to leave also.

HR will communicate verbal and a written announcement about the policy and process of the leave request again.


The business; The draft of the announcement is in the process and will share with Issara for proofreading.

11 May 2021. 
The business shared the photo of the written announcement.


The Sick leave procedure

If the worker got illness during the working time, there are two cases.
1. The worker can ask the supervisor directly to have sick leave and go back home to rest.
2. The worker can go to the first-aid clinic) room in the factory and then the nurse can check and let the worker know the status and inform HR that this worker can go home for rest or go to the hospital.

12 May,2021. 
The business shared the photo of the announcement.

-The business responded that workers are suggested to take the annual leaves based on the productions flow. The business did not mention the specific supervisor's behavior.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-Clarify to the business that according to LPA, workers are entitled to take 6 days of annual leave. The leave days requested by workers shall be approved by the employer but they should not be allocated by the employer. 

Understanding that the business approves leaves based on the production plans, it is recommended for the business to consider each worker leave request and give workers options in case the exact day requested by the worker is not a good moment for that worker to take leave. The business and workers shall come to an agreement on the days the worker can take leave, it should be a fair negotiation between both parties, so for instance, if production is very busy during one week, the business and the worker can find another time during the upcoming week or so for the worker to take leave (if the worker would like to do so). But the company should not say to the worker that they can only take leave during low season (which is a limited time during the year). 

Provide the abovementioned recommendations to the business, and explain that there should be a communication session and a written announcement about the workers right to take leave and the policy and process to get approval of the leave request.  


Time frame 1 pay period

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Nay Lin Aung from Ladybird reported that there are approximately 60+ workers who are going to take vaccine 3rd dose tomorrow (26 May 2022. In this case the business. This morning, the respective line supervisors asked the workers to fill out an annual leave request form for the tomorrow's vaccination. The workers wonder why the business asked them to request annual leave instead of sick leave and they think it is unfair. So they would like to ask the business clarification via Issara.

Recommendations for remediation:
Workers should be able to apply for business leave in this case, not annual leave since this is a vaccination drive that the business is recommending for the sake of keeping the workforce free from Covid-19
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business response
K. Leena, HR Manager, stated that according to policy, the company would use business leave or annual leave for the workers on the day who were shot (happened in the 1st and 2nd shot as well). Workers have the right to take sick leave after the shot dat if they have any symptoms. She will, however, re-communicate with the workers in order for them to understand the policy.

The line supervisors asked the workers to fill out an annual leave request form for the next day's vaccination. The workers don't understand why the business asked them to request annual leave instead of sick leave.
remediation_action: The business stated that according to policy, the company would use business leave or annual leave for the workers on the day workers receive their vaccinations.  The business clarified that the third dose was optional for workers and they could choose whether or not to get the vaccine.  The business added that workers had the right to take sick leave after getting the vaccine if they experienced any side effects. The business said it would announce this policy again so workers understand the policy.

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: dispute without violation of law or employment contract
closed_notes: Issara is closing this case as "fair" because the company has clarified with the workers the company's policy regarding quarantine days for Covid high-risk persons, that workers needing to quarantine as high-risk persons can take annual or business leave, or otherwise apply for Social Security compensation of 50% of wages for those days.  It is not providing allowances for workers to use sick leave or special Covid leave for such instances.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; Workers reported that the business would not provide paid sick leave or   COVID special leaves for high-risk quarantine workers.  It was not clear for the workers as well.  Workers sought clarification.


Talking Points; 

Workers reported not being paid for quarantine days as Covid high-risk persons, what is the business understanding on this issue? 
How many workers are in this situation and what has been the process for them so far? How many days of quarantine are required for close contact and positive cases? Who pays for those quarantine days? 
Has the business checked the government regulations on what Covid-related care services are to be covered by the business and/or SSO and whether and how quarantine days for Covid close contacts are to be paid?  


Recommendations. 
The business should confirm the latest government regulations related to quarantine periods for Covid close contacts and how to pay for missed working days due to quarantine is to be handled
We have received the update that the government regulations are as follows:  If a worker is found to be positive at the factory, she/he is supposed to be sent to the hospital for the PCR test and if confirmed as positive, receive the medical certificate and recommended to quarantine. The worker should get paid sick leave during those days. 
If a worker is in close contact, s/he should visit the hospital and report why she/he is at high risk and get the recommendations from the hospital. The regular recommendation for vaccinated people is to take 10 days of quarantine and do another test on the 10th day. 
If the result is negative, then the worker can start working. In terms of the wages for the high-risk workers who have a medical certificate for their quarantine days, the employer can submit the worker's information to the SSF for 50% of the wages. 
If the worker is not allowed to go to the hospital but the employer orders the worker to take quarantine, it is the responsibility of the employer to pay the worker wages. 
The business should communicate with the workers about how to quarantine days for close contacts and positive workers will be paid. 

Time Frame; 1 week.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara shared this issue with the business, the business will check with the HR team and get back to Issara.

K. Alisa, Director of Quality System responded and clarified the policy as follows.
1. High-risk colleagues who work together do not need to be quarantined.
2. But if the workers live in the same house, in the past, the workers had to quarantine for 7 days and show APK results before came to work.
3. Now adjusted to a 5-day quarantine, showing APK results before coming to work, adjusting according to the government

In conclusion, if the workers work together but wear a mask all the time, the workers don't have to quarantine.

Those who need to quarantine, can take any leave. For example, annual leave and business leave to get the full wage or Social Security 50% of wage which a reimbursement from SSF but it will be slow because SSF required the certificate of quarantine from Provincial Public Heath.

Therefore, this is an optional and provides the form for workers to select.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that they had heard that the business would not provide paid sick leave or COVID special leave for workers needing to quarantine as high risk or close contact persons.  They wanted clarification on the company policy on this.
remediation_action: Issara shared this issue with the business, and the Director of Quality Systems responded that the company policy allowed for high-risk persons to continue working if the whole group working together were all high-risk.  For high-risk persons that needed to quarantine for five days, they would not get sick leave or Covid special leave.  They could either choose to use annual leave or business leave to get full pay during those days, or claim Social Security compensation for those days, which would be paid at 50% wages.
remediation_validation: The worker confirmed that the business has posted the announcement in Burmese about how to apply for social security compensation.  For now, he doesn't know anyone who has the quarantine payment issue.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because the business has made the announcement and clarified with workers what kind of leave they can use for quarantine days for Covid high-risk persons, and the process for getting Social Security compensation as needed.

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: dispute without violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers’ annual leave days being deducted for their quarantine period. Workers reported that they had to quarantine as they had come in close contact with Covid-positive colleagues at work when they had gone to help in a production line where workers ended up Covid-positive.  However, since they were not Covid-positive, their quarantine days were not counted as sick leave.  Instead, their annual leave days were used up for those days in quarantine.  The workers feel this is unfair to them because Covid-positive workers got sick leave for their quarantine days because they were not Covid-positive, had to use their annual leave for their quarantine days.  As it is the end of the year, the business is paying workers for any unused annual leave days. While Covid-positive workers got money for their unused annual leave days, the workers that were Covid-negative but still had to quarantine had all their annual leave days used up for the quarantine days.  Workers added that they had approached their line supervisor,  but the line supervisor said that this was a management decision so they can not do anything. 

Recommendations;
-For the workers who were asked to stay quarantined by the business because they came in close contact with Covid-positive workers, the business should reconsider its position to count the quarantine period as sick leave only when a worker is Covid-positive and has a medical certificate.  It should count the quarantine period of those in the high risk group as sick leave as well, regardless of whether they have a medical certificate or not.
- have an open dialogue with the impacted workers.
-Clearly communicate to all workers the system of managing Covid-related staff absences and calculating the number of days allocated to sick leave, annual leave, and special leave. 


Talking Points
- For workers whose annual leave was used for quarantine, had they used up all 30 days of their sick leave, or was it not counted as sick leave because the workers were not Covid-positive and didn’t have a medical certificate?  If they were required to quarantine for health and disease prevention as high risk persons, why shouldn’t those days be considered sick leave, even though they don’t have a medical certificate saying they were Covid-positive? 
-When Issara received this Issue in July, the business said that they had communicated with the workers several times. If that was the case, why do workers still have issues on this? What is the business understanding on this issue? Because the workers who have reported to Issara are not aware of the business communication.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have already communicated this issue with the workers since they have used workers annual leaves and paid for daily wages, that is the reason that the workers are not receiving annual leaves payment because they have been paid once. The business added that they have already communicated with workers several times, if there are some workers who have not been communicated about the business decision, they should reach out to the HR. Issara is checking with the workers.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that earlier in the year, they were asked to quarantine as they had come in close contact with Covid-positive colleagues at work.  Since they were not Covid-positive, the business did not count this quarantine period as sick leave but used their annual leave days and then special leave granted by the company.  Workers said this isn't fair since those that did get Covid got to use sick leave for their quarantine period and were now being paid out any unused annual leave days at the end of the year.
remediation_action:
Issara raised this issue with the business, and the business responded that it had communicated several times to workers the policy of how quarantine periods would be dealt with, that for those that are Covid-negative and quarantining as a "close contact", sick leave would not apply since there is no medical certificate provided to those that don't contract the virus.  If workers still had questions, they could go to HR to make their queries.

The business has provided Issara with the announcement that has been communicated to workers, and Issara will provide suggestions on content so that the business can make the announcement again.

closed_notes:

Issara is closing this case with a high rating.  The business has made progress and adopted the policy of providing paid leave for high-risk workers who have to quarantine.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers’ annual leave days being deducted for their quarantine period. Workers reported that they had to quarantine as they had come in close contact with Covid-positive colleagues at work when they had gone to help in a production line where workers ended up Covid-positive.  However, since they were not Covid-positive, their quarantine days were not counted as sick leave.  Instead, their annual leave days were used up for those days in quarantine.  The workers feel this is unfair to them because Covid-positive workers got sick leave for their quarantine days because they were not Covid-positive, had to use their annual leave for their quarantine days.  As it is the end of the year, the business is paying workers for any unused annual leave days. While Covid-positive workers got money for their unused annual leave days, the workers that were Covid-negative but still had to quarantine had all their annual leave days used up for the quarantine days.  Workers added that they had approached their line supervisor,  but the line supervisor said that this was a management decision so they can not do anything. 


Recommendations;
-For the workers who were asked to stay quarantined by the business because they came in close contact with Covid-positive workers, the business should reconsider its position to count the quarantine period as sick leave only when a worker is Covid-positive and has a medical certificate.  It should count the quarantine period of those in the high risk group as sick leave as well, regardless of whether they have a medical certificate or not.
- have an open dialogue with the impacted workers.

Talking Points
- For workers whose annual leave was used for quarantine, had they used up all 30 days of their sick leave, or was it not counted as sick leave because the workers were not Covid-positive and didn’t have a medical certificate?  If they were required to quarantine for health and disease prevention as high risk persons, why shouldn’t those days be considered sick leave, even though they don’t have a medical certificate saying they were Covid-positive? 
-When Issara received this Issue in July, the business said that they had communicated with the workers several times. If that was the case, why do workers still have issues on this? What is the business understanding on this issue? Because the workers who have reported to Issara are not aware of the business communication.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have already communicated this issue with the workers since they have used workers annual leaves and paid for daily wages in 2021, that is the reason that the workers are not receiving annual leaves payment at the end of the year. The business added that they have re-communicated with workers about the business decision for the future and for the past, if there are some workers who have not been communicated about the business decision, they should reach out to the HR. In summary, the business used workers annual leaves for high risks quarantine by saying that high risks workers did not have medical certificte to provide paid sick leave. The business added that since they have already used workers' annual leaves and paid, the business did not considered for the cases that already happened. However, the business commited to improve in the future.  Issara checked with the workers, the workes confirmed being communicated and being provided with paid leaves for high risk quarantine days in 2022. The business has made the progress and adopted the policy of providing paid leave for high risks workers who have to stay quarantine.

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: dispute without violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; Issue with workers’ annual leave Workers from the “Breaded” line reported that they can not take annual leave for several consecutive days as they wish.  The business is only allowing them to take one annual leave day every two months, which is not helpful for the workers that may be planning vacation time over several consecutive days. 

Recommendations; 
The business should review its annual leave policy and how it is being practiced.
Workers should be able to determine when he/she will take days off for their personal rest and leisure, and not be restricted to being able to take only one leave day at a time
If the business already has a policy of allowing workers to request and take annual leave days when they would like, disciplinary measures should be  taken against the line supervisor that is restricting workers’ ability to take annual leave for multiple consecutive days


Talking Points
What is the business’s annual leave policy? 
Are workers allowed to take more than 1 day of annual leave per time?
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the business and suggested for the recommendations. As response, the business replied by saying that their investigation did not find the issue with the supervisor not approving workers annual leaves, however it was found that supervisor asking several questions when workers take leaves. The business added that they have communicated with the supervisor and emphasized the way of communication method with the workers. On top of that, the business added that the HR from the factory has a plan to provide refresher training with all supervisors by March 2022. The business also added that the workers have rights to take their annual leaves consecutively.  However, the business response has not reflected the communication with the workers about the business policy taking leaves. 

Issara is checking with the workers.
remediation_notes: Workers from a production line reported that they are not being allowed to take several consecutive days of annual leave as they wish.  The business is only allowing them to take one annual leave day every two months, which is too restrictive for those that would like to take vacation time over several consecutive days.
remediation_action:
Issara raised this issue with the business.  The business conducted the investigation with employees in the Chup Pang line, and found that supervisors would ask lots of questions when a worker would ask for several consecutive days of annual leave and some would shout at the workers. The HR department has issued warnings to such supervisors. In addition, HR plans to provide refresher training to all supervisors on communication methods in March 2022

It concerning that the company is holding the position that it has the right to determine when employees take their annual leave and has determined that employees can take 1 annual leave day every 2 months so as to distribute the vacation days throughout the year.  However, the business did allow that if the employee needs to use several leave days consecutively, she must make the request to her supervisor and it will be considered for approval.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
The business shall communicate with the workers about the business’s annual leave policy and clarify that workers can use annual leave days without restrictions (such as, only taking one annual leave day at a time).  
Also, take this opportunity to remind workers about the company’s grievance mechanism, the process of how grievances are reported and handled, any specific staff or committee that serves as the focal responsible person to respond to grievances, and encourage workers to report any issues they may have in the future

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: dispute without violation of law or employment contract
Issue with annual leave or sick leave: dispute without violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers at GFPT have been asked for medical certificates even if they request sick leave for one day. This happened to two workers, where their line supervisor asked to see their MCs for sick leave of only one day. These two workers did still receive their wages for their sick day but are confused as to why they were asked to submit their MCs. Workers want the business to clarify that MCs are needed only for sick leave that is 3 or more consecutive days, as per the Thai labor law.  

TPs:
-Is HR aware that line supervisors are asking for MCs from workers when they are sick for only one day?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Conduct a refresher with the line supervisors to make sure they understand that workers are not required to present a MC for sick leave that is less than 3 consecutive days
-Communicate, verbally and in writing, that all workers are entitled to take sick leave and are not required to present a MC for 1-2 days of sick leave.
remediation_business_steps_taken: The company policy has always been performed in accordance with the law. If the sick leave does not exceed 3 days, a medical certificate is not required. *** Medical certificates may be required for some workers who have a high rate of monthly sick leave. The reason for this is that the company cares about the worker and acknowledges the results of the doctor's diagnosis in order to adjust the work to the worker's needs.

Workers want the business to clarify that MCs are needed only for sick leave that is 3 or more consecutive days, as per the Thai labor law.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client was previously working in HT-91 and moved to Hong Seng when her MOU contract came to end with HT-91. She is reporting the issues which are happening in Building A, line no. 1-7 (B-U 1).

- Line supervisors should be trained to clearly understand that all workers are entitled to 30 days of sick leave per year, and should not be pressured in any way to feel like they can't take sick leave when needed
- Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, to refresh everyone's understanding on how the company implements its sick leave policy

-All supervisors who involve in this process should be communicated about the importance of the consent form process.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Workers who work for the night shift start at 4:30 PM, and they would like to request the business to change the starting time of this shift to 6:30 PM so that the workers can have enough sleep and feel rested, especially during the COVID-19 outbreak. 

Talking Points; 
-Workers would like to request the business to adjust the starting time of the night shift during this period of the COVID outbreak since they would like to be able to have good rest, have time to have proper meals, and be strong. 


-Workers have explained that the starting time of the shift is not good timing for them to have enough sleep as they are starting to work at 4:30 pm which means that they have to wake up around 2 pm to be ready for work and they also can not sleep well in the morning until their roommate (partner) go out for work as they share a small room. 
-Workers also have shared that many workers are being tested positive for COVID-19 which scares them a lot, so they want to be able to have a good rest and be strong. 
-Workers also added that this request is only during the COVID-19 outbreak and that the working hours can return to normal after the COVID-19 cases drop and the situation is controlled. 
-Workers have also added that they could refuse to start working at 4:30 but it impacts their OT working hours (do not get OT if they start to work at 6:30), so they wouldn’t want to lose the chance to work OT hours,  and it is also complicated for the workers to select any shift they want (in case they wanted to change the shift). 
-Given the workers' concern, Issara would suggest the business consider workers’ requests during this (COVID-19) outbreak time and have a dialogue with workers to come to an agreement.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had a meeting with the business, the business agreed to conduct the investigation by interviewing several workers for consideration of theirs request. A few days later, the business has updated removing OT hours before normal hours start which was the worker's request. Issara checked with the workers, workers confirmed the improved situation which aligns with the business response.
remediation_notes: The issue with workers on the night shift having to start work at 4:30pm, which is too early for them and they would like to request the business to change the starting time of this shift to 6:30pm so that the workers can have enough sleep and feel rested, especially during the COVID-19 outbreak.
remediation_action: The business explained that the night shift was from 6.30 pm - 4.30 am and that the 4:30pm to 6:30pm period was considered OT and so workers could choose to accept or refuse work during this time.  In case of the workers' concerns, HR will survey the workers, consider workers' requests, and come to an agreement.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Workers reported having to work at odd working hours that they were not aware of when they started their job. The job hours start from 11 PM to 8 AM and so on. Workes want regular working hours as they used to do in the past because they have challenges commuting to the factory during those hours. In addition to that, the workers added not having OT for several months makes them difficult to manage their financial situation. Workers want to know how long non-OT work will continue because they may have to find better income jobs if this will continue for another several months. 


Talking Points
-What are the working hours at the moment? How long does each rotation of shifts last?
-How are working being communicated? 
-What is the workload these days. Workes reported not receiving OT for several months, any changes or updates that the workers should be aware of? 


Recommendation; 

-The business should communicate with the workers about the work shifts and make sure that workers have safe communication channels for their work during odd hours, especially at night. 
-The business should also communicate with the workers about the business workload and OT hours so that workers can make decisions as they wish.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The business response: 
Piyabutr said this night shift was set according to another buyer, not HP. CC and line supervisors already had a discussion meeting and communicated to the workers. This shift started last two months ago and it’s just a temporary shift based on the order of the buyer.

Worker updates are being communicated by the business. The communication said that they will end odd working hours shifts and only have two shifts which are day and night. Workers do not have issues with this anymore. For the OT hours, workers heard from their supervisors that they will start receiving OT starting June. Workers do not have issues anymore.

description: Issues with overtime being involuntary/forced or illegal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue 1: The issue with the abusive manager with a broken arm at the building 3 raw shrimp peeling line being abusive with the workers. Workers added that the manager uses abusive words with workers, forces them to do OT, increases the target settings, and does not let workers have full lunch breaks. 


Recommendations for the issue with forced OT hours;

-The business to make sure that none of the workers are being forced to do OT. This issue is being reported by workers under this supervisor, therefore the business should provide training to the supervisor on the company policy and Thai law, and the severity of this issue. It is against the local law and international laws to force workers to work overtime. This should be acknowledged by all line supervisors.  

-The business to clearly communicate with all workers about the OT policy and the company‘s process to give their consent to work overtime. 
-All workers should have the right to refuse or accept working overtime. 

Talking points. 

-What is the process for getting consent from the workers to do OT?
-How does the business make sure that workers are not forced to do OT? 



Time frame - 2 weeks.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
06/18/2021 (ID-1276)
The business responded that they have conducted interviews with around 80 workers in that specific production line. The business's interview found that workers understand the voluntary nature of the OT working hours. The business explained that the workers will be asked to sign on the OT working hours document. In that time, workers can sing OT record sheets if they want to do OT in the evening or not sign if they want to skip OT. The business added that the workers can skip OT even an hour in advance if they have an issue with their health. However, some workers want to skip the OT at the last minute which impacts the products which might be the case for some workers.
remediation_notes: Workers have reported an abusive line supervisor, and added that the manager uses abusive words with workers, forces them to do OT, increases the target settings, and does not let workers have full lunch breaks.
remediation_action: The business responded that they have conducted interviews with around 80 workers in that specific production line. The business's interview found that workers understand the voluntary nature of the OT working hours. The business explained that the workers will be asked to sign on the OT working hours document, and are able to drop out of doing OT but that some workers do it at the last minute.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business to conduct training to this manager and any other supervisors that are found to be having the same behavior. The business should communicate to the manager what the company policy is on fair and ethical treatment of workers, especially of foreign migrant workers, and what are the disciplinary actions for those who do not follow those policies. 

-Recommend Issara Academy training to HR staff and Line supervisor. 

-Issara can also provide tailored training to full HR teams on-site, and provide systems review with tailored recommendations to eliminate labor risks. 
timeframe 2 pay periods 

-The business to make a clear announcement with all workers about the grievance channels to report such issues confidentially. This announcement should come from the HR manager and it should be clearly communicated to all workers including line supervisors and managers. The business should make sure a "no-retaliation policy" is in place, and that it is understood and followed by every employee.

description: Issues with overtime being involuntary/forced or illegal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Workers reported that the business allows only three workers to skip OT per day, however if there are more than three wokers who want to skip OT hours, they are not allowed to do so. In addition to that, the line supervisor are not allowing the workers to skip the OT  if they became sick at the last minute if they signed to do OT that morning. 

Talking Points
Is HR/management aware of this issue?
What are the production demand these days?  Is that putting pressure on supervisors to get more workers to work OT?

Recommendations for system change
The business should investigate whether supervisors are forcing and otherwise pressuring workers to work OT
The business should fully implement the OT policy, that OT is strictly on a voluntary basis and workers should in no way feel pressured to work OT if they don’t want to do so
The business should make a fresh announcement to workers that OT is to be worked on a voluntary basis

Time Frame; 1 week.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara has raised this issue with the business, the business agreed to conduct an investigation and get back to Issara.

IDENTIFIED POSSIBLE ROOT CAUSES
This may be due to misunderstandings between the supervisor and the worker.
- Workers have the right to request cancellation of the OT by requesting to cancel the OT in advance or within the morning of the signing date of the OT so that the factory can arrange the work in time, except in case of illness or emergency, the worker can cancel before OT hours.
- In this case, because the workers do not request cancellations in advance according to the policy procedures. In which the work segment has already prepared the raw materials, the worker's request to cancel the OT may cause the raw material to be damaged or/and other workers have to do more OT to fill the gap. The work segment, therefore, asked the workers to do the OT as agreement. However, there might be a communication discrepancy the workers understood that the supvisor is forced to do OT.

CORRECTIVE ACTIONS / REMEDY CONFIRMED BY SEAFRESH
1. 22-APR-2022: Clarify understanding to workers regarding the cancellation of OT in advance in order to avoid damage to the prepared raw materials
2. Re-training the supervisor to inform about the labor protection law. forced labor and Good Labor Practices in three sessions of the GLP & Business Ethics course on 21,22 and 23 April 2022.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that the business allows only three workers to skip OT per day. If there are more than three workers who want to skip OT hours, they are not allowed to do so. In addition to that, the line supervisor are not allowing the workers to skip the OT if they become sick at the last minute and they signed to do OT that morning.
remediation_action: The business investigated and responded saying that this may be due to a misunderstanding between the supervisor and the worker.  Workers have the right cancel OT in advance or within the morning of the signing date of the OT so that the factory can arrange the work in time.  In the case of illness or emergency, the worker can cancel before OT hour.  The business noted that there may have been incidents where workers did not cancel OT in advance and raw materials had already been prepared for processing, and so the supervisor asked the workers to work OT as their agreement that morning.  The business clarified with workers the process for skipping OT by cancelling in advance on April 22, 2022. The supervisors were also re-trained on the labor protection act and ensuring workers are not forced to work OT.

description: Issues with overtime being involuntary/forced or illegal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that the line manager sometimes makes workers work until 4:30-4:45pm even though the eight work shift ends at 4pm and they don't get paid OT for the extra working time.

NOTE: A few years ago, this manager had an issue with workers from Building 2, and she was moved to Building 3. She has a bad record, and the workers do not want to work with that manager anymore. The workers requested that Issara discuss this issue with the supplier and take serious action against her. The manager's name is P'Kyip.

TPs:
- How does the company record the time worked by its employees? How is the clock-in / clock-out system managed?

Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter: check why is it that the workers are working beyond their shift hours but are not being paid properly for it
- Repay workers for the time they worked and were not paid for their work
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Naruemon, HR, responded that HR is aware of the issue and has investigated it; the line manager has received a verbal warning. As the investigation result it was not the OT hours. It was that the workers kept things clean and organized before going home. Currently, the workers can finish the work on time.


IDENTIFIED POSSIBLE ROOT CAUSES:
The line supervisor's expectation for employees to speed up their work in accordance with the plan has led to instances of inappropriate behavior both in terms of verbal communication and physical actions.

CORRECTIVE ACTIONS / REMEDY:
On July 29, 2023, the HR Division manager talked to the supervisor in charge of Factory 2  to issue warnings regarding the following matters: 
1)Inappropriate behavior, both verbal communication and physical actions have affected workers.
2)Working time management and work plans for employees to have breaks and finish work on time. By providing a strong verbal warning notice aimed at fostering self-improvement. If inappropriate behavior reoccurs,  the line supervisor will be disciplined according to work policy.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that the line manager sometimes makes workers work until 4:30-4:45pm even though the eight work shift ends at 4pm and they don't get paid OT for the extra working time.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Review the time recording system that the company uses so that workers are paid properly for their work and line supervisors/managers are not able to force workers to work extra time and not pay them for it

description: Issues with overtime being involuntary/forced or illegal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the involuntary work on workers’ day off of the week. Workers from Roung Thor line (Textile machines) reported they were pressured to agree to work on their day off. The business threatened the workers saying they would be assigned to difficult jobs such as cleaning the sewers or they would be denied their diligence bonus (Bia Ka Yan) if they did not agree to work on their day off.  So, they felt they had to consent to working on their day off even if they didn’t want to do so. Workers also added that the manager switched their day off from Thursday to Tuesday without first consulting and getting their consent. 

Recommendations: 

-Regular shift hours and wages should be respected at all times, in line with contractual agreements. Changes in shifts should be made with the consent of workers and with reasonable notice, ensuring that total weekly working hours are in compliance with national law, and extra hours are paid at a premium rate. 
- Workers should not be forced or coerced to agree to the changes or to work on their day off. This includes threats to withhold certain benefits or to punish the worker in any way
- Shifts should not be changed in order to avoid paying premium overtime and holiday rates.
-The business shall conduct an investigation to find out why production demands are leading to workers being overworked, why line supervisors / managers are threatening to punish workers if they don’t agree to work on their days-off, and why the day-off was switched without prior consultation with the workers.  Appropriate disciplinary actions should be taken against the line supervisors / managers that are found to have inappropriately extracted consent from the workers to work on their days-off.  Appropriate training should be provided to supervisors / managers to improve their behavior in this regard.  Remediate the workers for the day-off that was switched to accommodate the factory’s production schedule. 
-The business is recommended to have conversations with the workers and come to an agreement for a fixed day off. 
The business should coordinate with the production and come up with a clear process to get workers consent in order to work on their day off without any coercion. Workers have the right to refuse to work on their day off so that they can make their personal plans for the rest. 
If there is work during the day off of workers, the business shall ask workers if they would like to work on that day, and if so, the business should pay the wages according to the LPA 2x and 3x for OT during day off. 
After the investigation process, the business should conduct communication in written and verbal with all workers who have been impacted by this issue.  

Talking Points: 
-Is HR aware of this issue? If yes, what has been the action plan to solve it? 
Are there any changes on the production which caused workers to change their day off from Thursday to Tuesday?  And if so, how is the business handling the workforce?
-In order to get workers consent to work on their day off, how does the business make sure that the workers fully consent and do so voluntarily?
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara has raised this issue with Nike given that the response from the Everest management was concerning for the previous issues, however, there was no clear respond from the Nike team upon this case. Issara has requested the Nike team to have a try party call to discuss this issue  but Nike has not respond on this request for several weeks. Issara has raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have the voluntary process for the workers to work on their day off and to agree to switch their day off.However, about the workers being assigned to do the cleaning tasks if they do not agree to work on their day off, the business responded having Five standard policy (cleaning, organizing, cleaning, standardizing, training, and discipline) and no workers to be pressured to do the cleaning. 

After the investigation result, the business responded that they have interviewed some workers and received the issues about switching day-off. For the switching day off, HR discussed and trained with production and supervisors that there would be no more switching days off, and that if they did, they would have to ask the workers and obtain their consent. Production and supervisors have received training and will proceed accordingly.

Issara is checking with the workers.

description: Issues with overtime being involuntary/forced or illegal
Issues with overtime being involuntary/forced or illegal
remediation_issara_recommendation:
WV Call Summary
---------------
This issue was reported by a worker named Ms.Poe Myar from MMP who is currently working in the fish-trimming line (C&D). Worker has reported that the line supervisor forces them to work OT till 10:00PM and does not allow them to skip OT. They start work at 7:30AM in the morning.

-------------------
KPI Issue Summary
-------------------
Issues with overtime being involuntary/forced or illegal 

----------------------
Other Related KPIs
----------------------
*** The worker reported 5 other issues that are dealt in relevant KPIs as outlined below: 
KPI#2392 - Issues with Break Timings and Rest periods
KPI#2394 - Occupational Safety and Health(OSH) issues. Irregular breaks issue is impacting the health of workers and some trimming line workers have started suffering from stomach problems. 
KPI#2393 - Insufficient lockers and security issues due to lack of CCTV cameras
KPI#2390 - Not enough tables and chairs in canteen

--------------------------------------------------------
Impacted Workers - Production Line/Shifts/Other Details
--------------------------------------------------------
500  - Worker is one of the 500 workers on the fish trimming line.

-----------------------------------------------
Additional O&E Fact-Finding Questions (if any)
-----------------------------------------------


----------------------------------------------
Relevant National Laws (Thailand)
----------------------------------------------

Thai Labor Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998) states the following in respect to OT work: 

1.Overtime Work and Overtime Pay
Section 24 & 25: Employers must obtain prior consent from the employee for overtime work. The employee has the right to refuse overtime work if it affects their health or safety, or if it conflicts with their personal obligations. Overtime work must be voluntary, meaning that workers cannot be forced to work overtime against their will. Any agreement to work overtime must be made freely by the employee.
Section 61: Overtime pay is required for any hours worked beyond the normal working hours. The standard rate for overtime pay is 1.5 times the employee’s regular hourly wage on regular work days.
Section 63: For work performed on holidays, overtime pay must be at least 3 times the normal hourly wage.

2. Working Hours and Rest Periods
Section 23: The normal working hours for factory workers should not exceed 8 hours per day and 48 hours per week. In cases where the work is deemed hazardous, the working hours should not exceed 7 hours per day and 42 hours per week.
Section 27: Workers are entitled to at least 1 hour of rest after working for 5 consecutive hours. This rest period cannot be counted as working hours.
Section 28: If an employer requires an employee to work overtime or on holidays, the employee must be compensated with overtime pay or holiday pay, as specified by the law.

3. Limitations on Overtime Work
Section 24&25: The Act limits the number of hours that employees can work overtime. This provision is designed to protect workers from excessive work that could endanger their health and safety. Generally, overtime cannot exceed 36 hours per week, though there may be exceptions in certain cases.

4. Payment for Overtime
Section 70: Overtime payments must be made on the next regular payday following the period in which the overtime work was performed. Employers are required to keep accurate records of all overtime work and payments.

-------------------------------
International/Global Standards
-------------------------------
Summary of the ILO standards on Overtime

ILO Conv 1 Article 6: Overtime should not be required unless agreed upon by the worker, and it should be voluntary. It also limits the number of overtime hours allowed, suggesting that normal working hours should not exceed 48 per week, with any additional hours subject to strict regulation. Specifies that overtime should be compensated at a higher rate than normal hours.

Article 10: Employers should keep transparent records of hours worked, including overtime, and ensure workers are informed about their rights and conditions of work.

ILO Conv 30 Article 7: Similar to Convention No. 1 Article 6 above, this article emphasizes the need to regulate overtime and limit it to protect workers' health.

ILO Recommendation No. 116 (Reduction of Hours of Work Recommendation), 1962 Para 7: Recommends that overtime compensation should be at least 25% above the regular wage, and encourages even higher rates where possible.

-------------------------------
Buyer CoC
-------------------------------
-------------------------------
ILM KPI Goal
-------------------------------
All overtime must be voluntarily consented to by the worker and paid at a premium rate in line with the law and employment contract. Numbers of hours of OT must be compliant with labour law as well.

---------------------------------
Possible Root Causes and Evidence
---------------------------------
-------------------------------
Environmental/Workplace Causes
-------------------------------
Plausible large orders or production demand spikes
Evidence: Reports of perpetual forceful OT for workers. 

----------------------------------
Business Systems/Shortfalls Causes
----------------------------------
Possibly understaffed factory  and management not hiring additional workers to cut costs. To avoid costs associated with machine downtime, the factory is possibly forcing workers to do OT perpetually.

Evidence: Workers have reported that forceful OT is a daily occurrence and supervisors do not allow workers to go home until 10PM at night when they have started their shifts at 7:30AM in the morning. 

------------------------
People-related Causes 
------------------------
Labor shortages due to a lack of available workers or high worker turnover rates. Unclear OT Policies and ignorance of labor laws by line supervisors
Evidence: Investigation needed

----------------------------------
Remediation Recommendations & TPs
----------------------------------
- Inquire from the business if the OT situation is temporary due to a spike in orders. Convey that since this seems to be a regular occurrence happening over a prolonged period of time, recommend the business to reassess workforce requirements as the number of workers may not be adequate to meet the production demands.
- Remind the business that according to the Thai Labor Protection Act, obtaining worker consent for OT is mandatory and all OT work must be voluntary. Workers should not be forced to work beyond their regular hours against their will. Workers have the right to refuse overtime and any retaliation by the line supervisor by denying them future OT work is unethical and unlawful.
- Adopt clear Overtime Policies: Communicate a clear overtime policy that outlines the conditions under which overtime may be requested. This policy should emphasize that overtime is voluntary and that workers have the right to decline without fear of retaliation. Include provisions that require management to provide advance notice of overtime, allowing workers to plan accordingly.
- Display the overtime policy in prominent areas within the factory in both Thai and other relevant languages spoken by the workers so both line supervisors and workers are aware of these policies. Ensure that all workers are aware of their rights regarding overtime, including their right to refuse.

---------------------------------------------
Worker Requests from Workers for Remediation
---------------------------------------------
Are the workers reporting the issue requesting anything in particular for remediation? - Workers want to skip OT when they do not want to do it.

Is the request from workers in line with international standards and norms?- YES

Is the request from workers safe for themselves, and presenting no possible risks or harms to others? - YES

In conclusion, can/should the request from workers be included in Issara’s recommendations to the business? - YES

What needs to be communicated back to the workers reporting the issue? -
That the issues have been communicated to the business and suggested action for remediation will also be communicated back to them through Issara.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Benefits to Business if the issues raised by worker(s) were properly addressed and no longer impacting the business’ operations/ workplace
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
By following these recommendations, MMP can ensure that overtime practices are compliant with Thai labor laws, respect workers' rights, and align with international standards/guidelines. This would not only help prevent forced overtime but also foster a positive and productive work environment with no retaliation against the worker, contributing to the overall success of the business and preventing any plausible future legal complaints and proceedings.

This would also help in retention of a satisfied workforce ensuring consistent production and help to uplift the brand image of the business infront of global buyers.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------
How could the issue, and Issara’s role in the remediation process with the business, be framed to the supplier (and the SP, if involved) as Issara helping to support that benefit (as a positive force)?
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Following Issara’s recommendations can help ensure that the business not only complies with Thai labor laws but also aligns with international best practices, providing a safe and healthy work environment for all workers and also strengthens their brand image and ethical work practices to global buyers making positive impacts on their sales and revenue.

Workers trust Issara and the business can leverage that trust to communicate policy changes, remediation measures and actions aimed at ensuring worker welfare and satisfaction. Issara can also help in educating workers on a number of issues and clarifying policies and rules that would prevent future disputes and confusion with the business.
remediation_notes: This issue was reported by a worker from MMP who is currently working in the fish-trimming line. Worker has reported that after forcing them with irregular breaks which are given at odd hours, the line supervisor forces them to work OT till 10:00PM and does not allow them to skip OT. They start work at 7:30AM in the morning.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- Ensure that workers are compensated fairly and transparently, with clear records of hours worked and pay received. The Thai LPA stipulates that all overtime pay must be at least 1.5 times the normal hourly wage and higher rates (usually 2X) for working on holidays.
- Encourage the business to provide training for line supervisors on respecting workers' rights, including the voluntary nature of overtime and the potential legal consequences of forcing overtime. Offer to schedule Issara Academy Line Supervisor Trainings.
- Educate workers on their rights under the Thai Labor Protection Act and international labor standards, empowering them to make informed decisions about overtime. Issara staff can help the business in this initiative.
- Recommend implementing a system for continuous feedback from workers regarding overtime practices. Use this feedback to refine policies and practices, ensuring they remain aligned with both legal requirements and ethical standards.
- The ILO encourages employers to promote a healthy work-life balance, which includes limiting excessive overtime to prevent burnout and health issues among workers. Hence, MMP should monitor the overall amount of overtime being requested and worked in the factory. If needed, consider implementing a cap on overtime hours to protect workers’ health and encourage workers to take regular breaks and utilize their entitled leave to prevent fatigue and promote well-being.

- What is the reason for requiring all workers to use the toilets on the third floor only?

- The business should ensure that workers, including pregnant workers, have convenient access to toilets.

They will investigate this case and get back to us within 7 days.

Case #1: 
The workers from factory 10 & 11 reported that during their lunch break, they have only 10-15 minutes left to have lunch because they have to spend so much time waiting in line for the following: 1) fingerprint scan, 2) change clothes, 3) get food, and 4) pay for the food. 

Case #2: 
In factory 11, the business uses a toilet pass-card system and they allow only 10 minutes for toilet breaks. Only one worker can go to the toilet at a time. In order to go to the toilet, a worker needs to get permission from the line supervisor, and get the toilet pass-card. There are many workers at each line so it is difficult to use the toilet when workers need it.

Recommendations for remediation:
- Investigate what is leading to the long lines during the lunch break that is leaving insufficient time for workers to enjoy their lunch; make appropriate changes to eliminate the congestion during the lunch break
- Review the toilet pass-card system, and make adjustments so that workers are able to use the toilet when they need to
