description: Issues with breaks including lunch/bathroom/OT breaks: minor issue with no violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client reported that the factory has two lunch breaks for the workers in the east and west buildings, with the 1st break from 11:30AM to 12:30PM and the 2nd break from 12:30 to 1:30PM. The workers have lunch during one break for two weeks and then switch to the other break hour every two weeks.  This frequent change in the lunch hour is negatively affecting the workers.  Those used to eating in the earlier hour feel starved when they have to switch to the later hour; when they have to switch back to the earlier hour again, they don’t feel hungry enough.  The business has applied this policy since the Covid-19 outbreak and it's been for almost a year. The workers would like to request that the business allow them to eat at the same time each day rather than having to switch back and forth every two weeks.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
She said that there are 13 workers working in Pine Apple Line C, and they usually start work at 7:30 and finish work at 4:30 in the evening. For the last two months, the line-supervisor has not allowed the workers to take a toilet break after 11:00 am and after 4:00 pm, saying in half an hour it will be the lunch break or the end of the work shift. Furthermore she allows the workers to go to the toilet one by one. 

TPs:
- What is the company policy regarding toilet breaks? Can workers go when and as needed?
- Is there a practice that only one worker from a line can go to the toilet at a time? Is that because a certain number of workers are needed for the line to operate normally? If so, how has this been communicated to the workers?

Recommendations:
- Workers should be able to use the toilet when needed, without having to wait for the lunch break or the end of the shift
- Communicate this clearly to all workers; train line supervisors so that they implement this properly and not limit toilet access at certain times
- Communicate clearly to workers production line requirements, such as a certain number of workers needed to be in a given line and how the company makes appropriate adjustments when workers take toilet breaks

description: Issues with breaks including lunch/bathroom/OT breaks: minor issue with no violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Last week, Marine Gold announced a new policy regarding restroom breaks for workers in the PR department. Previously, employees were allotted 15 minutes for a single toilet break, but now they are limited to 13 minutes. Those who exceed this time limit will face the following disciplinary actions:

1st offense: The line supervisor will issue a verbal warning to the worker. 
2nd offense: HR will summon the worker for a discussion. 
3rd offense: The worker will receive a first written warning. 
4th offense: The worker will receive a second written warning and will not be eligible to work overtime for one month. 
5th offense: The worker will be terminated from employment.

It's important to note that this same disciplinary process also applies to workers who arrive late for their shifts.

TPs: 
- What is the reason for this new policy? Is it because the business sees that some workers are taking breaks that are too long?  If so, what are the root causes of this?

Recommendations:
- Workers should be allowed to take toilet breaks when needed. The guidance on the length of these breaks should not be restrictive and punitive (leading to punishment for exceeding a time limit)
- Ask workers how long toilet breaks usually take, and how long they think the breaks should be
- Communicate with workers what the appropriate average toilet break should be, taking into account distance to the toilets from the work stations and the need to undress and redress the protective equipment of staff. Take out punitive measures regarding the toilet break policy

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that there is a written announcement that states that if workers take a toilet break longer than 13 minutes four times in a month, they won't get overtime hours for a month. If it happens five times in a month, they could be fired. Despite the employer saying the toilet break issue is not connected to overtime, this written announcement is connecting toilet breaks to OT. The worker suggested that MRG should really improve communication by making both verbal and WRITTEN announcements.

NOTE: This issue was only recently closed.

Recommendations:
- Retract the current written announcement.  Issue new written and verbal announcements to clearly state that there will be no punishment for taking long toilet breaks. 
- Managers and supervisors should be trained on this so that they can communicate this clearly to workers and implement the policy correctly
- Disciplinary measures to change the behavior of a few workers that may be seen to manipulate the toilet break policy should not be withholding overtime work or a threat of dismissal.

She'll send us the corrective action next week.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that there was a written announcement stating that if workers take a toilet break longer than 13 minutes four times in a month, a worker will not be allowed to work OT for a month and if it happens five times in a month, a worker could be fired.

DATE: 20 Oct 2023

Investigate Case:
This is due to PF3 line employees being assigned to replace other line employees that there is insufficient manpower. Each day, Line PF 3 replaces workers in another area and the arrangement is flexible dispatch to another line. It rotates based on the request from other departments. As a result, PF3 Line workers dispatched to another production line, would have break times the same as workers in that area. The workers will have uncertain break times if there is circulation to many areas. Each day is determined by the break time of the area being dispatched to assist.

Solution:
HR met with line PF3 workers via interpreter to discuss the break time arrangement for dispatching workers to help work in other departments. Workers are now organized as regular workers and have a fixed line, so they can take a break at the same time every day or not change frequently if necessary. It is organized as follows: 1. Take breaks when workers are aware of the situation of going to help in different departments at specific times and dispatching to help another line.  2. In the case of not going to help with work in another department, there will be two breaks: the first set at 10:30 a.m. or the second set at 11:00 a.m.


DATE: 14 Nov 2023

They are aware of the situation, according to the Issara update. They will speak with the supervisor to be trained on not forcing any workers to work after their shift has ended. They will communicate to all workers that no more than extra time is required for workers to work and that no one will be forced to work after the work time is completed by the end of November 2023.

remediation_action: HR investigated, and found that workers were being assigned to other lines with insufficient manpower and so would need to take breaks according to the schedule of that line. Workers are now organized as regular workers in a fixed line with regular break times but when they do need to be assigned to another line as per production demand, they should be aware that they will need to follow the break times of that line.

closed_notes:
Before Issara reached out to the business to discuss this issue, the worker reached out to HR and raised the case. HR conducted an investigation and talked with both workers involved (the supervisors and the client). The client updated that the supervisor denied the incident ever happened so no disciplinary actions were taken. However, the business encouraged the worker to reach out to the HR anytime she face such an issue again, so that the business can investigate and take action. In addition, the worker was also able to ask some questions she had about production, and the business responded to all of her questions. Now the worker updated that she felt satisfied with how the business handled the complaint and how she felt well with the business investigation even though the supervisor did not accepted any of the allegations. 

No actions were taken by Issara, as the client reported being satisfied with the business response and not needing any support. Thus, this case is being closed.

description: Verbal abuse and/or other poor treatment by HR or production (not illegal)
Verbal abuse and/or other poor treatment by HR or production (not illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that he was injured in the workplace while using the cutting machine on 13 Feb 2023 (Mr. Aung Thura, ID: 091190603052).  His fingernail was torn off and needed to take time to heal from the wound, with the doctor providing a medical certificate to stop work from Feb 13-20, 2023. His finger was still aching when he came back to work on 21 Feb, so he worked only in the morning and left in the afternoon. He requested HR to take additional leave on 22 Feb too. When he went to HR, the HR staff asked why he couldn't work because another worker with a similar injury had returned to work within a week. It seemed to him that HR didn't approve of his sick leave request. The issue is that he got the follow-up doctor's appointment on 23 Feb and doesn't have the MC for 21-22 Feb so is not sure if he will be paid for those days when he couldn't work.

He also added that if a Thai worker gets injured in the workplace, the business gives the workers 2,000-3,000 THB as a compassion fee. They also arrange the transportation for the Thai workers whenever they have follow-up visits with the doctor. For Burmese workers, there is no such support and feels as though there is preferential treatment to Thai workers.

TPs:
- Did this worker request sick leave on Feb 21-22nd?  What was HR's response?

Recommendations:
- The business should consider when the worker is fit to return to work, and if the injury is persisting should assist the worker in visiting the doctor again and getting the appropriate medical certificate to take sick leave for additional days required.
- If the business has not paid the worker for sick leave on Feb 21-22 because he doesn't have an MC for those days, reimburse him those wages because he was not fit to work and should have gotten to the doctor on Feb 21 and gotten a new MC.

description: Verbal abuse and/or other poor treatment by HR or production (not illegal)
Verbal abuse and/or other poor treatment by HR or production (not illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that a chief line supervisor (P Nway) asked the workers to use leftover starch powder that is used as batter for fried shrimp (tempura) in Oct 2022. It happened to the specific production at that time but is not happening anymore. The leftover starch powder which has turned hard P Nway collected and ground up to make it powdery again so that it can be used again. According to the worker, the texture of the powder is not the same as the original and it is difficult to create the shape of the food as desired.  Some of the food products coming off this line has been rejected at the quality control stage, and line supervisors were called for a meeting and investigated. According to the worker, those line supervisors may have shifted the blame onto the workers. The workers suggested that they should be invited for the discussion separately so that they can explain to the management what actually happened. They want to let the business know what is happening on the production line. 

The worker also reported that another line supervisor, P Skee, did not listen to the workers. In one incident, there was a small shrimp among the big shrimp in the package (all the shrimp should be the same size in the package), and the worker showed it to him and pointed out it should be checked and he should alert the other workers to be more careful. P Skee didn’t listen to the worker and let the production continue as if everything was fine. Because he doesn’t supervise the workers well, the workers are becoming more reckless and careless at work. The worker wants to let the business know about it. 

TPs:
-Does the company welcome feedback and suggestions for performance and quality improvement, no matter the level of the employee?  How can workers report concerns they might have about the quality of the products?
-Is HR aware that line workers have seen bad quality work that was overlooked by line supervisors, sometimes even after it was pointed out to the supervisor? 

Recommendations for remediation:
-Regarding the October incident with P Nway, were the line workers included in the investigation?  Conduct follow-up interviews with the workers, which could be very helpful to TUF, given that the workers have concerns about how the supervisor was having workers use bad quality ingredients.  Ensure worker safeguards according to TU's non-retaliation policy
-Announce to all workers how they can safely report any concerns about the quality of the products they are involved in producing.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Root Cause:
From investigation, The following facts were found:
1. Fried product production line pays attention to product safety and quality including the safety of workers. Because oil is used in frying, and various tools work in the production line which must comply with strict regulations
2. According to product quality control, the use of flour, can be reused within the specified period according to the production quality standards and there are random checks to ensure the quality control of the products in the production process, including requiring workers to strictly comply with hygiene requirements, such as washing hands every time during the washing cycle, and changing work equipment when it's time to change, including GMP (Good Manufacturing Practice) regulations, etc.
3. Khun Nui, the department manager, including the QC team, had a meeting with workers. and translate through an interpreter. To remind the various requirements that workers must comply with both preventively as well

Corrective Action:
HR trained the supervisors on how to listen to workers' opinions. Including providing information explaining quality standards, specifications, and methods for checking the quality of flour used to meet the standards for workers to have the same understanding.
If workers still have questions, they can ask the supervisors to clarify such doubts clearly

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The worker shared that while he was working, his hand got into the machine and was injured. The business doesn't care and takes no responsibility at all; they even called him to the HR office and scolded him. They said he is careless and doesn't pay attention at work. This is his second injury; the first injury got nine stitches on his hand and two stitches on the same hand for this second injury. But the business doesn't care about worker safety; at his workplace, it is very dangerous as he needs to work with sharp knife machines.

The other issue was that the worker mentioned that the factory cooperated with True Company, and they asked workers to subscribe to the True Sim card. The subscription is 200 baht per month, and it will be deducted directly from workers' accounts. Most workers want to refuse, but HR puts a lot of pressure on the workers to subscribe to the True Sim card by asking the interpreter to tell the workers that if they don't subscribe to the sim card, HR will consider eliminating them.

Recommendations:
- Workers should never be blamed for a workplace accident. Proper medical care should be arranged so that the worker can make a full recovery

Verbal abuse and/or other poor treatment by interpreter (not illegal)
Verbal abuse and/or other poor treatment by interpreter (not illegal)
closed_notes: TUF noted that interpreters in the production line don't receive proper training and for the interpreter in question, TUF noted that he had returned to Myanmar to renew his working permit and was still unable to return due to Covid-19 related border closures. In the meantime, workers that could help with interpretation temporarily would be trained on “Boosting Thai Language Communication”.  We could not contact the workers to confirm any business actions taken.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; This is an issue that comes from Building 5. The translator's name is Mr. Maung Zaw. The translator does not fully translate what the workers want to say. Issara recommendations. -The businesses to do immediate investigations and take action plan. -Safeguards should be in place during the investigations process.
-The business to revise the roles and responsibilities of the translators if needed. -The business to communicate with the workers about translators' roles and responsibilities. Talking Points; _What are the exact responsibilities of this translator? Is he officially appointed by the business? _What are the criteria for selecting/recruiting translators? _How often do the translators receive training? _How the business monitor the translation services? Workplace interpreters should be qualified and trained both in linguistic proficiency as well as professional conduct as a workplace interpreter. ☑ Accuracy. Interpreters should be aware of their responsibility to translate accurately and completely at all times, ensuring they do not leave out or embellish anything which either the employer or worker has said. Everything (including side conversations) must be translated, and the original tone and meaning of statements in the source language made must be preserved. Within 1 to 2 pay period.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
19 June 2020 The business investigation found the issue and committed to conduct training with the workers who have the ability to be able to help with the translation in the workplace. Issara also could not contact the workers from this specific building.

Issara could not contact the worker to confirm the issue.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: -The business to conduct frequent cross-check policy regarding translation services to make sure that the workers have access and proper translation services when needed. -Business shall communicate clearly (both in a verbal and written document) with all translators as well as all workers about the business policy on inappropriate behaviour. -Every detail information that was provided by the workes should be translated professionally. Communication. Effectively communicate to workers what the services are, the contact information of focal points and availability, actions that will be taken by the business for investigations and safeguarding, and timeframes. -Credible and safe grievance mechanisms should include transparency and safeguards for all workers. -Recommend Issara training to the translators. -Issara can also provide tailored training to full HR teams on-site, and provide systems review with tailored recommendations to eliminate labour risks."

description: Verbal abuse and/or other poor treatment by interpreter (not illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The line interpreter U Maung Pu is also not helpful in the production line if the workers requested him to support for some interpretation. He only interpreter what the supervisor would like to say to the workers and he asked the workers to talk to the supervisor by themselves if the workers would like to communicate with the line supervisor. He even mocked to the workers that even you report those case to the office, it will be in vain.

TPs:
- What is the role of the interpreter on the line?  Is this his full-time role or is he working on the line but also helping the others with interpretation?  What is expected of this interpreter and does he receive additional salary or other benefits for this interpretation role?

Recommendations:
- Interpreters should have the skills to be able to accurately interpret between the employer and employees, and to be objective and neutral in this role. He should be responsive to requests by the workers to interpret what they wish to communicate to their supervisors and any other staff. He should not neglect his duties nor verbally abuse or harass workers using his position of relative authority as compared to other workers who have to rely on him for interpretation support
- Ensure the interpreter understands his role and train the interpreter to be able to do his job effectively
- Assess and monitor the performance of all interpreters on a regular basis
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 24 Oct 2023

K. Somchoke, HR manager, explained that U Muang Pu is the production line interpreter, not an HR official interpreter. ITC has promoted this worker to help communicate with the Burmese worker on the PF3 production line. K. Rachade, HR, added that they are aware of this case because when Issara reported the issues in the PF3 line, they interviewed the workers and received feedback from the workers regarding this case. So they are investigating and trying to solve this case. They will respond with a corrective action plan within 7 working days.
remediation_notes: The interpreter in the production line only conveys messages from the line supervisor but doesn't help workers to interpret what they want to say to the supervisors and even mocks them saying their requests will not be heeded.
remediation_action: HR explained that this production line interpreter (not an HR official interpreter) was promoted to provide interpretation support for the Burmese workers. The business will investigate and will respond with a corrective action plan within 7 working days.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- Have a training program for interpreters on the production line so that they have clear expectations of their role and responsibilities
- Have a clear job description and appropriate salary and benefits to recognize the additional responsibilities the workers are fulfilling, both working on the line and providing interpretation support to his/her co-workers
next_description: get the business' corrective action.

DATE: 14 Nov 2023

On the follow-up remediation call according to K. Rachada, HR, the interpreter on the production line is a volunteer who works on the translation. There is no incentive or additional compensation for the interpreter. HR also provided interpreter training. They will, however, communicate all translations that the workers require, and the workers can contact the HR interpreter directly. They plan to communicate this clearly to all workers by the end of November 2023.

They shared the corrective action via email.
Investigation Result:
From the investigation of the facts Mr. Mongpu who is a volunteer interpreter in the production line provided information that in the case of language translation, he helps the supervisor communicate with workers. Sometimes too many workers struggle to speak, resulting in not being able to communicate every sentence. As a result, the supervisor was unable to listen to all workers at the same time. This makes the workers think that the interpreter is not impartial and refuses to help workers and the interpreter insists that there was no verbal abuse to workers or that the supervisor asked him to translate the scolding of the workers. description: Verbal abuse and/or other poor treatment by line supervisor/management (not illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that in the day shift at the T-6 line of the new building, she requested her line leader (blue-cap) to sign for her to get two new gloves (there are two types of gloves for different tasks, one for cleaning gloves and the other for chicken cutting) because both were old and can't be used any longer. But the line leader neglected her request and told her to get approval when the chief line leader comes. Actually the workers don't need to wait for the chief line supervisor who usually come at 8 am to get approval and Kathy Aung can approve this to get the gloves in time. So the worker went to the office and report this to Ma Dar (Office Translator) and came back to the production line. Around 2:30pm, the line leader yelled at her saying "How dare you report me to the office , don't you know your position and mine are different, that my position is higher then yours. And I don't care about you at all and you can report it to the office or Issara I don't F***king care. I really want top slap your face because your face shows no dignity nor grace. In this condition, Kyi Kyi feels so shy and feel very sorry. So she asked Issara for help.

Recommendations:
- Investigate the matter, identify the root cause of the issue. 
- Communicate the proper procedures for requesting and approving equipment replacements, so that line leaders and workers understand the procedures correctly.
- Ensure that there is clear communication regarding the non-retaliation policy anytime workers report grievances.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that they requested her gloves to be replaced but the line leader ignored it saying the worker should wait for the chief line supervisor. However, workers know that the line leaders have the authority to approve protective equipment replacements so they went to report this to HR. The line leader later yelled and cursed at the workers, and questioned why they had reported her to HR.
remediation_action: HR contacted Issara about this case and explained that they were aware of this case because the worker had come to report it to the HR interpreter. HR investigated by interviewing production line workers and reviewing the CCTV footage. HR discovered that the line leader had verbally abused the worker but then the worker had also chased the line leader and verbally abused her. So, they will both receive a written warning. Line leaders and workers will be trained on how to communicate professionally and also refresh the procedure for requesting glove replacements.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Review the grievance mechanism and to ensure there is no suppression of the mechanism and no retaliation against those using the grievance mechansim

And the worker was warned that if she complains again, she will be sent to another TUM plant.

- Based on the investigation result, revoke the warning that was issued to the worker that had provided feedback to the supervisor about being overloaded.
- Re-train line supervisors on appropriate ways of communication with workers and ensure they understand what is inappropriate and abusive communication / behavior towards workers.

description: Verbal abuse and/or other poor treatment by line supervisor/management (not illegal)
closed_notes: Issara is closing this case because the worker understands the product safety guidelines and the materials being used in the production process meet quality standards. The business interviewed workers during the investigation to get their direct feedback.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that a chief line supervisor (P Nway) asked the workers to use leftover starch powder that is used as batter for fried shrimp (tempura) in Oct 2022. It happened to the specific production at that time but is not happening anymore. The leftover starch powder which has turned hard P Nway collected and ground up to make it powdery again so that it can be used again. According to the worker, the texture of the powder is not the same as the original and it is difficult to create the shape of the food as desired.  Some of the food products coming off this line has been rejected at the quality control stage, and line supervisors were called for a meeting and investigated. According to the worker, those line supervisors may have shifted the blame onto the workers. The workers suggested that they should be invited for the discussion separately so that they can explain to the management what actually happened. They want to let the business know what is happening on the production line. 

P Skee often asks the workers to use leftover food ingredients which are not in good condition or quality. When there's a Chief supervisor, she wouldn't ask the workers to do so. But when the chief supervisor is not around, P Skee would ask the workers to quickly use those leftover ingredients. She would target and ask the workers to help out at other different lines if they talk back to her. And the worker said some batches of food were rejected as they didn't pass the Quality control.  Also, P Skee did not listen to the workers. In one incident, there was a small shrimp among the big shrimp in the package (all the shrimp should be the same size in the package), and the worker showed it to him and pointed out it should be checked and he should alert the other workers to be more careful. P Skee didn’t listen to the worker and let the production continue as if everything was fine. Because he doesn’t supervise the workers well, the workers are becoming more reckless and careless at work. The worker wants to let the business know about it. 

TPs:
-Does the company welcome feedback and suggestions for performance and quality improvement, no matter the level of the employee?  How can workers report concerns they might have about the quality of the products?
-Is HR aware that line workers have seen bad quality work that was overlooked by line supervisors, sometimes even after it was pointed out to the supervisor? 

Recommendations for remediation:
-Regarding the October incident with P Nway, were the line workers included in the investigation?  Conduct follow-up interviews with the workers, which could be very helpful to TUF, given that the workers have concerns about how the supervisor was having workers use bad quality ingredients.  Ensure worker safeguards according to TU's non-retaliation policy
-Announce to all workers how they can safely report any concerns about the quality of the products they are involved in producing.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Root Cause:
From investigation, The following facts were found:
1. Fried product production line pays attention to product safety and quality including the safety of workers. Because oil is used in frying, and various tools work in the production line which must comply with strict regulations
2. According to product quality control, the use of flour, can be reused within the specified period according to the production quality standards and there are random checks to ensure the quality control of the products in the production process, including requiring workers to strictly comply with hygiene requirements, such as washing hands every time during the washing cycle, and changing work equipment when it's time to change, including GMP (Good Manufacturing Practice) regulations, etc.
3. Khun Nui, the department manager, including the QC team, had a meeting with workers. and translate through an interpreter. To remind the various requirements that workers must comply with both preventively as well

Corrective Action:
HR trained the supervisors on how to listen to workers' opinions. Including providing information explaining quality standards, specifications, and methods for checking the quality of flour used to meet the standards for workers to have the same understanding.
If workers still have questions, they can ask the supervisors to clarify such doubts clearly
remediation_notes:
A worker reported that a chief line supervisor asked the workers to use leftover starch powder that is used as batter for fried shrimp (tempura) in Oct 2022. It happened to the specific production at that time but is not happening anymore. The leftover starch powder which has turned hard was collected and ground up to make it powdery again so that it can be used again. According to the worker, the texture of the powder is not the same as the original and it is difficult to create the shape of the food as desired.  Some of the food products coming off this line has been rejected at the quality control stage, and line supervisors were called for a meeting and investigated. According to the worker, those line supervisors may have shifted the blame onto the workers. The workers suggested that they should be invited for the discussion separately so that they can explain to the management what actually happened. They want to let the business know what is happening on the production line. 

The worker also reported that another line supervisor did not listen to the workers. In one incident, there was a small shrimp among the big shrimp in the package (all the shrimp should be the same size in the package), and the worker showed it to him and pointed out it should be checked and he should alert the other workers to be more careful. The line supervisor didn’t listen to the worker and let the production continue as if everything was fine. Because he doesn’t supervise the workers well, the workers are becoming more reckless and careless at work. The worker wants to let the business know about it.
remediation_action: The business investigated and explained that there are clear product safety and quality guidelines and the flour can be used within a specified period of time.  There are random checks to ensure production quality according to Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) regulations. The department manager had a meeting with workers and clarified this through an interpreter. HR also trained the supervisors on how to listen to workers' feedback and opinions.
remediation_validation: Issara updated the worker and she confirmed that she now understands clearly the product safety guidelines and until when raw materials can be used in the production process. She also mentioned that the behavior of the line supervisors has improved after the report.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because the worker understands the product safety guidelines and the materials being used in the production process meet quality standards. The business interviewed workers during the investigation to get their direct feedback.

KPI 2070 and 1626: on 16 October 2023, BHR called to follow up with Khun Krit. He has done the investigation in the cutting line and he insisted that there's no such case happened in the cutting line. On 30 September, he did the training on sick leave and leave in general, as well as, employer-employee communication, to all the line supervisors and conducted a special session with line supervisors in the cutting line. None of the supervisors had ever asked the workers to show a medical certificate for sick leave before. Often times when the workers want to take sick leave, the line supervisors give permission to all cases. None of the line supervisors accepted that they shouted at the workers or made the workers felt like they are servants.
He said he knows the worker who reported the issue but he didn't get a chance to talk to that worker. But he just talked to all the line supervisors in the cutting line. There're just a few line supervisors in that line. None of them accepted that such case ever happened. Khun Krit is happy to conduct further investigation and talk to the worker. BHR will follow up with him again at the end of this week.

20 Oct 2023: Khun Krit investigated yesterday by talking to 5 Myanmar workers in the cutting line one by one in his office, including the one he thinks has reported the issue. He asked questions like, "Have any of the supervisors ever made you feel like a servant?", "Do you feel like doing excessive work?", or "Have you ever been asked to show a medical certificate by a supervisor before?".  Everyone said no even when Khun Krit confirmed that they won't be targeted or there won't be any threats or retaliation against them. So I told him that we would have our O&E officer validate with the workers.

description: Verbal abuse and/or other poor treatment by line supervisor/management (not illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
She reported that she was asked to go and assist other sewing lines without getting any extra pay. Normally if a worker is asked to go and assist in another line, he or she receives an extra 40 THB per day as an incentive. On 16 Jun, her line supervisor P'Cha-Phai, All (Chief) Supervisor P'Chun-Phue, and technician (coach) P'Mae Sar, asked her to go and assist other lines as needed. At the end of July, she reported this to her supervisor but the supervisor dismissed her saying they hadn't asked her to go and assist in other lines. Then she went and reported it to the Burmese HR interpreter (Min Han Win Aung) and he said that since she didn't sign any documents regarding this, they cannot give her the extra payment. The client then asked, why hadn't they asked her to sign anything? The HR interpreter escalated this with the line manager Mae' Pha, and she also said the same thing: no record, no payment. 

The client asked the line manager to have her assigned to one specific line but they still had her work in other lines as needed.  She wants us to help her by having HR solving the issue properly with the unprofessional line supervisor. If they cannot pay her extra pay like the others, they should have her assigned to one line. She would like to work in another building as she doesn't want to work there anymore and she fears being targeted too. If possible, she would like to get the incentive pay she should have received for those days that she was assigned to help other lines. The client's name is "Mrs. Pan Pa Pa Phyo", ID:111140500, line no.A-16.

Talking points:

Recommendations for remediation:
-Investigate this matter, with worker safeguards because this worker fears retaliation, and identify why the supervisor had this worker work on different lines and then denied that she had asked the worker to do this?
-Discipline the supervisor according to the company's disciplinary policy if the investigation establishes that the supervisor did not treat the worker fairly and denied her the additional pay the worker is entitled to
-Communicate clearly with all workers about the incentive system, and what actions or performance will result in what monetary incentives, how it will be recorded and paid out

description: Verbal abuse and/or other poor treatment by line supervisor/management (not illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client reported that the chief line supervisor from E-Zone (P' Watt), often comes to the E-Zone line workers (especially to Walk-in workers in E-Zone) and accuses them of working slowly because they haven't been getting OT work since the Songkran Festival. But workers are trying to reach the target of 200 shirts within the 8-hour shift, regardless of whether they get OT or not.  They feel the chief supervisor is complaining for the sake of complaining and when she says, "if you don't want to work here, you can resign anytime and go back to Myanmar and we have many more to come", it hurts their feelings because of the unstable political and economic situation back home in Myanmar.

Recommendations:
- Supervisors should be verbally encouraging and affirming, rather than disparaging to the workers under their supervision
- To suggest migrant workers go back home is a xenophobic remark that is unprofessional and should not be spoken by supervisors in any circumstance
- Any criticism of low performance should be based on actual productivity numbers, and accompanied with advice on how to improve performance not verbal threats to leave the country.

This regard is about emotions at work, and everyone has different emotional controls. This is difficult to

(via Complaint box, internal hotline, and VOS (Voice of Stakeholders)) and reports to the top management

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client worked at a Korean BBQ restaurant located in KL Kepong Jalan Metro Perdana, which is one of fifteen branches of the restaurant chain. Out of the fifteen branches, this particular one was problematic. The restaurant has six Nepali and thirteen Burmese workers. The owner's son is abusive towards the Nepali workers, creating a hostile work environment. Issara is able to speak with two workers. They have been working for this employer for 10 months. They are all MoU workers. They are reporting as a group of 5 Nepali workers, but the client is quietly reporting. The client and the workers want to either be transferred to another branch under the same company or find employment in another company. The client has debts to pay and doesn't want to return to Nepal. The workers have a contract they made in Nepal, but the company made another contract which the client doesn't have and is unaware of its contents.
Following are the major issues reported by workers.

1) Document retention: Workers passports are held by the employer since they started their employment. The company also kept their passports and didn't provide them with worker ID cards (Jalan cards) or necessary documents. 

2) Restriction of Movement: The workers were not allowed to leave the premises, and this restriction also made it difficult for their friends to visit them.

3) Unfair suspension: Workers were frequently suspended for minor mistakes or even without any reason. During these suspensions, the company did not provide any food, and the workers were not allowed to go out and get their own. They were also denied access to basic amenities, like cooling fans, during these periods. One incident occurred when a friend of the client was suspended for simply asking a Burmese worker to clean a stain. The owner verbally abused him and kept him in detention (suspension) for 28 days. Throughout this time, the company did not provide any food or salary, leaving the workers in a dire situation. His friends attempted to provide food secretly, but they had to be cautious as the company would punish them if they were caught bringing in more substantial amounts of food or any food. 

Recently, the victim was suspended by the company for two months. During this period, he received no salary or food from the company. The suspension was a result of the employer demanding the victim to memorize the restaurant menu quickly.

If workers demand to change the employer, they are asked to work 4 months without pay and there are some workers who have accepted this situation as they could not bear the harsh working environment. 

4)Physical abuse: Physical assault includes being kicked, slapped on the face and belly, and having ears pulled. The employer even physically assaulted the client's genitals. Such harassment occurred almost daily and targeted everyone except.

5) Long working hours and incorrect payment: Workers have to work 14-15 hours a day. In return, they received a basic salary of 1500 RM and a 300 RM overtime allowance each month. 

6) Lack of Sick Leave: Even when the workers fell ill, they were forced to work, as the owner wouldn't allow them to stay in the hostel. 



Moreover, during salary payment time, the owner would abuse the workers and suspend them for minor mistakes. The owner often used the workers as a target for his frustrations, taking out his stress related to the business on them. Whenever the business is slow he will start abusing the worker for no reason.

description: Verbal abuse and/or other poor treatment by line supervisor/management (not illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported for the past couple months, they have not been given OT hours, with the manager citing a lack of orders but when there is OT, it is not given to Bangladeshi workers but given to Nepali and Myanmar workers.  The business also force them to meet daily targets which have been increased. When workers raise the issue of these increased targets, the employer will tell them they can leave and go back to Bangladesh if they can't keep up.

NOTE: The worker would like Issara to raise this issue with the business but doesn't want his identity to be disclosed.

Recommendations for the employer: 
- The employer should communicate clearly to workers about the production demands and the forecast for OT hours in the coming months. 
- The employer should clarify that daily targets are not tied to the daily wage. Workers are to be paid per 8-hour shift as per the contract, whether or not targets are met. Any time worked beyond the 8-hour period should be paid as OT.
- The employer should have an equitable and non-coercive OT system that doesn't favor workers from any nationality over another. Communicate how OT hours are offered to workers to show that it is fairly distributed and non-discriminatory

description: Discrimination – by gender/nationality/ethnicity/other by employer's systems
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A group of 11 workers who have submitted resignation a week ago and were preparing to depart are not being allowed to go by the business. The workers reported that their belongings were taken by the business when they were about to leave in a van and that they now do not have a place to stay since they have already given back their rooms. Workers reported the reason for leaving job is as follows:
(1) discrimination against nationalities at the workplace,
(2) the business not keeping the promise of paying double for the working hours during COVID-19 restriction as promised,
(3) translator not being helpful and being biased by just listening to the business and not the workers. 

Recommendations: 
-As it is a worker's right to resign and leave the company, the business shall immediately investigate why this group of workers were not allowed to leave. And then come to an agreement with workers for their departure from the company without restrictions.
-Since the business made the taxi driver leave without the workers, it will be challenging for workers to find a new driver, therefore, the business is suggested to help workers find a new taxi/van for workers safe return. -Since the vaccination is a workers personal health matter, the business should provide vaccination cards or any support documents as proof that workers have received vaccination. If the business does not have such documents, the business should coordinate with the health organization that provided the vaccine to make sure all workers receive the vaccination card. 
-The business should immediately check with all workers and provide their missing daily wages if any. 

System Change:
-It is the  business responsibility to have good working conditions that allows workers to feel ethically and fairly treated. This will reduce workers turnover rates, as workers would not feel the need to leave the job. In order to assess the level of satisfaction of workers and identify the areas of improvement, the business is recommended to conduct an internal survey or Issara’s worker satisfaction survey to address the root cause of the issue and improve the system. 
-The business to communicate with the HR and the security guard about the business policy on freedom of movement and rights to make decisions. The communication should include the action that will be taken against the offender. 
-The business should communicate with all the workers about their plan to improve the working conditions and maintain the workers. Otherwise, there could be more workers planning to leave the job. 

Talking Points: 
-What is the reason why this group of workers were stopped by HR? 
-Is business aware of this issue? 
-Workers have reported several workers leaving the job because of several repeated issues in the workplace, what is the business understanding of this? Does the business seek workers' feedback and have done anything to improve the working condition rather than stopping workers from leaving? 
- What was communicated to workers as reasons for not being allowed to leave the company?
-What was the reason for the business calling the police and threatening the workers? 

Added TPs; 
Because workers have resigned and are asking to depart, this situation should be addressed in less than the 3-4 day timeline suggested by SCC.
No resigned worker can be held against their will, or coerced into returning to work
Resigned workers can be provided vaccine certificates and COVID tests to ensure there are no positive cases before departure
Workers can be clearly offered a return to work, with no coercion, and with clear communication on next steps
Because this situation has escalated, Issara can jointly speak with HR and the group of workers if desired, to support communication.
Issara also recommends we provide training to HR reps at SCC, on COVID and other protocols for workforce management.

ETI Base Code 1.2. Employment is freely chosen; workers not required to lodge deposits or documents with employer, and free to leave with reasonable notice

Workers off-shift should be free to leave their workplace and dormitories, with no threats or assertions of control over their movements. Workers should never be treated as the property of employers, recruiters, brokers, or agents; and, their movements should never be restricted by these actors. Workers should be free to leave their jobs with reasonable notice.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had meetings including escalation call with the business immediately. The business argued that since the workers are under Bubble and Seal measures, it is not allowed for them to cross the     Bubble and Seal area and the COVID-19 provincial cross restriction. The business also added that since the taxi driver who came to pick up the workers was from another province, the business take it as illegal act , therefore the business wanted to make sure that their workers are not being cheated by the brokers. In addition to that the business added that they have responsibility to inform the policy about workers departure. Issara emphasized that since the workers have already submitted their resignation and they do not feel they are belong to SCC anymore, the business has no liability to control the workers movement. The business responded that they will escalate to their MD and get back to Issara.  It has been 4 four days that the workers are being forced to stay in the the SCC B&S housing against their will.
remediation_notes: A group of 11 workers who had submitted their resignation letters a week prior were preparing to depart by van when they were not being allowed to go by HR staff and the security guard.  They also packed up and left the company dormitory so now have no place to stay.
remediation_action:
Issara reached out to the business immediately.  The business explained that HR had communicated to the workers about the government's travel restrictions to prevent the spread of Covid-19, and that they are not allowed to travel outside Songkhla province because it is currently a Covid-19 red zone.  They said police had come to enforce the travel restrictions and the van driver left without taking the workers after talking to the police.  Regarding vaccination certificates that would be important for when the workers travel back to Myanmar, the business said the document issuance was delayed by the hospital and would be provided to the workers when issued.  For now, the business said the workers are still living in the private dorm and the workers can ask the landlord to stay in the same place. 

The business will get back to Issara with corrective actions within 3-5 days.

The business further updated Issara saying pictures of HR staff with negative comments regarding this incident had been posted on social media and they wanted the workers to remove the posts.

Issara escalated this issue with TU's Sustainability Director, and recommended that no worker that had already resigned should be held against their will or coerced into returning to work.  TU explained that they didn't want the workers leaving the province illegally given the current Covid-19 restrictions.  The Sustainability Director said they would escalate the matter to the factory MD.  The following day, TU completed the process of issuing official separation documents for the workers so that they can leave.
remediation_validation:
Issara followed up with the workers and provided an update, explaining that the business had said they were following government rules of not allowing inter-provincial travel and that the business would get to Issara in 3-5 days about next steps.  

The workers did not want to stay there anymore; they felt pressured and forced to go back to work.  They were even willing to pay any government fines if there were any for crossing province lines.  Since they have resigned, they don't understand why the business is not letting them leave.  They just want to be able to travel back to Myanmar. 

Regarding the social media posts, the workers said they did not take any photos or videos during the incident nor did they post anything on social media or ask their friends to do so.

The workers have confirmed that they have officially resigned from their jobs and are free to leave.
remediation_results: The business processed the official resignation of the workers and the workers have been allowed to leave.

description: Discrimination – by gender/nationality/ethnicity/other by employer's systems
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: this issue is related to the line supervisor treating workers poorly by threatening them to be sent to SCC if the can't reach the target. Workers also reported the discriminative behaviour of the same supervisor. This case is related to ID call 8964.  

The business should take action by conducting a proper investigation taken into account workers feedback and guaranteeing workers safeguards. Business to provide a verbal warning to that specific supervisor.

Timeframe: one payment period.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
16 March 2020 
The business said that they could not investigate individual supervisors because there are 13 supervisors in the same position from this line. That is why the business agreed to conduct communication with all of the supervisors including dos and don't regarding fair treatment in the workplace. The business also added that the supervisors promised to improve their behaviour. 

20 Apr 2020
The worker reported that the line supervisors in this line are behaving better now. Since then, Issara did not receive any complaints from the workers until the month of August. That is why this case was considered to be closed.
remediation_notes:
Talking points:

-Provide information about the working line and the line supervisor. Important note for BHR: the information about the client should NOT be shared with the business, but it is safe to share the information about working line and line supervisor. 
-Remind the business to have safeguards in place while conducting the investigation and that workers should not be blamed or targeted for reporting issues. 
-How is the target calculated for each worker/line and how is that target communicated to workers?
- Provide recommendations for remediation and system change
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business should provide training to line supervisors on ethics and how to treat workers properly. 
-The business should inform line supervisors what are the disciplinary consequences for those who do not follow the company policies and codes of conduct. 
-The business to revise if the targets provided to workers are realist and fair to all workers. 

Communication.
-The business should communicate to worker what are the grievance mechanisms available, who the focal person is, and guarantee safeguards are in place. In case the issue is related to line supervisors, the business should provide different channels for workers to raise their concerns safely.
systems_change_business_steps_taken: The supervisors received training.

remediation_issara_recommendation: Context: this is an issue with Cambodian workers being discriminated by their line supervisors and by Thai workers. The discrimination is leading to issues with toilet breaks and unfair treatment.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:

-The company policy should be clear on the prohibition of discrimination and what are the consequences for those who do not follow those policies. 

- In order to improve the relationship between Thai workers and foreign migrant workers, it is recommended that the company creates an environment of equity and cultural understanding. 

-The business should investigate what are the root causes of the issues, the extend of the issue (how many impacted workers there are and how they feel) what is causing the discriminatory attitudes from supervisors and workers? This issue should be taken as highly important by the business as the business should follow the buyers' CoC and ETI base code. ETI Base Code 9.1. No harsh or inhumane treatment allowed: physical and verbal abuse, threat of abuse, and sexual or other harassment prohibited.

description: Discrimination – by gender/nationality/ethnicity/other by employer's systems
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The workers reported that the line supervisor, P'New, in Line no.5 and other supervisors discriminated against Burmese workers.  The following examples of discrimination were reported.  
1) She is often verbally abusive, shouting at the Burmese workers if they did something wrong with their sewing task or asked to go to the toilet while she doesn't say anything to the Thai workers.
2) When the Burmese workers asked to change the working line, the supervisor denied their request but she allowed the Thai workers to change lines if requested
3) The supervisor pushed the heavier workload onto the Burmese workers, asking them to work on 2-4 tasks while the Thai workers handle only one.  When pieces accumulated where the Thai workers are working, the supervisor asked the Burmese workers to go and assist, but the reverse wasn't the case.
4) When a worker qualifies to start getting incentive pay is dependent on the supervisor's assessment. The Burmese workers say that they have to wait 1-2 months while Thai workers are entitled to get the incentive within 2-3 weeks.
5) There is a Thai woman who is assigned to replace the needles when they break during operation. This lady spoke loudly and blamed the Burmese workers when they asked for new needles but is nice to the Thai workers. She does not even give the workers pens to note down the stock-in/ stock-out and the workers have to bring the pen by themselves. 

The workers want to have clear policies and that everyone is treated equally.

Recommendations for remediation:
The business to investigate this matter with proper worker safeguards, especially the behavior of the supervisor in line #5 and the supervisor in charge of replacing the needles for the workers
The company’s non-discrimination policy to announced to all workers, and note channels to safely report incidents of discrimination
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K.Witsawad, Senior Management- comments on what the workload means by the worker because everyone works at the same time starting from 8 am and finishing 5 pm then continuing OT. The factory also has a clear policy. What is the workload meant by Burmese workers? Do they work more than 8 hours a day? 
He added the verbally abusive - that he and the HR team will go and check in the field and ask all the production line supervisors how they communicate with the workers. If he found the case he would always not allow this kind of issue to pass and let it be. This will take one week and get back to us.

The investigation result:
Reasons to speak loudly Because there are other sounds in the production area, such as the sound of the engine or the wind, it is necessary to speak loudly so that both Thai and Burmese workers can hear, but did not criticize or criticize the workers.

The balance of work has the following criteria;
1.Cycle Time of each step
2. Skills of each worker
3. Balance principle according to Yamazumi, if the sewing process takes less time, Cycle Time must add more jobs or allow sewing in other steps.
As a result, the supervisor's responsibility in line sewing is to maximize efficiency. Workers who can request changes to the sewing process will make the process difficult if there will be no sewing workers.

- communication techniques

- Effects that may occur in case of inconsistent practice

Employees must prepare for needle changes by doing the following:

According to the rules and regulations, workers would be warned, either verbally or in writing, if they violated work regulations. It has nothing to do with discrimination.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker raised the issue regarding bonuses provided to workers at Everest. The Cambodian workers received a very small annual bonus of 2,000 baht if they had a good record of working without taking any leave but Thai workers received a much higher annual bonus amounting to an additional month's salary. This practice has been going on for five years.

TPs:
- This has been raised with the business previously. The earlier response was that this was a decision made by management at the parent company in Taiwan.

Recommendations:
- The annual bonus should be given to workers on a fair basis, without discrimination based on nationality.  There is a significant difference in the annual bonus being provided to Cambodian workers as opposed to Thai workers, and this is seen as discriminatory based on nationality.
- Consult with management in Taiwan regarding this practice, given that the Thai LPA requires that workers are treated equally regardless of nationality
- Communicate clearly to workers that they will be treated fairly and without discrimination based on nationality

closed_notes: This is rated as "Good" because the business has introduced a QR code with all workers where they can access the grievance and learn the inquiries that the workers may have. Workers also confirmed that they have seen the QR code. Since then, Issara has not received a complaint from the workers.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: the business has appointed two focal persons (P Kung and P Saung)from HR for workers to approach in case of having any issue. However, according to workers' feedback, the focal persons are not available most of the time since they have many meetings. Also, many workers indicated that they do not know to whom they should report if they have an issue. Workers also shared that there have to get permission from, line leader, supervisors, senior supervisors, and office translator to see this assigned person which is very hard for the workers.

Talking points: explain to the business what is the feedback from workers and the challenges they face to access the grievance mechanism. And provide recommendations for system change.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:

-Communication. Effectively communicate to workers what the grievance mechanisms are, the contact information of focal points and availability, actions that will be taken by the business for investigations and safeguarding, and timeframes. 

-Credible and safe grievance mechanisms should include transparency and safeguards for all workers.  

-Training and planning sessions with Issara and HR on strengthening grievance mechanisms, then broader training for line supervisors and others.

Workers reported seeing a newly announced QR code. Since then, Issara has not received an additional report from the workers.
systems_change_business_steps_remaining: -Training and planning sessions with Issara and HR on strengthening grievance mechanisms, then broader training for line supervisors and others.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
During the most recent canteen outreach, the workers were informed to go back into the production line right after finishing lunch, and they were asked not to stay outside. The manager, line supervisors, and interpreters were watching who was talking with Issara's staff. So, no one dared share any information during the visit. The worker also reported that after the canteen outreach, the production manager asked the workers what Issara staff had talked to them about, and who was currently communicating with Issara staff. 

Recommendations:
- The business to publicly endorse workers using all available grievance channels, including both internal and external ones like Issara's, and should not in any way discourage workers from reaching out and reporting issues.
- Management and supervisors shouldn't exhibit behaviors that can be perceived by workers to be efforts at suppressing workers' freedom to express their grievances and report issues
remediation_business_steps_taken: John, Ana, and Pick discussed with K. Tithipol, Senior Human Rights Specialist from Tesco first. Because NR Instant does not want to talk with Issara directly. So the Issara team discussed with K. Tithipol how to address the issues. He suggested that he would set the tri-party call for Tesco, NR Instant, and the Issara team to have a remediation call.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that when Issara staff visited, the business informed them to go back to their production lines right after finishing lunch, to limit their interaction with Issara. The manager, line supervisors, and interpreters were watching who was talking with Issara staff so no one dared share any information during the visit. The worker also reported that after the visit, the production manager asked the workers what Issara staff had talked to them about, and who was currently communicating with Issara staff.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Review the grievance mechanism policy and the evaluate how effective the grievance channels are.  Revise the policy and/or protocols as appropriate to ensure both internal and external channels are active, responsive, and safe for workers to use

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that since February 7th, 2024, Gimmill announced workers will now only receive 50 RM for their medical checkups. Simply put, if a worker falls ill and visits the hospital's clinic, the company will reimburse them only 50 RM and any additional medical expenses will be the responsibility of the worker. The worker stated that the typical cost of a clinic visit ranges from 80 to 90 RM so this will become a financial burden and this policy is against the terms in their employment contract, which explicitly states that the employer is responsible for medical expenses. The company announced this change during a meeting with the workers. Despite protests from the worker, the company dismissed the objections. 

TPs:
- What are the requirements in terms of buying health insurance for migrant workers? If all workers are to be ensured, why has this policy change been instituted?

Recommendations:
- Any changes in the policy of wages and benefits should not go against what is stated in the employment contract and medical expenses should be covered as part of the insurance scheme, as required by law
- Communicate clearly to all workers about the details of the health insurance coverage and that medical expenses will be covered according to the insurance policy

description: Threats aiming to discourage lodging grievances
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that a fellow worker was punished for making a mistake in her task of not putting in a wifi chip into a device. She was made to write "I will never forget to put the chip into the device" 5,000 times as punishment. Even after this, she was made to hold up a poster displaying her punishment for a whole day. She reported this to HR (factory 6), feeling that this punishment was extreme. The line leader (P' Nata) was called into the office and both this line leader and the worker ended up receiving warning letters. Afterwards, the line leader threatened the worker saying she as the line leader would never get dismissed even if the worker were to report her and the line leader made her keep standing and holding up the poster.  All the workers are afraid to use the grievance mechanism, given what happened to this worker.   


Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter to establish how this worker report was handled and why the worker was not protected from the line leader that she made a complaint about. HR should handle any worker complaints in ways that ensures their safety.
- Consider withdrawing the warning issued to the worker
- Train line leaders / supervisors on the company's disciplinary policy and what disciplinary measures are considered to be appropriate and not appropriate
- Clearly communicate what disciplinary measures workers should expect for what kind of mistakes they make.  
- Clearly communicate that the company has a non-retaliation policy, and how the company will make sure workers are safe if and when they report any issues
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 14 Nov 2023

K. Piyabutr, CSR explained that according to the company policy, there is no punishment to write 5,000 sentences. However, this punishment might have come from the supervisor. They will investigate this case with worker safeguard and they will communicate to all employees that the has a non-retaliation policy. They will update and get back to us with the corrective action by next week.

Miscommunication between worker and foreman on how to handle the disciplinary action and re-training processes.

Discuss with this operator to describe the re-training processes. – Status : done on 14 Nov 2023

description: Threats aiming to discourage lodging grievances
remediation_issara_recommendation:
When the Issara team conducted canteen outreach and housing outreach in August 2022, many workers did not approach Issara staff in front of the Seafresh interpreter, HR staff, and dorm in-charge. Many workers felt uncomfortable when Issara staff approached them; they were guarded in their speech and did not respond openly and when Seafresh staff were nearby, the workers hid their face from the Seafresh staff. When Issara staff had moments with the workers without being observed by Seafresh staff, some workers said that they had heard second-hand information from previous workers that the line supervisors and HR staff did not like workers contacting Issara and that workers were targeted afterwards for doing so.  That's why they felt uncomfortable interacting with the Issara team.

Talking points:
- Is HR aware that the workers are feeling this way?
- How is HR communicating to workers to make it clear to them that Seafresh has a non-retaliation policy and that the business protects the right of workers to use worker voice channels, including Issara's?

Recommendations:
- Post a fresh announcement and make a verbal announcement to all workers that all have the right to express themselves without fear of retaliation by using any worker voice or grievance channels, including Issara's.
- Train all line supervisors about the non-retaliation policy and the disciplinary measures that will be taken if any supervisor attempts to suppress worker voice.  Use case studies to illustrate how and in what circumstance workers might be afraid to use worker voice channels, and how supervisors should promote rather than suppress worker voice.

K. Naruemon, HR emailed us the corrective action plan as a file attached.

The company encourages employees to voice suggestions or complaints via any and all channels. The Issara Institute is one of the firm channels HR always announces to employees as the grievance mechanism channel.

1. Public relations: on-board grievance channels, orientation training, and open talk discussion sessions

 -Target: daily employees 100%
3. Refresh training for the supervisor and leader on the labor protection law, forced labor, and good labor practices in the course GLP & Business Ethics.

description: Threats aiming to discourage lodging grievances
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that line supervisors were telling that them the company does not work with Issara anymore, implying that workers shouldn't reach out to Issara anymore. Workers want to know if this is really true because they think the line supervisors don't want them to reach out to Issara.

TPs:
-Although LB's customer is no longer Issara's Strategic Partners, we are still committed to making sure that if any worker has any issues or wants to reach out to Issara, we are there for him/her.
-Was this communication that LB no longer works with Issara from management or was this just something that line supervisors have assumed on their own and told the workers?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, that Issara is still available and workers can reach out to us at any time, that LB management endorses and promotes this worker voice channel, and that any suppression of worker voice will not be tolerated
remediation_business_steps_taken:
HR will consult with management regarding communicating to all workers, verbally and in writing, that Issara is still been a partner and the workers can reach out to Issara at any time.

BHR followed up with K. Leena, HR manager. She responded that now she is drafting the announcement and in process of translation. All three issues will be verbally announced via the morning talk session and written announcements will be posted on the boards around the factory. She will finish these things and get back to us by this week.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that line supervisors were telling that them the company does not work with Issara anymore, implying that workers shouldn't reach out to Issara anymore. Workers want to know if this is really true because they think the line supervisors don't want them to reach out to Issara.
remediation_action: HR will consult with management regarding communicating to all workers, verbally and in writing, that Issara is still been a partner and the workers can reach out to Issara at any time.
remediation_validation: Issara will follow up with the workers to let them know that the business is likely to make an announcement that they can continue to report any issues to Issara in the near future
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for remediation:
-Develop a non-retaliation policy that clearly states that workers are to be encouraged to use any worker voice channel, including Issara's, and that there will be clear disciplinary measures taken against those that suppress worker voice or retaliate against workers that have spoken out.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The issue with the translator who does not help or respond to the worker's issues. When workers try to access the translator he says that the HR is busy, it is impossible to raise this issue, or do not help the workers when workers need help in the production line.  Name - Htay Lwin. Station - office translator. 

Recommendations; 

-To conduct immediate investigations about the translator. The investigation should include workers' voices with the safeguard for the workers. Workers have reported that they have challenges accessing the company grievance mechanisms and requesting for support as this is generally blocked by the translator. Therefore, the company should take all necessary actions to access the translator response to workers and to make sure the translator role is clear (he/she should translate whatever workers would like to discuss with HR, he/she should not make decisions on what should or should not be mentioned to HR). 

-The business should take disciplinary actions towards the translator or any staff discouraging workers to use grievance mechanisms

(May-10th-2021) Added talking points. 

-Clarify with the business that the translator being reported by workers is Myat Shwe, therefore it is recommended for the business to follow previous recommendations on investigation and training for this specific translator. 
Please emphasize that the worker's main report here is about the attitude, workers reported that when they ask for help, the translator says that the office is busy or their issues are impossible to raise.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
HR responded that Htay Lwin is not an interpreter according to the employee list. There are three interpreters please find names as follows
Than Tar Aye (Ta Ta Ae) 
De De Lai, 
Myat  Shwe (Me Chui)
Day Shift - Myat  Shwe and Than Tar Aye are on the service. 
However, HR will investigate the name of Htay Lwin in the production line. He might be the worker who is able to speak Thai for translation.
HR will announce and post the interpreter names and photos in front of the HR office for the worker to see and be communicated. The interpreters will stand by to be on the service on time.

Business solution:  If there is a worker who contacts HR for consultation, they will ask to register in the logbook so HR could follow up with the worker. In addition, There will put an interpreter's name and photo on the board to communicate to all workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business to conduct the communication and the training to translators to make clear what their roles and responsibilities are and how they should handled workers grievances.
-The workers should not be blocked from accessing the grievance mechanism by the translators, this should be communicated broadly, at the same time that the business re-encourage workers to come to HR whenever they need their support and that the company will make sure HR staff (including the translator) listen to their grievances and take any necessary actions to address workers issues. 
-The business to communicate with the workers about the investigation results and the disciplinary measures taken (if any). In the communication, the business should make sure that the workers feel comfortable using the GB through translators.
