remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Workers reported having concerns about using the “Care Rooms” when they have issues. Those who did report issues found that their grievances were not being handled properly and they were harassed by their line supervisors for doing so.

Talking points:

-Explain to the business what are the consequences or risk for workers when their complaints/queries are not handled properly. Workers may face difficulties with their supervisors and/or peers as it happened with this worker.
remediation_notes: Workers reported being discouraged to use Issara Worker Voice Channels (suppression of worker voice) and also being targeted by their peers if any workers were found to have reported issues to Issara.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-Credible and safe grievance mechanisms should include confidentiality, transparency and safeguards for all workers. The business should guarantee to workers that their complaints will be treated ethically and confidentially. This, with the purpose of avoiding retaliation from the company staff (HR, production, and/or other workers).   

-Communication. Effectively communicate to workers what the grievance mechanisms are, contact information of focal points and availability, actions that will be taken by business for investigations and safeguarding, and timeframes. 


-Training and planning sessions with Issara and HR on strengthening grievance mechanisms, then broader trainings for line supervisors and others.
systems_change_business_steps_taken:
Yes, several meetings on this issue. It was escalated to the
Seafresh COO level. COO agreed to make public announcements to all workers and line supervisors, promoting the use of grievance mechanisms and emphasizing that workers are not to be discouraged from using the worker voice channels. After several weeks, the business replied to Issara's several follow-up emails by noting that they have conducted the training with all line supervisors and the translators. The business requested Issara to conduct the worker's satisfaction survey with the workers. However, the business did not conduct verbal communication with the workers as agreed in the escalation calls. As Issara has not received additional reports from the workers and also the business is not taking further actions, Issara considered closing this case.
systems_change_business_steps_remaining: Verbal communications with all workers about the grievance mechanism and safeguard.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; The issue with a worker being targeted by two clerks and one blue cap supervisor after she raised the issue with the business.

-The business to investigate with the staff involved in the issue and with the rest of workers in the working line to find out the root cause of the issue. 
-The business to make sure that the workers feel free to raise any issue they face and that the reported issues should be handled anonymously and confidentially. 
-The business to make sure that transparency is in place when making any decision towards the staff involved. 
-Issara can help with the online tri parties investigation if needed. 


**Talking Points**

Please share the issue detail including the worker's feedback on the business grievance not being anonymous. 
Ask the following questions with the business. 
-Is HR aware of this issue? If yes, what was the root cause of the issue? 
-How did they receive this issue and from whom? 
-How did they conduct the investigation and what made them decide this worker be moved to a different line? 
-What had the business done to make sure the safeguard for the workers. 
-Did the business aware that the worker was being targeted by the blue cap and the clerks after she raised the issue with the green cap about their poor behavior? 
-What has the business done to make sure that all supervisors are aware of the business's no retaliation policy and follow accordingly? 
-Has the business ever received any complaints about the blue cap and clerks in the past? If yes, what was the action that had been taken towards them?
-What are the grievance channels for the workers to raise their issues anonymously and how were they being introduced to the workers? 
-How often does the business receive the issues from those channels if any available.

timeframe: one pay period

As requested by workers, the business also changed the workers working line. The business also communicated with all workers regarding their action for such an issue. However, Issara could not contact the worker.

-The business to make a verbal and written announcement about the "no retaliation" policy. The announcement should include the disciplinary measure for those who do not follow the business policy.

-The business should make sure that workers feel safe and comfortable to use the company grievance mechanism, so the business shall take any actions needed to guarantee save grievance mechanisms are in place. 

-Issara can provide training to all supervisors and HR staff as needed.

Workers added that the supervisors express themselves very aggressively, they follow the workers at the toilets or even sometimes knock on the door of the toilets, challenge workers, accuse workers of using drugs, etc. Workers have reported sharing their complaints through the complaint box in the past, and HR would talk with workers about the issue but workers didn’t dare to speak openly fearing no confidentiality.  


Recommendations; 
-The business is recommended to work with the staff in charge of addressing workers' grievances and conducting investigations to establish adequate and effective systems where workers' safeguards are guaranteed and they can talk freely without fearing retaliation. 

- In regards to the grievance boxes, the business is recommended to investigate with the focal person how and when the complaints that are inserted by the workers are being handled. 

-The business shall assess if it is needed to assign a new focal to handle workers' reports. 

-In order to guarantee transparency and show responsiveness to workers, the business is recommended to share with workers what are the actions being taken to address this issue.  


Talking points; 
-Who is the focal person that handles the  GB, investigations, and solving the issues? 
-How does the business make sure that the worker's issues are being handled properly and adequately? Ask them to describe the system.
-Workers have reported that they have inserted the complaint letter in the GB to complain about these supervisors, is HR aware of this? 
-If yes, what was the investigation and the result of the investigation? 
-Workers raised that they were not confident to give the real information about these supervisors during the investigation process because they were not introduced to the confidentiality and safety process, we are providing some recommendations to address this kind of situation. Is there anything else you think the business can do to make workers feel safe to speak up? 
-Workers should feel free to raise their voice and have the right to be remediated. 

Time frame 2 weeks.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had several calls with the business to discuss the issues, the business responded having done the communication with the supervisors from the specific line. However, the business did not commit to doing the investigation, rather argued that the supervisors are not having such behavior but the workers are slandering their supervisor. Issara checked with the workers about the situation, the workers have updated the situation getting worse by being targeted by the supervisor and threatened for reporting to Issara. Issara tried to reach the MD of the factory, however never received any reply. Several weeks later HR of the factory reached to Issara that they have ceased working with Issara, therefore they do not need to take Issara's recommendation into account. Communication.

description: Unresponsive grievance mechanism / no action being taken
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The workers reported not having secure and responsive grievance mechanism. Workers said that if they have issues with the line supervisors or with the mangers and they report about the issues to the HR, the HR does not take proper actions, instead the  HR informs about the report to the relevant supervisors or the manager which resulted the workers benign targeted by them. There are some supervisors who even said that “even if you report the issue to the HR, don’t expect for the issues to be solved effectively”. There was a case where a worker was heading to the office to report the Issue, unfortunately, the production manager found that and stopped the workers from going to the office. 


The business shall conduct an immediate investigation about the issue. 
The investigation should ensure safeguards are in place and that there is no risk of retaliation. The investigation should be confidential, meaning that workers’ identities should not be exposed in order to mitigate the risks of being targeted. 
The business shall take disciplinary action based on the business policy and the investigation results. 
The business to make a fresh announcement to all workers about the different grievance mechanisms channels they can use to report their issues. The communication about the grievance mechanisms channels should also include information about the process of how the grievances are handled and the confidentiality of such channels. This will give more confidence to the workers to use the business's internal grievance channels. 
The business should clearly communicate with all supervisors and workers the business policy regarding behavior and what are disciplinary actions for those not following the company policy. 

Time Frame; 2 weeks.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
IDENTIFIED POSSIBLE ROOT CAUSES
Inappropriate supervisor attitude resulting in insufficient communication

CORRECTIVE ACTIONS / REMEDY CONFIRMED BY SEAFRESH
1. Re-training the supervisors to know about labor protection laws. forced labor and Good Labor Practices in three sessions of the GLP & Business Ethics course on 21,22 and 23 April 2022.
remediation_notes: The workers reported not having secure and responsive grievance mechanism. Workers said that if they have issues with the line supervisors or managers and report them to HR, HR does not take proper actions.  Instead, HR informs the relevant supervisors or the managers about the reports and workers are facing retaliation for having made such reports.  Some supervisors even said, “even if you report the issue to HR, don’t expect for the issues to be solved effectively”. There was also a case where a worker was heading to the HR office to report an issue but the production manager stopped him from going to make the report.
remediation_action: The business investigated this matter and found that the supervisors had an inappropriate attitude regarding the right of workers to safe channels to report their grievances.  The business re-trained the supervisors on the labor protection act and good labor practices on 21,22 and 23 April 2022.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for system change

Based on the results of the investigation and the assessment of the business on how the issues were responded to workers' grievances, the business shall provide training to the HR who receive workers cases and shall revise as needed the protocols to respond to workers. Since workers explained that they had reported the issue but nothing was solved but were targeted, the business is recommended to look into the grievance mechanism channels and identify what shall be amended or improved. 
Issara can also provide tailored training with HR and the supervisors.

description: Unresponsive grievance mechanism / no action being taken
remediation_issara_recommendation: The issue with unresponsive grievances boxes. 9702, 8691
remediation_notes:
Context: Workers reported that the business grievances is not supportive. There is a client who used to put the complaint into the complain box to report about the poorly behaviour supervisors but never got remediated or seen the action being taken. Many workers reported that they do not have rights to raise their voice. Supervisors keep saying that you will be fired from the job or be moved to a different line if you do not do a good job. 

Talking points.

-What is the business policy and process on grievances boxes?
-How does the business handle the cases that are filed by the workers? 
-Explain to the business what is the feedback from workers and the challenges they face to access grievance mechanism. And provide recommendations for system change.
-recommendations for line supervisor behaviour should be given as well. (internal note: talking points are under the respective KPI)
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-An immediate investigation is recommended. Credible and safe grievance mechanisms should include transparency and safeguards for all workers.  

-Communication. Effectively communicate to workers:
1. what the grievance mechanisms are, 
2.the contact information of focal points and availability,
3. actions that will be taken by the business to respond to workers feedback, suggestion and requests for assistance
4. Safeguards and time frames of the grievance mechanism. 

-Training and planning sessions with Issara and HR on strengthening grievance mechanisms, then broader training for line supervisors and others.
systems_change_business_steps_taken:
On 15-of-June, 
Issara had a meeting with the Okeanos. The business response shows not checking their grievances on a regular basis. Thus, the business agreed to check all of the complaints boxes and take action and get back to Issara with their action plan. 

On 23 June 2020, 
The business got back to issara by saying that HR coordinated with the production manager and started the investigation.  The investigation found that he/she is an interpreter  (Myanmar) in the production line, who communicates through the speaker which is always loud, so the workers feel like he/she is verbally abusive. That is the reason, the supervisor invited the interpreter to discuss how to communicate with colleagues, and not allow him/her to communicate in the same way as before. All supervisors were informed to be present in all of the communication along with the translator. In addition, the director invited all supervisors to discuss on how to communicate with subordinates and how to take care and to supervise them, and not allow them to raise the voice. 

On the 18/6/2020 also HR communicated with workers to reassure that they raise any concern to the HR without any hesitation. The workers were communicated to raise their issue/concern/complaint through other channels such as a suggestion box, helpline, or line application at any time, which HR will investigate and report back to the workers. 

20-Jul-20.
Issara could not contact with the direct worker who has reported about this issue. However, Issara has cross-checked with other workers and found out that direct reporter has returned to Myanmar as she could not manage the new working condition in TUF after her involuntary relocation. However, Issara cross-checks with other workers and one of the workers updated that she was told by one of her friend who is the translator from "Pe Lu" Line saying that communication regarding complaining boxes has happened in that line and the translator from that line was found out as a verbally abusive translator. 
Since then Issara has encouraged this worker to connect Issara with workers from "Pe Lu" line but the worker got back to issara and said that she could not get the contact number of the workers from that line. Since Issara waited for 2 weeks to be connected with the workers from the direct impacted line and could not manage to talk with, Issara considered closing this case at this point and re-open if we receive more complaint in the future.

description: Unresponsive grievance mechanism / no action being taken
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client reported that a Thai female worker is shouting and cursing at them, using offensive and swear words. Two Burmese workers feel assaulted and threatened by her behavior. They work in the cutting line and the cutting machine is very noisy.  The Burmese workers have reported this to HR and the interpreter since Monday, July 18, 2022, and the HR have not dealt with this issue yet.  This Thai female worker used to have a problem with other Thai workers and she has been warned in the past. But, this time, when the problem happens with Burmese workers, HR has not been responsive to their repeated reports, three times over the course of this week.

Talking points:
-What steps has HR taken so far to deal with this issue where Burmese workers are feeling threatened and being verbally abused by a Thai worker?
-Is HR aware that this worker has been issued a warning for this abusive behavior previously and therefore is a repeat offender?

Recommendations for remediation:
-HR should investigate this matter immediately given that the workers have reported this to HR three times already but have not received any response from HR.  Ensure safeguards for workers because they already feel threatened by the abusive worker
-HR should ensure that workers are not verbally abused, and they can work in an environment where they feel safe and protected from physical or verbal abuse
-HR to warn the abusive worker to stop verbally abuse others, and take appropriate disciplinary action since this worker has received a warning previously

description: Unresponsive grievance mechanism / no action being taken
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker Than Than Myint reported that HR has not been responsive to their request for help in accessing their bank account. 8 MOU workers (including her) who came in 2018 as a first MOU batch for TG-1 is having problems with accessing their bank account and withdrawing money. As their passport and visa expired in Nov 2022 and they have been working as pink-card workers until now, they can only withdraw their money from bank with business recommendation until 2023 August. After August 2023, the bank didn't allow them to withdraw their money anymore. As a result, their 1.5 months salary was stuck in the bank and now they are facing problems with their rent and food. 

TPs:
- Is the business aware of this new bank regulation?
- Has the business made an announcement to workers to explain the new bank regulations and how workers will be able to access their money?

Recommendations:
- Assist the workers to access their bank accounts immediately, by coordinating with the bank to understand what's required and to take action to re-open workers' access to their bank accounts
- Communicate with workers about any updated bank regulations and how the business is supporting them to access their bank accounts
- Communicate with workers about how the business will process the U-turn process for MOU workers given the new government announcement stating that MOU workers should do the U-turn process by April 2024
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 19 Oct 2023

K. Tunlaya, HR, will need to check the workers' status for this specific case and will get back to us as soon as this week or early next week.
remediation_notes: Issara received a report that MOU workers are not able to access their bank accounts given that their passports and visas expired and are currently working as pink card workers. They need help from the business but they have not received support even after going to HR to request assistance several times.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Ensure all workers have the proper documentation to work legally and have access to various services such as the banking system
next_description: follow up the business corrective action.

description: Unresponsive grievance mechanism / no action being taken
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with three supervisors ( 2 assistant and 1 senior, ลำใย  LB2 and เรณู  LB4 blue cap and เพียงพอ จัยจัย with green cap) being abusive with the workers. A group of workers has reported being constantly and verbally abusive with aggressive behavior and rude words by the supervisors. 

Talking Points. 
-Workers reported to Issara that they have reported the issues they are facing with these two assistant supervisors to the senior supervisor but there has been no improvement in these supervisors’ behavior. What is the role of the senior supervisors if some workers report such issues? Is the senior supervisor responsible to report workers' grievances to HR, or how should they handle such cases?
-For the past few years, workers’ grievances have been well handled by SEAPAC, and Issara noticed the improvement throughout those years, so we would like to know what has been the process in the past and if anything has changed in the grievance mechanisms processes from the company.  
-Does the company have any systems or processes to assess workers' experiences at the workplace, such as surveys or open talks? 
-Are there any activities or any training that the business has not been able to conduct recently which might have led supervisors to behave poorly? 
-Is HR aware of this issue? And if so, how is it being handled? 

Recommendations
-The business shall conduct an immediate investigation about the three reported supervisors.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with missing payment: A worker reported her missing payment. She said that the business replaced the new scanner on the 1st of Oct but the scanner did not scan her working hours properly on that day. That is why she had one day of missing payment from the business on her payroll. In addition to that, the worker reported that she had approached building 6 which is known as a building to report workers issues, but she was told to reach out to her line leader by the building 6 officer, when she approached her line leader, the line leader asked her to report to her foreman. She reported to her foreman, but the foreman did not take any action to address her issue. The worker wants her missing payment for one day. 

Recommendation for remediation: 
_The business shall check the payment system to identify the issue with the missing payment and remediate workers accordingly. 
-The HR team shall work with the finance team to make sure workers are paid correctly. And the timeframe to proceed with the payment should be communicated to workers. 
-The business should communicate to the impacted worker and explain the date of the payment that she will receive. The communicator should be from HR, NOT from the production line to avoid the risks for the worker. 
-The business should also make an announcement in writing and verbally, inviting workers to approach HR if they have also faced similar issues with the payment due to the system malfunction. And the business should remediate impacted workers accordingly. 

Talking Points: 
-What kind of issues are being handled in building 6? 
-Is building 6 being managed by HR or any other team? 
-What is the responsibility of the leaders and the foreman if workers have issues? 
-What is the business response on this issue where the worker's issue was not being managed or reported by the foreman? 


Recommendations for system change
-The business shall re-communicate with all workers who or where to reach out if their issues are not solved by relevant staff. 
-For the issue with the unresponsive grievance mechanism, the business should clearly communicate with all relevant staff about their responsibilities to make sure that workers’ issues are properly responded to. 
-Issara recommends training for all parties in charge of handling and responding to workers' grievances. Tailored training on this matter can be provided by Issara Institute. And/or the business can conduct comprehensive training for all relevant staff. 

Time frame: One pay period.

Context; A group of workers reported their colleagues being arrested by the local police for watching gambling conducted by local people in front of their housing. -What is the understanding of the business about this issue? Has there been any communication with the police? 
-What is the legal document status of these workers? Has the business applied for a work permit for them?

-The business shall closely follow up with the police and immigration to make sure the case is handled appropriately. 
-The business shall provide all of the required legal documents to the police to avoid workers being sent to jail for not having proper legal documents. 
-The business communicates with the colleagues of the victims about their status and the work that the business has been doing to take these workers out of the detention center. 

Time Frame; 1 week.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Oct 26th: The client is the husband of HT91 interpreter Mrs. Kyu Kyu Hlaing. He is also working in HT91 in the packing line. In his line there is only one Burmese worker and most of his Thai co-workers are treating him very poorly. One of the Thai workers, A-Tart, is acting very bossy and asking him to do this and that, shouts at him, or throws things at him instead of handing it to him carefully. Although they are all at the same position, A-Tart and the other Thai workers ask him to do more work than them. As they are in the packing line and they have to deal with carrying or wrapping the stuff, he ends up doing more work than the others

He would like to report this case but, as his wife is the interpreter, he is worried that they will both be in Target. He will wait and make a decision and let O&E know when to raise the case.

Update on 31 Oct 2022: He has agreed that we can report this case without mentioning his name. He said, other Thai workers are not bad like A-Tart. A-Tart used to also shout at other Thai workers too. So he requested to submit the case by referring to A-Tart only. It would be great if the supervisor is aware of this and monitors A-Tart's behaviour.

He said he reported this to HR 2 months ago, using the LINE messaging app and his wife interpreted the message to the Thai HR staff. But, he didn't receive any feedback from HR and nothing has changed with A-Tart.

Nov 3rd update: He said, it's ok even if HR knows that he is the one reporting this issue. Because he cannot bear to be treated in the current condition anymore. So he requests us to talk with business about this.

Talking Points:
-How does the business deal with conflicts arising between Thai and Burmese workers?
-Is HR aware that this issue of a Burmese worker being mistreated by a Thai worker was reported in the past but HR did not take any concrete action?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Investigate this matter, and identify the cause of the mistreatment of the Burmese worker by Thai workers. Conduct the investigation without naming who reported this issue to safeguard the worker that reported it.
-Clearly communicate with all workers regarding the expected behaviors between co-workers.  Monitor the workers for improved performance.  Ensure that the workers understand that the business will not tolerate any retaliatory behavior, to ensure the safety of the worker that reported this issue.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker said he didn't receive his wage for one sick leave day because he failed to inform his supervisor. He tried to call both the supervisor and assistant supervisor to inform them but they did not pick up his calls. Even though he went to HR and explained his situation and presented the medical certificate for the sick day, HR still did not agree to pay him for that day. Instead, he was scolded by the supervisor (who was also at his meeting with HR) that he would be given a warning letter if he raised the issue like this in the future.

NOTE: The worker doesn't want to be identified. He just wants the supplier to effectively provide warnings or train all the supervisors.

TPs:
- Make sure the business provides safeguards to workers for having reported any issues
- When a worker has an issue or grievance, what channels are there for that worker to report it to the business (HR, grievance box, etc.)?

Recommendations:
- When there is a worker grievance, there should be clear protocols for response and timeline within which the business takes action

Line supervisors cannot ask the worker for a medical certificate for a one-day sick leave, but 3 days can. BHR called Nan Yang NKPT today and gave them the info of that line supervisor (P Pyin, line no. 12). The business is happy to investigate again in more detail, and will get back to Issara at the end of next week.
remediation_notes: A worker said he didn't receive his wage for one sick leave day because he failed to inform his supervisor. Instead, he was scolded by the supervisor (who was also at his meeting with HR) that he would be given a warning letter if he raised the issue like this in the future.

A worker from TUM Factory-2 (Worker ID- FH 2399) from fish trimming line reported that she gave birth to a baby on 7th September 2023, and she had to stay in the hospital for like 10 days since her baby is not well. As she thinks she needs a birth certificate and hospital card for her baby as fast as possible, she took birth certificate application and hospital card application from hospital and submitted to TUM office on 11th Sep with the help of her cousin sister to get employer's signature. However she hasn't got the form back with the employer's signature. Until 25th Sep, she went to the office in person 4 times to get it. In last time, the office interpreter angrily told her that "you don't need to come very often, we are not working only for you, we will call you when the form is ready". When she asked around other friends who had experience in this matter, her friends told her that you need to go to the office very often to remind them otherwise they would forgot and even your form would lost. remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client reported that 3 MOU workers from HT-70 got arrested during the U-Turn process in Myanmar. They were sent back to Myanmar on 27 Oct 2023 thru the Myawaddy-Maesot border. They signed the contract at Pin-Lone hall on 29 Oct 2023 with Aung Pyae Recruitment Agency. During the contract signing ceremony, the police official from the military came and arrested them. These three workers include Mrs.Yamin with her husband "Mr.Kyaw Win" and "Mrs.Su". (Mrs.Yamin is now pregnant).  Workers are being sent for the U-turn process batch by batch and they have come to know that 13 workers' names are on the government list to be arrested. At the factory, there is a pro-military group of workers and a pro-democracy group that have voiced their differences.  The pro-military group may have reported the workers from the opposing side to the Myanmar military regime to be arrested. As HT-70 started the MOU U-turn by batch by batch. The next earliest batch is 3 Nov 2023. Some workers discussed with business that they do not want to go back for U-Turn are they are under high risk. But the business said, if they do not want to do a u-turn, they can resign. So, some workers are planning to resign, while some workers expect that they still want to work if we can help them negotiate with business.

What the workers' request: If we can negotiate with the business for the sake of  the rest of 12-13 workers who are at high risk, not to come back to do U-Turn currently. So the mobilizer will let those workers not leave the factory. Or if the business or RA can cooperate together to help those workers from being arrested or not. For the 3 workers who were arrested, only one worker is visible in terms of anti-government in social media and not the other two workers. They are wondering if we can also check with RA and business to help the couple too because the wife is now pregnant.

TPs:
- Is the business aware of the three workers that were arrested in Myanmar for suspected anti-military actions?
- Is the business aware that workers fearing they will be arrested in Myanmar came to voice their concerns to HR but their request was ignored?

Recommendations:
- Coordinate with the RA to negotiate the release of the three workers that have been taken into custody
- Delay the return of workers for the U-turn process until April 2024, especially those 13 workers whose names are on the Myanmar military list and have a high risk of being arrested.
- Monitor the situation and update the risk assessment until it is clear that it is safe for the workers to return for the U-turn process
- Respond to worker requests appropriately, given the current situation where three workers have known to have been arrested by the Myanmar military for suspicion of involvement in anti-junta actions
remediation_business_steps_taken:
HIT 70 knew the case already before I called. They were informed by a worker that the 3 workers got arrested on the Myanmar side. They are well aware of the 13 workers who are in the list but they haven’t seen the list so they don’t know who these 13 workers are.  Actually no one has seen the list, neither HIT 70 nor the workers. They said they have heard about that list from 2 years ago from the workers. The information about the list spreads widely by word of mouth. Yesterday they had a meeting with a group of workers who are going back for U-Turn next Friday and asked if they have any concerns about going back. They said no, so this is how HIT 70 is making sure that there’s no workers who are in that list going back for the U Turn. They are also aware of the 3 October 2023 cabinet resolution but the cabinet resolution cannot apply because the cabinet resolution refers to migrant workers who finished MoU 4 or 6 years (from 1 July 2020 - 31 December 2023 only), but they have workers whose MoU will finish in Jan 2024 too. But it’s good to know that they are communicating with the workers before they send them back for the U Turn, making sure that the workers’ concerns will be addressed.

6 Nov 2023 - Hear Tong acknowledged the case and is trying his best to help the 3 workers who got arrested on the Myanmar side. There was 1 pregnant worker who managed to get out of the prison but she decided to stay further to take care of her husband who is still in jail. There's another female worker who is still in jail but HIT 70 doesn't know where she's located and her cousins are working out where she's imprisoned. For the MoU U Turn process, HIT 70 is already communicating with every batch of workers who are going back for the U Turn, which is a good thing, and Issara encourages them to keep doing that. For the workers who will finish 4 or 6 years MoU in January next year, the 3 October 2023 cabinet resolution cannot apply. Issara recommends HIT 70 that they ask the workers' consent if they want to go back for the U Turn or not, and it's up to the workers' decision. Issara also recommended that they communicate with the group of workers who came back from doing the U Turn, so they'll get a better sense of what's happening during the process. Hear Tong also emphasized that our O&E officer should encourage the workers to use the internal grievance mechanism first before going to Issara. So HIT 70 will give us the contact details of the 3 worker representatives and 2 interpreters.

13 Nov 2023 - Regarding the MoU U turn, HIT 70 has been continuously communicating with groups of workers who are going back to Myanmar for MoU U Turn. In the first week of November, HIT 70 communicated with a group of 25 workers who will be going back to Myanmar. Within this group, only 1-2 workers have raised concerns about going back, however, they decided to go back anyway. This group of workers have returned to Thailand on 8 Nov and nothing bad happened. 

Another group of 35 workers will be going back to Myanmar on 11 November. HIT 70 communicated with them on 8 November to see if they have any concerns or fear about going back. No one has raised concerns.
remediation_notes: Issara received reports that workers have been arrested in Myanmar under suspicion of anti-junta actions while they were in the process of doing the MOU U-turn process.  Another 13 current workers that are soon to return to Myanmar for the U-turn process are feared to be on the military list of persons to be arrested.  Workers went to HR to request they not return to Myanmar yet but HR simply noted they can resign if they didn't want to do the MOU U-turn process.

description: Lack of worker representation; includes dysfunctional worker welfare committees
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Contest; The issue with the workers not being allowed to wear NLD clothes or conduct any political activities. 

Since this is a controversial issue; Issara has sent an email to the business as follows. 

Dear Business Partner:
Since the military coup took place last month in Myanmar, the Burmese people are facing an uncertain future but have risen up in large numbers to peacefully protest against the takeover.  In addition to the Covid-19 situation, this political crisis back home is causing even more stress and anxiety for the many Burmese migrant workers here in Thailand.  For businesses that are employing Burmese migrant workers, we understand it is a challenging time to balance workers' right to freedom of expression while allowing such expression to be made in appropriate and safe ways that do not disrupt the work of the business.  

We would like to recommend that the business maintain healthy and open discussions with the workers and come to an agreement with them on what would be allowed as appropriate expressions of their views but at the same time does not impact the workplace.  The business could be supportive in allowing them to express their views, during breaks and outside of work hours, and in a form that is discussed and agreed to between the business and workers.  Any sharing online of such events by workers should not include identification of their workplace, for the safety of the business and the workers alike. Also, we would recommend that the business makes a clear announcement to all workers about what is allowed and what is not, the "do's and don'ts" for the workers, explaining to the workers what their rights are, and what kind of activities are risks for the workers and/or business and therefore is not allowed.

We at Issara Institute hope the political crisis will be resolved peacefully very soon, for the benefit of the people of Myanmar.

closed_notes: The business was recommended to have open discussion with the workers on what was allowed for workers to do at the workplace to express themselves regarding the political situation in Myanmar. There was no response from the business regarding the recommendations but the business explained to Issara that the company didn't allow workers to wear any object as a political statement at the workplace to avoid any kind of issues with other workers and to keep a neutral environment at the workplace. Issara explain this policy to workers and we didn't receive any further update from workers on this matter, therefore, this case is being closed.

description: Hazardous or unsanitary living/dorm/canteen conditions
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Issara received calls from workers about the company shutting down due to positive cases of COVID being found among workers. Workers have also reported that the quarantine center set by the business does not have good ventilation and the temperature inside is extremely high. 

Recommendations;
-To arrange fans and ventilation in the quarantine center to make sure the temperature is not high inside and workers do not face health issues due to the extreme temperatures.  
-To provide enough water to workers to make sure they do not suffer from dehydration.

In regards to COVID measures, it is recommended for the business to:
 -To make announcements in writing and verbally to explain to workers how the business is handling COVID 19 testing, what the timeframes are, and if this is being done by groups.
 -The business should communicate what is the plan for those who test positive, what would be the quarantine plan, the process of taking sick leave according to the LPA, and any other assistance they would get, such as provision of food and basic needs. 
- The business shall also provide information on who to contact in case of emergency or if workers suspect they have been exposed to COVID or present any symptoms. The focal contact information (name, contact number, etc.) should be widely communicated to all workers. 

-The business to make sure that all QCs are well accommodated and the food provided has enough protein and vitamins to keep workers healthy and reduce the serious conditions. 


Talking Points; 
-How many workers are there at the quarantine center set by CC?
-How many workers have been tested and how many workers have been found COVID-19 positive so far?
 -What are the processes and plans for those who have been tested positive and for those who are at high risk (close contact with positive cases). -Which quarantine centers are the workers have been sent to? Is it only the one set at CC or are there any others set by the gov?
 -Are the workers getting paid during their quarantine/sick leave? 

Please share the following information with the business:
 1. After people tested positive for COVID-19 they need to immediately quarantine for 14 days, which means total isolation from ANYONE else who has tested negative or is untested. Absolutely nobody who is COVID-negative should be indoors in the same space and air with them. It does NOT matter if COVID-positive people have symptoms or not – all must quarantine. Total isolation of all COVID-positive cases is the #1 concern for preventing spread. · Is this quarantine isolation happening or not? If not, people are being put at risk. It is worrying that this is one of the main areas that the people do not know about; the people seem to be focusing on symptoms and not isolation, which isn’t correct. 
2. For people testing positive for COVID-19, it is normal for severe cases to go to the hospital and mild cases to rest at home in isolation. And, asymptomatic cases must stay home too. But are people prepared to live in isolation? · Do people in isolation have a way to get food and supplies safely? For example, getting supplies or food delivered to their door, but nobody being exposed to them? Please be aware to make sure your workers are ready for this so that the spread can be minimized. 
3. For COVID-exposed people: all must be tested starting at 5-7 days from the day when they were exposed. It’s not just symptomatic who should be tested, but all – 100%, not just “under suspicion” which is unscientific, and unsafe. They need to know the day they were exposed, and the day that the COVID-positive person got their first positive test. It does no good to test less than 5 days after being exposed; at that stage, it’s too early to tell. If the test at 5-7 days is negative and you have no symptoms, you still have to continue quarantine, and normally there is a re-test again at one of two points: (a) if the person starts feeling symptoms, or (b) another 5 days later because sometimes it takes more than 7 days for their infection to be detectable. · Is testing happening at the correct timeframes to be effectively detecting infection? If tests are being done too early, there’s a risk of false negatives and not catching the cases that actually exist. Are negative tests at Day 5-7 being followed up with a second test around Day 10-14 to confirm that the person is okay to exit quarantine?
 4. Being COVID-exposed is a scary thing: there is a lot of anxiety associated with waiting for test results, and even if they are negative, not being sure if they are really negative. It’s also risky when they see people who are positive or possibly positive mixing around with others, or if they are positive and waiting to see if their family members may have gotten sick from them (and the guilt/helplessness associated with that). So many sources of anxiety, stress, and fear here. The supplier should be ready to provide extra time and attention to the psychosocial aspects of being COVID-exposed and isolated: validating feelings of stress and anxiety, explaining more facts about the infection and quarantine process, helping workers in isolation find productive ways to spend their time while in isolation).
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had meetings with the business, the business arranged and provided more fans for the workers. However, there were several issues additionally raised by the workers such as electric shortage, insufficient food, and lack of medical at the quarantine center. Hundreds of workers participated in the demonstration to request their needs at the quarantine center. The business managed to solve all of the issues in a few days upon the worker's request. Workers have recently reported not having such issues anymore.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that the company has shut down due to positive Covid-19 cases among workers, and the quarantine center set up on the factory premises  does not have good ventilation with few fans and the temperature inside is intolerably high.
remediation_action: The business has arranged and provided more fans to the workers, and provided sufficient food and drink to the workers being housed in the quarantine center on-site.  The business also noted the quarantine center is fully staffed by government doctors and appropriate care is being provided to those in the center.

description: Hazardous or unsanitary living/dorm/canteen conditions
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A Worker reported finding two maggots in his meal, on the fried chicken which looked very old on 13.12.2021, L/1, night shift. Canteen No. 1. The quality and cleanliness of the food provided in the canteen is seen as substandard, with workers having raised this issues many times in the past.  He added that he felt as though he was not being provided with human food.

Recommendations: 
-The business should investigate this incident, and establish whether the contracted food vendor is maintaining hygiene and nutrition standards in the food provided.  
- If the vendor is found to have failed to meet the necessary food quality standards, the vendor should be monitored for improvement or discontinued according to the 3-strike rule as stated in the contract with the vendor.

-HR should regularly check the quality of the food to ensure the food vendor provides clean and nutritious food to the workers, at an affordable and transparent price (500-700 calorie meal = 1 cup rice + 300-500 cals protein and fat).

-The business to communicate with the workers about the issues with food quality in the canteen and what the business is doing to improve and ensure an acceptable quality in the food provided in the future. 
-Workers to be encouraged to use the internal grievance channels when they have any concerns regarding their meals in the future. 

Talking Points: 
- How many canteens does the business have?  How many food vendors have been contracted to serve food to the workers?  What food quality standards are specified in the vendor contract?
- How many times has this vendor been warned in the past for providing poor quality food to workers?
-Is HR aware of this issue?  Have workers reported this to HR? 
-What will the business do to rectify this issue, given that this has been reported by workers on multiple occasions in the past and the vendor continues to provide substandard food?
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara raised this issue with the business and suggested to conduct investigation.
remediation_notes: A worker reported finding two maggots in his meal, on the fried chicken which looked very old during the night shift in Canteen No. 1. The worker noted that the quality and cleanliness of the food provided in the canteen was substandard, an issue various workers have raised multiple times in the past.  He added that he felt as though "he was not being provided with human food".
remediation_action: Issara raised this issue during an escalation call, and the business agreed to conduct an investigation into the matter.  The new HR staff noted that she had herself eaten in the canteens recently and found that the food was very good and delicious, intimating that the canteen food service was of a good standard.  Issara noted that this issue has been reported by workers many times already, and the business should hold the food vendors accountable for maintaining clear standards of providing nutritious and hygienic meals to the workers.
remediation_validation: Issara will follow up with the workers once the business has taken corrective action

description: Hazardous or unsanitary living/dorm/canteen conditions
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue #1 

Context: the issue with the COVID-19 infection. Workers reported the spread of the virus and increasing infected workers in the factory, however, they are still being asked to continue working. Workers raised their concerns about getting infected and requested clear communication about the business plan to control the infection rate and also to test 100% of the workers in the factory. In addition to that, the workers reported being threatened of not receiving their wages and of not having access to basic needs supplies such as water and food, and losing their job if they do not come to work before completing their quarantine. Workers added that they were suggested to stay 14 days of quarantine by the doctor but the business asked them to work after a few days (5 -8 days) of quarantine. 

Added Context: Workers updated that around 20 workers who have been tested positive and staying quarantined in the business quarantine center continued not receiving meals and water on (1 Sep 2021). In addition to that, the workers also have reported being forced to work OT in order to receive dinner.

Added Context: Workers updated not having purified drinking water on the 14th and 15th of September. In addition to that, workers added having polluted tap water for their daily use which causes allergics on their skin.

Recommendations: 
-The business to clearly communicate with the workers about the business plan to control the spread of the virus to a bigger number of workers in the factory and in the community.
-The business should also clearly communicate with the workers i) why they are being pushed to get back to work before completing the 14 days of quarantine, which is against the doctors’ recommendation, ii) what are the measures being taken by the business to make sure that those that have been exposed and in closed contact with positive cases do not spread the virus at the workplace if they are being asked to work before being able to confirm if they are positive or not. 
-The business should assign focal and introduce the vocals with the workers for the workers to reach out to them whenever they have questions and concerns related to COVID-19. 

Talking points:
-Is the business aware that the workers are being asked to get back to work before completing their 14 days of quarantine suggested by the doctor?  
-Workers reported being threatened of not receiving regular meals, not receiving wages for quarantine days, and even getting fired from work if they do not follow the business suggesting to get back to work before completion of 14 days of quarantine. What is the business understanding of this? 
-What has been the business action to control the number of impacted workers? 
-How many workers have been tested for COVID-19 so far and what is the testing process? 
-Are the COVID-19 regulation measures applied equally for Burmese and Thai workers, if not how so? According to the workers' report, there are different regulations for Thai, for instance, they have fewer restrictions of movement. This creates a feeling of insecurity among Burmese workers to work along with Thai workers who could have greater exposure to the virus. So what is the company policy, what is the plan to deal with these issues, and are the regulations applied equally for all workers?  


Issue #2. Added issues on 16th September 2021. 

(1) The issue with insufficient drinking water: This issue happened on 14th September, Issara raised this issue with HR in the evening of the same day, the HR responded that they were going to take immediate action, however, there were only 5 bottles of water added to only one Zone. At the rest of the Zones, workers reported not receiving water. On the 15th, workers again reported the same issue and Issara informed HR on the same day. In addition, workers have reported the issue to the focal person, however, the issues haven’t been resolved. Despite all the reports made by workers about the issue with water, which is a basic need, the business hasn’t addressed it and workers continue to experience difficulties accessing clean water. 

Recommended next steps: 
To conduct the investigation and provide enough drinking water to all of the workers with the ratio of at least two liters of purified water per worker per day. 
To introduce the focal person from HR for workers and the housing focal to reach out if they have issues. And have clear communication with workers about the actions the business will take to solve the issues and the timelines of those actions. 
To set up an emergency group to work on such issues immediately. 
Set up the system so all workers have access to adequate drinking water and water containers are not taken away by some workers to their rooms. The system should guarantee access to clean water and it should be effective and hygienic. 

(2) The issue with polluted tap water: Issara received the issue on 14th and reached out to the business immediately, however workers updated the situation on 15th September evening. Workers said that they have to use other medicines or powder to alleviate the rushes they got from the polluted water. Despite all the reports made by workers about the issue with water, which is a basic need, the business hasn’t addressed it and workers continue to experience difficulties accessing clean water. 

Recommended next steps: 
The business to closely work with the maintenance team and find out the root cause of the issue and take action immediately. 
Workers should be given a time frame for the issue to be solved and the other options if any available. 

(3) Waterbottles without dispensers: Workers reported not having dispensers on the provided water container and workers having difficulties using drinking water. The business responded that they have provided the pump which the workers can use to transfer the water to their small bottles, however, workers updated not having seen those pumps. 
To have easy access to the water, the business shall provide the water containers with the appropriate dispenser so that the workers can access them as needed without having to lift the heavy container. 

(4) The issue with not having an ATM: Workers who have been placed for quarantine in the SEALIGHT hotel have reported not having access to an ATM. There are 4 mothers with around one-year-old babies who need basic needs. They said that they have to give their ATM card to the focal when they want to buy any goods or baby sanitary stuff. 

Recommended next steps: 
Workers having to give their ATM card is not safe and secure, therefore, the business should find a way to solve this problem. 
The business to find a way where workers can do the online transaction when they order the product via focal or the business to arrange cash and exchange with the online payment from the workers. 

(5) The issue with lack of bed sheets: Eight workers who are in the SEALIGHT hotel for quarantine reported not having bedsheets to sleep. It is reported that they are provided with only a mat without a mattress. Workers said that they have reported to  P'Kyi Ya from HR about this a few days ago, however, no action has been taken. Workers added that it gets cold in the morning and they are not able to have a good rest at night. 

Recommended next steps:
The business should immediately investigate why workers haven’t received proper items for their beds and work closely with the hotel to make sure that all workers in the hotel quarantine receive proper mattresses, blankets, and bedsheets.

If the factory found a positive case for Covid,

The factory should do a deep cleaning and disinfecting the area
 If there are more than 5% positive cases found from the random test (10% of the workforce), or there is any risk of spreading to the neighboring community. The factory should implement the Bubble and Seals" measures.

preparing accommodation for workers in the factory, the workers who wish to continue working shall stay in the compound. They could not commute between their dormitory and factory. set up organization quarantine/factory quarantine
set up field hospital or community isolation for the workers in the factory
The factory shall provide provisions (Food, essential goods, medicine, and medical equipment) and facilities to workers who stay in the bubble and seals.

remediation_notes:
Workers that were in quarantine reported that the business expected them to report back to work after only 5-8 days of quarantine, against the recommendation of Thai health officials. In addition, the business had told them they might not receive their wages, not be provided with basic necessities such as water and food during quarantine, and might even lose their jobs if they did not report back to work as the business instructed.

One group that has tested positive and quarantined in the business quarantine center also did not receive meals or water; we have asked for this to be urgently addressed. This was finally addressed after Issara communicated the urgency of the case to TUS.

(Update)- Workers have reported not receiving adequate drinking water in their dormitories during the bubble & seal period, with a lack of proper water dispenser and workers have to lift big water containers to pour water into water bottles with small openings.  Also, the tap water was polluted, which the workers couldn't use for their cooking or showers.  In addition, some female workers in a hotel quarantine could not use their ATM cards to withdraw money to buy necessary items for their babies.  Some other workers in hotel quarantine did not receive bedsheets in their rooms.
remediation_action:
Issara raised this issue with the business. The business responded that it was a misunderstanding and miscommunication, and committed to make sure that all workers receive proper meals. However, this took sometime before it was finally solved by the business.

Issara has raised this issue with the site as well as central TU's Director of Sustainability.

(Update)- The additional issues were reported to TUS HR and then to TU's Director of Sustainability
remediation_validation:
Workers confirmed that they didn't receive meals on the day they reported the issue and also their electricity was cut off as punishment for not reporting to work as instructed by the business. 

Workers that did not work overtime did not receive their dinners after their shift and felt they were being punished for not working overtime. (Note: the business has to provide workers with all meals for workers living on-site, to comply with Thai govt "bubble and seal" quarantine measures.)

(Update)- After Issara reported the worker issues regarding drinking water and polluted tap water to HR, the workers confirmed the next day that they had not received any remedies yet.

(Update)- The workers have now confirmed that the tap water is now clean and has been fixed.  For the drinking water, the water containers will be refilled three times a day so that there is sufficient water for all the workers.  They also heard that the business will provide the water pumps soon to dispense the water from the containers.
remediation_results:
Issara had an escalation meeting with TU which was attended by K Prad, K Vorarat (corporate HR), K Supana (business partner in charged on TUS) to discuss these issues. 

For the quarantine period, TU noted that they were following protocols given by the government health department.

TU responded that the issue with the provision food was due to problems of mis-communication with workers and an inadequate food distribution plan but that they had taken immediate actions after getting the workers report from Issara. For the issue with workers not working OT and not receiving food, the business responded that it was an issue with the quantity of food and some workers from earlier shifts taking more than one meal. That for this reason food was delayed but that workers had finally received their meals.

(Update)- Regarding the issues of drinking water, water dispenser, polluted tap water, access to ATM machine and bedsheets for those in the hotel quarantine, TU's Director of Sustainability took note and committed to solving the issues immediately

description: Hazardous or unsanitary living/dorm/canteen conditions
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue #1 

Context: the issue with the COVID-19 infection. Workers reported the spread of the virus and increasing infected workers in the factory, however, they are still being asked to continue working. Workers raised their concerns about getting infected and requested clear communication about the business plan to control the infection rate and also to test 100% of the workers in the factory. In addition to that, the workers reported being threatened of not receiving their wages and of not having access to basic needs supplies such as water and food, and losing their job if they do not come to work before completing their quarantine. Workers added that they were suggested to stay 14 days of quarantine by the doctor but the business asked them to work after a few days (5 -8 days) of quarantine. 

Added Context: Workers updated that around 20 workers who have been tested positive and staying quarantined in the business quarantine center continued not receiving meals and water on (1 Sep 2021). In addition to that, the workers also have reported being forced to work OT in order to receive dinner.

Added Context: Workers updated not having purified drinking water on the 14th and 15th of September. In addition to that, workers added having polluted tap water for their daily use which causes allergics on their skin.

Recommendations: 
-The business to clearly communicate with the workers about the business plan to control the spread of the virus to a bigger number of workers in the factory and in the community.
-The business should also clearly communicate with the workers i) why they are being pushed to get back to work before completing the 14 days of quarantine, which is against the doctors’ recommendation, ii) what are the measures being taken by the business to make sure that those that have been exposed and in closed contact with positive cases do not spread the virus at the workplace if they are being asked to work before being able to confirm if they are positive or not. 
-The business should assign focal and introduce the vocals with the workers for the workers to reach out to them whenever they have questions and concerns related to COVID-19. 

Talking points:
-Is the business aware that the workers are being asked to get back to work before completing their 14 days of quarantine suggested by the doctor?  
-Workers reported being threatened of not receiving regular meals, not receiving wages for quarantine days, and even getting fired from work if they do not follow the business suggesting to get back to work before completion of 14 days of quarantine. What is the business understanding of this? 
-What has been the business action to control the number of impacted workers? 
-How many workers have been tested for COVID-19 so far and what is the testing process? 
-Are the COVID-19 regulation measures applied equally for Burmese and Thai workers, if not how so? According to the workers' report, there are different regulations for Thai, for instance, they have fewer restrictions of movement. This creates a feeling of insecurity among Burmese workers to work along with Thai workers who could have greater exposure to the virus. So what is the company policy, what is the plan to deal with these issues, and are the regulations applied equally for all workers?  


Issue #2. Added issues on 16th September 2021. 

(1) The issue with insufficient drinking water: This issue happened on 14th September, Issara raised this issue with HR in the evening of the same day, the HR responded that they were going to take immediate action, however, there were only 5 bottles of water added to only one Zone. At the rest of the Zones, workers reported not receiving water. On the 15th, workers again reported the same issue and Issara informed HR on the same day. In addition, workers have reported the issue to the focal person, however, the issues haven’t been resolved. Despite all the reports made by workers about the issue with water, which is a basic need, the business hasn’t addressed it and workers continue to experience difficulties accessing clean water. 

Recommended next steps: 
To conduct the investigation and provide enough drinking water to all of the workers with the ratio of at least two liters of purified water per worker per day. 
To introduce the focal person from HR for workers and the housing focal to reach out if they have issues. And have clear communication with workers about the actions the business will take to solve the issues and the timelines of those actions. 
To set up an emergency group to work on such issues immediately. 
Set up the system so all workers have access to adequate drinking water and water containers are not taken away by some workers to their rooms. The system should guarantee access to clean water and it should be effective and hygienic. 

(2) The issue with polluted tap water: Issara received the issue on 14th and reached out to the business immediately, however workers updated the situation on 15th September evening. Workers said that they have to use other medicines or powder to alleviate the rushes they got from the polluted water. Despite all the reports made by workers about the issue with water, which is a basic need, the business hasn’t addressed it and workers continue to experience difficulties accessing clean water. 

Recommended next steps: 
The business to closely work with the maintenance team and find out the root cause of the issue and take action immediately. 
Workers should be given a time frame for the issue to be solved and the other options if any available. 


 Workers reported not having dispensers on the provided water container and workers having difficulties using drinking water. The business responded that they have provided the pump which the workers can use to transfer the water to their small bottles, however, workers updated not having seen those pumps. 
To have easy access to the water, the business shall provide the water containers with the appropriate dispenser so that the workers can access them as needed without having to lift the heavy container. 

(4) The issue with not having an ATM: Workers who have been placed for quarantine in the SEALIGHT hotel have reported not having access to an ATM. There are 4 mothers with around one-year-old babies who need basic needs. They said that they have to give their ATM card to the focal when they want to buy any goods or baby sanitary stuff. 

Recommended next steps: 
Workers having to give their ATM card is not safe and secure, therefore, the business should find a way to solve this problem. 
The business to find a way where workers can do the online transaction when they order the product via focal or the business to arrange cash and exchange with the online payment from the workers. 

(5) The issue with lack of bed sheets: Eight workers who are in the SEALIGHT hotel for quarantine reported not having bedsheets to sleep. It is reported that they are provided with only a mat without a mattress. Workers said that they have reported to  P'Kyi Ya from HR about this a few days ago, however, no action has been taken. Workers added that it gets cold in the morning and they are not able to have a good rest at night. 

Recommended next steps:
The business should immediately investigate why workers haven’t received proper items for their beds and work closely with the hotel to make sure that all workers in the hotel quarantine receive proper mattresses, blankets, and bedsheets. 


Please share the latest government announcement regarding Bubble and Seal measures. 

If the factory found a positive case for Covid,
They should notify the authority within 3 hours.
The public health authority will conduct a random test for 10% of their workforce (in the working station where the covid patient found and related working station).
The factory should do a deep cleaning and disinfecting the area
 If there are more than 5% positive cases found from the random test (10% of the workforce), or there is any risk of spreading to the neighboring community. The factory should implement the Bubble and Seals" measures.
For the Bubble and Seals, the factory shall do as follows:
preparing accommodation for workers in the factory, the workers who wish to continue working shall stay in the compound. They could not commute between their dormitory and factory. In the case where the factory provides accommodation to workers outside the factory compound, they shall provide the transport between accommodation and factory (sealed route).
set up organization quarantine/factory quarantine
set up field hospital or community isolation for the workers in the factory
The factory shall provide provisions (Food, essential goods, medicine, and medical equipment) and facilities to workers who stay in the bubble and seals.
6.	Failure to comply, may result in temporary shutdown and may be subject to a Maximum THB 100,000 fine or 1-year imprisonment, or both.
This order is effective since 4 Aug 2021

Source: 
https://covid.songkhla.go.th/files/com_announce/2021-08_62565c030491197.pdf

Additional guidelines for COVID prevention and response can be found in the “Guidance for Thai Companies: Care of Workers Affected by
COVID-19” some of the recommendations includes the following:
Keep workers informed
Ensure the correct timing for testing 
Ensure no discrimination
Ensure workers are properly paid during the quarantine period 
Ensure decent quarantine conditions 
Provide mental health support
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the business several times including escalation calls. The business argued and said that they have been following the government's instruction to control the spread, however added that the main causes of these issues are because of miscommunication, therefore, the business formed a special team and assigned one focal for each Bubble & Seal housings in order for the workers to seek and access their basics needs and report any issues that they face in their bubble and seal dorms. However, workers additionally reported several repeated issues for several weeks even though the business has the focal for each housings. Issue #1. CLOSED. 
The issue with concern regarding COVID-19 measures. Workers reported having a huge crowd at the place where workers keep their shoes when they finish their work at 5:30. 

Recommendations; 

-To make an announcement to all workers to make sure that all workers follow all COVID-19 measures every time and  in every place including social distancing and wearing masks.  

Talking Points; 

-Have there been any workers who have been tested positive? If yes how many and what was the process to deal with the cases, and how does the business monitor and handle the quarantine process for all nationalities. 

Please share the following knowledge with the business if the business has COVID-19 positive workers.

1.       After people test positive for COVID-19 they need to immediately quarantine for 14 days, which means total isolation from ANYONE else who has tested negative or is untested.  Absolutely nobody who is COVID-negative should be indoors in the same space and air with them.  It does NOT matter if COVID-positive people have symptoms or not – all must quarantine.  Total isolation of all COVID-positive cases is the #1 concern for preventing spread. 

·         Is this quarantine isolation happening or not?  If not, people are being put at risk.  It is worrying that this is one of the main areas that the people do not know about; the people seem to be focusing on symptoms and not isolation, which isn’t correct.

 

2.       For people testing positive for COVID-19, it is normal for severe cases to go to the hospital and mild cases to rest at home in isolation.  And, asymptomatic cases must stay home too.  But are people prepared to live in isolation?

·         Do people in isolation have a way to get food and supplies safely?  For example, getting supplies or food delivered to their door, but nobody being exposed to them? Please be aware to make sure your workers are ready for this so that the spread can be minimized. 

 

3.       For COVID-exposed people: all must be tested starting at 5-7 days from the day when they were exposed.  It’s not just symptomatic who should be tested, but all – 100%, not just “under suspicion” which is unscientific, and unsafe.  They need to know the day they were exposed, and the day that the COVID-positive person got their first positive test.  It does no good to test less than 5 days after being exposed; at that stage, it’s too early to tell.  If the test at 5-7 days is negative and you have no symptoms, you still have to continue quarantine, and normally there is a re-test again at one of two points: (a) if the person starts feeling symptoms, or (b) another 5 days later because sometimes it takes more than 7 days for their infection to be detectable.

·         Is testing happening at the correct timeframes to be effectively detecting infection?  If tests are being done too early, there’s a risk of false negatives and not catching the cases that actually exist.  Are negative tests at Day 5-7 being followed up with a second test around Day 10-14 to confirm that the person is okay to exit quarantine?

 

4.       Being COVID-exposed is a scary thing: there is a lot of anxiety associated with waiting for test results, and even if they are negative, not being sure if they are really negative.  It’s also risky when they see people who are positive or possibly positive mixing around with others, or if they are positive and waiting to see if their family members may have gotten sick from them (and the guilt/helplessness associated with that). description: Hazardous or unsanitary living/dorm/canteen conditions
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue from workers who are back to work after the explosion nearby factory reported having to breathe unhygienic air pollution, not having proper space for their lunch, and not having purified drinking water in their workplace.

Talking Points:
-Workers have reported that the quality of the air is not good, that they can smell smoke and they do not have proper masks to protect them from that air. In addition, workers are reporting that they do not have a proper space to have lunch and that the drinking water provided is not purified. What is the current situation at the factory and how are these issues reported by workers being addressed? 
-What has been the official order for this matter? Any measures recommended by the government?
-Have the official permission to resume operations been communicated with the workers?  

Recommendations: 
-The business shall conduct a communication session with the workers about the official order related to the incident. The communication should address workers’ concerns regarding health consequences for having breath to the smelly air. The business is recommended to emphasize that the operations have been resumed because it is safe to do so according to official announcements so that workers do not need to worry about it. 
-Workers have added that the ground where they have their lunch has some flooding and mud, so it is suggested that the business communicates to workers the steps and timeframe of the canteen reconstructions. It is also suggested to communicate with the workers if the company could arrange other areas for lunch breaks in the meantime. 
-Regarding the drinking water: some workers have reported being offered tap water for drinking while others are being asked to bring their own drinking water. Therefore, the business is recommended to provide purified drinking water to all workers to reduce the risks of workers getting sick. For the workers that are being asked to bring their own water, what they can carry might not be enough to keep them hydrated throughout the workdays, so it is recommended that the business find another solution in the meantime.  If there has been an official announcement from the government about the safe consumption of the water, then the business is recommended to make this clear to all workers to address their concerns.

·         We (Supplier and Issara) should be ready to provide extra time and attention to the psychosocial aspects of being COVID-exposed and isolation: validating feelings of stress and anxiety, explaining more facts about the infection and quarantine process, helping workers in isolation find productive ways to spend their time while in isolation (maybe even create a group forum on social media!).
