The business added that all of the COVID test and quarantine will be paid by the business and the workers will receive their daily wages for their quarantine days. The business requested Issara to communicate with the workers about the steps that are being taken by the business and not to worry about their daily wages and the medical treatment fees. A few days later, workers have confirmed not having any issues and concerns regarding COVID-19 measures.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that some workers had Covid-19 like symptoms but were not being tested, and they didn't know the business' plan for Covid testing and preventing the spread of the virus.
remediation_action: The business clarified that there was a previous Covid test of some workers but it was a random test operated by the government. The business also conducted testing for all workers at employer's cost, and followed the COVID measures as ordered by the government. The business also paid workers their wages for any days needing to be in quarantine.
remediation_validation: Workers have confirmed no longer having any issues and concerns regarding the business' COVID-19 measures.
remediation_results: The business has communicated with the workers about testing and other Covid-19 measures being taken, and took appropriate measures to prevent and control the virus.

description: Hazardous or unsanitary living/dorm/canteen conditions
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers who have been tested positive for COVID-19 being provided only two meals per day at the hotel set up by the hospital and the workers who are in close contact with the positive workers being locked in their rooms for quarantine and not being provided with any supplies by the business. 


Recommendations: 

-The workers reported that they are being locked from the outside by the security guard without being provided with any meals and other needed supplies. For this issue, Issara recommends the business immediately discontinue this practice, given that this can lead to workers’ mental and physical health being harmed. In addition to that, this process can lead to life-threatening risks in case of emergency as the workers do not have the freedom to move for emergency matters, such as fire, or other health-related cases. It is understandable that the business is trying to control the spread of COVID, however, the measures to do so shall respect workers’ human rights and basic needs. To control the spread and avoid workers needing to move around and leave their rooms, the business can:
explain to workers the importance of self-quarantine and what are the regulations during this period (workers are asked to not leave their rooms unless it is an emergency). Depending on the dormitory building spaces, the business could arrange separate living areas for those being asked to quarantine, so other workers are not at risk either 
Workers should be advised who they should contact to request the assistance they need (medical assistance, meals, and any other assistance they may need while staying in quarantine). 
The business should make sure all workers being asked to quarantine receive food, water, and any other supplies needed to respond to workers basic needs
Proper ventilation is very important and a basic necessity, therefore, the business shall make sure the rooms where workers are staying have enough ventilation 

Recommendations to assist workers at the hotel quarantine: 
-If the hotel is being managed by the business, the business is suggested to immediately arrange the provision of three meals per day to all of the workers in the hotel. 
-If the hotel quarantine center is being managed by the government and/or hospital, the business is suggested to immediately work with the government officials/hospital management to make sure that all workers are provided with an adequate amount of meals and medical assistance. 
-Receiving proper meals is fundamental for workers recovery and health therefore, this should be taken by the business seriously 

Talking Points. 

-Who is managing the hotel quarantine for workers who have tested positive for COVID-19? 
-Is the business aware that the workers in this hotel are being provided with only two meals? 


Note for BHR:

Given the previous response from K, Sarayuth was that he is not fully aware of this situation as there is a team working on this, we suggest that BHR request an urgent meeting with K Sarayuth and the team in charge of handling the situation to discuss this issues and address them asap.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had several meetings including escalation and try-party meetings. The business argued that they provide meals to the workers who make a special request and lock all of the quarantine workers from the outside as per the local authority order. Issara and Tesco made further recommendations and suggested the business remove the lock and provide proper meals to all quarantine workers with a default system since it is clear that the quarantined workers have no options to go out to get their food. The business agreed to follow the recommendations, however workers updated Issara receiving meals but being replaced with cable-tie instead of metal lock. Another try party call took place again. The businesses expressed their concern if they remove all of the locks and the workers will move around which will cause the fine by the local authority. The business was suggested to make a clear announcement with all workers explaining the consequences for leaving their quarantine house. At the end, the business agreed to make an announcement with all workers. However, it already took several months.  Issara has supported the business by reviewing the  communication announcement. After that, Issara made  follow up calls with the workers, the workers confirmed not being impacted by the COVID and therefore, no quarantine is needed anymore.
remediation_notes: The issue with workers who have tested positive for COVID-19 being provided inadequate meals at the quarantine center set up by the hospital. Workers that came in close contact with infected persons are being made to self-quarantine in their dorms but are locked in, and food and essential supplies have not been provided to them.
remediation_action:
The business investigated and found that the rooms were actually locked, and they did this based on advice from the government Public Health officer saying that those in quarantine could not leave their residence for 14 days.  The business also noted that 3 meals were being provided for those in quarantine but there were no workers at a government-run quarantine facility.

Two tri-party calls were organized between the supplier, SP, and Issara.  The supplier said it was in the process of unlocking the doors for those in quarantine, having workers sign consent forms about the quarantine rules, and this would be completed by July 20, 2021.

Issara followed up with the business after hearing from workers and the business said the locks had been replaced with cable ties which they claimed was easily breakable.  However, this is still an obstruction securing the doors.

(Update): Issara had another tri-party call with the business.  The business provided an update saying they would remove the cable ties, and a revised consent form would be provided to workers clarifying the quarantine rules, what would be provided to workers in quarantine, and disciplinary measures for those breaking quarantine rules.  Issara provided recommendations on the content of the consent form, and also provided a review and feedback on the Burmese and Khmer translations.
remediation_validation:
Workers provided updates saying they were still locked in, and not receiving food or water.

After July 20, 2021 when GFPT was to have unlocked the doors of those in quarantine, Issara received an update from a worker in quarantine saying that the padlock had been removed but now a cable tie was being used to keep them locked in.

description: Hazardous or unsanitary living/dorm/canteen conditions
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers have been informed since a month ago that they can no longer bring their own food and curries to the canteen due to the renovation of the lunch box shelves. Workers have to buy food from five vendors in the factory but some have found the curries they bought has gone bad when buying it in the afternoon to eat during the evening break before their OT starts.

TPs:
- Is the business aware that workers are being negatively affected by this ongoing renovation?
- What are the operating hours of the food vendors? Is food available for sale when workers need to buy food?
- How does the business monitor the quality and cleanliness of the food being sold by vendors in the factory canteen?

Recommendations:
- Investigate the quality of the food being sold by the vendors, as workers have noted that some food they have bought was spoiled and couldn't be eaten
- Ensure that the operating hours of the food vendors matches the times when workers would like to buy food, such as in the evening before starting their OT work 
- Communicate to workers how the food being sold by vendors is being monitored to ensure its quality and cleanliness, and the operating hours of the vendors during which time workers will be able to buy food
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 6 Nov 2023

They explained why workers no longer bring their own food and curries to the canteen.
1. There is currently insufficient space for the workers' food containers.
2. The canteen is undergoing renovations.
3. GFPT is a company that produces human food, so they are on the food standard industry to ensure that the outside food that comes to the factory is safe and does not harm the manufacturing process.

So they will investigate the quality of the food being sold by the vendors and ensure that the operating hours of the food vendors match the times when workers would like to buy food they will communicate to workers how the food being sold by vendors is being monitored to ensure its quality and cleanliness. They will send the corrective action by the end of next week.

DATE: 16 Nov 2023

They will have a meeting with the food vendors on November 27th to make sure the food provided for the workers is good quality. They will share with us with the result after the meeting.
remediation_notes: Workers have been informed since a month ago that they can no longer bring their own food and curries to the canteen due to renovations. Workers have to buy food from five vendors in the factory but some have found the curries they bought has gone bad when buying it in the afternoon to eat during the evening break before their OT starts.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Have a monitoring system in place so that any food provided / sold to workers is of good quality

description: Hazardous or unsanitary living/dorm/canteen conditions
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the worker's concern regarding the lack of medical staff in the quarantine center arranged by the business. Workers reported having asked to do the medical process (COVID test, taking oxygen level, fever, and so on)  by themselves and having asked to show the result with the assigned production staff. 

Recommendations:
-The business shall make sure that all of the staff who are closely working with the infected workers are fully equipped. 
-The business shall clearly communicate with the workers about the process of COVID cases management in the factory QC. The communication should include the following information:  
What the communication has been between the government and the factory regarding the case management and why the production staff is assigned to perform this task. 
How those from productions that are monitoring workers health have been trained to do this task 
Information about the focal person to contact in workers language in case of emergency. 
The business attempt to get medical professionals (If any) 


Talking Points:

-How are the production staff being selected to perform these tasks? Have they received any training? 
-What has been the communication from the government? Has the business tried to find professional medical staff from the government or any hospital (even any online consultation)? 
-Are the production staff who are performing as medical staff fully equipped with the PPE? 
-What is the process for workers to follow in case of an emergency? Has these guidelines and procedures been communicated with the workers? 
-How many workers have been tested Positive for COVID-19 so far? 
- How has the business managed the infected and noninfected workers? Are all workers being quarantined in the business QC? 
Time Frame 1 week.
remediation_notes: The issue with the worker's concern regarding the lack of medical staff in the quarantine center arranged by the business. Workers reported having to administer their own COVID-19 tests, measure oxygen levels, measure body temperature, etc.
remediation_action: The business responded that the quarantine centers arranged by the company are managed by the provincial Public Health Office. All the Covid tests are under the supervision of nurses, and even when some workers did the tests themselves, they were first trained by the nurses. Now, all workers that were in the quarantine centers have recovered and left those centers.

description: Hazardous or unsanitary living/dorm/canteen conditions
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the food supplies during workers' quarantine and the condition of the quarantine center. Workers reported that they are identified as COVID-19 positive and placed to stay quarantined in a facility that used to be a chicken coop. The facility still has a bad smell which workers find difficult to tolerate. In addition to that, the workers said they have to pay for the meals (80 B for meals) and drinking water each day, and the cost is quite high for them

Issara recommendations;
-As an employer, the business is suggested to reconsider reducing the price for the meals or provide it for free if possible.
-Provide a feedback channel so that workers in quarantine can communicate their issues regarding the facilities and services to the business
-Make improvements to the quarantine facility being used, such as sanitizing the structure and surrounding areas to eliminate the strong odor that is making it difficult for workers to stay there
 
Talking points
-How many workers have been tested and found positive so far? How has the business managed infected workers? Have they been tested by government officials? 
-How has the business managed the quarantine center and provided the food and other basic needs for the workers during their quarantine?




Update from the government regarding quarantine rule; 

Infected workers currently have the right to take sick leave and be paid in accordance with the LPA. Workers/employees can receive a free recovery in accordance with their Social Security. The quarantine costs (stay and food) are determined by the symptom and group of Green, Yellow, and Red (UCEP PLUS). If the workers are in the green group, they will have to do the home isolation and there will be no food provided; the workers will only be given medicine. However, the yellow and red workers must be admitted to the hospital, where food and a bed will be provided. However, in the case of providing food, the government encourages employers to provide food and a place for infected workers, according to the Department of Communicable Disease Control, but there is no law requiring employers to do so. According to the Department of Communicable Disease Control, for the factory sandbox, it just happened last year, that the big factories only (over 500 workers) must have a quarantine center and make sure that the employees must be quarantined and no movement to another area to prevent infection.

description: Hazardous or unsanitary living/dorm/canteen conditions
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The workers reported the following issues related to their living and canteen conditions.
1) The canteen area is very small and the business is using some of that space as storage.  It is difficult for the workers to find sufficient space in the canteen to eat their lunch.
2) The drinking water on the ground floor is not cool and has foul smell so the workers have to bring their own water from home or buy water.
3) The factory clinic provides only paracetamol as treatment for all kinds of illnesses experienced by the workers
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Case#1-K. Yuppadee has been aware of this issue before. Addressing the issue, the company has purchased more tables and put them in the canteen. And of course, there are two lunch times for the workers.

Case#2-This is related to the case one because when the first group of workers have lunch break they get the cold water and the second group of workers might not get the cold water because the cooler might not be cold enough in the short time. However, she will investigate and check this matter.

Case#3 K. Witsawad- according to health care policy the medicine service provided based on First-Aid that might be limited and not much more same as the hospital. If the workers were in a bad condition they should go to hospital. 

K. Yuppadee will investigate this matter and get back to us within one week.


Case #1: Canteen not sufficient space for workers having lunch.
The investigation result:
Because of the covids situation two years ago, the dining room area was set up by keeping distance. To avoid infection, the majority of the employees returned to their rooms for lunch. As a result, there is no shortage of space.
Present circumstances Coronavirus infection has declined. Some employees returned to the restaurant more frequently. resulting in insufficient space to meet needs

Action: Timeline, week 3-4 of June
1. Increasing the size of the dining room and purchasing additional tables and chairs
2. Communicating with workers who live nearby the factory, please go to your room for lunch to reduce your risk of contracting coronavirus.

Case #2: The water dispenser on the ground floor is not cool, has a bad smell, and is undrinkable
The investigation result:
Drinking water is currently not cold and smells. Caused by: 
1. The company has 6 drinking water dispensers and 16 water dispensers, enough for 407 employees.
2. The canteen's drinking water dispensers have two machines and four faucets, one of which does not have cold water due to a faulty compressor.
3. A water dispenser on the first floor. Because the compressor is broken, the drinking water is not cold.
4. Examine each point of drinking water and the result is no unpleasant smell.

Action: Timeline, week 3-4 of June
1. Send the water dispenser to the machine's seller for inspection and repair or replacement of the compressor (waiting for return)
2. Check the results of drinking water for smell through the standard criteria.

Case #3: Issue with medicine: the factory clinic provides only paracetamol as a treatment for all illnesses.
The investigation result:
Rules for dispensing medicines in the factory's medical room.
1. All medicines used in the medical room must be prescription-only drugs. which some workers are unaware
2. When workers experience headaches, toothaches, or other pains, the nurses administer paracetamol.
3. Workers are experiencing muscle aches. The nurse will include it as a topical medication, such as balm or pain reliever.

Action: Timeline, week 3 of June
Additional communication sessions;
1. A meeting of the Welfare Committee and the Safety Supervisors Committee to discuss employee suggestions/complaints.
2. A meeting to communicate to the workers about the rules for dispensing medicines in the medical room when an illness occurs. To take time off work and care for one's health in order to keep one's body healthy and ready to work.
3. Nurse meeting to improve communication about rules when a worker visits the hospital and ask an interpreter to assist the worker in explaining things more clearly. (In case of that worker are unable to comprehend)

3) The factory clinic provides only paracetamol as treatment for all kinds of illnesses experienced by the workers

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The drinking water provided by the factory smells like river water, and the workers cannot drink it. So, the workers have to buy their own bottled water during the lunch break but they are not allowed to take it out of the canteen area and so they have to throw it away if they cannot drink all of it.

Talking points:
What is the company policy regarding drinking water and where workers are allowed to take their water bottles and drink water?

Recommendations for remediation:
Inspect the quality of the drinking water provided to workers, identify and fix the problem to ensure workers have access to clean hygienic drinking water
Get feedback from workers about their experiences regarding the drinking water situation and recommendations on improving the drinking water provided by the business and also where workers are allowed to take and keep water bottles
Communicate to workers how the business has improved the quality of the drinking water and workers’ access to drinking water
remediation_notes: The drinking water provided by the factory smells like river water, and the workers cannot drink it. So, the workers have to buy their own bottled water during the lunch break but they are not allowed to take it out of the canteen area and so they have to throw it away if they cannot drink all of it.
remediation_action: The businesses responded that it is not allowing workers to have water bottles on the production line because the workers do not throw the bottles into the trash bins.  Therefore, the company restricts the water bottles to the canteen only. The company is aware of the drinking water issue. Previously, the drinking water filter was changed twice a year; now, it is changed every quarter, and the quality and smell are checked every week. As a result, the business insists that the workers get to drink high-quality water. The business will announce to the workers how it is monitoring the drinking water quality and send us the action plan by next week.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue # (1) 

Food served at the factory canteen: workers reported not having options to choose the vendors for them to eat for their meals. They said that the meals provided in the canteen have poor hygiene and the taste is unsatisfactory. They see worms,bullet fragments and insects, hair or stone in the meals they buy from the inside canteen. Notably in the curry and rice dishes. Attempts to eat outside are thwarted by security guards who report such behavior to management, leading to warning letters. 

Issue # (2) 

Toilet issues: Workers reported there are around 30 toilets for them and it is not enough especially in the morning when everyone needs to use it. The business has previously argued having the standard of one toilet for 6 workers according to the buyer policy. However, approximately 10 toilets in the facility are either broken or not functioning properly, reported by workers. In addition to that, hostel residents also rely on these toilets, as the bathroom and toilets are in the same space and result in long morning queues. 

Issue # (3) 

Daily Water Shortages: The water scarcity issue primarily occurs at night, when a large number of workers return from their shifts and require water. It takes 20 to 30 minutes for the water supply to resume, causing considerable inconvenience for workers after their long day of work. It's possible that some senior employees have addressed this, but many of others are apprehensive about approaching HR due to concerns about potential repercussions.


Issue # (4). **Internal NOTE*: The business said that they follow the standard of the Dyson and they did not agree with this issue in our first meeting. 

Cooling fans in the housings: Workers reported that they are provided with two ceiling fans for 10 of them and it is not enough especially for the day time when the weather is too hot for day shift workers. 





Talking Points
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business: It is optional for workers to eat anywhere they like and there are sound 10 vendors that supply food to workers. Workers can choose any vendor however the vendors have to be registered with the SKPJB to make sure they are legal vendors and the business can take action if there is any issue with food poisoning. The business said that they can choose the vendors. 
About the hygiene of the food, it would be good to have evidence. 

The issue with insufficient toilets

Business: There are 116 toilets for 780 workers in total in the hostel. It means 1 toilet for 6 people according to the Dyson standard. The business did not agree with the number that workers reported about the number of toilets and workers. 

Cooling fans 

Business:There are two fans per room 8 feet high and it is according to the Dyson policy. Having a wall fan or portable fan is not permitted by the Dyson policy and it will be too crowded to install more fans on the ceiling. 

Can we have some photos of how far and how it is not sufficient?

description: Issues with security in living/dorm conditions
Issues with security in living/dorm conditions
remediation_issara_recommendation:
WV Call Summary
---------------
KPI#2393 - Worker has reported that there are inadequate lockers for workers and currently four workers have to share one locker and some locker rooms like cat food stations have no CCTV cameras installed and that these things pose a security risk to their belongings.

-------------------
KPI Issue Summary
-------------------
Issues with security in living/dorm conditions

----------------------
Other Related KPIs
----------------------
*** The worker reported 5 other issues that are dealt in relevant KPIs as outlined below: 
KPI 2390 Inadequate Canteen Furniture
KPI 2391 Forced OT
KPI 2392 Irregular Lunch Breaks
KPI 2393 Security Issues-Locker n CCTV
KPI 2394 OSH Stomach Problems

--------------------------------------------------------
Impacted Workers - Production Line/Shifts/Other Details
--------------------------------------------------------
500  - Worker is one of the 500 workers on the fish trimming line.

-----------------------------------------------
Additional O&E Fact-Finding Questions (if any)
-----------------------------------------------

----------------------------------------------
Relevant National Laws (Thailand)
----------------------------------------------
Thai Labor Law doesn't explicitly mandate providing locker facilities or storage boxes to factory workers.

In seafood or fish factories, or generally in food processing industries where workers handle raw seafood, dairy or meat products, maintaining hygiene and safety is critical and the following industry aspects are mandated:

1) Occupational Safety and Health: The Occupational Safety, Health, and Environment Act, along with related Ministerial Regulations, emphasizes the need for a safe and hygienic working environment. This could be interpreted to include providing facilities like lockers or storage boxes, particularly if they contribute to worker safety, health and well-being. In seafood factories, where workers are exposed to wet and cold conditions, providing lockers or storage for personal items helps prevent contamination and ensures hygiene.

2) Hygiene Regulations: The Ministry of Public Health's regulations require certain standards for hygiene in food processing areas. Lockers could be necessary to store personal belongings away from the processing areas to prevent contamination.

In practice, many factories in the food processing industry in Thailand and abroad do provide such facilities to meet both legal and industry-specific standards.

 --------------------------

Thai Labor Law doesn't specifically mandate the installation of CCTV cameras in factory premises. However, the installation and use of CCTV cameras are generally governed by privacy laws and regulations related to workplace safety and security. Here are some relevant points:

1) Privacy Concerns: The Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) in Thailand, which came into effect in June 2022, requires employers to notify employees if CCTV cameras are installed. The purpose of the surveillance, the areas covered, and how the footage will be used must be clearly communicated.

2) Workplace Safety: While not specifically required by labor law, CCTV cameras are often installed in factories for security and to monitor compliance with safety regulations. This can help prevent theft, ensure safety protocols are followed, and provide evidence in case of incidents.

3) Employee Consent: It’s important for employers to obtain consent from employees or at least provide clear notification about the presence of CCTV cameras. This is particularly important under the PDPA, which emphasizes the protection of personal privacy and data.

-------------------------------
International/Global Standards
-------------------------------
The requirement to provide lockers isn't universally mandated across the entire seafood industry but can be influenced by the following factors:

1. Industry Standards and Certifications:

- Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) & Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP): These standards are often required in the seafood industry to ensure food safety. While they don't explicitly require lockers, they emphasize hygiene, which could imply the need for proper storage facilities for personal belongings to prevent contamination.

- BRCGS (Brand Reputation Compliance Global Standards): This is another standard that may indirectly encourage the provision of lockers to ensure a clean working environment.

2. Trade Union Agreements:

Trade unions in seafood industries like the Australian Seafood Workers Union advocate for better working conditions that includes providing secure places for workers to store their personal belongings.

In the US, some national labor unions AFL-CIO, UAW, USW and independent unions like UE Union have bargained for specific provisions in collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) regarding worker welfare, including access to lockers or storage facilities.

3. Company Policies:

Individual companies within the seafood industry might have their own policies requiring lockers as part of their commitment to worker safety and hygiene. These policies are often influenced by the need to comply with international safety and quality standards.

—-----------------------------
International laws governing the installation and use of CCTV cameras in factories largely focus on privacy, data protection, and human rights. While there isn't a single global law, several international frameworks and guidelines influence how CCTV can be used, especially in the workplace:

1. International Labour Organization (ILO) Guidelines:
- Worker Privacy: The ILO emphasizes the importance of respecting worker privacy and human dignity. While it doesn't have specific laws on CCTV, the ILO's conventions on privacy and worker rights suggest that surveillance should be balanced against workers' rights to privacy and must be justified by a legitimate purpose.
- Health and Safety: The ILO advocates implementation of an OSH surveillance system that may support using CCTV for safety and health monitoring if it contributes to creating a safer working environment. (Source: Implementing a safe working environment: Where are we now? - ILO 2023)

2. General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) - European Union:
- Scope: The GDPR is one of the most comprehensive data protection regulations and applies to any organization that processes the personal data of EU citizens, regardless of where the organization is based.
- Requirements: Under the GDPR, the use of CCTV in workplaces, including factories, must comply with principles of data protection, including lawfulness, fairness, transparency, purpose limitation, data minimization, and security. Employers must inform employees about the presence of cameras, the purpose of recording, and how the data will be used and stored.
- Consent: In most cases, explicit consent from employees is required, or there must be a legitimate interest in using CCTV, such as for security or safety reasons.

-------------------------------
Buyer CoC
-------------------------------
-------------------------------
ILM KPI Goal
-------------------------------
Workers living in employer-managed dorms have the right to safe, secure, and sanitary living conditions, as provided by the employer. Workers living in privately-managed dorms have the right to safe, secure, and sanitary living conditions, as provided by the landlord. This includes private rooms/apartments as well as shared spaces.

---------------------------------
Possible Root Causes and Evidence
---------------------------------
-------------------------------
Environmental/Workplace Causes
-------------------------------
Significant increase in the workforce has led to a shortage of lockers.

Evidence: Workers have reported the hiring of a large number of walk-in workers.

----------------------------------
Business Systems/Shortfalls Causes
----------------------------------
------------------------
People-related Causes 
------------------------
Possible thefts, damage or mishandling of personal belongings by workers with whom lockers are shared have prompted the demand for CCTV cameras to be installed in locker rooms.

Evidence: No worker asked for CCTV cameras to be installed until the lockers had to be shared with other workers, 4 workers in the present scenario.

----------------------------------
Remediation Recommendations & TPs
----------------------------------
- Recommend the business to provide additional lockers as the number of workers have increased. This is to eradicate or minimize instances of possible thefts, damage or mishandling of personal belongings of workers by others.
- Issara believes that if each worker is provided a separate locker as before then workers would not require CCTV cameras to be installed. However if the business decides to install CCTV cameras in locker rooms then it must be in line with Thai PDPA rules with express worker consent and announcement since locker rooms are often perceived as personal spaces where workers may change clothes or remove certain things from their bodies and CCTV cameras can pose an invasion of privacy.

---------------------------------------------
Worker Requests from Workers for Remediation
---------------------------------------------
Are the workers reporting the issue requesting anything in particular for remediation? - Workers want adequate locker facilities and want CCTV cameras installed in the locker room of cat food stations. 

Is the request from workers in line with international standards and norms?- YES for additional lockers but probably NO for CCTV cameras in locker rooms.

Is the request from workers safe for themselves, and presenting no possible risks or harms to others? - YES

In conclusion, can/should the request from workers be included in Issara’s recommendations to the business? - YES for additional lockers but probably NO for CCTV cameras in locker rooms.

What needs to be communicated back to the workers reporting the issue? -
That the issues have been communicated to the business and suggested action for remediation will also be communicated back to them through Issara.
Workers need to be aware of PDPA rules about CCTV camera installations in private places like locker rooms.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Benefits to Business if the issues raised by worker(s) were properly addressed and no longer impacting the business’ operations/ workplace
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
By following these recommendations, MMP can ensure that security facilities provided to workers are compliant with Thai labor laws, respect workers' rights, and align with international standards/guidelines. This would not only help prevent any thefts of personal belongings of the workers and prevent any plausible future legal complaints or law enforcement proceedings.

This would also help in retention of a satisfied workforce ensuring consistent production and help to uplift the brand image of the business infront of global buyers.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
How could the issue, and Issara’s role in the remediation process with the business, be framed to the supplier (and the SP, if involved) as Issara helping to support that benefit (as a positive force)?

description: Issues with rent/utilities/other housing costs and how these should be paid
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Cambodian workers reported that for the past three months, they have not been receiving the separate monthly bill for their electricity and water use in their dorms, which is deducted from their pay.  This deduction is not stated in their monthly pay slips either.  Therefore, they don't know how much they are being charged for the utility bill each month.  They only see the final amount they are paid after the deductions.

TPs:
-Why has ITC discontinued the practice of providing the electricity and water bill each month so that they can know how much they are being charged for this?
-Why is this deduction not stated clearly in the pay slip?

Recommendations for remediation:
-ITC should be transparent with the deductions for the workers' pay, and resume the practice of providing the monthly bills for the electricity and water charges.
-ITC to communicate with workers about this might have been provided to them for the past three months, and when they will resume providing these bills so that workers know how much they are being charged each month.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
All bills were given to the HR representative in the dorm by HR. And the representative should distribute them to the workers. However, HR will conduct the following investigation.
Did all representatives receive the bills?
Did the representatives present all of the bills to the workers? If not, HR will ensure that all bills are distributed to the workers.

Investigate Case:
Because some dormitory representatives did not come to receive the slips as well as the bill for dormitory maintenance and electricity bills distributed to the workers, causing the worker didn't receive the complete slips.

Solution:
HR assigned the interpreter to follow up and make an appointment for the dormitory representative who did not receive the slip to distribute to the workers and informed the time that must be delivered to workers within the payroll period. In the near future, HR is coordinating with programmers to adjust and develop wage slips to be able to specify the cost of maintenance, water, and electricity costs in each payslip so that they can be viewed with salary slips.

description: Issues with rent/utilities/other housing costs and how these should be paid
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Issue with electric bills and punishment for using over-limited bills. Workers reported that the business allows them to use only 20 kWh per month for each person and if any workers' bills exceed 20 kWh, the business asks workers to do gardening for 2-3 hours as a punishment on their day off. In addition to that, if workers' EC bills cross set the limit for more than two months, the business will ask workers to leave the housing and charge for that extra bill from workers. Room number of the workers who are being asked to leave the housing are 13/4 and 13/14. Workers said that there is a new housing manager who just joined three months ago to BFI and he is the one asking workers to leave the housing. In addition to that, workers also reported that they only have rice cooker, curry cooker and a fan, they do not even have fridge like other workers, however, they are the one being told of exceeding the limit. Workers also have no idea why their bills are over than others even though they do not have many EC devices. 

TPs; 

What is the business policy related to worker housing?  Does it set a monthly limit on electricity usage for the workers?  If so, how did you determine this limit?  What happens if a worker exceeds the limit?
Is the business aware that workers are only allowed to use 20 KWH per head (which is about 75B per month)?
If a worker exceeds the limit in any given month, s/he has to perform ‘gardening tasks’ for free on his/her day off?
If a worker exceeds the limit for two consecutive months, s/he is asked to leave the company housing and to find a rented room outside? 
Who is the focal person who manages the company housing?

Recommendations, 
Conduct an investigation about this issue to find out about workers having to do gardening on their day off and having to leave the housing if they exceed the electricity consumption limit. 
Review the conditions of the free housing that’s being provided to workers as a company benefit.  The limit set for free electricity should be realistic, and there should be a fair policy for charging workers for any excess use rather than setting punishments such as having to do gardening work or having to leave the dorm altogether.  
Communicate this housing and utilities benefit and its conditions clearly to all workers so they understand what is being provided to them by the business
remediation_business_steps_taken:
According to K. Onanong, HR office in charge of the dorm, all workers who live in the dorm are allowed to use a limit of electricity of 20 kWh/person if three workers live in the same room, which equals 60 kWh. The reason for the limit is that the workers are not required to pay anything, and the company calculates the cost of electricity as 20 kWh/person is sufficient and based on the company cost. If a worker used more than 20 kWh, the workers would request a maximum of three hours of clean service (sweep things, collect tree leaves, etc.)around the dorm, no gardening (cutting the trees), this isn't punishment but ask for collaboration, and also insists that no extra bill for the workers ever more than 20kWh in accordance with the dorm policy. However, if the worker is unavailable on a particular weekend, the worker may postpone to another week.

Furthermore, the company has no policy requiring workers to leave the dorm if they have used more than 20 kWh for more than two months. On the other hand, the company would assist the workers in investigating and determining why the electric bill was so high, as well as checking and repairing the electric devices for the workers.

Next step, K. Panida mentioned that the company will make verbal and written announcements to remind workers of the policy. The corrective action plan will be sent to us by next Wednesday.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that in their factory dorms, the business allows them to use only 20 kWh of electricity per month for each person and if any workers' bills exceed 20 kWh, the business asks workers to do gardening for 2-3 hours as a punishment on their day-off. In addition to that, if any workers' electricity bill exceeds this limit for more than two months, the business will ask the worker to leave the housing and find a rental outside the factory.
remediation_action:
HR explained that in the factory dormitory, each resident worker is allowed a maximum of 20 kWh of electricity. The business has this limit because this is provided free to workers and 20 kWh/person is sufficient. If a worker uses more than 20 kWh, the worker will be requested a maximum of three hours to  clean the dorm area (sweeping the floors, collecting tree leaves, etc.). This isn't punishment but the business is asking the worker to volunteer and insists that workers don't pay any money for exceeding the 20kWh limit.

Furthermore, the company has no policy requiring workers to leave the dorm if they have used more than 20 kWh for more than two months. On the other hand, the company would assist the workers in investigating and determining why the electric bill was so high, as well as checking and repairing any electric devices for the workers.

The company will make a verbal and written announcements to remind workers of the policy.
remediation_validation: Issara explained the business' position to the workers and they thanked us for the update.  They were not using many devices during this time and for cooking, they were using charcoal instead of an electric cooker. And in terms of the forcing workers to leave the dorm for two months of excess electricity usage, they also agreed that this may have been a rumor.

description: Issues with rent/utilities/other housing costs and how these should be paid
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A batch of workers were sent back to their home country for a MOU u-turn. Normally, workers wait 5–6 months until they can process the documents and come back to work.So,workers need to move out of their rental room (a condo near the factory). The workers don't want to be in this place because:
- High rental fee: 3300–3600 baht/month for a normal room; 6000–6500 baht/month for a ground-floor room.
- High deposit: 7500 baht; and when workers leave, they never get it back.
- The owner is very rude.  
The workers expected that once they left due to the MOU u-turn,they don't want to stay in this place after they arrived back in Thailand. But there is an announcement in the Facebook group by the HR interpreter: ask the workers who went back to Cambodia; they must respond to them whether they are willing to stay in the same rental place (a condo named by the workers) or not; if not, the business will not renew the documents for them.
The workers wonder why it is related to document renewal. The business or anyone else should respect the workers choice, as they don't like to stay in that place. The workers are entitled to stay anywhere they would like because it is at their own expense.

Recommendations:
- Investigate this immediately.  The interpreter or HR should not put conditions on completing the MOU U-turn documents for the workers
- Workers are free to find rental accommodation where they choose, and should not be forced to choosing a particular place to rent
- Discuss with the landlord on behalf of the workers regarding unpaid deposits of 7,500 Baht and facilitate the negotiations so that workers receive back what they are entitled to
remediation_business_steps_taken: K. Chaiyuth, HR manager responded that they were unaware of this message from the interpreter before. According to the company policy, they do not have the policy to arrange for the worker to stay at the same dorm after the MoU U-Turn. The workers can decide for themselves to stay in any apartment. The interpreter miscommunicated to the workers. However, they will investigate and get back to us next week.
remediation_notes: Cambodian workers currently in Cambodia to do the MOU U-turn process were informed by the company interpreter via social media that if workers did not consent to return and continue renting from the previous landlord, the company will not process the MOU U-turn documents for them. Workers have issues with the high monthly rent prices and also noted that the landlord doesn't return deposits to tenants when they leave.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Where the company doesn't provide accommodation, the company should ensure they provide guidance and support to workers to be able to find accommodation that is reasonable and affordable for the workers

description: Issues with rent/utilities/other housing costs and how these should be paid
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1. 

Context: Issue with a centralized kitchen. Workers reported that the kitchen organized by the company for male workers is not helpful for them because it  is located at Building "A" but male workers live in Building "B, C, D, E". In addition to that, the allowed timeline to cook also is  not sufficient as some of the food takes one hour but they have to leave the kitchen in  45 minutes after cleaning the used dishes. Workers want the business to organize at least 10 to 15 stoves per building so that it is not too far for them to bring all of their cooking stuff such as oil, salt, vegetables, and rice. Now, they have to bring their cooking stuff all the way from building E to Building A and if they forget one, then they do not have sufficient time to go back and bring it back to cook.


Case #2. 

Workers reported not having utensils and stove at the centralized kitchen for them to cook. They used to have them in the past but recently the business has taken them back.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issue #1. 

Business Response: The business said that it is the Dyson who did not approve of having the kitchen in every building. The business also added if workers are keen to cook, they would manage to do so and would not complain about the distance because, they have to come all the way from building B, C, D, E to Building A to take their delivered food at the moment. The business assumes the workers request is  not efficient. 28th Oct, 2023.

The female centralised kitchen is fully utilised by the female workers, as the male kitchen is situated at Block A. The current usage for the Male kitchen is very low and not being fully utilised. we have been encouraging the workers to make more use of the kitchen before the Management can decide another alternative for the workers to cook.
The Management will consider to add on the centralized kitchen to others blocks unless block A centralized kitchen is 100% fully occupied which the necessary to add on more due to high demand. (1 Nov,2023).

Issue #2. 

The business responded that they have  placed stoves and rice cookers in the kitchen back. The reason they restored back was because not many workers were using the kitchen.
remediation_notes: Issue with a centralized kitchen. Workers reported that the centralized kitchen provided for male workers is not well utilized because it is far and not convenient as they have to bring all their stuff and the allowable time for cooking is not sufficient to prepare, cook and clean. Workers would like to request business to organize at least 10 to 15 stoves per building. Nepalese workers used to cook compared with Myanmar workers so business can consider having a quick survey on who or which rooms want to cook in order to decide the number of stoves for the building.
remediation_action:
The business said it is the Dyson that did not approve of having a kitchen in every building. The business also shared their view that if workers are keen to cook, they would not complain about the distance and will use the kitchen. 

If it is Dyson's policy/advice, business to communicate to workers that the customer does not allow to have kitchen in every building so workers can understand the reason.
remediation_results: So far, business will not consider having cooking facilities in each building.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: The business should conduct a survey with the workers from different blocks to find out the percentage that is willing to cook if the kitchen is to be more flexible.
next_description:
To have an escalation meeting with the higher management of the SKP group to confirm whether it is Dyson's policy or not, and management view to consider workers' feedback.

7th Dec, 2023. Ma Chaw to close the case.

description: Issues with transportation to workplace
Issues with transportation to workplace
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Shuttle bus transportation: The workers would like shuttle bus to stop at another side of the road, which is on the same side of their housing. Because the pregnant workers have difficulties getting on the overhead bridge to get to another side of the road. The shuttle bus actually have to do a U-turn after dropping workers. That’s why the driver should drop workers after taking a U-turn. 

The workers would like the HR staff to assign the ferry drivers to drop workers after U-turn, at the same side of the housing. So, the pregnant workers won't have trouble to use overhead bridge. Other workers will be convenient too.

TPs and Recommendation:
Investigate the feasibility of stopping the shuttle bus at the requested location. 
Determine why the driver cannot drop off workers after the U-turn. 
Ensure the safety of workers using the shuttle bus.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
On July 16, 2024, Issara Institute conducted a remediation call with SEAPAC SMPK.

- The bus routes and stops have already been predetermined based on the location of the worker housings. The drivers cannot make a U-turn to accomodate pregnant workers because they need to continue driving towards the next designated stop on the route. It therefore does not make any sense for the drivers to make a U-turn in order to make an exclusive drop-off everytime there are pregnant workers on board and then make a second U-turn to continue with their route. This would heavily affect other workers who live in the following stops. However, while the company is unable to change or adjust their bus stops to meet the demands of pregnant workers, they are aware of pregnancy-related medical and health concerns, so the company will instruct the bus drivers to be extra careful when there are pregnant workers on board, such as accommodating them with seats or extra time to get on and off the bus, etc.

- The business will share a report about the investigation and next steps with Issara by the end of this week (July 20). Further calls and discussions can be scheduled if needed.
remediation_notes: The workers request that the shuttle bus stop on the same side of the road as their housing, after the U-turn, to avoid pregnant workers having to use the overhead bridge. They suggest that HR staff instruct shuttle bus drivers to drop workers off after the U-turn for greater convenience for everyone.

Regularly check if the drivers follow the protocol

description: Issues with transportation to workplace
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that the shuttle bus to PT housing is overcrowded, with the bus carrying 60-70 workers when the maximum capacity should be 40 persons.  He thinks that it is very dangerous to have to commute to work in these overcrowded buses. 

TPs:
-How is ITC's current shuttle bus service set up?  How many buses are made available to workers at what times and to what locations?  What is the maximum capacity that should be allowed on these vehicles?

Recommendations for remediation:
-ITC should investigate the current shuttle bus arrangements and find out why more than the legal limit of the number of persons allowed in the vehicle are being packed into the buses, making it overcrowded and unsafe.  
-Ensure that adequate vehicles are provided so that workers can use the service to commute to and from work and that they are safe and not overcrowded.  
-Communicate to the workers clearly about how the arrangement will be improved, with the shuttle service schedule and increased number of the shuttle buses
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The shuttle bus picks up and drops off workers on the same route several times. And the maximum number of workers per shift is 40 passengers. They will investigate the existing shuttle bus arrangements and get back to us.


Due to more new workers staying as members of PT dormitories, including other dormitories in Tha Nang Hom zone. Therefore causing the need to increase the running round in the run to receive more workers who enter the work in the morning in time to enter the workplace at 6.30 a.m. The shuttle bus will pick up at 5.40, 6.00, and 7.00. The inspection found that there are workers who should enter the work at 6.30, do not get on the shuttle bus on time at 5.40, but will go on the bus at 6.00, combined with many workers who enter at 7.00, which makes the number of workers plus the 7.00 shift workers are too many workers in the bus which get to the factory in the time 6.20 - 6.25 am crowded because the workers refused to get on the bus on the first trip. Causing the number of workers per bus in the first trip just 15-20 workers and the second trip normally 40-50 workers increased to 50-60 workers in the second round, causing the workers to feel crowded in the car.

Solution:
The company announced for workers to board the bus according to the timetable. Because the workers start work at 6.30, if the workers get in the car at 6.00, they may sometimes be late because the bus in the round takes 20-25 minutes, with the bus running at a safe normal speed and walk into the factory 10-15 minutes to scan the card. In order to avoid problems with workers not getting on the bus on the lap time, the company will make a sticker separating shift colors between 6.30 and 7.00 hours, informing the Master to let the driver observe and remind the workers to get on their own round. Also, the interpreter will be asked to go to the area to communicate and distribute dormitory cards with color-coded stickers indicating the entry time.

description: Issues with transportation to workplace
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1: 
The business has three work shifts; many late night shift workers commute to work by bicycle or motorbike and some have been robbed of their phones or money by thieves with knives or broken bottles. Although the business has arranged for security guards along the way, the workers say the security guards do not provide the protection they need and are often not on guard during the whole night. 

Case #2: 
For workers taking the shuttle bus, the schedule for night shift workers is very unorganized, with the bus often coming late for pick-up and drop-off.  The workers who work overtime often cannot find their shuttle bus at all and have to take other available buses.

Talking points:
- Is the business aware that some workers have been robbed under threat of serious physical harm during the nighttime commute to work?
- Is the business aware that the security guards posted are not doing their jobs and keeping workers safe?
- What has the company done to check that workers commuting using their own transport (bicycles, motorbikes) are safe during the nighttime?
- What is the current shuttle bus schedule and is it available for all workers for the night shift?

Recommendations for remediation:
- Investigate the current situation, listen to workers that have been directly affected, and support the filing of police reports as appropriate
- Adjust the current security system set in place to ensure that the commute for workers is safe especially during the nighttime given the late night shifts that some workers need to work
- Adjust the shuttle bus service to ensure there are sufficient vehicles for pick-up and drop-off, and that the schedules are clearly communicated to the workers that will use the service

However, it is a watchful situation, and volunteers are still on patrol. On the other hand, Issara can assist in communicating with workers that they should not go out alone at night or carry valuable items to avoid risk.

description: Issues with transportation to workplace
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The business provides shuttle bus service for the HIT70 workers who live near HIT91 but for HIT91 workers that live near HIT70 do not get this shuttle bus service. Currently, HIT91 workers living near HIT70 need to commute using their own motorbikes or need to pay for motorbike taxis. It's about a 10-min drive between HIT91 and HIT70.

TPs:
-Is shuttle bus service provided to HIT91 workers that need to commute to work?
-If HIT70 provides this shuttle service for its workers, can HIT91 provide a similar service for its workers?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Provide appropriate transportation services for HIT91 workers, including those that live near HIT70
-Communicate with workers, verbally and in writing, the transportation services that are provided to workers and the timetable and pick-up/drop-off locations so that workers know when and where to take the shuttle bus to commute to and from work.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Raweeroge, HR manager, explained that previously there was only Hi-Tech 91 site, which was later expanded to Hi-Tech 70. At the time, Hi-Tech 91 employed only Thai employees, and when the company expanded to Hi-Tech 70, they provided a shuttle bus to transport employees from Hi-Tech 91 to Hi-Tech 70. As stated by the Hi-Tech 70. The shuttle bus from Hi-Tech 70 to Hi-Tech 91 does not exist. HR will communicate clearly with employees about the transportation service.


K. Raweeroge, HR has been verbally announcing through the internal broadcast system since last week as well as HR posted the written announcement to the LINE group. Please see the photos at the link below.
https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1jmHBd8op-58A8rb6OCPfmaTO85a9PjUe

description: Issues with transportation to workplace
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that the business announced in September 2nd week that they will no longer arrange transportation service for going to the medical center (clinic or hospital) and the workers have to arrange this by themselves. Workers are not being reimbursed for the transportation fees they have to pay out of pocket.

TPs:
- What are the reasons for discontinuing the transportation support for workers needing to go to the hospital? Are they expected to pay for the transportation cost themselves?

Recommendations:
- Resume transportation support so that workers can get this support without having to pay for this out of pocket
- Reimburse workers for transportation fees they have paid during the time that the business discontinued the transportation support
- Communicate clearly with workers about the support the business provides, and the procedures workers should follow to request and receive this support
remediation_business_steps_taken: KPI 2090: Khun Da was checking with the interpreter at Vertex and Hear Tong also confirmed that there was no such announcement that the transportation service was cancelled. The interpreter reported that there's 1 case that 1 pregnant worker took an annual leave and she came to the factory asking for an interpreter and transportation to the hospital because she had a doctor appointment on that day thinking that the factory would provide transportation for her. Khun Da said usually the factory will provide transportation for every worker to the hospital if they are sick when at the factory, but not when the worker is at home or is taking leave. However, for this case, the worker took leave so the factory didn't provide her transportation. She has to go on her own because she took leave basically. I was trying to ask if the worker could be reimbursed for the transportation she spent out of her pocket, however, Vertex refused on the ground that she was on leave. Hia Tong said he'll emphasize with the Vertex team that they should have compassion and provide transportation to a pregnant lady even when she was on leave, or at least help her to call a taxi if the factory van is not there.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that the business announced recently that transportation service to get to the hospital or outside clinic was being discontinued. Workers have to arrange for their own transport and are not being reimbursed for the transportation fees they have to pay out of pocket.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Ensure adequate transportation and interpretation support is provided for workers that need to access health care.  Communicate regularly to workers the procedures and steps on how workers can request and receive this support.
next_description: reach out to the business

description: Lack of (or greatly restricted) freedom of movement
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A group of 11 workers who have submitted resignation a week ago and were preparing to depart are not being allowed to go by the business. The workers reported that their belongings were taken by the business when they were about to leave in a van and that they now do not have a place to stay since they have already given back their rooms. Workers reported the reason for leaving job is as follows:
(1) discrimination against nationalities at the workplace,
(2) the business not keeping the promise of paying double for the working hours during COVID-19 restriction as promised,
(3) translator not being helpful and being biased by just listening to the business and not the workers. 

Recommendations: 
-As it is a worker's right to resign and leave the company, the business shall immediately investigate why this group of workers were not allowed to leave. And then come to an agreement with workers for their departure from the company without restrictions.

System Change:

In addition to that the business added that they have responsibility to inform the policy about workers departure. Issara emphasized that since the workers have already submitted their resignation and they do not feel they are belong to SCC anymore, the business has no liability to control the workers movement. remediation_action:
Issara reached out to the business immediately. Regarding vaccination certificates that would be important for when the workers travel back to Myanmar, the business said the document issuance was delayed by the hospital and would be provided to the workers when issued. remediation_validation:
Issara followed up with the workers and provided an update, explaining that the business had said they were following government rules of not allowing inter-provincial travel and that the business would get to Issara in 3-5 days about next steps.  

The workers did not want to stay there anymore; they felt pressured and forced to go back to work.  They were even willing to pay any government fines if there were any for crossing province lines.  Since they have resigned, they don't understand why the business is not letting them leave.  They just want to be able to travel back to Myanmar. 

Regarding the social media posts, the workers said they did not take any photos or videos during the incident nor did they post anything on social media or ask their friends to do so.

The workers have confirmed that they have officially resigned from their jobs and are free to leave.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client worked at a Korean BBQ restaurant located in KL Kepong Jalan Metro Perdana, which is one of fifteen branches of the restaurant chain. Out of the fifteen branches, this particular one was problematic. The restaurant has six Nepali and thirteen Burmese workers. The owner's son is abusive towards the Nepali workers, creating a hostile work environment. Issara is able to speak with two workers. They have been working for this employer for 10 months. They are all MoU workers. They are reporting as a group of 5 Nepali workers, but the client is quietly reporting. The client and the workers want to either be transferred to another branch under the same company or find employment in another company. The client has debts to pay and doesn't want to return to Nepal. The workers have a contract they made in Nepal, but the company made another contract which the client doesn't have and is unaware of its contents.
Following are the major issues reported by workers.

1) Document retention: Workers passports are held by the employer since they started their employment. The company also kept their passports and didn't provide them with worker ID cards (Jalan cards) or necessary documents. 

2) Restriction of Movement: The workers were not allowed to leave the premises, and this restriction also made it difficult for their friends to visit them.

3) Unfair suspension: Workers were frequently suspended for minor mistakes or even without any reason. They were also denied access to basic amenities, like cooling fans, during these periods. One incident occurred when a friend of the client was suspended for simply asking a Burmese worker to clean a stain. The owner verbally abused him and kept him in detention (suspension) for 28 days. 6) Lack of Sick Leave: Even when the workers fell ill, they were forced to work, as the owner wouldn't allow them to stay in the hostel.

description: Lack of (or greatly restricted) freedom of movement
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A batch of workers were sent back to their home country for a MOU u-turn. Normally, workers wait 5–6 months until they can process the documents and come back to work. So, workers need to move out of their rental room (a condo near the factory). The workers don't want to be in this place because:
- High rental fee: 3,300–3,600 baht/month for a normal room; 6,000–6,500 baht/month for a ground-floor room.
- High deposit: 7,500 baht; and when workers leave, they never get it back.
- The owner is very rude.  
The workers expected that once they left due to the MOU u-turn,they don't want to stay in this place after they arrived back in Thailand. But there is an announcement in the Facebook group by the HR interpreter: ask the workers who went back to Cambodia; they must respond to them whether they are willing to stay in the same rental place (a condo named by the workers) or not; if not, the business will not renew the documents for them. The workers wonder why it is related to document renewal. The business or anyone else should respect the workers choice, as they don't like to stay in that place. The workers are entitled to stay anywhere they would like because it is at their own expense.

Recommendations:
- Investigate this immediately.  The interpreter or HR should not put conditions on completing the MOU U-turn documents for the workers
- Workers are free to find rental accommodation where they choose, and should not be forced to choosing a particular place to rent
- Discuss with the landlord on behalf of the workers regarding unpaid deposits of 7,500 Baht and facilitate the negotiations so that workers receive back what they are entitled to
remediation_business_steps_taken: K. Chaiyuth, HR manager responded that they were unaware of this message from the interpreter before. According to the company policy, they do not have the policy to arrange for the worker to stay at the same dorm after the MoU U-Turn. The workers can decide for themselves to stay in any apartment. The interpreter miscommunicated to the workers. However, they will investigate and get back to us next week.
remediation_notes: Cambodian workers currently in Cambodia to do the MOU U-turn process were informed by the company interpreter via social media that if workers did not consent to return and continue renting from the previous landlord (workers want to find a new place to rent upon return due to high rental rates in the previous place), the company will not process the MOU U-turn documents for them.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - The company should have a clear policy that workers will not be forced to live in a certain place and this is not set as a condition for providing other rights to workers, i.e. receiving proper working document papers in the MOU U-turn process

Since 2023, the broker has recruited pink card holders, run-away MOU, and CI holders to MMP, charging job seekers 2000-6000 Baht based on their documentation status. Workers with complete documents were charged 2000-4000 Baht, while those without were charged 5000-6000 Baht. HR prioritizes candidates recruited through the broker. -What is the current recruitment practice? 
-Who is the focal points from HR for the recruitment?
-How is the job post announced and what information is included?
-Do the job seekers need to pay any fee for the recruitment?
-Does any broker involved in recruitment process?

-Investigate the recruitment issue involving brokers and illegal fee charges.
-Implement safeguards to protect workers who come forward with complaints and uphold a strict non-retaliation policy.
-If it is confirmed that job seekers were charged illegal or unethical fees, reimburse them.
-Hold accountable any individuals found to have violated the company's recruitment policies or engaged in unethical practices.
-Communicate the recruitment policy to all the workers and HR focal points, in verbal and writing.

Issara contacted the business to report an issue related to recruitment. She explained that she and K Tae, the HR manager, are responsible for the recruitment process. #Issue 1
Context: Workers from Building 4, 3rd floor who were recruited by "Ngwe Kyel Sin Hein" recruitment agency were charged 500 THB for the extension of the two years of MoU documents. Call Id; 9356


#Issue 2

Context: The issue with the workers when they did 2 years MoU extension in August 2019, having asked to pay 1,000 THB for their sub-Wanna for transportation. They were 300 of them at the time who were recruited by Shwe Pyi Nyein.

Issara's recommendations for both issues. 

-The business to do an immediate investigation to assess the number of impacted workers at building 4. Safeguards should be in place throughout the investigation, workers should not be targeted by the supervisor or recruitment agency representative. The investigation should also cover the staff from the recruitment agency to identify the root causes of the issue and understand who was involved in the collection of the money. Actions should be taken towards those who collected the money and the business should clarify with the recruitment agency that no fees should be charged to workers. 

-The business to conduct a confidential survey to identify the impacted workers and payback to them. 

-The business to re-engage with the recruitment agency and revise their agreement if needed. 

-Effective communication in a wide range should be conducted in the written and verbal post including disciplinary action for those who break the business's recruitment policy or do not follow accordingly.  


#Issue 3; 27-Nov-2020

Context; the issue with the walk-in workers in building 7 being asked to donate recruitment fees to the Sub-wanna (RA staff). Workers were asked to donate up to three thousand THB.

-The business to do an immediate investigation to assess the number of impacted workers at building 7 and the amounts they have paid. Safeguards should be in place throughout the investigation, workers should not be targeted by the supervisor or recruitment agency representative and the company should guarantee that the workers job will not be compromised. The investigation should also cover the staff from the recruitment agency to identify the root causes of the issue and understand who was involved in the collection of the money. Actions should be taken towards those who collected the money and the business should clarify to the recruitment agency that no fees should be charged to workers as it is against the company policy. 

-The business to conduct a confidential survey to identify the impacted workers and payback to them while explaining the company policy of "0 fees", guaranteeing that they job will not be at risk and that they will be no retaliation for speaking up". 
-The business to work with the recruitment agency to make sure there is no retaliation towards workers, solve the root causes of the issue by identifying the people involved in the collection of money and clarifying Cal-comp policy of "0 fees". Cal-comp should revise the agreement with the RA as needed. 

-Effective communication in a wide range should be conducted in the written and verbal post including disciplinary action for those who break the business's recruitment policy or do not follow accordingly.  
 


Time Frame 2 pay period.

description: Fees charged by recruitment agency: illegal and unethical
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the recruitment fees being charged by the Wanna said (sub-supervisor). The worker reported contacting a person whose name was included in a job announcement to work at Cal-comp. After contacting the phone number from the announcement, the worker was asked to contact another person, a “Wanna said” who told the worker that she had to pay 2,500 THB for the job application. 

The worker did not mention the channel through which the announcement about the job vacancy was done nor the name of the supervisor who asked her to pay. In addition to that, the worker added that one of her friends was being charged 3500 THB to get a job in Cal-Comp. NOTE: So far, Issara knows about 2 workers being impacted however there could be many more. 

Recommendations for remediation: 
-The business to do an immediate investigation to assess the number of impacted workers and identify the people involved in the recruitment process that has been charging workers. Safeguards should be in place throughout the investigation, and workers should not be targeted by the sub-supervisor or recruitment agency representative. 
-The investigation should also cover the staff from the recruitment agencies to identify the root causes of the issue and understand who was involved in the collection of the money.
- Actions should be taken towards those who collected the money, and the business should clarify with the recruitment agency that no fees should be charged to workers and what are the consequences for not following that policy, such as termination of the contract or disciplinary actions if those involved are Cal-Comp  employees. 
-As part of the investigation and remediation process, the business shall assess how much money new workers have paid and reimbursed them those recruitment fees. 

-The business should set a plan of action with the recruitment agency involved, such as revision of the contract and the penalties for not following the company policy about “zero recruitment fees for workers”, and the actions the agency will take to avoid this from happening again. 

-The business should cross check through different means with the recruitment agency and workers being recruited, how are the services being provided to job seekers, what is the communication like about the job and the recruitment process, etc. 
-One way of conducting the investigation and a vetting process is for Cal-comp to check all the announcements about job vacancies and verify that there are no fees being charged, that the process is handled legally and ethically and that all the recruitment agencies being used work professionally. 

Past history of this case:

Last year (2020) there was a similar case reported and the business conducted investigations for all issues and remediated the impacted workers which is considered a good step made by the company to address issues with recruitment. However, the process took several months and the business did not share with Issara the details of the last investigation conducted regarding walk-in workers being asked to make monetary donations to the Thai RA staff, and only one worker received compensation for that issue. In addition, the company did not follow Issara's recommendation on system change to have communication sessions with all workers and Thai RAs about the company policy of recruitment fees.

Timeframe 1 pay period
