-The business to do an immediate investigation to assess the number of impacted workers and identify the people involved in the recruitment process that has been charging workers. Safeguards should be in place throughout the investigation, and workers should not be targeted by the sub-supervisor or recruitment agency representative. 
-The investigation should also cover the staff from the recruitment agencies to identify the root causes of the issue and understand who was involved in the collection of the money.
- Actions should be taken towards those who collected the money, and the business should clarify with the recruitment agency that no fees should be charged to workers and what are the consequences for not following that policy, such as termination of the contract or disciplinary actions if those involved are Cal-Comp  employees. 
-As part of the investigation and remediation process, the business shall assess how much money new workers have paid and reimbursed them those recruitment fees. 

-The business should set a plan of action with the recruitment agency involved, such as revision of the contract and the penalties for not following the company policy about “zero recruitment fees for workers”, and the actions the agency will take to avoid this from happening again. 

-The business should cross check through different means with the recruitment agency and workers being recruited, how are the services being provided to job seekers, what is the communication like about the job and the recruitment process, etc. 
-One way of conducting the investigation and a vetting process is for Cal-comp to check all the announcements about job vacancies and verify that there are no fees being charged, that the process is handled legally and ethically and that all the recruitment agencies being used work professionally. 

Past history of this case:

Last year (2020) there was a similar case reported and the business conducted investigations for all issues and remediated the impacted workers which is considered a good step made by the company to address issues with recruitment. However, the process took several months and the business did not share with Issara the details of the last investigation conducted regarding walk-in workers being asked to make monetary donations to the Thai RA staff, and only one worker received compensation for that issue. In addition, the company did not follow Issara's recommendation on system change to have communication sessions with all workers and Thai RAs about the company policy of recruitment fees.

Timeframe 1 pay period


Issue # 2. 

Context: the issue with the workers who were recruited by the Thai RA being charged for the transportation and the recruitment fees. The experiences that the workers shared about their recruitment process are as follows: 
Three groups of workers were recruited by a broker from a Thai RA Number 17 and 64.
Ms. Than Than Soe and her business partner,  Ko Min ( Sub-recruiter of Thai RA No.17) were the recruiters. 
Workers were charged 5500 THB (3500 for service fees and 2000 for transportation fees). 
The workers gave 3500 for transportation and 2000 for recruitment fees) to  Ms.Than Than Soe on the day they arrived at Phetchaburi.
Workers have issues with the housing, they are staying somewhere very far from the factory. The recruiter arranged a track for them. The place they live has an issue with the internet, shopping, and emergency medical assistance problem
There are around 50 workers recruited by these recruiters very recently. 


Remediation recommendations:

-The business to do an immediate investigation to assess the number of impacted workers and identify the people involved in the recruitment process that has been charging workers. Safeguards should be in place throughout the investigation, and workers should not be targeted by the sub-recruiter or recruitment agency representative. And the business staff conducting the interviews should make sure that workers are explained and guaranteed safeguards and that their jobs will not be at risk, and that the information they share will be anonymized to make sure workers do not encounter any retaliation or risks from informal brokers and/or RA staff. 
-The investigation should also cover the staff from the recruitment agencies to identify the root causes of the issue and understand who was involved in the collection of the money.
- Actions should be taken towards those who collected the money, and the business should clarify with the recruitment agency that no fees should be charged to workers and what are the consequences for not following that policy, such as termination of the contract, penalties or disciplinary actions imposed by the recruitment agency towards the staff involved in such practices, etc. 
-The business should set a plan of action with the recruitment agency involved, such as revision of the contract and the penalties for not following the company policy about “zero recruitment fees for workers”, and the actions the agency will take to avoid this from happening again. 
-As part of the investigation and remediation process, the business shall assess how much money new workers have paid and reimburse them those recruitment fees. 
-The business should cross-check through different means with the recruitment agency and workers being recruited, how are the services being provided to job seekers, what is the communication like about the job and the recruitment process, etc. 

Talking Points: 

-How is the recent recruitment being handled? How many workers have been recruited recently? 
-How does the business work with the Thai recruitment agency? What is the definition of a recruitment agency with different numbers such as 64, 17, and so on? What is the position of the recruiters Ms. Than Than Soe and her business partner,  Ko Min from recruitment agency 64 and 17? 
-Have there been any recent communication with the Thai recruitment agency based on the previous issue? 

Expected meeting format: 
Business: HR Department, Recruitment Department, Translator. 
Issara: BHR, Involved O & E, Ma Chaw, Sandy, Ana, and John?
HP: K Narisa 

Note* we do not say that these workers are from Songkhla to avoid the risks of workers being targeted.


Case #3 (new case, there are two existing cases for this KPI):
A worker from Cal-Comp Building 9 (HP product) and Building 10 (apple product) reported that workers had to pay 1,000 THB for renewing their passports for their 4-year MoU extension. It was collected by sub recruiter #34 who said that if workers do not want to pay 1,000THB, they would have to go to the embassy by themselves for the extension. He said that all workers have paid already.

Talking points:
Is the business aware that workers are being charged for their MOU extensions?
How is the business checking to ensure recruitment agents don’t charge any fees to workers?

Recommendations for remediation:
The business to investigate this matter immediately
Issue a warning to the recruiter for having violated the employer pays policy and require the recruiter to return the money it charged to the workers
Return the money that workers paid to the recruiter

Case #1-2:

The business is in the process of investigation and have identified certain suspected persons that may have charged recruitment fees from the workers. 
Once the business competes the investigation, impacted workers will be reimbursed.  The business surveyed new employees that joined in August 2021 but found only 1 worker had paid recruitment fees. 

The Strategic Partner (SP) has requested that Issara conduct a recruitment fee survey on behalf of the business to verify recruitment fees paid.  The SP is in the process of securing agreement on the part of the business to move forward with this.

Case #3:

remediation_validation:
Case #1-2:
These issues have been discussed additionally with the Strategic Partner, who has been working with CalComp on escalating issues and CalComp developing a more responsible recruitment process and implementation.  However, issues with current in-country recruitment practices continue to be uncovered, with concerning behavior by Thai recruitment agencies engaged by CalComp and fees being reported by workers.  There is a need to both immediately investigate and repay fees charged to workers in this recruitment, but also develop a more comprehensive plan to address structural issues and resources dedicated to worker recruitment - moving beyond internal company investigations and audits of contracted agencies.  This is particularly pressing given continuing worker reports, continued worker recruitment, and planning for working with Myanmar recruitment agencies for the potential reopening of cross border recruitment.

Issara has conducted the recruitment fee survey with the workers that were hired in 2021. The survey results will be shared with the business and the Strategic Partner for further action to remediate fees paid and improve the recruitment system.

Case #3:
Issara followed up with the workers and learned that this was not about the business charging workers for the passport renewal but workers choosing to pay a broker to expedite the passport renewal.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1:
Six Cambodian workers were charged fees by a sub-recruiter to issue their pink cards (1,300 THB).  They were hired as walk-in workers. At first, they had only their passports and they were referred by their friends to the sub-recruiter who is able to process the pink card, work permit and visa for workers. They paid 13,000 THB each for the whole process. However, six months later, they have only received their work permits but they haven't received their pink card yet. 

Note: This issue was raised during in-person outreach.  The workers that reported these issues did not want to share their identities.

Talking points:
How is the company handling the hiring of walk-in workers?  
Is there a recruitment agency involved?  If so, what is its role?

Recommendations for remediation:
Investigate this issue, include worker voice in the investigation and ensure worker safeguards
Identify the recruiter that has received money from the workers, and require this money be returned
The business should follow the employer pays policy, identify the amount paid by workers for the recruitment, and repay them
Communicate to all workers that the company has an EPP and that workers should not pay for any recruitment fees, including work permit, visa, 90-day extensions


Case #2:
One worker mentioned that for the Cambodian and Burmese workers who received the wages from the sub-contractors, 3% of their wages were being deducted.

Talking points: 
- Is the company aware that some workers are being paid their wages via a sub-contractor and not directly by F&D?
- Is the company aware that the sub-contractor is deducting money for the workers' wages?

Recommendations for remediation:
- All wages of F&D workers should be paid directly by the company and through a sub-contractor, with pay slips provided to the workers in their languages
- Any deductions of workers' wages should be repaid to the workers
- The practice of the sub-contractor deducting a percentage of the workers' wages should be discontinued immediately

They paid 13,000 THB each for the whole process. However, six months later, they have only received their work permits but they haven't received their pink card yet.

Case #2: 
For Cambodian and Burmese workers that are receiving their wages through a sub-contractor, 3% of their wages were being deducted.

description: Fees charged by recruitment agency: illegal and unethical
remediation_issara_recommendation:
# Issue 1: 
Context: Issara received this issue in our housing outreach to Cal-Comp (SMSK) on April 3, 2022.  According to workers that we met at the "pink" dormitory, they heard about other workers having to pay around 5,000 Baht to brokers to get a job at Cal-Comp in Samut Sakhon. And they also heard that workers have to pay 1,000 Baht to brokers to get job cancellation letters.

Recommendations for remediation: 
-The business to do an immediate investigation to assess the number of impacted workers and identify the people involved in the recruitment process that has been charging workers. Worker safeguards should be in place throughout the investigation, and workers should not be retaliated against for having spoken out. 
-The investigation should also cover the staff from the recruitment agencies to identify the root causes of the issue and understand who was involved in the collection of the money.
- Disciplinary actions should be taken towards those who collected the money, and the business should clarify with the recruitment agency involved that no fees should be charged to workers and the consequences for not following that policy, such as termination of the contract or disciplinary actions if those involved are Cal-Comp  employees. 
-As part of the investigation and remediation process, the business shall assess how much money workers have paid and reimburse such amounts. 

-The business should set a plan of action with the recruitment agency involved, such as revision of the contract and the penalties for not following the company policy about “zero recruitment fees for workers”, and the actions the agency will take to avoid this from happening again.
remediation_notes: According to workers that we met at the "pink" dormitory during a housing outreach on April 3, 2022, they heard about other workers having to pay around 5,000 Baht to brokers to get a job at Cal-Comp in Samut Sakhon. And they also heard that workers have to pay 1,000 Baht to brokers to get job cancellation letters.
remediation_action: The business responded that it hasn't recruited any workers in 2022, and therefore there couldn't have been any cases of workers having to pay to get a job at Cal-Comp SMSK.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change
- The business should should develop vetting and selection criteria for the recruitment agencies it will work with.  Issara can provide support with the vetting and selection tool
- Do a full review of current recruitment agencies in Thailand and source countries using the vetting and selection criteria, and consider which RAs to continue working with, which it will stop working with, or new RAs to work with in the future
- Review the management service agreements with each RA, update the MSAs to ensure transparency and zero fees for workers.  Develop MSAs with source country RAs directly.  Issara can provide support with the MSA checklist tool
- Check all job vacancy announcements that its RAs are posting, ensure the announcements make the zero fee policy explicit
- Provide full and accurate job description information for all future job vacancies to the RAs

description: Fees charged by recruitment agency: illegal and unethical
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that in April 2022, SFP recruited 150 undocumented workers. The SFP interpreter posted the job on the SFP Facebook page. The post mentions that there’s no need to pay the application fee. But they heard that some workers had to pay 2,000-5,000 Baht to brokers to secure their jobs. There are some brokers amongst the workers who are closely working with the SFP interpreter (Than Ko Lin). One worker’s close relatives had to pay the application fee to a broker. They heard that there will be another round of recruitment for undocumented workers, and many are waiting to be recruited and are staying in private housing near the factory. 

Talking points:
- What is the business policy on hiring undocumented workers?
- Is the business hiring the workers directly or through a recruitment agency?
- Is SFP implementing the employer pays policy and not charging workers any fees for their recruitment?

Recommendations for remediation:
- Conduct an investigation into reports that undocumented workers that were hired to work at SFP had to pay fees to the recruiters.
- Based on the investigation, determine who has been charging fees to workers and take steps to repay workers that paid any recruitment fees
- Communicate, verbally and in writing, that any recruitment of SFP workers will be zero cost to the workers

description: Fees charged by recruitment agency: illegal and unethical
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Newly hired Lao MOU workers noted that they paid 3.8 million kip and 10 million kip (31,240 Baht); they paid to the recruitment agency but have not received the reimbursement.  The Lao workers also said they had been informed that they would be provided with the essential items such as a mattress, bed, pillow, rice cooker, etc.  However, when they arrived, their dorm room was empty. 

Talking points:
-Is HR aware that workers paid recruitment fees to the recruitment agency and haven't been reimbursed?
-How is Seafresh implementing the zero fee policy and ensuring that workers don't pay any fees?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Investigate what happened during the recruitment process and what amounts workers paid to the recruitment agency.
-Reimburse workers for the recruitment fees that they paid
-Communicate to all workers regarding the Employer Pays Policy and that no fees are to be collected from workers during the recruitment process
-Train the recruitment agencies working with Seafresh to ensure that the agencies are not collecting any fees from workers
-Revise the management service agreements (MSA) with the recruitment agencies so that it clearly states the breakdown fees and costs, and which party will pay for those fees and when.  Also clearly state that workers will not be charged these fees and include clauses of actions to be taken if it is discovered that fees have been paid by workers.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Narumon, HR mentioned that HR conducted the survey with the workers. There are two groups of Lao workers. The first group already got the reimbursement. The second group is in the process of reimbursement. She will send us in detail of the plan and timeline for this reimbursement next week.

Seafresh had a meeting and trained with the recruitment agency regarding the cost and fee that the workers paid and also the facilities that the worker misunderstood that provided the essential items such as a mattress, bed, pillow, rice cooker, etc. According to Seafresh policy, the dorm provides for the room and bed not items that were mentioned previously. However, Seafresh clearly communicated with the workers regarding the employer pay policy and dorm policy when the worker arrived at the orientation session.


K. Narumon, HR send us the corrective action as the follows link and detail below.

ISSUE & WORKER REPORTS
MoU Lao workers reported complaints to Issara as follows:
(1) received communication from the the origin country before coming to work that The dormitory will have amenities such as pillows and bedding, but when they arrive, they don't have them. Workers have to buy
(2) Workers are paid to recruitment companies, some of whom pay 3 million kip.

IDENTIFIED POSSIBLE ROOT CAUSES
(1) Caused by misunderstanding And there is no verification of understanding with the workers. The company has informed on the day of the job interview (origin side) that there are beds and mattresses provided, which workers may misunderstand that pillows and sheets are provided as well.
(2) Workers have expenses related to apply the Passport which is a personal document. Workers are responsible for their own expenses.

(1) 12-17 May 2022: The communication of the dorm provided has been made to workers from the date of the job interview (orgin side)
     25-Aug-22: Worker Orientation Day clarified about the dormitory regulations and the facilities provided
(Details: For clarification of dormitory information, please refer to the dormitory sheet.)
     
(2) 10-Sep-2022: Interview with 100% Lao MoU workers to verify expenses that workers have to pay for transportation to work with the company.
     18-Sep-2022: A Lao Recruitment Agency came to discuss the details of all expenses paid by workers. and answer questions together with the company
     The expenses that workers pay are travel expenses from the agency's office to the border. The agency will return the workers 500 baht each for 74 people within 30-Nov-2022.
(Details of expenses from workers interview and procedures, please refer to the expense sheet)

  In addition, before the interview workers selection, The company has sent a letter of acknowledgment to the agency. Read the details of the company for workers to acknowledge. which will contain details about Principles of ethical recruiting of the company Expenses/recruitment fees for which the employer is responsible including explaining the nature of work, working time, working hours, holidays, leave days, wages, OT, accommodation, medical treatment and termination of employment for workers to make decisions before applying for a job. The interested and acknowledged workers will sign the letter and attend an interview.
(For an example of an acceptance letter, please see Sheet: Letter of Acknowledgment.)


K. Narumon, HR, informed us that the 500 THB reimbursement will be transferred into the workers' bank accounts on December 16.

Context: Cambodian workers who completed 4 years of MoU reported saying that they were charged by the recruitment agency (SMS) for the U-turn process. -The business immediately communicates with SMS and other HR focals who are responsible to do the extension of workers documents and stop charging workers for the extension fees.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Star Butterfly general service Co.ltd
Hoi Yun SDN.NHD. 
 
Recruitment background.
 
10 workers 5 Male and 5 Female were recruited in Mid November 2022. However 2 female workers out of 10 had to pay 5,100,000 Kyats (2424.50 USD)  for the recruitment fees to the broker who was recruiting workers for an Agency named “ Star Butterfly general service” in Myanmar. The rest of the 8 workers did not have to pay any fees for different reasons such as having their relatives in the workplace, being recruited with Zero fees however they also heard that they will be deducted their salary by the employer. However, the contract does not mention the zero recruitment fee. 

Main issues 

They started working on the 18th of November,2022. Two female workers out of 8 called Issara to report the following issues. 

1) Different working conditions from what they were promised for. Their contract does not mention the type of work.Once they apply for the job, the broker said it is packaging of the seafood product, however, workers are having to work at the place which is similar to the pier where they have to sort fresh fish. These two workers said that they have health issues working with the ice and water which is why they did ask the broker about the type of work, the broker said that they will not need to touch water and ice at all but now things turn out the other way around. 
2) Not getting a weekly day off as mentioned in the contract. 
3) Having to work on an hourly rate not daily rate which is against  the contract. 
4) Not getting Malaysian Public holidays.
5) Not having their documents such as passport and permit  in their hand, only provided with the copy of it. 
6) Not knowing when they will receive their wages. They started working on 18th Nov but have not received their wages yet and are not sure when they will receive it. 
7) Not having a safe community to live in; they said that there are only 3 single girls and two females with their husband then the rest of the workforce is male workers, the environment is not safe because of the drug users. These two workers do not feel safe to continue working there. They called the broker to complain about the situation but were told not to complain as they have been working already. They do not have contact with the recruitment agency.

Issara sent a message to follow up with her to learn her expectations for her cases, she said that she and her friends received a salary for 8 days only even though they have worked for about 25 days. The employer said to them that they retain their 15 days of wages as deposit. In addition to that, the employer did not pay for the days that he was not able to provide job, did not get paid for over time as worked, they worked 3 hours of IT some days but received only 2 hours of wages. Workers tried to negotiate to work daily basis but not on an hourly basis, however the employer forced them to work hourly basis. Workers said that they will discuss with the broker who they worked with to get this job, however the employer said not to discuss with the agency or the broker but to decide by themselves. Given that, the workers have called the broker, the broker said that they will inform the agency and agency will try to negotiate. Workers were asked to wait and see for one month.

The worker said that they have reported to the broker about their situation, the broker had suggested them to wait one month until next pay day and see if they need to reach out to the recruitment agency. However, their current situation is that they are not provided with a full day of work, it has been three days that they have been working for only half a day. Given that, the employer asked them to do the office cleaning as a domestic worker which workers did not like the most. Workers wanted Issara to suggest whether they should directly reach out to the Recruitment agency without waiting for another month as suggested by the broker or should they wait for a month? 

Issara provided the contact information of the recruitment agency and asked them to make a proper decision before contacting them and making sure there are no risks for them for contacting the RA. She added that they have been asked to do work here and there with male workers as the employer does not have enough work.

description: Fees charged by recruitment agency: illegal and unethical
Fees charged by recruitment agency: illegal and unethical
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that the recruitment agency is asking them to pay various fees frequently but they don't understand what they are paying for and the recruitment agency isn't clearly explaining what the fees are for. They are having to pay high fees, with the workers needing to pay 4,000 THB to renew their passports and 12,000-14,000 THB for the one-year visa extension fee this year.
NOTE: Some of the mobilizers during the training said they had paid fees to the RA while  others had not.  They think other workers have also paid.

In 2022, an electronic factory named JCY from Saraburi province dismissed around 1,000 workers who had completed a 4-year MoU contract. That factory contacted 'The First Good Man' Thai RA, and most of the workers were directly recruited by King Pac. The workers were divided into two to three groups, and those who raised the issue with Issara arrived on February 16, 2022, mostly. It affects over 600 workers, at least, according to the worker. When the workers arrived at King Pac, those who needed to renew their passports were collected 4,000 Baht to apply for a new passport on March 2, 2022, by Ma Phyu, who is the focal interpreter from 'The First Good Man'. On November 22, 2022, the interpreter announced the cost of a visa and work permit extension on their internal Facebook closed group. The post said the worker had to pay a total of 23,700 THB for the document extension in three allotments: the first payment was 10,000 THB, the second payment was 8,100 THB, and the third payment was 5,600 THB, which was confirmed by the HR office. No workers were informed of the clear cost breakdown. The workers are not aware of what kind of visa and work-permit status they are entitled to now. Their passports and work permits have been retained as reasons for the document extension. When the workers asked the Thai RA for the documents, Ma Phyu said they were in the process of being extended.


TPs:
- Which source-side and Thai RAs is King Pac working with?
- Are RAs allowed to collect money from workers directly?
- How many workers were hired in 2022, when and as what kind of worker (walk-in, MOU)?

Recommendations:
- Clearly communicate the employer pays policy to all workers, so that they know they shouldn't be paying any recruitment fees to recruitment agencies
- Investigate the matter; Issara can conduct the recruitment fee survey on behalf of the business. Any fees workers that have paid should be reimbursed
remediation_business_steps_taken: Khun Jarunee, QSM, asked when the workers were asked to pay these fees. (O&E mentioned that in 2022, but did not specify which month or quarter.) (O&E will get more information and get back to the business)
remediation_notes: Workers reported that last year in 2022, the recruitment agency asked them to pay various fees but they don't understand what they are paying for and the recruitment agency isn't clearly explaining what the fees are for. remediation_action: Issara raised this with the business and the business asked when the workers paid these fees. This will be helpful for their investigation into this matter.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The issue with 30 workers being asked by the business to pay for the U-turn process (15,500 Baht per person, of which they paid the first installment of 7,500 Baht in May 2020) and then in September 2020 being asked to pay for a one-year extension rather than doing the U-turn process due to Covid-19 (2,460 Baht, of which they have been asked to pay 1,400 Baht by Sept 7th), without having been paid back the 7,500 Baht they already paid for the U-turn process. Call-ID - 11063.

Issara recommendations:

-The business to clearly explain to workers about the legal document extension process (given the Covid-19 situation) and what fees are being charged to workers.
-The business to charge workers only the legal amounts allowed by the government for workers' document extensions. 
-The business to coordinate with the recruitment agency to return the money the workers paid in May 2020 and charge only for the one-year extension fees. It is the responsibility of the business to make sure that all workers received their money back regardless of the recruitment agency agrees to pay back or not. 

Time Frame 1 week.

-The business to consider abiding by ethical recruitment principles, and commit to the employer pays principle for all recruitment and legal documentation fees

-Key HR and other personnel to attend Issara Academy's Ethical Recruitment Training.

-The business to have a clear and official agreement with the recruitment agency for the further process of both recruitment agencies (Thai and Myanmar).

description: Fees charged by employer: illegal and unethical
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with workers being charged a different amount of fees compared to past years for their document extension process. 

Issara recommendations remediation:

-The business to clarify what are the fees being collected for document processes, what is the breakdown of those fees, and why are the fees that high? And to explain to all workers how the process will be done during this time (COVID 19). 

-The business to charge workers only the legal amounts allowed by the government for workers' document extensions. 

-Workers should be remediated for any fees they paid above the legal amount. 

-The business to coordinate with the recruitment agency to return the money to the different batches of workers who were impacted. It is the responsibility of the business to make sure that all workers received their money back regardless of the recruitment agency agrees to pay back or not. 

-Workers should receive their money back within a pay period.



Talking Points 
-Ask the business how is the process of document extension for four years of MoU workers being handled? How much do workers have to pay and to whom? 

Please ask for the cost break down. 

-Who is the focal person for the document extension process from the business? Is a Thai RA handling this process, if so, what is the name of the RA and what is the agreement between the RA and GFPT? 

-How many workers are going through this process at the moment, how many have done it this year and how many more would need to extend the documents?

-Please ask the same questions for 2 years of document extension. 

-Please ask the business about the 14500 B that the workers paid in May and whether that will be returned to workers.

-Please share with the business the official amount that can be charged to the worker for the one-year extension. 

-Share information about the August 2020 Cabinet Resolution, that allows workers to complete their 4 years of the MOU contract to register to work in Thailand until March 2022.


Additional talking points Nov 30, 2020
Recommendations for remediation:

Ask for the cost breakdown of these fees (the breakdown that GFPT shared after the last meeting is for Fresh MOU, so that is not applicable/relevant for this case). Explain that the fees workers have reported having to pay are much higher than the official fees. 

Provide the details of the official fees as follows:
MOU 2 years document extension: 1,900THB (work permit) + 500THB (medical check-up) + 1,900 THB (visa for 1 year)+ 80THB (registration fee): 4,380THB. Workers should be reimbursed for any amount they have paid that is above the official cost. 
MOU 4 years extension (as per the Cabinet Resolution 4 August 2020): 1,450 THB (work permit)+500 (medical check-up)+1,900 (visa from Aug/Oct to March 2012)+ 80 THB (registration fee): 3,930 THB. GFPT said during the last meeting that this process is still ongoing for 200-300 workers, ask where exactly is the process, how many batches or number of workers are covered under the Cabinet Resolution of Aug and how many are not? What is the process and what are the fees for those who may not be covered with the Cabinet resolution (maybe those that completed the 4 years before Aug)? The business to share the details of the process being followed for workers completing 4 years of MOU. If GPFT says that they do not know and that it is all being handled by the Thai RA, explain the importance of GFPT being aware of the full process and the cost breakdown. Recommend GFPT to work with the RA to get all the detailed information to be shared with workers. 
The business should communicate with all workers what is the cost breakdown, how would the process be handled by GFPT and the RA(s), and how long would the process take to be completed. 


Recommendation for the plan to prepare for Tesco Zero fees policy that will enter into force in March 2021:

Explain to GFPT that we can provide guidance and recommendations to help them prepare for the enforcement of Tesco Employer Pays Policy that will be going into effect in March 2021
According to Tesco Employer Pays Policy :

All suppliers must obtain a clear understanding of the processes and costs associated with migrant worker recruitment. remediation_issara_recommendation:
The issue with the workers being charged increased amount (100 B) for 90 days report. 


# Issue 1, Talking Points.

-What are the recruitment fees that the business cover for workers at the moment, and would there be any changes once Tesco policy enter into force? (when asking about the fees, please check with the business if the consider the 90 days report as a recruitment fee, if they say yes then ask if the company covers it, if they say no then explain that the 90 days report should be consider a recruitment fees because workers have to go through this process in order to be able to work at the company)

- Ask about the the process of 90 days report, who is in charge of doing it, and why are fees being charged for this process if it is supposed to be a free of charge process. 

- Ask to the business how much are workers having to pay for this process and ask why it has recently increased? 

- How is the business preparing to implement the Employer Pays Principle that is entering into force in March according to their buyer's code of conduct?

Recommendations:
-If the company says that based on their policy workers should NOT pay for these fees: i) explain to the business that workers should be compensated for the fees they had paid, so there should be an investigation to identify the impacted workers and pay them back, ii) the investigation should also aim to identify who is not following the company policy and if collecting money for this process, and take disciplinary actions according to the company disciplinary protocol. 

BUT 

-If the business confirms that all workers have been paying for these fees and according to their policy these fees should be covered by workers, recommend the business to revise their policy and include the 90 days report fees under the list of fees to be covered by the business to be aligned with the buyer code of conduct. Once the policy is revised the company should inform all workers the company policy changes by written and verbal announcements. 

Timeframe: one pay period 

#Issue 2, Talking points. INTERNAL NOTE; This talking point is not for this issue, the reason is that we are facing system errors so that the talking points for the issue with the Utility are being placed here. When the system works properly, these talking points will be moved to the related KPI. 

Context; the issue with the worker's housing fees being increased. 
-How many housings do the business own? What are the rental fees? Are there any changes to the rental fees recently for the housings? If there are any changes, increased, what was the process? Did the business communicate with all workers? Did the business renew the new contract? If not, please recommend the business to communicate with all workers and renew their contract. Each household should be received one updated contract. 

**Internal Note for BHR team**
 If the business responds neither collecting any fees nor increasing the fees, please do not provide any recommendation and wrap up the conversation because we need to confirm with more workers.

Context: The issue with the workers whose visas were not extended on time due the government’s policy which caused the delay of 90 days report, having to pay 500 THB as a fine to the immigration officer. The worker reported that one of the staff from the business collected 500 THB from each worker and asked one worker to do the process. The TUF staff did not do the full process, instead, asking a worker to do his job when they arrive at the immigration. 

Recommendation: 
-The business shall conduct an investigation to find out why the workers are being charged 500 THB and also to find out the root cause of why there were delays in the document extension process that then caused the delay on the 90 days report. 
- In addition, the business should investigate why some specific workers are asked to be involved in the document extension process for other workers, and why this process was not fully handled by the company staff
-The business shall find out the number of impacted workers and reimburse all impacted workers who had to pay for the 90 day report fine. 

Talking Points: 
-Workers reported being asked to pay 500 THB for the fine for delaying the 90 days report. What is the business understanding of this? 
-Who is the person responsible for handling these kinds of processes, why was the process delayed, and why are specific workers being asked to do the process on behalf of other workers?
-How many workers have been delayed for their 90 day report so far? 
-What is the business plan to avoid this happening in the future? 
- What is the reason why workers' documents are being delayed for the extension even though they have informed the HR on time?
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had meeting with the business, the business responded that they charge the fees for work permit and visa, however this fees should be the fine for the 90 days report overdue which the business agree to conduct the investigation and come up with the remediation plan within seven days.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
System change recommendations:
-The business shall make clear verbal and written announcements about the business policy for the document extension process and also the focal person who is assigned to do this job. The communication should include the roles and responsibilities of the focal and it should be clear that the workers should not be asked to handle the documents and fees of other workers. 
-The business shall also communicate the reimbursement plan to the workers.

remediation_action:
Issara raised this issue with the business, and the business noted that this delay was due to the government authorities not being able to process the documents amidst the current Covid-19 situation.  The workers' visas are in the process of being extended, and the business has communicated this update to workers.

The business committed to continue working with the government to make sure that the worker's documents are extended on time without any delay. In addition, the business confirmed it will reimburse the impacted workers for the late payment fine (500 Baht) they had to pay.
remediation_validation: Issara checked with 11 workers and they confirmed receiving the reimbursement for the late payment fine (500 Baht) for the visa extension.
remediation_results:
The time to complete the visa extension process is uncertain due to the current COVID outbreak and the delay from government offices. 

Workers have now received the visa extension and were reimbursed for the late payment fee of the visa extension.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
System change recommendations:
-The business shall make clear verbal and written announcements about the business policy for the document extension process and also the focal person who is assigned to do this job. The communication should include the roles and responsibilities of the focal and it should be clear that the workers should not be asked to handle the documents and fees of other workers. 
-The business shall also communicate the reimbursement plan to the workers.
systems_change_business_steps_taken: The business agreed to work with the government officials to make sure workers' documents are extended on time. However, it was not clear about the process and the approach.

description: Fees charged by employer: illegal and unethical
remediation_issara_recommendation: Context: The Issue with excessive recruitment fees being collected by the HR staff. Workers reported that  Ms. Tu from HR was the one who had collected recruitment fees from workers. It was in two payrolls ( 8600 baht and asked them to give another 5000 baht). These are the workers whose 4 years of MoU have ended. In addition to that, the workers added that the business charges up to 32,000 THB to the workers for the documentation process. There are some of the workers who have been hired without having proper legal documents by the business, added by the workers.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara is checking with the Betagro about the recruitment policy of the Kaipann Pi Pi. Issara has not shared the issue detail with the business as they have expressed concern given the small workforce on the farm.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that HR collected recruitment fees from workers whose 4-year MOU ended. It was over two payrolls (8,600 baht and 5,000 baht). In addition to that, the workers added that the business charges up to 32,000 THB to the workers for the documentation process. There are even some workers who have been hired by the business without the proper legal documents.
remediation_action: Though Betagro has a business relationship with this business, Betagro has noted that it has no leverage over it because Betagro is only its supplier and not a buyer.  Without Betagro's support, Issara will not share this issue with the business because of the risk that the workers that reported this issue may be identified with possible retaliation from the business.
remediation_validation: We did not follow up with workers because we have not raised this issue with the business.
remediation_results: This case is being closed with a poor rating due to the risks to workers if Issara were to discuss it with the business, as there is no leverage from its buyer.

description: Fees charged by employer: illegal and unethical
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A woroker from ISA Value stated that he came to Thailand via the undocumented channel in October 2021 and started working on Oct 2021 and the business collected 2,450 Baht after 15 days of working in ISA Value for pink card application. The client said, in his recruitment journey, he had to pay transportation fees and other expenses from his own pocket.

NOTE* I would suggest generally sharing the issue and also giving some example based on this issue but not sharing the information of the worker. 

TPs:
- What are the company’s current hiring practices, whether through the formal MOU channel or hiring walk-in workers already in Thailand?
- Is it aware of Amazon’s Employer Pays Policy and the company’s obligation to ensure that workers don’t pay for any recruitment-related fees or expenses?

Recommendations for remediation: 
-The business to do an immediate investigation to assess the number of impacted workers and identify the people involved in the recruitment process that has been charging workers. Worker safeguards should be in place throughout the investigation, and workers should not be retaliated against for having spoken out. 
- Disciplinary actions should be taken towards those who collected the money, and the consequences for not following that policy, such as disciplinary actions if those involved are ISA Value staff. 
-As part of the investigation and remediation process, the business shall assess how much money workers have paid and reimburse such amounts. 
-Request to conduct workers recruitment fees survey by Issara.
remediation_business_steps_taken: The ISA Value recruitment policy still requires the worker to pay for the document. They intend to be the employer step by step, such as which fees and costs should be covered by the employer. Work permit 1,450 and health issurance 990 and stamp 10.
remediation_notes: A worker stated that he had migrated to Thailand via the undocumented channel in October 2021 and found work at this business through his sister's introduction who is already working here. He said the business collected 2,450 Baht from him for the pink card application.
remediation_action: The company's recruitment policy still requires the worker to pay for the recruitment-related fees of personal document processing. They intend to gradually implement the Employer Pays Policy in phases.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change
- The business should review its current hiring practices, including how it is hiring workers that are already in Thailand or those that may have migrated to Thailand recently but not through the MOU channel
- Ensure that for all new hires, it is fully compliant with the Employer Pays Policy
- Attend the second ER training for Amazon suppliers, which will be scheduled later this year (tentatively Oct or Nov 2022)

description: Fees charged by employer: illegal and unethical
closed_notes: Issara is closing this case.  The business has stated that it is currently not covering the fees for the pink card application and currently is not able to implement the zero fee recruitment of workers.

description: Fees charged by employer: illegal and unethical
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issara had an ongoing meeting with the business where the business explained that they only cover the recruitment fees for new MOU workers when workers are first recruited. However, other recruitment related fees such as document extension (work permit renewal, ongoing documentation related to employment) are not covered by the business. The business pays the fees in advance but those fees are then deducted from workers paychecks. This practice is against an employer pays policy, as all recruitment fees, including document extension costs, should be covered by the employer.


Talking points:
- We really appreciate our open discussion on current practices, recruitment in general, and how our partnership can work.
- Thanks a lot for raising that currently workers are paying for work permit and visa renewal, or other fees related to ongoing employment such as an updated health check.
- In our ongoing discussions with Nike, we clarified that these fees would fall under their employer pays policy, and should be covered by the employer.  This is also pretty standard for all definitions of employer pays.
- Our recommendation would be to change this practice now, and clarify with workers that these fees will be paid directly by Everest.  You can confirm this shift to us and to Nike.
- Issara and Nike will follow up on the previous practice and include this in our discussions with all Nike suppliers on ways forward in recruitment practice and learning.
- Issara can support the business to fully investigate if all workers are being charged these types of costs, and ensure full documentation of all affected workers, costs paid, and recommendations for repayment of recruitment and employment fees charged.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara has escalated this issue with the business, the business was not very clearly aware of the Nike policy regarding the Employer Pay Policy. The business responded and said that they will conduct payback to the workers. It was not clear with the process and the timeline. The business added that they will start following the employer pay policy starting from 2022.
The workers confirmed receiving their documents extension fees back from the employer. The amount that they have received was 13,500 THB per worker. 
This issue will remain open until Issara conducts the recruitment fees survey and analyse the amount that the workers have paid so far. After the verification through survey, Issara will consider to close the case with associated rating. At this point, it is hard to say whether the paid amount to the workers is align with what the workers have paid.
remediation_notes: Issara had an ongoing meeting with the business where the business explained that they only cover the recruitment fees for new MOU migrant workers (there are an estimated 28 Cambodian workers affected) when workers are first recruited.
remediation_action:
The business explained that they pay the fees in advance but those fees are then deducted from workers paychecks.

This issue was escalated to the company management and the company responded that they had consulted with the Strategic Partner in Thailand and that the Cambodian workers' recruitment fees would be reimbursed.

Starting in 2022, the company will implement the employer pay policy for extension fees. The company has shared the draft policy announcement with Issara, which will be reviewed and feedback provided.

The business has paid back the workers the amount of 13,350 Baht to the Cambodian workers.  It has also agreed to have Issara conduct the recruitment fee survey with the Cambodian workers, and this is in progress.
remediation_validation: The reported fees charged to workers would violate an employer pays or responsible recruitment policy or commitment, as these types of costs are directly related to recruitment and ongoing employment, such as a work permit renewal.  Issara will be conducting a recruitment fee survey to fully investigate if all workers are being charged these types of costs, and ensure full documentation of all affected workers, costs paid, and recommendations for repayment of recruitment and employment fees charged.
remediation_results: This issue will be closed after we get preliminary findings from the recruitment fee survey to determine additional fees workers may have paid in addition to what the business has paid back to workers.

15 Sep 2023 Tri-party call
The business noted that the business pays for all official receipted fees that workers need to pay for document extension. There is no policy that worker pays half and the business pays half. K. Tithipol, Senior Human Rights Specialist, Tesco Thailand sent an email for NRF's corrective action.

remediation_action: The business noted that the business pays for all official receipted fees that workers need to pay for document extension. There is no policy that worker pays half and the business pays half. The business provided evidence that no deductions for recruitment fees were made from workers' pay slips. For unofficial fees though, the worker is expected to pay. The business will discuss internally about repaying workers for unofficial recruitment and document extension-related fees.  In the future, it will not allow for any unofficial payments, such as for express service fees.
remediation_validation: A worker updated Issara saying that he did not see any workers resign these days, and so he is not aware of any departing workers having to pay back recruitment and document extension fees.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue 1

The issue with the workers being asked to come 20 mins early and not getting paid. 

Recommendations for issue 1.
-Initiate the remediation process.  
-Determine the impact on workers and pay back the unpaid OT owed. 

-Determine the desired policy and shift, and implement/communicate accordingly. Clarify to all workers the true and complete working hours, and pay them according to those working hours at the appropriate rate according to Thai law.

Issue 2 (Aug 14, 2020)

Context: The issue with the workers being paid with OT rate for working on Sundays and public holidays. 

Recommendations for issue 2.

-The business to initiate the remediation process. Investigate to identify the impacted workers and payback owed wages. 

-Clarify to all workers the true and complete working hours, and pay them according to those working hours at the appropriate rate according to Thai law. 

-The workers should not work on Sundays if they have already worked the maximum number of hours per week from Monday to Saturday.

Additional talking points:
General questions for Issue 2. 

-Please ask the business about their production plan for this season and how does this vary throughout the year?

-How many Sundays do the workers have to work during this time.

-Why are only some workers being asked to work on Sundays and Public holidays? How does the workload vary across buildings? 

-How does the business calculate the payment for working on Sundays and Public holidays?

description: Issues with wages: in violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; On 24 May, workers reported loudspeaker announcements from the business that if they find more positive cases in the factory and they have to shut down the factory after 25 May, they will not pay any wage to the workers for those days they are closed. In addition to that, workers reported that issue with workers' annual leaves being deducted for the days that the workers had to take home isolation to monitor the situation of high risks workers from COVID-19 outbreaks. The workers were asked to take home quarantine during 3-6 May 2021 and 7-15, but the workers' annual leaves have been deducted without workers' consent. 


Recommendations. 
-The business should reinstate workers' annual leaves and use the medical leave instead for the days that were closed due to COVID-19 outbreaks. 


Talking points. 

-How many days in total did the factory close for? 
-How many days of workers' annual leaves have been deducted? How many worker's leaves have been deducted? 
-Workers reported not being communicated about the deduction of their annual leaves, is the business aware of this? If yes, what was the understanding of the business about workers' annual leaves?

Within two weeks.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had several meetings including country level escalation and Try party meetings with (SP, Issara and the business). The business argued that since the deduction was for the COVID-19 high risk workers to take home isolation, the workers do not have any sickness relevant document to approve it as a sick leave. Therefore, the business does not agree to provide sick leave but decided to deduct worker annual leaves. After several meetings and the recommendations from Issara, the business acknowledged the consent that is required from the workers, however did not agree to reimburse or remediate the already impacted workers. The business committed to improve in the future but not to reinstate for this case. Since the business clearly stated not returning workers annual leaves, Issara considered closing this case at this point.
remediation_business_steps_remaining: To reimburse the workers annual leaves back.

description: Issues with wages: in violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the shortage of OT working hours payment. Workers reported that whenever they are asked to do the overtime working hours, the employer does not pay them for those hours. The employer asks workers to do free OT and say that it is helping each other. However, if workers are late to work for even a few minutes, the employer cut their wages up to an hour for being late.

Recommendations: 

-The business shall conduct an investigation, and reimburse the worker's wages immediately. 
-All workers should be paid according to the LPA. 
-All workers should be communicated about the business plan to solve this issue.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara had a call with Betagro K Thanat and K Tithipol about the Kaipan PP case.
Bategro will discuss this matter with Kaipan PP but K Thanat noted again that they don't have much influence over Kaipan PP, that Betagro is a supplier of animal feed to Kaipan PP as the customer and although Betagro buys some chicks from Kaipan, it's a small volume and Kaipan doesn't really need to supply to them.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that they were not paid for their OT hours, with the employer saying this was about helping each other out.  This has been happening about twice a week, with 1-2 OT hours each time based on the workload, and for several years now, and affects workers in the chick injection line.
remediation_action: Issara doesn't have direct contact with this business (A).  However, Issara has spoken to a business (B) that sells a large amount of feed to, and buys a small amount of chicks from, this business (A).  Business (B) will provide this case information to Business (A) for their consideration and action.
remediation_validation: The worker provided an update saying that the farm has recruited more workers to distribute the workload and has also started paying OT wages recently, about a month ago in November 2021. However, this worker noted that there were other issues that workers at the farm were facing, such as being charged to renew their visas and pregnant workers being unfairly dismissed.

description: Issues with wages: in violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The factory owner appears to have changed a few months ago, as the workers were asked to sign a sheet about the new employer, and all workers were switched to being piece-rate workers rather than daily workers. When the workers asked the business about signing, they were not given any explanation but were forced to sign. The workers have to work from 6:00 to 16:00 (9 hours) but they earn only around 350 Baht on average if they can work very fast. The new walk-in workers that don't have experience cannot work fast, and they earn less than minimum wage (like 150, 280, etc.) even after working 9 hours per day. No worker understands the calculation of payment and working hours. They are not happy about being piece-rate workers. 

TPs:
-All workers should be on employment contracts that provide at least minimum wages for 8 hours and OT pay for any work beyond that.  Pay cannot be calculated on a piece-rate basis

Recommendations for remediation:
-Ensure that workers are paid for their work according to the law; that employment contracts for workers clearly state the payment terms and conditions
-Reimburse workers for lost wages since the workers were told that they would be paid according to piece rate wages.  Calculate the hours worked per worker and pay according to day rates and OT rates set by the government

The factory owner appears to have changed a few months ago, as the workers were asked to sign a sheet about the new employer, and all workers were switched to being piece-rate workers rather than daily workers. When the workers asked the business about signing, they were not given any explanation but were forced to sign. The workers have to work from 6:00 to 16:00 (9 hours) but they earn only around 350 Baht on average if they can work very fast. The new walk-in workers that don't have experience cannot work fast, and they earn less than minimum wage (like 150, 280, etc.) even after working 9 hours per day. No worker understands the calculation of payment and working hours. They are not happy about being piece-rate workers. 

TPs:
-All workers should be on employment contracts that provide at least minimum wages for 8 hours and OT pay for any work beyond that.  Pay cannot be calculated on a piece-rate basis

-Ensure that workers are paid for their work according to the law; that employment contracts for workers clearly state the payment terms and conditions
-Reimburse workers for lost wages since the workers were told that they would be paid according to piece rate wages.  Calculate the hours worked per worker and pay according to day rates and OT rates set by the government

When they worked on public holidays, they were not paid at the double rate. In 2023, the business didn't fully give 13 public holidays as required by law. A worker called to report a recurring issue of suppression from the line supervisors.
The worker raised that in these few months, 1-2 times the line supervisor asked workers to complete the target first before they could leave during their two hours of OT work. Each time that line supervisor asks workers to complete the target of two hours of OT, the workers need to do 5–10 minutes extra, but they receive only two hours paid for OT.The workers don't appreciate this practice, even though it doesn't happen all the time, because they need to catch the bus on time; otherwise, the bus will leave them.
The worker suggests that the line supervisors should be trained and not suppress the worker's efforts to complete the target. On the other hand, the OT hours should be counted or summed up of all the minutes or hours that worker worked.
Details information:
- Plant: Processing Plant (Brae Roub)
- Department: Kirami
- Line: S3
- There are 6 lines, and each line has 70–80 workers.

1. Will I be targeted if I urge or raise an issue against supervisors or an issue that happened at the workplace? The worker's concern that the business will not do visa extensions or renew the documents for him when he completes the 2/4 MOU contract.
2. Any disciplinary action that leads to not renewing or terminating the workers' contracts? The decision made by the line supervisor or HR?

description: Issues with wages: in violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: the client arrived in Malaysia on 19th October 2023. upon arrival they were picked up by a Tamil broker who they referred as Boss. the first month or so after they came they did not have any work, until the Tamil broker sent them to this place to work. following are the issues and findings from the client:

- there are 5 of them.
- before departure from Bangladesh they were told their job is in plum oil industry. however, they are given work to harvest tomatoes. 
- they have been working in this place for 17 days. 
- instead of 8 hours shift they have to work 12 hour shifts. 
- they were promised that they could make up to RM2200-RM2300, but are told they will be paid RM20 per day.
- the Tamil guy who sent them here is not replying to their calls and messages, asking them "why they have so many problems".
- they asked the Tamil broker to give them different job, but he did not agree.
- they do not have their passport with them, they believe their passport is with the Tamil broker. 
- they are planning and trying to leave the place and find other places to work. 

Issara had a follow up call with them and following are the updates received from the client: 

- 5 of them left the workplace in the afternoon. 
- they contacted the Tamil broker prior to them leaving, stating their plan to leave and come to him. he responded by saying, if they leave the place he will not be liable for them. 
- they also consulted their recruitment agency back in Bangladesh. the agency suggested them to leave and go to the Tamil broker and assured them if they face any problems they will help. 
- together all 5 of them received RM500 for working 12 hour shift of 17 days. 
- they are paying the taxi they rented by themselves. 
- location they are going to is: Taman Desa Aman, 09400 Karangan, Kedah, Malaysia

Issara staff is engaged with them following all the updates provided by the client.

- together all 5 of them received RM500 for working 12 hour shift of 17 days.

- location they are going to is: Taman Desa Aman, 09400 Karangan, Kedah, Malaysia

- they went to the Tamil broker and took their passport.

- through the help of the RA back in Bangladesh (Baron Overseas Limited) they got a job in plum industry.

description: Issues with wages: in violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that he needed to get surgery for which he was in the hospital for 15 days, with costs covered by the employer. He said it seems he was discharged at the urging of the employer who wanted him to return to work.  However, his surgical wound has not healed and it seems the stitches are tearing apart. He has also received less than what his monthly salary should be last month, and his passport is being withheld by the employer.

Recommendations:
- Advise the worker to go to the hospital and seek medical attention directly. Also, he should contact the Nepal embassy for assistance.
- Option 1: Issara to contact the employer directly to advise him of his responsibilities that the worker is given the proper medical care and time to fully heal before returning to work and that the costs should be covered by insurance or the employer rather than the worker.  This is of primary concern.  However, there is also the issue of withholding of wages and document retention, which the employer should be advised to correct. This advice may need to be given after the worker has received the proper medical attention first, lest there be a risk that the employer may refuse to support the worker on all counts.
- Option 2: Issara to refer to partner CSOs if such appropriate partners are available

description: Issues with wages: in violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers arrived on Dec 22, 2023 (sent by Pwint Phoo Aung RA), and started work on Jan 15, 2024. They all had to work and paid as piece-rate workers. About 10 workers cannot finish the target, and they requested the Thai RA interpreter to become daily rate workers. However, the Thai RA interpreter told them that they have to pay money if they want to be daily wage workers. They work from 6:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. but they earn only 348 THB, which is only the daily minimum wage. The employer also deducted six days of their wages as a "deposit" on Jan 24, 2024.

Recommendations:
- The business to pay all workers according to the daily minimum wage, and pay OT rates for any work beyond the 8-hour daily shift.
- Communicate this clearly to workers so they understand the terms and conditions of payment.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 7 Feb 2024

K. Nutthapol, MD received the case detail with the issues. They will investigate and get back to us with the investigation result and corrective action by next week.
remediation_notes: Workers started work in January 2024 and were told they would be paid on a piece rate basis but they are working around 11 hours each day but only being paid approximately the daily minimum wage.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - HR systems should have a clear policy on complying to Thai labor laws, and to pay workers at least the daily minimum wage.
next_description: get the business corrective action.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
#Issue 1. 
Context: The issue with a worker who has an injury with his eye at the workplace.

Issara recommendation. 

-The business to provide every update information to the client from the hospital and the SSF regarding this case.
-The client has the right to know all of the information regarding his health issue.

#Issue 2. (6-Oct-2020) 
The issue with the 100THB incentive has been ceased since a year ago. 

-No recommendations for remediation. 

Time Frame; 1 week.


Talking Points 

Context: The client reported that he is in the process of requesting compensation for his loss of sight. The client wants to know where the process is now, and when he will receive compensation from the SSF. How much longer does he need to wait?

Internal note for BHR: 
-The client reported that he finds it inconvenient to ask all this detail to the factory translator as the translator is not friendly or willing to talk to him.


Questions to the business. 
-What is the status of the process? Who is handling this specific case? Is there a specific translator involved? 
-What is the percentage of the loss of sight? 
-How and when does the business expect the payment from the compensation fund to be received by the client?
-What is the doctor's comment regarding the client's injury? Is this injury treatable or not?

#Issue 2. (CLOSED)
Please ask the following questions to the business. 

-Why are the workers not receiving this incentive? 
-Any communication has been done if the policy has been changed?


#Issue 3. 2021-02-10
The issue with the workers who have concerns using the business application. 

Recommendations;

-The business is suggested to conduct the communication about the purpose of the app and it's use including 
(1) how does it works 
(2) how is personal data of the users handled (this is a question related to data security and confidentiality) and also what kind of data is collected with the app, does it collects data on workers location during their free time? and if so, how is that info handled, and what other information this app will track) 
(3) does the application collects any information on other apps used by the workers on their phones and/or the browser and the websites they visit?
and
(4)the data usage (whether this app needs credits from workers to use it or not). 
-Communication should also include the benefits of using this app and also the guidance on how to use it effectively. 

**Talking Points**

-What is this application for? How does this application track the worker's activities? 
-How did the business explain what the app is about to the workers?
-How is the confidential information of users being handled?
-What kind of information users need to provide in order to use this application? 
-When do workers need to use this application?
-How many workers have registered on this application so far?

Timeframe - One week
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issue # 1.
The business has been helping the worker to follow the process to get compensation from SSF. However, the status of the process hasn't been clearly communicated to the worker because the evaluation has to come from the doctor which has not come yet. The worker has been communicated about the business response and also suggested reaching out to the translator if he has more inquiries. Issara could not contact this worker for several weeks, therefore, this case is considered to be closed. 

Issue# 2. (CLOSED) 

The business updated that their investigation found providing 100 B incentives to the workers who agree to switch their day off from Sunday to weekdays. O & E could not contact the workers to verify. As Issara has not received additional complaints from other workers, this issue is considered to be closed. 

Issue # 3. 
The business responded having done the communication about the purpose of the applications to all workers. The business added that they also have a station where workers can reach out and have clarity if they have any questions about the application.
Workers confirmed that using this application is not of the high priority given the improved situation about the COVID-19 measures in the province.

None

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with some workers whose visas have expired as it was not extended by the business even though workers provided to HR staff their passports and visa fees extension on time. Workers added that only their work permits have been extended so that some of them have been working without a valid visa since June, 2021. 


Talking Points

-Workers reported to Issara that their visas are not being extended on time and now the workers are working with invalid visas. What is the business understanding on this issue? 
-How many workers are there in this situation?
-What is the process for this group of workers? 
- What is the company’s plan to prevent workers from having issues with the local police for not having valid visas? And what kind of support would they provide in case it actually happened? 

Recommendations

-The business shall have a communication session with the workers and explain in detail how the process is being handled, by whom, timeframes and an explanation of why their documents have not been extended, and how would the company respond in case there are any penalties imposed by the immigration office. 
-The communication should also include information on how the company would protect workers from having any issues with the local police for not having valid documents.
-In ethical recruitment practices, it is the employer's responsibility to make sure all workers' documents are up to date and workers receive clear information about the process.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers whose visas were not extended on time due the government’s policy which caused the delay of 90 days report, having to pay 500 THB as a fine to the immigration officer. The worker reported that one of the staff from the business collected 500 THB from each worker and asked one worker to do the process. The TUF staff did not do the full process, instead, asking a worker to do his job when they arrive at the immigration. 

Recommendation: 
-The business shall conduct an investigation to find out why the workers are being charged 500 THB and also to find out the root cause of why there were delays in the document extension process that then caused the delay on the 90 days report. 
- In addition, the business should investigate why some specific workers are asked to be involved in the document extension process for other workers, and why this process was not fully handled by the company staff
-The business shall find out the number of impacted workers and reimburse all impacted workers who had to pay for the 90 day report fine. 


Talking Points: 
-Workers reported being asked to pay 500 THB for the fine for delaying the 90 days report. What is the business understanding of this? 
-Who is the person responsible for handling these kinds of processes, why was the process delayed, and why are specific workers being asked to do the process on behalf of other workers?
-How many workers have been delayed for their 90 day report so far? 
-What is the business plan to avoid this happening in the future? 
- What is the reason why workers' documents are being delayed for the extension even though they have informed the HR on time?
