The worker reported that one of the staff from the business collected 500 THB from each worker and asked one worker to do the process. The TUF staff did not do the full process, instead, asking a worker to do his job when they arrive at the immigration. 

Recommendation: 
-The business shall conduct an investigation to find out why the workers are being charged 500 THB and also to find out the root cause of why there were delays in the document extension process that then caused the delay on the 90 days report. 
- In addition, the business should investigate why some specific workers are asked to be involved in the document extension process for other workers, and why this process was not fully handled by the company staff
-The business shall find out the number of impacted workers and reimburse all impacted workers who had to pay for the 90 day report fine. 


Talking Points: 
-Workers reported being asked to pay 500 THB for the fine for delaying the 90 days report. What is the business understanding of this? 
-Who is the person responsible for handling these kinds of processes, why was the process delayed, and why are specific workers being asked to do the process on behalf of other workers?
-How many workers have been delayed for their 90 day report so far? 
-What is the business plan to avoid this happening in the future? 
- What is the reason why workers' documents are being delayed for the extension even though they have informed the HR on time?
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had a meeting with the business, the business responded that they have conducted the investigation and found the root cause which the immigration had a limited number for document extension because of COVID-19 spread which causes workers documents to get delayed for the extensions. However, the business committed that they will continue working with the government to make sure that the worker's documents are extended on time without any delay. In addition that, the business confirmed to reimburse the impacted workers by the second week of October. Issara checked with the workers that have reported issues, workers confirmed being reimbursed. It is added that 115 workers were being announced to do the extension during this period.
remediation_notes: The issue with some workers whose visas have expired since June 2021 but have not been extended by the business even though workers provided their passports and visa extension fees on time to HR staff.  Workers also had to pay a 500 Baht fine for visa extension past the expiration date.
remediation_action:
Issara raised this issue with the business, and the business noted that this delay was due to the government authorities not being able to process the documents amidst the current Covid-19 situation.  The workers' visas are in the process of being extended, and the business has communicated this update to workers.

The business committed to continue working with the government to make sure that the worker's documents are extended on time without any delay. In addition, the business confirmed it will reimburse the impacted workers for the late payment fine (500 Baht) they had to pay.
remediation_validation: Issara checked with 11 workers and they confirmed receiving the reimbursement for the late payment fine (500 Baht) for the visa extension.
remediation_results:
The time to complete the visa extension process is uncertain due to the current COVID outbreak and the delay from government offices. 

Workers have now received the visa extension and were reimbursed for the late payment fee of the visa extension.

According to workers and based on the announcements based by the business regarding document extension during that period, it is calculated that 115 workers were also impacted by this issue. The business did not provide any details to Issara about the number of impacted workers, however, they said that all impacted workers were compensated.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
System change recommendations:
-The business shall make clear verbal and written announcements about the business policy for the document extension process and also the focal person who is assigned to do this job. The communication should include the roles and responsibilities of the focal and it should be clear that the workers should not be asked to handle the documents and fees of other workers. 
-The business shall also communicate the reimbursement plan to the workers.
systems_change_business_steps_taken: The business agreed to work with the government officials to make sure workers' documents are extended on time. However, it was not clear about the process and the approach.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the short notice for the 90 days extension. Workers added the timeframe that the business gives to submit their passport for the extension is too short and limited which means the workers have challenges following the announcement. The time given was only two days in advance (25 Nov to 27 Nov) within two-time slots (7-9 am and 4-6 PM) which some workers could not do as their shift overlapped with the provided time. 

Recommendations:
-The business should investigate to find out why only two days advance notice was provided for workers to submit their documents for the 90-day report. and consider the timeframe as requested by the workers. 
- The business should interview and seek feedback from workers as to what would be a realistic timeframe in which to be notified that they need to submit their documents for the 90-day report 
-Since the 90-day report could be done two weeks in advance, the business should provide more advance notice and a flexible timeframe within which workers can submit their documents with no challenges. 


Talking Points: 
-How many times does the business do the 90 days extension per month?
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara raised this issue with the business, the business said that they have communicated with the workers and also did the follow-up with them to make sure their documents are extended, however, for this case workers fail to submit the documents on time for the 90 days extension that is the reason there are some workers whose 90 days reports have been expired. The business agreed to continue helping workers even though they have failed to submit on time and make the announcements for the future. Issara has communicated with the workers. Workers have not raised additional concern since then.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that the business did not provide enough advance notice for them to hand in their passports to process the 90-day report.  The business had announced it only two days in advance and provided only two time slots (7-9am and 4-6pm) when they could submit their passports, which only conflicted with their work shift hours.
remediation_action: Issara raised this issue with the business, and the business said that they had made the announcement and also a follow-up announcement but the workers had failed to submit their passports for the 90-day report extension.  The business agreed to continue helping workers who didn't get their 90-day reports done on time.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:

-The business should set up a system that provides sufficient advance notice so that workers have plenty of time to submit their documents for visa and work permit extensions, and 90-day reports, and can be submitted at a time that doesn’t conflict with their work shift hours.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_business_steps_taken:
They confirmed that the company policy clearly states that no one can ask for money to purchase a gift for another. They will conduct an investigation with workers' safeguard and return to us with a corrective action plan within 7 working days.

Please find the corrective action table from TUF.
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RpMMpmNU-UKDNmHH_Xs6Zo9gZDj_O-qP/edit#


Root cause:

The company investigated and found the following information; 
Before the New Year, employees at the fry production line discussed giving New Year’s gifts to their supervisors as a ‘Thank you gift’ for taking good care of the employees throughout the year. A daily employee was the person who collected money from fellow employees. The total amount collected was 9,000 THB.
Before collecting the money, the employee will ask for their willingness to contribute or not, including not telling the exact amount of money they would like to give. Some colleagues gave 100, 200, and 300 THB. After collecting such money, it was given to another employee. The money was used to buy gifts. And the employees gave them to 5 supervisors.  

Corrective/Preventive

- The company will conduct further investigations with all involved parties. If it is found that the action is inconsistent with the company’s regulations, disciplinary action will be taken. 
- The company has created public relations materials, such as posters and videos in languages that the employees can understand, communicating among Thai Union Group to emphasize compliance with the company’s policy.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
This call is from Zu Zu, a worker from TUF (Frying shrimp Line) reported that since April 2023, the business didn't allow workers to keep prescription medicine and water bottles in their lockers outside the production line. Workers that need to take medicine and drink purified room-temperature water for health reasons are finding this regulation difficult to follow. The business often does unannounced locker inspections, which they did on 16th June, 2023. If they find prohibited items such as sweets, tiger balm, lipstick, or water bottles in the locker, the worker will be suspended for 3 days. If they find betel nut, cigarettes, drugs, or knives, the worker will be dismissed. The worker had to skip taking medicine that she supposed to take every 4 hours. Some of her friends that need to drink warm water had to drink iced water from the tank. The worker would like more flexibility regarding prohibited items.

TPs:
- Why does the business prohibit some items from being kept in lockers by the workers?
- Why has this list been updated in April 2023 to include prohibition of medicine and water bottles?
- If workers cannot keep certain items in their lockers, is there somewhere else that they can keep important items such as medicine that they have to take during the day?
- What is the policy on disciplinary measures if certain items are found in a worker's locker?

Recommendations:
- The business should allow access to necessary items such as medicine and water bottles since workers need to take them for health reasons, whether it is in their lockers or an alternative place where such items can be stored safely and easily accessible by workers
remediation_notes: A worker reported that since April 2023, the business didn't allow workers to keep prescription medicine and water bottles in their lockers outside the production line. Workers that need to take medicine and drink purified warm water for health reasons are finding this regulation difficult to follow. The business will punish workers if any prohibited item is found during surprise locker inspections (3-day suspension or dismissal).
remediation_action:
The business responded that it was following various food safety standards, which include prohibition of the storage of water bottles and medicines in workers' lockers for reasons that it may contaminate the food being processed in the production line. 
This has already been communicated to workers but the business has made an additional announcement regarding this food safety policy.

remediation_business_steps_taken:
Root Cause:
- With the company being a food factory therefore must comply with various relevant criteria such as strictly since the beginning of production of products such as Methodology for safe food production (GMP), Food Safety Management System (HACCP), and customer requirements which are International standards for consumers to eat quality and safe food.
-During April 2023, the company reviewed the aforementioned standards and practices by having a training and public relations campaign for employees Including reviewing regulations on the use of lockers, which is considered One of the requirements, emphasizing the prohibited items entering the company. Items that cannot be brought are stored in the locker, including the storage of medicines and water bottles.
- Medicines: according to the regulations, establishing codes of practice on the carrying of drugs and prohibiting the storage of drugs
in the locker, where, if ill, the employee can ask for permission from the supervisor to come in for service at the infirmary which has 
professional nurses and basic medicine as required by law to provide services to employees, except for heart disease and asthma medicines, which are considered a group of medicines that are permitted for employees to carry. By employees bring medicine to be registered at the infirmary. Based on these requirements, the drug is considered a foreign thing that can be mixed with water and food products. which if slipping may contaminate the product which may be harmful to customers who eat contaminated food.
- Food and beverages: according to the regulations, there are guidelines for prohibiting employees from bringing
All kinds of food, beverages, glass bottles, candy, chewing gum, gloves, or equipment used in the production area, come to store in the locker to prevent animal carriers of germs such as cockroaches, flies, and rats from entering different areas and may cause contamination of the product
- Measures to randomly check lockers is one of the steps to control, prevent, deter, and bring items that are forbidden to be brought into the factory or stored in a locker including actions that may result in contamination with the products, which the company has communicated with employees and conducted random checks of lockers continuously. Employees would be aware of random checks but would not know the schedule and without prior notice on the day of random inspection, the company notified and invited the locker owners and supervisors to the locker area by asking the locker owner who opened, which the company checked in front of such employees.


Corrective/Prevention:
- On 25 July 2023, communicated further under Food Safety & Quality Culture to make employees aware of the production of safe food by the emphasis on medicine and bottle storage water, including random measures check-in such activities as well


K. Sukrid, HR, responded that HR made verbal and written announcements about the locker measurement to all employees. He will share with us the written communication that is posted on the locker room bulletin board.


DATE: 5 Oct 2023

K Prad emailed the corrective action table as per the link below.
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/18w_cHkTFDYU98DN9MkRiwKnAHvjHfj9g

- Communication by relevant departments and supervisors: During April 2023, the production department and product Refresh Training activities have been organized for employees in every department of the product production division and related to product production by inviting employees to a meeting in the conference room with the lecturer is the person responsible for GMP work including various quality systems at the company. The company holds and practices this training including discussion and opportunities for employees.
Q&A and review of locker use regulations, which is considered one of the requirements, emphasizing the items prohibited from entering the company, the things that cannot be kept in the locker including storing medicines and water bottles.

- A nursing room is provided in the common area of the company: TUF Rong Kung has provided a room. Nurses provide services to employees who need services, such as consulting about illnesses. Basic steps to receive medicine, treat disease, provide first aid, deposit medicine for personal illnesses, including a hot water service point, etc. The nursing room is open all the time, 24 hours a day on business days, with professional nurses on both shifts continuously. The nursing room is located on the 2nd floor of the building, which is the same building as the production building. It is the same area as the cafeteria which is an area for selling and storing food. For employees who have rice boxes from home to eat at the company, including drinking water points and a dining area for all employees.

- How to get to the nursing room: From the locker area, employees can use the stairs from the production area or stairs outside the building going up to the 2nd floor of the building is the cafeteria area and keep walking on the left, approximately 20 meters further, will be the location of the nursing room.
remediation_notes: Issara received a report that since April 2023, the business didn't allow workers to keep prescription medicine and water bottles in their lockers outside the production line but many workers need to take medicine and drink purified warm water several times daily for health reasons.
remediation_action:
The business responded that it was following various food safety standards, which include prohibition of the storage of water bottles and medicines in workers' lockers for reasons that it may contaminate the food being processed in the production line. 
This has already been communicated to workers but the business has made an additional announcement regarding this food safety policy. After the worker update saying he hadn't heard the announcement, HR made verbal and written announcements again about the locker measurement to all employees.

In the latest update, the business will check how the worker can take the medicine as needed and is able to access the clinic where the medicine is supposed to be kept, which is far from the production line. 

The business has set up a nursing room, which is close to the cafeteria and upstairs from the locker area. It is staffed by nurses for both shifts, accessible 24 hours a day. The workers can keep their medicine there, and a hot water service point is provided as well.
remediation_validation: Regarding the locker issues, a worker updated Issara saying that he saw the written announcement about items prohibited from being stored in the lockers but it is not very clear and also there was no the verbal announcement.
next_description: Confirm with workers they have received the announcements and know where the nursing room is

Context; Workers raised their concern about the business announcement regarding the status of the document extension process. Recommendations; 

-According to DoE, workers (with support from the employer) have to process the extension of their documents 1 month prior to the expiration date (Medical check up, Visa, Work permit). Therefore, the business is recommended to contact the local DOE and get advise on how to process the documents from workers whose visas and/or work permits are expiring soon.  

- In addition, the business is suggested to contact Bangkok Myanmar Embassy for the worker's passport extension. Embassy Contact number;  02 233 2237 (Thai and Burmese language).

-Once the business has clarify the right process for workers, it is recommended for the business to conduct clear announcements (verbal and written) with all workers in this situation about the documentation process as the government's requirement.


Talking points; 

-What is the business plan for this group of workers? 
-How many workers are there in this situation?

timeframe 2 pay periods
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The business; According to Seafresh's policy for retaining the workers, all migrant workers whose documents are expiring will be done the document extension and will be called one month in advance of the expiration date. The business updated having done the communication with all workers via written post. 

Workers confirmed the communications and expressed their satisfaction.
remediation_business_steps_remaining:
None.


Rating; Excellent. 
The business responded by not having a plan to stop workers' contracts. To help the workers, the business conducted the communication verbally and in a written post. Workers also confirmed being communicated and expressed their apprecistions.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue#1. 

Context: The issue with the work setting, workers reported having to do cleaning for 15 days after regular working hours if they were found to have even one shrimp not being cleaned properly. Workers reported that it used to be only 3-7 days in the past, however, the business recently increased it to 15 days which the workers feel the policy is not fair for them as they did not sign to work as a cleaner. Building 2.

Talking Points;
What is the business policy for this kind of issue?
What does the cleaning work entail?
If a worker is re-assigned to cleaning duties for 15 days after regular working hours, how does that affect production? 
What happens if there are many workers who have uncleaned shrimp on the same day?
Recommendations for system change.
The business to have an open discussion with the workers to agree on how this matter should be handled 
The business should revisit the policy and revise it as needed. 

Issue#2. 

Context:  The issue with the new announcement regarding sick leave request process. The workers said that the production manager announced on 22 March 2022 that if the workers are sick, they have to report their sick leave in person regardless of their condition. Building 2. 
Talking Points
Is HR aware of this announcement? 
What is the business policy for requesting sick leave? 
How has the policy been communicated to the workers?  

Recommendations for the system change. 
According to the law, employees do not need to present MC for taking sick leave for less than 3 consecutive days, therefore, the business is suggested to conduct an investigation about this announcement that was made by the manager and revise as needed.
The business should have a policy where workers can report their sick leave to their supervisors or HR via phone or message rather than having to make the request in person. 
The business to make an announcement to all workers and clarify the process for requesting sick leave.  The communication should be in writing and verbally announced.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business response
IDENTIFIED POSSIBLE ROOT CAUSES
1. Ineffective communication because the supervisor wants workers to work properly. therefore using inappropriate methods causing misunderstandings in communication
2. From the worker groups meeting, Building 2, divided into 2 subgroups:
 2.1 The group with good performance statistics, Neither history of absenteeism nor warning: the workers understands the supervisor's reasoning and think that workers who have the wrong behavior often should be punished
 2.2 The group with statistics of inactivity, absenteeism and frequent warnings: workers understand the reason but they was affected, causing a lack of income therefore do not agree with the punishment

CORRECTIVE ACTIONS / REMEDY CONFIRMED BY SEAFRESH
1. Re-training the supervisors to know about labor protection laws. forced labor and Good Labor Practices in three sessions of the GLP & Business Ethics course on 21,22 and 23 April 2022.
2. Review and verify the internal requirements of building 2 and removed the invalid requirements. Any terms used must be approved by the Human Resources Department with reference to work regulations only
3. Adjust your attitude of workers with a history of absenteeism and received frequent warnings to behave in accordance with the rules and regulations of the work and strictly production requirements

remediation_notes:
Case #1: Workers reported having to do cleaning for 15 days after regular working hours if they were found to have even one shrimp not being cleaned properly. Case #2: The workers said that the production manager announced on 22 March 2022 that if the workers are sick, they have to request their sick leave in person regardless of their condition.
remediation_action:
Case #1: The business investigated and found that supervisors wanted their workers to work more productively but used inappropriate methods.  The business re-trained its supervisors on business ethics, and reviewed and removed all invalid requirements, such as cleaning requirements used as punishment.

Case #2:  The business investigated and found that some workers were absent without notice and when they returned to work, they explained that they had informed the business about their sick leave via their relatives but the supervisor had not been informed. Therefore, the supervisor told these workers to inform about their sick leave in person to have their leave records corrected.  This may have led to the misunderstanding that workers need to request for sick leave in-person to be able to take sick leave.
The business held a meeting with the workers to explain the process for submitting the sick leave request to obtain full wages.  The business also clarified with workers that when workers return from sick leave, they are allowed the shift where they start later in the day and not have overtime work assigned so that workers have more time to recuperate and ease back to work.

Case #1

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1: A female worker (Thet Thet Htwe) injured her hand in a workplace accident back in 2019. In February 2022, she had to be hospitalized for a month, and took medical leave for three months from March-May 2022. For the month in the hospital, the supplier paid daily wages as sick leave days, but for the three additional months of medical leave, the supplier submitted an application for workmen's compensation with the social security office. She followed up several times with the HR office, and the HR staff kept saying that it was in the process. She will have to return to Myanmar in May 2023 because her four-year MoU contract is coming to an end. This morning, on April 21, she asked HR staff, and they said she will not receive the compensation from social security before she leaves to return to Myanmar. HR told her keep her Thai bank card with her friend and when the social security office pays the compensation, the supplier will transfer the money to her bank account, and then her friend can transfer her the money. She would like to get the compensation before she goes back to Myanmar.

TPs:
- Why has there been such a delay in getting the compensation for her medical leave from the workmen's compensation fund if this took place almost a year ago?

Recommendations:
- The business to follow up with the social security office and expedite the request to process this payment from social security, which is already grossly overdue
= Ensure that the worker receives this compensation prior to returning to Myanmar
- Communicate clearly to the worker the status update in terms of processing the compensation payment and when the worker can expect to receive it

Case #2 (April 21, 2023): A worker reported that the business had a communication session with the workers on April 20th and informed the workers whose 4-year or 6-year MoU contracts are ending will need to return to Myanmar on May 3rd. For those renewing their contracts (MoU U-Turn), each worker has to pay 5,960 THB for the recruitment fees to the HR office by May 24th and 300,000 Kyats to the Golden Sea Myanmar RA. In 2022, the business already collected 6,500 THB for passport renewals and at that time had promised them that their visa and work permit would be extended in Thailand. The workers feel unhappy because the business has changed what they had announced earlier, and most do not want to go back to Myanmar given the current political situation. Some do not have the money for the MoU U-turn process. Some would like to continue working until their current visa ends. For others, they would like to know how many months they have to wait in Myanmar for the U-turn process.

TPs:
- Seafresh has a policy where the business will pay for the recruitment costs, except for the passport fees and any travel related costs to the point of departure (Yangon).  Workers reported they have been asked to pay 5,960 Baht to HR and another 300,000 Kyats to the Myanmar RA.  What is this for?

Recommendations:
- Clarify with workers what the fees are, for which workers have been asked to pay
- Clarify the timeframe for the U-turn process, so that workers know when they can expect to get back to Seafresh to resume work
- Clarify with the workers about the safety of the U-turn process and that Seafresh and the Myanmar RA can ensure that the workers will be able to return with renewed MOU contracts.

In July 2023, the worker will receive an 18,000 baht reimbursement from SSO for 96 days of work. The worker agreed to extend the MoU U-turn process and will receive the reimbursement when she returns to Thailand in July. 

Case #2: Seafresh responded that they consulted the Department of Employment (DOE) and determined that workers would need to return to Myanmar for the MOU U-turn process. Workers will pay 5,940 Baht, and Seafresh will arrange transportation for the workers. If the workers do not want to extend this MoU process, the workers can work until the work permit ends. Currently, 40 of 133 workers agreed to do the U-turn process. In Myanmar, the timeline for U-Turn is three months. Seafresh had a communication session with the cost breakdown of 5,940 Baht to all workers on April 20, 2023. However, Seafresh will have another session to make a clear explanation to those whose visa will end in June. Issara escalated this to the Seafresh MD because according to its responsible recruitment policy and agreement with the recruitment agencies dated May 31, 2022, Seafresh would be covering these recruitment fees for workers.  The MD noted that there was a new policy dated December 5, 2022, which notes that "Seafresh is implementing a stepped plan for eliminating recruitment fees by January 2024" and this replaces the May 31, 2022 policy.  He said this "stepped plan" means that in 2023 Seafresh is putting a hold on covering all recruitment fees for workers and will move to full implementation of covering all fees starting in January 2024. However, Issara is of the position that the December 5, 2022 policy shouldn't cancel out the May 31, 2022 policy but rather build on it because it states a "stepped" plan. In practice, the May 31, 2022 agreement states almost full coverage of recruitment fees (except for the passport and the travel costs from home village to Yangon) and the Dec 5, 2022 policy says it is implementing a stepped plan to eliminate all fees but in practice they are going backwards and are making workers pay for the U-turn process costs 2023.  In the latest update, the MD noted that 31 workers went for the U-turn process in May 2023 and another 60 will do the U-turn in August 2023.

She went back to Myanmar on 3rd May and Issara provided our Yangon office contact number so she can stay connected and ask any questions she may have.

Case #2: 31 workers have returned and arrived safely in Myanmar for the U-turn process.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers sick leave and the medical certificate during their home quarantine. Workers reported an increasing number of COVID positive cases in the factory. The factory does the ATK test and asks the workers to take 10 days of home quarantine if they have tested positive and have no severe symptoms. However, it is not clear what will happen with their wages since they do not have the MC from the doctor as they are taking home quarantine. The factory interpreter said not to worry about the MC, however it was not clear if they will get fully paid without having MC. Workers wanted to hear from the business about how their Covid-related quarantine days will be handled. All workers in the factory have received booster doses of the COVID-19 vaccine. 

Recommendations: 
-The business should clearly communicate with the workers about how their Covid-related quarantine days will be processed and whether they will be considered sick leave days, with or without a medical certificate, and the workers paid accordingly for those days.
- If the business’ policy requires workers to present a medical certificate for taking sick leave for more than 3 days, the business should facilitate COVID-Positive workers to visit the hospital to get an MC, even if they are self-isolating at home. However, if the business does not require MC and an ATK test is sufficient, this should be clearly communicated to the workers. 

Talking Points; 
-How many workers have tested positive and are in-home quarantine at the moment? 
-What is the business policy for the workers’ wages when they do not have MC from the hospital for the quarantine period?  Will the Covid-related quarantine period without a medical certificate be considered sick leave? 

Time Frame ; within 1 week.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara has reached out to the business to discuss this issue, the business said that they will pay 100% of workers wages for the days that they take quarantine. The business agreed to conduct another announcement with the workers.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Leaves are being improperly recorded for not being provided the leaves request form. In addition to that, the announced sick leave policy is not clear to the workers. 

Issara recommendations. 

-The business to conduct communication with all workers regarding the process of taking any kind of leaves and also the way that they will be recorded. 

-The business to inform all workers that if they have been impacted by this issue they can approach HR for the business to investigate and make the correction. 

-The business to make sure that the worker's leaves are being recorded properly by the in-charge focal at C&B.

-Please share workers' concerns and feedback on the sick leave announcements. Share Issara's feedback to the business if the business is willing to take it. 

Time Frame - One pay period


**Talking Points**
(14-Sep). Please share the worker's update detail.

-Share with the business that Issara has received reports from workers stating that the sick leave policy is not clear to them, thus we would like to provide some recommendations on how to clarify some points of the policy.  

Please ask the following questions to the business:

-What is the leave request form look like? Why are the workers saying that there is only one form and if that form is not available, they have to make verbal requests. 

-What have they communicated to workers in the past and how are the workers supposed to request personal and business leave?

-How does the business make sure that the sick leave is being translated and communicated correctly?

# Issue 2.

The issue with the workers' annual leave being deducted by the business.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The line supervisors have the sick leave form. Actually, the leave form should keep at the production lines. The workers can ask the supervisor not HR for the leave form. Then the supervisor submitted the form. HR makes a record of it then gives it back to the line supervisor.  

HR knows that some supervisors might not understand. So The HR will work with the line supervisor to communicate this sick leave policy again.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business to clarify the leave request process and review it if needed making improvements in the system so that workers are able to make requests for leave in an efficient manner. 
-The business shall revise the sick leave announcement which was recently announced considering the feedback provided by Issara and workers unclarity of the announcement. 


Time frame - One pay period.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; There are some workers whose passports and visas are expiring end of March and April. Some of them have given 50 baht and a copy of their passport to HR for document extension a few months ago. There's been no update about the extension yet. They are worried if they cannot do the extension anymore and will be out of a job. The workers want to hear from MRG on the extension status. Some workers heard that the business will not extend the contract for those who have tested positive for COVID-19. 

Issara recommendations. 

-Have clear communication with workers about their document process, status, and timeframes. 

- It is recommended that the company inform workers at least 2-3 months in advance before the contract ends if the company is planning to renew the contract or not. -What is the status of these workers? How many workers are in this group?
-Who from HR is managing this process so that workers can contact him/her directly in case they have more questions?

 -N/A

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers from the PR line and DH line being asked to work till 9 PM interferes with the provincial curfew when workers travel back to their residence. 

Talking Points: 
-Workers from the PR and DH line reported being asked to work till 9 PM since last Monday, is business aware of this situation that interferes with the provincial curfew? 
-How would the business protect the workers from being arrested by the local police for being out during the curfew time? 

Recommendations:
-HR shall coordinate with production and all line supervisors to make sure all operations stop in a time that would allow workers to have enough time to return home and be able to buy what they need for the night and the next days such as food and other basic items before the curfew starts.  
-The measures and regulations shall be communicated to all line supervisors and workers.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A worker was dismissed after receiving two warning, however, the worker understanding was that he/she could only be dismissed after receiving 3 warnings.

It is recommended for the business to remind all workers about the GMP policy and other company policies that leads to disciplinary actions such as warning and ultimately termination.

-Please check with the business about their perspective on dismissal during the COVID-19 outbreak and given the worsened situation in Myanmar what are their considerations for workers that can't return home (This is a point the business should consider in case they have clear evidence of the company had followed their policy and the worker having 3 warnings). description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with lack of communication about the COVID-19 test and the workers who were found positive. They said that they wanted to be clearly communicated about the business procedure and the management of the situation does not improve.  Workers raised their questions and concerns about whether they will be paid for their quarantine days, who will pay for the medical treatment costs, and so on. 


Recommendations; 
-The business shall provide clear guidance about the assistance for workers that test positive for COVID-19. The guidance shall be provided in writing accompanied by verbal announcements in all workers languages and it should cover the following information: 
-are there different measures/procedures depending on the severity of the symptoms 
-who will cover the treatment costs (SSF, employer?) 
-quarantine centers and services
-the process that the infected and not infected workers will have to follow (self-quarantine, etc.)
-the payment of the wages for the days of quarantine whenever needed

Talking points
-How many workers have been tested and found positive so far? How has the business managed infected workers? 
-Which hospital or quarantine centers are the workers being sent to?
-Workers raised that some of the workers have been tested positive and only a few of the closed workers are being asked for 14 days of quarantine. How has the business managed the workers who share the dormitory and production lines?  
-How have the workers been communicated about the COVID-19 treatment fees?

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1: [Issue from in-person outreach]
Workers reported that there is no clear protocol and procedure for the workers to follow when they need medical assistance.  There is an on-site nurse in the factory clinic but she doesn't accept calls outside of working hours. The business provides a car to transport workers to the hospital when needed but the workers cannot reach the driver most of the time and instead have hire their own transport and go to the hospital with the help of the factory interpreter. The workers also noted that the health services at the factory clinic is not good, with the doctor rarely providing medicine or recommending workers be sent to the hospital when needed.  

Recommendations for remediation:
- Communicate, verbally and in writing, the process for requesting medical services and related services (interpretation and transportation to the hospital) at the factory clinic and at the public hospital, both during daytime and nighttime hours
- Conduct a survey with workers regarding the quality of the services provided by the in-house nurse and doctor working in the factory clinic and consider worker suggestions for improvement

Case #2: (Opened Nov 14, 2022)
In November 2023, the company announced that for workers whose work permits were due to expire on Feb 21st, 2023, their contracts wouldn't be extended. In December 2023, the business HR met with 29 workers to offer 10,620 Baht for the separation and asked them to sign receipt of the money.  Of the 29 workers, 11 workers refused to accept the offer because they suspected this was a resignation letter. They were dismissed and stopped working on December 13th, 2023. They decided to call the Labor Attache for support to get severance pay because their employment was terminated, and later managed to get assisted from a local NGO to file a complaint with the Department of Labor Protection and Welfare (DLPW).  They also wanted to get cancellation letters so that they could find new employers.  The workers moved out of SFP housing on Jan 7, 2023 and are looking for new jobs. 

Recommendations for remediation:
- Communicate, verbally and in writing, about the process of passport renewal and work permit extension.  Clarify what costs will be borne by the worker and what will be covered by the company.  For workers whose contracts will not be extended, be clear about the terms for separation and whether there will be any severance pay provided to workers.

Case #3:
A worker reported that hundreds of their colleagues paid 6,500 Baht to the SFP interpreter "Than Ko Lin" for passport extension fees. The workers claimed that they were afraid that SFP would not renew their passports in time for the visa and WP extension process, as the company did not provide clear instructions on the matter. As a result, they ended up using Than Ko Lin's services for passport extensions.
(Note: This is secondary information.)

Case #4 (opened April 19, 2023):
A worker reported that approximately 40 workers, who have completed their 4-year MOU contracts, are being asked to return to Myanmar for the MOU U-turn process. The workers have three specific questions for clarification:
1. The workers need information on when they are required to return to Myanmar and how SFP will arrange transportation for them.
2. The workers seek details on how the U-Turn MOU process will be arranged by SFP, including the timeline, cost, and name of the recruitment agency involved.
3. The workers noted that they were asked to stop working on April 12th, 2023, despite the expiry date of their employment contracts being April 20th. Their work permits are valid till May 1st. They want to know why they had to stop working before their contract expiration and if they are entitled to receive compensation of 75% of their wages.
Despite having communicated with SFP multiple times, the workers have not received a clear response.

Business Response: 10 June 2022
K. Sophon responded about the medicine. According to the first-aid room in the house, there is a list of medicine that nurses can give to the workers. The medical room service is open until 8-9 pm and in an emergency case, the workers can contact Line or phone the nurse. He will check and communicate with the workers for medical service.


workers don’t know what medical services are available in the factory clinic and how to get it

When the workers go to the medical room, the doctor will check the worker’s health and in some cases should go to the hospital, the company will provide interpreters and transportation. 2. The workers seek details on how the U-Turn MOU process will be arranged by SFP, including the timeline, cost, and name of the recruitment agency involved.
3. The workers noted that they were asked to stop working on April 12th, 2023, despite the expiry date of their employment contracts being April 20th. Their work permits are valid till May 1st. They want to know why they had to stop working before their contract expiration and if they are entitled to receive compensation of 75% of their wages.
Despite having communicated with SFP multiple times, the workers have not received a clear response.
remediation_action:
Case #1: The business responded that in the factory clinic, the nurse is only allowed to administer a set list of medicines.  The clinic is open for both the day and night shifts with the nurse present.  The doctor is in during the daytime from Monday to Friday. When the workers go to the clinic, the doctor will check the worker’s health and in some cases if they need to go to the hospital, the company will provide interpreters and transportation. Currently, there’s an interpreter always available in the medical room. The business has noted what its policy is but hasn't addressed the issues raised by the workers. Issara is planning to visit and meet with the business HR in-person but the business has yet to agree to a visit.

Case #2: Issara made numerous phone calls to the business. Finally, we were able to contact the business.  HR had notified the Department of Employment (DOE) of the workers that were let go in the second week of January 2023. They will receive the cancellation letter as soon as DOE issues it. The workers can follow up with HR directly. HR noted that the business wanted to continue employing workers but the workers must return to Myanmar to renew their passports and complete the MoU U-Turn process. The business said 15 of the 20 workers agreed and received financial assistance in the amount of 10,000 Baht to assist with the MOU U-turn process in Myanmar. This does not match the worker reports.

After pressure from the Strategic Partners, Issara was able to meet with SFP HR at the Bangkok Headquarters.  HR explained that migrant workers were hired as MOU workers or walk-in workers with different contract end dates.  For one group of 258 workers, SFP checked to see whether their contracts could be extended as per Thai government regulations and also whether their performance was satisfactory.  For 30 workers from this group, SFP decided not to extend their contracts and they have been provided with cancellation letters.  

For a second group of 28 workers, SFP wanted to retain them but the government regulation didn't allow for their work permit and visa extension.  Of this group of 29 workers, 10 workers agreed to do the U-turn process, and SFP provided a 10,000 Baht allowance and arranged and paid for their transportation back to Myanmar.  14 workers took the 10,000 Baht “allowance” and decided to stay in Thailand to try and find a new job here. 4 workers went to the Labor office to file a complaint and SFP noted that the Labor office had issued the decision in Feb 2023 that SFP didn't have to pay severance to the workers.  These 4 received the allowance and received the cancellation letters. SFP acknowledged that there was a lack of timely communication with migrant workers and this led to workers not understanding what was happening.

Case #3: HR was aware that some workers had decided to get their passports extended on their own, even traveling up to Chiang Mai to the Myanmar consulate there and incurring greater expenses.  SFP is following the Employer Pays Policy and is facilitating and paying for the workers' passport extensions, either processing this themselves or paying a Thai recruitment agency to do it. Again, SFP acknowledged that there was a lack of clear communication on this to workers, which led to workers taking measures into their own hands to get their passports extended. In April 2023, the business said it will consider paying 1,000 Baht for the legal passport renewal fee and the transportation cost and may return that amount to the 180 workers that paid 6,500 Baht for passport renewal in Jan 2023. The business has since confirmed payment of 1,000 baht to the workers.

Case #4: The business said that it will use Golden Gate (Thai RA) and Arborfield (Myanmar RA) to facilitate the MoU U-turn process for workers. They shared that in the latest group that went back to Myanmar, the workers chose by themselves to go by airplane and the workers paid 1,000 Baht and SFP paid 3,000 Baht for the airfare. However, the company would like the workers in the next batch to go by land and the company will pay for all costs.

Case #1:

Case #2: The worker that reported this issue updated Issara saying that of the 29 workers, it seems that now there are only 5 workers that are still working with the local NGO to pursue severance pay (with official complaint submitted to the Department of Labor Protection and Welfare), 7 workers may be doing the MOU U-turn process with SFP, and the rest are looking for other jobs.  Of the 5 workers, 4 have found a new employer and don't need cancellation letters because the new employer will register them as pink card workers while 1 worker is still requesting the cancellation letter from SFP.

In a further update, the worker that wanted to get the cancellation letter from the business still hasn't been able to secure employment that would extend her visa and work permit. She mentioned that she has not received a cancellation letter, and she no longer wants it since it is useless for undocumented workers like her. Currently, she is staying with her sister (who is still working at SFP) in private housing outside the factory compound. She expressed her disappointment with SFP for not extending their documents earlier, which would have prevented them from becoming undocumented workers. She is now hoping for another round of amnesty period where she can apply for a pink card with a new employer and be legalized to stay and work in Thailand again. Of the 4 that had found employment, three are still working with the new employer as undocumented workers, and waiting for the amnesty period to apply for a pink card. Two other workers who were part of this group have been reinstated at SFP following intervention from a representative from an importer. There are now only four workers that are still proceeding with the complaint to DLPW with support from a local NGO.

March 15, 2023 update: Three workers had found work at the aluminum factory resigned as they could bear the hard working conditions. These three workers and the worker who called Issara are undocumented and without employment. These four workers filed the case with the Department of Labor Protection and Welfare against SFP with the help of a Thai legal aid NGO and they will be appearing in court on March 17th.

Subsequently, the labor case was brought by the workers, and the out-of-court settlement was for the business to pay severance to the workers, in the amount of 20,000 Baht for each of the 4 workers.

Case #3: A worker provided an update to Issara saying they had not received 1,000 Baht for the passport renewal that the business had promised to the 180 workers.

- HR and line supervisors to be trained on the company's responsible recruitment policy and how to communicate the policy clearly and accurately to the migrant workers

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1: [Issue from in-person outreach]
Workers reported that there is no clear protocol and procedure for the workers to follow when they need medical assistance.  There is an on-site nurse in the factory clinic but she doesn't accept calls outside of working hours. The business provides a car to transport workers to the hospital when needed but the workers cannot reach the driver most of the time and instead have hire their own transport and go to the hospital with the help of the factory interpreter. The workers also noted that the health services at the factory clinic is not good, with the doctor rarely providing medicine or recommending workers be sent to the hospital when needed.  

Recommendations for remediation:
- Communicate, verbally and in writing, the process for requesting medical services and related services (interpretation and transportation to the hospital) at the factory clinic and at the public hospital, both during daytime and nighttime hours
- Conduct a survey with workers regarding the quality of the services provided by the in-house nurse and doctor working in the factory clinic and consider worker suggestions for improvement

Case #2: (Opened Nov 14, 2022)
In November 2023, the company announced that for workers whose work permits were due to expire on Feb 21st, 2023, their contracts wouldn't be extended. In December 2023, the business HR met with 29 workers to offer 10,620 Baht for the separation and asked them to sign receipt of the money.  Of the 29 workers, 11 workers refused to accept the offer because they suspected this was a resignation letter. They were dismissed and stopped working on December 13th, 2023. They decided to call the Labor Attache for support to get severance pay because their employment was terminated, and later managed to get assisted from a local NGO to file a complaint with the Department of Labor Protection and Welfare (DLPW).  They also wanted to get cancellation letters so that they could find new employers.  The workers moved out of SFP housing on Jan 7, 2023 and are looking for new jobs. 

Recommendations for remediation:
- Communicate, verbally and in writing, about the process of passport renewal and work permit extension.  Clarify what costs will be borne by the worker and what will be covered by the company.  For workers whose contracts will not be extended, be clear about the terms for separation and whether there will be any severance pay provided to workers.

The worker can contact the supervisor, the interpreter, or the number listed on the announcement board. They will verbally communicate with the workers again during the workers' communication session, which will take place on October 16-17, 2023.

Case #2: Issara made numerous phone calls to the business. Finally, we were able to contact the business.  HR had notified the Department of Employment (DOE) of the workers that were let go in the second week of January 2023. They will receive the cancellation letter as soon as DOE issues it. The workers can follow up with HR directly. HR noted that the business wanted to continue employing workers but the workers must return to Myanmar to renew their passports and complete the MoU U-Turn process. The business said 15 of the 20 workers agreed and received financial assistance in the amount of 10,000 Baht to assist with the MOU U-turn process in Myanmar. This does not match the worker reports.

After pressure from the Strategic Partners, Issara was able to meet with SFP HR at the Bangkok Headquarters.  HR explained that migrant workers were hired as MOU workers or walk-in workers with different contract end dates.  For one group of 258 workers, SFP checked to see whether their contracts could be extended as per Thai government regulations and also whether their performance was satisfactory.  For 30 workers from this group, SFP decided not to extend their contracts and they have been provided with cancellation letters.  

For a second group of 28 workers, SFP wanted to retain them but the government regulation didn't allow for their work permit and visa extension.  Of this group of 29 workers, 10 workers agreed to do the U-turn process, and SFP provided a 10,000 Baht allowance and arranged and paid for their transportation back to Myanmar.  14 workers took the 10,000 Baht “allowance” and decided to stay in Thailand to try and find a new job here. 4 workers went to the Labor office to file a complaint and SFP noted that the Labor office had issued the decision in Feb 2023 that SFP didn't have to pay severance to the workers.  These 4 received the allowance and received the cancellation letters. SFP acknowledged that there was a lack of timely communication with migrant workers and this led to workers not understanding what was happening.

Case #3: HR was aware that some workers had decided to get their passports extended on their own, even traveling up to Chiang Mai to the Myanmar consulate there and incurring greater expenses.  SFP is following the Employer Pays Policy and is facilitating and paying for the workers' passport extensions, either processing this themselves or paying a Thai recruitment agency to do it. Again, SFP acknowledged that there was a lack of clear communication on this to workers, which led to workers taking measures into their own hands to get their passports extended. In April 2023, the business said it will consider paying 1,000 Baht for the legal passport renewal fee and the transportation cost and may return that amount to the 180 workers that paid 6,500 Baht for passport renewal in Jan 2023. The business has since confirmed payment of 1,000 baht to the workers.

Case #4: The business said that it will use Golden Gate (Thai RA) and Arborfield (Myanmar RA) to facilitate the MoU U-turn process for workers. They shared that in the latest group that went back to Myanmar, the workers chose by themselves to go by airplane and the workers paid 1,000 Baht and SFP paid 3,000 Baht for the airfare. However, the company would like the workers in the next batch to go by land and the company will pay for all costs.

Case #5: The business stated that for workers whose MOU contracts are ending, they will not be renewing them due to low production and needing to manage the appropriate workforce level. This group would be repatriated on October 6, 2023. The company made this announcement to this group in advance for a month.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue # 1. 
Context; Asking the workers to sign the documents  On Saturday, the business holds an HR meeting where all the workers have to attend that meeting and they can raise their issues happening in the working line. All the workers attended that meeting except workers in the Cut Site line. But, on Monday, workers in the Cut site line are asked to sign three papers by the line clerk and she said that it was to acknowledge that they have attended that training too.

Talking Points; 

-What is the meeting about? Why did the business exclude this group of workers?
-Is the business aware of the issue that the workers from this group are facing now?
 
Recommendations; 
-Based on the response from the business on the question above, assess if this group of workers should receive the same training o communication session. 
-Explain to the business that workers should not be requested to sign any documents that they do not understand what they are about, so the business shall investigate why this group of workers is being asked to sign the document even though they did not attend the meeting.  

Time Frame; 1 week.

Issue # 2. 
The issue with lack of drinking water glass. The business has stopped providing disposable glasses as in the past. The workers are not allowed to bring their own bottles from their house so that they have to buy water bottle in the factory canteen to replace the water glass, however, the cleaning staff throws their bottles which makes workers buy the bottles often and also create more inconvenient in the production line. 

Recommendations; 

-The business to clarify to the workers including cleaning staff the reasons why the business has stopped providing glasses and what is the alternative solution for it. 
-Workers should be allowed to bring their water bottle/glasses from their home if the business decided not to provide the glasses/bottles. 
-It is encouraged for the business to provide workers options for them not to have to buy plastic bottles every day, it could be by allowing workers to bring their own reusable bottles or the business providing re-usable cups to avoid creating a big waste of plastic and making workers buy new bottles every day. 
-If the business is concern about hygiene with the re-usable cups, the business can assign a cleaning station where workers can wash their cups, and/or assign a person to help with the cleaning. 


Talking points; 
-Why has the business stopped providing glasses? 
-Is HR Aware of this issue? If so, how are they responding to it?

timeframe 1 pay period

Issue # 3. 

Context: A worker who broke his hand from a workplace accident on “May 31st” reported not being assisted by the factory translator which made him hire a private translator and paid on his own. He added that he also had to pay for the transportation fees to commute to the hospital but the business did not mention anything about the reimbursement. Worker ID -  MA 1594. He reported paying 1000 THB for the translator and more for the transportation fees. This issue is also being dealt with under KPI _ 655.

Recommendations. 
-The business shall investigate why this worker was not assisted by the factory translator. 
-Workers in this serious situation should be assisted by the factory translator to make sure that the workers receive proper medical treatment and that all steps are clear for the workers and the factory regarding the treatment.  
-Worker, in this case, should be reimbursed 1000 THB for the translator service and additional fees for the transportation as per the worker’s report. 

Talking points;
-What was the reason that this worker was not provided with the translator?
-Are there any transportation services provided by the company for workers to go to the hospital when needed?

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: the issue with the COVID-19 infection. Workers reported the spread of the virus and increasing infected workers in the factory, however, they are still being asked to continue working. Workers raised their concerns about getting infected and requested clear communication about the business plan to control the infection rate and also to test 100% of the workers in the factory. In addition to that, the workers reported being threatened of not receiving their wages and of not having access to basic needs supplies such as water and food, and losing their job if they do not come to work before completing their quarantine. Workers added that they were suggested to stay 14 days of quarantine by the doctor but the business asked them to work after a few days (5 -8 days) of quarantine. 

Added Context: Workers updated that around 20 workers who have been tested positive and staying quarantined in the business quarantine center continued not receiving meals and water on (1 Sep 2021). In addition to that, the workers also have reported being forced to work OT in order to receive dinner.


Recommendations: 
-The business to clearly communicate with the workers about the business plan to control the spread of the virus to a bigger number of workers in the factory and in the community.
-The business should also clearly communicate with the workers i) why they are being pushed to get back to work before completing the 14 days of quarantine, which is against the doctors’ recommendation, ii) what are the measures being taken by the business to make sure that those that have been exposed and in closed contact with positive cases do not spread the virus at the workplace if they are being asked to work before being able to confirm if they are positive or not. 
-The business should assign focal and introduce the vocals with the workers for the workers to reach out to them whenever they have questions and concerns related to COVID-19. 

Talking points:
-Is the business aware that the workers are being asked to get back to work before completing their 14 days of quarantine suggested by the doctor?  
-Workers reported being threatened of not receiving regular meals, not receiving wages for quarantine days, and even getting fired from work if they do not follow the business suggesting to get back to work before completion of 14 days of quarantine. What is the business understanding of this? 
-What has been the business action to control the number of impacted workers? 
-How many workers have been tested for COVID-19 so far and what is the testing process? 
-Are the COVID-19 regulation measures applied equally for Burmese and Thai workers, if not how so? According to the workers' report, there are different regulations for Thai, for instance, they have fewer restrictions of movement. This creates a feeling of insecurity among Burmese workers to work along with Thai workers who could have greater exposure to the virus. So what is the company policy, what is the plan to deal with these issues, and are the regulations applied equally for all workers?  



Please share the latest government announcement regarding Bubble and Seal measures. 

If the factory found a positive case for Covid,
They should notify the authority within 3 hours.
The public health authority will conduct a random test for 10% of their workforce (in the working station where the covid patient found and related working station).
The factory should do a deep cleaning and disinfecting the area
 If there are more than 5% positive cases found from the random test (10% of the workforce), or there is any risk of spreading to the neighboring community. The factory should implement the Bubble and Seals" measures.
For the Bubble and Seals, the factory shall do as follows:
preparing accommodation for workers in the factory, the workers who wish to continue working shall stay in the compound. They could not commute between their dormitory and factory. In the case where the factory provides accommodation to workers outside the factory compound, they shall provide the transport between accommodation and factory (sealed route).
set up organization quarantine/factory quarantine
set up field hospital or community isolation for the workers in the factory
The factory shall provide provisions (Food, essential goods, medicine, and medical equipment) and facilities to workers who stay in the bubble and seals.
6.	Failure to comply, may result in temporary shutdown and may be subject to a Maximum THB 100,000 fine or 1-year imprisonment, or both.
This order is effective since 4 Aug 2021

Source: 
https://covid.songkhla.go.th/files/com_announce/2021-08_62565c030491197.pdf

Additional guidelines for COVID prevention and response can be found in the “Guidance for Thai Companies: Care of Workers Affected by
COVID-19” some of the recommendations includes the following:
Keep workers informed
Ensure the correct timing for testing 
Ensure no discrimination
Ensure workers are properly paid during the quarantine period 
Ensure decent quarantine conditions 
Provide mental health support

Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that it was the misunderstanding and the miscommunication, however, the business committed to making sure that all workers receive proper meals.

Workers have requested the business to add some shop inside the housing for workers to access their basics needs which has been rejected by the business.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with a worker who was asked to take quarantine by the business as she was exposed to high-risk colleagues and her COVID-19 positive son not receiving daily wages for her quarantine days. The worker said that she had to take quarantine for more than a month, the business used most of her sick leave and paid for those quarantine days, however, there are still remaining days that the worker did not receive the daily wages as she runs out of her sick leave. The worker expects to receive her daily wages since the business asked her to stay quarintine. 

Recommendation:

-The business shall check the payment system to identify the issue with the missing payment and remediate workers according to what they are supposed to be paid. 
-All workers should receive the right payment within the next pay period 
-The business shall communicate with the workers to approach the HR focal person if they have any issue with their wages so that the HR can verify the right amount workers should receive. The focal person should be clear on how to communicate with the workers when workers approach the office. 
-Workers who were quarantined or placed in Bubble and Seal housing and not working should have a clear leave policy that is paid properly. 

Talking Points:
-What is the business understanding on this issue with the payment? 
-Have there been any changes with the payroll recently? 
-Have there been any communication with the workers on this issue?
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara raised this issue with the business, the business initially responded that they have already communicated with all workers about their missing payment and all workers clear understanding on this matter. However the worker in the other hand reported not being communicated and not having understanding of her missing payment. The worker gave the consent to share her information with the business, the business conducted the investigation, however the worker ended up not receiving her remaining wages. Since it has passed several months since her wages have been unpaid, the worker reported not to pursue the issue anymore. This is the only worker who did not receive her wages for 11 days for taking quarantine because her son was found COVID-19 positive. Other workers whose sick leaves also have been run out received 50% of wage from the employer and remaining 50% from the Social Security Fund office.
remediation_notes: A worker was asked to quarantine twice by the business for coming in close contact with other Covid-infected workers and because her son got COVID-19.  She had to quarantine for over a month, and she did not receive her daily wages for those days that exceeded the 30 sick leave days.
remediation_action: Issara raised this issue with the business, and the business initially responded that they had already communicated with all workers about their missing payment. However, the worker had not received this communication.  The worker gave consent to share her name and worker ID with the business, and the business conducted the investigation.  In the end, the business did not reimburse her for the missing wages.  This is the only worker who did not receive her wages for 11 days for taking quarantine because her son was found to be COVID-19 positive and she had exceeded 30 days of sick leave.  It should be noted that other workers who also exceeded the 30-day sick leave quota had been reimbursed fully, receiving 50% of wage from the employer and remaining 50% from the Social Security Fund office.
remediation_validation: Since it has been several months since her missing wages were unpaid, the worker said she did not want to pursue the issue anymore.
remediation_results: The business has not reimbursed missing wages for quarantine days that exceeded 30 days of sick leave for this worker.  The worker does not want to pursue this issue any longer since there hasn't been any business response for several months.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 15 Dec 2023

According to K. Sirilak, HR director, the MoU U-Turn process typically takes 2-3 months for workers to return and stay in Myanmar. TUS uses two Myanmar recruitment agencies, International Focus and Alpha World Link. This group must investigate how the process works and which recruitment agency should be responsible for carrying it out. They inquired if Issara had any additional information for this group to investigate. We informed them that this group first arrived in Thailand with an international focus in January 2018. So they will look into this group and get back to us within 7 business days.

26 Dec 2023:
TUS got back to us today re TUS issues with corrective actions. They investigated and it was found that there are a total of 40 MoU workers who came to work with TUS in January 2018 with an employment period of 6 years. These workers have a valid visa to stay in the country until 8 January 2024 and are not included in the 4-year MoU workers who are allowed to temporarily stay in the country until 30 April 2024 according to the 3 October 2023 Cabinet Resolution. 

The company has called this group of workers for a meeting twice in December to explain the details of the MoU U Turn. The first meeting was on 4 December 2023 and the second meeting on 22 December 2023 to inform additional details about the MoU U Turn trip. In both meetings, the company had clarified the travel details, steps for document extensions, agency used, and processing time. They also gave a chance to the workers to ask questions, for example, can they bring their children back with them, accommodation in the Myanmar side in case they don’t want to return home, pick-up and drop-off point at the border, etc. The HR officers answered all the questions that the workers have or are concerned about. The workers also signed and gave their consent for voluntary MoU U Turn. 

With regard to the time frame, even though the company has completed the passports for all the workers, it still takes time both in Thailand and in Myanmar side approximately 2 months until the workers can come back to work at the factory. The company has explained all the details to the workers during the meetings.
next_description: get the business corrective action.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The issue with the urine test process not being clearly communicated with the workers. Workers said that they are tested positive even they did not have to consume any drugs. In that case, the business will call them for the investigation. 

Please refer to the system change for the recommendations. 

Talking points; 

-What is the purpose of this test? 
-How often does the business conduct the test? And is the test voluntary or part of the company policy? if it is part of the company policy when are workers being informed about it?
-How does the business communicate to the workers about the process and result? 
-Workers reported being tested positive even though they did not use any drug, what it the business understanding about this and how does the business explain to the workers about such incident?

timeframe 1 pay period
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara raised this issue with the business, the business gave a detailed explanation to Issara about the purpose of the drug test. The business also agreed to conduct the communication and take action as follows to improve the system and solve the issue. As an action, the business added one more staff in the annual training to explain the purpose of the drug tests to the workers. And communicated to the workers via the sound system, through worker representative in a welfare committee meeting, and another communication in the special remediation meeting sessions. Workers confirmed every step that is taken by the business and all of the clear communications that taken place.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with lack of communication about the COVID-19 test and the workers who were found positive. Workers raised their questions and concerns about whether they will be paid for their quarantine days, who will pay for the medical treatment costs, and so on. 

Recommendations; 
-The business shall provide clear guidance about the assistance for workers that test positive for COVID-19. The guidance shall be provided in writing accompanied by verbal announcements in all workers languages and it should cover the following information: 
-are there different measures/procedures depending on the severity of the symptoms 
-who will cover the treatment costs (SSF, employer?) 
-quarantine centers and services
-the process that the infected and not infected workers will have to follow (self-quarantine, etc.)
-the payment of the wages for the days of quarantine whenever needed

Talking points
-How many workers have been tested and found positive so far? How has the business managed infected workers? 
-Which hospital or quarantine centers are the workers being sent to?
-Workers raised that some of the worker's have been tested positive and only a few of the closed stationed workers are being asked for 14 days of quarantine while other workers in the same line are still being asked to come to work. How has the business managed the workers who share the dormitory and production lines?  
-How have the workers been communicated about the COVID-19 treatment fees?

timeframe 1 week
remediation_business_steps_taken:
06/22/2021
ID - 1281

Issara had a meeting with the business, the business responded that the positive cases so far not migrant workers, it is the full-time staff. However, the business will get back to Issara with the detail next week.
remediation_notes: The issue with lack of communication about the COVID-19 test and the workers who were found positive. Workers raised their questions and concerns about whether they will be paid for their quarantine days, who will pay for the medical treatment costs.
remediation_action: Issara had a meeting with the business, the business responded that the positive cases so far were all Thai full-time staff and no migrant workers.
