description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue  1. 

Context; The issue with a foreman worker who was attacked by an employee and broke her arm. Building 7, Line 7. Foreman Name - Vilakarn (Victim) who was attacked by a male employee. Accident date; 29 March 2021. 

Please be noted that the worker did not report to Issara, some of the witnesses have raised the concern regarding the workplace incident where a female worker was attacked by a  male worker. 

Talking Points ; 

Some workers reported that a Thai female worker from line 7 was attacked by the male worker and broke her arm and that she is going under treatment. And we would like to understand how this case is being handled.
In terms of her physical condition, how is the worker doing now? What kind of treatment has she received? Is she working or on sick leave? 
What are the actions and steps that the business has taken towards the male worker who attacked the female worker? (Note for BHR: if they say the worker was dismissed, then go to the next question, if they say that the worker is on probation or something else, note  immediate termination would be expected as appropriate punitive action for basically committing a crime on the production floor) 
What kind of assistance has the worker received so far from the company? Has the worker received any compensation? If so, from whom (CC, SSF, worker that attacked her?) And how much has she received/ will receive?


BHR to check with the business whether the following actions according to the law have been taken or not and if the timeframes of the actions followed the timeframes stipulated in the Workmen’s Compensation Act B.E. 2561.

Article 13 which requires the employer to immediately pay the medical expense,
Article 15 requires the employer to pay for any required rehabilitation expenses.
Article 18 where the employer should pay 70% of wages when the employee is unable to work, with the payment to be made from the first day the employee is unable to work and not exceeding one year.
Article 48 notes the employer must notify the govt within 15 days of injury and Article 49 notes the employee may need to submit claims to the govt office.

Criminal Code Section 295 (bodily injury) and 391 (attack on other). 
Anyone’s right who is physically attacked would involve filing police reports and taking a case to court or settling, which would most often involve lawyers and so on. Has this taken place yet?


Issue # 2. 25-May-2021. 

Context: The issue with the workers who are in Quarantine Center arranged by the business not having access to the medical care when it comes to the emergency situation. Workers added that there are some of the workers with symptoms that need immediate action are not being sent to the hospital as needed. 

Recommendations; 
-The business should clearly communicate to workers what the protocol are to assist workers that present serious symptoms and require medical assistance. 
Lack of communication and awareness could lead to uncertainty and unnecessary risks if workers do not know what to do and how to avoid further risks. Therefore, the business should conduct the announcement/ communication to all workers and provide information on:
-Contact information for the focal person to request medical assistance 
-Protocol of assistance for those presenting serious symptoms (timeframes, location, service provider - is it in a hospital, or a different quarantine center, is the assistance provided/arranged by the gov, etc.)
-How testing and monitoring is being handled

In addition, the business should make sure that everyone at the quarantine center receives proper food with enough protein and vitamins to keep workers healthy and reduce the serious conditions, and that the "living" conditions are good (good ventilation, the acceptable temperature of the close areas, etc.)

Talking Points
-Several workers have reported their concern being in the quarantine center and not having proper access to medical assistance, how does the business assign the medical staff for each QC? What are the processes? 
-How many workers have bees sent to the hospital so far? 
-What is the process for workers to be sent to the hospitals?
remediation_business_steps_taken:
05/14/2021

The business responded that the worker is on paid sick leave. The worker refused to receive compensation from the SSF as she has sued the offender herself. The case is being proceeded.

- Is it being processed in the Myanmar embassy in Bangkok and is there a long delay on the part of the embassy?

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The workers reported two instances of poor communication of company policies:
1) The workers did not know how the business determined the incentive pay for workers, saying incentives received were different from line to line. Workers in some lines earned 10,000-12,000 Baht per pay period but those in other lines received 5,000-6,000 Baht, which is a big difference.  Workers earning much less also had their incentive amount per piece decreased from 20 Baht to 15 Baht.
2) The workers also wanted clear communication regarding the company-wide coffee break at 10am.  Every worker received a 10 min coffee break between 10:00-10:10am but the workers in line no.9-10 didn't get this break.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Witsawad- the workers’ income in the pay period is not just about the incentives but also depending on the minimum wages that there are some different skills different workers get different wages. And the incentive depends on the design and style. There are different styles and different qualities. However, the worker will get the incentive with the completed product. For example, the cutting line, the sewing line and the packing line, all these lines have to finish all and get the incentive together. For communication, the line supervisor always explains to all workers before they start working on a new design and style based on the quality of pieces and they will get different rates of incentive. 

K. Raweeroge- It’s not the coffee break but it is after the worker does ‘Improving the fundamental condition of operating daily work’ (5S) 1. Clearing up 2. Organizing 3.Cleaning 4. Standardizing 5. Training & Discipline. All workers can take a rest break. However, he will investigate it. 

He added that for the incentive issue, it is difficult for all workers because of the step and work quality that have been mentioned in above. The HR will make sure for re-communication.


Case#1; incentive
The investigation result:
Incentive;
1. Each type of work necessitates the preparation of various pieces of equipment. associated with complete and complete
2. Employees in that affiliation must be able to sew in each style.
3. Collaborative effort ready to work together to achieve Time to Cycle Participate in the Balance Line
There are the reasons that, of all the components, the each line receive the different incentives

Action:
HR Morning Talk
- Communicating and reviewing the incentives to the workers, including working as a team

Case2# break
The investigation result:
Workers in Lines 9 and 10 know and understand that between 10:00 and 15:00, workers will be scheduled to do 5S; 10 minutes, and if they have time left, they can have a break such as drinking water and going to the bathroom. But most do not want to go out to rest. Because during the break, workers come out to meet a lot, they afraid that there will be a chance to get infected with Covid-19, so they might decide to do not go out to meet the others. but they will leave to break after a large group of workers have returned to work. This might cause some workers who want to go out with a large group of workers do not dare to take a break.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that his visa was expiring on 27 March 2023 and his passport expired in Feb 2024. On 24 Mar 2023, the business told him that they will not do the extension for him anymore. He is walk-in MOU worker from another factory and he started working with HIT-91 in 2021. Even they cannot extend the visa on the Thai side, he is happy to go back Myanmar and do the U-Turn process. Another worker said his 4-year visa and work permit will expire on 30 May 2023. There are lots of other workers whose documents are expiring in 2023 and they are not sure whether the business will arrange for their contract and document extension. The workers would like to know whether the supplier will extend their documents in Thailand or have them return to Myanmar for the U-turn process. Some workers went to the HR office on 27 March 2023 but HR did not respond to them with a clear answer. Some workers don't want to go back to Myanmar because of the security situation back home. Some are wondering if the business will do the pink card registration for them if the government announces another round.

For MOU workers whose visas and work permits will expire in May 2023, the business will send them back to Myanmar on 3rd May 2023. They need to do the U-Turn from Myanmar side and come back after the process is done. However, the business did not clearly explain the process and timeframe for this. There are a total of 64 workers in total and 13 workers have already done the passport extension. Some workers' visa and work permits will expire on 21 or 21 May 2023. They are wondering if the business can send them back by this time as they still need to inform their landlord one month in advance to leave their room so that they can get a deposit.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that for many MOU workers, their contracts and legal documents (visas, work permits) were expiring, some in March 2023 others in May 2023, but the business had not communicated to them as to whether their contracts and legal documents would be extended, and if so, whether they could have them extended in Thailand or they would need to return to Myanmar for the MOU U-turn process. For a group of 64 MOU workers whose visas and work permits will expire in May 2023, the business said they would need to do the U-turn process but did not clearly explain the process and timeframe for this.
remediation_action: Issara received updates from workers that the business held a communication session with them on 4 May 2023. The business has contracted Smart Thai RA to send the demand list to DOE with name list of 64 workers. The workers will go back to Myanmar on May 21 and stay for three months before returning to Thailand.
remediation_validation: Workers provided an update saying that 50 of 64 workers crossed the border at the Ranong-Kawthaung checkpoint. A Myanmar recruitment agency picked them up at the border and processed the passport renewals at the border. They have all arrived home, needing to stop overnight 3-4 nights in their journey home. The 3,000 Baht they received from the business was not enough for various expenses during this journey.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; The issue with lack of communication about the COVID-19 test. Workers raised that they have heard that the business is will not cover medical fees if they get infected. Workers also are concern about how the business handles infected workers. 

Recommendations; 
-The business to provide clear guidance about the assistance for workers that test positive for COVID-19. The guidance shall be provided in written accompany by verbal announcements and it should cover the following information: 
-are there different measures/procedures depending on the severity of the symptoms 
-who will covered the treatment costs (SSF, employer?) 
-quarantine centers and services
-the process that the infected and not infected workers will have to follow (self-quarantine, etc.)
- the wages payment for the days of quarantine whenever needed

Talking points

supplier_name: Hi-Tech Chaiyaphum Apparel Co., Ltd. (Lat Yai)
description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; The issue with the announcement that the business made regarding vaccination for workers Burmese only. The announcement did not include detail in case of side effects that might occur to the workers. 


Recommendations:
Given that workers have raised many concerns about the announcements related to the vaccination and they reporting a lack of understanding of how it will be handled, it is recommended that the business make written and verbal announcements including the following information before the workers are vaccinated: 

When is the process starting?
Who is leading the process?
Is the process the same for Burmese and Thai workers? If not, how is it different and why?
Reassurance that the vaccines that will be used have been approved by the World Health Organization and the Thai Government, therefore, they are safe
Who to contact in case there are any questions about the vaccine? (could be the government hotline)
-Information on typical side effects and how long these last. And what kind of support workers would receive if they get side effects (medical assistance, paid sick leave, etc.)

Understanding that this is a topic of concern for all workers, it is recommended that the business is open to dialogue with workers, hear their concerns and be able to reply to their questions so that the process can be smooth and workers feel secure about it. Issara can provide support by reviewing the language of the announcement so the information can be easily understood by all migrant workers. 

In addition to migrant workers’ communication, it is recommended that the business provide similar information to Thai workers. 

Talking points:
Ask the business for information about the vaccination plan: -
-When is this happening?
-Is this organized by the government?
-Is it the same plan for Burmese and Thai workers? If not, how is it different and why?
-How is vaccination being communicated about to workers?  How can Issara support the business policy and information on how workers at your business will get vaccinated?
-Are you providing paid time off for workers to get vaccinated, and for medical leave if they experience short time side effects?  Short term effects are very typical, and workers will probably need short periods off - are you preparing for this?
- Many in the world, and many workers calling, do receive information on some more serious side effects of COVID vaccines, such as reports of strokes in very few cases.  Are you communicating the science and prevalence of these to workers, and do you have a plan in case a worker has a serious side effect (even such as being sick for over 1-2 days)? 
- What is the business response in the event a worker declines to get vaccinated?
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had a meeting with the business, the business responded that they were following the government's order to collect the survey from the migrant workers. It is not about the vaccination plan that came from the business. However, the business agreed to recommunicate with the workers to make them understand the purpose of the survey that they have collected. Issara checked with the workers for their verification, workers updated being recommunicated about the voluntary process of the vaccination plan. Workers added not having concerns regarding COVID-19 vaccinations at the moment.
remediation_notes: Announcements have been made by the business regarding upcoming vaccination of workers, but workers report a lack of detail on vaccines and potential side effects they have heard about.
remediation_action: The business has filled out the Social Security Office's required forms for vaccination interest/plans, and will communicate further with workers on vaccine safety and protocols.

supplier_name: Hi-Tech Chaiyaphum Apparel Co., Ltd. (Lat Yai)
description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that workers in her line (B18) didn't understand how the targets were set and how that was awarded as "maung incentive" pay.  Those in line B18 used to receive this incentive under the former line supervisor but has stopped receiving it since the new supervisor (P Nu) took charge.  She noted that this is happening in line B17 as well. Right now, Wanna Yin is in charge of lines B16 and B17, while Wanna Kai is taking care of lines B18 and B29.

TPs:
- What targets need to be met for workers to receive the "Maung incentive"? Is it based on the production of the whole line and incentive awarded to the whole group?
- How often is this incentive provided?
- The worker noted that this incentive ceased after the new line supervisor started.  Why might this be the case? Has the criteria for providing this incentive changed?

Recommendations:
- Investigate to find out how the Maung incentive is set up and what targets need to be reached for the incentive to be paid and why suddenly workers have stopped receiving the incentive with the change of the line supervisor.
- Communicate clearly to the workers the criteria upon which the company determines that a worker will receive this incentive.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Wachirapon, HR manager, stated that she is unsure what the 'Maung Incentive' is 
. Typically, the incentive is determined by the design and product of the order. And the worker would be paid fairly based on the effectiveness and efficiency of the finished product. In terms of supervisors, the line supervisors are sometimes rotated according to company policy because different supervisors have different skills and are rotated for the most effective production.

She will, however, look into it further and get back to us by next week.



BHR followed up and shared about ‘Maung Incentive’ and also case 1,2, and 4.
Case 1. According to the production, every worker at that line must pass the sawing test. If the worker passed, he or she can work and remain on that line. If not, the worker will be transferred to another line.
Case 2. This is not the case; every morning, the production manager will calculate the workforce who will report to work that day. As a result, there is no workload for the workers.
Case 3. HR held a communication session with all workers on the lines. Currently, the company has lower orders and the workers do not have OT. As a result, this occurred and affected every line. There is also no rotation of supervisors on the lines. HR is also available to any workers who have questions but no one is asking. When HR explained the incentive scheme to the workers, they said they understood.
Case 4. HR trained these supervisors on how to communicate with workers. Because these supervisors simply did not communicate with the workers on an ongoing basis. However, these supervisors would improve after the training.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that workers in her line didn't understand how the targets were set and how that was awarded as the "Maung incentive" pay.  Those in her line used to receive this incentive under the former line supervisor but has stopped receiving it since the new supervisor took charge.  She noted that this is happening in line B17 as well.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations:
- Co-organize line supervisor training with Issara, with a focus on effective communication on the company's policies and procedures so that workers are not confused about them.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the public holiday. Workers reported that they were being asked to sign a consent form which was written in Thai without an explanation and later realised it was the consent to agree to work for a public holiday (13th Oct). It also happened on 23rd Sep. Workers added that they were asked to sign the document first only after the workers signed the documents the line supervisor explained the purpose. Workers want to take a rest and be well explained about the documents before they sign.

Recommendations; 
The business  shall immediately make an announcement to all workers noting that the consent received earlier is void because workers did not understand what they were consenting to, request the voluntary consent of workers that are willing to work on the upcoming public holiday on Oct 13th, and provide the consent forms to work on Oct 13th in the languages of the workers, without pressure to sign
The business is to make sure that all communication documents are in the native language of the workers, especially those documents requiring their informed consent
The business is to make sure that workers understand what the business is requesting, and that the worker has the right to voluntarily consent to the request by fully explaining the nature of the request in a language the workers understand, prior to asking for the workers’ consent.

Talking Points: 
Is the business aware that the consent form that the workers had to sign was only in Thai and not in Burmese (Khmer) and that the line supervisors that were tasked to get the consent from workers only explained what the workers were consenting to after the worker had already signed? 
What is the production plan for 13 Oct? Is the business planning for full production on that day?
How many workers have agreed to work on 13 Oct? 
Have there been any workers that have reported to HR or through the grievance channels about this issue?
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Closure note 

 
Isara raised this issue with the business, and the business initially noted that the consent form that workers need to sign was already in workers' native language and the workers were notified one month in advance.  However, the consent form that the worker provided showed that the form did not provide sufficient information to help the worker understand what he/she was voluntarily signing up for. Issara escalated this issue, with support from the Strategic Partner, and suggested the business revise the consent form so that there was sufficient information in it to help the workers understand what they were consenting to (i.e. working OT or on a holiday). The business provided a new form that the company will use to get management approval for additional work hours to be performed by employees as per production demands, which lays out the policy that employees are to voluntarily consent to any such OT hours or work on a holiday.  The business noted that this document is now attached as a cover sheet to the consent form that workers will sign, in the workers’ languages. Although the consent form itself was not revised by the business, Issara is closing this case because the business is providing the cover sheet that provides an explanation that the additional work is to be voluntary.
remediation_business_steps_remaining: The business to revise the consent from where workers need to sign.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker went back to Cambodia from 20 April 2023 and returned to work on 2 May 2023. Before he left Thailand, he requested 7 leave days (mix of annual and business) plus 3 holidays (3 holidays between 20 Apr - 30 Apr are the special holidays provided by GFPT as the Islamic holidays), and was supposed to go back to work on 30 April 2023. But he couldn't get back on time and missed a day at work, and tried to request one more leave day from the line supervisor through his friend but the line supervisor did not approve. Before he left for Cambodia, he was warned that if he returned late, we would be suspended from OT work and receive a warning letter. As a consequence of missing one day at work without proper leave, he got suspended from OT work for two months and received a warning letter (he signed a letter in Thai which he couldn't read but knows it's a warning letter).  He hasn't received any OT for a month already. The line supervisor who suspended OT of the worker name Ky at line BL of Chin Soun department. The worker tried to go to HR two times to check about this OT policy but the interpreters were not available so couldn't discuss this with HR.

NOTE: The worker is afraid that if Issara mentions his name or specifically, he is afraid that the line supervisor will target him so, it is better to raise it in general and clarify with the business.

TPs:
- What is the company's policy on OT work?  Is OT work offered to workers generally and workers are allowed to consent to it?  Or does the company offer OT work to some workers and not others? If so, based on what criteria is this selection made?  Who gets to make this decision (i.e. the line supervisor)? 

Recommendations:
- Workers should not be denied overtime work opportunities as a form of punishment or in a discriminatory way
- Communicate to workers the company's policy and practice regarding how OT work is offered to workers, that it is not discriminatory or selective in a way that is not fair to workers
remediation_business_steps_taken: According to K. Sarayuth, the GFPT's policy on OT work is that it is offered to workers generally and equally in the same production line, that workers are allowed to consent to it, and that there is no punishment for workers' leave. In this case, if Issara can provide the name of the production line, supervisor, or worker, HR will investigate with the worker's safeguard. Reasa explained that Issara needs to get consent from the workers before getting back to GFPT.
remediation_notes: A worker returned Cambodia on 20 April 2023 and came back to work on 2 May 2023. Before he left Thailand, he requested 7 days of annual leave in addition to 3 special holidays provided by the business, and intended to return to work on 30 April 2023. But he missed a day at work, and tried to make a request for one additional leave day through his friend as he couldn't get back to Thailand in time but the line supervisor did not approve. As a consequence, he was suspended from OT work for two months and received a warning letter, and has had no OT work for a month now. The worker tried to go to HR two times to check about this OT policy but the interpreters were not available so couldn't discuss this with HR.
remediation_action: Issara raised the issue of how OT is offered to workers, without disclosing the specifics of the worker report because the worker is afraid of retaliation. The business HR noted that it is GFPT policy that OT work is offered to workers generally and equally in the same production line, and that workers are allowed to consent to it.  Offer of OT is not used to punish workers, say for taking leave without proper approval. In this case, if Issara can provide the name of the production line, supervisor, or worker, HR will investigate with the worker's safeguard. Issara noted that we have not gotten consent from the worker yet to disclose his personal details.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- Conduct a regular survey of workers to understand whether the company's policies are being properly implemented as they pertain to management and treatment of workers
- Conduct regular training and refreshers with line supervisors to build their capacity to properly communicate and implement the company's policies relevant to relations with workers, especially migrant workers

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers have been informed since a month ago that they can no longer bring their own food and curries to the canteen due to the renovation of the lunch box shelves. They have no choice but to buy food sold at the canteen and the business has not informed them how long this situation will last.

TPs:
- What renovation is taking place that makes it necessary that workers cannot bring their own food and have to buy food at the canteen?
- How has this been announced to the workers?

Recommendations:
- Investigate why this renovation is taking so long, recognizing the impact this is having on the workers who want to bring their own food but cannot
- Announce clearly to workers why they are not being allowed to bring their own food and also provide a clear timeframe as to when they will be able to resume bringing their own food to the canteen

remediation_action:
On November 27, 2023, GFPT management, HR, and Production will meet to make a final decision on whether or not to allow workers to bring their own food to the canteen. Then they will communicate to the workers about the situation clearly.

The factory has enough food vendors in the cafeteria to accommodate all workers, and they will also allow workers to eat at shops outside the factory if they wish. Because of food safety policies and the prevention of contamination in the manufacturing process, they will not allow workers to bring food from outside to eat in the cafeteria.

In the latest update, HR tried to say technically workers can still bring their own food (changed from their earlier position that it was due to food safety policies that outside food is not allowed) but there is no storage space where workers can keep their food until lunchtime so, in effect, workers can't bring their own food. HR will clearly communicate this policy to workers through verbal and written announcements by February 15, 2024.

The business responded to worker concerns about the canteen food, providing evidence about how food is stored when being sold to workers to ensure that the food does not go bad.
remediation_validation:
Workers updated Issara that since the business decision, the workers have not received the official announcement about why workers cannot bring their own food to eat in the canteen.

Workers updated Issara that the lack of food storage shelves for the workers makes it difficult for them because they are concerned about the quality of the canteen food. For night shift workers, for example, sometimes they have to buy food in the evening that the vendor made earlier in the morning, which may have gone bad and is causing upset stomachs and diarrhea. More recently, workers said the food quality has been getting better, with the food vendors serving food from heated containers but the business should continue to pay more attention to controlling the food quality because she still recently found a small worm in one of the dishes.

Workers confirmed that they received the communication that they are not allowed to bring the food from outside.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The workers raised their concern regarding the factory shut down and daily wages. They added that they wanted to know how they will be paid for their daily wages during the factory shut down. Some workers heard that only workers in the business dorm will receive the wages. 

Recommendations; 
The business shall provide clear communication with the workers regarding the payment during the factory shut down and also about the process of treatment if they have been tested positive. It is recommended to share detailed information in writing with all workers covering the following points:
How would workers be paid for the days the company is shut down? Would all workers receive 100% of the wages, or 75%, etc?
In case of workers being positive for COVID: 
Who will cover the treatment costs (SSF, employer?) 
Information on quarantine centers and services
The process that the positive and non-positive workers have to follow (self-quarantine, etc.)
Contact information in case of emergency, such as experiencing serious symptoms 

Talking points
-How many workers have been tested and found positive so far? How is the business managing the situation for those that have tested positive? 
-Which hospital or quarantine centers are workers being sent to?
-How has the business managed the workers who share the dormitory and production lines?  
-How have the workers been communicated about the COVID-19 treatment fees? And the payment of their wages?
remediation_business_steps_taken:
ID-1337
Isara has raised this issue with the business, the business responded having done communications with the workers and also had several teams working to minimize the spread of COVID-19, however, the business agreed to get back to Issara.
remediation_notes: Workers did not receive clear information from the business about whether they would be paid their daily wages while the factory was shut down due to Covid-19.  Those staying outside in private accommodation during the shutdown heard that only those in the factory dorms would receive their wages.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with a worker who was told by the business not to come back to work as she is in her advanced pregnancy period. The worker said that she has not received her daily wages during the days that she was not allowed to work. The worker added not being clearly communicated about her rights as a pregnant worker and not knowing whether she will receive the payment and maternity leave according to the LPA or not. Worker’s personal information : Passport: N01017427, Name: Sreypeou Nuon, and Working ID:  0104347.

Recommendations: 
-The business to conduct clear communication with the worker and explain her rights as a pregnant worker in Thailand and how the business will support her to get her benefits from the business and the social security fund. 
-The worker should be provided with 90 days of paid maternity leave and 8 days of unpaid leave if the worker wishes to take those 8 days. 50% of the maternity leave payment should come from the employer and the rest 50% to be reimbursed from the Social Security fund. 
-Worker added that she will deliver her baby in a few weeks, therefore the business shall provide/facilitate assistance to the worker as needed such, as interpretation, full information on medical assistance, and how to get all proper documentation such as the baby’s birth certificate, the child-raising fund process, etc. 
-The worker added not receiving her wage for September, the business shall provide her wages in a timely manner.  

Talking Points;
-Is the business aware of this worker's condition? If yes, what has been communicated to her about her job position, her wages, and her benefits as a pregnant worker? 
-What was the reason why the worker did not receive her wage for the month of September? And how is the company processing the benefits for the worker through the SSO?
-How many workers are there in this situation? 

Time frame: 1 week.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had several meetings with the business, the business responded that they are open to providing maternity leave starting from the date as requested by the worker and also assisting the worker with the required documents for the social security benefits for her delivery. The business confirmed to provide the daily wage for the workers for the first 45 days according to the law and help coordinate with the SSF for the rest of 45 days of her daily wages. Issara follow up with the worker, the worker updated having close contact with the HR for the further process and confirmed not having concerns anymore. The worker will receive 27000THB of daily wages during her maternity leave.
remediation_notes: A worker who was told by the business not to come back to work because she is in an advanced stage of her pregnancy. She has not received her daily wages during the days that she was not allowed to work.
remediation_action: Issara had a meeting with the business, and the business responded that they have been working with the worker and will approve worker's maternity leave starting from the date that she was admitted to the hospital as requested by the worker. And the business will process the documents for compensation from Social Security during the maternity leave period and will receive the worker back whenever she is ready to get back to work.
remediation_validation: The worker confirmed that she wanted to take maternity leave from the date she was admitted to the hospital for the period of leave allowed to her, and receive daily wage compensation for that period as according to the law.
remediation_results: The pregnant worker and the business have agreed on the period of the maternity leave, the business will process the daily wage payment during the maternity leave period and will welcome the worker back to work once she is ready to return to work.

DATE: 13 Dec 2023
Sopida, BFI's HR manager, explained that for the payment system working day, all workers who work from the first to the fifteenth of the month will receive their wages, attendant allowance, and incentive on the 25th of the month. According to company policy, workers who have an MoU contract until the 25th of December will receive the bonus proportionately. In this case, the worker's contract expires on December 16, 2023; however, the workers were required to return for an MoU U-Turn on December 13, 2023. So, when the workers return, they are given new contracts, begin a new year of work, and receive a full-year bonus the following year. According to the policy, because the workers returned to Cambodia on December 13th, they must work until December 15th to receive the attendant allowance. However, the worker will still receive the performance incentive on December 15th.  They will then communicate with the workers again about this policy when they return on December 19, 2023.

DATE: 5 Jan 2024

K. Sopida, HR manager confirmed that they communicated the policy on 16 December 2023

remediation_issara_recommendation: The worker reported that her MOU-U turn has to expire on 19th December but HR asked to go to re new MOU-Uturn on 14th December. And payday will be on the 15th. She explained business tried to re-new her MOU cycle before payday as the business does not want to pay incentives, and bonuses based on workers' MOU cycle. The worker mentioned the amount of incentives, and bonuses that workers have to receive was around 9000 THB to 10000 TH per worker (One year incentives, and bonuses) and 17 workers have to face this issue, they feel unfairer and not transparent. remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 13 Dec 2023
Sopida, BFI's HR manager, explained that for the payment system working day, all workers who work from the first to the fifteenth of the month will receive their wages, attendant allowance, and incentive on the 25th of the month. According to company policy, workers who have an MoU contract until the 25th of December will receive the bonus proportionately. In this case, the worker's contract expires on December 16, 2023; however, the workers were required to return for an MoU U-Turn on December 13, 2023. So, when the workers return, they are given new contracts, begin a new year of work, and receive a full-year bonus the following year. According to the policy, because the workers returned to Cambodia on December 13th, they must work until December 15th to receive the attendant allowance. However, the worker will still receive the performance incentive on December 15th.  They will then communicate with the workers again about this policy when they return on December 19, 2023.

DATE: 5 Jan 2024

K. Sopida, HR manager confirmed that they communicated the policy on 16 December 2023
remediation_notes: Workers reported that those that needed to return to their home countries to process the MOU U-turn process were scheduled to return before the MOU contract expiry date and before payday and they think the business did this to not have to pay for certain incentives and bonuses that they would have received if they had been allowed to work until the MOU expiry date.
remediation_action: HR explained that all workers who work from the first to the fifteenth of the month will receive their wages and attendance allowance. According to company policy, workers who have an MoU contract until the 25 December 2023 will receive the bonus proportionately. In this case, the worker's contract expired on 16 December 2023 and they were required to return for the MoU U-turn process on 13 December 2023. Therefore, they will not receive the attendance allowance but will still receive the performance incentive. HR communicated this again to the workers.
remediation_validation: The worker confirmed that the manager had clarified this with them, and they now understand that although they will not receive the attendance allowance, they will still receive their performance incentive.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case. The workers confirmed they now understand how the company calculated their allowances and incentives.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the COVID-19 issues management. The workers reported that the spread of the virus in the factory is increasing day after day, however, the business has not managed on-site tests for all workers. As a result, the workers have to go to their Social Security Hospital for the test. To get the test, workers have to wake up at midnight to be able to get in the queue. Workers reported being sick and having to do this all process makes them sicker. 

Talking Points
_Wokers have reported an increased number of COVID positive cases in the factory, what is the ratio at the moment? 
-What are the steps that the business is taking to minimize the spread of the virus?

Recommendations:
-The business shall inform the ministry of health and request on-site tests for high-risk workers. This would help have better visibility of how serious the situation is at the factory and it will also help to minimize the spread within the province especially because this would avoid sick workers having to commute to the hospital. 
-The business shall communicate with all of the employees about the business action to address this issue.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara raised this issue with the business to provide the recommendations, by the time Issara reached out to the business, 100% of the workers have been tested for COVID-19 already by the government process. Since then Issara has not received additional complaints from the workers as they have gone through the government testing process.
remediation_notes: The issue with workers reporting that more and more workers are falling sick due to Covid-19 on a daily basis but the business has not arranged for on-site Covid-19 tests for all workers. Instead, workers that have Covid-19 symptoms have to go to the hospital for the test, with long waiting lines requiring some workers to wake up at midnight to be able to get in the queue.

Context: A worker from Sewing Line 2 reported that in the second week of February, her line supervisor announced that workers can’t get free Covid tests or Covid-related medical care at the hospital under social security coverage anymore.  From now on, the workers will have to pay 2,500 Baht for a Covid test. 

Talking  Points; 
-Workers have reported not having access to their SSF for Covid-related care. What is the business understanding on this issue? 
-Has the business checked the government regulations on what Covid-related care services are to be covered by SSO?  

Recommendations:
- The business should clarify with the SSO as to what Covid-related medical services are covered for those with social security coverage
- Communicate with all workers about their health care coverage including Covid-related care under the social security system
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have the policy where if a worker is feeling unwell, they have to approach the HR and request for the ATK test kit. If the ATK kit result positive, the workers will have to go to the Social Security Hospital for the additional test. If any workers want to do the PCR test by themselves, they have to pay by themselves. The business will make the announcement to the workers.
remediation_notes: A worker from Sewing Line 2 reported that in the second week of February, her line supervisor announced that workers can’t get free Covid tests or Covid-related medical care at the hospital under social security coverage anymore. remediation_action: Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have the policy where if a worker is feeling unwell, they have to approach the HR and request for the ATK test kit. The business clarified that if any worker wants to do the PCR test by herself, this would be on personal expense. The business will make the announcement to the workers to clarify this point.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; Workers who are requested to quarantine at home due to being in close contact with a Covid-positive person who is not an LB worker will not get paid for those days.


Talking Points; 
Workers have reported not receiving their daily wages if they have to take quarantine for being in close contact with their family members who are not the workers of Ladybird, what is the business policy in this case? 
How many workers are in this situation and what has been the process for them so far? 
How many days of quarantine are required for close contact cases? Who pays for those quarantine days? 
Has the business checked the government regulations on what Covid-related care services are to be covered by SSO and whether and how quarantine days for Covid close contacts are to be paid?  

Recommendations:
-The business should confirm the latest government regulations related to quarantine periods for Covid close contacts and how pay for missed working days due to quarantine is to be handled
We have received the update that the government regulations are as follows:  
-If a worker is found to be positive at the factory, she/he is supposed to be sent to the hospital for the PCR test and if confirmed as positive, receive the medical certificate and recommended to quarantine. The worker should get paid sick leave during those days. 
-If a worker is a close contact, s/he should visit the hospital and report why she/he is at high risk and get the recommendations from the hospital. The regular recommendations for vaccinated people is to take 10 days of quarantine and do another test on the 10th day. -If the result is negative, then the worker can start working. In terms of the wages for the high risk workers who have a medical certificate for their quarantine days, the employer can submit the worker information to the SSF for the 50% of wages. 
-If the worker is not allowed to go to the hospital but the employer orders the worker to take quarantine, it is the responsibility of the employer to pay the worker wages. 
The business should communicate with the workers about how quarantine days for close contacts will be paid.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have a policy where workers have to practice social distancing at any time including in their home. The business added that they assigned the suspected workers to take 5 days of quarantine without pay because they get to close contact which is against the business policy. Issara has provided the recommendations, the business agreed to have an internal meeting with the management and get back to Issara.
After the investigation, the business has revised the policy and created a separate work area for the high risks workers to work for 5 days. They will then be ATK tested again, and if the results remain negative, they will be able to return to the normal production line. This new policy was announced last week and will be implemented this week.
remediation_notes: Workers who are requested to quarantine at home due to being in close contact with a Covid-positive person who is not a LB worker will not get paid for those days.

After the investigation, the business has revised the policy and created a separate work area for the high risks workers to work for 5 days. They will then be ATK tested again, and if the results remain negative, they will be able to return to the normal production line.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that there has not been clear communication from the business about the process for getting their OWIC cards and all this time, their passports and work permits are being retained by the business. It has been months now and workers have been hearing from other people that the Myanmar Embassy has temporarily suspended issuing OWIC cards and they may need to do it in Myanmar.  Now they only have copies of their passports.

Recommendations:
- Workers should have access to their identity documents, and should not be retained by the business for months 
- Communicate clearly to workers about the timeline and when workers can get their identity documents back
- If the OWIC process is suspended, return passports and WPs to workers until this process can be re-started
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Review how document extensions process steps and timelines are communicated to migrant workers. Develop a communication plan so workers are informed well in advance and know when the company needs to take their identity documents for extension purposes.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1: Workers reported that there has not been clear communication from the business about the process for getting their OWIC cards and all this time, their passports and work permits are being retained by the business. It has been months now and workers have been hearing from other people that the Myanmar Embassy has temporarily suspended issuing OWIC cards and they may need to do it in Myanmar.  Now they only have copies of their passports.

Recommendations:
- Workers should have access to their identity documents, and should not be retained by the business for months 
- Communicate clearly to workers about the timeline and when workers can get their identity documents back
- If the OWIC process is suspended, return passports and WPs to workers until this process can be re-started

Case #2: A worker had been working in TUM until 2023 June had returned to Myanmar for U-Turn Process. His wife went back to Myanmar with a TUM arrangement on 1st June 2023 along with other 141 workers. Before the U Turn trip, Ms. Lin ( Myanmar translator) announced that all workers will be called back as U Turn MOU and the business will still pay for the holiday wages while they are staying in Myanmar. However, it has been 6th month TUM hasn't give any information of when they will be  called back and which agency will the workers contact. 

Recommendations:
- Provide clear information to workers currently waiting in Myanmar since June 2023 about the U-turn process, what will happen when, and which RA to contact in Myanmar
- Maintain channels of communication with this group, such as via FB messenger group, and send update announcements on a regular basis.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 1 Nov 2023

Case 1
K. Wichai, HR Manager, apologized for the delay in corrective action due to a high volume of audits in recent weeks. He added that they are working on a corrective action plan that will be shared with us next week.

Case 2
K. Wichai, HR Manager, mentioned that there may be a delay on the Myanmar recruitment agency's end. However, he needs to investigate this matter and report back to us with the corrective action next week.


DATE: 13 Nov 2023
Case #1
Investigation Detail:
HR distributed copies of documents to the workers. Because the original passport must be submitted to immigration for a stamp VISA for the new passport. After HR receives the passports back from immigration, HR needs to do the photocopy + scan for keeping and record the information in the company's register as well. Because there are a lot of workers in the group making new passports this time, it will take time to process.

Corrective Action:
HR has planned to schedule a meeting and distribute the original passports and work permits to the workers during the period of 11-14 Nov 2023.


DATE: 30 Nov 2023

Case #2

Investigation Result:
TUM checked with the recruitment agency that the process is being delayed by the Myanmar government. 

Corrective Action:
HR contacted the recruitment agency and requested that they explain to the workers the MoU U-Turn process situation.
HR communicated and explained the situation to the workers in Myanmar via the company's Facebook page, and the interpreter notified them.
remediation_notes:
Case #1: Workers reported that there has not been clear communication from the business about the process for getting their OWIC cards and all this time, their passports and work permits are being retained by the business. It has been months now and they only have copies of their passports.

Case #2: Workers that returned to Myanmar in June 2023 to do the U-turn process are still waiting and have not received information as to when they will return and which recruitment agency will coordinate their return
remediation_action:
Case #1: HR investigated and noted that it has taken time to process getting visas stamped on the workers' passports at immigration.  In the meantime, photocopies of passports were provided to workers. HR will schedule a meeting and return the original passports and work permits to the workers during the period of 11-14 Nov 2023.

Case #2: HR checked with the recruitment agency and found that the process is being delayed by the Myanmar government. HR asked the recruitment agency to explain the situation to the workers in Myanmar. In addition, HR has communicated this directly to workers via facebook
remediation_validation:
Case #1: Workers confirmed that they received the announcement about the process of getting their passports back and some have already received them, and others will receive them in batches.

Case #2:
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Review how document extensions process steps and timelines are communicated to migrant workers. Develop a communication plan so workers are informed well in advance and know when the company needs to take their identity documents for extension purposes.
next_description: validate with the worker.

supplier_name: Nan Yang Garment Co., Ltd. (Nakhon Pathom)
description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Around 800 workers hold the CI, pink cards, and PJ passports, and most of their documents have expired since March 2022.  The workers want to know when and how the business will extend their documents. The workers want to get a clear sense as soon as possible because the CI center will shut down in July.

Talking Points:
What is the company doing to process the passport and pink card extensions for the workers?
When will the process be completed, given that it has already been three months since their identity documents have expired?
What is causing this delay in the identity document renewals?

Recommendations for remediation:
Communicate to all workers about the process and schedule for their identity document extensions; explain the reasons for the delay and what the company is doing to push forward with the process
Ensure the identity documents are done without further delay
remediation_notes: Workers reported that for around 800 workers that hold the Certificate of Identity (CI), "pink" cards, or PJ passports (passport type for jobs), their documents have expired since March 2022.  The workers want to know when and how the business will extend their documents. The workers want to get a clear sense as soon as possible because they heard that the Certificate of Identity processing center will shut down in July.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for System Change
Suggest business introduce the HR focal that workers should contact at any time as needed. 
Communicate and encourage workers to reach out to internal channels whenever they have issues regarding documents.

supplier_name: (SKP -BP) Syarikat Sin Kwang Plastic Industries Sdn. Bhd. (BP Plant)(18591-D)
description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue Detail; There are around 50 workers who moved to SKP during the COVID-19 outbreak because their employers got bankrupt.  At that time, SKP recruited those workers officially with a contract and said that they will apply for a work permit. They all had a valid passport at that time. However, the worker said that it seems SKP has not applied for the work permit or has not been successful to do so. Malaysia ended its "RECALIBRATION PROGRAMME" last month (30th June ) which means workers with no official documents will be taken action against the "RECALIBRATION PROGRAMME".Meaning that the Malaysian Government has given a special time period under a program that is called "RECALIBRATION PROGRAMME" for undocumented workers to return back to their homes or be legalized in Malaysia. Those who failed to do so within the given time frame will be taken action by the Malaysian government. 
SKP neither has communicated with the workers about their plan for them nor has returned their documents. However, SKP has recently collected the name list of those workers. Workers are not sure what the plan is from the SKP side but they are very worried about their status given the recent announcement about the "RECALIBRATION PROGRAMME" being ended.   

Workers situation, 
Workers are very concerned and feel helpless, there are some workers who are over-worried and mentally sick and can not even go to work. Some cry when they talk about their documents and status. They also think that, since SKP has recently recruited Nepalese MoU workers from Nepal, they may kick out these Burmese workers whose status is uncertain. They heard some rumors that they will be Buang (Malaysian language which means Kick out in English) by the SKP. 
Workers want to be clearly communicated about the business plan for them and make them legalize.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have been working very hard to apply documents for all of the workers who were recruited under "RECALIBRATION PROGRAMME" however, the process from the government side is very delay. The business confirmed that all of the workers are legal workers and their documents are in the process. The business added that they will distribute a supporting paper that will proof their legal status. In addition to that, the business said that they will also conduct communication with the workers. 


Issara checked with the workers, workers updated that they have received the communication letter which is in English. Issara helped them  with the translations. Some workers confirmed receiving supporting document that explain their legal status.

supplier_name: (SKP -BP) Syarikat Sin Kwang Plastic Industries Sdn. Bhd. (BP Plant)(18591-D)
description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Death of Nepalese wokers;  Frequent death of Nepalese workers due to different reasons, death from accidents outside the workplace, some suicide in their housing, and some from sickness. Workers wanted to know if they have the right to get any compensation from the company. The latest death happened on 4 July 2022. When the death happens the company normally pays around 2,000 Ringgit only. Workers think that they are supposed to get more than that. 

Issue #2. Lack of information about workers' rights; Several workers reported not knowing their rights, they said that they want to know the benefits that they have such as annual leaves, sick leaves, life insurance, and the procedures to take leaves. They added that they do not have a workers' manual that they can refer to if they want to know something. 

Talking Points; 
How does the business communicate with workers about their rights, and other policies that are related to them - what language and how often, etc? Who from HR is responsible to make sure that workers are updated with all of the information they need? 
What are the business understanding and awareness of the frequent death of Nepalese workers? 
How does the insurance policy work for foreign workers and local workers? 
Do workers have life insurance in case of death? 
Is there a worker's manual that workers can refer to when they need it? If not, any plan to have it? How can Issara support the business in the development of the manual and dissemination? To share that general information on the rights of migrant workers is on Golden Dreams that Burmese workers can read and we are in the process of having that for Nepalese workers but not for all the workers.  

Recommendations;
The business to clearly communicate with all workers under Ramatex group about the insurance policy in case of work-related and non-work-related death. The communication should also cover the process of reporting to different departments, the time frame, and benefits for the family of death worker. 

Reference; Work accidents and deaths for foreign workers are regulated under the Workmen Compensation Act 1952. However, death under this Law is related to work
According to this Law, if the injury related to work caused death, the compensation is 60 months' earnings or 18 thousand ringgit, whichever is less.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
If a worker is dead inside the workplace, the business will consider case by case for compensation, however, if a worker is dead outside of the factory, they are not entitled to get compensation. SOCSO and SKIPA cover up to 20,000 MYR for medical expenses. For death cases outside of the workplace, the business provides 2000 MYR as solidarity support. The business does not buy life insurance because there were some cases workers would suicide to get compensation for their family members. The business has stops the practice of buying life insurance 10 years ago. However, there are some workers who have insurance in Nepal, if they died they will get compensation from Nepal. The factory is working with the recruitment agency to get the recommended insurance company in Nepal so that workers can be benefited when needed.

The company agreed to clarify the company policy with the workers. 


It has passed several weeks now the business has not come with the update. Issara is facing challenges to get updates or responses from Ramatex HR.

Issue#2. 

Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that for the workers who were recruited under the "Re-calibration Program", we just got the confirmed result from Immigration last week and currently arranging the FOMEMA health check. Issara suggested doing the communication before the result came out from the immigration to avoid workers having to decide about their future at the very last minute as Issara has learned from other factory workers. 

The business has not replied to these suggestions. Since it has been over several months, Issara is closing these issues with poor remarks.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The worker said he and around 20 Cambodian workers came to work in the same batch and their visas will expire in mid-June 2023. The workers hold 10-year validity passports and have completed their 4-year MOU contracts during Covid which was extended during that time for 2 more years but this is now going to expire. When the workers checked with the business about whether their legal work documents will be extended, there was no clear response. If they were to go back home for the MOU U-turn process, the workers also have questions about whether they will get their current jobs back when they return. 

TPs:
- How does the business communicate with workers when their visas, WPs, MOU contracts are going to expire?  Do they alert them about next steps, whether they will be extended or not?  How soon in advance before the expiration date does the company communicate with each worker or batch of workers?

Recommendations:
- Hold a communication session with this batch of 20 Cambodian workers, to help them understand what the process will be given that their visas are going to expire in mid June.  
- If their contracts will be extended, inform them about the MOU U-turn process, the steps involved, the parties involved (like the RA), cost and who will pay, and the timeframe. Be clear on the nature of their jobs, roles and responsibilities when they return to start a fresh MOU cycle.
remediation_business_steps_taken: K. Anchan, HR will communicate with the Cambodian workers on May 26. They intend to continue hiring Cambodian workers and will proceed with the MoU Uturn. When the workers return, they will all be given the same role and responsibilities.
remediation_notes: A batch of 20 Cambodian workers came to work together and their visas will expire in mid-June 2023. The workers hold 10-year validity passports and completed their 4-year MOU contracts during Covid which was extended during that time for 2 more years but this is now going to expire. When the workers checked with the business about whether their legal work documents will be extended, there was no clear response. If they were to go back home for the MOU U-turn process, the workers also have questions about whether they will get their current jobs back when they return.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations:
- As there are many batches of workers whose legal documents will be expiring at different times, the company should set a protocol so that xx days in advance of a contract/visa/WP expiration date, workers will be informed about the next steps.
- HR to conduct these communication sessions with each batch of workers according to the protocol

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A walk-in MOU worker moved to King Pac from Saraburi with the service of The First Good Man RA. He reported that the business asked 13-14 workers whose passport will expire in Feb 2024 to give 5,000 Baht the next day for the passport renewal process. As it is the very last minute notification, the workers are facing difficulties to give 5,000 baht.

TPs:
- Are passport renewal fees not covered by the employer as part of its EPP?
- Why were the workers informed about needing to cover this cost on such short notice?

Recommendations:
- Communicate well in advance with workers regarding all document processes, such as passport/visa/WP renewals, so that any preparations needed on the part of the workers can be made without having to rush because of the short notice given by the business
- Communicate clearly with migrant workers about all the fees and costs involved in recruitment and all document renewals/extensions, and a breakdown of what is covered by the employer and what is to be covered by the worker, if any.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 18 Jan 2024

K. Jarunee, QMS responded that she needs to investigate this case to get clarification internally from recruitment team staff and the recruitment agency. If this is the case, they would reimburse the workers and communicate to all workers, company staff, and the recruitment agency staff about the company recruitment policy and a zero-tolerance policy. They will get back to us with the investigation results and corrective action next week.
remediation_notes: Workers whose passport will expire in February 2024 were informed to pay 5,000 Baht the following day for the passport renewal process. They are facing difficulties to prepare this amount given the last minute notification.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Ensure there is an annual plan with a clear schedule for the year about when document processes need to be processed, and communicate the requirements to workers well in advance so that they know what they need to prepare on their side
next_description: get the corrective action.

remediation_notes: Workers whose passport will expire in February 2024 were informed to pay 5,000 Baht the following day for the passport renewal process by the Thai recruitment agency interpreter. They are facing difficulties to prepare this amount given the last minute notification.
remediation_action:
HR will investigate this case to get clarification internally from recruitment team staff and the recruitment agency. The business investigated and found that the Thai recruitment agency interpreter had communicated about the 5,000 Baht passport fee to workers employed by other factories in the same area and the King Pac workers had heard about it through those workers and no money was collected from any King Pac worker.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that there was a sudden announcement from the business saying more than 200 workers completing their 4-year MOU contracts would need to return to Myanmar to complete the U-Turn process. The business explained this to the workers in batches and told them they needed to wait in Myanmar until the demand was approved by the government. The business would not be responsible for the expenses that workers would incur during this unspecified waiting period. Additionally, the workers would have to pay for the costs of the U-turn process themselves.

The workers are concerned about the following:
1. Some workers (currently 7) cannot go back home during the waiting period because their villages are in the conflict zone and are worried about their safety.
2. Workers don't know why they have to pay for U-turn process costs, how long this process will take, or which recruitment agency will facilitate the process.
3. The business said workers would need to decide and inform the business on the very day this was announced. If a worker chooses not to do the U-turn process, the business will let them go without providing any severance pay. 

Talking points:
- Does the business know some workers are from conflict zones and they could be at risk of bodily harm if they had to go there during the waiting period?

Recommendations:
- The business should cover the costs of the U-turn process as a responsible and ethical recruiter, aligning with customer EPP expectations
- The business should make arrangements with the Myanmar recruitment agency to ensure that workers can be safe during the waiting period and don't need to return to their home villages during this time
- The business should communicate clearly the steps of the U-turn process, the timeline from start to finish, and the recruitment agency that will facilitate the process.
- If workers still choose not to do the U-turn process, provide them with severance pay as per the number of years of service
remediation_business_steps_taken:
According to K. Narisra, HR manager, the company is aware that some workers are afraid to return to Myanmar. Currently, CPH has submitted the demand and given the name list to SHWE HPAAN SERVICE RA in order to obtain approval from MOLIP, and the RA has said that the workers do not need to return to their home village but will instead stay and wait in Myalawadee. The RA will specify how long workers must wait and provide accommodations. 

She added that there are 2 options.
1. Mou U-Turn - CHP covers all the recruitment fee
2. As a result of the government announcement, HR is now considering registering MoU workers who have completed four years in Thailand. HR will, however, discuss this with top management next week. They will then communicate clearly with workers.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that there was a sudden announcement from the business saying more than 200 workers completing their 4-year MOU contracts would need to return to Myanmar to complete the U-Turn process. The business explained this to the workers in batches and told them they needed to wait in Myanmar until the demand was approved by the government. The business would not be responsible for the expenses that workers would incur during this unspecified waiting period. Additionally, the workers would have to pay for the costs of the U-turn process themselves.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: The business should have an annual schedule for visa, WP, and contract extensions so that workers have their documents extended in a timely manner; ensure that workers are informed well in advance of the extensions and how the process will be handled so that they are not left wondering and stressed about what will happen to them; ensure the business covers the costs of the U-turn process as per EPP and customer requirements.

According to K. Narisra, HR manager, the company is aware that some workers are afraid to return to Myanmar. The business would not be responsible for the expenses that workers would incur during this unspecified waiting period. Additionally, the workers would have to pay for the costs of the U-turn process themselves.
remediation_action: Issara reached out to the business, and the HR manager noted that the company is aware that some workers are afraid to return to Myanmar. supplier_name: Hong Seng Knitting Co., Ltd. (Branch Thungkhu)
description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client was previously working in HT-91 and moved to Hong Seng when her MOU contract came to end with HT-91. She is reporting the issues which are happening in Building A, line no. 1-7 (B-U 1).

No transparency in Public Holiday Announcement: She said that there is no announcement regarding Public Holidays and the workers don't know when their 13 public holidays are. Rather than setting at the beginning of the year, the business seems to allocate the public holidays based on its production needs. The workers just know from word-of-mouth in the production line a few days before each public holiday.

Recommendations:
- Post before the start of each year, the calendar for when the 13 public holidays will be for the workers so that they can plan ahead to use those rest days to their full benefit
- Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, the remaining public holidays scheduled for the rest of the year
remediation_notes: A worker reported that the business doesn't announce the annual dates for the 13 public holidays and are only informed a few days ahead of each holiday.
remediation_action: Though this business is currently not an active supplier of the Strategic Partner, Issara has reached out to the business to discuss this issue.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Consult with workers when they would like their 13 public holidays, to be considered when the business makes the decision on the holiday schedule each year

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A worker reported his contract not being extended by the business. He was informed only 13 days in advance before he was asked to stop working. He was asked to sing a document about the renewal of the contract about two weeks ago, however, suddenly was informed of not being extended his contract anymore. 



Recommendation: 
- It is the best practice to inform workers one month in advance before they are asked to stop working. Otherwise, it would be best to compensate for the days that the business failed to inform the worker. In this case, the worker was informed 13 days in advance which means he should be compensated for 17 days of his wages. 




Internal Note; 

The business screen shared the worker contract, the contract only mentioned the procedures about dismissal. This issue is not dismissal, therefore the business argued saying that the reason they did not inform one month in advance to the worker is because there is no written policy for not renewing contract. Since they did not have written policy, Issara highlighted the best practice about recruitment which include workers to be informed about their status so that he/she can be financially and mentally ready for the next steps if the business decide not to renew the contract. The business agreed with that and they said that they will propose to the management and get back to us.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business; we will propose the management based on the recommendations from Issara if this worker can get the compensation as he was not informed one month in advance. If the management agrees with the proposal, the HR team will communicate with the worker and get back to Issara. The HR team added that they will notify one month in advance if there are any workers that they decide not to extend their contract.

Worker update: 
The worker have updated that he have received 865 MYR for the days that the business missed to inform him in advance. The worker thanked Issara for the intervention.
