supplier_name: Daorae (Desa Sri Hartamas) Sdn Bhd, a Korean BBQ restaurant
description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client worked at a Korean BBQ restaurant located in KL Kepong Jalan Metro Perdana, which is one of fifteen branches of the restaurant chain. Out of the fifteen branches, this particular one was problematic. The restaurant has six Nepali and thirteen Burmese workers. The owner's son is abusive towards the Nepali workers, creating a hostile work environment. Issara is able to speak with two workers. They have been working for this employer for 10 months. They are all MoU workers. They are reporting as a group of 5 Nepali workers, but the client is quietly reporting. The client and the workers want to either be transferred to another branch under the same company or find employment in another company. The client has debts to pay and doesn't want to return to Nepal. The workers have a contract they made in Nepal, but the company made another contract which the client doesn't have and is unaware of its contents.
Following are the major issues reported by workers.

1) Document retention: Workers passports are held by the employer since they started their employment. The company also kept their passports and didn't provide them with worker ID cards (Jalan cards) or necessary documents. 

2) Restriction of Movement: The workers were not allowed to leave the premises, and this restriction also made it difficult for their friends to visit them.

3) Unfair suspension: Workers were frequently suspended for minor mistakes or even without any reason. During these suspensions, the company did not provide any food, and the workers were not allowed to go out and get their own. They were also denied access to basic amenities, like cooling fans, during these periods. One incident occurred when a friend of the client was suspended for simply asking a Burmese worker to clean a stain. The owner verbally abused him and kept him in detention (suspension) for 28 days. Throughout this time, the company did not provide any food or salary, leaving the workers in a dire situation. His friends attempted to provide food secretly, but they had to be cautious as the company would punish them if they were caught bringing in more substantial amounts of food or any food. 

Recently, the victim was suspended by the company for two months. During this period, he received no salary or food from the company. The suspension was a result of the employer demanding the victim to memorize the restaurant menu quickly.

If workers demand to change the employer, they are asked to work 4 months without pay and there are some workers who have accepted this situation as they could not bear the harsh working environment. 

4)Physical abuse: Physical assault includes being kicked, slapped on the face and belly, and having ears pulled. The employer even physically assaulted the client's genitals. Such harassment occurred almost daily and targeted everyone except.

5) Long working hours and incorrect payment: Workers have to work 14-15 hours a day. In return, they received a basic salary of 1500 RM and a 300 RM overtime allowance each month. 

6) Lack of Sick Leave: Even when the workers fell ill, they were forced to work, as the owner wouldn't allow them to stay in the hostel. 



Moreover, during salary payment time, the owner would abuse the workers and suspend them for minor mistakes. The owner often used the workers as a target for his frustrations, taking out his stress related to the business on them. Whenever the business is slow he will start abusing the worker for no reason.

Context: 

-One of the clients shared that his nephew came to KL, Malaysia on October 4th, 2023 through AGA International, RL: 530, a recruitment agency in Bangladesh. he paid a total fee of 420,000tk to the agency for visa and everything. an addition of 10,000tk was spent for medical check up on their own. Total 3905 USD. 

- a total of 400 workers came in separate groups along with him through the same agency. the clients nephew signed a contract for Orionplus Construction (M) SDN BHD, for the contract he paid 2,000tk in Bangladesh (which is a common practice for signing and getting contract in hand, according to the client). 

- since their arrival in Malaysia they have not been provided with any job yet. they are kept together in groups in a facility on factory site. the agency and Orionplus promised them that between 15th-17th November they will provide them with CIDB card and only after then they can start working. 

- in the beginning they were told that if someone finds work and wishes to leave the place they could, by paying RM1,000-RM1,500 they can take their passport and leave. soon after, they announced and stopped the practice. 

- from 4th October they were given RM50 weekly for food, which is to be deducted from their salary once they start working. 

the client provided a contact number of a representative of Orionplus, (03-4131 9961) and upon request of Issara staff shared the contract of his nephew and one of his friend, who were contacted directly to double check the issues. they shared the same concern, that they have not started working yet and they are worried that they can not start earning money after leaving their country. 

according to the management of the business, since the workers got their training classes to acquire the CIDB card on 4th November 2023, they should be receiving their CIDB card within the next 15 days since the test. but until now they have not received the card nor any work. 

the current updates are the followings:

- the workers has done the CIDB training, but they have not received the physical card yet. 
- online tracking of the card says its in the process of delivery (find it in the issue link along with the contract).
- the Bangladeshi broker who was the focal to bring them here is not answering their calls anymore.

the client is requesting Issara to if possible contact the management and ask when can they start working, because when the victims ask these questions to the management they are not given any answer and are often ignored.

Issara is trying to get the consent from the clients to refer their case to another local organization in Malaysia.

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that April 13-16, 2024 were set as public holidays at the beginning of the year. Line supervisors in the packaging line in the warehouse asked them to work on April 14-16 due to urgent production demands.  When workers refused, the supervisors tried to say let's do a lucky draw then to see who would come to work on those days. When the workers refused that as well, the company unilaterally decided all would work on April 14-16. In addition to being forced to work on these holidays, it is not clear what kind of wages they will receive for those days and whether there would be substitute days off.

TPs:
- When did the company decide to make this holiday change and require workers to work during Songkran? What has led to this sudden change (i.e. unexpected new orders)?

Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter to determine what led to this public holiday change and who made this decision.
- The company should not unilaterally decide to change the public holidays it announced at the beginning of the year. The company should consult and negotiate with the workers and come to a consensus, rather than deciding against the wishes of the workers.
- Communicate the consensus decision clearly to workers, including the wage rates that will be paid and whether substitute holidays will be given and when.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
10 April 2024
KPI 2325 and 2324: Not only the business received this case from us but they also received this case from the interpreter as well. Her name is Moh Moh. The business admitted that the root cause of this case was the poor and unclear communication in the warehouse department. They also admitted that there's an increase in order to the point that they cannot finish the packing in time so they need more workforce during Songkran around 500 workers. After the business got our request for the remediation call, they responded to the issue right away by talking and meeting with the workers in the warehouse department on 1 April 2024. In the meeting, the business communicated this clearly to the workers why they needed more workforce and asked the workers voluntarily who wanted to work during Songkran (14 - 16 April). 250 workers in the warehouse department volunteered to work on 14 - 16 April. The other 250 more workers that the business needs, they also asked voluntarily in other departments too. So now, the workforce problem is resolved. The business got 500 workers to work during Songkran. In terms of the wage and substitute holidays, 14 April is Sunday,so if the workers come to work on 14 April, they'll get double of their daily wage. 15 - 16 April are public holidays, the workers already get the daily wage on public holidays so if they come to work during those days, they'll also get daily wage on top of that. There's no substitute holidays for them but the business will prepare drinks for the workers on those days in return for their good cooperation.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that April 13-16, 2024 were set as public holidays at the beginning of the year but recently they were asked to work during this period due to urgent production demands.  The company made this decision even after the workers voiced that they want to take the holidays as per the announced list of public holidays. Moreover, it is not clear what kind of wages they will receive for working those holidays and whether there would be substitute days off.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- The annual public holiday list that is announced for each year should be changed during the course of the year, and workers should be consulted and agree on any such adjustments.
- Forecast production demands for the whole year to ensure there are not sudden changes that will culminate in such public holiday date changes.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Business does not have policy on payment system, overtime, sick leave, public holidays are not officially posted, and not having HR interpreters hence, no clear communication of policies. 

TPs and recommendation:

-What are the policy and practice of payment system, overtime, sick leave and public holidays?
-Develop Comprehensive Company Policies: Create detailed written policies on key areas such as the payment system, overtime, sick leave, and public holidays. 
-Develop an comprehensive worker manual that includes all company policies and procedures, translated into both Khmer and Burmese.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara has escalated the issue with relevant Strategic Partners after multiple attempts to engage the supplier to discuss worker feedback alleging serious labor issues.  The supplier has been unresponsive. Following escalation with SPs, Issara will now be meeting with RS Cannery to discuss the open cases on 05-Sep-2024.

5-Sep-2024
Business Response #3279
Payslip: 
Even though the payslip is not in the workers’ languages, the business does post the explanation on the information board. Assign the line interpreters to explain to the workers, and especially all the workers got oriented when they first started work with RS Cannery. However, Issara can share the payslip sample with them first for their consideration of adopting the sample, but it is not easy to change the payslip system. 

Sick leave:
RS has a clear policy for requesting sick leave; if workers request the leave less than 3 days, there is not necessarily to show the MC. There are the nurses and clinic in the factory for checking the workers’ health, and they can take leave if they get sick. And the workers can easily request the leave with their line supervisor via LINE. The business has communicated this policy with the workers many times. RS will find out more about this.

No Burmese interpreters despite hundreds of Burmese workers:
RS mentioned that there are interpreters/workers who could speak Thai in each line to support the workers in translation. And RS also has 5 interpreters in the office as well. The business suggests that the workers can easily reach out to their line interpreter for interpretation matters or otherwise contact office interpreters. And if the workers have concerns about how to find interpretation support in the hospital, the SSO hospital “Sikharin” has interpretation support already, so workers don’t need to be worried. 

Public holiday:
RS has 13 public holidays within a year; it has been announced multiple times and posted on the information board and production line as well. The business suggests to workers to have a look.

description: Social Security issue (access to health care): violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation: Context ; The issue with a foreman worker who was attacked by an employee and broke her arm. Building 7, Line 7. Foreman Name - Vilakarn (Victim) who was attacked by a male employee. Accident date; 29 March 2021. Please be noted that the worker did not report to Issara, some of the witnesses have raised the concern regarding the workplace incident where a female worker was attacked by a male worker. Talking Points ; Some workers reported that a Thai female worker from line 7 was attacked by the male worker and broke her arm and that she is going under treatment. And we would like to understand how this case is being handled. In terms of her physical condition, how is the worker doing now? What kind of treatment has she received? Is she working or on sick leave? What are the actions and steps that the business has taken towards the male worker who attacked the female worker? (Note for BHR: if they say the worker was dismissed, then go to the next question, if they say that the worker is on probation or something else, note immediate termination would be expected as appropriate punitive action for basically committing a crime on the production floor) What kind of assistance has the worker received so far from the company? Has the worker received any compensation? If so, from whom (CC, SSF, worker that attacked her?) And how much has she received/ will receive? BHR to check with the business whether the following actions according to the law have been taken or not and if the timeframes of the actions followed the timeframes stipulated in the Workmen’s Compensation Act B.E. 2561. Article 13 which requires the employer to immediately pay the medical expense, Article 15 requires the employer to pay for any required rehabilitation expenses. Article 18 where the employer should pay 70% of wages when the employee is unable to work, with the payment to be made from the first day the employee is unable to work and not exceeding one year. Article 48 notes the employer must notify the govt within 15 days of injury and Article 49 notes the employee may need to submit claims to the govt office. Criminal Code Section 295 (bodily injury) and 391 (attack on other). Anyone’s right who is physically attacked would involve filing police reports and taking a case to court or settling, which would most often involve lawyers and so on. Has this taken place yet?
remediation_business_steps_taken: The business responded that the worker refused to take compensation from the Social Security Fund and have sued the offender by herself. The case is being proceed at the court which has no control over. Issara received this issue from a witness however, have no contact with the direct victim. Therefore, this case is considered to be closed.

remediation_action: The business covered the initial expenses of the hospital costs and the assault victim is on paid sick leave.  The business dismissed the worker that attacked the foreman.  The victim is not claiming social security compensation benefits as she has sued the offender in court.

description: Social Security issue (access to health care): violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that his wife received care at Pi Mem hospital in May 2021 to deliver her baby and also receive treatment for Covid-19 as she tested positive at that time. 
More than a year later in September 2022, he received a call from the hospital saying he owed the hospital a bill for 9,900 Baht for the Covid-19 treatment her wife had received (which totaled 23,000 Baht and Social Security covered some of this cost).  He had already paid 8,000 Baht for the baby delivery fees.  Now, he is wondering why he needs to pay this amount of 9,900 Baht and has asked the business for support. description: Social Security issue (access to health care): violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The factory owner appears to have changed a few months ago, as the workers were asked to sign a sheet about the new employer, and all workers were switched to being piece-rate workers rather than daily workers. The social security contribution is deducted from their pay but no workers cannot access medical services at the hospital under social security coverage. A new mother did not get the social security support of 15,000 THB for delivering her baby. 

TPs:
-Have the workers been provided with the Social Security card?  
-Has the company explained to workers the procedures for workers to access health care (such as which hospital to go to, what documents should be presented when registering at the hospital, etc.)?
-Is the company providing interpretation support for workers?  Are workers not being able to access health services because of the language barrier?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Investigate why workers are not able to access health care under social security coverage.  Identify the root cause and take action to remove the barriers to health care access (i.e. provide workers with the SS card or explain the steps for accessing health care in an easy-to-understand manner or provide the appropriate interpreter support)
-Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, how workers can fully utilize the social security benefits that they are entitled to.  Answer questions that workers might have about how to practically get medical care

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1:
Workers reported having worked at King Pac for one year but had not yet received their Social Security cards and the business has not made social security contributions.

- Investigate the matter and identify for which workers the business has failed to pay monthly social security contributions for, and retroactively make the payments as should have been paid since each worker's hiring date

Case #2:
The worker delivered a baby on 19th April 2023. Name: Ms. SREY BEN
Employee code: 791299

Recommendations:
- Investigate the matter, and identify which documents are missing for this SSO benefit to be paid out to the worker and help the worker to submit the complete papers to SSO.

Case #3 (WV-57145, opened 4-Jun-2023):
A worker from KPI-Plastic Cutting Line started working in King Pac on 24th August 2022 as a walk-in worker. She got a work related injury on 30th May 2023. She got injured while she was doing the bag handle cutting work. On the day she got injured, the business brought her to a clinic near the factory. The client said that she should have been brought to the SSF hospital to get better treatment but she was not brought to the SSF hospital as she doesn't have a valid SSF card. King Pac did not make SSF contributions since she started working in King Pac. Regarding the treatment in the co-operative clinic, she had to use 220 baht from her pocket but the treatment is not good enough. She went for further treatment at a private clinic in the evening and she had to use 1,000 Baht for treatment. - Are all workers covered under the Social Security coverage, with monthly employer and employee contributions paid to the Social Security Office?

- Ensure that all workers have Social Security health coverage and monthly contributions are being properly made to the government 
- Communicate to all workers the Social Security insurance coverage that workers receive, and how they can access health care using this social security health coverage without having to pay out-of-pocket

A worker reported that he needed to get surgery for which he was in the hospital for 15 days, with costs covered by the employer. He said it seems he was discharged at the urging of the employer who wanted him to return to work.  However, his surgical wound has not healed and it seems the stitches are tearing apart. He has also received less than what his monthly salary should be last month, and his passport is being withheld by the employer.

Recommendations:
- Advise the worker to go to the hospital and seek medical attention directly. Also, he should contact the Nepal embassy for assistance.
- Option 1: Issara to contact the employer directly to advise him of his responsibilities that the worker is given the proper medical care and time to fully heal before returning to work and that the costs should be covered by insurance or the employer rather than the worker.  This is of primary concern.  However, there is also the issue of withholding of wages and document retention, which the employer should be advised to correct. This advice may need to be given after the worker has received the proper medical attention first, lest there be a risk that the employer may refuse to support the worker on all counts.
- Option 2: Issara to refer to partner CSOs if such appropriate partners are available

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that since February 7th, 2024, Gimmill announced workers will now only receive 50 RM for their medical checkups. Simply put, if a worker falls ill and visits the hospital's clinic, the company will reimburse them only 50 RM and any additional medical expenses will be the responsibility of the worker. The worker stated that the typical cost of a clinic visit ranges from 80 to 90 RM so this will become a financial burden and this policy is against the terms in their employment contract, which explicitly states that the employer is responsible for medical expenses. The company announced this change during a meeting with the workers. Despite protests from the worker, the company dismissed the objections. 

TPs:
- What are the requirements in terms of buying health insurance for migrant workers? If all workers are to be ensured, why has this policy change been instituted?

Recommendations:
- Any changes in the policy of wages and benefits should not go against what is stated in the employment contract and medical expenses should be covered as part of the insurance scheme, as required by law
- Communicate clearly to all workers about the details of the health insurance coverage and that medical expenses will be covered according to the insurance policy
remediation_notes: Workers reported that since February 7th, 2024, the business announced that workers will now only receive 50 RM for health care visits and any additional medical expenses will be the responsibility of the worker. The workers understand that the employment contract explicitly states that the employer is responsible for medical expenses.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
#Issue 1.
Initiate remediation process: assess workers impacted (those who took sick leave but were not paid); make payments within 2 pay periods.

Issara can assist with communicating effectively to workers in all languages, and also with how to scope impacted workers (if needed).  Issara will verify completion of actions through worker voice/worker surveys.

----------
(4-July). 
As per workers update after the business announcement on sick leave remediation.

-Check with the business how many workers have already received their money back. 
-Suggest the business to check the sick leave records for the past 6 months to properly remediate the impacted workers. (Internal note: Depending on the information the business find different timeframes and strategies can be recommended)
-If the business does not have proper recording system for the sick leave, Issara can help to identify the impacted workers. 

Within 2 pay periods.

#Issue 2. (September 29). 
"Impacted workers should received their money back for the days that they took leave and did not get paid. 

Context:
Workers reported that they have been impacted for many years because line supervisors would request medical certificates even for 1 day of leave. According to workers, if they didn't have an MC the line supervisor would mark the sick leave as absent, thus workers wouldn't get paid. The challenges for this case is that there is probably no documentation that can be revised to identify all impacted workers, and workers might not remember all days when they were sick, did have an MC and didn't get paid. 

Next steps: talk with the business to understand better their record system, what kind of documents they have that can be reviewed, and start discussions on remediation. Some of the recommendations that can be given to the business to create a plan of remediation are i) inform all worker that if they have been impacted by this issue they can approach HR for the business to investigate and provide the right payment ii) for the business to conduct a survey to assess the number of impacted workers and compensate them, iii) for the business to propose another way to identify impacted workers and compensate them based on their system to record sick leave or any other records (and Issara to provide feedback on what is proposed by the business iv) Issara to conduct a survey to assess the number of impacted workers and develop a plan with the employer to compensate workers.


Discuss with Issara management: How far back would/should remediation calculations be done?

Talking points for July 8: 

_Provide the workers feedback that issara has talk with several workers via hotline call and social media channels and learnt that some workers are not feeling comfortable to reach out to the business to claim their rights, Some said that they do not exactly remember the date that they took sick leave, Some said that they have not taken any sick leave so far, Other workers said they used their annual leave for their sick days and some said that the business might have record in their system. 

-Provide recommendations for the system review and proper remediation.

The business did write an announcement on the sick leave policy and put it on board. However, the business has not done a verbal announcement yet so that the workers are not aware of it.

4-July

2 Nov 2020 
For the sick leave and MC issue, the business updated that they had communicated the sick leave policy to all line supervisors. The business also wanted to have more information about the line supervisor who does not follow the business policy. The business suggest Issara encourage the workers to reach out the HR if they are impacted 
 

Issara has had to monitor this issue for several weeks, as Issara has not received additional reports from the workers, this issue is considered to be close at this point.
remediation_business_steps_remaining:
4-July 
The business did not really go into detail investigation for the remediation.
remediation_notes:
Issue: Workers report being required to show a medical certificate for taking sick leave for less than 3 days, in violation of Thai Labor Law and Ladybird policy. Workers also report not being allowed to go home when sick or after being involved in an accident, and feeling pressured to go back to work after visiting the nurse at the clinic.

Actions: Issara has held several meetings with Ladybird on this issue. Ladybird has communicated with  workers to encourage impacted workers to reach out to the HR. Workers, however, are not comfortable approaching HR. Therefore, Issara suggested the business be more proactive and ensure legal compliance by reimbursing all impacted workers by paying back one day of daily wage or return one annual leave day for each instance, based on their records.

Context: Workers who are wanting to leave and want to have a proper job cancelation letter when they leave. The reason they want to leave the job from Ladybird is because of a heavy workload, discriminations against nationalities, unsafe grievance mechanisms to report their issues, unavailable translation service whenever is needed. 

Please see the recommendations for the system change.  

Talking Points;
-Several workers have expressed their challenges with supervisors which lead them to resign from their job, what is the business understanding of these challenges?
remediation_business_steps_taken: Please refer to the system change.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations; 
-To have open discussion sessions between  HR and workers to understand better what are the challenges being faced by workers and what is driving them to resign. During these discussions, the business is encouraged to share with workers what the business actions are to address these issues.
-The business could also conduct an internal survey to learn why workers want to resign and what can help them remain in Ladybird. Issara can help with the survey questionnaire. Surveys should be conducted in a confidential way where workers feel safe to share the issues that they are facing. 
-The business shall work on a plan to address the issues that are raised in the survey by the workers. 
-The business shall provide training to all supervisors including translators.
-The business shall revise the grievance channels that are meant for workers to raise their issues. The revision should focus on workers' confidentiality and the no retaliation policy. Workers have expressed their concern about raising issues with HR, out of fear of retaliation from their supervisors, therefore it is strongly recommended for the business to reinforce a no retaliation policy and make sure all supervisors are aware of the policy, follow it and face consequences if they commit any actions against such policy.

With the simplified process, the workers will not have to deal with the supervisors to request the leaves which will minimize the issue and reduce the burden of the workers. Since then Issara has not heard any update from the workers. In addition to that, the business is also temporarily closed due to the nearby factory explosion and uncertain opening date. Since Issara has not heard more complaints from the workers, Issara is closing this issue at this point.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that on October 10th, they had received two announcements, one of which was that when asking for sick leave, a worker can inform his/her supervisor by phone for one day but if it is longer than that, the worker must present a Medical Certificate in order to get paid for that day.

-Is HR aware that this announcement was made to workers?

-Refresh the knowledge of supervisors or others that made this announcement, so that the correct policy according to the law is communicated to workers

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue # 1. (CLOSED) 
KPI Description: issues with annual leave
Context: Annual leave allowance (6 days) of all workers was deducted during the New Year Holiday in January 2020. Workers should have received paid holiday leave, as per Thai labor law. Workers reported feeling pressured to sign - there was no voluntary process of consent, though Cal-Comp reports that they did receive full consent. Many workers have confirmed that they have no personal leave left for the remainder of 2020 as a result.

- Suggested remediation: the 6 days of annual leave should be reinstated in the balances of all impacted workers’ annual leave. (CLOSED) 

Issue # 2.  (MONITORING)
Context: workers reported being asked to present a medical certificate for less than 3 consecutive days of sick leave.

-Suggested remediation: assess the number of impacted workers and pay them the amounts they are owed (those who took sick leave but were not paid); make payments within 2 pay periods. Issara can assist with communicating effectively to workers in all languages, and also with how to scope impacted workers (if needed).  Issara will verify the completion of actions through worker voice/worker surveys.

Issue #3 (Dec 13, 2020)
As it is the end of the year workers want to use their annual leave but when they check the system by scanning their card, the system says that they have no annual or sick leave left. Workers added that they have not used them. This issue needs immediate action since this is the end of the year. Workers added that when they reach out to the leader about their missing leaves, leaders asked to check with the foreman and then the foreman asked the worker to go to HR at building 6 which is very far and workers do not know who to contact at the HR office. Therefore, workers do not use business grievance. 


Issue #4
Supervisors from Building 7 Line 7 and 8 do not approve workers' leaves. They added that the supervisors only approve the leave to those who get along with them. 


Recommendations:
-The business to conduct an immediate investigation, with safeguards to avoid retaliation towards workers.
-Leave days for workers that have no leaves left in the system but confirm that they have not used them should be reinstated to the workers.
-Line supervisors that have not been approving leave for workers should be disciplined.  If these supervisors are the same ones that previously did not approve sick leave and other leave for workers as requested (see Nov 26 and Oct 4 issues above), then next level disciplinary measures should be taken.

Issue # 5. (28-Dec-2020.)

The issue with an annual leave being deducted for the new year holiday on 30-Dec-2020. Workers reported being forced to sign a consent form by the leader. Leaders said that they will not receive a daily wage if they do not sign the form. Therefore, all workers had to sign the form.

-The business is suggested to conduct an anonymous survey to be able to understand the voluntary nature of the form and if any worker felt coerced to sign the document to take leave. Or the business could also conduct an investigation by talking with workers in an open discussion where workers can safely and freely shared their experience. The survey/investigation purpose is also to identify which line supervisors might have coerced/forced workers to sign the form. Safeguards and guarantee of no retaliation should be in place. 

-Issara can help to create short questions and also help with the survey as needed.  
-The business to take action based on the result of the survey. Actions would include i) restate the annual leave for those how were forced to used their annual leave in Dec 30th, and ii) to take disciplinary actions towards those supervisors that forced/coerced workers to sign. 

Talking points.
-How does the business make sure that the consent process is voluntary? 
-If the consent was voluntary, how many workers refused to work for that day?

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
480: Annual Leave: Both factory 10 and 11 workers reported that the business forced the workers to use the annual leave when the production line had low production or no raw materials. 

Talking points:
- What has been the company’s production levels this year?
- What does the company do when there is not enough production demand and there is insufficient work for workers on some days?

Recommendations for remediation:
- Investigate when workers were forced to use their annual leave for days when the factory had lack of work for workers
- Workers should be able to choose when they will use their annual leave days.  At the very least, the business should consult workers and get their consent for any annual leave days to be used.
- Return the annual leave days to impacted workers
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Piyabutr, CSR: Building 11 has not yet started a production line, but it is in the process of doing so. Building 10 hasn't had much OT recently. There was also no announcement of annual leave for insufficient work. He mentioned that the LPA allows the employer to arrange leave for employees.
K.Pick: Based on the LPA, we understand well, but we need to obtain worker agreement and consent to use their annual leave. There is a problem if the employee does not agree. Employees should request their annual leave on their own. He, on the other hand, will look into the matter and get back to Issara. Is there any worker agreement? etc.


Workers have options, they can choose whether or not to use their annual leave, and if they do not, they can ask their supervisors to work at the other departments (production lines).
remediation_notes: Both Factory 10 and 11 workers reported that the business forced the workers to use the annual leave when the production line had low production or no raw materials.

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
During the recruitment fee survey, a worker raised an issue about the annual leave. 
He said trying to use his annual leave days was very difficult even if it was mentioned on the pay slip that he has 6 days annual leave days. When he requests the leave from line supervisor or manager, they said he could use his annual leave days only if he worked during the public holidays without payment. Workers that agreed to work on public holidays were allowed to use annual leave days later.

In the C.OH line there are almost 300 workers. And specifically, the C line there is around 200 workers and the OH line there is around 100 workers. The line C and OH are under one department that's why it is called C.OH. The worker also mentioned this policy does not apply to all production lines but in Line C.OH, it is like that. Workers request to raise the issue generally but not specify the working line if possible.

TPs:
-What is the company's policy and process for approving annual leave for workers?
-Is HR aware that line supervisors are saying unless workers volunteer to work on a public holiday without pay, they cannot get approval to use their annual leave days?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Conduct an investigation to find out why workers are being made to work for free on public holidays just so they can get approvals to use their annual leave days
-If workers have worked on public holidays and not been paid, reimburse the workers immediately
-If line supervisors have been found to make workers to work for free on public holidays just so that they can get to use their annual leave, those supervisors should be disciplined according to the company's disciplinary policy
-Communicate verbally and in writing that workers can request annual leave as needed and this is not conditional on working on public holidays without pay.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Panida, HR, shared the findings of the investigation, which revealed that workers from production line C and OH and DE were chosen at random interviewed about the issue. It turns out that the workers claimed that no such incident occurred.

They had a meeting with the supervisors about the issue. Even so, the supervisor confirmed that there was no incident. However, HR trained the supervisors on the company's leave policy. This includes instructing and publicizing the supervisors on the production line in order to prevent such incidents from occurring.

Please see the photos of the the interview and training.
https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1zhf38B7UVrdswKxC86mVMlbNIs0A4Hco
remediation_notes: A worker report that he tried to use his annual leave days was very difficult even if it was mentioned on the pay slip that he has 6 days annual leave days. When he requests the leave from line supervisor or manager, they said he could use his annual leave days only if he worked during the public holidays without payment. Workers that agreed to work on public holidays were allowed to use annual leave days later.  This seems to be what's happening to workers in the production line where he is working.
remediation_action: HR shared the investigation results, which revealed that workers claimed that no such incident occurred.  The supervisors also replied that such instances did not occur.  Still, HR trained the supervisors on the company's leave policy.

Workers wanted to use their annual leave when they needed to, especially for urgent matters.
remediation_action:
Issara reached out to the business, and HR investigated this case.  The management interprets Section 30 of the Labor Protection Act as follows: "..the Employer is obliged to fix the Holiday in advance for the Employee...or as agreed by the Employer and Employee." So, according to company policy, the company is obliged to plan the annual leave (holiday) for its employees in advance. The company informs employees one month in advance that they will be on leave.

Issara has recommended that Section 30 be interpreted as the employer fixing the number of holidays but not to decide when the employee will choose to take those holidays.  At the very least, there should be agreement between the employer and employee because in this case, the employees do not agree with the business unilaterally deciding when the workers will use their annual leave days.  HR responded that management may review the policy in mid-September to consider and revise it.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change
Revise the company policy on extended holiday breaks for factory-wide closures, and make it optional for workers as to whether they want to use annual leave for the additional days or whether they want to work during those days.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
# Case (1) Issue with sick leave being denied: this refers to the worker that requested sick leave, but it was denied by the line supervisor and then the worker passed away. 

-Suggested remediation: 
assess workers impacted (those who took sick leave but were not paid); make payments within 2 pay periods. Issara can assist with communicating effectively to workers in all languages, and also with how to scope impacted workers (if needed).  Issara will verify the completion of actions through worker voice/worker surveys.
In order to identify impacted workers one or more of the following actions are recommended: 
1. the business can conduct a survey to assess the number of impacted workers and compensate for them. 
2.the business can propose other ways to identify impacted workers and compensate them based on their system to record sick leave or any other records (and Issara to provide feedback on what is proposed by the business)
3. the business can make official announcements verbally and in written to all impacted workers to approach HR for investigation and compensation 
4. Issara to conduct a survey to assess the number of impacted workers and develop a plan with the employer to compensate workers. Issara can provide the training to the line supervisors and HR if needed.

In addition to the identification of impacted workers, it is recommended for the business to investigate who (from line supervisors and/or HR staff) is not following the company policies and take actions accordingly.
The business should conduct an investigation and take disciplinary actions against the line supervisor that did denied the worker request to take sick leave.

# Case (2). The issue with the missing sick leave payment due to the fact that the HR losing the workers's sick leave request documents. Call ID- 9149, 9503

1) The business to investigate how the documents were handled, who is responsible for the sick leave request approval and payment, and pay the worker the money she is owed.
2) Disciplinary action should be taken for the person who misplaced the worker's sick leave documents and did not process the correct payment for the worker. 
3) The worker should receive her payment in the next payment period.

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context case 1: Worker reports: Unpaid 2 days lay-off. 
This was the issue with the New Year holiday when the factory closed for 6 days, 4 days were paid as holiday and the other 2 days were deducted from workers' annual leave or business leave. New MOU workers reported that they did not get paid for those 2 days. 

-Those days of annual leave and business leave should be reinstated in the balances of workers’ annual leave; leave forcibly taken should be noted as paid holiday leave. A verbal and written announcement with the remediation plan should be provided to all workers. 

-New workers who did not have annual leave should be paid for those days and noted as paid holiday leave. 

Talking points. 


Workers reported that the business closed 6 days for New Year Holiday but 4 days were paid and 2 days
were deducted from the workers’ annual leave or marked as unpaid leave. This issue was escalated to the supplier senior leadership as per agreed escalation arrangements. He agreed to consider returning annual leave to affected workers on a case-by-case basis and encouraged workers to report this to HR. However, the business has not sent out the announcement to the workers regarding this remediation.

timeframe 1-2 payment periods

Business 
(20-Aug)The business responded that they have communicated with the workers and encouraged them to reach out to the HR office for the remediation. However, the business added not having any workers approaching HR for the remediation. 


Workers.

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the COVID vaccinations side effect. Workers reported not receiving medical certificates from the in-house medical staff to be paid for sick leave when they have vaccine side effects and wanted to take rest. 

Recommendations: 
-The business shall communicate with all workers including medical staff about the potential side effects those receiving the vaccine might experience in the next few days after getting the shot. The communication should inform workers that those experiencing some side effect symptoms that would not enable them to work properly can take medical leave according to the business procedure of informing the focal person about their leave. 
-Workers who took sick leave and were being asked to present a medical certificate issued by the medical staff should be reimbursed and paid according to the sick leave section from LPA. 
-To avoid impacts on production due to many workers from the same line taking sick leave, the business could rearrange the schedules for different groups of workers getting the vaccine, for instance, instead of doing it by production lines, it could be by batches from workers from different lines.  


Talking Points 
-How many workers have been vaccinated so far? 
-How has the business communicated with the workers about the common side effects that those receiving the vaccine might experience and what is the process to take sick leave? 
-How many workers have been approved for sick leave after the vaccinations? 
-Has the in-house medical staff received any communication about the vaccine side effect that the workers could face? If yes, what was the communication?
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have communicated with all workers about the post-vaccination process. The business added that once a worker is vaccinated, she or he will be checked by the nurse to make sure the workers are safe to get back to work. In case of a worker has side effects during their work in the production, they have to reach out to the Nurse so that the nurse can approve their symptoms and the medical certificate, the business argued that the workers who have reported Issara might be the ones who did not reach out to the nurse according to the business policy. Issara is checking with the workers.

Issara additionally raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they did not receive notification from the worker informing about his sickness, which contrast the worker report. However, the business agreed to check with the worker and confirm his sickness and reimburse the wages.

The business has updated Issara they have been working on the investigation process and will reimburse the worker's wage in October payroll.
remediation_notes: A Worker reported experiencing side effects after receiving the Covid-19 vaccine but did not receive medical certificates from the in-house medical staff to take sick leave and was not paid for those days.
remediation_action: The business said that once a worker is vaccinated, she or he will be checked by the nurse to make sure the workers are fit to get back to work. The business responded that they did not receive such request for sick leave from any workers, which contrasts with the workers' report. However, the business agreed to check with the workers to confirm the sickness and reimburse the wages accordingly.
remediation_validation: The business is in the process of investigation; we will get an update from the worker once he has been reimbursed.

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers having issues with taking leave for more than 3 consecutive days.  If the worker takes consecutive leave for three days or more, the manager asks the worker to sign in a book, with the worker promising not to take any additional leave in the next month or sometimes three months.

NOTE: Only three workers recently faced this issue and so the caller is very scared that she and the others will be targeted.  Issara needs to discuss this issue with the business in a way that will not negatively affect these workers. 

Talking points:
What is the company’s process for workers to request annual leave?  
Are there any limitations or restrictions on when workers can take annual leave?

Recommendations for remediation:
Review the process for approving annual leave for workers and any limitations placed on granting annual leave.  Workers should not be required to sign any documents about when workers won’t request annual leave
Investigate the matter and if any approver (manager or line supervisor) is not implementing the company policy and forcing workers to sign a document promising he/she won’t take any more leave for the next 1-3 months, take appropriate disciplinary measures and retrain the approver on the proper process to be followed 
Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, the process for requesting and being approved for when to take annual leave
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Narumon, HR, responded that, according to the leave policy, the production manager must track and record the workers' absences, but If a worker takes three days of consecutive leave, the manager simply asks why and makes no commitment that the worker will not take any other leave within a month or sometimes three months. And she's the one who double-checks the tracking and found no statement about it. However, there were a few infected workers in this case, and the workers should be targeted. HR will carefully consider taking action. She will create an action plan and send it to us within the next week.



Meeting with supervisor and division manager on July 8, 2022, to discuss rights and leave obligations and make sure that the entire management team of factory2 are aware of them and acting appropriately.

Provide the Sit on Site project, which has been in progress since July 1, 2022. The Employee Retention supervisor will observe and collaborate closely with production manager on labour management at the production office of factory 2 so that they can effectively listen to complaint and handle the grievance mechanism.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:

Conduct the worker satisfaction survey (WSS); Issara can conduct this survey together with the recruitment fee survey

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that Seafresh announced that starting on January 28, there will be more days when the factory shuts down due to no production, and has decided workers will use their annual leave for these days. The workers are not happy about this and would rather get paid 75% of wages if the employer cannot provide a regular job. The workers are pushed to use annual leave, and new workers will need to borrow annual leave from next year to use now.

Recommendations:
- The business should allow workers to choose when to use annual leave and at least get workers' agreement if the business is going to propose specific dates that workers should use their annual leave
remediation_notes: Workers reported that Seafresh announced that starting on January 28, there will be more days when the factory shuts down due to no production, and has decided workers will use their annual leave for these days. The workers are not happy about this and would rather get paid 75% of wages if the employer cannot provide a regular job. The workers are pushed to use annual leave, and new workers will need to borrow annual leave from next year to use now.
remediation_action:
Issara raised this with Seafresh, and the business HR stated that Seafresh is currently experiencing problems with low customer orders and a lack of raw materials. They are attempting to get all employees paid, so this announcement applies to all employees in Seafresh (all staff and all workers), and they have decided when workers will use those 6 annual leave days. Furthermore, according to the LPA. HR also noted that the Labor Protection Act allows the employer to fix holidays in advance for the employee.

Issara escalated this issue to the Managing Director.  The MD noted that production at Seafresh is currently only at 50-60% and so the business will have to reduce the production days.  It’s a difficult time for the company and it’s requesting the workers that they use annual leave so that at least they can get 100% pay rather than just 75%. Seafresh is mindful that they pay workers fully because cost of living has increased and they don't want workers to have money issues (they even increased wages for workers by 5% in Oct 2022). Usually, Seafresh will allow workers to choose when they would like to take annual leave and will in most cases approve their leave requests.  But this is a special year and the company has decided to prioritize workers getting full pay and have asked the workers to use annual leave days when the factory has no production.  If there are more days of no production after annual leave days are used up, then Seafresh will use 75% compensation pay for those days. Seafresh will meet with workers to explain why the business is doing this and hear from them as well, informally surveying their preferences.

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with sick leave. Workers from the PR line reported that the business has recently posted an announcement that says that if a worker takes sick leave on Monday or Saturday, it will be marked as unpaid leave. In addition, the worker added that some workers' photos have been posted in front of the production line, and he heard that it was the photos of those who took sick leave frequently. 

Recommendations for the remediation.
-The business should immediately cease the practice of not allowing workers to take sick leaves on Monday and Saturday
-The business should investigate why sick leave on Monday or Saturday is being considered unpaid leave, and how many workers have been affected so far.
-During the investigation process, the business should make sure workers share their perspectives and that no workers are targeted for having participated in the investigation. To make sure that no workers are targeted, the business should communicate with the reported Line supervisor about the business' no retaliation policy and workers right to take sick leave as required. 
-The business should clearly communicate to all workers about its sick leave policy and that workers are entitled to sick leave when they are ill, regardless of what day this might be
-The business should check its HR records and identify any workers that had taken sick leave were docked pay and considered unpaid leave.  Those workers should be paid back for those day’s wages.

K. Juthamas, HR, explained that production considers workers who are on sick leave or taking business leave because they care about the worker's ability to work more than 8 hours per day. remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Workers reported their annual leaves being used by the business for quarantine days if workers were found positive or at high risk from COVID. 

Talking Points; 

Workers have reported their annual leave being used for the quarantine days, could the business explain what is the current practice for this issue? 
How many workers are in this situation and what has been the process for them so far? How many days of quarantine are required for close contact and positive cases? Who pays for those quarantine days? 
Has the business checked the government regulations on what Covid-related care services are to be covered by the business and/or SSO and whether and how quarantine days for Covid close contacts are to be paid?  

Recommendations:
The business should confirm the latest government regulations related to quarantine periods for Covid close contacts and how pay for missed working days due to quarantine is to be handled We have received the update that the government regulations are as follows:  If a worker is found to be positive at the factory, she/he is supposed to be sent to the hospital for the PCR test and if confirmed as positive, receive the medical certificate and recommended to quarantine. The worker should get paid sick leave during those days. 
If a worker is in close contact, s/he should visit the hospital and report why she/he is at high risk and get the recommendations from the hospital. The regular recommendation for vaccinated people is to take 10 days of quarantine and do another test on the 10th day. 
If the result is negative, then the worker can start working. In terms of the wages for the high-risk workers who have a medical certificate for their quarantine days, the employer can submit the worker information to the SSF for 62% of wages. 
If the worker is not allowed to go to the hospital but the employer orders the worker to take quarantine, it is the responsibility of the employer to pay the worker wages. 
The business should communicate with the workers about how to quarantine days for close contacts and positive workers will be paid. 

Time Frame; 1 week.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
TUM explained that the business policy is as follows.  For close contacts (living in close quarters with Covid-positive persons) and Covid infected workers: TUM will use 2 annual leave days first, then 3 business leave days second, and then to use sick leave for the remainder.  The business made it a point to say that the workers will receive full wages during the quarantine period, including their incentives and bonus pay.  This is applied to all nationalities.  Used to be 14 quarantine days; this year, it’s 7 quarantine days, and then ATK before returning to work for close contact cases.  For Covid-positive workers, it’s 10 quarantine days; after 7 days ATK, and then on the 10th day.  The business provides a separate quarantine area for such workers.  For quarantine days, no MC is required.
This policy has been communicated to all workers.

The business noted that their current policy pays the workers fully including incentive pay for all quarantine days whereas the government policy allows for 62% of wages from SSF for close contact cases.

TUM to make the public announcement again about this policy next week.  TUM will send the written policy in three languages to Issara as well.  TUM will consider with management whether they can be flexible with the Covid quarantine policy, to accommodate requests from workers that wish to use their annual leave at another time and not be required to use annual leave for quarantine days.
remediation_notes:
Workers reported their annual leave days were being used by the business for quarantine days if workers were found to be positive or at high risk to COVID-19.

The latest Thai government regulations regarding Covid-19 measures are as follows: 
- If a worker is found to be Covid-positive at the factory, she/he is to be sent to the hospital for the RT-PCR test and if confirmed as positive, receive a medical certificate and recommended to quarantine. The worker should get paid sick leave during those days. 
- If a worker is comes in close contact with a Covid-infected person and is a "high risk", s/he should visit the hospital and report why she/he is at high risk and get the recommendations from the hospital. The regular recommendation for vaccinated people is to take 10 days of quarantine and do another test on the 10th day. If the test result is negative, then the worker can resume working. In terms of the wages for the high-risk workers who have a medical certificate for their quarantine days, the employer can submit the worker information to the Social Security Office to receive 62% of wages. 
- If the worker is not allowed to go to the hospital but the employer orders the worker to quarantine, it is the responsibility of the employer to pay the worker's wages.
remediation_action:

For close contacts (living in close quarters with Covid-positive persons) and Covid infected workers: TUM will use 2 annual leave days first, then 3 business leave days second, and then to use sick leave for the remainder. remediation_issara_recommendation:
4-Jan-2020

The issue with the workers being deducted 4 of their annual leaves by the business for the new year (2), Chinese new year (1), and Songkran (1). This is for the year 2020. The business does not ask for any consent. This is set by the business without asking for the worker's consent. The reason that the workers shared the issue now is that they do not want this issue to be continued in 2021. 


Talking points:
-Ask the business what is their policy about annual leave to check what is their understanding of LPA Section 30. 
-Ask the business how was workers annual leave from last year handled. Ask if the business asked workers consent to allocate the annual leave on specific dates.  1) If the business says that they did not ask for consent because their interpretation of the law is that they can allocate annual leave, please explain to the business the actual interpretation of the law and the nature of the Labour Protection Act. 2) If the company says that they asked workers consent and that it was voluntary, shared with the business the conflicting information coming from WV channels where workers reported not being aware of the allocation of annual leave, thus the process was not voluntary. 

Remediation recommendations:
-The business should restate workers annual leave if the decision of using annual leave during those days was not voluntary. This means that, all workers should receive 4 days of annual leave back. 
-Workers should are entitled of 6 days of annual leave per year, and they can request to the employer when they would like to use it, and the business shall approve the days requested by the worker. But the business is not entitled to allocate workers annual leave. 

-In order to avoid misunderstanding regarding public holidays and business closure dates, it is recommended for the business to share the 13 public holidays for the years of 2021 with all workers and Issara. 

LPA; Section 30.An employee who has worked for an uninterrupted period of one year, is entitled to annual holidays of not less than six working days in one year, to be determined by the employer in advance for the employee or as agreed by the employer and employee.  In the following year, the employer may determine annual holidays exceeding six working days for the employee.  The employer and the employee may agree in advance to accumulate and carry forward any unused annual holiday to be included in the following year.  For the employee who has not completed one year of service, the employer may set annual holidays for the employee on a pro rata basis. 
The Employer and the Employee may agree in advance to accumulate and postpone any annual Holiday that has not yet been taken in a year to be included in the following years. For the Employee who has not completed one year of service, the Employer may set annual Holidays for the Employee on a pro-rata basis.

Time Frame ; 2 weeks.

interpretation of the word “or”. The
the fundamental underlying issue, however, is if an employer selecting a worker's annual leave is ethical and meets international standards and global buyer’s supplier requirements/expectations - not just if it is legal under Thai labor law or not.

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; The issue with two repeatedly reported supervisors in the respective production lines. Supervisors are reported being verbally abusive, discriminative, and providing preferences towards Thai workers only, complaining to Burmese workers for any request they make. Supervisor name P'Lei, in Line no. 110. and P'Bua, in Line no. 405. 

Previously Provided Recommendations; -The business to conduct an investigation with this specific supervisor. In order to assess the behavior of the supervisors, the business can conduct a survey where workers can rate their supervisors confidentially. Given that workers may not know their supervisors' Thai names, it is recommended that the business arrange an org-chart with all supervisors' names and titles. -There should not be any coercion or retaliation towards workers during the investigation and survey processes. The investigation process must be confidential, workers should not be needing to provide any of their personal information, such as working IDs, their names, etc. 

-The business should create a plan of action based on the results of investigations and surveys. Such actions should include training and disciplinary actions (if necessary). -To communicate to workers the actions the business is taking to respond to workers' grievances, would help the business to strengthen the trust of workers in the business grievance mechanism. Business actions for the previous report; -The business conducted an investigation, then took disciplinary actions towards the line supervisor and provided training on fair and ethical treatment of workers. 


-The business didn't share the details of the investigation with Issara. Recommendations that are missing to follow by the business. NOTE FOR BHR; Please suggest the business follow the following missing recommendations. - Recommend the business to take disciplinary actions towards these supervisors following the company protocol. Since this is the second time these supervisors are reported, please ask the company what would be the appropriate disciplinary actions in this case? Is it a written warning? - Workers reported that the previous actions taken by the business helped improve the situation for a while, but now the supervisors are having abusive behaviors again. For this reason, it is recommended for the business to have a monitoring plan where they can hear from workers directly what the situation is and if further actions are needed. 


-The monitoring plan could be done by creating safe spaces for workers to share their feedback (e.g. morning talks) or the company could also conduct a confidential survey with all workers under these two supervisors. There should not be any coercion or retaliation towards workers during the investigation, open dialogue sessions, and survey processes. The investigation process must be confidential, workers should not be needing to provide any of their personal information, such as working IDs, their names, etc. and workers should receive an explanation of the no retaliation policy that would guarantee safeguards. 


-To work on a plan of actions based on the result of the survey/investigation/dialogue with workers. -To communicate to workers the actions the business is taking to respond to workers' grievances, would help the business to strengthen the trust of workers in the business grievance mechanism. Talking Points. -What is the business action for such repeated issues? -Please propose to the business that Issara is happy to provide training to all supervisors and HR after the business investigation. timeframe 1 pay period

Issue #2 (29-Jul-2021) 

Context: The issue with the workers' annual leave being deducted for the days that the business did not run as it was preparing for a quarantine center in the factory. Workers added that the business deducted their two days of annual leaves (6-7 Jul-2021).

Recommendations. 
-The business should reinstate workers' annual leaves and use the medical leave or COVID-19 special leave instead for those two days. 
- The business is recommended to use any of those leaves (medical or special leave) as both are applicable for COVID -19 since it is a health-related issue. 
- The LPA is a law that protects the rights of workers, including the right to have rest during annual leave days, which means the worker being able to consult with the employer about when the worker would take annual leave, and at a time that is most beneficial to the worker. For this reason, annual leave shall not be allocated by the employers without workers' consent. 
-For this case, workers were not consulted in advance about getting their annual leave days used up for the factory shut down for preparation of setting up the quarantine center. For these reasons, the business shall reinstate workers; annual leave and use sick leave/special leave instead for those two days.  

Talking points. 

-Workers reported not being asked for their consent about the deduction of their annual leaves, is the business aware of this? If yes, what was the understanding of the business about workers' annual leaves?

Within two weeks.

supplier_name: Hi-Tech Chaiyaphum Apparel Co., Ltd. (Na Siao)
description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with sick leave. Workers reported being followed by the business when workers take sick leave. If workers take sick leave, the business sends its staff to check workers status. In that situation, the workers feel pressured by the business for taking sick leave. In addition to that, workers also feel pressured when they take sick leave for more than 2 days because the business makes a phone call and puts pressure towards the workers and explains how the business could be impacted if workers take longer leave. Apart from that, the workers also added not being assisted by the business to access their SSF benefits, as the SSF hospital is far from the company and the business does not provide transportation . In that case, workers reported having to pay their own money for their health purpose. This is happening in the lines 21,22,23,24,25,26,27.

Recommendations for the remediation.
-The business shall conduct a wide range of investigations to assess the issue with workers' sick leave and also to assess the number of impacted workers. The investigation should include workers' voices. 
-During the investigation process, the business should make sure that no workers are being targeted by the supervisors. To make sure that no workers are targeted, the business should communicate with the reported supervisor about the business' no retaliation policy and workers rights to have full rest without any corciotion and pressure when they are sick. 
-The business clearly communicates with the workers what their plan will be for this issue.
-The business should look back to their system and make sure that workers are properly paid during their leaves. 
-The business should immediately cease the practice of visiting sick workers without their request. Workers have the right to take 30 days of sick leave annually, and the business may ask for proof of the sickness only if the sick days are more than 3 consecutive days. This is according to the LPA, therefore, the company policy should be aligned with the law, and this should be communicated to all employees, including supervisors. The business should make a clear announcement that visiting a sick person against their will is a violation of the basic human rights, and rights of privacy of a patient. 

-All workers should be introduced to the business grievance mechanism channels and encouraged to use any channel (internal or external as Issara) that they feel comfortable using. . 
-The business shall clearly communicate with the workers about their rights to access their SSF in case they are sick and want to see a doctor. The business should assist the workers with the transportation and the translation if workers want to visit the SSF hospital, or find a closer hospital where the company can register workers through SSF so that they can easily access the service. 
-When communicating business channels with all employees, the business should also explain how workers’ grievances are managed and how safeguards are kept for the workers.

Talking Points:
-What is the process for taking sick leave for workers? 
-Workers reported being visited by the factory staff when they are sick, what is the business understanding of this? 
-Is there any focal person to assist the workers when they are sick and want to visit SSF hospital? If yes, has the business introduced this person to the workers? 
-How many workers are there in each production line? 

Thai Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998), Section 57: Paid Sick Leave
Description: An Employer shall pay Wages to an Employee for sick leave under Section 32 equivalent to Wages of a Working Day throughout the Leave period, but not exceeding 30 Working Days per year. Whereas an Employee takes Leave for sterilization under Section 33, the Employer shall pay Wages to the Employee for such Leave.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that the reason they visit the workers when they are sick for more than 2 days because to make sure that they have enough medicines and treatment. For the issue with the transportation to the hospital when workers are sick, the business responded having policy to assist the workers with the translation upon request. 
The business agreed to conduct the communication in written post within one week.
remediation_notes:
Workers reported being pressured to not take sick leave.  When taking sick leave, HR staff would visit and check on them, and when taking more than two consecutive sick days, they would receive calls from HR telling them how the business will be negatively impacted if they are away for a long time.   

In addition, the workers noted that the hospital is far from their workplace but the business doesn't arrange for transportation to access health care, leading to the workers having to pay out of their own pockets to access medical care.
remediation_validation: Issara will follow up with the workers after the business has taken corrective action
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-All of the line supervisors, production staff and the workers should be clearly communicated in written and verbal about the business plan to solve this issue. All relevant staff should be clearly communicated about the business’s policy related to  sick leave and employee right to access it. The communication should include the disciplinary action that will be taken towards the staff who againsts the business policy. 
-Recommend Issara Academy training to HR staff and line supervisor. 
-Issara can also provide tailored training to full HR teams on-site, and provide systems review with tailored recommendations to eliminate labour risks.

- What is the business policy about getting approval for sick leave? If a worker doesn't inform his supervisor about sick leave, will the business withhold payment for that day?

- The business should allow workers multiple channels to inform the business when they are sick and will be absent from work.  Communicate this clearly to workers, verbally and in writing.
