remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue # 1. Not getting sick leave when needed. The supervisor does not approve their leaves so they have to work while they are sick. This happens to most of the workers in different buildings. 

Issue # 2. Not getting annual leave approved.  Workers said that they received a number of annual leaves every year, however, their supervisors do not approve them when they want to use them. Only local workers can use it anytime they want but not for foreign workers.

Talking Points; 
What is the process for taking sick leave and annual leaves?
 How often is the business policy being communicated to the workers about their rights and the internal process for workers and the line leaders to follow? 
How does the business make sure workers have access to their rights when they are sick or when they want to take annual leave?

Recommendations 
The business shall create communication about the sick and annual leave policy in writing and post it on the announcement board where most of the workers can see it and reference it. In addition to that, the business should also communicate with all of the workers and the line leaders, and production managers, to make sure that every staff member understands the business policy with regard to sick and annual leaves. 
The communication should also clearly mention the business disciplinary action to those who do not follow the company policy. 
All workers should be able to take sick leave based on the business policy when they are sick and also should have access to their annual leaves anytime they wish. However, the business should make it clear to the workers about the procedure of taking leaves.

Recommendations for System Change. 
Issara to provide training to line supervisors, leaders, and managers.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Sick leave; Normally, if workers are sick, they just do not come to work, and leaders do not even have a chance to approve their sick leaves. The normal process is that if a worker is sick, he/she will report to their line leader, and the leader will report to HR. The normal policy for the workers is if they are sick, they have to report to line leaders, and leaders to report to HR. Once workers come back from sick leaves, they will have to present MC to get paid. Sometimes, when workers just take leaves, the business has issues with the production to fill up the vacant spot. To solve this issue, the business is training a group of workers who can fill such gaps as required. Issara has not received additional complaints from the workers. 

Annual leaves; 
If workers' annual leaves are not used up at the end of the year, the business will calculate and pay for the remaining leave days. However, the business did not agree to conduct an investigation. 

The business did not show interest in conducting communication with a wider group of workers as suggested. As it has been over several months, Issara will close the case.

Issara to provide training to line supervisors, leaders, and managers.

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; Issue with annual leaves; workers reported that they are entitled to annual leaves after one year of working experience, however, they do not get it approved by the supervisor as they want to take it. However, local workers get it approved anytime they want. Workers want to have access to their annual leaves as they desire. Workers also added that they do not get to use all of their annual leaves because they do not get approved, but those leaves will be cut off at the end of the year. 

Talking Points; 
What is the process for the workers to take annual leave? 
How does the business (HR) make sure that all employees have access to the leaves that they are entitled to without being discriminated against?
In case of workers were refused to take annual leaves in previous years, what would be the plan?
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The business responded that they provide 13 days of annual leaves for the workers who have been working for Mapa for less than 2 years, however, the business had some workforce issue during the COVID that might be caused some workers not to get their leaves approved, however, the business has recently recruited new workers and started letting workers take long leaves are there were 18 workers took long leaves within two weeks and returned back home. The procedure of taking leaves is for the workers to inform their supervisor, and the supervisor to get approval from HR, however, workers can also reach out to HR directly if they have any issues. 

Issara suggested communicating with the supervisors. The business agreed to do so.

The business later updated Issara saying that they had low demand from their buyers which caused not enough work for workers, given the struggle that the business is facing regarding insufficient workload for the workers, the business had to suggest workers use their annual leaves during the days that the business could not provide jobs. Therefore, given the unexpected situation, this case has to be closed with the condition.
remediation_notes: Workers do not get the annual leave approved by superviors, and the unused annual leaves will be cut off at the end of the year.
remediation_action: Mapa HR Head will conduct communication session with the line supervisors and will also inform workers to reach out to HR should they have their leave not approved by supervisor. Issara to also help communicate this to workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:

The business to conduct the investigation to access the number of impacted workers and conduct communication with them about their rights to access the leaves. When conducting the investigation, the business could conduct an anonymous survey where workers can anonymously answer the questions. If the survey finds the workers being impacted, the business should conduct communication with the workers and all of the supervisors about workers' rights to access all of their annual leaves as entitled before the year ends. 
Supervisors should be clearly communicated about fair treatment towards all nationalities, the communication should also include the business procedures if the business policy is not followed by the employees including supervisors. 
The business should also communicate with the workers about alternative ways for them if their supervisors do not approve their leave request, and the business to ensure that there will be no retaliation toward those who use alternative ways. 
Issara is to offer training to line supervisors in the near future, and have an HR officer and/or any responsible person reinforce the message so line supervisors will clearly understand that it is not Issara pushing for this but the business.
systems_change_business_steps_taken: The business responded that they are struggling to maintain workers due to low orders from their buyers, therefore, the business had to suggest workers use their annual leaves during the days the business could not provide work.However, the business has agreed to conduct a workers' satisfaction and recruitment survey where the findings will be shared with the business and Issara will provide relevant support for the system strengthening based on the workers feedback.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The factory owner appears to have changed a few months ago, as the workers were asked to sign a sheet about the new employer, and all workers were switched to being piece-rate workers rather than daily workers. Since the workers are considered piece-rate workers, no one can request paid sick leave according to the labor law, even if the workers submit a medical certificate. A worker was recently involved in an accident on the shuttle bus and had to take five days of sick leave but the company did not pay her daily wages saying that it didn’t happen at the work place.

-Encourage workers that have not been paid for sick leave to report to HR and for HR to consider each case
-Reimburse all workers that have taken sick leave but were not paid their daily wages for those days
-Announce to all workers, verbally and in writing, the company's policy for sick leave as per the labor law (30 sick days per year; MC not required for 1-2 days of sick leave each time)

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers in Line B and C reported needing a medical certificate even for being sick for 1 day. It seems this is not required for workers in other lines.

Recommendations:
- Investigate the matter and find out why the supervisors in Lines B,C are requiring medical certificates for 1-2 sick leave days
- If any worker has been denied sick leave because he/she didn't produce a MC, reimburse those workers for the lost wages
- Communicate to all, verbally and in writing, that for less than 3 consecutive sick leave days, medical certificates are not required.  That there would be no punishment for workers that take sick leave.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Khun Jarunee, QSM responded that the supervisors may request that the workers visit the hospital due to the COVID concern. However, HR insists workers be paid for sick days even if they do not have MC. (O&E shared that no workers complain that they do not get paid for sick leave days yet) HR will also communicate and train supervisors on sick leave.
remediation_notes: Workers in Line B and C reported needing a medical certificate even for being sick for 1 day. It seems this is not required for workers in other lines. Another worker said the supervisor suspends those who take sick leave frequently for 7 days as punishment.
remediation_action: The business responded that workers are always paid for sick days even if they do not have a medical certificate. HR will also communicate and train the supervisors on not requiring medical certificates for sick leave that is less than 3 consecutive days.
remediation_validation: The workers provided an update saying they have not heard any announcements from HR about the sick leave policy yet.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations:
Conduct regular training of line supervisors, including how to implement key company policies such as the sick leave policy

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:

remediation_business_steps_taken:
Khun Jarunee, QSM responded that the supervisors may request that the workers visit the hospital due to the COVID concern. Investigation result:
Inquiring with the supervisor It was discovered that the majority of supervisors Obtain a medical certificate from a current employee. The following are the reasons given by the supervisor for the request.
1. To prevent the spread of COVID-19, employees who become ill should seek medical attention. to detect COVID-19 and obtain a medical certificate to confirm the absence of COVID-19
2. To prevent frequent sick leave behavior that may be false on the part of some employees. not seriously ill
3. To protect employees' interests when it comes to annual worker evaluations. Absence/absence / (Time Attendance) is a criterion for evaluating employees' annual performance. Sick leave with medical certification It's preferable to taking sick leave without a medical certificate.

Immediately Action:
- On 9 June 2023, Organize a meeting and training to clarify complaints and remind supervisors of their legal right to sick leave if they want to protect the employee's benefits. must explain the reason Allow the staff to acknowledge rather than force or request a medical certificate. In the case of employees taking 1-2 days of sick leave as required by law, Providing a medical certification is the employees' right to decide whether or not to retain their rights
- On 14 June 2023 communicate with workers by holding a meeting to clarify the workers' rights again


BHR recommended that King Pac communicate with the impacted workers who did not receive proper sick leave, and that the workers contact HR directly for remediation. They agreed and will make the verbal and written announcement this week.
remediation_notes: Workers in some production lines reported needing a medical certificate even for being sick for 1 day. Another worker said the supervisor suspends those who take sick leave frequently for 7 days as punishment.
remediation_action:
The business responded that workers are always paid for sick days even if they do not have a medical certificate. HR had a meeting with line supervisors on June 9th and with workers during the morning talk on June 14th, the business has communicated about the sick leave policy in all languages of the workers. Based on the worker update, the business will also announce to workers that those affected by this should contact HR directly for remediation.

In the country escalation, HR met with supervisors and workers, and explained that workers have the right to take sick leave, no MC needed for 1-2 days. If they were not approved for sick leave, they should go to HR directly and they will check case by case. HR (verbal and written) announced this on Aug 29, 2023.

Some workers saw the written announcement about the sick leave policy in one building but other workers haven't seen the announcement.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations:
Conduct regular training of line supervisors, including how to implement key company policies such as the sick leave policy

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The worker shared that while he was working, his hand got into the machine and was injured. The business doesn't care and takes no responsibility at all; they even called him to the HR office and scolded him. They said he is careless and doesn't pay attention at work. This is his second injury; the first injury got nine stitches on his hand and two stitches on the same hand for this second injury. But the business doesn't care about worker safety; at his workplace, it is very dangerous as he needs to work with sharp knife machines.

Moreover,he got sick after that and asked for a day of sick leave from the line supervisor; they required him to present them the medical certificate, but as he just rested in his room, he couldn't provide them the medical certificate. As a result, he received a warning letter.


Recommendations:
- The business to reimburse the worker for lost wages, and the warning letter should be retracted

description: Issue with holidays or other benefits: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue #1. 
Context: The issue with the public holiday. Workers reported that they were being asked to sign a consent form which was written in Thai without an explanation and later realized it was the consent to agree to work for a public holiday (13th Oct). It also happened on 23rd Sep. Workers added that they were asked to sign the document first only after the workers signed the documents did the line supervisor explain the purpose. Workers want to take a rest and be well explained about the documents before they sign.

Recommendations; 
The business  shall immediately make an announcement to all workers noting that the consent received earlier is void because workers did not understand what they were consenting to, request the voluntary consent of workers that are willing to work on the upcoming public holiday on Oct 13th, and provide the consent forms to work on Oct 13th in the languages of the workers, without pressure to sign
The business is to make sure that all communication documents are in the native language of the workers, especially those documents requiring their informed consent
The business is to make sure that workers understand what the business is requesting, and that the worker has the right to voluntarily consent to the request by fully explaining the nature of the request in a language the workers understand, prior to asking for the workers’ consent.

Talking Points: 
Is the business aware that the consent form that the workers had to sign was only in Thai and not in Burmese (Khmer) and that the line supervisors that were tasked to get the consent from workers only explained what the workers were consenting to after the worker had already signed? 
What is the production plan for 13 Oct? Is the business planning for full production on that day?
How many workers have agreed to work on 13 Oct? 
Have there been any workers that have reported to HR or through the grievance channels about this issue?

Issue #2.

Context: The issue with a worker who has been suspended from working OT hours for seven days for missing work on the business’s public holiday. The worker said that she missed her job because of the translator’s announcement that working for a public holiday on (23rd) is optional. In addition to that, the worker added not receiving OT for several days since she took sick leave for 4 days with the proper Medical Certificate. The worker added that it has been 23 days in total that she has not to received OT working hours. Worker information: Working ID; C 105033, Nwe Nwe Win. 

Recommendations: 
The business should conduct an investigation on this issue to find out why this work has not received OT hours for 23 days and why she was suspended from working OT for seven days for not working on a public holiday. If the investigation finds an issue with the worker being punished for not working on a public holiday, the worker should be remediated with the OT hours or wages that are equal to the 7 days of OT hours. The worker should not be punished for not working on public holidays. 
The business should communicate with the worker specifically and also all workers generally about the company’s OT policy, including that withholding OT is not used as a form of punishment and clear guidance on why OT might be reduced immediately after a worker has returned from sick leave for the worker’s health.
The business should provide training to all supervisors and clerks on appropriate ways to grant OT hours to workers so it is based on the voluntary consent of the worker and not used in any way to punish workers.  

Talking Points:
Is the business aware of this case?
In a previous escalation meeting related to this issue, the business has agreed to revise the consent form and conduct more investigation, what has been the investigation result and the action plan? Has the consent form been revised? 
What is the business OT policy for sick workers? If there is a policy for sick workers and OT hours, has this policy been communicated with the workers? 
How often does the business provide training to supervisors on how to properly implement company policies, such as those related to OT hours for workers?
remediation_business_steps_taken: Isara raised this issue with the business, the business argued that they have all of the documents that needs worker's to sing in workers' native language and the process to get the consent in one month in advance and the business follow the voluntary process in getting consent from workers to work for public holidays.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that they were asked to sign a form in Thai which they couldn't read and only after they had signed it were they told that it was consent to work on the upcoming public holiday on October 13th.
remediation_action: The business responded by saying that all consent forms are provided in all the languages of the workers (Thai, Burmese, and Khmer), provided with a one-month notice, and that the workers receive an explanation of what they are consenting to prior to signing.
remediation_validation: Issara will follow up with workers after the business has taken corrective action.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for system change, 
The business to clearly communicate with all line supervisors that workers are to voluntarily consent to any business requests, such as working on a public holiday, and that in no way should the line supervisor seek to gain the consent of the worker without fully informing the worker of the choice in the language of the worker and checking that the worker has understood what has been communicated.
The business is to clearly communicate the disciplinary actions that will be taken against those that gain consent of workers through pressure, manipulation, or not fully informing the worker of the business request. 
The business is to remind workers that they have the right to be fully informed of the choice prior to giving consent and that they should use the grievance channel to report any incidents where they have felt they were not fully informed or were pressured into giving consent.

remediation_business_steps_taken:
Closure note 

Issue #1. 
Isara raised this issue with the business, and the business initially noted that the consent form that workers need to sign was already in workers' native language and the workers were notified one month in advance.  However, the consent form that the worker provided showed that the form did not provide sufficient information to help the worker understand what he/she was voluntarily signing up for. Issara escalated this issue, with support from the Strategic Partner, and suggested the business revise the consent form so that there was sufficient information in it to help the workers understand what they were consenting to (i.e. working OT or on a holiday). The business provided a new form that the company will use to get management approval for additional work hours to be performed by employees as per production demands, which lays out the policy that employees are to voluntarily consent to any such OT hours or work on a holiday.  The business noted that this document is now attached as a cover sheet to the consent form that workers will sign, in the workers’ languages. Although the consent form itself was not revised by the business, Issara is closing this case because the business is providing the cover sheet that provides an explanation that the additional work is to be voluntary.  


Issue#2. 
Issara raised this issue with the business, and the business agreed to conduct the investigation.   The worker provided an update that she started getting OT hours again starting on 19 Nov 2021 but was not sure why she started getting OT hours again, and for that matter why she had been denied OT hours in the first place.  The business had noted that it was taking time to investigate the issue while safeguarding the worker but it has been several months since with no specific action taken by the business.  Therefore, Issara is closing this case.
remediation_business_steps_remaining:
Issue #1. 

The business to revise consent form for the workers to sing. 

Issue #2. 
The business to conduct investigation and take action based on the business policy.

Workers reported that they were asked to sign a form in Thai which they couldn't read and only after they had signed it were they told that it was consent to work on the upcoming public holiday on October 13th.

Case #2: 
Issara raised this issue with the business, and the business agreed to conduct the investigation.  The business noted it would take time to investigate this issue in order to make sure that the worker is not identified by the line supervisor.
remediation_validation:

We have not received confirmation from workers as the cover sheet to be used with consent forms will be initiated in future instances.

The worker confirmed that she started receiving OT hours starting from 19 Nov 2021.  However, she is not sure why she was targeted and denied OT hours earlier.

The business  shall immediately make an announcement to all workers noting that the consent received earlier is void because workers did not understand what they were consenting to, request the voluntary consent of workers that are willing to work on the upcoming public holiday on Oct 13th, and provide the consent forms to work on Oct 13th in the languages of the workers, without pressure to sign
The business is to make sure that all communication documents are in the native language of the workers, especially those documents requiring their informed consent
The business is to make sure that workers understand what the business is requesting, and that the worker has the right to voluntarily consent to the request by fully explaining the nature of the request in a language the workers understand, prior to asking for the workers’ consent.

Talking Points: 
Is the business aware that the consent form that the workers had to sign was only in Thai and not in Burmese (Khmer) and that the line supervisors that were tasked to get the consent from workers only explained what the workers were consenting to after the worker had already signed? 
What is the production plan for 13 Oct? Is the business planning for full production on that day?
How many workers have agreed to work on 13 Oct? 
Have there been any workers that have reported to HR or through the grievance channels about this issue?

Issue#2. Closed

Context: The issue with a worker who has been suspended from working OT hours for seven days for missing work on the business’s public holiday. The worker said that she missed her job because of the translator’s announcement that working for a public holiday on (23rd) is optional. In addition to that, the worker added not receiving OT for several days since she took sick leave for 4 days with the proper Medical Certificate. The worker added that it has been 23 days in total that she has not to received OT working hours. Worker information: Working ID; C 105033, Nwe Nwe Win.

The business should conduct an investigation on this issue to find out why this work has not received OT hours for 23 days and why she was suspended from working OT for seven days for not working on a public holiday. If the investigation finds an issue with the worker being punished for not working on a public holiday, the worker should be remediated with the OT hours or wages that are equal to the 7 days of OT hours. The worker should not be punished for not working on public holidays.

Is the business aware of this case?

Closure note 

Issue #1. 
Isara raised this issue with the business, and the business initially noted that the consent form that workers need to sign was already in workers' native language and the workers were notified one month in advance. Issara escalated this issue, with support from the Strategic Partner, and suggested the business revise the consent form so that there was sufficient information in it to help the workers understand what they were consenting to (i.e. working OT or on a holiday). The business noted that this document is now attached as a cover sheet to the consent form that workers will sign, in the workers’ languages. Although the consent form itself was not revised by the business, Issara is closing this case because the business is providing the cover sheet that provides an explanation that the additional work is to be voluntary.  


Issue#2.

The worker provided an update that she started getting OT hours again starting on 19 Nov 2021 but was not sure why she started getting OT hours again, and for that matter why she had been denied OT hours in the first place.  The business had noted that it was taking time to investigate the issue while safeguarding the worker but it has been several months since with no specific action taken by the business.  Therefore, Issara is closing this case.

# Issue 1 (CLOSED) 
Issara Recommendations:
The issue with the workers being asked to work on Sunday but not getting double wages. The employer provides the workers with compensation day-off on weekdays.
Recommendation. 
-The business to conduct an investigation to find out the impacted workers and pay them back. The investigation process should include workers' voices. 
-Workers should not be forced or pressured to work on Sundays. 
-Workers should receive a fixed day off to let the workers have their plans for their personal activities.
-The business to make sure that all workers fully consent to work on Sundays. 
-HR to involve in the consent form process along with the supervisors. 

26-Nov-2020

-Issara suggests the business clearly communicate by providing the option for the workers such as, if you are not comfortable working on Sunday, you are allowed to say no.
Time Frame - 1 pay period


Notes (Talking Points):
Please give the detail of the story and ask the following questions. 

-What are the terms and conditions of the day off in the contract? 
-Workers said that they are being questioned and forced to agree to work on Sundays by the super supervisors. How does the business make sure that all of the consent forms that the workers signed really consent? 
-What is the reason only this specific line's workers having this issue?

26-Nov-2020

-The business said that they will have a communication section, have they done this? If yes, when and how? 
-If a worker does not want to sign the consent form and does not agree to work on Sunday, what will happen with that worker?

#Issue 2
Context; Workers reported being threatened that if they refused to give consent to work on December 10th (a Thai public holiday) that they would not receive future opportunities to work on Sundays

-The business to do an immediate investigation and take disciplinary actions towards the specific supervisor who indirectly forced/coerced workers to agree to work on public holidays. 

-The investigation should be conducted ethically taking into account safeguards for the worker. -The investigation should aim to understand why the workers were told that they will not be provided work for the following Sundays, this could be perceived as a repercussion for not accepting to work on a holiday which should be voluntary. Workers should not feel at any point forced or coerced to work on their day off and there should be no retaliation or consequences for not wanting to work on the day off. The investigation should include workers' voices and safeguards should be in place. 

-The business to clearly re-communicate with impacted workers and involved staff immediately about the voluntary nature of the work for Public holidays and Sundays in the written and verbal communication. 
-Workers should not be threatened from losing other opportunities for not agreeing to work for Public holidays, this should be clearly communicated to all supervisors and workers. 
-The business to revise its policy and procedure of consent agreement process to make sure that workers feel free to work or refuse.  

Talking Points : 
-Please share the story in general by saying that workers were forced/coerced to agree to work on Dec 10th. The supervisor P Mint (blue cap) threatened the workers by saying that the workers will lose opportunities to work on the following Sundays. Therefore, Issara suggested the business to re-communicate with all workers that what P Mint said is against the company policy and against workers rights.

The business did not take any specific investigation and action towards the supervisor who threatened and forced the workers to agree to work for a public holiday. Issara will escalate with the Strategic partners instead of going back to the business.

description: Issue with holidays or other benefits: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with workers not being provided all 4 days of public holidays during Songkran (Thai New Year) as announced by the business. Workers reported that the factory closed for only two days (12,13 April) but was not given double for the remaining two days (14-15 April) that they had to work. 

Recommendations; 
-The business to reinstate those two public holidays or give double wages to the workers. The business should consult with the workers whether they want their holidays back or get double paid. 
-The business shall communicate with all workers about the reason why the factory did not close those two days and what will the business do to prevent such issues from happening again in the future. 

Talking points. 

-It is mentioned that those 4 days were the business’s approved public holidays, so what was the reason for the business not to close for the remaining two days? 
-Were there any communications sessions with the workers about the business decisions? 

Time Frame within 1 week.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had meetings with the business, the business responded that 2 holidays out of 4 had been replaced for the holidays in August. Meaning that the business did not close those two days in Songkran but closed later. Workers were informed in writing about the holiday's changes. Basically, the business has given all 13 public holidays to the workers according to the LPA. It seems that some workers were not aware of the announcement. Issara later check with the worker and to discuss the announcement, the workers confirmed now seeing the announcement.
remediation_notes: The issue with workers not getting all 4 days of public holidays during Songkran (Thai New Year) as announced by the business. Workers reported that the factory closed for only two days (12,13 April) but was not given double for the remaining two days (14-15 April) that they had to work.
remediation_action: The business clarified that the two public holidays not taken during the Songkran period will be substituted to two other days later this year.  The business also made verbal and written announcements to communicate this to workers.
remediation_validation: Workers confirmed that they had seen the announcement and understand that two substitute holidays will be given to them later this year.
remediation_results: Issara had meetings with the business, the business responded that 2 holidays out of 4 Songkran holidays will be substituted for holidays in in August. The business also clarified this change with the workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
System change recommendations:
The business has posted the calendar of the public holidays for the company which is a good practice and it is what should be done according to the law. However, there have been changes on those dates which have impacted workers leave. Therefore, it is recommended for the business to follow the dates that have been posted or if the company needs to make some changes, the company should consult with workers, get their consent to make such changes and pay wages accordingly.

description: Issue with holidays or other benefits: violation of law
Issue with holidays or other benefits: violation of law
Issue with holidays or other benefits: violation of law
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that April 13-16, 2024 were set as public holidays at the beginning of the year. Line supervisors in the packaging line in the warehouse asked them to work on April 14-16 due to urgent production demands.  When workers refused, the supervisors tried to say let's do a lucky draw then to see who would come to work on those days. When the workers refused that as well, the company unilaterally decided all would work on April 14-16. In addition to being forced to work on these holidays, it is not clear what kind of wages they will receive for those days and whether there would be substitute days off.

TPs:
- When did the company decide to make this holiday change and require workers to work during Songkran? What has led to this sudden change (i.e. unexpected new orders)?

Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter to determine what led to this public holiday change and who made this decision.
- The company should not unilaterally decide to change the public holidays it announced at the beginning of the year. The company should consult and negotiate with the workers and come to a consensus, rather than deciding against the wishes of the workers.
- Communicate the consensus decision clearly to workers, including the wage rates that will be paid and whether substitute holidays will be given and when.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
10 April 2024
KPI 2325 and 2324: Not only the business received this case from us but they also received this case from the interpreter as well. Her name is Moh Moh. The business admitted that the root cause of this case was the poor and unclear communication in the warehouse department. They also admitted that there's an increase in order to the point that they cannot finish the packing in time so they need more workforce during Songkran around 500 workers. After the business got our request for the remediation call, they responded to the issue right away by talking and meeting with the workers in the warehouse department on 1 April 2024. In the meeting, the business communicated this clearly to the workers why they needed more workforce and asked the workers voluntarily who wanted to work during Songkran (14 - 16 April). 250 workers in the warehouse department volunteered to work on 14 - 16 April. The other 250 more workers that the business needs, they also asked voluntarily in other departments too. So now, the workforce problem is resolved. The business got 500 workers to work during Songkran. In terms of the wage and substitute holidays, 14 April is Sunday,so if the workers come to work on 14 April, they'll get double of their daily wage. 15 - 16 April are public holidays, the workers already get the daily wage on public holidays so if they come to work during those days, they'll also get daily wage on top of that. There's no substitute holidays for them but the business will prepare drinks for the workers on those days in return for their good cooperation.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that April 13-16, 2024 were set as public holidays at the beginning of the year but recently they were asked to work during this period due to urgent production demands.  The company made this decision even after the workers voiced that they want to take the holidays as per the announced list of public holidays. Moreover, it is not clear what kind of wages they will receive for working those holidays and whether there would be substitute days off.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- The annual public holiday list that is announced for each year should be changed during the course of the year, and workers should be consulted and agree on any such adjustments.
- Forecast production demands for the whole year to ensure there are not sudden changes that will culminate in such public holiday date changes.

Moreover, it is not clear what kind of wages they will receive for working those holidays and whether there would be substitute days off.
remediation_action: The business were aware of this issue and accepted that there was poor communication about what was to happen during the Songkran holiday period.  The business has received an increase in orders and so need workers during the holidays. The business met with the workers to explain the situation and has requested the workers to volunteer to work during the period of April 14-16, 2024. The workers will get paid double wages during this period, and substitute holidays will not be provided.
remediation_validation: The workers report that the company announced that working during the Songkran holiday is voluntary. Those who choose to work on those days receive double wages.
remediation_results: We're closing this case because the workers were informed about voluntary holiday work, and those who participated received double pay as per the Labor Protection Act (LPA). All the workers are satisfied with the outcome.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- The annual public holiday list that is announced for each year should be changed during the course of the year, and workers should be consulted and agree on any such adjustments.
- Forecast production demands for the whole year to ensure there are not sudden changes that will culminate in such public holiday date changes.

closed_notes: This case is being closed because after having several conversations with the supplier and the buyer during months, the supplier did not accepted the recommendations done by Issara to pay workers 75% of their wages for the Saturdays off (as stipulated on the Thai Labour Protection Act). Thus, this case is being close with a poor score.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
-Workers should be paid for the 6th day of work that they did not receive, as per the MOU contract (and also based on Labor Dept (Central). Workers report feeling pressured to sign document - not a voluntary reduction of days.
-Impacted workers should receive compensation for all Saturdays off, since the policy entered into force. Workers are legally entitled to a minimum 75% of wages for the withdrawn working day(s).
-Ensure that there are disciplinary measures / policy in place for staff and supervisors who try to coerce workers to sign documents.
-Strengthening grievance mechanism for workers (same as 3.4.)"

Talking points:

- Cal-Comp HR indicated that provincial DLPW indicated that this practice was legal but Central DLPW and the Myanmar Government have both confirmed it is a violation of the bilateral MOU employment contract.  It is prohibited to hire workers and promise one level of work and pay, but then offer them something less after their arrival.

- Workers are owed 75% pay for the 6th day and this should be repaid within 1-2 pay periods.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Per Cal-Comp:
- Before Cal-comp let the employees sign the consent letter, our HR did consult with Phetchaburi labour department. But to make sure, our HR did manage to consult with labour department in Bangkok. The result is the same line as consulted with Phetchaburi labour department.

- Our HR has checked with the department of employment who is responsible for foreign migrant workers. This condition is acceptable once the employees sign the consent letter.

- This temporary working condition involving 2,247 people of CR division will end in April 10th, 2020

-The business did not agree with Issara suggestions to compensate workers.
remediation_business_steps_remaining:
Per the existing CAT that K Narisa/Cal-Comp/Issara drafted: 
A. Cal-Comp HR team to recheck with labor department (central); obtain any agreement in writing.
B. Cal-Comp HR team to also check with Myanmar side as it could impact MOU. MOU stipulates 6 days work week.
C. Cal-Comp HR team consult with business unit on feasibility

Per meeting on May 8:
-CC position continues to be that they can make the changes without having to pay workers for the Saturdays off. CC explained that according to DLPW Thai and migrant workers fall under Thai law. However, Issara emphasized that that according to MOLIP and our consultation with DoL central. workers should receive payment for those days. Further information was given on why laws and regulations from both countries are important in this case and what could be the consequences for businesses (RAs and employers) with this kind of cases. According to recent feedback from workers, there are some workers who didn't work for some Saturdays on April, but according to the business that only happened once and it was under the date indicated in the memo, however the dates indicated by workers were different. 

-HP recommended CC to discuss this issue internally with a higher level and to consult with Myanmar side.

description: Issues with regular shift hours or other shift issues: violation of law and/or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; Workers reported long hours of OT, the business has been having OT till 11 PM total of 79 hours of work per week according to the worker's payslip (The payslip was issued on 1-Mar-2021). 

-It is recommended for the business to strictly follow the buyer COC regarding the working hours. 
-HR should closely work with the production to make sure that the workers are not working overtime than the buyers COC allows. 
-HR should be aware of this situation, the supervisor who does not follow the business policy should be taken action effectively. 
-As the workers have to work by standing for more than 13 hours per day it is affecting the worker's health, therefore, the business is recommended to again following the buyer COC and also take into account the worker's wellbeing. 


Talking Points; 
-Issara has received this issue repeatedly, How is HR managing working hours? Who is responsible for this? Does HR aware of the long working hours that have exceeded the buyer's COC? 
-Workers have reported getting fainted often, does the business have a record of it? If yes, how many workers per week or month? Who takes this record? How does the business manage such a situation to minimize the risk in the supply chain?
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had several meetings with the business to provide recommendations for the system improvement, the business firstly responded saying that they are aware of the issues and trying to recruit 100 more workers to solve the worker's challenges, and also argued that they are trying to comply with the buyer COC which does not allowed exceeding 72 hours of work per week, however, the business also recognized that a few numbers of workers in a certain line being asked to work for more than 72 hours of work per week.  The business update that they have conducted communication with the production manager to try to manage working hours within 72 hrs per week. A few weeks later, the third wave of COVID-19 started and the business had to shut down most of the production building in the factory and re-arrange the production which delayed the recruitment process for the business. Issara checked with the workers and learned of workers not being asked to work for more than 72 hours of work per week. Since it has passed several months and the business does not have a clear set time to recruit more workers, Issara considered closing this case at this point.
remediation_notes: Workers reported long hours of OT, the business has been having OT till 11 PM total of 79 hours of work per week according to the worker's payslip
remediation_action: Following several months of discussion and escalation with Strategic Partners, the business responded that their long-term improvement has been pending due to the COVID-19 situation which causes the factory closure, quarantine, and so on. However, the business is following the RBA standard at the moment and trying not to ask workers to work more than 72 hours of work per week.
remediation_validation: Workers have updated not being asked to work more than 72 hours per week recently.
remediation_results: The business responded that their long-term improvement has been pending due to the COVID-19 situation which causes the factory closure, quarantine, and so on. However, the business is following the RBA standard at the moment and trying not to ask workers to work more than 72 hours of work per week.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business should revise its OT policy.

-The business should communicate to all workers and supervisors immediately about the allowed working hours and also introduce the different grievance channels and the focal if the working hours exceed 72 hours per week. 

-The business should communicate to supervisors what are the disciplinary consequences for those not following the business policy regarding OT working hours.

-Recommend Issara Academy training to HR and supervisors.  

-Issara can also provide tailored training to full HR teams on-site, and provide systems review with tailored recommendations to eliminate labor risks."
systems_change_business_steps_taken: The business responded that they have conducted communication with the production manager to manage the working hours within 72 hours per week.

description: Issues with regular shift hours or other shift issues: violation of law and/or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker working in Building 10 reported that his contract states that he will alternate day and night shift work every two weeks. The workers were asked to alternate day and night shift once a month but now they are being asked to alternate every two months. When workers told their supervisors that they could not work the night shift for 2 straight months, the manager told them that they would be moved to another building but they would still have to work according to that schedule and the workers had no choice. The worker is not happy being assigned to work the night shift for two months. Most of the workers on Line 8 are facing that issue.

TPs:
-What is the day and night shift working arrangements for workers in Building 10?
-Is there a schedule for workers to alternate between day and night shifts?  How often are they supposed to change shifts?
-Is this arrangement noted in the workers' contracts?

Recommendations for remediation:
-The business should listen to workers that have expressed that they cannot handle working the night shift for two straight months, and come up with a negotiated solution so that the shift arrangement is acceptable to the workers
-The business should not unilaterally change shift arrangements that is contrary to what is stated in the workers' contracts and without consulting the workers first
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Piyabutr, CSR, has no information on the shift details. He'll consult with the production manager and get back to us with the details.

K. Piyabutr, CSR checked with the production and found that no workers are required to alternate day and night shifts every two months. There are alternate day and night shifts every two weeks only.

description: Issues with regular shift hours or other shift issues: violation of law and/or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Shine Min Htet Factory 11 worker reported that starting from Dec 20th 2022, Cal-Comp practiced 3 shifts a day in Factory 10 & 11 and the reason given was low orders from the buyers. The 3 shifts are: 1) 5 AM to 1:40 PM, 2) 1 PM to 9:40 PM, and 3) 9 PM to 5:40 AM. As a result, the workers assigned to work in the 1st shift have to wake up very early (3-4am) to catch the shuttle bus. The 2nd shift workers have faced security issues during this late night commute back home, with workers getting attacked by gangsters, especially in Bang Kway area. The gangsters try to take the workers' phones, jewelry, or money. On 14th March, one of the night-shift workers was attacked by two local gangsters near the Bar Bar shop (Bang Kway area) and seriously injured. Women also face sexual harassment by the locals and gangsters during their late night commute, with motorcycle riders touching the hips of the women workers. In addition, the food at the canteen often has gone bad by the time the 3rd shift workers get their meal break. Many workers are feeling physically weak due to sleeplessness, not having fresh food, and mentally distressed due to the dangers during the commute. Now, the business has decided to extend 3-shift work arrangement for another 3 months.

TPs:
- What are the reasons for moving to a 3-shift system?
- Is the business aware of the negative effects this is having on the workers?

Recommendations:
- The business should provide working hours and conditions as stated in the employment contract
- Given the negative impact on workers, consider going back to the 2-shift system as was the arrangement previously and the working hours that the workers signed up for when they signed their employment contracts.
- Investigate any cases where workers may have been victims of robbery, assault, or sexual harassment during their commute to work

description: Issues with regular shift hours or other shift issues: violation of law and/or employment contract
Issues with regular shift hours or other shift issues: violation of law and/or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers being asked to switch their day off from Sunday to weekdays as the business wants to avoid paying double for working on Sundays. Workers added that it has been 2 Sundays that the business asked them to work on Sundays which is their holiday and substitute weekdays which also mean that the workers' day off per week is not stable. 

Added on 17 Dec, 2022. 
Context: In regards to this issue, 7 workers who refused to switch their day off reported being moved to a different line as retaliation. Since the business has ceased/solved this issue, for the time being, those workers want to come back to their original working line.

Recommendations; 
-Regular shift hours and wages should be respected at all times, in line with contractual agreements. Changes in shifts should be made with the consent of workers and with reasonable notice, ensuring that total weekly working hours are in compliance with national law, and extra hours are paid at a premium rate. Workers should not be forced or coerced to agree to the changes. Shifts should not be changed in order to avoid paying premium overtime and holiday rates.
-The business shall conduct an investigation to find out the root cause of the issues and remediate the workers if the result found workers being forced to change their day off. 
-The business is recommended to have conversations with the workers and come to an agreement for a fixed day off. 
The process that the business has been practicing should be on a voluntary basis. No workers should be forced to change or switch their day off against their will.
The business should coordinate with the production and come up with a plan where workers' days off are not being switched or changed often. Workers have rights to have a fixed day off so that they can make their personal plans for the activities. 
If there is work during the days off of workers, the business shall ask workers if they would like to work on that day, and if so, the business should pay the wages according to the LPA 2x and 3x for OT during day off. 
The investigation with the line supervisor and the manager should be taken to investigate the treatment that they had with the workers and provide the training and disciplinary measure according to the business policy. 
Workers should not be threatened with being moved to a harder production line, getting fired from their job or having to find a new buyer for not agreeing to switch their day off.
After the investigation process, the business should conduct communication in written and verbal with all workers who have been impacted by this issue.  

Talking Points: 
Is HR aware of this issue? If yes, what has been the action plan to solve it? 
Are there any changes on the production which caused workers to change their day off from Sunday to the weekdays?  And if so, how is the business handling the workforce?

12 Dec 2021. Potential talking points added by Jarrett:

- Thank you for moving to quickly resolve the recent payments for Sunday work to be the legal rate of 2x wage. However, workers are reporting non-payment of the correct Sunday work wage for a much longer period beforehand, some saying this has not been happening correctly for years. What is the TUF plan to further look into these reports?
- A key principle for TU and for all buyers is that workers must have a functioning grievance mechanism that is safe to report issues to. Workers are now repeatedly reporting intimidation and threats of being moved to different production lines when they approach HR with an issue, or speak or ask questions during meetings with supervisors or HR. What steps will TU and TUF take to ensure a functioning grievance mechanism, and ensure there is no retaliation for workers that raise issues? Issara provides clear and actionable training to HR and supervisors on these issues and ways to handle grievances - we strongly recommend this training for TUF. If not from us, then we strongly suggest you arrange more concrete and actionable capacity building for HR and managers, and either inform us or have us observe, so we can help you track what changes take place or not.
- We understand you have explained changes in production schedules and movement of working days to often include Sunday, which now should be paid at the proper 2x rate. But what steps are being taken to ensure that Sunday work - a typical day off - is voluntary and well communicated?



Update from workers (14 Jan 2022) : 

(Group 1) 
Among 7 workers there are two workers who have been working for a new working line, however do not want to come back to their original line given that they have been treated poorly by the line supervisor but the business did not conduct any proper action to address the issues. In detail, these two workers did not receive overtime working hours like other workers for two weeks because they refused to switch their day off as requested by the business. The workers approached the ER as they were left out from the OT working hours. The ER staff did not conduct an investigation against the line supervisor but simply asked the workers if they wanted to change to new lines. Workers accept to work for the new line and have been working in that line. Last week, these two workers were provided with a warning letter by their supervisor (P Yat) for going to the HR office during working hours. Workers were called to the officer to sign the warning letter, but the workers did not sign because they had informed their supervisor about their visit to ER and they only took around 30 minutes which contrasted with the accusation of the supervisor who said that they took around one hour going out without her permission. 

Note: 
In summary, these two workers do not want to go back to their original, however, Issara wants to highlight how workers' issues are being handled improperly by the ER without a proper investigation to find out the root cause. This is to explain to the business how the grievance is not working effectively which drives workers reporting to Issara and losing trust of using internal grievances. 

(Group 2) 
There are another 5 workers who were moved to a different line for speaking up during the business communication sessions to work on Sundays off. 1 worker out of 5 left the job. There are 4 workers still working for a new line.  Issara has suggested the business relocate these workers to their original as requested, however the business response laid out that these workers moved with the consent which contrasts the workers' report and update.. Workers still report Issara and say that they want to go back to their original line. 

Talking Points; 
These 4 workers reported being invited for a meeting after Issara’s escalation call. Workers reported that one of the officers at the office apologized about them being sent to a different line, however did not clearly say what the next steps would be. Why is the business response saying workers consented to move? Workers are still reporting Issara about their willingness to return back to their original line, what is the business response to this? 
How did the investigation take place? Was that done by someone who joined the meeting with Issara? 

Recommendations: 
-For the two workers, investigate the line supervisor and the manager’s treatment of the workers (OT hours not given, warning letter given for going to ER); provide the training and disciplinary measure according to the business policy. 
-After the investigation process, the business should provide an update on the investigation results to the impacted workers. 
-For the four workers, reassign them to their original lines, since they did not consent willingly to switch lines 
-The business should focus on the safeguard for the workers and clearly communicate with the supervisors that there should be no reprisals against these workers after relocation to their original line.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the business, the business argued that they have a policy that notifies employees in advance to make sure that employees voluntarily and agree to come to work, they will sign a written consent and pay double wages. However, to solve the issue, the business updated to pay double to the workers in the future and make sure that workers are communicated about the voluntary process and have consent. The business did not reflect or consider the reimbursement for the past. The business response neither reflects the issue with the workers being forced or threads to switch the day off nor conducted any investigation to access the poor treatment of the Employment Relation staff. 

Issara checked with the workers, the workers have updated being communicated to receive double wages during December onward if they are asked to work on Sundays. However, they were not communicated for the reimbursement about the past Sunday's work. In addition to that, 7 workers who spoke during the business communication have been sent to a different line for refusing to switch their day off. These 7 workers want to come back to their original working line.

Issara escalated this issue with the business again to provide the workers updated complaints and provide more recommendations. The business was suggested to conduct further investigation to find out the root cause of the issue. As a response, the business again repeat that their investigation found this group of workers moved to different line with the consent. For the issue with the behavior of the ER staff who treated workers poorly, the business have communicated with her and Verite will provide training in the early 2022. 

Issara had another follow up escalation call with the business and focus on the group of workers and recommended for the relocation since the workers are feeling that they are being retaliated.
remediation_notes:
Workers in the “Pla Sod” line reported being asked to work on Sunday (the typical day off for workers) to meet production demands, and switch their day off to another weekday day. Some workers reported this was not voluntary or communicated in advance, and workers reported not being paid the 2x legal rate for Sunday work.  This was reported for Nov 7 and 14, and some workers noted this practice had been long-standing.  Worker contracts provide for one rest day a week, and Thai labor law establishes a 2x daily wage for Sunday work, and 3x daily wage for official holiday day work. 
 
In a follow up communication session on this issue held by the business, 7 workers reported being moved to different working lines as retaliation for speaking up and not consenting to switch their regular Sunday day off.  Workers have reported that being switched to different lines, or being threatened with moving to a new production line, as retaliation for raising issues is a common practice at TUF.
remediation_action: This issue was escalated to TU corporate HR and to the Sustainability Director.  The business conducted an investigation and noted that it has followed company policy to notify employees in advance to make sure that employees voluntarily agree to work, and they will sign consent for it.  To solve the issue, the business said it would pay double wages to the workers when they are asked to work on their weekly day-off on Sunday in the future and make sure that workers understand that it is voluntary.  However, the business did not say whether it would reimburse workers the double wages for days-off worked in the past.  Issara has recommended an immediate investigation to pay workers correctly for all previous Sundays worked, and to review systems to ensure that any Sunday work proposed is communicated well in advance and is voluntary.  Issara has also recommended that TUF work with Issara or others to improve grievance mechanisms, and to train all HR and supervisors to ensure there is no retaliation for raising issues or not consenting to switch days off.
remediation_validation: Issara checked with the workers, the workers have updated being communicated to receive double wages during December if they are asked to work on Sundays. However, they did not hear anything about reimbursement for work on past Sundays.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
The business should provide training to production staff and HR on fair and ethical treatment towards workers. 
HR shall work closely with production to make sure workers rights are respected, that they receive the right payment according to the LPA, and that the company policies are clearly communicated and followed by all relevant staff. Workers should not be forced or coerced to work during their day off.

This was reported for Nov 7 and 14, and some workers noted this practice had been long-standing.  Worker contracts provide for one rest day a week, and Thai labor law establishes a 2x daily wage for Sunday work, and 3x daily wage for official holiday day work. 
 
In a follow up communication session on this issue held by the business, 5 workers reported being moved to different working lines as retaliation for speaking up and not consenting to switch their regular Sunday day off.  Workers have reported that being switched to different lines or being threatened with moving to a new production line was retaliation for their having raised issues and that this was a common practice at TUF.

However, the business did not say whether it would reimburse workers the double wages for days-off worked in the past.  Issara has recommended an immediate investigation to pay workers correctly for all previous Sundays worked, and to review systems to ensure that any Sunday work proposed is communicated well in advance and is voluntary.  Issara has also recommended that TUF work with Issara or others to improve grievance mechanisms, and to train all HR and supervisors to ensure there is no retaliation for raising issues or not consenting to switch days off.

Investigate this issue, include worker voice in the investigation and ensure worker safeguards
Workers should be consulted and consent to any re-assignment of work duties
Discipline the line supervisors that was verbally abusive to workers and and sent them home without pay
Remediate the workers directly affected for the lost wages

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case with a poor rating. The business has resorted to laying off workers when workers expressed their request to work on a 2-shift system.
remediation_issara_recommendation: A worker reported that the business assigned workers to work 3 shifts since December 2022. In the current situation, there are approximately 3000 workers who are working 3 shifts. The working hours in 3 shifts are: 8 am to 4:40 pm (first shift), 4 pm to 12:40 am (2nd shift) and 12 to 8:40 am (3rd shift). Since the business started 3 shifts, the workers have been facing different kinds of challenges such as sleeplessness, lack of appetite, attacks from gangsters during the commute (especially 4 pm to 12:40 am shift workers). The business tried to extend the 3-shift system until June 2023 so the workers went on strike on 24th March 2023. In order to stop the uprising of the workers, the manager of Cal-Comp called the Line Leader meeting and propose 2 options. The first option is the business will change from 3 shifts to 2 shifts but many workers will have to be dismissed with cancellation letters and one month severance pay. And the second option is the business will keep practicing the 3 shifts but the business will take more care of workers' security and may consider to provide 1,000 Baht to workers as a shift bonus. After calling line leader meetings, the business distributed the voting forms to all workers to choose 3 shifts or 2 shifts to work. Unfortunately the voting system was not anonymous. The workers had to mention their ID and names in the voting form.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that the business assigned workers to work 3 shifts since December 2022. Since the business started 3 shifts, the workers have been facing different kinds of challenges such as sleeplessness, lack of appetite, attacks from gangsters during the commute. The business tried to extend the 3-shift system until June 2023 so the workers went on strike on 24th March 2023. In order to stop the uprising of the workers, the business allowed the workers to vote whether they wanted to go back to the 2-shift system, which would have to involve lay-offs, or to stay with the 3-shift system without lay-offs and a 1,000 Baht shift bonus.  The voting was not anonymous, and the workers had to mention their names and worker ID # in the voting form.
remediation_action: The business called Issara with a request to help explain the situation to the workers and that they should agree to keep on with the 3-shift system.  Issara declined and noted that we are not here to side with the business and communicate this message that the business requested.
remediation_validation: The workers voted to move back to the 2-shift system and this ended with the business laying off more than 1,000 workers.  The workers that had reported the issue about the business trying to pressure them to keep to the 3-shift system have been let go.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case with a poor rating. The business has resorted to laying off workers when workers expressed their request to work on a 2-shift system.

description: Issues with regular shift hours or other shift issues: violation of law and/or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client is reporting about the abusive line supervisor in her working line. The line supervisor's name is Siriwat, and the workers call her “Wa-Na-Yai”. She is managing line no.1,2,3,4, wearing “Yellow Cap” in Fish Peeling Line in Building-1. The workers have to arrive at work by 6:30 AM and sometimes they have to work until 4:30 PM without getting OT payment although the working hour is between “7:00AM-4:00 PM”. If the workers have not arrived at the working line by 6:30 to 6:40 PM, she shouts at the workers and she treats them poorly. Sometimes, she also asks the workers to stay until 4:20PM or 4:30PM when they are not finished with their workload. The workers do not get the OT payment for the extra 20-30 min working hours. The line supervisor is punishing the workers to take leave without pay when she finds out that there is some fish bone and blood in the fish flesh/meant they have peeled. Before this kind inspection of fish bone and blood were allowed until 4-5 trays per day. But now, when the bone and blood are found in the fish meat by 2 trays, the line supervisor gives a punishment to those workers not to do OT and not to come to work by having them taking leave without pay. Sometimes, the workers thought that the supervisor would deliberately get some fish blood and bone and she just put this to the fish meat/flesh so that QC found this when they were checking. Because the workers said they tried their best not to include the fish blood and meat in the fish they have peeled. So the workers said, it would be good if the business can have an investigation about this.

TPs:
- Does the company have a practice where workers are required to report to work earlier than their work shift hours?  If so, how is the clock-in / clock-out system recording the hours worked and are they paid for all the time on the job?

Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter where workers are saying they are not being fully paid for the time they are working and if they peel fish in a way that doesn't meet the company standards they are penalized for it by being asked to leave and not being paid for it
- Ensure safeguards for workers and that supervisors understand the company's non-retaliation policy
- According to the investigation results, discipline the supervisors that did not follow company policy in regards to paying workers fully and not penalizing them for mistakes that may be made accidentally by workers
- Communicate with all workers that they will be paid fairly for all the hours they work and clarify how their hours worked are logged properly so that they are paid fully. Also, clarify that no workers would be penalized unreasonably for mistakes that may be made by workers on the job.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that a line supervisor managing several lines would force workers to arrive at work by 6:30AM and sometimes they have to work until 4:30 PM without getting OT payment for the additional time worked (the working shift is between 7AM-4PM). The line supervisor is also punishing the workers to take leave without pay when she finds out that there is some fish bone and blood in the fish meat they have peeled. Sometimes, the workers suspect that the supervisor would deliberately put some fish blood and bone into the fish meat to get them in trouble because the workers tried their best to prepare the fish meat according to the required standards.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Ensure supervisors are trained to properly implement company policies related to logging the time worked by workers and paying them fully for those hours

remediation_issara_recommendation:
On July 15th, during an immigration check-in at RS Cannery, Burmese workers were instructed to report to work at 3:00 p.m. after the immigration officials had left. Feeling discriminated against and uncertain about their pay for that day, some workers chose not to return. When they came back on July 16th, they were allowed to work but were then suspended for three additional days by line supervisors due to their absence during the immigration visit. This issue would not have occurred if the Burmese workers had not been asked to hide and report at 3 p.m.

If Issara addresses the three-day suspension, it could lead to the workers who reported the issue being easily identified and facing retaliation.

BHR Recommendations and Talking Points:
-Highlight the discriminatory practice of asking Burmese workers to hide during immigration visits.
-Emphasize the confusion and uncertainty faced by the workers regarding their work schedule and pay.
-Point out the unfair suspension of workers who were absent due to the unclear instructions.
-Address the potential risk of retaliation against workers who reported the issue to Issara.
-Conduct a thorough review of current policies regarding worker attendance during inspections.
-Ensure policies are clear, fair, and communicated effectively to all workers.
-Ensure all workers are treated equally during inspections and not asked to hide based on their nationality.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
#Issue 1 Context: According to workers' feedback, they can now use the toilet throughout the working day, however, there are workers from a building 4 that still have issues with toilet breaks.

Recommendations: Allow workers to use the toilet throughout the working day instead of only allowing them to use the toilet during their 60-minute total break time.

4 Nov 2020
The workers from building 4, the circuit producing line, downstairs reported that they are still having difficulties accessing the toilet breaks.

Additional talking points: 
-Workers said that they have to find someone to replace them to access the toilet break, what has the business done to address this issue? 


#Issue 2. 
(14-Aug-20) 
Context; Long OT working hours with an insufficient break; The workers have to work for around 6 hours of OT but only 30 minutes of break for the whole 6 hours. This is the issue that comes from Building - 4 and Buiding 9. However, the workers also reported that there are some of the lines in the same building which has no OT at all.

Issara recommendations.

-The business should immediately investigate and to revise their OT policy and the breaks before and during overtime working hours. Base on the result of investigations, the business should take action should guarantee that the policy is aligned with Thai law and the buyer's CoC. And there should be disciplinary action towards those who do not follow the policy. 

-The break schedule should be aligned with the labor protection act (there should be a break after 5 consecutive hours and 20 minutes of break before starting more than 2 hours of OT work). 

Talking Points:

-Ask the business about their OT break schedule in general and specific to this building. Why are some workers in the same building receiving 6 hours of OT and some of them are not receiving any at all? Are these increasing OT hours happening because of increased production? 

-Is the business aware of the HP COC and the maximum hours of OT for workers during COVID-19? 

-Explain to the business that workers should not be working more than 5 hours without a break and only 30 minutes of break for 6 hours of OT is not enough for the workers health. 

-Explain the business that the workers should get 20 minutes of break after their normal working hours. 

Update Oct 4, 2020
-Share with the business that the workers are being asked to work more than 5 consecutive hours during the OT work, which is a violation of the law according to Act B.E.2541, Article 27.

Reference : 
Act B.E.2541, Article 27; 
On a Working Day, an Employer shall arrange a rest period during work for an Employee of not less than one hour per day after the Employee has been working for not more than five consecutive hours. An Employer and Employee may agree in advance that each rest period may be less than one hour but the total rest period per day shall not be less than one hour. Whereas an Employer and Employee agree to specify rest periods during work other than paragraph one, the agreement shall be applicable only if it is more favorable to the Employee. Whereas any Overtime Work after normal working time is more than two hours, the
The employer shall arrange for the Employee to take a rest period of not less than twenty minutes before the Employee commences the Overtime Work.

Time frame   
1 pay period.
