remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers from the Pla-Sud line reported about OT working hours not being informed in advance, workers not getting 20 minutes of breaks before starting OT hours, workload being discriminatively distributed against the nationality however, the worker did not give full consent to Issara to raise this issue with the business. 

Talking Points

-We understand that TU has a no retaliation policy that should be used to protect workers when they share their grievances through any channel. So we would like to learn more about TUF investigation processes whenever there is a case that is affecting workers on a small working line. 
-How would HR investigate a case, if the issue is connected to the line supervisors? How would sage guards be put in place to make sure workers on the small working line are not targeted or seen negatively by the supervisor or other employees? Can you please describe the process of investigation?
-When the business conducts an investigation involving a line supervisor, is the supervisor notified about the issue in that specific production line? Or how is that information handled?
-If workers have an issue from a small line but also have concerns about being retaliated by the supervisor, what is the business’s strategy to resolve such issues in such condition? 
-Has the TUF communicated about TUs no-retaliation policy to all workers and supervisors? If so, when and how? If not, any plan for that? 
Because workers express not being aware of the TUs’ no retaliation policy.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Since the worker did not give consent to share the issue with the business and it also has risks to share the name of the production line with the business as it is a small production with a small number of workers, Issara approached the business to learn about their process of investigation for such kind of issues where has risks for the workers being target by their supervisors as it is a small room. Issara checked with the business about their No Rataliaiton posily. The business responded that  No retaliation policy has been implemented since 2015, this was communicated to all workers in both Thai and Burmese languages. This is also emphasized in the annual training. Therefore, workers feel to raise their concern directly to HR. In addition to that, the business's external audit also has not found any issue with the compliance of the policy. The business added having different ways to conduct the investigation based on the issues. As the business response was not very clear for raised concern, the Issara team decided to escalate with the presentation with the Thai Union Groups team about the issues that need systemic improvement.

Timeframe 1 week

description: Issues with breaks including lunch/bathroom/OT breaks: violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The worker mentioned that whenever visitors come to visit the production line, there is always an announcement for the workers to be prepared and stay at the working place until the visitors leave. So, the workers need to be at their place for about 2–3 hours and can't go anywhere, even to the toilet. During that time, it is very difficult for some workers as they need to go to the toilet.

Moreover, these are some requests and concerns that the worker would like to raise with the business for consideration:
1. During working hours, some workers went outside to get some coffee and eat food. Now the business is very restricted because the workers used the toilet break time to do something else. The restriction makes sense to the worker, but they ask for understanding as the nature of work is hard for them; they need to stand for long hours and work a lot. They need to fill in more energy by eating or getting a cup of coffee to be awake, well-concentrated, and more productive. If the worker goes out for more than 15 minutes, they will accept that it is their fault.
2. The worker is happy to work in GFPT, but the business should consider motivating the workers more, such as by providing a due diligence allowance. By providing such an allowance, the workers will be more happy, and it is helpful to support the worker's lives in the inflationary moment (price increases in the market).

TPs:
- What are the company's expectations of the workers when there are external visitors? Workers received the communication that they must be in their working lines and cannot leave, even to go to the toilet.  Is this the company's policy?
- Are workers allowed to go to the toilets when needed? Is there a time limit given to the workers?
- Are there general breaks (not toilet breaks) provided to workers? If so, when (i.e. 15 minutes in the morning and 15 minutes in the afternoon)?

Recommendations:
- Investigate how this announcement is being made and enforced on the working line.  Regardless of whether there are visitors or not, workers should be allowed to take toilet breaks when needed for the sake for their health
- Communicate clearly to workers regarding the use of toilets when needed.  If there are general breaks, remind workers about these breaks as well, when workers can get some coffee and snacks if they want to.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 25 Jan 2024

K. Sarayuth stated that workers can use the toilets freely, even if they have visitors. However, the production might work as a good arrangement when hosting visitors. They will look into what was happening on the production line. They will also communicate clearly to workers about the use of toilets when needed by February 15th.


Adding some requests and concerns from the workers:
1. They stated that if workers request a toilet break, they must use the toilets as requested but not eat food and take too long time during working hours. GFPT provides coffee and snack breaks at different times.

2. HR is aware of the attendant incentive requested by workers. HR is currently meeting with the Worker Welfare Committee. And they will conduct a worker survey to gather useful information for discussing the attendant incentive with top management.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that whenever there are visitors, there is always an announcement for the workers to be prepared and stay in their working lines for 2-3 hours until the visitors leave. During this time, they can't go anywhere, even to the toilet.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Consider instituting break times, if this is not available already. Consult workers as to what breaks would be most preferred by them, to increase motivation and productivity in the workplace.

validate with the workers.
update the business response.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
(24-August -2020) 
Context; The issue with the workers not getting 20 minutes of break before starting OT for more than 2 hours. This Issue comes from TUM factory 1, Fish packaging line, 4th floor of the Main building. The supervisors with red cap forcing the workers to do OT. ID - 10723

Issara recommendations 

-The business to conduct an investigation to identify the workers the root cause of the issue. 
-The investigation should be conducted ethically taking into account safeguards for the workers. 
-The business to make sure that all workers have a break before starting OT for more than 2 hours. 
-The break schedule should be aligned with the labor protection act (there should be a break after 5 consecutive hours). 
-Workers' OT working hours should reflect on the payslip. 

ime Frame 1 pay period.
remediation_notes:
-How are the OT hours being recorded and how are the OT payments being made?
-Do the workers have access to look back at their recorded OT working hours?
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business should make an announcement on break policy before starting OT. 

-All OT hours worked must be officially recorded and payments must be reflected in the workers' payslip.

-The business should revise their OT policy if needed. 

-Recommend Issara Academy training to HR and supervisors.  

-Issara can also provide tailored training to full HR teams on-site, and provide systems review with tailored recommendations to eliminate labour risks."

remediation_issara_recommendation:
#Issue 1
The business should immediately investigate and revise their lunch break schedule. The break schedule should be aligned with the labour protection act (there should be a break after 5 consecutive hours) 

-The business to immediately investigate these specific lines.  
-The business to revise its lunch break policy.
-The business to make sure that all workers have rest after 5 hours of consecutive work.

1 week.

#Issue 2. (13-October). ID - 11457
Workers should not be asked to work for more than 5 hours without having a break. The business should be clear with line supervisors (and others responsible of break times) that workers should have break time no later than completing 5 hours of work. If this isn't followed, the business should take disciplinary actions towards those not following this regulation.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
25-Sep-2020
Business response 
The business admitted that there was a break issue (working
more than 5 hours before taking a break) because during that period they had an external audit visit to the factory. The workers need to prepare the line for the visit which caused some workers to work more than 5 hours before a break. For the resolution, The business scheduled the break for this line at 11.30 a.m., and in case if there is a visitor, they will take turns to take a break.

9 Nov,2020
 HR coordinated with the line to investigate the issue in the fish-peeling line, where the workers have to work longer than 5 hours before taking break. They found that there was an issue in the dau shift when the audit visit. There were 2 workers reported that they have to work more than 5 hours before taking a break, to prepare the line, but this was happen a long time ago. After that the supervisor arrange that break time at 11.00 a.m. for workers who clock in at 6.30 and 7.00 a.m. which is not over 5 hours. 

Business Solution: 
- Fish-peeling line in PF arranged the same breaktime at 11.00 a.m. for workers who clock-in at 6.30 and 7.30 a.m., The workers in other line will rotate to take a break which start from 10.30, 11.00, and 11.30 a.m. No worker will work more than 5 hours under this arrangement. If there is an audit visit, the workers will take turn to take a break, which is not over 5 hours time cap. The manager will cosider the visit time for client or audit, to avoid workers breaktime.

18 Nov-2020
Workers from Par Mint Aung, and PF3 Line stated that the lunch break issue is improved. Now in these two lines, their lunch break is not too early and not too late. The latest time is 12:00
remediation_business_steps_remaining:
-Revise business policy regarding lunch break. 

-Arrangement of break times should be done in agreement with workers. 

-Recommend Issara Academy training to HR staff. 

Issara can also provide tailored training to full HR teams on-site, and provide systems review with tailored recommendations to eliminate labour risks.
remediation_notes:
Context: Workers from a working line have been working for more than 5 consecutive hours. Workers indicated that their lunch break is very early so the working hours in the afternoon are more than 5 consecutively. This is happening at the Fish Peeling Line. Workers have their lunch break at 9 am and work till 4 pm without a break. 

Talking Points ; 

- Ask the business about their lunch break schedule in general and specific to this line.

-Explain to the business that workers should not be working more than 5 hours without a break 

-Provide recommendations for remediation and system change. When the business revise their lunch break schedule we can suggest the business to:
1. Have the lunch break of 1 hour later in the day 
or
2. Have 2 breaks one in the morning and one in the afternoon (but the total time of breaks should not be less than 1 hour) NOTE: To arrange a new schedule there should be an agreement between the employer and employee, so the business should consult with the workers how they want to take the break and come to an agreement.

description: Issues with breaks including lunch/bathroom/OT breaks: violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with breaks; workers reported if their toilet breaks per day exceed more than 40 minutes per day the extra minutes they use to go to the toilet throughout the day is deducted from their OT payment. Meaning if a worker's toilet break exceeds more than 40 minutes, workers will have to work for those exceeded minutes in their OT time and they do not get paid for those minutes of work. Production Line; MAKKEOU (packing meat),  uncooked chicken Line.


Recommendations:

-The business to investigate and take disciplinary measures towards the supervisor and/or any other staff implementing this penalty, and clarify with them the company policy and the worker's right to take toilet breaks when and as needed. 
-The business to reimburse impacted workers if the investigation finds an issue. 
-The investigation should be done with workers guaranteeing confidentiality to make sure workers feel safe to share how this practice has been impacting them and who is responsible for it. 
-The impacted workers should be provided with information on where to report if they have been impacted and what would be the process the company will take to compensate them.. 
-In addition, the business should take disciplinary measures towards the supervisor based on the results of the investigation and the company protocol. 
-Workers should be allowed to use the toilets throughout the working day and they should not be blamed or punished by cutting from the OT minutes for taking more than 40 minutes of breaks in a day.
 

timeframe 2 pay period
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The business - Apr 22, 2021; The OT is for the company (supervisor can assign any worker who has the potential and skill to do the OT) to assign for the workers and HR agrees with this.

14-June-2021. Business response ID - 1397.

The business till suggests Issara give more information such as the date however, the business also committed to conducting the investigation and get back to issara.

Meaning if a worker's toilet break exceeds more than 40 minutes, workers will have to work for those exceeded minutes in their OT time and they do not get paid for those minutes of work.
remediation_action: Initially, the business response focused on how OT is assigned at the discretion of supervisors.  On June 14, 2021, the business committed to looking further into this issue and also requested additional information.

description: Issues with breaks including lunch/bathroom/OT breaks: violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: 1) the issue with the workers being asked to work long hours of OT without 20 minutes of break across the factory including VNP line, 2) Workers having to start working since 6:30 to 12 (more than 5 hours without a break) and 3) workers receiving only 2 toilet breaks per day and not receiving OT if they take more than 15 minutes for a toilet break. 

1)Regarding OT hours without break: The business should immediately investigate and take action to make sure business practices are aligned with the LPA. The OT working hours schedule should be in accordance with the labour protection act, which indicates that there should be a 20 minutes break before starting OT work if the overtime period is longer than 2 hours. 

2)The business to make sure that all workers have rest before they start OT for more than 2 hours of work. 

3) Regarding more than 5 hours of work before lunch: the business to immediately investigate across the factory, adjust the break time as necessary (with workers' consent)to make sure workers' breaks are aligned with the LPA regulations. To adjust the break time, the business should consult with workers and make clear announcements of the new break schedules. (Legal reference: Workers being asked to work more than 5 hours of work before is the violation of the LPA). 

4) Regarding toilet breaks the business should not limit the frequency of using the toilet. Toilet breaks are health-related break so that the workers should be allowed to access it as needed.     
-Immediately make a verbal and written announcement reaching all workers and line supervisors about allowing toilet breaks throughout the working day as needed by workers.


Timeframe: Within 5 business working days.

Talking Points:

Ask the business about their OT break schedule and toilet breaks in general and specific to this line.

-The business should immediately investigate this specific line supervisor. The investigation should include worker voice with the safeguards for the workers, which implies protecting and guaranteeing confidentiality during and after the investigation process to avoid any kind of retaliation.

-Workers breaks should not be interfered by anyone in order to them to complete targets. Therefore, it is recommended for the business to communicate this to all line supervisors and to encourage workers to use any grievance mechanisms they like to report such issues. 

-Workers should not be followed when they take toilet breaks given that that is unethical and violates workers privacy.

description: Issues with breaks including lunch/bathroom/OT breaks: violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the breaks. Workers reported not receiving proper breaks during their lunch time and also before starting OT hours. They said that they take only 15 to 20 minutes of break as they have the pressure to complete the target by the end of the working hours. This is also reported from the production line called (Roung Thor).

Recommendations: 
The business should conduct an investigation across the factory to identify the root cause of the issue. The investigation should be conducted by the HR. All of the workers' information during the investigation process should be kept confidential.
The investigation should include workers' voices and the no retaliation policy to be explained with the line supervisor and manager to avoid the retaliation that can take place during and after the investigation. 


The business shall take action towards the staff that violates the business policy regarding breaks hours. 
All workers should have a rest period of not less than one hour for their lunch and at least 20 mins before starting OT if their OT hours are more than 2 hours according to the LPA section No.27.  
OT working hours should be aligned with the LPA and the buyer's COC. 

Talking Points: 
Is the business aware that workers are not receiving one full hour of breaks during their lunch time? 
What is the OT hours policy for the workers per week? If the OT hours are more than 12 hours per week based on the buyer's COC, has this been communicated with Nike? 

ETI; Goal: All workers have the right to take lunch breaks, in line with the law, which specifies minimum amount of time allowable. Further, workers should be allowed to take bathroom breaks whenever needed. Limiting use of bathrooms for the purpose of controlling or maximizing productivity can have adverse effects on the health of workers, and should be strictly prohibited. Breaks are required by law as well, in between regular working hours and OT shifts.

Code: ETI Base Code 6.1. Working hours are not excessive; must comply with national laws, collective agreements
Description: Working hours must comply with national laws, collective agreements, and the provisions of 6.2 to 6.6 below, whichever affords the greater protection for workers. Sub-clauses 6.2 to 6.6 are based on international labour standards.
LPA Section 27. On a Working Day, an Employer shall arrange a rest period during work for an Employee of not less than one hour per day after the Employee has been working for not more than fve consecutive hours. An Employer and Employee may agre in advance that each rest period may be less than one hour but the total rest period per day shall not be less than one hour. Whereas an Employer and Employee agree to specify rest periods during work other than paragraph one, the agreement shall be applicable only if it is more favourable to the Employee. A rest period during work shall not be counted as working time except where the total rest period is more than two hours per day, where the amount of time exceeding two hours shall be counted as normal working time. Whereas any Overtime Work after normal working time is more than two hours, the Employer shall arrange for the Employee to take a rest period of not less than twenty minutes before the Employee commences the Overtime Work. The provisions in paragraph one and paragraph four shall not apply where an Employee is required to do work of a continuous nature or character with the consent of the Employee, or in case of emergency work.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara has escalated this issue with the business, the business was not aware of the Nike policy regarding OT working hours. The business responded and said that they will conduct an investigation and get back to Issara. 

The business reply that the workers receive one hour of breaks within a day with several breaks. It was not clear if the business has actually conducted the investigations with the workers. The business also did not provide the break rest hour breakdown with Issara. Workers update has been conflicting with the business response. 

Issara has escalated this issue with Nike team given that the response from the Everest management was concerning, however, there was no clear response from the Nike team. Issara has requested the Nike team to have a try party call to discuss this issue  but Nike has not respond on this request for several weeks. 
Since Issara has raised this issue with the relevant responsible team, however, there was no proper support for the proper investigation and the remediation, Issara considers closing this case with poor remark.
remediation_notes: Workers reported not receiving sufficient lunch breaks and OT rest periods due to high workload as the factory has reduced the number of workers, and a worker needs to monitor many machines (30-40 textile machines).  Workers are allowed only a 15-minute break during an 8-hour shift and another 15-minute break for 4 OT hours. And sometimes, workers don't even get rest if the machines have problems or the clothes are ruined because the line supervisor will report to Taiwanese manager and deduct their wages for any product damage.  They were not allowed to take a nap during break time and even if they were sick, the supervisor would deny sick leave and not allow them to go home until they finished their duty hours.  Workers need to work 12 hours including OT, and they feel sick and don't want to work OT, the factory still requires them to do OT.  If they refuse to do OT, they will be punished by not getting OT for the next week.
remediation_action:
This issue was escalated to the business management team.  The business said it was not aware that Nike’s policy for maximum OT hours per week is 12 hours, not 24 hours.  The business also talked about how some workers were not really sick but asked for sick leave and produced MCs that are very easy to get in Thailand and were abusing the sick leave policy. 

The business investigated, and stated that workers are normally given a full one-hour break, but they are required to take multiple breaks within an eight-hour workday. As a result, workers will be given a full hour of break time over the course of the working day.
remediation_validation: Workers have confirmed that they get only a fifteen-minute break during the whole 8-hour working period, which conflicts with the business' investigation resuts.
remediation_results: The business saying that workers get a full hour break spread out over the 8-hour work day conflicts with what the workers have reported.  Also, the business suggested some workers were taking advantage of the sick leave policy to take off work even when they are not sick, which is shifting blame to the worker rather than taking seriously the worker reports that they were being denied sick leave.  Considering that this is the response after escalation to the management, and further action is not likely to be taken, we are closing this case with a poor rating.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
System Change; 
The business to clearly communicate with the line supervisor, manager and the production about the business plan to improve this issue. 
The communication should take place in written and verbal in all workers language. 
Issara to provide training to the HR and the line supervisor.

-The business shall conduct an investigation regarding the manager's behavior and take the necessary disciplinary actions towards this person.

 In order to assess the behavior of the manager, the business can conduct an investigation by talking with workers under this line supervisor or can conduct a survey where workers can rate their supervisors and managers confidentially. Given that workers may not know their supervisors and managers' Thai names, it is recommended that the business arrange an org-chart with all supervisors/and managers' names and titles. 

-There should not be any coercion or retaliation towards workers during the investigation and survey processes. The investigation process must be confidential, workers should not be required to provide any of their personal information, such as working IDs, their names, etc. And workers participating in the investigation should be protected from any kind of retaliation by anyone. 

-The business should create a plan of action based on the results of investigations and surveys. Such actions should include training and disciplinary actions (if necessary). 

-The workers should be treated humanely. 

Talking points. 
-What is the target set for the workers in this line? 
-Workers have reported an increased target setting since this supervisor/manager has started working in this production line, is that the HR and production decision? If yes, were there any communications about the changes?

description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by HR/production (illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the poor treatment of the supervisor. Workers said that the supervisor from UC1, in line no.2 (blue hat) named P'Soup is abusive toward migrant workers. He treats Burmese workers more poorly than Thai workers. The abusive words that he uses are such as, yelling, saying “what’s wrong with your poor eyes, can’t you check it clearly, And so on. In addition to that workers said that the supervisor also indirectly forces them to do OT. If a worker do not agree or refuse to do OT, the supervisor will not provide OT for the next 15 days. Workers want the supervisors to treat them equally and be fair with the OT hours. 

TPs:
Has the business received any complaint from workers about this supervisor? If yes, what was the action that has been taken? 
What is the OT distribution system? What happens if a worker does not sign up to work OT on any given day?  Does this affect OT hours offered to the worker in the future?
What channels are available for workers to report any issues? How are these channels being communicated to the workers? Are the business channels being used by the workers (if any)? 

Recommendations for remediation:
The business to conduct an investigation about the behavior of this supervisor. The investigation process should include worker voice and safeguards in place so that workers don’t suffer any retaliation as a result.
Disciplinary action should be taken if the supervisor is found guilty of having mistreated and discriminated against the workers. 
The business should also make a clear announcement to the workers about its zero tolerance against discrimination and verbal abuse in the workplace, and the OT distribution policy.


Code: ETI Base Code 6.3. Working hours are not excessive; all OT is voluntary and paid at a premium rate no less than 125% of regular pay
Description: All overtime shall be voluntary. Overtime shall be used responsibly, taking into account all the following: the extent, frequency and hours worked by individual workers and the 
workforce as a whole. It shall not be used to replace regular employment. Overtime shall always be compensated at a premium rate, which is recommended to be not less than 125% of the regular rate of pay.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change:
Provide a refresher to all supervisors about the company’s policies against discrimination and verbal abuse, the fair and voluntary OT system, and how they are to implement them in practice

supplier_name: Daorae (Desa Sri Hartamas) Sdn Bhd, a Korean BBQ restaurant
description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by HR/production (illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client worked at a Korean BBQ restaurant located in KL Kepong Jalan Metro Perdana, which is one of fifteen branches of the restaurant chain. Out of the fifteen branches, this particular one was problematic. The restaurant has six Nepali and thirteen Burmese workers. The owner's son is abusive towards the Nepali workers, creating a hostile work environment. Issara is able to speak with two workers. They have been working for this employer for 10 months. They are all MoU workers. They are reporting as a group of 5 Nepali workers, but the client is quietly reporting. The client and the workers want to either be transferred to another branch under the same company or find employment in another company. The client has debts to pay and doesn't want to return to Nepal. The workers have a contract they made in Nepal, but the company made another contract which the client doesn't have and is unaware of its contents.
Following are the major issues reported by workers.

1) Document retention: Workers passports are held by the employer since they started their employment. The company also kept their passports and didn't provide them with worker ID cards (Jalan cards) or necessary documents. 

2) Restriction of Movement: The workers were not allowed to leave the premises, and this restriction also made it difficult for their friends to visit them.

3) Unfair suspension: Workers were frequently suspended for minor mistakes or even without any reason. During these suspensions, the company did not provide any food, and the workers were not allowed to go out and get their own. They were also denied access to basic amenities, like cooling fans, during these periods. One incident occurred when a friend of the client was suspended for simply asking a Burmese worker to clean a stain. The owner verbally abused him and kept him in detention (suspension) for 28 days. Throughout this time, the company did not provide any food or salary, leaving the workers in a dire situation. His friends attempted to provide food secretly, but they had to be cautious as the company would punish them if they were caught bringing in more substantial amounts of food or any food. 

Recently, the victim was suspended by the company for two months. During this period, he received no salary or food from the company. The suspension was a result of the employer demanding the victim to memorize the restaurant menu quickly.

If workers demand to change the employer, they are asked to work 4 months without pay and there are some workers who have accepted this situation as they could not bear the harsh working environment. 

4)Physical abuse: Physical assault includes being kicked, slapped on the face and belly, and having ears pulled. The employer even physically assaulted the client's genitals. Such harassment occurred almost daily and targeted everyone except.

5) Long working hours and incorrect payment: Workers have to work 14-15 hours a day. In return, they received a basic salary of 1500 RM and a 300 RM overtime allowance each month. 

6) Lack of Sick Leave: Even when the workers fell ill, they were forced to work, as the owner wouldn't allow them to stay in the hostel. 



Moreover, during salary payment time, the owner would abuse the workers and suspend them for minor mistakes. The owner often used the workers as a target for his frustrations, taking out his stress related to the business on them. Whenever the business is slow he will start abusing the worker for no reason.

description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by interpreter (illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A group of 11 workers who have submitted resignation a week ago and were preparing to depart are not being allowed to go by the business. The workers reported that their belongings were taken by the business when they were about to leave in a van and that they now do not have a place to stay since they have already given back their rooms. Workers reported the reason for leaving job is as follows:
(1) discrimination against nationalities at the workplace,
(2) the business not keeping the promise of paying double for the working hours during COVID-19 restriction as promised,
(3) translator not being helpful and being biased by just listening to the business and not the workers. 

Recommendations: 
-As it is a worker's right to resign and leave the company, the business shall immediately investigate why this group of workers were not allowed to leave. And then come to an agreement with workers for their departure from the company without restrictions.
-Since the business made the taxi driver leave without the workers, it will be challenging for workers to find a new driver, therefore, the business is suggested to help workers find a new taxi/van for workers safe return. -Since the vaccination is a workers personal health matter, the business should provide vaccination cards or any support documents as proof that workers have received vaccination. If the business does not have such documents, the business should coordinate with the health organization that provided the vaccine to make sure all workers receive the vaccination card. 
-The business should immediately check with all workers and provide their missing daily wages if any. 

System Change:
-It is the  business responsibility to have good working conditions that allows workers to feel ethically and fairly treated. This will reduce workers turnover rates, as workers would not feel the need to leave the job. In order to assess the level of satisfaction of workers and identify the areas of improvement, the business is recommended to conduct an internal survey or Issara’s worker satisfaction survey to address the root cause of the issue and improve the system. 
-The business to communicate with the HR and the security guard about the business policy on freedom of movement and rights to make decisions. The communication should include the action that will be taken against the offender. 
-The business should communicate with all the workers about their plan to improve the working conditions and maintain the workers. Otherwise, there could be more workers planning to leave the job. 

Talking Points: 
-What is the reason why this group of workers were stopped by HR? 
-Is business aware of this issue? 
-Workers have reported several workers leaving the job because of several repeated issues in the workplace, what is the business understanding of this? Does the business seek workers' feedback and have done anything to improve the working condition rather than stopping workers from leaving? 
- What was communicated to workers as reasons for not being allowed to leave the company?
-What was the reason for the business calling the police and threatening the workers? 

Added TPs; 
Because workers have resigned and are asking to depart, this situation should be addressed in less than the 3-4 day timeline suggested by SCC.
No resigned worker can be held against their will, or coerced into returning to work
Resigned workers can be provided vaccine certificates and COVID tests to ensure there are no positive cases before departure
Workers can be clearly offered a return to work, with no coercion, and with clear communication on next steps
Because this situation has escalated, Issara can jointly speak with HR and the group of workers if desired, to support communication.
Issara also recommends we provide training to HR reps at SCC, on COVID and other protocols for workforce management.

ETI Base Code 1.2. Employment is freely chosen; workers not required to lodge deposits or documents with employer, and free to leave with reasonable notice

Workers off-shift should be free to leave their workplace and dormitories, with no threats or assertions of control over their movements. Workers should never be treated as the property of employers, recruiters, brokers, or agents; and, their movements should never be restricted by these actors. Workers should be free to leave their jobs with reasonable notice.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had meetings including escalation call with the business immediately. The business argued that since the workers are under Bubble and Seal measures, it is not allowed for them to cross the     Bubble and Seal area and the COVID-19 provincial cross restriction. The business also added that since the taxi driver who came to pick up the workers was from another province, the business take it as illegal act , therefore the business wanted to make sure that their workers are not being cheated by the brokers. In addition to that the business added that they have responsibility to inform the policy about workers departure. Issara emphasized that since the workers have already submitted their resignation and they do not feel they are belong to SCC anymore, the business has no liability to control the workers movement. The business responded that they will escalate to their MD and get back to Issara.  It has been 4 four days that the workers are being forced to stay in the the SCC B&S housing against their will.
remediation_notes: A group of 11 workers who had submitted their resignation letters a week prior were preparing to depart by van when they were not being allowed to go by HR staff and the security guard.  They also packed up and left the company dormitory so now have no place to stay.
remediation_action:
Issara reached out to the business immediately.  The business explained that HR had communicated to the workers about the government's travel restrictions to prevent the spread of Covid-19, and that they are not allowed to travel outside Songkhla province because it is currently a Covid-19 red zone.  They said police had come to enforce the travel restrictions and the van driver left without taking the workers after talking to the police.  Regarding vaccination certificates that would be important for when the workers travel back to Myanmar, the business said the document issuance was delayed by the hospital and would be provided to the workers when issued.  For now, the business said the workers are still living in the private dorm and the workers can ask the landlord to stay in the same place. 

The business will get back to Issara with corrective actions within 3-5 days.

The business further updated Issara saying pictures of HR staff with negative comments regarding this incident had been posted on social media and they wanted the workers to remove the posts.

Issara escalated this issue with TU's Sustainability Director, and recommended that no worker that had already resigned should be held against their will or coerced into returning to work.  TU explained that they didn't want the workers leaving the province illegally given the current Covid-19 restrictions.  The Sustainability Director said they would escalate the matter to the factory MD.  The following day, TU completed the process of issuing official separation documents for the workers so that they can leave.
remediation_validation:
Issara followed up with the workers and provided an update, explaining that the business had said they were following government rules of not allowing inter-provincial travel and that the business would get to Issara in 3-5 days about next steps.  

The workers did not want to stay there anymore; they felt pressured and forced to go back to work.  They were even willing to pay any government fines if there were any for crossing province lines.  Since they have resigned, they don't understand why the business is not letting them leave.  They just want to be able to travel back to Myanmar. 

Regarding the social media posts, the workers said they did not take any photos or videos during the incident nor did they post anything on social media or ask their friends to do so.

The workers have confirmed that they have officially resigned from their jobs and are free to leave.
remediation_results: The business processed the official resignation of the workers and the workers have been allowed to leave.

remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had meetings including escalation calls with TU's Sustainability Director and recommended that no workers that had already resigned should be held against their will or coerced into returning to work.  TU explained that they didn't want the workers leaving the province illegally given the current Covid-19 restrictions.  The Sustainability Director said they would escalate the matter to the factory MD. The following day, TU completed the process of issuing official separation documents for the workers. However, workers were held by the business against their will for 3 days. In addition to that, the workers mentioned having some missing payments for their daily wages from the business. Workers added that they refused to wait for the business to conduct the investigation for their missing payment as they wanted to leave the area as soon as possible. However, it is the business's responsibility to make sure that all workers are paid all of their wages upon their departure. Having a debt to pay to the workers after they left their job is against the local law. Issara is checking with the workers if they want the business to process their missing payment since they are free from business control. If the workers request Issara to discuss with the business, the issue will be opened under other KPI related to the missing payment. In general, workers added that two-third of Burmese workers have left the business by several means because of the poor working conditions.

Issara reached out to the business immediately.  The business explained that HR had communicated to the workers about the government's travel restrictions to prevent the spread of Covid-19, and that they are not allowed to travel outside Songkhla province because it is currently a Covid-19 red zone.  They said police had come to enforce the travel restrictions and the van driver left without taking the workers after talking to the police.  Regarding vaccination certificates that would be important for when the workers travel back to Myanmar, the business said the document issuance was delayed by the hospital and would be provided to the workers when issued.  For now, the business said the workers are still living in the private dorm and the workers can ask the landlord to stay in the same place. 

The business will get back to Issara with corrective actions within 3-5 days.

The business further updated Issara saying pictures of HR staff with negative comments regarding this incident had been posted on social media and they wanted the workers to remove the posts.

Issara escalated this issue with TU's Sustainability Director, and recommended that no worker that had already resigned should be held against their will or coerced into returning to work.  TU explained that they didn't want the workers leaving the province illegally given the current Covid-19 restrictions.  The Sustainability Director said they would escalate the matter to the factory MD.  The following day, TU completed the process of issuing official separation documents for the workers so that they can leave.

Regarding the wages, the business noted that they could investigate what had happened with workers wages and compensate workers accordingly.
remediation_validation:
Issara followed up with the workers and provided an update, explaining that the business had said they were following government rules of not allowing inter-provincial travel and that the business would get to Issara in 3-5 days about next steps.  

The workers did not want to stay there anymore; they felt pressured and forced to go back to work.  They were even willing to pay any government fines if there were any for crossing province lines.  Since they have resigned, they don't understand why the business is not letting them leave.  They just want to be able to travel back to Myanmar. 

Regarding the social media posts, the workers said they did not take any photos or videos during the incident nor did they post anything on social media or ask their friends to do so.

description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by line supervisor/mgt (illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers being forced to take Andrographis (fah talay jone) by the line supervisor in building 2, the Shrimp processing line. Workers reported that they are forced to take fah talay jone in front of the line supervisor before they start their shift. The worker reported not being aware of the benefit of it, however having concern about the side effect. 

Talking Points: 
-The workers reported being forced to take them in front of the line supervisor and that these are provided for free. Why are workers being forced to consume medicine? Has there been any communication from the business to line supervisors or general workers about the consumption of this medicine? If so, what has been communicated?  
-Who made the decision to provide this medicine to workers, what is the company policy about this, and has this been consulted with medical professionals? 

Recommendation; 
The business is suggested to conduct an investigation and stop this practice immediately. 
The supervisor and the other involved staff should be communicated immediately about why this action is not acceptable and what will be the disciplinary actions the business will take as a result of their actions, and also the consequences of any similar practice happens again in the future. Forcing workers to consume medicine should be taken by the business as a serious and unacceptable behavior. 
Workers should not be asked to take any medication, especially without the prescription of licensed medical professionals, and without them being aware of what they are taking, and without their consent.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had an immediate escalation call with the business,the business responded that it was consulted and prescribed by the medical professionals and meant to control the COVID-19 infections. However, the business argued that it is not forced to take this medicine, therefore, the business agreed to conduct the communication and make it clear that no workers are forced to do  so. The business later updated having the communication about the voluntaryness to take the provided medicine. Issara is checking with the workers.
remediation_notes: Workers reported being forced to take Andrographis (fah talay jone) by the line supervisors in building 2, the Shrimp processing line. The workers were not aware of its benefits but had heard of the potential negative side effects.
remediation_action: This issue will be escalated to the company's senior management
remediation_validation: In the process of discussing with the business; worker validation will follow after business has taken action
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
The business shall make verbal and written announcements to all employees on the business policy for such issues and the disciplinary measure that will be taken towards those who do not follow the business policy. 

Relevant laws and guidelines:
-ETI base code: “3. Working conditions are safe and hygienic: 3.5 The company observing the code shall assign responsibility for health and safety to a senior management representative”. Medical recommendations should not be handled by line supervisors at any time, anything related to workers' health should be handled by senior management in an ethical and professional way.

description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by line supervisor/mgt (illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue #1. 

Case summary: Seafresh requires employees to wear two masks. On 22-Mar, a female worker who was ill and couldn't breathe did not wear one mask. When the supervisors discovered her, she stated that she couldn't breathe well and asked if she may only wear one mask. The supervisors, however, refused to accept this and dragged her out of the room, forcing her to wear two masks. She became unwell afterward and went to the hospital, but she died there. 

Recommendations:
 
-Try to contact any close relatives of the worker and get more information on what happened to her, what did the hospital say, how was she treated by the business (supervisors, interpreters, ect.)
 
-Have a call with the business and ask more information about the case:
 
Share that Issara received information from worker voice channels about a worker that was expressing not feeling well, had requested not to wear a double mask as she couldn’t breathe properly but was asked by the supervisor to wear a double mask and return to the working line. The worker later requested sick leave and later in the day passed away. 
 
Can the business provide more information about what happened with the worker, who is taking care of the investigation and what has been discovered so far? Is the business taking any actions based on the investigation results? 
 
What is the business protocol for workers that express feeling unwell during working hours? 
As part of the investigation, were the supervisor and other workers interviewed? And if so, what have they said about what happened at the working line?
Does the worker have any relatives working at Seafresh? If so, what kind of support is being provided and if not, is Seafresh already in touch with the family outside Seafresh?
Who is the RA that has recruited this worker? Has the RA been informed about what happened?

Issue #2. 

Physical abuse by Line Supervisor(Name - Mae Tar). Many workers raised that the supervisor pinches (squeeze the skin) or scrapes the workers' hands while walking around the production line. She seems to be joking, but her actions irritate the workers.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
# Issue 1. 
Seafresh said it has investigated what happened to this case.  The worker worked normally on the "value added" line on Saturday as well as the whole of that week.  This worker has worked at Seafresh for a long time, and her daughter also works there.  The business checked her sick leave history, and found that she had taken sick leave for other reasons in the past year but nothing related to her cause of death.  On Saturday, March 19 she worked a normal day 9am-6pm, with no OT.  Sunday, March 20 was a rest day.  On Monday, March 21, she reported sick and did not go to work, and informed the cleaner at 7am, and was taken to the hospital.  On Tuesday, March 22, she passed away, was informed at 2am to inform the employer and her daughter was at the hospital.  Cause of death was lung infection and blood infection, according to Chumporn Hospital.  The company has arranged for the funeral for three days, with more than 50 workers in attendance.  The business said her daughter who works in the same line as this worker had not heard her mother talk about being ill or requesting to wear only one mask during work hours.  K Pairoj noted that the company doesn’t require workers to wear double masks.  

Many workers observed the line supervisor pulling the worker out and making her wear the double mask.  Follow up with the business on the line supervisor's behavior.

IDENTIFIED POSSIBLE ROOT CAUSES
This may be due to misunderstandings between the supervisor and the worker.
1. According to the company's announcement on measures for surveillance, prevention and control of the spread of Covid-19, No. 21, dated November 10, 2022, workers must wear masks properly. The hygienic mask must be attached to the face. covering both the nose and mouth **No specifying to put 2 layers**
2. On 22-APR-2022: From a random questionnaire of 90 (50%) workers in the fresh shrimp product section, the workers stated that they are not compelled to wear two masks. Workers can only wear one mask. must be wear correctly

CORRECTIVE ACTIONS / REMEDY CONFIRMED BY SEAFRESH
22-APR-2022: Verify and explain to workers about wearing the mask correctly according to surveillance measures to prevent and control the spread of Covid-19

Issue # 2. 
For the issue with the physical abuse; Seafresh will investigate, as this is considered physical abuse and unacceptable.

IDENTIFIED POSSIBLE ROOT CAUSES
The supervisor has inappropriate teaching behavior.

CORRECTIVE ACTIONS / REMEDY CONFIRMED BY SEAFRESH
1. 04-APR-2022: Called the supervisor to come talking with attitude adjustment and the supervisor got the written warnings
2. Re-training the supervisors to know about labor protection laws. forced labor and Good Labor Practices in three sessions of the GLP & Business Ethics course on 21,22 and 23 April 2022.
3.22-APR-2022: Attach a bulletin board to educate about inappropriate behavior. The rules and regulations that what should and should not to treat with workers and contact numbers to report clues or internal complaints. In the case that inappropriate practices are found and to verify understanding with workers
remediation_notes:
Case #1: Seafresh requires employees to wear two masks. On 22-Mar, a female worker who was ill and couldn't breathe did not wear one mask. When the supervisor discovered her, she stated that she couldn't breathe well and asked if she could only wear one mask. The supervisor, however, refused to accept this and dragged her out of the room, forcing her to wear two masks. She became unwell afterwards and went to the hospital, but she died there. 

Case #2: Many workers reported that one supervisor pinches or scrapes the workers' hands while walking around and checking work on the production line. The supervisor acts like she's joking but the workers are irritated by this unwanted physical contact.
remediation_action:
Case #1: Seafresh said it investigated what happened in this case.  The deceased worker worked at Seafresh for a long time, and her daughter also works there.  The business checked her sick leave history, and found that she had taken sick leave for other reasons in the past year but nothing related to her cause of death.  On Saturday, March 19 she worked a normal day 9am-6pm, with no OT, and had worked as usual that whole week.  Sunday, March 20 was a rest day.  On Monday, March 21, she reported in sick and did not go to work, informed the cleaner at 7am, and was taken to the hospital.  In the early morning of Tuesday, March 22, at 2am, she passed away.  The cause of death was lung infection and blood infection, according to Chumphon Hospital.  The company arranged for her funeral for three days, with more than 50 workers in attendance.  The business said her daughter who works in the same line as this worker had not heard her mother talk about being ill or requesting to wear only one mask during work hours.

Regarding the requirement to wear double masks, the business confirmed that this may have been a misunderstanding and that the announcement was made on November 10, 2022, that workers must wear masks properly. The hygienic mask must be attached to the face covering both the nose and mouth, but no requirements for two masks.  On April 22, 2022, the business conducted a random questionnaire with 90 workers in the fresh shrimp product section (50% of workers in this section), and they responded that they were not compelled to wear two masks. Workers must wear one mask, and to be worn correctly.

Case #2: The business investigated and found that the supervisor was using inappropriate teaching behavior.  HR gave this supervisor a written warning and talked about adjustments needed.  The supervisor was also re-trained in business ethics.  Finally, rules and regulations on appropriate and inappropriate behavior towards workers was posted publicly, with contact numbers for workers to directly report any inappropriate behavior of supervisors.
remediation_validation: Case #1: Issara checked with workers, and they confirmed that the announcement was for workers to wear one face mask properly and two masks were not required.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that 6 Burmese informal interpreters have been pressuring workers to lend them money.  If workers refuse to lend them money, the informal interpreters will target them to be assigned to menial jobs like cleaning the production floor every day or to be moved from this line to that. If workers do lend them money, the workers often have a hard time getting it back.

TPs:
- What is the business policy in terms of money lending/borrowing among employees?
- If there is a situation of employees reporting unpaid debts from fellow employees, how does the business deal with the matter

Recommendations:
- The business should not tolerate any staff using their position to demand favors, such as loans, and retaliating against those that don't relent to their requests.
- Communicate this policy clearly to all workers, and be clear about the disciplinary actions that will be taken if staff higher up the authority chain tries to use her position to extract a favor from another employee

description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by line supervisor/mgt (illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that the manager of the shrimp peeling line in building 2 is verbally and physically abusive. She can speak Burmese and yells at workers, "Don't you have a brain to think? Why don't you understand if I tell you?" While she is yelling at the workers, she will point at them, touching their heads and pushing their shoulders. In July, she poked a female worker's eye, for which she offered no apology. The female worker feels insecure about raising the issue, even though the interpreter came to investigate.

NOTE: A few years ago, this manager had an issue with workers from Building 2, and she was moved to Building 3. She has a bad record, and the workers do not want to work with that manager anymore. The workers requested that Issara discuss this issue with the supplier and take serious action against her. The manager's name is P'Kyip.

Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter, noting that this manager has had issues with workers in the past.
- There should be zero tolerance to physical and verbal abuse.  Discipline the manager according to the company's disciplinary policy
- Communicate to all workers about the definition of verbal and physical abuse, and what is appropriate vs. unacceptable physical and verbal behavior
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Naruemon, HR, responded that HR is aware of the issue and has investigated it; the line manager has received a verbal warning and was trained by HR to improve and communicate with the workers properly.


IDENTIFIED POSSIBLE ROOT CAUSES:
The line supervisor's expectation for employees to speed up their work in accordance with the plan has led to instances of inappropriate behavior both in terms of verbal communication and physical actions.

CORRECTIVE ACTIONS / REMEDY:
From July 13-15 Jul 2023, the employee retention team conducted observations within the production area. During this time, they addressed supervisors who did inappropriate behavior and provided verbal warning notices.

Why don't you understand if I tell you?" While she is yelling at the workers, she will point at them, touching their heads and pushing their shoulders. In July 2023, she poked a female worker's eye, for which she offered no apology.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Regularly train all supervisors about the company's zero tolerance policy against verbal and physical abuse, and communicate clearly about what is considered verbal and physical abuse, and the disciplinary measures to be taken against the abusers.

description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by line supervisor/mgt (illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
#Issue 1
The issue with physically abusive supervisors. 
#Recommendations for Issue 1
-Physical assault should be responded to with an appropriate disciplinary measure.  Typical disciplinary systems include written warnings for serious infractions, followed by dismissal. 

-Physical assault on the company premises, as a serious human rights violation and violation of the Thai Criminal Code, would be expected to be met with immediate dismissal. 

Talking points:

- Disciplinary action should be taken.  Reports of crimes against workers should be addressed seriously by the company, including safeguards for reporting workers, credible investigations, and appropriate disciplinary measures.

- Cal-Comp explained they documented the incident on file but did not give the supervisor a warning.  This does not constitute an "appropriate disciplinary measure" for a violation which is essentially illegal - a violation of the Thai Criminal Code, typically punishable by fines and sometimes imprisonment.

- The lack of any disciplinary action by the business to physical assault of workers creates an environment of impunity.  This can create a high level of uncertainty and fear amongst the workforce when they see that management allows supervisors to physically assault workers with no consequences.

CLOSED 

# Issue 2 (14 Aug)
Punishment for workplace mistakes - This comes from supervisors at ATP line building 4. The worker reported that if the supervisor found the workers making workplace mistakes accidentally or the quality of work is not good enough, they are punished by being asked to stand at the corner of the working line for the whole day. ID - 10534. 

# Recommendations for Issue 2 

-The business should investigate this case in all lines from building 4 but also include other working lines to see if that is also an issue with other lines.   The investigation should be conducted ethically taking into account safeguards for the worker.  The investigation should include workers' voices.

-Disciplinary measures should be taken toward line supervisors imposing such punishment.  Typical disciplinary systems include verbal warnings and written warnings.

4 Nov, 2020
-Workers from building 4, downstairs, circuit producing line called and reported that the system to punish the workers for workplace took place very recently. This is becoming a chronic issue, Issara strongly suggests the business to take investigation and disciplinary measures toward line supervisors imposing such punishment.  Typical disciplinary systems include verbal warnings and written warnings.

Additional talking points:

(4 Nov,2020)
-The business said that they have communicated to all supervisors regarding this issue, what was the communication process? Was the communication conducted with the supervisor from this working line? 
-What is the business policy for those who against the business policy? 
-Please provide the recommendation for the system change again.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
#issue 1
Cal-Comp HR explained during the last meeting (May 8) that the business took disciplinary actions. They provided a verbal warning and a warning letter to the supervisor.
(10-Jun) : 
No announcement regarding this policy yet. No physical abuse so far.  
CLOSED 

#Issue 2

The business responded that they have done the investigation and found no issue for such a case. However, the business did communicate with all line supervisors about their policy for such activities.

Actions have been taken, however, the dismissal was not considered by the business in this case.

-The business should investigate this case in this specific line and take proper actions.  The investigation should include workers' voices. and it should be conducted ethically making sure safeguards are in place for the worker.  Keeping confidentiality during the investigation process shall be a priority   to avoid any kind of retaliation from the assistant supervisor. 

-Disciplinary measures according to the business policy should be taken toward line supervisors practicing such poor behavior towards the workers.  

-Physical assault should be responded to with an appropriate disciplinary measure.  Typical disciplinary systems include written warnings for serious infractions, followed by dismissal. 

-Physical and verbal assault on the company premises, as a serious human rights violation and violation of the Thai Criminal Code, would be expected to be met with immediate dismissal.

-Has the business received any report about this assistant supervisor from the workers in the past? If yes, what was the investigation process and the actions taken.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The business response ID. 1315

Issara has reached out to the business, the business has agreed to conduct the investigation with the specific supervisor and get back to Issara with the action plan.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for system change. 

-The business to communicate with all of the workers about the business policy for such behavior from any employees. 
-The communication should include information on the business actions to respond to this issue and avoid this kind of issue from happening again and also the disciplinary measure that would be taken for the violators of the business policy. 
-Workers shall be reminded about the grievance mechanisms they can use to report any issue/concern and the company shall explain to workers what are the safeguards for workers when making such complaints. This will help build workers' trust in the company grievance mechanisms.

remediation_notes:
#ISSUE 1
Context: The issue with the PF-3 ( Cat Food Plastic bag packaging Line), Ms Wai Wai Khaing who passed away due to stroke for not being able to access the medical care on time. 
Talking Points:
Information from worker voice: 
Recent updates from Jonah: we have many different  stories on supervisor behavior. Only thing I can confirm is that  the client  was denied sick leave. Her supervisor forced her to work OT.
Talking points:
Can the business explain what is their understanding of what happened to the worker? And what is the diagnosis and cause of death given by the doctor?
Please describe the process of the business’ investigation of the circumstances leading up to the death.  [Probe: Did the business conclude that the line supervisor denied the worker sick leave just before her death?]  
It was reported to Issara by several people that the worker requested sick leave but was denied it by the line supervisor.  It was also reported that this line supervisor forced her to work OT against her will.  She then died soon after.  
Is the business aware of the worker requesting sick leave?  Of how the line supervisor handled the worker request to take sick leave?  Of the forced OT?   
[If yes, good.  If no, then follow up with]  How do you plan to deal with the fact that a number of workers reported witnessing your line supervisor forcing a sick person to work OT and then denying her sick leave when she felt very ill, leading to her death shortly after?  [Probe: is it possible that there may be a flaw in their investigation?  Please note: what is their overall attitude?]
The business has responsibilities to the family of the worker - what has been identified by the business as its main responsibilities to the family, and what has been paid and done so far?   [Probe: Monetary compensation for the funeral, any additional compensation from the business, acknowledgement of wrongful death and an appropriate compensation]
What has been communicated to the recruitment agency?
What disciplinary actions are the business taking towards the line supervisor that forced the sick person to work OT then denied them sick leave?

# ISSUE 2
Please ask the business following questions.  

- What was the investigation process and result of this issue?
- What was the disciplinary action towards that supervisor? Did the supervisor received any training to improve the behavior? 
- How is the business monitoring the behavior of this particular supervisor to make sure that she/he does not repeat her/him behavior again. 
- Workers were denied to be shifted to different line, how does the business make sure that the workers are not being targeted by the supervisors?

Based on the findings of the facts It was discovered that the supervisor admitted to having a loud voice and a fierce face, but he did not speak rudely. So when speaking to workers at work, loud voices and facial expressions are used.

If it happens again, If it happens again, you will be punished in accordance with the company's policies.

Context:this issue is related to line supervisor treating workers poorly and threatening them to be sent to SCC if the can't reach the target. This case is related to ID call 8964.  

The business should take action by conducting a proper investigation taken into account workers feedback and guaranteeing workers safeguards. Business to provide a verbal warning to that specific supervisor.

Timeframe: one payment period
remediation_business_steps_taken:
16 March 2020 
The business said that they could not investigate individual supervisors because there are 13 supervisors in the same position from this line. That is why the business agreed to conduct communication with all of the supervisors and dos and don't regarding fair treatment on the workers. The business also added that the supervisors promised to improve their behaviour. 

20 Apr 2020
The worker reported that the line supervisors in this line are behaving better now. Since then, Issara did not receive any complaints from the workers until the month of August. That is why this case was considered to be closed.
remediation_notes:
Talking points:

-Provide information about the working line and the line supervisor. Important note for BHR: the information about the client should NOT be shared with the business, but it is safe to share the information about working line and line supervisor.

-How is the target calculated for each worker/line and how is that target communicated to workers?
- Provide recommendations for remediation and system change
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business should provide training to line supervisors on ethics and how to treat workers properly. 
-The business should inform line supervisors what are the disciplinary consequences for those who do not follow the company policies and codes of conduct. 
-The business to revise if the targets provided to workers are realist and fair to all workers. 

Communication.
-The business should communicate to worker what are the grievance mechanisms available, who the focal person is, and guarantee safeguards are in place. In case the issue is related to line supervisors, the business should provide different channels for workers to raise their concerns safely.

description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by line supervisor/mgt (illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker called to report the behavior of the supervisor from the Production line called - RP - Pelu site. The supervisor ("P Dam") treats workers poorly, (i) Workers' sick leave not always being approved as requested, she makes the decisions based on her mood and relationship with that certain worker. (ii) In other production lines, according to the business policy, each worker has to do cleaning for 15 days in rotation; however, in her line she assigned the workers to do cleaning as she wants. If some worker takes sick leave and she does not like that person, she will assign that worker to do the cleaning for as many days as she wants. (iii) She discriminates against nationalities by saying you Burmese people do not follow the rules, only Thai people follow the rules and policy. Workers added that they have reported the issue of this supervisor via grievance boxes, however, they have not noticed any improvement.

Recommendations for remediation:
The business should conduct an investigation regarding the supervisor’s behavior, with worker safeguards to ensure that workers don’t face retaliation afterwards 
Based on the investigation, take disciplinary action against the supervisor and develop an improvement plan; identify the number of workers who were denied sick leave and remediate (return pay if it was considered unpaid leave)
The business should investigate why reports about this supervisor put into the grievance box went unheeded 
Communicate to the workers the actions that the business will be taking to solve the issue
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business response: 
(i) The HR department randomly had 15 workers at the processing line where Mr. Dam was the supervisor to ask if the supervisor had ever refused to allow the workers to take sick leave. All workers randomly asked said that the supervisor never refused sick leave but only asked about the symptoms of illness.

The HR department and the factory manager called the supervisor "Dam" to ask more questions. Dam insists that he has never denied sick leave but only asked about the symptoms of illness with concern for the workers. However, Dam admits that he has some loud conversations with the workers but never scolded or spoke badly to them in this regard. The factory manager has verbally warned Dam about proper communication and dialogue with workers as well as to adjust the tone of speech not to be loud in order not to misunderstand workers. 

All supervisors are communicated, trained, and emphasized on communication methods. Continuously, treating workers appropriately and the company has always been given importance. 


(ii) The business noted that the cleaning process of the production area is part of the scope of duties and responsibilities of the workers. All workers are informed from the first day they join the company.

However, the supervisor will arrange manpower in each process to suit the amount of work by considering the amount of work, the number of workers, skills and abilities, the performance of each workers; workers are notified the workers at least 1 week in advance.

In addition, the production department is considering a change in the form of assignments. All workers are required to switch roles throughout the process, including cleaning the production line. All workers will be switched every 15 days, which the supervisors and factory managers plan to communicate to workers during 16-20 May and start implementation from 1 June onwards


(iii) After investigation, the business found that it received complaints from workers on April 18, 2022, and the HR department responded to the complaints by clarification through the company's public relations board at the canteen on April 28, 2022.

However, the HR department and supervisors will have an appointment to communicate with all the processing line workers about the assignment of cleaning work during 16-20 May.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that his supervisor treats workers poorly, such as 1) not approving sick leave for some workers and basing her decisions on her mood; 2) assigning some workers to do the cleaning duties more than other workers if she doesn't like them, instead of assigning duties by rotation, and 3) discriminating against Burmese workers, saying "you Burmese people do not follow the rules, only Thai people follow the rules and policy." The worker added that he had reported the issues with his supervisor via the company's grievance boxes but had not noticed any improvement.
remediation_action: The business investigated and reported that HR had randomly interviewed some workers working under this supervisor and none reported that their sick leave requests had been denied.  However, the business noted that this supervisor sometimes shouted at the workers, for which she has received a verbal warning.  In regards to assignment of duties, it is the supervisor's discretion to assign various roles, including cleaning to the workers but the business will change this to an automatic rotation of duties every 15 days starting in June 2022.  The business didn't respond to how the supervisor was discriminatory towards Burmese workers.  The business also stated that it had received the complaint about the cleaning duties and that it had posted on the bulletin board the company's policy about assignment of duties earlier; however, it will announce the new arrangement of automatic rotation of duties during the week of May 16-20.
remediation_validation: The worker provided an update that the supervisor had been moved to another different line.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change:
Ensure capacity building training for supervisors include the correct implementation of the sick leave request process and the non-discrimination policy.  Issara can provide this training to the supervisors and the HR staff.
