description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by line supervisor/mgt (illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with three supervisors ( 2 assistant and 1 senior, ลำใย  LB2 and เรณู  LB4 blue cap and เพียงพอ จัยจัย with green cap) being abusive with the workers. A group of workers has reported being constantly and verbally abusive with aggressive behavior and rude words by the supervisors. 

Talking Points. 
-Workers reported to Issara that they have reported the issues they are facing with these two assistant supervisors to the senior supervisor but there has been no improvement in these supervisors’ behavior. What is the role of the senior supervisors if some workers report such issues? Is the senior supervisor responsible to report workers' grievances to HR, or how should they handle such cases?
-For the past few years, workers’ grievances have been well handled by SEAPAC, and Issara noticed the improvement throughout those years, so we would like to know what has been the process in the past and if anything has changed in the grievance mechanisms processes from the company.  
-Does the company have any systems or processes to assess workers' experiences at the workplace, such as surveys or open talks? 
-Are there any activities or any training that the business has not been able to conduct recently which might have led supervisors to behave poorly? 
-Is HR aware of this issue? And if so, how is it being handled? 

Recommendations
-The business shall conduct an immediate investigation about the three reported supervisors. 
-The investigation should make sure safeguards for the workers are in place and that there would be no risk of retaliation. The investigation should be confidential, meaning that workers’ identities should not be exposed in order to mitigate the risks of being targeted. 
-The business shall take disciplinary action based on the business policy and the investigation results. 
-Workers should be treated humanely and this should be followed by all company staff. 


Time Frame - 2 weeks.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had a meeting with the business, the business agreed to conduct the investigation and get back to Issara.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-Based on the results of the investigation and the assessment of the business on how the senior supervisor responded to workers' grievances, the business shall provide training to this senior supervisor and shall revise as needed the protocols to respond to workers. Since workers explained that they had reported the issue but nothing was solved, the business is recommended to look into the grievance mechanism channels and identify what shall be amended or improved. 
-The business to remind workers of the different grievance mechanisms channels they can use to report their issues. The communication about the grievance mechanisms channels should also include information about the process of how the grievances are handled and the confidentiality of such channels. This will give more confidence to the workers to use the business's internal grievance channels. 
-The business should clearly communicate with all supervisors and workers the business policy regarding behavior and what are disciplinary actions for those not following the company policy. 
-The business to conduct the training with the supervisors. 
-Issara can also provide tailored training with HR and the supervisors.

description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by line supervisor/mgt (illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with workers being treated poorly by their line supervisor and the line manager regarding their holidays. Workers added that they were being asked to switch their day off from Sunday to weekdays as needed as the business wants to avoid paying double for working on Sundays. Workers added that the line supervisor and the manager threaten them by saying that they can be fired, moved to a different working line which has poor working conditions, or workers to find buyers if they refuse to work on Sunday and have a rest during weekdays. 

Added on 17 Dec, 2022. 
Context: In regards to this issue, 2 female workers who refused to switch their day off reported being moved to a different line as retaliation. Since the business has ceased/solved this issue, for the time being, those workers want to come back to their original working line.

Regular shift hours and wages should be respected at all times, in line with contractual agreements. Changes in shifts should be made with the consent of workers and with reasonable notice, ensuring that total weekly working hours are in compliance with national law, and extra hours are paid at a premium rate. Workers should not be forced or coerced to agree to the changes. Shifts should not be changed in order to avoid paying premium overtime and holiday rates.
The business shall conduct an investigation to find out the root cause of the issues and remediate the workers if the result found workers being forced to change their day off. 
The business is recommended to have conversation with the workers and come to an agreement for a fixed day off. 
The process that the business has been practicing should be on a voluntary basis. No workers should be forced to change or switch their day off against their will.
The business should coordinate with the production and come up with a plan where workers' days off are not being switched or changed often. Workers have rights to have a fixed day off so that they can make their personal plans for the activities. 
If there is work during the days off of workers, the business shall ask workers if they would like to work on that day, and if so, the business should pay the wages according to the LPA 2x and 3x for OT during day off. 
The investigation with the line supervisor and the manager should be taken to investigate the treatment that they had with the workers and provide the training and disciplinary measure according to the business policy. 
Workers should not be threatened with being moved to a harder production line, getting fired from their job or having to find a new buyer for not agreeing to switch their day off.
After the investigation process, the business should conduct communication in written and verbal with all workers who have been impacted by this issue.


Update from workers (14 Jan 2022) : 

The two female workers who were sent to a different line for speaking up during the business communication session updated that they do not want to come back to their original line given that they have been treated poorly by the line supervisor but the business did not conduct any proper action to address the issues. In detail, these two workers did not receive overtime working hours like other workers for two weeks because they refused to switch their day off as requested by the business. The workers approached the ER as they were left out from the OT working hours. The ER staff did not conduct an investigation against the line supervisor but simply asked the workers if they wanted to change to new lines. Workers accepted to work for the new line as they did not have any other options and have been working in that line. Last week, these two workers were provided with a warning letter by their original working line supervisor (P Yat) for going to the HR office during working hours. Workers were called to the officer to sign the warning letter, but the workers did not sign because they had informed their supervisor about their visit to ER and they only took around 30 minutes which contrasted with the accusation of the supervisor who said that they took around one hour going out without her permission. 

Note: 
In summary, these two workers do not want to go back to their original, however, Issara wants to highlight how workers' issues are being handled improperly by the ER without a proper investigation to find out the root cause. This is to explain to the business how the grievance is not working effectively which drives workers reporting to Issara and losing trust of using internal grievances. 


Recommendations: 
-For the two workers, investigate the line supervisor and the manager’s treatment of the workers (OT hours not given, warning letter given for going to ER); provide the training and disciplinary measure according to the business policy. 
-After the investigation process, the business should provide an update on the investigation results to the impacted workers. 
-For the four workers, reassign them to their original lines, since they did not consent willingly to switch lines 
-The business should focus on the safeguard for the workers and clearly communicate with the supervisors that there should be no reprisals against these workers after relocation to their original line.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara raised this issue with the business, the business argued that they have a policy that notifies employees in advance to make sure that employees voluntarily and agree to come to work, they will sign a written consent and pay double wages. However, to solve the issue, the business updated to pay double to the workers in the future and make sure that workers are communicated about the voluntary process and have consent. The business did not reflect or consider the reimbursement for the past Sundays work that workers have done. Issara checked with the workers, the workers have updated being communicated to receive double wages only December and onward if they are asked to work on Sundays. The business response neither reflects the issue with the workers being forced or threads to switch the day off nor conducted any investigation to access the poor treatment of the Employment Relation staff. Issara re-escalated this issue with the business and highlighted to conduct an investigation about the poor treatment of the line supervisors toward two female workers and the case management of the Employment Relation staff, the business responded that they have communicated with the ER staff and will provide the training by Verite in the Q1 or 2 of the year. However, for the behavior of the line supervisor who mistreated the workers and provided the warning letter to the workers, the business argued that their investigation found workers going to report to the ER without the permission of the line supervisor which is why the workers were given with the warning letter. However, the workers in the other hand reported refusing to sing the warning as they know that they have informed the line supervisor about their visit to the ER. Issara wants to highlight how workers' issues are being handled improperly by the ER without a proper investigation to find out the root cause. This is to explain how the grievance is not working effectively which drives workers reporting to Issara and losing trust of using internal grievances.
remediation_business_steps_remaining: The business to conduct proper investigation to access the behavior of the supervisor and take proper action.
remediation_notes:
Workers in the “Pla Sod” line reported being asked to work on Sunday (the typical day off for workers) to meet production demands, and switch their day off to another weekday day. Some workers reported this was not voluntary or communicated in advance, and workers reported not being paid the 2x legal rate for Sunday work.  This was reported for Nov 7 and 14, and some workers noted this practice had been long-standing.  Worker contracts provide for one rest day a week, and Thai labor law establishes a 2x daily wage for Sunday work, and 3x daily wage for official holiday day work.
 
For two workers that had refused to work on their Sunday day-off, their line supervisor targeted them and denied them the opportunity to work on future Sundays after the company made the policy change to keep Sundays the day-off and pay workers double if worked on Sundays.  When the workers went to Employee Relations (ER) office to report being denied work on Sundays, they were just told they could move to a different line if they wanted rather than the ER staff addressing the line supervisor’s retaliatory behavior.  On top of that, they received warnings for having gone to the ER office without receiving permission from their line supervisors beforehand
remediation_action:
This issue was escalated to TU corporate HR and to the Sustainability Director.  The business conducted an investigation and noted that it has followed company policy to notify employees in advance to make sure that employees voluntarily agree to work, and they will sign consent for it.  To solve the issue, the business said it would pay double wages to the workers when they are asked to work on their weekly day-off on Sunday in the future and make sure that workers understand that it is voluntary. description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by line supervisor/mgt (illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with workers being treated poorly by their line supervisor and the line manager regarding their holidays. Workers added that they were being asked to switch their day off from Sunday to weekdays as needed as the business wants to avoid paying double for working on Sundays. Workers added that the line supervisor and the manager threaten them by saying that they can be fired, moved to a different working line which has poor working conditions, or workers to find buyers if they refuse to work on Sunday and have a rest during weekdays. 

Added on 17 Dec, 2022. 
Context: In regards to this issue, 2 female workers who refused to switch their day off reported being moved to a different line as retaliation. Since the business has ceased/solved this issue, for the time being, those workers want to come back to their original working line.

Regular shift hours and wages should be respected at all times, in line with contractual agreements. Changes in shifts should be made with the consent of workers and with reasonable notice, ensuring that total weekly working hours are in compliance with national law, and extra hours are paid at a premium rate. Workers should not be forced or coerced to agree to the changes. Shifts should not be changed in order to avoid paying premium overtime and holiday rates.
The business shall conduct an investigation to find out the root cause of the issues and remediate the workers if the result found workers being forced to change their day off. 
The business is recommended to have conversation with the workers and come to an agreement for a fixed day off. 
The process that the business has been practicing should be on a voluntary basis. No workers should be forced to change or switch their day off against their will.
The business should coordinate with the production and come up with a plan where workers' days off are not being switched or changed often. Workers have rights to have a fixed day off so that they can make their personal plans for the activities. 
If there is work during the days off of workers, the business shall ask workers if they would like to work on that day, and if so, the business should pay the wages according to the LPA 2x and 3x for OT during day off. 
The investigation with the line supervisor and the manager should be taken to investigate the treatment that they had with the workers and provide the training and disciplinary measure according to the business policy. 
Workers should not be threatened with being moved to a harder production line, getting fired from their job or having to find a new buyer for not agreeing to switch their day off.
After the investigation process, the business should conduct communication in written and verbal with all workers who have been impacted by this issue.


Update from workers (14 Jan 2022) : 

The two female workers who were sent to a different line for speaking up during the business communication session updated that they do not want to come back to their original line given that they have been treated poorly by the line supervisor but the business did not conduct any proper action to address the issues. In detail, these two workers did not receive overtime working hours like other workers for two weeks because they refused to switch their day off as requested by the business. The workers approached the ER as they were left out from the OT working hours. The ER staff did not conduct an investigation against the line supervisor but simply asked the workers if they wanted to change to new lines. Workers accepted to work for the new line as they did not have any other options and have been working in that line. Last week, these two workers were provided with a warning letter by their original working line supervisor (P Yat) for going to the HR office during working hours. Workers were called to the officer to sign the warning letter, but the workers did not sign because they had informed their supervisor about their visit to ER and they only took around 30 minutes which contrasted with the accusation of the supervisor who said that they took around one hour going out without her permission.

Context: In regards to this issue, 2 female workers who refused to switch their day off reported being moved to a different line as retaliation. Since the business has ceased/solved this issue, for the time being, those workers want to come back to their original working line.

Regular shift hours and wages should be respected at all times, in line with contractual agreements. Changes in shifts should be made with the consent of workers and with reasonable notice, ensuring that total weekly working hours are in compliance with national law, and extra hours are paid at a premium rate. Workers should not be forced or coerced to agree to the changes. Shifts should not be changed in order to avoid paying premium overtime and holiday rates.
The business shall conduct an investigation to find out the root cause of the issues and remediate the workers if the result found workers being forced to change their day off. 
The business is recommended to have conversation with the workers and come to an agreement for a fixed day off. 
The process that the business has been practicing should be on a voluntary basis. No workers should be forced to change or switch their day off against their will.
The business should coordinate with the production and come up with a plan where workers' days off are not being switched or changed often. Workers have rights to have a fixed day off so that they can make their personal plans for the activities. 
If there is work during the days off of workers, the business shall ask workers if they would like to work on that day, and if so, the business should pay the wages according to the LPA 2x and 3x for OT during day off. 
The investigation with the line supervisor and the manager should be taken to investigate the treatment that they had with the workers and provide the training and disciplinary measure according to the business policy. 
Workers should not be threatened with being moved to a harder production line, getting fired from their job or having to find a new buyer for not agreeing to switch their day off.

description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by line supervisor/mgt (illegal)
Physical and/or other serious abuse by line supervisor/mgt (illegal)
Physical and/or other serious abuse by line supervisor/mgt (illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that during the new year, they had to contribute money to buy presents for the line supervisors, with contributions ranging from 200-500 Baht per worker.  Line leaders collecting this money record worker names and their worker ID numbers.  Any worker that doesn't chip in are targeted for mistreatment.  This includes line supervisors intentionally finding fault in a worker's output to deny that worker to incentives that are awarded when workers meet set targets.  As an example, a worker in the fish skimming line that is tasked to debone the fish may have his work tampered with and the line supervisor will claim that there are still bones in the fish meat and therefore the worker will miss out on his incentive pay.  Or, workers will be called names often, assigned to dirty, smelly, and harsh tasks, assigned to carry heavy things, or given more work to do than others.

Talking points:
Does TU have a policy prohibiting bribes and gifts?
Is the business aware that there is a practice where workers collect money to buy gifts for their supervisors?  And that workers are being targeted for maltreatment if they don’t pitch in for these gifts?

Recommendations for remediation:
Investigate this matter, with proper worker safeguards
Take disciplinary action against any supervisors that have asked for such gifts with the threat of retaliation if workers don’t comply
Make an announcement, verbally and in writing, that any such gifts are prohibited and disciplinary actions will be taken against those that demand them
remediation_business_steps_taken: K. Wichai, HR manager, stated that TUM has a policy and that no money must be collected from any workers. K. Prad requested Issara to get more information and provide the line leader's name, line number, and so on. So then TUM will investigate this issue.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that during the new year, they had to contribute money to buy presents for the line supervisors, with contributions ranging from 200-500 Baht per worker (this practice happens annually).  Line leaders collecting this money record worker names and their worker ID numbers.  Any worker that doesn't chip in are targeted for mistreatment.  Workers don't want to contribute to this "gift buying" but are afraid to refuse.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change:
Review the company policy that prohibits any forms of bribes and gifts, including the disciplinary measures the company will take against those that break the rule
In training of line supervisors, include training on the company policy that all bribes and gifts are prohibited

The supervisor targets the workers that don't report to work by 6:30 AM and latest by 6:40 AM, even though the shift begins at 7am. She would grab the workers’ ears, cap, or apron and embarrass them in front of all the other workers. Sometimes, the line supervisor will hit the workers hands with her hands when she found some fish blood and bone in the fish flesh.

- How are line supervisors expected to communicate with and treat their workers?  Does the company have a clear policy that bans verbal and physical abuse by supervisors? How does the company define physical abuse? verbal abuse?

- Discipline the supervisor according to the investigation findings and the company's disciplinary policy
- Communicate to all supervisors and workers about what is acceptable and unacceptable behavior when it comes to verbal and physical interactions between employees (supervisors and workers)

description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by line supervisor/mgt (illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue#1. 
The issue with poor behavior of the supervisors in production lines 6 and 8. 

- Recommend the business to take disciplinary actions towards these supervisors following the company protocol. Since this is the second time these supervisors are reported, please ask the company what would be the appropriate disciplinary actions in this case? Is it a written warning?

- Workers reported that the previous actions taken by the business helped improve the situation for a while, but now the supervisors are treating workers poorly again. For this reason, it is recommended for the business to have a monitoring plan where they can hear from workers directly what the situation is and if further actions are needed. 

-The monitoring plan could be done by creating safe spaces for workers to share their feedback (e.g. morning talks/tea time) or the company could also conduct a confidential survey with all workers under these two supervisors.

-There should not be any coercion or retaliation towards workers during any kind of investigation, open dialogue sessions, and survey processes the business undertakes for this issue. The investigation/survey must be confidential, workers should not be asked to provide any of their personal information, such as employee IDs, their names, etc. In addition,  workers should receive information about the company’s no retaliation policy and how the company would guarantee safeguards. 

-To work on a plan of actions based on the result of the survey/investigation/dialogue with workers. 

-To communicate to workers the actions the business is taking to respond to workers' grievances, would help the business to strengthen the trust of workers in the business grievance mechanism.

Talking Points.
-What is the business action for such repeated issues? 
-Please propose to the business that Issara is happy to provide training to all supervisors and HR after the business investigation.

timeframe 1 pay period

-Workers who are wanting to leave and want to have a proper job cancelation letter when they leave. 

Please see the recommendations for the system change.

remediation_business_steps_taken:
06/04/2021
HR will discuss this issue with senior management and production manager and investigate and work on a plan of action based on the result of the investigation. They will get back to us next week.

11-June-2021.Business response ID - 1255.

The business - The business responded that the workers are not happy to participate in skill training which is required by the buyers. The business said that they will conduct the investigation, however, gave an uncertain response about the recommended survey to access the collective response from the workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-To communicate to workers the actions the business is taking to respond to workers' grievances, would help the business to strengthen the trust of workers in the business grievance mechanism.

-Issara to provide training to the supervisors and the HR.

Issue#2. Recommendations; 
-To have open discussion sessions between  HR and workers to understand better what are the challenges being faced by workers and what is driving them to resign. During these discussions, the business is encouraged to share with workers what the business actions are to address these issues.
-The business could also conduct an internal survey to learn why workers want to resign and what can help them remain in Ladybird. Issara can help with the survey questionnaire. Surveys should be conducted in a confidential way where workers feel safe to share the issues that they are facing. 
-The business shall work on a plan to address the issues that are raised in the survey by the workers. 
-The business shall provide training to all supervisors including translators.
-The business shall revise the grievance channels that are meant for workers to raise their issues. The revision should focus on workers' confidentiality and the no retaliation policy. Workers have expressed their concern about raising issues with HR, out of fear of retaliation from their supervisors, therefore it is strongly recommended for the business to reinforce a no retaliation policy and make sure all supervisors are aware of the policy, follow it and face consequences if they commit any actions against such policy.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue # 1. 

Context; The issue with the announcement that the business made regarding vaccination for Burmese migrant workers only. The issue with the announcement that the business made regarding vaccination for Burmese migrant workers only. Workers reported that the business announced to the Burmese workers that the Burmese workers from MMP will receive vaccines on 16th May 2021 etc. Some supervisors said to the workers that if the workers do not want to get vaccines then they will have to sign documents and the consequences might be dismissal. 


Recommendations:
Given that workers have raised many concerns about the announcements about the vaccination and reporting lack of understanding of how it will be handled, it is recommended that MMP make written and verbal announcements including the following information before the workers are vaccinated: 

When is the process starting?
Who is leading the process?
Is the process the same for Burmese and Thai workers? If not, how is it different and why?
Reassurance that the vaccines that will be used have been approved by the World Health Organization and the Thai Government, therefore, they are safe
Who to contact in case there are any questions about the vaccine? (could be the government hotline)

                       Understanding that this is a topic of concern for all workers, it is recommended that the business is open to dialogue with workers, hear their concerns and be able to reply to their questions so that the process can be smooth and workers feel secure about it. Issara can provide support by reviewing the language of the announcement so the information can be easily understood by all migrant workers. 

In addition to migrant workers’ communication, it is recommended that the business provide similar information to Thai workers. 

Talking points:
Ask the business for information about the vaccination plan: -
When is this happening?
Is this organized by the government?
Is it the same plan for Burmese and Thai workers? If not, how is it different and why?

Issue # 2. (2-June-2021) 

Context: Workers reported an  issue with the abusive supervisors at the operator line "Mr. P Kong (Thai nationality) and Mr. Ko Win (Burmese Nationality)" who is being abusive with the workers. Workers added that the supervisors express themselves very aggressively, they follow the workers at the toilets or even sometimes knock on the door of the toilets, challenge workers, accuse workers of using drugs, etc. Workers have reported sharing their complaints through the complaint box in the past, and HR would talk with workers about the issue but workers didn’t dare to speak openly fearing no confidentiality.  

Recommendations ; 

-The business conducts an investigation with these specific supervisors. There are different ways in which the business can investigate this issue such as conducting a survey where workers can rate their supervisor's behavior confidentially. Or the business could conduct an investigation by talking with workers under these supervisors directly making sure that the investigation protects workers for any kind of retaliation and that it is handled confidentially. For this, the company shall make sure the investigation is conducted in a safe space with trained staff and explaining to workers how the company is placing safeguards for them.  

-There should not be any coercion or retaliation towards workers during or after the investigation and survey processes. The investigation process must be confidential, workers should not be required to provide any of their personal information, such as working IDs, their names, etc. 

-The business should create a plan of action based on the results of investigations and surveys. Such actions should include training and disciplinary actions (if necessary). 
-The workers should be treated humanely.

-Workers have reported that they have inserted the complaint letter in the GB to complain about these supervisors, is HR aware of this? 

-If yes, what was the investigation and the result of the investigation? 

-Workers raised that they were not confident to give the real information about these supervisors in the investigation process, because they were not introduced to the confidentiality and safety process, what is the business response to this?

-All workers should be introduced with the business available grievance channels and encouraged to use any grievance mechanism channel they feel comfortable using (internal or external as Issara). 
-When communicating to workers what the company grievance mechanism  channels are, the business should also explain how workers grievances are managed and how safeguards are put in place for workers.

description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by line supervisor/mgt (illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the poor treatment by the line supervisor and the manager at the production line called (Roung Thor).Workers reported being pressured to complete the target without a proper rest during break time as they are being told to be reported to the manager and cut off their wages even there was delay because of the machine error. They also added that they do not dare to request sick leave and annual leave since their supervisor does not encourage them to do so. Sometimes, they feel not healthy enough to work for OT, however they feel pressure to do so because they will not receive OT for the following one week consecutively for refusing one day. 


Recommendations: 
The business should conduct an investigation across the factory to identify the root cause of the issue. The investigation should be conducted by the HR. All of the workers' information during the investigation process should be kept confidential.
The investigation should include workers' voices and the no retaliation policy to be explained with the line supervisor and manager to avoid the retaliation that can take place during and after the investigation. 


The business shall take action towards the staff that violates the business policy regarding breaks hours. 
All workers should have a rest period of not less than one hour for their lunch and at least 20 mins before starting OT if their OT hours are more than 2 hours according to the LPA section No.27.  
OT working hours should be aligned with the LPA and the buyer's COC. 

Talking Points: 
Is the business aware that workers are not receiving one full hour of breaks during their lunch time? 
What is the OT hours policy for the workers per week? If the OT hours are more than 12 hours per week based on the buyer's COC, has this been communicated with Nike? 

ETI; Goal: All workers have the right to take lunch breaks, in line with the law, which specifies minimum amount of time allowable. Further, workers should be allowed to take bathroom breaks whenever needed. Limiting use of bathrooms for the purpose of controlling or maximizing productivity can have adverse effects on the health of workers, and should be strictly prohibited. Breaks are required by law as well, in between regular working hours and OT shifts.

Code: ETI Base Code 6.1. Working hours are not excessive; must comply with national laws, collective agreements
Description: Working hours must comply with national laws, collective agreements, and the provisions of 6.2 to 6.6 below, whichever affords the greater protection for workers. Sub-clauses 6.2 to 6.6 are based on international labour standards.
LPA Section 27. On a Working Day, an Employer shall arrange a rest period during work for an Employee of not less than one hour per day after the Employee has been working for not more than fve consecutive hours. An Employer and Employee may agre in advance that each rest period may be less than one hour but the total rest period per day shall not be less than one hour. Whereas an Employer and Employee agree to specify rest periods during work other than paragraph one, the agreement shall be applicable only if it is more favourable to the Employee. A rest period during work shall not be counted as working time except where the total rest period is more than two hours per day, where the amount of time exceeding two hours shall be counted as normal working time. Whereas any Overtime Work after normal working time is more than two hours, the Employer shall arrange for the Employee to take a rest period of not less than twenty minutes before the Employee commences the Overtime Work. The provisions in paragraph one and paragraph four shall not apply where an Employee is required to do work of a continuous nature or character with the consent of the Employee, or in case of emergency work.
remediation_business_steps_taken:

The business shall take action towards the staff that violates the business policy regarding breaks hours. 
All workers should have a rest period of not less than one hour for their lunch and at least 20 mins before starting OT if their OT hours are more than 2 hours according to the LPA section No.27.  
OT working hours should be aligned with the LPA and the buyer's COC.

ETI; Goal: All workers have the right to take lunch breaks, in line with the law, which specifies minimum amount of time allowable. Further, workers should be allowed to take bathroom breaks whenever needed. Limiting use of bathrooms for the purpose of controlling or maximizing productivity can have adverse effects on the health of workers, and should be strictly prohibited. Breaks are required by law as well, in between regular working hours and OT shifts.

Code: ETI Base Code 6.1. Working hours are not excessive; must comply with national laws, collective agreements
Description: Working hours must comply with national laws, collective agreements, and the provisions of 6.2 to 6.6 below, whichever affords the greater protection for workers. Sub-clauses 6.2 to 6.6 are based on international labour standards.
LPA Section 27. On a Working Day, an Employer shall arrange a rest period during work for an Employee of not less than one hour per day after the Employee has been working for not more than fve consecutive hours. An Employer and Employee may agre in advance that each rest period may be less than one hour but the total rest period per day shall not be less than one hour. Whereas an Employer and Employee agree to specify rest periods during work other than paragraph one, the agreement shall be applicable only if it is more favourable to the Employee. A rest period during work shall not be counted as working time except where the total rest period is more than two hours per day, where the amount of time exceeding two hours shall be counted as normal working time. Whereas any Overtime Work after normal working time is more than two hours, the Employer shall arrange for the Employee to take a rest period of not less than twenty minutes before the Employee commences the Overtime Work. The provisions in paragraph one and paragraph four shall not apply where an Employee is required to do work of a continuous nature or character with the consent of the Employee, or in case of emergency work.

supplier_name: Daorae (Desa Sri Hartamas) Sdn Bhd, a Korean BBQ restaurant
description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by line supervisor/mgt (illegal)
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client worked at a Korean BBQ restaurant located in KL Kepong Jalan Metro Perdana, which is one of fifteen branches of the restaurant chain. Out of the fifteen branches, this particular one was problematic. The restaurant has six Nepali and thirteen Burmese workers. The owner's son is abusive towards the Nepali workers, creating a hostile work environment. Issara is able to speak with two workers. They have been working for this employer for 10 months. They are all MoU workers. They are reporting as a group of 5 Nepali workers, but the client is quietly reporting. The client and the workers want to either be transferred to another branch under the same company or find employment in another company. The client has debts to pay and doesn't want to return to Nepal. The workers have a contract they made in Nepal, but the company made another contract which the client doesn't have and is unaware of its contents.
Following are the major issues reported by workers.

1) Document retention: Workers passports are held by the employer since they started their employment. The company also kept their passports and didn't provide them with worker ID cards (Jalan cards) or necessary documents. 

2) Restriction of Movement: The workers were not allowed to leave the premises, and this restriction also made it difficult for their friends to visit them.

3) Unfair suspension: Workers were frequently suspended for minor mistakes or even without any reason. During these suspensions, the company did not provide any food, and the workers were not allowed to go out and get their own. They were also denied access to basic amenities, like cooling fans, during these periods. One incident occurred when a friend of the client was suspended for simply asking a Burmese worker to clean a stain. The owner verbally abused him and kept him in detention (suspension) for 28 days. Throughout this time, the company did not provide any food or salary, leaving the workers in a dire situation. His friends attempted to provide food secretly, but they had to be cautious as the company would punish them if they were caught bringing in more substantial amounts of food or any food. 

Recently, the victim was suspended by the company for two months. During this period, he received no salary or food from the company. The suspension was a result of the employer demanding the victim to memorize the restaurant menu quickly.

If workers demand to change the employer, they are asked to work 4 months without pay and there are some workers who have accepted this situation as they could not bear the harsh working environment.

remediation_notes: Line Manager from S4 (Malaysian Citizen) is abusing her authority and threathen workers for reporting issues to Issara taht has led to investigation against her. She had workers in her production line met with her group by group and blamed them for launching report to Issara and also checked the phone of the workers. She also targetted migrant workers for reporting about her bad behaviour to Issara, transferred one burmese line leader to the other site as she did not corperate with her when she asked her to check the phone of other burmese workers who reported to Issara. She also warned a few other workers that they would be transferred to the other site, and on Sep 5th, almost all burmese workers are not given overtime hence, workers have concern over her action.
remediation_action:
Business is now aware of the situation and planning to talk to senior management and production manager to reinstate the line leader and to also stop all the abusive behaviour and actions. HR also shared with Issara that there have been previous report of her mistreatment to workers. HR will continue with their investigation and aim to have the investigation report by next week which will be shared with Issara and discuss the action steps. On 10 Sep, business started the investigation with 20 workers however, workers shared their views that majority of the selected workers are not the ones who dare to speak. It was suggested that business to have more inclusive channels that allow any workers to report anonymously. Business shared the company grievance channel that workers can report anonamously by using the QR code. 

The business is conducting investigation and there have been issues with the Line Manager threathening the workers, abuse of authority by moving one burmese line leader to the other site and not providing overtime. As the situation is getting worse, new KPIs have been added and the case has been escalated to level 3. Business will complete the investigation on 19th Sep, and will take all the necessary action to have fair and smooth investigation. On 22nd Sep, business informed Issara that the abusive Line Manager was terminated, and the line supervisor got the warning. The termination will prevent the line supervisor from abuse the power.

description: Substandard living conditions and privacy in dorm/bathrooms/living space
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the restriction of movement. The workers reported that the landlord is being too strict with them when workers want to go out to buy their basic needs. Therefore, they reach out to the white cardholder who is assigned to assist the workers and buy the needs that the workers want but the assigned person is being biased among the workers and provides preference. In addition to that, the workers added not having a backup person for the white cardholder when he is not available to help them. Workers added that the grocery store in the compound does not have everything that workers need. 


Recommendations:
-The business shall talk with workers to find out what their daily needs are and suggest the landlord add those missing supplies to his/her shop and/or on the grocery truck to reduce workers having to rely on the white cardholder for their needs. To collect this information, the business could conduct a survey or seek workers' feedback through different channels.  
-The business shall consider expanding or assigning a backup person for the white cardholder so that workers can access him/her if the focal is not available. 
-The business shall communicate with the workers about what will be the business action to solve this issue. 
-The business shall communicate with the white cardholders about the expected behavior when dealing with the workers. The communication should include no discrimination policy, no bias behavior policy, and be ethical. 
-The business to introduce the HR focal person for the workers to report if they have any concerns or challenges with their stay or dealing with the white cardholders. 

Talking Points:
_Has the business received any complaints from the workers about white card holder’s behavior? 
_What has been the communication with the white cardholder?

Time Frame 1 week
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had several meetings with the business on this issue, the business first assigned a white cardholder to assist the workers and buy their needs from the outside. However, workers updated white cardholder being bias among the workers and also not having back up person for him. Given the workers' update, Issara gave further recommendations to the business. The business arranged grocery vender inside the workers housing compound for every other day. Since then workers have confirmed not having such issues as they could access their needs from the vendor.

description: Substandard living conditions and privacy in dorm/bathrooms/living space
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1: 
The business is housing up to 3 married couples in a room and 5-6 single workers in a room without proper partitions so there is a complete lack of privacy. The room is not very big and conflicts between the occupants happen often. In addition, they require the workers to rotate rooms 3-4 times per year. The workers don’t like this kind of management as they have to move all their belongings every time they have to change rooms. And then, when one party fights, all workers have to leave the housing and they are automatically disqualified to get the transportation allowance that the business started providing to the workers who live outside the business housing.

Recommendations for remediation:
- Survey the dorm residents to ask about the overall conditions and receive suggestions for improvements
- Dorm rooms should be assigned so that there is adequate privacy and couples can be housed in separate rooms


Case #2:
There are 12 toilets and bathrooms in the women's dorm where more than 100 female workers are being accommodated. Many toilet doors and locks are broken and cannot be closed properly. Some water taps are not working. Workers have to fight to get to use the toilets and bathrooms. 

Recommendations for remediation:
- Inspect the toilet and shower facilities in the dorms to ensure that all doors, door locks, and water taps are working properly 
- Fix all doors, locks, and water taps that are in disrepair
- Survey the dorm residents to ask about the overall conditions and receive suggestions for improvements

description: Substandard living conditions and privacy in dorm/bathrooms/living space
Substandard living conditions and privacy in dorm/bathrooms/living space
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A group of 8 MOU workers called our hotline to report about crowded accommodation arranged by TUS. TUS arranged for three couples (6 workers) to stay in a single room. They paid 3,000 baht as a deposit to the TUS’s interpreter. The workers said that the room is too crowded and unethical for 3 couples to share the same room. These workers arrived at TUS in Oct 2022 as MOU workers. There were around 100 MOU workers in this particular batch. The Myanmar recruitment agency was Alpha World Link. They didn’t know they will be asked to stay like this. On the Myanmar side, U Hlwan Moe from AWL asked the workers how they would like to share the room. The workers said “A room with two workers (a couple)”. U Hlwan Moe noted down their name and the workers thought that they would be arranged to stay as they requested. UHM didn’t confirm to the workers that their request will be fulfilled. To make it worse, some couples were arranged to stay separately in different rooms. Out of frustration, these 8 workers tried to find a new housing near TUS factory and they found one. The housing is not ready yet to stay as it is still under construction. But the landlord told them they can stay at the housing once ready. The 8 workers paid 3,000 baht to the landlord as a deposit for two rooms. The workers are planning to share the room with 4 workers each which is a lot better than the housing arrangement done by TUS. However, the landlord returned the deposit yesterday after making the payment for the deposit 10 days ago. The landlord said that TUS made him return the deposit. The landlord didn’t give any further reasons why the deposit was returned to the workers. The workers would like to ask Issara to help with the housing issues. It’s too crowded at the housing arranged by TUS. But when they tried to find a better place by themselves, TUS prevents them. The workers do not know what agreement TUS and the landlord have.

TPs:
-What is the company's policy regarding worker housing and the number of persons per room?
-How does the company consider privacy for married couples that are being housed in the company dorms?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Company housing should ensure that housing arrangements for workers in company dorms should adequately accommodate the privacy requests of the occupants, especially married couples.
-Investigate the incident where workers that had paid a deposit to rent a room outside were denied, with the landlord saying that TUS had convinced him to reject accepting these workers as tenants
-Workers should be able to choose where they live, whether in the factory dorm or outside in private rented housing
remediation_business_steps_taken: According to K. Siliruk, HR, the company's policy regarding worker housing is that there are usually 3-4 workers per room. And some workers (couple) request private rooms, for which they must pay extra. Furthermore, workers have the option of living in the factory dorm or outside in private rented housing. So they will investigate why these workers stay in the same room with six other people, as well as the incident in which workers who had paid a deposit to rent a room outside were denied, with the landlord claiming that TUS had convinced him not to accept these workers as tenants.
remediation_notes: A group of 8 MOU workers reported that three couples were arranged to stay in a single room in the company dormitory, with limited privacy. The workers said that the room is too crowded and unethical for 3 couples to share the same room. They arrived as MOU workers in October 2022.  When asked by the recruitment agency in Myanmar about the housing, one worker had stated his desire to be in one room with his wife and had assumed that this request would be met.  Out of frustration, these 8 workers tried to find a new housing near the factory but the landlord who had initially taken a deposit from them returned the money and told them that the company had made him return their deposit.

description: Substandard living conditions and privacy in dorm/bathrooms/living space
remediation_business_steps_taken:
According to K. Wichai, HR manager, according to company policy, no lockers for workers are opened and checked by TUM officers without their permission. And the workers have either purchased or have their own master key. As a result, the company does not have the key to unlock it. They will, however, investigate this issue and respond to us within 7 working days.


Investigation/Explanation

Mr. Kanyakorn, Assistant HR Manager, investigated and checked with the production department on 28/1/2023. The production manager 2 informed that on that day, a customer went to randomly inspect the locker without notice, resulting in the workers who own the lockers not being present.

Corrective/Responsible

Khun Kanyakorn, Assistant Manager of HR Department, discussed with Production Manager 2 and Production Manager 2 to prevent recurrence as follows:
1. There is a communication sign for randomly inspecting the Locker in order to communicate with the male/female Locker Room worker.
2. If the inspection locker is opened for GMP purposes, the owner of the locker must be present at all times for inspection.

remediation_action: Issara raised this with the business.  At first, the business HR claimed that according to company policy, no private lockers of workers can opened and checked by TUM officers without workers' permission. In addition, the workers had purchased their own locks and so the company does not have the key to unlock it. In the future, the business will ensure that there is a clear communication about any random inspections of lockers and that if any locker is to be opened for Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) purposes, the owner of the locker must be present at all times during the inspection.

description: Insufficient security and high crime risk in living/dorm conditions
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Nyi Nyi reported that he was attacked by the gangsters on the way back home from work on 16th August 2023 at 4:30 am after his night shift. He and his two friends were attacked with a metal rod by the gangsters on a motorbike. On the same day, another gangster attack happened at 68 Sub-agent owned compounds and another incident happened at the place near Factory 11 Gate. In these attacks, the gangster used a metal chain and metal rod as well. The workers assume that the gangsters attacked them to get money or valuable things. It is apparent that the gangsters often attack more on the paydays like the 16th & 30th of the months. For this latest incident, the workers reported to the fore-men of their respective production lines but the workers haven't known yet how the business will take action on this.

- Investigate this matter immediately; police report should also be filed
- Develop a corrective action plan with immediate safety measures for workers commuting to the workplace, especially in the late night / early morning times
- Communicate to the workers what actions the business is taking to make the commute safer for workers and update them on police investigation and actions as well

Deadline for business response: 2 weeks
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Anchan and K. Chalinee, HR will investigate this matter immediately. They will also increase the security guard in the areas and report to the police for increasing the petrol frequency. They asked Issara if Issara could get more information about what exactly the incident was happening so CC could investigate in a specific area and report to the policy as well. They shared with us the image of a CCTV camera set up in front of the F11 area.

https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1lS19pEy-KujIuQAGbELkqVRUsdn9ELHs

They will develop a corrective action plan communicate it to the workers and share with us any progress updates next week.
remediation_notes: A worker reported several violent attacks by gangsters on motorbikes committed against workers returning home from their nigh shift, in several different locations.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- Since this is a recurring issue and a serious lack of security for the workers, the business needs to put in place safety measures that will guarantee a level of safety for workers on their commute.
- The early hours for the commute home is putting workers in a particularly vulnerable situation so the business must take into consideration changing the shift hours so such hours for the commute can be avoided.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case with a poor rating. The business has resorted to laying off workers when workers expressed their request to work on a 2-shift system.
remediation_issara_recommendation: A worker reported that the business assigned workers to work on a 3-shift system since December 2022, which led to workers facing different challenges such as sleeplessness, lack of appetite, and lack of security during the commute to work.  Workers were attacked and robbed of money and mobile phones. The business tried to extend the 3-shift system until June 2023 so the workers went on strike on 24th March 2023. In order to stop the uprising of the workers, the business had the workers vote between two options. The first option is the business will change from 3 shifts to 2 shifts but many workers will have to be dismissed with cancellation letters and one month severance pay. And the second option is the business will keep practicing the 3 shifts but the business will take more care of workers' security and may consider to provide 1,000 Baht to workers as a shift bonus. After calling line leader meetings, the business distributed the voting forms to all workers to choose 3 shifts or 2 shifts to work. Unfortunately the voting system was not anonymous. The workers had to mention their ID and names in the voting form.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that the business assigned workers to work 3 shifts since December 2022. Since the business started 3 shifts, the workers have been facing different kinds of challenges such as sleeplessness, lack of appetite, attacks from gangsters during the commute. The business tried to extend the 3-shift system until June 2023 so the workers went on strike on 24th March 2023. In order to stop the uprising of the workers, the business allowed the workers to vote whether they wanted to go back to the 2-shift system, which would have to involve lay-offs, or to stay with the 3-shift system without lay-offs and a 1,000 Baht shift bonus.  The voting was not anonymous, and the workers had to mention their names and worker ID # in the voting form.
remediation_action: The business called Issara with a request to help explain the situation to the workers and that they should agree to keep on with the 3-shift system.  Issara declined and noted that we are not here to side with the business and communicate this message that the business requested.
remediation_validation: The workers voted to move back to the 2-shift system and this ended with the business laying off more than 1,000 workers.  The workers that had reported the issue of the lack of security and risk of crime have been let go.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case with a poor rating. The business has resorted to laying off workers when workers expressed their request to work on a 2-shift system.

description: Deception/misinformation related to disclosure of job requirements/costs/timing/other terms and conditions of employment
remediation_issara_recommendation: Context: The issue with a worker whose documents were not extended by the business so that the worker ended up being arrest by the local police and being detained from June 22 till today (14-Jul). The worker said that she had given her document and the extension fees to the business since February - 2021 but the business was not able to extend her work permit. She added that she had been working for the business without a valid work permit since February. It is also added that there could be more workers in this situation.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The business response ID- 1332

Issara raised this issue with Nike, Nike responded that they have checked with Hong Seng and found as following - The problem is that the DOE said it didn't have the client's information in the system, even though HS had processed her work permit. HS does not know how this could be the case. HS decided to continue to employ her after Jan 2021 without the proper documents.  With rising Covid cases, there was a government Internal Security Operations Command (ISOC) inspection of the factory and they found the client to be working with an expired visa.  HS tried to negotiate with the police but she was taken to the immigration detention center, first to Suan Plu now to another IDC in Bang Khen, and awaiting deportation.  HS was providing her with 3 meals a day while in Suan Plu IDC and also has been paying her daily wages from the date of her arrest.  Now, she is in the Bang Khen IDC, where she is more isolated and HS cannot provide her with the daily meals as they used to at Suan Plu IDC.  HS wants to hire her back after she goes through the MOU process back in Myanmar. Issara has shared the newly announced document by the government which has options for the workers to apply their documents in Thailand.
remediation_notes: The issue with one worker that was arrested by the police because her work permit had expired, which the business failed to extend even though she had already paid the business for her medical check-up, work permit, and visa.  She is currently in a detention center and has been told she will be deported when the borders open.
remediation_action: Issara has alerted the Strategic Partner about this issue, and the SP is in the process of working with the business to resolve the matter.

remediation_action:
Issara has alerted the Strategic Partner about this issue, and the SP is in the process of working with the business to resolve the matter.

The SP provided an update saying that the business had arranged for the worker to be released from the immigration detention center, and processed her working papers.  She will begin work at the business as before.
remediation_validation: The worker has confirmed that she has received assistance to leave the detention center.  She also received her daily wages during the whole time she had to stay in the detention center.  However, because the business had to send the money to her through the immigration police, the police charged a 100 Baht fee for every 1,000 Baht transferred to the worker.  This is an illegal deduction and the police should not have charged the worker such fees.  However, she did not want to request the return of the money the police had taken from her, and was happy to have received wages from the business and to be out of the detention center.
remediation_results: The business worked with relevant government departments to secure her release from the immigration detention center, processed her legal working documents so that she can resume work at the business as before, and paid for her wages during the time she had to stay in the detention center.  The worker has confirmed all this and is happy to be free and back to work.  However, the business had to transfer payments to her through the police at the detention center, and the police made illegal deductions on the money received, so the worker ended up receiving less than what she should have received.

description: Deception/misinformation related to disclosure of job requirements/costs/timing/other terms and conditions of employment
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Mr. Tun Tun Win: Worker ID #91190603131.  The client joined HIT91 as an MOU worker in 2019 but was being assigned to the Hi-Tech warehouse in Suksawat Soi 64. This location was known as HIT64 and there are about 7-8 workers there. In HIT64, the business stocks rolls of different garments and the workers in that site have to work with stock-in/out and deliver the garments to-from HIT91 and HIT70. The workers have to carry the heavy garment rolls. After working there for two years, he is suffering from a stomach problem and so he cannot manage to work there anymore. He has to be hospitalized for a week and then after he is  discharged from the hospital, the doctor recommends that the job is not suitable for him anymore. So on 16 Apr 2022, he asked to move and work at HIT91 as a sewing worker.

But now, he is in a probation period and the production manager, P'Man, told him that his performance is not satisfactory as a sewing worker. They had him try and work in the ironing section too but because he injured his foot in an accident while he was working in HIT64 and he cannot manage to stand for very long. If a worker with 3 years sewing experience can sew 40 pieces per hour, he can manage to sew like 30 pieces.  And he has been asked to sew many different patterns and designs, with each taking time to get better at.  He would like the business to give him more chances to try as a sewing worker or if they are not happy with his performance, to consider having him work in the cutting or printing lines because he cannot manage to carry heavy loads in HIT64 and he cannot stand for long to do ironing work.

Talking points:
-Why is this worker who has been with HIT for more than two years being asked to pass a probation period?
-How does the business determine whether a worker passes or fails the probation?
Recommendations:
-Clearly communicate to the worker the company’s expectations for his performance and the objective criteria based on which the company determines the worker’s performance
-Consider whether this worker can be assigned to a job that he can do competently at HIT91 because he cannot for health reasons go back to work at HIT64
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The following are the rules for transferring workers:
- The transferee line must have a vacancy rate in order to receive the transfer.
- The transferee line that will receive the transfer must have a need to hire more workers.
- Workers applying for transfer must have the necessary qualifications or skills.

This worker previously worked at DC64 and requested to be transferred to branch factory 91 as a sewing apprentice despite not being a probationary employee but is a sewing apprenticeship based on the worker's preferences, it has nothing to do with the probation. Approximately one month into sewing training, the worker informed the trainer that I do not want to practice sewing and would like to move on to another job. The trainer had spoken with HR and suggested that the ironing position be filled. Asked if the worker is interested in becoming an ironing worker, which the worker refused. Currently, the worker works as a sewing worker for Line Sewing 15. The worker has not been transferred to another position, and HR has communicated and explained with the employee to gain a better understanding.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that he had joined HIT91 as an MOU worker in 2019 but was assigned to the Hi-Tech warehouse in Suksawat Soi 64 known as HIT64. As this warehouse stocks rolls of different garments and the workers have to lift these heavy rolls and deliver the garments to-from HIT91 and HIT70, he ended up suffering from a stomach problem and a foot injury, with the doctor recommending that this job was not suitable for him anymore.  He asked and was reassigned to work in HIT91 as a sewing worker. However, he was given a probation period and the production manager, P'Man, told him that his performance was not satisfactory as a sewing worker. He would like the business to give him more time to improve as a sewing worker or to consider having him work in the cutting or printing lines because he cannot go back to carry heavy loads in HIT64 and he cannot stand for long to do ironing work.

description: Deception/misinformation related to disclosure of job requirements/costs/timing/other terms and conditions of employment
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Thein Lwin Oo (Ko Fatee) reported that 380 Burmese MOU workers arrived to Cal-Comp on 28th September with the service of Aye Lin Leh Htut ALLH (Myanmar recruitment agency) but haven't started working yet. Most of these workers are staying in a place that is a 45-minute drive from the factory. Since they haven't started work and have no income, they had to rent their rooms and buy food with the money they brought from home. Some of the workers are facing a very difficult situation. When they asked why they haven't started work yet, the Thai recruiter requested them to wait for 2 weeks but they didn't give the proper reason. When they asked some responsible persons from the business directly, they said it might be a month before there is work for them.  These workers received their MOU contracts and work permits, having signed the contract on 24 June 2022 in Yangon. However, when they arrived at the factory, the sub-recruiter PS-1P2 (36), U Tar and Ko Sa Nay, took all the MOU contracts and the workers don't know why or when they will get them back. They still have their work permits (dated 27 Sep 2022) and OWIC cards in their possession.

TPs:
-How is CC managing the hiring of MOU workers?
-How is CC working with ALLH? with the Thai recruiter?  What are their responsibilities?  
-Is HR directly involved when MOU workers arrive in Thailand?
-Is HR aware that there are Myanmar workers that were hired by CC and have arrived in Thailand since Sept 28th but have no work?  That they seem to be under the control of the Thai recruiter?
-Have these workers signed an employment contract with a specific start date?  What is the starting date of their employment contracts?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Investigate this matter immediately, and identify why MOU workers hired by CC have arrived at the factory and yet have not started work for weeks
-For the time that they have been in Thailand without being given work to do by CC, provide the 75% of the wages as required by the law
-Ensure the workers get their employment contracts with a clear starting date (with the date being the date they arrived in Thailand) as soon as possible, and ensure the Thai recruiter returns their MOU contracts immediately
-Ensure that the workers receive immediate relief for food and daily essential supplies including rent for this month since many don't have enough money to buy those provisions

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Star Butterfly general service Co.ltd
Hoi Yun SDN.NHD. 
 
Recruitment background.
 
10 workers 5 Male and 5 Female were recruited in Mid November 2022. However 2 female workers out of 10 had to pay 5,100,000 Kyats (2424.50 USD)  for the recruitment fees to the broker who was recruiting workers for an Agency named “ Star Butterfly general service” in Myanmar. The rest of the 8 workers did not have to pay any fees for different reasons such as having their relatives in the workplace, being recruited with Zero fees however they also heard that they will be deducted their salary by the employer. However, the contract does not mention the zero recruitment fee. 

Main issues 

They started working on the 18th of November,2022. Two female workers out of 8 called Issara to report the following issues. 

1) Different working conditions from what they were promised for. Their contract does not mention the type of work.Once they apply for the job, the broker said it is packaging of the seafood product, however, workers are having to work at the place which is similar to the pier where they have to sort fresh fish. These two workers said that they have health issues working with the ice and water which is why they did ask the broker about the type of work, the broker said that they will not need to touch water and ice at all but now things turn out the other way around. 
2) Not getting a weekly day off as mentioned in the contract. 
3) Having to work on an hourly rate not daily rate which is against  the contract. 
4) Not getting Malaysian Public holidays.
5) Not having their documents such as passport and permit  in their hand, only provided with the copy of it. 
6) Not knowing when they will receive their wages. They started working on 18th Nov but have not received their wages yet and are not sure when they will receive it. 
7) Not having a safe community to live in; they said that there are only 3 single girls and two females with their husband then the rest of the workforce is male workers, the environment is not safe because of the drug users. These two workers do not feel safe to continue working there. They called the broker to complain about the situation but were told not to complain as they have been working already. They do not have contact with the recruitment agency.

Issara sent a message to follow up with her to learn her expectations for her cases, she said that she and her friends received a salary for 8 days only even though they have worked for about 25 days. The employer said to them that they retain their 15 days of wages as deposit. In addition to that, the employer did not pay for the days that he was not able to provide job, did not get paid for over time as worked, they worked 3 hours of IT some days but received only 2 hours of wages. Workers tried to negotiate to work daily basis but not on an hourly basis, however the employer forced them to work hourly basis. Workers said that they will discuss with the broker who they worked with to get this job, however the employer said not to discuss with the agency or the broker but to decide by themselves. Given that, the workers have called the broker, the broker said that they will inform the agency and agency will try to negotiate. Workers were asked to wait and see for one month.

The worker said that they have reported to the broker about their situation, the broker had suggested them to wait one month until next pay day and see if they need to reach out to the recruitment agency. However, their current situation is that they are not provided with a full day of work, it has been three days that they have been working for only half a day. Given that, the employer asked them to do the office cleaning as a domestic worker which workers did not like the most. Workers wanted Issara to suggest whether they should directly reach out to the Recruitment agency without waiting for another month as suggested by the broker or should they wait for a month? 

Issara provided the contact information of the recruitment agency and asked them to make a proper decision before contacting them and making sure there is no risks for them for contacting the RA. remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: 

-One of the clients shared that his nephew came to KL, Malaysia on October 4th, 2023 through AGA International, RL: 530, a recruitment agency in Bangladesh. he paid a total fee of 420,000tk to the agency for visa and everything. an addition of 10,000tk was spent for medical check up on their own. Total 3905 USD. 

- a total of 400 workers came in separate groups along with him through the same agency. the clients nephew signed a contract for Orionplus Construction (M) SDN BHD, for the contract he paid 2,000tk in Bangladesh (which is a common practice for signing and getting contract in hand, according to the client). 

- since their arrival in Malaysia they have not been provided with any job yet. they are kept together in groups in a facility on factory site. the agency and Orionplus promised them that between 15th-17th November they will provide them with CIDB card and only after then they can start working.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The issue with the unavailable interpreter at the production line. A worker went to HR to access translation service to submit a sick leave request, however, the translator said that she/he is now allowed to go to the production line to see the supervisor and assist the workers.

-Issara recommendations.  
-The businesses to conduct an investigation for the actions of the interpreter and potential reasons for not helping the worker at the production line. 
-Safeguard should be in place during the investigation process and there should not be any retaliation against the worker (following TU no-retaliation policy). 



Time frame 1 pay period.


-Please ask the following questions to the business. 
-What is the role of this translator? 
-Who helps the workers at the production line. Is there another translator assigned to provide interpretation services to workers on the working line?
-if the HR translator is the one assigned to assist workers on the working line, what is the process for workers to request the service?
remediation_business_steps_taken:
23,Dec,2020.
The business; The HR has investigated and already communicated and responded that their investigation found that the translator was not available on that day to help the worker in the production line. However, the business conducted communication with the translator and confirmed that the worker has received sick leave payment accordingly.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business to communicate with the workers about the availability of the translators including roles and responsibilities for any type of assistant workers may need.
- Based on the results of the investigation, the business shall consider if any changes are needed to guarantee workers can access interpretation services whenever they need to.
