description: Interpretation is unavailable/inadequate/unprofessional
remediation_issara_recommendation:
There is only a Cambodian interpreter in ITC and there are around 400 workers right now. As there is the only interpreter sometimes workers can't get sufficient support from the interpreter, for instant recently there are some Cambodian workers accompanied by the interpreter to the hospital but he need to rush back to the factory as there are urgent task for him to complete so, workers end up at the hospital without fully support from the interpreter. Moreover, it is also difficult for night shift workers to seek support from the interpreter because he works on the day shift.

TPs:
-Does the business have plans to hire additional Cambodian interpreters, since the workers have expressed they are not receiving sufficient interpretation support?
 
Recommendations for remediation:
-Assess the need and hire additional interpreters: Ensure that there are enough Cambodian interpreters for the 400 plus Cambodian workforce, so that workers can adequate interpretation support at the factory and also at the hospital when they need to be able to communicate with the doctors and nurses regarding their health care needs and that night shift workers also have an interpreter available during their shift.
remediation_business_steps_taken: According to K. Kung, HR, the three new interpreters are Burmese. There are currently 400 Cambodian workers. They have an official interpreter and a group of volunteer Cambodian workers who can speak Thai and can assist with translation when workers request it. There are ten volunteers working as interpreters. For the requesting procedure, the worker can approach the supervisor or HR directly. The interpreter will then be prepared by HR.
remediation_notes: There is only one Cambodian interpreter at ITC and there are around 400 Cambodian workers right now. With only one interpreter, sometimes workers can't get sufficient interpretation support. For instance, recently there were some Cambodian workers that went to the hospital accompanied by the interpreter but he needed to rush back to the factory as there was an urgent task for him to complete so workers ended up at the hospital without any interpretation help. Moreover, it is difficult for night shift workers to seek support from the interpreter because he only works the day shift.
remediation_action: HR noted that there are currently 400 Cambodian workers. They have one official Khmer interpreter and a group of 10 volunteer Cambodian workers who can speak Thai that assist with interpretation when workers request it. In regards to requesting interpretation support, the worker can approach the supervisor or HR directly, and HR will prepare the available official interpreter or volunteer.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change:
-Regularly assess worker needs for interpretation support to improve employer-employee communication
-Set standards in terms of the number of interpreters per set number of workers so that there is always sufficient interpreters available
-Regularly train the interpreters so that they build the skills needed to be able to provide good quality interpretation services to the workers

description: Interpretation is unavailable/inadequate/unprofessional
remediation_issara_recommendation:
There are around 400 Cambodian workers with additional new batches of MOU workers arriving but there is only one Cambodian interpreter at ITC. Workers shared examples about how this lack of interpreters at ITC has negatively affected them.  A worker who needed interpretation support at the hospital because his wife was sick couldn't get it because the interpreter had gone to pick up a new batch of MOU workers at the border. Also, the interpreter only works the day shift and so when night shift workers need interpretation support or workers need to go to the hospital at night, the interpreter says he cannot help.  The workers would like more interpreters to be available to support them in both the day and night shifts. 

TPs:
-Does ITC have plans to hire additional Cambodian interpreters, given that there is this additional need for the number of Cambodian workers in the day and night shifts?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Ensure that there is adequate interpretation support for the Cambodian workers during both the day and night shifts, with at least two interpreters each for the day and night shifts so there is a back-up if one interpreter is unavailable during each shift
-Hear directly from the Cambodian workers as to what kind of interpretation support needs they have for what kinds of instances and when so that the company can be responsive to their needs
-Communicate with the Cambodian workers the company's plan to increase the number of interpreters so that there is adequate support, and by when this will be in place
remediation_business_steps_taken:
There are currently 260 Cambodian workers. HR will communicate with all Cambodian workers in the following ways.
HR collaborates with the hospital interpreter and pays the fee service for workers who require help facilities at the hospital.
Inform the workers about the volunteer interpreter group that can assist them during the night shift.


Investigate Case:
Because at present, the total number of Cambodian workers is 230 people and most of them have been working for a long time and can understand Thai other than HR's interpreters.

Solution:
There will be a transportation service to take the worker to the hospital every day. If it's an emergency case, night shift, the supervisor would use the interpreter from the nationality interpreter register that HR regularly updates to inform the supervisors every month. Emergency sickness workers must be sent to the hospital and every time the worker needs an interpreter, the supervisor will look at the interpreter register to help communicate and explain the work in the area. In addition, the HR department will communicate with the interpreter registered in Messenger, and representatives of each dormitory, so that representatives, including Cambodian workers who are members, are informed.
remediation_notes: There are around 400 Cambodian workers with additional new batches of MOU workers arriving but there is only one Cambodian interpreter at ITC. Workers shared examples about how this lack of interpreters at ITC has negatively affected them.  A worker who needed interpretation support at the hospital because his wife was sick couldn't get it because the interpreter had gone to pick up a new batch of MOU workers at the border. Also, the interpreter only works the day shift and so when night shift workers need interpretation support or workers need to go to the hospital at night, the interpreter says he cannot help.  The workers would like more interpreters to be available to support them in both the day and night shifts.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change:
-Have a long-term plan for ensuring there is an appropriate number of Cambodian interpreters and forecast the expected total number of Cambodian workers year-on-year and plan for the number of Cambodian interpreters accordingly
-Develop a training program for Cambodian interpreters so that they are trained to provide accurate, unbiased, and objective interpretation support to the Cambodian workers.  Issara can provide ethical interpretation training to the interpreters

description: Interpretation is unavailable/inadequate/unprofessional
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The issue with an unsupportive translator at Building 5 cold storage.

Issara recommendations.  

-The businesses to do immediate investigations and take action plan. 
-Safeguards should be in place during the investigations process.
-The business to revise the roles and responsibilities of the translators if needed. 
-The business to communicate with the workers about translators' roles and responsibilities.

Withing 1 to 2 pay period.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
11 June 2020

The business investigation found the issue and committed that the Human Resource (HR) to co-organized the training on “Boosting Thai Language Communication” for workers who have this ability in order to help communicate (Thai & Myanmar) for other workers in case the Translator/Language Communicators is not present at the factory.


** Since then, the business has not got back to us. 
Issara also could not contact the workers from this building.
remediation_notes:
Context; This is an issue that comes from Building 5. The translator's name is Mr. Maung Zaw. The translator does not fully translate what the workers want to say.

Talking Points ;

_What are the exact responsibilities of this translator? Is he officially appointed by the business? 
_What are the criteria for selecting/recruiting translators?
_How often do the translators receive training? 
_How the business monitor the translation services?


Workplace interpreters should be qualified and trained both in linguistic proficiency as well as professional conduct as a workplace interpreter.  

☑  Accuracy. Interpreters should be aware of their responsibility to translate accurately and completely at all times, ensuring they do not leave out or embellish anything which either the employer or worker has said. Everything (including side conversations) must be translated, and the original tone and meaning of statements in the source language made must be preserved.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business to conduct frequent cross-check policy regarding translation services to make sure that the workers have access and proper translation services when needed. 

-Business shall communicate clearly (both in a verbal and written document) with all translators as well as all workers about the business policy on inappropriate behaviour.

-Every detail information that was provided by the workes should be translated professionally. 

Communication.

Effectively communicate to workers what the services are, the contact information of focal points and availability, actions that will be taken by the business for investigations and safeguarding, and timeframes. 

-Credible and safe grievance mechanisms should include transparency and safeguards for all workers.  

-Recommend Issara training to the translators.  

-Issara can also provide tailored training to full HR teams on-site, and provide systems review with tailored recommendations to eliminate labour risks."

- Have they communicated to the workers what services the interpreters will provide?

Same as for Case #1

description: Interpretation is unavailable/inadequate/unprofessional
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Workers reported that the translator do not want to accompany workers to the hospital when they are sick and that the translator is bias and not always open to provide interpretation services to workers. 

Talking points:
-What is the company policy regarding interpretation services for workers with health needs? What is the interpreter availability to do so? 

Recommendations: 

The businesses to take action by clarifying the roles and responsibilities of the interpreter and to investigate the potential reasons for not providing interpretation services to workers whenever they need it. During the investigation, the business should make sure that workers do not face any kind of retaliation for raising this issue. 

In order to understand the quality of the service being provided by the interpreter, it is recommended for the business to get workers feedback and to monitor the interpreter performance.

Interpreters are key actors in grievance mechanisms as workers seek for their assistance for translation to share their concerns, needs and feedback. Therefore, the business should take this issue as a priority to make sure workers can safely and actively use the company grievance mechanisms.   

 
Timeframe 1 pay period
remediation_business_steps_taken: The business did not specifically take action or conducted the investigation towards the translator. However, it has responded having done the communication to reassure the policy and policy regarding this issue.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
The business to work with the interpreter on his/her roles and responsibilities to make sure workers can access the service whenever needed and that the quality of the service is appropriate so that workers feel comfortable of approaching the interpreter anytime. 

In terms of communication, the business should share with workers what are the roles and responsibilities of the interpreter, along with his/her availability. 

It is recommended for the business to provide training to the interpreter on ethics and principles on interpretation.

11-June-2021.Business response ID - 1255.

systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations; 
-To have open discussion sessions between  HR and workers to understand better what are the challenges being faced by workers and what is driving them to resign. During these discussions, the business is encouraged to share with workers what the business actions are to address these issues.

description: Interpretation is unavailable/inadequate/unprofessional
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that they had received the announcement that the business will no longer arrange for the interpreters to accompany them to the hospital when needed.  When workers are sick, they would have to go to the factory clinic first to get checked out, and if the factory nurse determined that the worker needed to go to the hospital, she would write the illness on the paper and the worker would have to go to the hospital without an interpreter. The business would provide interpretation support via phone if needed.  If workers use external interpreter on their own will, the business will not reimburse the cost. The business said that this is a trial period and if this process does not work, the business will try to find an official interpreter. Workers know that the single interpreter the business employed just resigned and so are depending on informal volunteer interpreters to provide workers with this interpretation support.

Talking Points:
-Is the business changing the policy on providing interpretation services to workers because of the lack of an interpreter?
-Is this a short-term change or is the business considering to continue without hiring adequate, qualified interpreters?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Recognizing that workers need the interpretation support when getting medical care, and it is something the business has been providing in the past, the business should hire 1 or more qualified interpreters as soon as possible
-Announce to all workers that this is a temporary measure during the interim period when there is no interpreter
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Leena, HR manager, stated that the last official interpreter recently resigned and that HR is currently recruiting interpreters. So, HR requires the worker who requests the interpreter to contact HR. And HR will find some temporary workers who both speak Thai and Burmese. Following the arrival of the new interpreter, the interpreter will assist workers in translating at the hospital and other locations as needed. They will announce to all workers that this is a temporary measure during the interim period when there is no interpreter.

BHR followed up with K. Leena, HR manager. She responded that now she is drafting the announcement and in process of translation. All three issues will be verbally announced via the morning talk session and written announcements will be posted on the boards around the factory. She will finish these things and get back to us by this week.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that they had received the announcement that the business will no longer arrange for the company interpreter to accompany them to the hospital when needed. The business would only provide interpretation support via phone if needed.  If workers use external interpreter on their own will, the business will not reimburse the cost. The business said that this is a trial period and if this process does not work, the business will try to find an official interpreter.
remediation_action: HR stated that the one official interpreter recently resigned and that HR is currently recruiting interpreters. Following the arrival of the new interpreter, the interpreter will assist workers in translating at the hospital and other locations as needed. They will announce to all workers that this is a temporary measure during the interim period when there is no interpreter.

Recommendations for remediation:

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Cambodian workers reported that the Khmer interpreter is not being helpful. When the workers are sick and need an interpreter for assistance, the interpreter would not be available. Because the worker expects the interpreter to take them immediately or to have the interpreter (the person contacted by the worker) take them on the interpreter's day off, the interpreter may be unable to go. They stated that there are already enough Cambodian interpreters in the factory.
remediation_notes: Cambodian workers reported that the Khmer interpreter is not being helpful. When the workers are sick and need an interpreter for assistance, the interpreter would not be available.  The interpreter also blamed the workers for finding excuses not to work. description: Interpretation is unavailable/inadequate/unprofessional
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue #1. 

Context; Worker who had issues with the supervisor approached HR to request to be moved to a different line under a different line supervisor as she was being treated poorly by this supervisor being denied for her request which led her to submit the resignation. Worker name - Zin Mar Wai, ID:721626. Used to work for line PU-4, no.67 managed by the line supervisor P'Pa-Yin. 

Recommendations (already given):
-The business shall immediately investigate the issues with the worker, supervisor, and translator and make sure that the worker has the opportunity to share what happened and what led her to submit her resignation. 
-It is fundamental that the business takes necessary steps to guarantee there would not be any retaliation towards the worker during or after the investigation. Because any kind of retaliation not only impacts the worker but also the company grievance mechanisms since workers would feel afraid of sharing any issues with HR in the future. Therefore, the business shall make sure that the supervisor and the translator do not have any negative attitudes towards the worker following the investigation. 
-The worker should be provided with the option of bringing a colleague to support with translation/clarification as needed. 
-The business is suggested to come to an agreement with the worker based on the result of the investigation

Issue # 2. (added on 21-June-2021). 
Context: The issue with lack of communication about the COVID-19 test and the workers who were found positive. Workers raised their questions and concerns about whether they will be paid for their quarantine days, who will pay for the medical treatment costs, and so on. Workers at the business make announcements in the morning which is about 5 minutes of the announcement but only in the Thai language. 

Recommendations; 
-The business shall provide clear guidance about the assistance for workers that test positive for COVID-19. The guidance shall be provided in writing accompanied by verbal announcements in all workers languages and it should cover the following information: 
-are there different measures/procedures depending on the severity of the symptoms 
-who will cover the treatment costs (SSF, employer?) 
-quarantine centers and services
-the process that the infected and not infected workers will have to follow (self-quarantine, etc.)
-the payment of the wages for the days of quarantine whenever needed

Talking points
-How many workers have been tested and found positive so far? How has the business managed infected workers? 
-Which hospital or quarantine centers are the workers being sent to?
-Workers raised that some of the workers have been tested positive and only a few of the closed stationed workers are being asked for 14 days of quarantine while other workers in the same line are still being asked to come to work. How has the business managed the workers who share the dormitory and production lines?  
-How have the workers been communicated about the COVID-19 treatment fees?

timeframe 1 week
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The business response ID 1250.

Issara reached out to the business to raise worker's concerns and provide recommendations. The business responded by not having another production to change this impacted worker as requested. Therefore, the business decided the worker to let go with a proper job cancellation letter. It was not clear from the business side about the investigation process that leads the worker to submit her resignation. The worker updated receiving job cancellation letter and she is in the process of finding a new employer.

Issue #2. 
Id - 1280
06/22/2021

The business responded that they have been working closely with the providential government to make sure all of the COVID-19 policies are followed. It is added that the workers who have bees required for the quarantine will receive payment with sick leave. The business will have an internal meeting on the recommendations that are provided by Issara and get back to update Issar.

remediation_action:

 Therefore, the business provided the worker with the proper job cancellation letter.
remediation_validation: The worker confirmed receiving the job cancellation letter and has found a new employer.

description: Interpretation is unavailable/inadequate/unprofessional
remediation_issara_recommendation:
There is only one interpreter at the HR office and no interpreter in production line. Whenever workers need interpretation support in the working line, they cannot find her.  Also, she cannot accompany them to the hospital outside of office hours so workers have to hire their own interpreter.

Talking points:
What is the company policy regarding interpretation support?  
Does the company provide interpretation support to workers when they have to get medical care at the hospital?

Recommendations for remediation:
Assess whether the current number of interpreters is sufficient for the needs expressed by the workers, by asking workers when they need interpretation support and whether the interpreter is available when needed.
Communicate verbally and in writing when the interpreter is available and whether interpretation support is provided to workers that need to visit the hospital in the evenings or weekends.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Yuppadee- the company does not have an issue with not enough interpreters. The worker can get assistance from interpreters to help accompany them to hospital. Even Though, the company has only one official interpreter who is a man but there are 14 workers in the production lines who speak both languages. If the female worker needs assistance the company will arrange some female interpreters from the Welfare Committee to accompany them.


The investigation result:
There is one HR interpreter (male). There are 280 Burmese workers and another 20 production line interpreters, as shown below.
1. Captain of sewing line; 6 interpreters
2. Interpreter for cutting department 1 person, stock 1 person, person 1 person
3. Interpreter on duty at job translation, mechanic 5 people, QC 1 person
4. Interpreters from the working group 3 people and the safety working group 2 people

Action: Timeline, week 3 of June
Conducting the interpreters' meeting, which includes the welfare/safety working group, to review the interpreter's roles and responsibilities in order to provide timely assistance in problem resolution. Bringing problems that have been forwarded to the responsible person for consideration in order to make workers feel at ease. It is secure to work and meet with supervisors (Sewing department every Monday and Thursday, other departments every Tuesday)
- Clarification of the company's communication channels

-Introduce the interpreters and their roles and responsibilities.

Also, she cannot accompany them to the hospital outside of office hours so workers have to hire their own interpreter.
remediation_action:
The business HR responded that the company does not have an issue with insufficient interpreters. The worker can get assistance from interpreters to help accompany them to hospital. Even though the company has only one official male interpreter, there are also 20 workers in the production lines who speak both languages and function as informal interpreters. If a female worker needs assistance at the hospital, the company will arrange a female interpreter who is also a Welfare Committee member to accompany them.

In addition, the business will conduct a meeting with the interpreters to review their roles and responsibilities in order to provide timely assistance to workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change:
Conduct training for the interpreter (recommend Issara training), so that he is available and responsive to the support needs of the workers
Hire additional interpreters that can provide interpretation support on the production floor and during out-of-office hours if workers require interpretation support during hospital visits.

description: Issue with targets and/or bonuses (related to production and incentives): Minor violation
remediation_issara_recommendation:
In some production lines, the line supervisors implicitly pressure the workers to reach the daily target within 8 hours by promising them OT hours if the workers hit the target but actually the supervisors didn't give them OT even when the workers reached the target.

TPs:
- What daily production targets are set for workers, how does this affect their pay or working hours (i.e. is OT work given based on ability to hit targets during the regular shift?), and how are these targets communicated to the workers?

Recommendations:
- If OT hours are offered to workers based on some performance criteria, the criteria should be fair and the system the business uses to select workers for OT should be clearly communicated to, and understood by workers
- Investigate how workers are feeling pressure to reach targets, whether the conditions for getting OT hours is being to apply this pressure, and why the conditions (giving OT work if workers meet the target) are not being met
- Communicate clearly to workers, verbally and in writing, the business' practice of having production targets, how they are set, and that they are not coercive
remediation_notes: In some production lines, the line supervisors implicitly force the workers to reach the daily target within 8 hours by promising them OT hours if the workers hit the target but actually the supervisors didn't give them OT even when the workers reached the target.
remediation_action: The business stated that it doesn't have any OT work provided to workers.
remediation_validation: Since mid-April 2023, the workers said the business doesn't have any OT work for workers so the original report is not currently relevant.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Survey workers on a regular basis regarding how they perceive the treatment they are receiving from their supervisors, to identify issues of inadequate implementation of company policies by supervisors.

description: Issue with targets and/or bonuses (related to production and incentives): Minor violation
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; the issue with the incentive that the workers are not receiving since they have a new supervisor in their production line. Workers reported that they used to receive intentive up to 2000 per pay period but they have not received it since they have a new line supervisor. 
Working Line; Cut Site" (In the Thai language) where the raw prawns firstly arrived and the workers have to sort them out by size and take out those which are not fresh anymore. 

Workers have reported to line supervisor, the supervisors said "take it easy(chai yin yin), and not helping workers to solve this issue. Workers have reached out to HR, the HR responded that the supervisor didn't share with HR any info on incentives so they do not have any information.
 
Recommendations: 

-The business to conduct the investigation on this working line to assess how incentives are being calculated and recorded, and what could be the reasons for workers not receiving incentives recently.

-The investigation should include production (whoever is responsible for setting targets and calculating the incentives amounts and the line supervisor who records the workers' work) and also feedback from workers.

- Based on the results of the investigation and analysis of the targets the business should compensate workers accordingly if needed. 

-Disciplinary actions should be taken towards the supervisor if the investigation found an issue of misconduct by the supervisor. 

-It is recommended for the business to clarify to line supervisors and workers how incentives are calculated and what actions is the business taking to respond to workers concern on incentives and also the actions to improve their grievance mechanisms systems to make sure there are actions taken when workers report a case to HR or to any other grievance mechanism channel. 
 

Talking Points; 
-What is the incentive process for this line? 
-The workers said that they have reported to HR, why did HR not conduct the investigation? HR just putting the issue to the supervisor instead of conducting the investigation can lead the workers to discontinue using the business grievance channel. 

Time Frame; 2 weeks.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that they used to receive incentive up to 2000 baht per pay period but they have not received it since they have a new line supervisor. They additionally reported they were not able to get further information on the change from the line supervisor or HR.
remediation_action: HR investigated the issue but focused on providing workers with a reason they did not get the incentive (not meeting a target, quality of work). The investigation on the incentive payment found that the incentive was given to eligible workers according to the rule which was communicated to all workers.
remediation_results: The business investigation did not include any focus on the conduct of the line supervisor and how incentives are calcuated and communicated to workers. It is recommended for the business to clarify to line supervisors and workers how incentives are calculated and what actions the business is taking to respond to workers concern on incentives and also the actions to improve their grievance mechanisms systems.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business to conduct the communication with all workers and supervisors in a written and verbal announcement about the result of the investigation. 

-The communication should include the process to calculate and record the incentives for reaching targets, this helps to increase transparency and workers' understanding of the company policies and systems. In addition, workers can understand better how they can improve their performance. 

Time Frame; 2 weeks.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker in a production line for descaling and deboning fish reported that there are different incentive being paid to workers.  They work as a team of 8, with one descaling while the other 7 debone, and the de-scaler gets daily incentive of only 10 Baht while the de-boners get 60 Baht per day. The worker said they work together as a team and don't think they should receive different incentives. 

TPs:
- How are incentives calculated? Is there a reason why workers working as a team receive different daily incentives?

Recommendations:
- The incentive system should be fair and incentive pay should be reviewed and revised accordingly. As per this case, it is questionable as to why one team member gets 10 Baht and the others get 60 Baht as daily incentive pay.
- The incentive and bonus system should be clear to all workers and perceived to be fair; communicate, verbally and in writing, what incentives and bonuses are paid for what reasons so that workers fully understand what they can expect to receive.

description: Issue with targets and/or bonuses (related to production and incentives): Minor violation
Issue with targets and/or bonuses (related to production and incentives): Minor violation
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that there was a lack of clarity of the business policy related to targets and incentives.  Workers in different lines received different amounts.  Also, it seems the business has increased the target because they used to receive 120-130 Baht when they finished 6,000-7,000 pieces but now they receive only 80-90 Baht when they finish 8,000-9,000 pieces.  They don't know how the incentive pay is calculated and only see what they received when they receive their pay slips.

Talking points:
How are the incentives calculated?  Do certain tasks receive a higher incentive rate than others?  Are some incentive rates being decreased?
Is HR aware that workers don’t understand how the incentives are calculated and they feel it is unfair to some of them?

Recommendations for remediation
Communicate verbally and in writing to all workers the incentive system and how much incentive pay workers can expect to receive so that workers understand why some workers may get more than others
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Yuppadee- the workers’ income in the pay period is not just about the incentives but also depending on the minimum wages that there are some different skills different workers get different wages. And the incentive depends on the design and style. There are different styles and different qualities. However, the worker will get the incentive with the completed product. For example, the cutting line, the sewing line and the packing line, all these lines have to finish all and get the incentive together. For communication, the line supervisor always explains to all workers before they start working on a new design and style based on the quality of pieces and they will get different rates of incentive. 

If the worker has any questions they can ask the Captain Team who can speak Burmese.


The investigation result:
Incentive;
1. Getting the Cut to Box job ready for the sewing machine. (The production department holds a meeting to emphasize the work's readiness.)
2. Employees in that affiliation must be able to sew in each style.
3. Collaborative effort ready to work together to achieve Time to Cycle Participate in the Balance Line
There are the reasons that, of all the components, the each line receive the different incentives

Action: Timeline, from week 3 of June to end of July
Human Resources/Security Talk with supervisors (every Monday and Thursday for the sewing department, and every Tuesday for the other departments) - Safety should be communicated. Each working area has a unique environment. PPE is strictly prohibited in order to reduce workplace accidents.

- Communicating and reviewing the elements that will make employees receive incentives, such as team breaks, teamwork, help, Self.QC to reduce work quality problems (reject), pulling team members to practice skills before changing work styles, and so on.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that there was a lack of clarity of the business policy related to targets and incentives.  Workers in different lines received different amounts.  Also, it seems the business has increased the target because they used to receive 120-130 Baht when they finished 6,000-7,000 pieces but now they receive only 80-90 Baht when they finish 8,000-9,000 pieces.  They don't know how the incentive pay is calculated and only see what they received when they receive their pay slips.
remediation_action: The business responded that the workers will get the incentive pay based on the finished product so workers in the cutting line, the sewing line and the packing line will get the incentive together. For communication, the line supervisors always explain to all workers before they start working on a new design and style of a product the rates of the incentive pay.

description: Issue with targets and/or bonuses (related to production and incentives): Minor violation
remediation_issara_recommendation:
She reported that she was asked to go and assist other sewing lines without getting any extra pay. Normally if a worker is asked to go and assist in another line, he or she receives an extra 40 THB per day as an incentive. On 16 Jun, her line supervisor P'Cha-Phai, All (Chief) Supervisor P'Chun-Phue, and technician (coach) P'Mae Sar, asked her to go and assist other lines as needed. At the end of July, she reported this to her supervisor but the supervisor dismissed her saying they hadn't asked her to go and assist in other lines. Then she went and reported it to the Burmese HR interpreter (Min Han Win Aung) and he said that since she didn't sign any documents regarding this, they cannot give her the extra payment. The client then asked, why hadn't they asked her to sign anything? The HR interpreter escalated this with the line manager Mae' Pha, and she also said the same thing: no record, no payment. 

The client asked the line manager to have her assigned to one specific line but they still had her work in other lines as needed.  She wants us to help her by having HR solving the issue properly with the unprofessional line supervisor. If they cannot pay her extra pay like the others, they should have her assigned to one line. She would like to work in another building as she doesn't want to work there anymore and she fears being targeted too. If possible, she would like to get the incentive pay she should have received for those days that she was assigned to help other lines. The client's name is "Mrs. Pan Pa Pa Phyo", ID:111140500, line no.A-16.

Talking points:
-What is the company's incentive system and do workers get paid extra for working in different lines as needed by their supervisors?
-How has the incentive system been communicated to workers?  Is it clear, fair, and properly implemented?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Investigate this matter, with worker safeguards because this worker fears retaliation, and identify why this worker was not paid the incentive pay as she should have been.  If there is a process for a worker to sign a consent form to document evidence for the additional pay, did the line supervisor follow the process correctly?
-Pay the incentive amount to the worker after having established that she worked in other lines as requested and is entitled to that amount
-Communicate clearly with all workers about the incentive system, and what actions or performance will result in what monetary incentives, how it will be recorded and paid out

description: Issue with targets and/or bonuses (related to production and incentives): Minor violation
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The workers reported that the business has increased the production targets and offering OT work only to those workers that meet the target.  Sometimes, the workers will be allowed OT work if they reach 70-80% of the target and even then, the line supervisors might increase that threshold to 90% of the target.  And even when the workers meet the varying targets, they might still not be offered to do OT work because the business does not have more garments to be sewed that day. 

TPs:
-How is OT work offered to workers?  Is OT work offered to all workers or only to those workers that meet a certain daily target during normal working hours?
-How are the daily production targets set and have the targets been increased recently?

Recommendations for remediation:
-If it is the company's policy that OT hours are offered to all workers and not tied to performance during their normal working hours, investigate how line supervisors are acting against the said policy
-Train line supervisors on how to communicate clearly about the production targets to workers and the way OT work is offered to workers
-Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, the company's system for OT work, that it is offered to workers without discrimination.  If it is offered based on performance, this should be clearly explained as to how this is done objectively
-Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, how the daily production targets are set.  If the targets change or fluctuate, there should be an explanation as to how these targets are calculated and why there might be changes in the set targets

description: Issues with workforce and workloads: no violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context : The issue with over work load due to less work force as the workers from Ingredient Line are being shift to different line to full fill the workforce in the other lines. Workers reported facing challenges to complete their workforce with less workers since the work load is remain same event he workforce is decreasing. 

Issara recommendations 
-The business to conduct an investigation ethically taking into account safeguards for the workers. The investigation should aim to understand why the workers are being asked to do overwork load. The investigation should include workers voice. In order to generate a plan of action, the business shall coordinate with production department to make sure workloads are balanced, fair, and do not affect workers health. 

-The business to communicate with impacted workers, supervisors and manager the plan of action to address this issue. The communication should include information about workload and tasks in the written and should be explained verbally to workers. 
 
-Workers should have a humane environment in their working line.
-Workers should not be asked to work or cover when there some of their co-workers are being rotated or absent. 

Time frame 1 pay period
remediation_notes:
Talking Points : 

Please ask the business following questions ; 

-What is the recent turnover rate of this line/factory? If the current turnover rate is high, what has the business done to make sure that workers are not overworked?
-Ask the business if there are any extra incentives for these workers with high levels of workload. And what system does the business uses to track workloads and to make sure incentives are being paid accordingly?
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Communication. 
Effectively communicate to workers, manager and the line supervisors what the plan of action is to address this issue. 
-Training and planning sessions with Issara and HR on strengthening working condition, then broader training for line supervisors and others.
timeframe 1 pay period

#Issue (1) The issue with heavy workload and manpower with Cambodian workers. 

Issara recommendations 

-Recommend immediate investigation by employer, with safeguards by Issara.  If needed, the appropriate discipline of offender and apology to the worker. Beware of retaliation.  
-Ensure overworked workers have been remunerated fairly.


#issue (2) 24-August-2020

Context: The issue with heavy workload and manpower with Cambodian workers. 

-The business to conducts an investigation ethically taking into account safeguards for the workers. The investigation should aim to understand why the workers are being asked to work the same amount of workload with fewer workers. The investigation should include workers' voices. 
-In order to generate a plan of action, the business shall coordinate with the production department to make sure workloads are balanced, fair, and do not affect workers' health. 

-The business to communicate with impacted workers, supervisors, and managers the plan of action to address this issue. The communication should include information about workload and tasks in the written and should be explained verbally to workers. 
 
-Workers should have a humane environment in their working line.

Timeframe 1 pay period. 

# Issue (3). 1-Oct-2020.

The issue with a Cambodian worker being abused by a Thai worker after having an overwhelming workload being sent to the only Cambodian worker. ID - 11261. 

-The business to conduct an investigation immediately. The investigation should determine why the line supervisor was not able to ensure that the workers in this particular line all did their fair share of the work. 

-Disciplinary actions should be taken according to business policy. 

**Internal Note 

- This issue would also be discussed under the different KPI (
Unresponsive grievance mechanism / no action being taken).


Talking Points

Issue 1. 

Please share the issue detail with the business. 
-How often is production setting a new target and how is that analyzed and how is HR involved in that process?
-What is the recent turnover rate of the factory? If the current turnover rate is high, what the business has done to make sure that works are not overworked?

#Issue (3) 

Please see the talking points in different KPI (Unresponsive grievance mechanism / no action being taken).
remediation_business_steps_taken: BFI would like to know more about how insufficient manpower is or how excessive the workload is. They strongly against this because the manpower is calculated from the production capacity to avoid the wasted product. The average turnover rate is 6%.  They don't accept this issue if you do not have specific information to get to the point. However, they see that the root cause of this issue is that the worker takes a longer break time that may affect the workload in the production line.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business to clearly mention the workload and incentives process in the workers mannual and provide to each worker.

-Effectively communicate to workers, manager and the line supervisors what the plan of action is to address this issue. 

-Training and planning sessions with Issara and HR on strengthening working condition, then broader training for line supervisors and others.

Timeframe 1 pay period
systems_change_business_steps_taken: The business responded having done communication with the workers to make them understand the workload system. However, the workers still report having this issue.

description: Issues with workforce and workloads: no violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1
In the production line “chin suon”, the line supervisors pressured workers to meet increased targets.  For the past six months, the production targets have been increased based on the type of piece of meat (for chicken wing or leg, increased from 10 to 14kg per hour, for big pieces, increased from 25 to 30kg). When some workers can’t complete these targets, the line supervisor will notice those producing less and not offer them OT work in the future. Until now, but workers did not dare to raise this concern. 

Case #2
A worker reported that in his line with around 60 workers, he received a lot of pressure from the line supervisor to reach a certain target, to finish 100 kg/person within 5 hours before the 1-hour break.  That means workers have to slice 20kg of chicken meat per hour, which normally a worker completes around 10-15 kg only. If the worker does not complete the target, the line supervisor stares and says to the workers that "they are lazy and always going on toilet breaks". Workers feel they are being paid by piece rate, and feel pressured and irritated by the line supervisor's behavior. 

The detail info:
- There are around 60 workers on the production line
- Production line: Prer Roub - Kirami S3
- Line supervisor: Female; Monyrat

TPs:
-Have hourly production targets been increased in the past six months?  What is the reason for increasing the target?
-If workers are seen to not meet the target, line supervisors are denying them OT hours (Case #1).  Is OT work offered to workers on a conditional basis?
-If workers are seen to not meet the target, a line supervisor is using degrading language and calling workers lazy (Case #2).


Recommendations for remediation:
-Assess how the company determines production targets, and evaluate whether they are realistic and appropriate for the workforce.  Include workers' perspectives as part of this evaluation.
-Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, the company's production targets and how they are set (or increased) so that workers understand why they may be asked to increase efficiency
-Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, the company's policy regarding OT work, and how workers are selected for OT

description: Issues with workforce and workloads: no violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers from the Pla-Sud line reported about OT working hours not being informed in advance, workers not getting 20 minutes of breaks before starting OT hours, workload being discriminatively distributed against the nationality however, the worker did not give full consent to Issara to raise this issue with the business. 

Talking Points

-We understand that TU has a no retaliation policy that should be used to protect workers when they share their grievances through any channel. So we would like to learn more about TUF investigation processes whenever there is a case that is affecting workers on a small working line. 
-How would HR investigate a case, if the issue is connected to the line supervisors? How would sage guards be put in place to make sure workers on the small working line are not targeted or seen negatively by the supervisor or other employees? Can you please describe the process of investigation?
-When the business conducts an investigation involving a line supervisor, is the supervisor notified about the issue in that specific production line? Or how is that information handled?
-If workers have an issue from a small line but also have concerns about being retaliated by the supervisor, what is the business’s strategy to resolve such issues in such condition? 
-Has the TUF communicated about TUs no-retaliation policy to all workers and supervisors? If so, when and how? If not, any plan for that? 
Because workers express not being aware of the TUs’ no retaliation policy.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Since the worker did not give consent to share the issue with the business and it also has risks to share the name of the production line with the business as it is a small production with a small number of workers, Issara approached the business to learn about their process of investigation for such kind of issues where has risks for the workers being target by their supervisors as it is a small room. Issara checked with the business about their No Rataliaiton posily. The business responded that  No retaliation policy has been implemented since 2015, this was communicated to all workers in both Thai and Burmese languages. This is also emphasized in the annual training. Therefore, workers feel to raise their concern directly to HR. In addition to that, the business's external audit also has not found any issue with the compliance of the policy. The business added having different ways to conduct the investigation based on the issues. As the business response was not very clear for raised concern, the Issara team decided to escalate with the presentation with the Thai Union Groups team about the issues that need systemic improvement.

description: Issues with workforce and workloads: no violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
In the fish inner organ cleaning room (Compoda Room) is a sub-room of the raw fish room. Mr.Kyaw Hla reported that 6 workers from Compoda room was moved to the fish trimming line without the workers' consent. 

Since the time these workers started applying for jobs in TUF, they were assigned for this specific line and the workers like the nature of this working line and they agree to work in this line. But in the second week of August 2023, these 6 workers were temporarily moved to the fish trimming line, since that time these workers clearly stated that they can only work temporarily in fish trimming line. 

On 8th September 2023, the chief line-supervisor of Compoda room asked these 6 workers again to move to the fish trimming line by 11th Sep permanently. The workers don't understand why the chief line-supervisor keeps trying to move them to the fish trimming line. The business said they are moving these 6 workers to fish trimming line because of lesser work in Compoda room but the other line workers keeps moving to Compoda room and new workers have many tasks to do in Compoda room.

In TUF working nature, Compoda Line is more busy and more OT than other lines, in this particular event, the chief line-supervisor of Pla Sot (Raw Fish Line), Phee Myuu and new Chief Line supervisor who moved from PH-1 Phee Moo are intentionally manipulate the workforce by playing favoritism. They welcomed their favorite workers to Compoda where there is more OT but they moved the workers they don't like to fish trimming lines where there is no OT. In this particular workforce shifting, the chief supervisors told the 6 workers that we will have no more OT in Compoda room, so we moved the workers regardless of OT opportunities.

TPs:
- What is the company policy in terms of moving workers from one line to another?  Is it based on the nature of work?  How are such re-assignment decisions made?  Are workers consulted and able to consent before the move?

Recommendations:
- Workers feel they are being moved from the line that has more OT and this is directly affecting their income.  The business should provide a clear rationale as to why this decision was made. If the re-assignment was not a fair, transparent decision with the workers' consent, the business should consider to assign the workers back to where they have always been working.
- Communicate clearly to workers how work and production line assignments are made, when changes might be made for what reason, and have a transparent process where workers consent to such moves.
remediation_notes: Issara received a report that workers were being moved from one line that typically has a lot of OT to another line where there is less OT work, and the line supervisors are replacing them in that line with more OT with workers that they favor.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- Regularly assess worker satisfaction regarding the work and tasks they are performing
- Have a clear transparent process for any work or line re-assignments of workers

description: Issues with workforce and workloads: no violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; Workers being asked to do excessive workload with only 32 workers where it used to be 50 workers. Workers have reported to a supervisor about this issue but the supervisor said that they can leave the job if they can not manage it. Workers reported having callouses on their hands due to heavy workload.
-working line; Cut Site" (In the Thai language) where the raw prawns firstly arrived and the workers have to sort them out by size and take out those which are not fresh anymore.

Recommendations; 

-The business conducts an investigation ethically taking into account safeguards for the workers. The investigation should aim to understand why the workers are being asked to work a heavy workload with fewer workers.

-The investigation should include workers' voices. In order to generate a plan of action, the business shall coordinate with the production department to make sure workloads and targets are balanced, realistic and fair (based on the number of workers), and that they do not affect workers' health.
 
-Workers should have a humane environment in their working line. Workload should not impact workers health. 

Talking Points;

-What is the standard amount of prawns for a worker per day? What is the maximum amount of Kg for this production line? Please report the business that the workers have reported having asked to do 800KG to 1500KG per day. Is the business aware of this amount?  
  
-What is the system that the business uses to track workloads and to make sure that workers are being distributed with a fair workload? 

-What is the recent turnover rate of this line? If the current turnover rate is high, what the business has done to make sure that works are not overworked? is there any plan to recruit more workers? 

NOTE FOR BHR; 
Please remind the business that Issara receive workload issue frequently from the TUS workers, which highlight the TUS's system need to be more strong when addressing this issue. 

Time Frame 2 weeks.
remediation_notes: Workers reported being asked to complete the same amount of work with only 32 workers whereas previously there used to be 50 workers on this line.
remediation_action: The business investigated and found that there were 26 workers in the segregation line, and noted that the raw material in that line was also halved, decreasing the ratio of workload per worker.
remediation_validation: Workers provided an update saying the number of workers had reduced further to 26. Also, the workload before New Year was around 50 tons of prawn on average per day but now it was reduced to 40 tons, only a 20% decrease.  The workload was still too high for the number of workers available.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-Effectively communicate to workers, managers and the line supervisors what the plan of action is to address this issue. The communication should include information about workload and tasks in the written and should be explained verbally to workers. 


-Training and planning sessions with Issara and HR on strengthening working conditions, then broader training for line supervisors and others.


Time frame 2 weeks.

The business said that they would conduct an internal survey to assess the situation and be able to find out the root cause of the issue and the actions needed to respond to the issue of line supervisors’ behaviour. However, the business later got back to Issara by saying that they were not able to conduct the survey at the moment because of the third wave of COVID-19 issue, but that the company had simplified the process of taking annual leave and the sick leaves by workers getting approval from HR staff instead that getting it from line supervisors. Since there is no clarity on any further steps the company would take given the COVID -19 situation and the current closure of the factory, Issara has decided to close all of the cases related to this report at this point and will update it as needed once the company resumes operations and workers can confirm if the issues have been solved.

description: Issues with workforce and workloads: no violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers from sewing line 6 reported having a hard time dealing with their line supervisor because she asks for the high demand of up to 40 pieces per hour, it used to be 15-20 in the past. Workers reported being pressured to work faster, the supervisor shouts and put pressure on them to work faster, and threatened them by saying that they will be moved to a different production line or sent to HR if they can not reach the target. Workers reported since the news increased wages, the business is putting pressure on workers to work faster, there was also an issue at line 5 where all workers left the production yesterday and went home as they could not bear the pressure to complete the expected workload.

Talking points:
-Are there changes in the production demands and are workers being asked to reach double the previous target?
-Is HR aware that line supervisors are threatening punishment to workers for not meeting targets?
-What are the incentives if the workers meet the target?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Investigate this matter, whether line supervisors have been unprofessional by shouting at workers and threatening punishment for workers not meeting increased targets
-Train supervisors on how to communicate production targets without the use of shouting and threatening punishment to workers
-Review the production targets set by the company, as workers have expressed that there's too much pressure from the increased workload
-Communicate clearly with all workers the company's target system, and the reason for any adjustments in the targets made
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Line 6, K. Leena, the HR manager will investigate this matter and get back to us next week. She mentioned that currently, the company does not have an incentives policy.
Line 5, She was aware of this issue, she investigated and the root cause is the line supervisor of line 5 was on sick leave for a week. Then another supervisor came to help but he didn't know how to communicate or care for the workers. That is why workers walk out and do not work overtime. However, HR trained supervisors on how to communicate production targets without shouting and threatening workers with punishment. Simultaneously, HR communicated clearly with the workers' Line 5 and the reason for any changes to the targets made. Line 5 is currently functioning normally.
remediation_notes: Workers reported having a hard time dealing with their line supervisor who was demanding they complete up to 40 pieces per hour, whereas the target used to be 15-20 in the past. The supervisor shouts and put pressure on them to work faster, and threatened them by saying that they will be moved to a different production line or sent to HR if they can not reach the target.

Recommendations for systems change:
-Consult workers about the production demands when the company forecasts that there will changes in the demand and need to adjust the targets

description: Issues with workforce and workloads: no violation of law or employment contract
Issues with workforce and workloads: no violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; the issue with the workload and insufficient workers. There used to be 12 workers in this line where they are only 9 at the moment for the same amount of workload. 

Recommendations; 
-The business to conduct an investigation ethically taking into account safeguards for the workers. The investigation should aim to understand why the workers are being asked to do the same amount of work with fewer workers? The investigation should include workers' voices. 
-HR should coordinate with the production department to develop a corrective action plan to make sure workloads are balanced, fair, and do not affect workers' health. 
-The business to have a clear standard for the workload distribution system depending on the number of present workers.

Talking Points; 

-What is the business plan for these working lines? Are they planning to recruit more workers? 
-How does the business manage the workload when they have fewer number workers? 
-Has the business reduced the workload since three workers have left this production line?

May-7-2021. Added talking points; 
-Workers have updated only one worker being recruited but 4 more steaming pots being added to this product line which would increase the workload. What are the steps that the business is taking to solve the manpower issue in this line, is the company hiring more workers or is the company revising the workloads? 
-What is the business plan to balance the workload and the manpower while they can recruit more workers? 

-Please suggest adding more workers or adjust the workload. 

Timeframe 1 pay period
remediation_business_steps_taken:
HR updated that of course the demand for productivity is higher. The turnover is increasing especially Thai workers because most of Thai workers who are Muslim and they resigned for their religion activities. And SCC is recruiting 400 workers more. However, HR will investigate at PF2 and all the production. The PF2 line may have more workers next week.

Business solution: HR found the workers to replace the workers who resigned, they are 2 workers started working on 26 March, there is one more on the way, which will start working in early April. They need time to recruit workers to work in this shift, which the SCC provide incentives to work at this shift.


Workers; 
Workers updated that only one worker has been recruited, however, four more steaming pots have been added in this specific line. That means that the workload has been increased too.

18 May 2021.

HR clarified that now the company is recruiting more workers. In this period of time, it’s difficult to recruit more workers, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic situation. Some job seekers/workers are Muslim, they have to travel to Pattani province for religious activities so they have to be quarantined for 14 days. 
HR added more that now the company has been recruiting more than 300-400 workers per month.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Communication.
-The business to have a regular monitoring system of the working line to ensure that an adequate number of workers are in each line, to prevent a situation where there are not enough workers in a particular line leading to overwork. 

-The business to communicate to workers what are the actions being taken to address this issue. 

-Issara can provide tailored training to line supervisors and productions as needed.

-Training and planning sessions with Issara and HR on strengthening working conditions, then broader training for line supervisors and others.

description: Issues with workforce and workloads: no violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue 1: The issue with the abusive manager with a broken arm at the building 3 raw shrimp peeling line being abusive with the workers. Workers added that the manager uses abusive words with workers, forces them to do OT, increases the target settings, and does not let workers have full lunch breaks. 

Recommendations; 

The business to make a clear announcement regarding the target setting for the workers in this line. 

Talking points. 
-What is the target set for the workers in this line? 
-Workers have reported an increased target setting since this supervisor/manager has started working in this production line, is that the HR and production decision? If yes, were there any communications about the changes? 


Time frame - 2 weeks.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business to conduct training to this manager and any other supervisors that are found to be having the same behavior. The business should communicate to the manager what the company policy is on fair and ethical treatment of workers, especially of foreign migrant workers, and what are the disciplinary actions for those who do not follow those policies. 

-Recommend Issara Academy training to HR staff and Line supervisor. 

-Issara can also provide tailored training to full HR teams on-site, and provide systems review with tailored recommendations to eliminate labor risks. 
timeframe 2 pay periods 

-The business to make a clear announcement with all workers about the grievance channels to report such issues confidentially. This announcement should come from the HR manager and it should be clearly communicated to all workers including line supervisors and managers. The business should make sure a "no-retaliation policy" is in place, and that it is understood and followed by every employee.

description: Issues with workforce and workloads: no violation of law or employment contract
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported for the past couple months, they have not been given OT hours, with the manager citing a lack of orders but when there is OT, it is not given to Bangladeshi workers but given to Nepali and Myanmar workers.  The business also force them to meet daily targets which have been increased. When workers raise the issue of these increased targets, the employer will tell them they can leave and go back to Bangladesh if they can't keep up.

NOTE: The worker would like Issara to raise this issue with the business but doesn't want his identity to be disclosed.

Recommendations for the employer: 
- The employer should communicate clearly to workers about the production demands and the forecast for OT hours in the coming months. 
- The employer should clarify that daily targets are not tied to the daily wage. Workers are to be paid per 8-hour shift as per the contract, whether or not targets are met. Any time worked beyond the 8-hour period should be paid as OT.
- The employer should have an equitable and non-coercive OT system that doesn't favor workers from any nationality over another. Communicate how OT hours are offered to workers to show that it is fairly distributed and non-discriminatory

When workers raise the issue of these increased targets, the employer will tell them they can leave and go back home if they can't keep up.

description: Pregnant workers facing issues with workloads and working conditions: minor issue
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1 (Oct 5, 2022)
A pregnant worker reported that 11 pregnant workers work in the shrimp peeling line 4 was poorly treated by the line-supervisor (green cap), Ms. Kyae Oah. The line supervisor didn't let the pregnant workers sit and work and complained to the pregnant workers and shouted at them if the pregnant workers took toilet breaks more than 1-2 times a day. Under her supervision, all pregnant workers have to work just like normal workers. In other lines, the supervisors usually distribute the worker IDs to pregnant workers earlier than other workers so that the pregnant workers can leave first at the end of the work shift and not have to wait in a long queue. However, in this line, the supervisor doesn't let the pregnant workers to sign out earlier.

Talking points:
-Does the company have a policy to temporarily change the duties to suitable work for pregnant workers?
-Is HR aware that some pregnant worker are treated differently, depending on the supervisor? That some pregnant workers are made to work just like normal workers rather than considering a temporary adjustment to suit the health concerns of pregnant workers?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Investigate the behavior of the line supervisors in the shrimp peeling line and the work duties that are being assigned to pregnant workers.
-Make a verbal and written announcement to clarify with the pregnant workers regarding the temporary adjustments being made to work duties for pregnant workers
-Train line supervisors so that the temporary adjustment in the work duties of pregnant workers is implemented consistently across different lines.


Case #2 (Nov 16, 2022)
One of the pregnant workers reported that on 16th and 17th Nov, the business asked the 14 pregnant workers to leave their working line and hide at a place nearby the toilets. The clients thought that the business asked them to hide to avoid the visitors or audit seeing pregnant ladies working as normal workers. Since there is no shelter in their hiding place some pregnant ladies are feeling unwell and tired. So the client ask help from Issara to help them free from this condition.
